nodes.title: ATLAS roadmap

nodes.summary: Logic studies formal languages, proof, models, semantics, consistency, and the foundations of mathematical reasoning.
nodes.title: Logic

nodes.summary: Logics of necessity and possibility interpreted on Kripke models, their axiomatizations, completeness and decidability, and extensions such as epistemic logic, dynamic logic and the modal μ-calculus.
nodes.title: Modal logic
Epistemic logic

nodes.summary: Given a type of worlds $W$, a type of atoms and a type of agents, an epistemic model consists of a binary accessibility relation $R_i$ on $W$ for each agent $i$ and a valuation assigning to each world the atoms true there; the world type $W$ is required to be nonempty.
nodes.title: Epistemic models

nodes.summary: Given a type of atoms and a type of agents, the formulas of epistemic logic are built inductively: every atom $p$ is a formula, falsity $\bot$ is a formula, if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so is the implication $\varphi \to \psi$, and if $\varphi$ is a formula and $i$ is an agent then $K_i \varphi$ (read "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$") is a formula.
nodes.title: Epistemic formulas

nodes.summary: The negation $\neg\varphi$ of an epistemic formula $\varphi$ is the implication $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation of epistemic formulas

nodes.summary: The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of epistemic formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the implication $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of epistemic formulas

nodes.summary: Satisfaction of an epistemic formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined by recursion on the formula, writing $R_i$ for the accessibility relation of agent $i$ in $M$ and $K_i \varphi$ for the formula "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$": an atom $a$ holds at $w$ when the valuation of $M$ makes $a$ true at $w$; $\bot$ holds at no world; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ when $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does;…
nodes.title: Satisfaction in an epistemic model

nodes.summary: A formula $\varphi$ is valid in an epistemic model $M$ when $\varphi$ is satisfied at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Validity in an epistemic model

nodes.summary: In every epistemic model, the formula $\bot$ is not valid: it fails at some world.
nodes.title: Falsity is not valid in an epistemic model

nodes.summary: In an epistemic model $M$, the disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of two formulas, defined as $\neg \varphi \to \psi$, is satisfied at a world $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ or $\psi$ is satisfied at $w$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a disjunction

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". For every epistemic model $M$, every agent $i$ and all formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the formula $K_i (\varphi \to \psi) \to (K_i \varphi \to K_i \psi)$ is valid in $M$: knowledge distributes over implication.
nodes.title: Distribution axiom K

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is reflexive. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $K_i \varphi \to \varphi$ is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Truth axiom T

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is transitive. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $K_i \varphi \to K_i K_i \varphi$ is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Positive introspection axiom 4

nodes.summary: Write $K_i \varphi$ for "agent $i$ knows $\varphi$". Let $M$ be an epistemic model in which the accessibility relation $R_i$ of agent $i$ is euclidean: for all worlds $a$, $b$, $c$, if $a \mathrel{R_i} b$ and $a \mathrel{R_i} c$ then $b \mathrel{R_i} c$. Then for every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\neg K_i \varphi \to K_i \neg K_i \varphi$ is valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Negative introspection axiom 5

nodes.summary: The epistemic model whose worlds are the two booleans, with $\mathrm{true}$ read as heads and $\mathrm{false}$ as tails, with a single atom $p$ true exactly at the heads world, and with two agents $0$ and $1$: agent $0$ sees the coin, so its accessibility relation is equality of worlds, and agent $1$ does not, so its accessibility relation relates every pair of worlds.
nodes.title: The two-agent coin model

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At a world $v$ of that model, the formula $K_0 p$ holds if and only if $v$ is the heads world: agent $0$ sees the coin.
nodes.title: Agent 0 knows the coin is heads exactly at heads

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At a world $v$ of that model, the formula $K_0 \neg p$ holds if and only if $v$ is the tails world.
nodes.title: Agent 0 knows the coin is tails exactly at tails

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. The formula $K_1 p$ is false at the heads world: agent $1$ considers the tails world possible.
nodes.title: Agent 1 does not know that the coin is heads

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the atom "the coin is heads" of the two-agent coin model. At every world of that model the formula $K_1(K_0 p \lor K_0 \neg p)$ holds: agent $1$ knows that agent $0$ either knows $p$ or knows $\neg p$.
nodes.title: Agent 1 knows that agent 0 knows whether the coin is heads
Kripke semantics

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of atoms, the formulas of basic modal logic over $\alpha$ are generated as follows: every atom $p \in \alpha$ is a formula; falsity $\bot$ is a formula; if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so is the implication $\varphi \to \psi$; and if $\varphi$ is a formula then so is the necessity formula $\Box\varphi$.
nodes.title: Modal formulas

nodes.summary: The negation of a modal formula $\varphi$ is the formula $\neg\varphi := \varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation of modal formulas

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the formula $\Diamond\varphi$ ("possibly $\varphi$") is $
eg\Box
eg\varphi$, where $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: The possibility operator

nodes.summary: The formula $\top$ is the negation $\neg\bot$ of falsity, that is, the implication $\bot \to \bot$.
nodes.title: The truth constant

nodes.summary:
For modal formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is the formula $
eg(\varphi 	o 
eg\psi)$, where $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Conjunction

nodes.summary: The disjunction of modal formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the formula $\varphi \lor \psi := \neg\varphi \to \psi$, where $\neg\varphi$ is $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of modal formulas

nodes.summary: For modal formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the distribution axiom K is the formula $\Box(\varphi \to \psi) \to (\Box\varphi \to \Box\psi)$.
nodes.title: Axiom K

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, the reflexivity axiom T is the formula $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$.
nodes.title: Axiom T

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, the transitivity axiom 4 is the formula $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$.
nodes.title: Axiom 4

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the seriality axiom D is the formula $\Box\varphi 	o \Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\psi$ is $
eg\Box
eg\psi$ and $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Axiom D

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the symmetry axiom B is the formula $\varphi 	o \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\psi$ is $
eg\Box
eg\psi$ and $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Axiom B

nodes.summary:
For a modal formula $\varphi$, the euclidean axiom 5 is the formula $\Diamond\varphi 	o \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\psi$ is $
eg\Box
eg\psi$ and $
eg\chi$ stands for $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Axiom 5

nodes.summary: A Kripke model consists of a nonempty collection of worlds, an accessibility relation, and an atom valuation.
nodes.title: Kripke model

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model with accessibility relation $R$. Satisfaction of a modal formula at a world $w$ of $M$ is defined by recursion on the formula: $w$ satisfies an atom $p$ if and only if the valuation of $M$ makes $p$ true at $w$; $w$ never satisfies $\bot$; $w$ satisfies $\varphi \to \psi$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\psi$ whenever it satisfies $\varphi$; and $w$ satisfies $\Box\varphi$ if and only if…
nodes.title: Satisfaction in a Kripke model

nodes.summary: A formula $\varphi$ is globally valid in a Kripke model $M$ when $\varphi$ is satisfied at every world of $M$.
nodes.title: Global validity in a Kripke model

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, the formula $\bot$ is not valid in $M$: since $M$ has at least one world and no world satisfies $\bot$, some world of $M$ fails to satisfy $\bot$.
nodes.title: Falsity is valid in no Kripke model

nodes.summary:
Let $M$ be a Kripke model with accessibility relation $R$, and let $\Diamond\varphi$ denote the formula $
eg\Box
eg\varphi$, where $
eg\chi$ is $\chi 	o  ot$. For every world $w$ and modal formula $\varphi$, $w$ satisfies $\Diamond\varphi$ in $M$ if and only if there is a world $v$ with $w \mathrel{R} v$ such that $v$ satisfies $\varphi$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Semantics of possibility

nodes.summary: The K axiom is valid on every Kripke model.
nodes.title: Validity of axiom K on Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is reflexive: $R\,w\,w$ for every world $w$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the T axiom $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom T is valid on reflexive Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is transitive: $R\,u\,v$ and $R\,v\,w$ imply $R\,u\,w$ for all worlds $u, v, w$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the 4 axiom $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$ is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom 4 is valid on transitive Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is serial: every world $w$ has some world $v$ with $R\,w\,v$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the D axiom $\Box\varphi \to \Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$, is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom D is valid on serial Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is symmetric: $R\,u\,v$ implies $R\,v\,u$ for all worlds $u, v$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the B axiom $\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$, is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom B is valid on symmetric Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation $R$ is euclidean: $R\,u\,v$ and $R\,u\,w$ imply $R\,v\,w$ for all worlds $u, v, w$. Then for every formula $\varphi$ the 5 axiom $\Diamond\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$, where $\Diamond\varphi$ abbreviates $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$, is globally valid in $M$.
nodes.title: Axiom 5 is valid on euclidean Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be Kripke models over the same atoms, with sets of worlds $W$ and $V$ and accessibility relations $R_M$ and $R_N$. A bounded morphism from $M$ to $N$ is a map $f : W \to V$ such that every atom holds at a world $w$ in $M$ if and only if it holds at $f(w)$ in $N$; whenever $w \mathrel{R_M} w'$, also $f(w) \mathrel{R_N} f(w')$ (forth); and whenever $f(w) \mathrel{R_N} v'$, there is a world $w'$ with…
nodes.title: Bounded morphism

nodes.summary: Two bounded morphisms $f$ and $g$ between the same Kripke models are equal if $f(w) = g(w)$ for every world $w$.
nodes.title: Extensionality for bounded morphisms

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, the identity map on the worlds of $M$ is a bounded morphism from $M$ to itself.
nodes.title: Identity bounded morphism

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$, $M_2$, $M_3$ be Kripke models over the same atoms. If $f$ is a bounded morphism from $M_1$ to $M_2$ and $g$ is a bounded morphism from $M_2$ to $M_3$, then the composite map $g \circ f$ on worlds is a bounded morphism from $M_1$ to $M_3$.
nodes.title: Composition of bounded morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a bounded morphism from a Kripke model $M$ to a Kripke model $N$ over the same atoms. Then for every modal formula $\varphi$ and every world $w$ of $M$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ in $M$ if and only if $f(w)$ satisfies $\varphi$ in $N$.
nodes.title: Invariance of modal satisfaction under bounded morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be Kripke models over the same atoms and let $f$ be a bounded morphism from $M$ to $N$ whose map on worlds is surjective. Then for every formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is globally valid in $M$ if and only if $\varphi$ is globally valid in $N$.
nodes.title: Surjective bounded morphisms preserve and reflect validity
Bisimulation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be Kripke models over the same atoms, with sets of worlds $W$ and $V$ and accessibility relations $R_M$ and $R_N$. A relation $Z \subseteq W \times V$ is a bisimulation between $M$ and $N$ when, for all $w \in W$ and $v \in V$ with $w \mathrel{Z} v$: each atom $a$ is true at $w$ in $M$ if and only if $a$ is true at $v$ in $N$; for every $w'$ with $w \mathrel{R_M} w'$ there is $v'$ with…
nodes.title: Bisimulation

nodes.summary: Let $Z$ be a bisimulation between Kripke models $M$ and $N$ over the same atoms. If $Z$ relates a world $w$ of $M$ to a world $v$ of $N$, then every modal formula $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied at $v$ in $N$.
nodes.title: Bisimulations preserve modal formulas

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be Kripke models over the same atoms. A world $w$ of $M$ and a world $v$ of $N$ are bisimilar if some bisimulation between $M$ and $N$ relates $w$ to $v$.
nodes.title: Bisimilar worlds

nodes.summary: If a world $w$ of a Kripke model $M$ and a world $v$ of a Kripke model $N$ over the same atoms are bisimilar, then every modal formula $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfied at $v$ in $N$.
nodes.title: Bisimilar worlds are modally equivalent
Modal μ-calculus

nodes.summary: The formulas over a type of atoms are built from atoms $a$, negated atoms $\neg a$, variables $X_n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ (de Bruijn indices for the fixed-point binders), $\bot$ and $\top$ by conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$, disjunction $\varphi \vee \psi$, the modalities $\Box\varphi$ and $\Diamond\varphi$, and the fixed-point binders $\mu\varphi$ and $\nu\varphi$.
nodes.title: Formulas of the modal μ-calculus

nodes.summary:
The meta-level negation $
eg\varphi$ of a μ-calculus formula $\varphi$ swaps each connective with its dual. It is defined by recursion: an atom $p$ becomes the negated atom $\overline{p}$ and $\overline{p}$ becomes $p$, each variable $x_n$ stays $x_n$, $
eg ot = 	op$, $
eg	op =  ot$, $
eg(\varphi \wedge \psi) = 
eg\varphi \vee 
eg\psi$, $
eg(\varphi \vee \psi) = 
eg\varphi \wedge 
eg\psi$,…
nodes.title: Negation of μ-calculus formulas

nodes.summary:
Write $
eg\varphi$ for the meta-level negation of a μ-calculus formula $\varphi$, which swaps each connective with its dual. For every μ-calculus formula $\varphi$, negating twice gives back $\varphi$: $
eg
eg\varphi = \varphi$.
nodes.title: Meta-level negation is an involution

nodes.summary: An environment $\rho$ assigns to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$ a predicate $\rho(n)$ on worlds. Its extension by a predicate $S$ on worlds is the environment that assigns $S$ to index $0$ and $\rho(n)$ to index $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Extending an environment under a binder

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model with accessibility relation $R$ and valuation $V$, and let $\rho$ be an environment assigning a set of worlds to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For a set of worlds $S$, write $\rho[0 \mapsto S]$ for the environment sending index $0$ to $S$ and index $n + 1$ to $\rho(n)$. The set $[\![\varphi]\!]_\rho$ of worlds satisfying a formula $\varphi$ in $M$ under $\rho$ is defined by…
nodes.title: Satisfaction in the modal μ-calculus

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and let $\rho$ and $\rho'$ be environments (each assigns a set of worlds of $M$ to every variable $n$) with $\rho(n) \subseteq \rho'(n)$ for every $n$. Then every μ-calculus formula $\varphi$ holds under $\rho'$ at every world of $M$ where it holds under $\rho$: enlarging every variable's denotation can only enlarge a formula's denotation.
nodes.title: Satisfaction is monotone in the environment

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment assigning a set of worlds to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. For a set of worlds $S$, write $\rho[0 \mapsto S]$ for the environment sending index $0$ to $S$ and index $n + 1$ to $\rho(n)$. If $S_1 \subseteq S_2$ are sets of worlds, then every world that satisfies $\varphi$ in $M$ under $\rho[0 \mapsto S_1]$ also satisfies…
nodes.title: Monotonicity in the bound variable

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. Write $\llbracket\psi\rrbracket_\sigma$ for the set of worlds of $M$ at which $\psi$ holds under the environment $\sigma$, and $\rho[S]$ for the extension of $\rho$ under a binder by a set of worlds $S$ (variable $0$ denotes $S$ and variable $n + 1$ denotes $\rho(n)$). For $T = \llbracket\mu\varphi\rrbracket_\rho$, where…
nodes.title: The least fixed point is a pre-fixed point

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, environment $\rho$ and μ-calculus formula $\varphi$, every world satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $\rho$ also satisfies $\varphi$ in the extension of $\rho$ by the set of worlds satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $\rho$.
nodes.title: The least fixed point is contained in its unfolding

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment assigning a set of worlds to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. Let $A$ be the set of worlds satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $M$ under $\rho$. Then $A$ is exactly the set of worlds satisfying $\varphi$ in $M$ under the environment that sends index $0$ to $A$ and index $n + 1$ to $\rho(n)$.
nodes.title: The μ unfolding

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. Write $\llbracket\psi\rrbracket_\sigma$ for the set of worlds of $M$ at which $\psi$ holds under the environment $\sigma$, and $\rho[S]$ for the extension of $\rho$ under a binder by a set of worlds $S$ (variable $0$ denotes $S$ and variable $n + 1$ denotes $\rho(n)$). For $T = \llbracket\nu\varphi\rrbracket_\rho$, where…

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. For $T = \llbracket\nu\varphi\rrbracket_\rho$, where…
nodes.title: The greatest fixed point is a pre-fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment assigning a set of worlds to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. Let $A$ be the set of worlds satisfying $\nu\varphi$ in $M$ under $\rho$. Then $A$ is exactly the set of worlds satisfying $\varphi$ in $M$ under the environment that sends index $0$ to $A$ and index $n + 1$ to $\rho(n)$.
nodes.title: The ν unfolding

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment, $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula and $P$ a predicate on worlds. If every world satisfying $\varphi$ in the extension of $\rho$ by $P$ satisfies $P$, then every world satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $\rho$ satisfies $P$.
nodes.title: Park induction

Write $\llbracket\psi\rrbracket_\sigma$ for the set of worlds at which $\psi$ holds under the environment $\sigma$, and $\rho[P]$ for the extension of $\rho$ under a binder by $P$ (variable $0$ denotes $P$ and variable $n + 1$ denotes $\rho(n)$). If $P \subseteq \llbracket\varphi\rrbracket_{\rho[P]}$,…
nodes.title: Coinduction for the greatest fixed point

nodes.summary: Given a Kripke model $M$, an environment $\rho$ (a set of worlds $\rho(n)$ for each variable $n$) and a μ-calculus formula $\varphi$, this is the monotone map on sets of worlds of $M$ sending $S$ to the set of worlds at which $\varphi$ holds under $\rho[S]$, the extension of $\rho$ under a binder by $S$ (variable $0$ denotes $S$ and variable $n + 1$ denotes $\rho(n)$).

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment assigning a set of worlds to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. For a set of worlds $S$, write $\rho[0 \mapsto S]$ for the environment sending index $0$ to $S$ and index $n + 1$ to $\rho(n)$. Then the set of worlds satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $M$ under $\rho$ is the least fixed point of the monotone operator on sets of worlds…
nodes.title: The μ formula denotes the least fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment assigning a set of worlds to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula. For a set of worlds $S$, write $\rho[0 \mapsto S]$ for the environment sending index $0$ to $S$ and index $n + 1$ to $\rho(n)$. Then the set of worlds satisfying $\nu\varphi$ in $M$ under $\rho$ is the greatest fixed point of the monotone operator on sets of…
nodes.title: The ν formula denotes the greatest fixed point

nodes.summary: For every environment $\rho$ (assigning to each variable index $n$ a predicate $\rho(n)$ on worlds) and every predicate $S$ on worlds, complementing every predicate of the extension of $\rho$ by $S$ gives the extension of the complemented environment $n \mapsto \neg\rho(n)$ by the predicate $w \mapsto \neg S(w)$.
nodes.title: Complementing an extended environment

nodes.summary: For every predicate $S$ on worlds, the predicate $w \mapsto \neg\neg S(w)$ equals $S$.
nodes.title: Double complement of a predicate

Let $\neg\varphi$ be the dual formula of $\varphi$, obtained by swapping atoms with negated atoms, $\bot$ with $\top$, $\wedge$ with $\vee$, $\Box$ with $\Diamond$ and $\mu$ with $\nu$, and keeping variables. Write $\overline{\rho}$ for the environment sending…
nodes.title: Duality

reading_title.source: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$, $\mathsf{EF}\,p$ is the least fixed point formula $\mu X.\,(p \vee \Diamond X)$. It expresses that some state reachable from the current one satisfies $p$.
nodes.title: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$

reading_title.source: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$, $\mathsf{AG}\,p$ is the greatest fixed point formula $\nu X.\,(p \wedge \Box X)$. It expresses that every state reachable from the current one satisfies $p$.
nodes.title: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$

reading_title.source: $\mathsf{EF}$ is reachability

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, every environment $\rho$ (an assignment of a predicate on worlds to each variable index), every atom $p$ and every world $w$, the μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$ holds at $w$ in $\rho$ if and only if $p$ is true at some world reachable from $w$ in zero or more steps of the accessibility relation of $M$.
nodes.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ is reachability

reading_title.source: $\mathsf{AG}$ is universal reachability

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, every environment $\rho$ (an assignment of a predicate on worlds to each variable index), every atom $p$ and every world $w$, the μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$ holds at $w$ in $\rho$ if and only if $p$ is true at every world reachable from $w$ in zero or more steps of the accessibility relation of $M$.
nodes.title: $\mathsf{AG}$ is universal reachability

reading_title.source: The formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ is false everywhere

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ and every environment $\rho$, the formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ holds at no world of $M$ under $\rho$. In de Bruijn form this formula is $\mu\, \mu\, x_1$: inside the inner binder, variable $1$ refers to the outer binder, not to the inner one.
nodes.title: The formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ is false everywhere

reading_title.source: The formula $\nu X.\, \nu Y.\, X$ is true everywhere

nodes.summary:
For every Kripke model $M$ and every environment $ho$, the formula $
u X.\, 
u Y.\, X$ holds at every world of $M$ under $ho$. In de Bruijn form this formula is $
u\, 
u\, x_1$: inside the inner binder, variable $1$ refers to the outer binder. This is the dual of the fact that $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ is false everywhere.
nodes.title: The formula $\nu X.\, \nu Y.\, X$ is true everywhere

nodes.summary: A formula is closed at depth `d` when every free de Bruijn variable is `< d`: only `μ` / `ν` increase the depth; `□` / `◇` do not bind variables and preserve it.
nodes.title: μ-calculus formula closed at a given binding depth

nodes.summary: A formula is closed when it is closed at depth `0`: every variable is bound.
nodes.title: Closed modal μ-calculus formula

nodes.summary: The depth of a formula: the length of its longest root-to-leaf path, counting each connective once.
nodes.title: Depth of a modal μ-calculus formula

nodes.summary: A closed formula does not depend on the environment: environments agreeing below the depth give the same denotation.
nodes.title: Denotation of a closed μ-calculus formula is environment-independent

nodes.summary: An injective encoding of μ-calculus formulas over `ℕ` atoms as natural numbers, via the Cantor pairing function `Nat.pair`. This is a Nat code only, not a complexity input encoding: repeated pairing squares the code at every unary connective, so the binary length of the code of `box^d (atom 0)` doubles at each `box` and is exponential in `d`. nodes.title: Theorems of a normal modal logic

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas. The local consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ form the least set of modal formulas that contains every member of $\Gamma$ and every theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ and is closed under modus ponens: whenever it contains $\varphi \to \psi$ and $\varphi$, it contains $\psi$.
nodes.title: Local consequence in a normal modal logic

nodes.summary: The set of extra axioms of the normal modal logic K is the empty set of modal formulas over a given type of atoms; that is, K adds no axioms to the propositional axioms and the distribution axiom.

nodes.summary: The extra axioms of the modal logic T are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of T

nodes.summary: The extra axioms of the modal logic S4 are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T) and $\Box\varphi \to \Box\Box\varphi$ (axiom 4), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of S4

nodes.summary: For a modal formula $\varphi$, write $\Diamond\varphi$ for $\neg\Box\neg\varphi$. The extra axioms of the modal logic S5 are the formulas $\Box\varphi \to \varphi$ (axiom T) and $\Diamond\varphi \to \Box\Diamond\varphi$ (axiom 5), for all modal formulas $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Extra axioms of S5

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas. For every modal formula $\varphi$, the formula $\varphi \to \varphi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Self-implication is a theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda \subseteq \Lambda'$ be sets of modal formulas. Every theorem of the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is a theorem of $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda'$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of theorems in the extra axioms

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$, $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be sets of modal formulas with $\Gamma \subseteq \Delta$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Delta$ in $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of local consequence in the hypotheses

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be sets of formulas such that every formula of $\Delta$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$. If a formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Delta$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of local consequence

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. If $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\psi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\psi \to \varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: The deduction theorem for local modal consequence, forward direction

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be modal formulas. In the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\psi\}$ if and only if $\psi \to \varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: The deduction theorem for local modal consequence

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas. A modal formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the empty set of hypotheses in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$ if and only if $\varphi$ is a theorem of $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Consequences of no hypotheses are the theorems

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas. If a modal formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then there is a finite set $\Delta \subseteq \Gamma$ such that $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Delta$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Compactness of local modal consequence

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $\Gamma$ a set of hypotheses. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then every formula $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Ex falso quodlibet

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and let $\varphi$ be a modal formula. If both $\varphi$ and its negation $\neg\varphi$ are local consequences of the hypotheses $\Gamma$ in the normal modal logic $\mathbf{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then so is $\bot$.
nodes.title: Contradiction yields falsity

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $\Gamma$ a set of hypotheses and $\varphi$ a formula. nodes.title: Proof by contradiction

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\bot$ is a local consequence of the hypotheses $\Gamma \cup \{\varphi\}$ in the normal modal logic $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, then $\neg\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, where $\neg\varphi$ abbreviates $\varphi \to \bot$.

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\Lambda$ a set of modal formulas each of which is valid in $M$. Propositional dynamic logic (PDL)

nodes.summary: A model of propositional dynamic logic with set of worlds $W$ consists of a binary accessibility relation $R_a$ on $W$ for each atomic action label $a$, and a valuation that says which atoms are true at each world.
nodes.title: PDL model

nodes.summary: The formulas of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type of atomic action labels are the atoms $p$, falsity $\bot$, implications $\varphi \to \psi$ of formulas, and boxes $[\alpha]\varphi$ of a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$. Formulas and programs are defined by simultaneous induction.
nodes.title: PDL formulas

nodes.summary: The programs of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type of atomic action labels are the atomic actions $a$, sequential compositions $\alpha ; \beta$, nondeterministic choices $\alpha \cup \beta$, iterations $\alpha^*$, and tests $\varphi?$ of a formula $\varphi$. Programs and formulas are defined by simultaneous induction.
nodes.title: PDL programs

nodes.summary: For a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$, the formula $\langle\alpha\rangle\varphi$ is defined as $\alpha \to \bot$, that is, as $\neg[\alpha]\neg\varphi$: possibility is the dual of necessity.
nodes.title: Possibility in PDL

nodes.summary: In a model $M$, each program $\alpha$ denotes a binary relation $R_\alpha$ on worlds: an atomic action $a$ denotes its accessibility relation $R_a$; $(w, v) \in R_{\alpha;\beta}$ iff $(w, u) \in R_\alpha$ and $(u, v) \in R_\beta$ for some world $u$; $R_{\alpha \cup \beta} = R_\alpha \cup R_\beta$; $R_{\alpha^*}$ is the reflexive-transitive closure of $R_\alpha$; and $(w, v) \in R_{\varphi?}$ iff $w = v$ and…
nodes.title: Relation denoted by a PDL program

nodes.summary: Truth of a formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined by recursion: an atom $p$ holds at $w$ iff the valuation of $M$ makes $p$ true at $w$; $\bot$ holds nowhere; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ iff $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does; and $[\alpha]\varphi$ holds at $w$ iff $\varphi$ holds at every world $v$ with $(w, v) \in R_\alpha$, where $R_\alpha$ is the relation denoted by $\alpha$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of PDL formulas

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha;\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $[\alpha][\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$.
nodes.title: Box of a sequential composition

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha \cup \beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if both $[\alpha]\varphi$ and $[\beta]\varphi$ hold at $w$.
nodes.title: Box of a choice

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, program $\alpha$ and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ and $[\alpha][\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$.
nodes.title: Unfolding the box of an iteration

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$ and formulas $\psi$ and $\varphi$, the formula $[\psi?]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\psi$ holds at $w$.
nodes.title: Box of a test

nodes.summary: The PDL model whose worlds are the two Booleans $\mathsf{true}$ and $\mathsf{false}$, with a single atomic action $a$ and a single atom $p$: the action $a$ relates each world $s$ exactly to its negation $\lnot s$, and $p$ holds exactly at $\mathsf{true}$.

Sahlqvist formulas

nodes.summary: Positive and negative modal formulas are defined by simultaneous recursion: every atom is positive, $\bot$ is positive, $\varphi \to \psi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is negative and $\psi$ is positive, and $\Box\varphi$ is positive if $\varphi$ is positive.
nodes.title: Positive modal formulas

nodes.summary: Negative and positive modal formulas are defined by simultaneous recursion: no atom is negative, $\bot$ is negative, $\varphi \to \psi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is positive and $\psi$ is negative, and $\Box\varphi$ is negative if $\varphi$ is negative.
nodes.title: Negative modal formulas

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a modal formula $\varphi$, the iterated box $\Box^k \varphi$ is defined by $\Box^0 \varphi = \varphi$ and $\Box^{k+1} \varphi = \Box\,\Box^k \varphi$.
nodes.title: Iterated box

nodes.summary: The Sahlqvist antecedents form the smallest class of modal formulas that contains every boxed atom $\Box^k p$ (an atom $p$ under $k \ge 0$ boxes) and every negative formula, and is closed under $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\Diamond$.
nodes.title: Sahlqvist antecedents

nodes.summary: The set of atoms (propositional variables) occurring in a modal formula.
nodes.title: Atoms of a modal formula

nodes.summary: A modal formula is a Sahlqvist implication if it is an implication $\alpha \to \beta$ whose antecedent $\alpha$ is a Sahlqvist antecedent and whose consequent $\beta$ is a positive formula.
nodes.title: Sahlqvist implications

nodes.summary: The Sahlqvist formulas form the smallest class of modal formulas that contains every Sahlqvist implication, is closed under $\wedge$ and $\Box$, and contains $\varphi \vee \psi$ whenever $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are Sahlqvist formulas with no atom in common.
nodes.title: Sahlqvist formulas

nodes.summary: For every atom $p$, the instance $p \to \Box\Diamond p$ of the B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula: its antecedent $p$ is a boxed atom with zero boxes and its consequent $\Box\Diamond p$ is positive.
nodes.title: The B axiom is a Sahlqvist formula
Soundness and completeness of normal modal logics

nodes.summary: CSLib's unimodal propositions are translated into modal formulas in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis by recursion, writing $\varphi'$ for the translation of $\varphi$: an atom $p$ goes to $p$, falsehood to $\bot$, $\neg\varphi$ to $\varphi' \to \bot$, $\varphi \lor \psi$ to $(\varphi' \to \bot) \to \psi'$, and the diamond (the unimodal triangle) applied to $\varphi$ goes to $\Diamond\varphi'$, that is, to…
nodes.title: Translation of CSLib's modal propositions

nodes.summary: For a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on a nonempty type of worlds, the associated Kripke model has the same worlds, the binary accessibility relation of $m$ as its accessibility relation, and the valuation of $m$ as its valuation.
nodes.title: Kripke model of a CSLib model

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a CSLib unimodal model on a nonempty type of worlds, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis holds at $w$ in the Kripke model of $m$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $m$.
nodes.title: The translation preserves satisfaction

nodes.summary: A Kripke model $k$ on worlds $W$ gives the CSLib unimodal model on $W$ whose frame is the unimodal frame built from the accessibility relation of $k$ and whose valuation is the valuation of $k$.
nodes.title: The CSLib unimodal model of a Kripke model

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a Kripke model on a nonempty type of worlds. Converting $k$ to a CSLib unimodal model and converting that model back to a Kripke model gives $k$.
nodes.title: Kripke to CSLib and back is the identity

nodes.summary: For a nonempty type of worlds $W$, converting a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on $W$ into a Kripke model and then back into a CSLib unimodal model returns $m$: a unimodal frame is determined by its binary accessibility relation.
nodes.title: Round trip from CSLib models through Kripke models

nodes.summary:
Each modal formula built from atoms, $ ot$, $	o$ and $\Box$ is translated into a CSLib unimodal proposition by recursion: an atom $p$ goes to the atom $p$, $ ot$ goes to false, $\varphi 	o \psi$ goes to $
eg\varphi' \lor \psi'$, and $\Box\varphi$ goes to $
eg\Diamond
eg\varphi'$, where $\varphi'$ and $\psi'$ are the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$ and $\Diamond$ is the possibility operator of CSLib's…
nodes.title: Translation of modal formulas into CSLib propositions

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a Kripke model, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a modal formula in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis. Then $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $k$ if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition holds at $w$ in the CSLib model associated with $k$.
nodes.title: The reverse translation preserves satisfaction

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is valid in a Kripke model $k$ (true at every world of $k$) if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition is satisfied at every world of the CSLib unimodal model associated with $k$.
nodes.title: Validity agrees with its CSLib translation

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a class of CSLib unimodal models on a type of worlds and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Suppose that, if the type of worlds is nonempty, the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is valid in the Kripke model of every model in $S$. Then $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic of $S$: it holds at every world of every model in $S$.
nodes.title: Validity of the translation gives membership in CSLib's logic

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system K, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic K: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type.
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's K

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic T: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive.
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's T

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system S4, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic S4: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive.
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's S4

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system S5, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic S5: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation $R$ is reflexive, transitive and Euclidean ($R(w, u)$ and $R(w, v)$ imply $R(u, v)$).
nodes.title: Soundness for CSLib's S5

nodes.summary: For sets of formulas $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$, the set $\Gamma$ is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ when $\bot$ is not deducible from $\Gamma$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Consistency relative to a normal modal logic

nodes.summary: For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, a set of formulas is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ iff all its finite subsets are.
nodes.title: Consistency is of finite character

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas that is consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is contained in a set $M$ of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for normal modal logics

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every formula that is a local consequence of $M$ in that logic belongs to $M$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets of modal formulas are deductively closed

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, and $\varphi$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ modal formulas. If $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots) \in M$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n \in M$, then $\varphi \in M$.
nodes.title: Iterated modus ponens in maximal consistent sets

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas, $\varphi$ a modal formula and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ a list of modal formulas. If $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n\}$ in the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, then $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots)$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the same logic.
nodes.title: Discharging a list of hypotheses

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms, let $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ be formulas (with $n \ge 0$) and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $\Box(\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \gamma_n \to \varphi) \to (\Box\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \Box\gamma_n \to \Box\varphi)$ is a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Boxing an implication chain

nodes.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, the worlds of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$: the sets of formulas that are consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ and have no consistent proper superset.
nodes.title: Worlds of the canonical model

nodes.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of modal formulas and maximal $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent sets $M$ and $N$ (worlds of the canonical model), $M$ is related to $N$ iff every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$ belongs to $N$.
nodes.title: The canonical accessibility relation

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms such that $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. The canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ is the Kripke model whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$ (there is at least one, by Lindenbaum's lemma), in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff…
nodes.title: The canonical model

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, $M$ a canonical world, that is, a set of modal formulas maximal among the sets consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$, and $\varphi$ a modal formula. If $\Box\varphi \notin M$, then there is a canonical world $N$ with $\varphi \notin N$ that is accessible from $M$ in the…
nodes.title: Existence lemma

nodes.summary: A formula holds at a world of the canonical model iff it belongs to it.
nodes.title: Truth lemma

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ belongs to every maximal $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set that contains $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Deducibility from maximal consistent extensions

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas such that $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$, let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ holds at every world of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.
nodes.title: Completeness relative to the canonical model

nodes.summary:
For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms and every modal formula $\psi$, the formula $\Box\psi 	o \Box
eg
eg\psi$ is a theorem of the normal modal logic $K \oplus \Lambda$, where $
eg\chi$ abbreviates $\chi 	o  ot$.
nodes.title: Double-negation introduction under a box

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a class of Kripke models, given as a predicate on models. A set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas locally entails a formula $\varphi$ over $C$ when, for every Kripke model $M$ in $C$ whose type of worlds lies in the universe of the atoms and every world $w$ of $M$, if every formula of $\Gamma$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$, then $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Local semantic consequence over a class of Kripke models

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in K.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of K

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in T.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of T

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S4.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of S4

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S5.
nodes.title: Strong completeness of S5

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K if and only if $\varphi$ is valid, that is, true at every world, in every Kripke model whose worlds live in the universe of the atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of K

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of T if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of T

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S4 if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of S4

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S5 if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of S5

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $C$ a class of Kripke models whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, such that $C$ contains the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ whenever $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. Then every $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set $\Gamma$ of formulas is satisfiable in $C$: some model in $C$ has a world at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence from the canonical model

nodes.summary: For every K-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for K

nodes.summary: For every T-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a reflexive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for T

nodes.summary: For every S4-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a reflexive transitive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for S4

nodes.summary: For every S5-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence and whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Model existence for S5

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in K if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over all Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of K

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in T if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of T

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S4 if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive transitive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S4

nodes.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S5 if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over Kripke models whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every such Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.
nodes.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S5

nodes.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, this is the unimodal model of CSLib's modal semantics whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$, in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff $p \in M$.
nodes.title: The canonical model as a CSLib model

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms, and let $S$ be a set of CSLib unimodal models whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$. If $S$ contains the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$, viewed as a CSLib model, and a CSLib proposition $\varphi$ holds at every world of every model in $S$, then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of…
nodes.title: Validity in a class containing the canonical model gives derivability

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of K if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic K over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model with worlds $W$.
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's K

nodes.summary: For a CSLib unimodal proposition $\varphi$, the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T if and only if, for every type of worlds in the universe of the atoms, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic T over that type, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive.
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's T

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of S4 if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic S4 over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model with worlds $W$ whose accessibility relation is…
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's S4

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proposition of CSLib's unimodal language over a type of atoms $A$. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of S5 if and only if, for every type of worlds $W$ in the universe of $A$, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic S5 over $W$ and $A$, that is, $\varphi$ holds at every world of every CSLib model with worlds $W$ whose accessibility relation…
nodes.title: Completeness for CSLib's S5
Filtration and the finite model property

nodes.summary: The finite set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of a modal formula $\varphi$, including $\varphi$ itself, is defined by recursion: $\mathrm{sub}(p) = \{p\}$ for an atom $p$, $\mathrm{sub}(\bot) = \{\bot\}$, $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi \to \psi) = \{\varphi \to \psi\} \cup \mathrm{sub}(\varphi) \cup \mathrm{sub}(\psi)$, and $\mathrm{sub}(\Box\varphi) = \{\Box\varphi\} \cup \mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$.
nodes.title: Subformulas

nodes.summary: If $\psi$ is a subformula of a modal formula $\varphi$, then every subformula of $\psi$ is a subformula of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The subformula relation is transitive

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be a nonempty finite set of finite sets of formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of finite sets of formulas. The Kripke model on $U$ with relation $R$ has the elements of $U$ as worlds, a world $s$ sees a world $t$ iff $(s, t) \in R$, and an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff $p \in s$.
nodes.title: Finite Kripke model on sets of formulas

nodes.summary: Given a finite set $U$ of finite sets of formulas, a finite set $R$ of pairs of such sets and a finite set $s$ of formulas, the Boolean value of a formula at $s$ is defined by recursion on the formula: an atom $p$ is true iff $p \in s$; $\bot$ is false; $\varphi \to \psi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is false or $\psi$ is true at $s$; and $\Box\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is true at every $t \in U$ with $(s, t) \in R$.
nodes.title: Boolean evaluation in a finite model

nodes.summary: Given a Kripke model $M$ and a modal formula $\varphi$, the type (or $\Sigma$-type, for $\Sigma$ the set of subformulas of $\varphi$) of a world $w$ of $M$ is the finite set of subformulas of $\varphi$ that hold at $w$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Type of a world

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula. The worlds of the filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$ form the finite set of types occurring in $M$: the subsets $s$ of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$ such that $s$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at some world of $M$.
nodes.title: Worlds of the filtration

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. The smallest filtration relation is the finite set of pairs $(s, t)$ of types such that there are worlds $w$ and $w'$ of $M$ of types $s$ and $t$ with $w'$ accessible from $w$.
nodes.title: Smallest filtration relation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. Every world $s$ of the filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$, that is, every element of the finite set of types occurring in $M$, is the type of some world of $M$.
nodes.title: Filtration worlds are realized types

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. If two worlds $w$ and $v$ of $M$ have the same type, then every subformula $\psi$ of $\varphi$ holds at $w$ iff it holds at $v$.
nodes.title: Worlds of the same type agree on subformulas

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a modal formula, $\Sigma$ the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, and for a world $w$ let $[w]$, the type of $w$, be the set of formulas of $\Sigma$ true at $w$ in $M$. A relation $R$ on finite sets of formulas is a filtration of $M$ through $\Sigma$ when (min) for all worlds $w, v$ related in $M$, the pair $([w], [v])$ is in $R$, and (max) for all worlds $w, v$ with…
nodes.title: Filtration relations

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a modal formula, and for a world $w$ let $[w]$, the type of $w$, be the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at $w$ in $M$. Let $R$ be a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$, and let $M^R$ be the Kripke model whose worlds are the types of the worlds of $M$, with accessibility relation $R$ and an atom true at a type iff the type contains it. Then for every…
nodes.title: Filtration lemma

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at a world $w$ the type of $w$. The relation that relates two types when some worlds of those types are related in $M$ is a filtration of $M$ through the set of subformulas of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The smallest filtration is a filtration

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a modal formula, and call the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world $w$ of $M$ the type of $w$. The filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$ is the Kripke model whose worlds are the types occurring in $M$, in which a type $s$ sees a type $t$ iff some world of type $s$ sees some world of type $t$ in $M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff…
nodes.title: Smallest filtration of a Kripke model

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a modal formula, and for a world $w$ let $[w]$, the type of $w$, be the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at $w$ in $M$. For every subformula $\psi$ of $\varphi$ and every world $w$ of $M$, $\psi$ holds at $[w]$ in the smallest filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$ iff $\psi$ holds at $w$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Filtration lemma for the smallest filtration

nodes.summary: A modal formula that is not a theorem of K fails at some world of some Kripke model.
nodes.title: Completeness of K, countermodel form

nodes.summary: A formula that is not a K-theorem fails in a Kripke model with at most `2 ^ |sub φ|` worlds.
nodes.title: Finite model property of K

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ passes the finite check when, for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$, every relation $R \subseteq U \times U$ and every $s \in U$, the formula $\varphi$ is true at $s$ in the Kripke model with set of worlds $U$, accessibility relation $R$, and an atom $p$ true at a world $t$ iff $p \in t$; truth is computed by recursion on…
nodes.title: Finite validity check for K

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K iff it passes the following finite check: for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$, every relation $R \subseteq U \times U$ and every $s \in U$, $\varphi$ evaluates to true at $s$ in the finite Kripke model on $U$ with relation $R$ in which an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff $p \in s$.
nodes.title: Finite-check criterion for K-theorems

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K iff for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of the set $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ of subformulas of $\varphi$ and every finite set $R$ of pairs of finite sets of formulas, $\varphi$ holds at every world of the Kripke model whose worlds are the elements of $U$, in which $s$ sees $t$ iff $(s, t) \in R$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $s$ iff $p \in s$.
nodes.title: K-theorems via finite models on sets of subformulas

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\varphi$ a formula and $R$ a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$. If $\varphi$ fails at some world of $M$, then $\varphi$ is not valid in the finite model whose worlds are the types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world), with relation $R$ and an atom true at a type iff it belongs to it.
nodes.title: A filtration refutes what the model refutes

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a formula, and let $U_\varphi$ be the set of types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world). The Lemmon relation is the relation $R$ on $U_\varphi$ such that $s \mathrel{R} t$ iff for every formula $\psi$ with $\Box\psi$ a subformula of $\varphi$, $\Box\psi \in s$ implies $\Box\psi \in t$ and $\psi \in t$.
nodes.title: Lemmon filtration relation

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and $\varphi$ a formula, and let $U_\varphi$ be the set of types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world). The S5 relation is the relation $R$ on $U_\varphi$ such that $s \mathrel{R} t$ iff for every formula $\psi$ with $\Box\psi$ a subformula of $\varphi$, $\Box\psi \in s$ iff $\Box\psi \in t$.
nodes.title: S5 filtration relation

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ with a transitive accessibility relation and every formula $\varphi$, the Lemmon relation of $M$ and $\varphi$ is a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The Lemmon relation is a filtration of a transitive model

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and every formula $\varphi$, the S5 relation of $M$ and $\varphi$ is a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The S5 relation is a filtration of an equivalence model

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be a finite set of finite sets of modal formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of such sets. Then $R$ is reflexive on $U$ when $(s, s) \in R$ for every $s \in U$.
nodes.title: Reflexivity on a finite set of worlds

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be a finite set of finite sets of modal formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of such sets. Then $R$ is transitive on $U$ when $(s, r) \in R$ for all $s, t, r \in U$ with $(s, t) \in R$ and $(t, r) \in R$.
nodes.title: Transitivity on a finite set of worlds

nodes.summary: Let $U$ be a finite set of finite sets of modal formulas and $R$ a finite set of pairs of such sets. Then $R$ is symmetric on $U$ when $(t, s) \in R$ for all $s, t \in U$ with $(s, t) \in R$.
nodes.title: Symmetry on a finite set of worlds

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive, let $\varphi$ be a modal formula, and let $R$ be a filtration of $M$ through the subformulas of $\varphi$. Then $(s, s) \in R$ for every set $s$ that is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$ true at some world of $M$.
nodes.title: Filtrations of reflexive models are reflexive

nodes.summary: If a modal formula $\varphi$ is not a theorem of T, then there is a Kripke model with finitely many worlds, at most $2^{|\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)|}$ of them, where $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, whose accessibility relation is reflexive and in which $\varphi$ is false at some world.
nodes.title: Finite model property of T

nodes.summary: If a modal formula $\varphi$ is not a theorem of S4, then there is a Kripke model with finitely many worlds, at most $2^{|\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)|}$ of them, where $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive and in which $\varphi$ is false at some world.
nodes.title: Finite model property of S4

nodes.summary: If a modal formula $\varphi$ is not a theorem of S5, then there is a Kripke model with finitely many worlds, at most $2^{|\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)|}$ of them, where $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$ is the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and in which $\varphi$ is false at some world.
nodes.title: Finite model property of S5

Let $M$ be a Kripke model, let $U_\varphi$ be the set of types of worlds of $M$ (the sets of subformulas of $\varphi$ satisfied at a world), and let $R \subseteq U_\varphi \times U_\varphi$ satisfy $C(U_\varphi, R)$. Then…
nodes.title: The finite check covers the filtration worlds

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of T if and only if, for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$, the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, and every relation $R \subseteq U \times U$ that is reflexive on $U$, the formula $\varphi$ is true at every world $s \in U$ of the finite model with worlds $U$, accessibility relation $R$, and each atom true at $s$ exactly when it belongs to $s$.
nodes.title: T-provability via finite reflexive models

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S4 if and only if, for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$, the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, and every relation $R \subseteq U \times U$ that is reflexive and transitive on $U$, the formula $\varphi$ is true at every world $s \in U$ of the finite model with worlds $U$, accessibility relation $R$, and each atom true at $s$ exactly when it belongs…
nodes.title: S4-provability via finite reflexive transitive models

nodes.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S5 if and only if, for every nonempty set $U$ of subsets of $\mathrm{sub}(\varphi)$, the set of subformulas of $\varphi$, and every relation $R \subseteq U \times U$ that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive on $U$, the formula $\varphi$ is true at every world $s \in U$ of the finite model with worlds $U$, accessibility relation $R$, and each atom true at $s$ exactly when…

Standard translation of modal logic

nodes.summary: Relation symbols of the modal first-order language: accessibility `R` (binary) and a unary predicate `P_a` for each atom `a`.
nodes.title: Relation symbols of the modal first-order language

nodes.summary: For a set of atoms, the first-order language of modal logic has no function symbols; its relation symbols are a binary symbol $R$ (accessibility) and a unary symbol $P_a$ for each atom $a$.
nodes.title: The first-order modal language

nodes.summary: The relation symbols of the first-order frame language, indexed by arity: a single binary symbol $R$ for accessibility, and no symbols of any other arity.
nodes.title: Relation symbols of the frame language

nodes.summary: The first-order language of frames: no function symbols, one binary relation `R`.
nodes.title: First-order language of Kripke frames

nodes.summary: A Kripke model $M$ with set of worlds $W$ makes $W$ a structure for the modal language: the accessibility symbol $R$ is interpreted as the accessibility relation of $M$, and the predicate $P_a$ for an atom $a$ holds at exactly the worlds where $a$ is true under the valuation of $M$.
nodes.title: A Kripke model as a first-order structure

nodes.summary: A binary relation $r$ on a set $W$ (a bare Kripke frame) makes $W$ a structure for the frame language, in which the accessibility symbol $R$ is interpreted as $r$: $R(w, w')$ holds if and only if $r(w, w')$.
nodes.title: A frame as a first-order structure

nodes.title: Standard translation

nodes.title: Bisimulation-invariant formulas

nodes.title: Modal formulas are bisimulation-invariant under the standard translation

nodes.summary: Classical propositional logic: truth-table semantics, natural deduction and its completeness, functional completeness, normal forms and CNF transformations, resolution, interpolation, SAT-solving procedures (Davis–Putnam, DPLL, 2-SAT, Horn-SAT) and binary decision diagrams.
nodes.title: Propositional logic and satisfiability
Propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Given a Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms, the truth value of a proposition is computed recursively: an atom $x$ has value $v(x)$, $A \wedge B$ is true iff both $A$ and $B$ are, $A \vee B$ is true iff at least one of them is, and $A \to B$ is true iff $A$ is false or $B$ is true. Falsum $\bot$, when present, is itself an atom, so its value $v(\bot)$ is part of the valuation and need not be false.
nodes.title: Truth-table evaluation

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then for every proposition $A$, the truth-table value under $v$ of $\neg A$, defined as $A \to \bot$, is the Boolean negation of the truth-table value of $A$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Truth value of a negation

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory (a set of propositions), $\Gamma$ a context (a finite set of propositions) and $A$ a proposition. Then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of $\Gamma$ in $T$ when every Boolean valuation of the atoms under which all members of $T$ and all members of $\Gamma$ evaluate to true also makes $A$ evaluate to true.
nodes.title: Truth-table consequence

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, $\Gamma$ a context and $A$ a proposition. For every natural-deduction derivation of $\Gamma \vdash A$ with axioms from $T$, every Boolean valuation of the atoms that makes all members of $T$ and of $\Gamma$ true makes $A$ true.
nodes.title: Soundness of natural deduction for truth tables

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, $\Gamma$ a context and $A$ a proposition. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in natural deduction with axioms from $T$, then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of $\Gamma$ in $T$: every Boolean valuation of the atoms that makes all members of $T$ and of $\Gamma$ true makes $A$ true.
nodes.title: Truth-table soundness of derivability

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then every instance $\bot \to B$ of ex falso, that is every axiom of intuitionistic propositional logic, is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Ex falso is true when falsum is false

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then every instance $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination, that is every axiom of classical propositional logic, is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Double-negation elimination is true when falsum is false

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in classical propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination) and every member of $\Gamma$ is true under $v$, then $A$ is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Classical derivability implies truth under valuations with false falsum

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. If the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in intuitionistic propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\bot \to B$ of ex falso) and every member of $\Gamma$ is true under $v$, then $A$ is true under $v$.
nodes.title: Intuitionistic derivability implies truth under valuations with false falsum

nodes.title: Consistency of classical propositional logic

nodes.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$. For every atom $x$, including $\bot$, the proposition $x$ is not derivable from the empty context in classical propositional logic (natural deduction whose axioms are all instances $\neg\neg B \to B$ of double-negation elimination).
nodes.title: Classical logic proves no atom

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of propositions is satisfiable when some Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ makes every member of $S$ true.
nodes.title: Satisfiable sets of propositions

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, that is, a set of propositions. A set $S$ of propositions is consistent relative to $T$ when there is no finite set $\Gamma \subseteq S$ such that the sequent $\Gamma \vdash \bot$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$.
nodes.title: Consistency relative to a theory

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory. Every set $S$ of propositions that is consistent relative to $T$ is contained in a set $M$ that is consistent relative to $T$ and not properly contained in any other set consistent relative to $T$.
nodes.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. If a proposition $A$ is not in $M$, then there is a finite set $\Gamma \subseteq M$ such that the sequent $\Gamma \cup \{A\} \vdash \bot$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$.
nodes.title: Propositions outside a maximal consistent set are refuted by it

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. If $\Gamma$ is a finite subset of $M$ and the sequent $\Gamma \vdash A$ is derivable in natural deduction from $T$, then $A \in M$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets are deductively closed in propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. Then every proposition of $T$ belongs to $M$, that is, $T \subseteq M$.
nodes.title: A maximal consistent set contains its theory

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory and $M$ a maximal set of propositions consistent relative to $T$. Then for every proposition $A$, either $A \in M$ or $\neg A \in M$, where $\neg A$ is the proposition $A \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Each proposition or its negation lies in a maximal consistent set

Let $M$ be a set of propositions that is consistent relative to $T$ and not properly contained in any other set consistent relative to $T$, and let $v_M$ be the valuation that makes an atom $x$ true exactly when the atomic proposition $x$ belongs to $M$. Then a proposition $A$ evaluates to true under $v_M$ iff…
nodes.title: Truth lemma for propositional natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be an intuitionistic theory, that is, one that derives $\bot \to B$ for every proposition $B$. If a set $S$ of propositions is consistent relative to $T$, then $T \cup S$ is satisfiable: some Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$ makes every member of $T$ and every member of $S$ true.
