nodes.title: Compactness
Binary decision diagrams
Reduced ordered binary decision diagrams: canonicity and apply

nodes.summary: A binary decision diagram, in tree form, is either a leaf carrying a Boolean value, or a node consisting of a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and two diagrams: the low child, for $v$ false, and the high child, for $v$ true.
nodes.title: Binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: Under an assignment $\sigma$ of a Boolean value to each variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$, the value of a leaf is its Boolean value, and the value of a node testing $v$ is the value of its high child if $\sigma(v)$ is true and the value of its low child if $\sigma(v)$ is false.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: The size of a diagram is its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form: a leaf has size $1$, and a node with children $\ell$ and $h$ has size one more than the sum of the sizes of $\ell$ and $h$.
nodes.title: Size of a diagram

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a diagram is ordered from $n$ when every variable it tests is at least $n$ and the tested variables strictly increase along every path. Recursively: every leaf is ordered from $n$, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is ordered from $n$ when $n \le v$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are ordered from $v + 1$.
nodes.title: Diagrams ordered from a variable

nodes.summary: A diagram is reduced when no node in it has two equal children: every leaf is reduced, and the node testing $v$ with children $\ell$ and $h$ is reduced when $\ell \ne h$ and both $\ell$ and $h$ are reduced.
nodes.title: Reduced diagrams

nodes.summary: A binary decision diagram is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram (ROBDD), for the natural order on variables, when it is ordered from $0$ (the tested variables strictly increase along every path) and reduced (no node has two equal children).
nodes.title: Reduced ordered binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram ordered from $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $v < n$ be a variable. For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) equals the value of $t$ under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Independence from variables below the order

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a node testing the variable $v$ with low child $\ell$ and high child $h$, and suppose $t$ is ordered from some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables and every Boolean $b$, the value of $t$ under $\sigma[v \mapsto b]$ (the assignment $\sigma$ with $v$ set to $b$) is the value of $h$ under $\sigma$ if $b$ is true, and the value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ if $b$…
nodes.title: Fixing the top variable of an ordered node

nodes.summary: For every binary decision diagram $t$, the size of $t$ (its number of leaves and nodes, counted in tree form) is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Binary decision diagrams have positive size

nodes.summary: Canonicity (Bryant): two reduced ordered diagrams with the same function are equal.
nodes.title: Canonicity

nodes.summary: If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are reduced ordered binary decision diagrams, then $t_1 = t_2$ if and only if $t_1$ and $t_2$ have the same value under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.
nodes.title: Reduced ordered diagrams are equal iff they have the same values

nodes.summary: A reduced ordered binary decision diagram $t$ is the leaf with value false if and only if $t$ has value false under every assignment of Boolean values to the variables.
nodes.title: Unsatisfiable reduced ordered diagrams

nodes.summary: For a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and diagrams $\ell$ and $h$, the diagram $\mathrm{mk}(v, \ell, h)$ is $\ell$ if $\ell = h$, and otherwise the node that tests $v$ with $\ell$ as its false-child and $h$ as its true-child.
nodes.title: Node constructor removing a redundant test

If $t_1$ and $t_2$ are leaves with values $a$ and $b$, it is the leaf with value $\mathrm{op}(a, b)$. nodes.title: Bryant's apply operation

nodes.summary: For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$, all binary decision diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the variables, the value under $\sigma$ of the diagram $\mathrm{apply}(\mathrm{op}, t_1, t_2)$ obtained from $t_1$ and $t_2$ by Bryant's apply operation under $\mathrm{op}$ is $\mathrm{op}(a_1, a_2)$, where $a_i$ is the value of $t_i$ under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Apply computes the operation pointwise

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{op}$ be a binary Boolean operation and $n$ a natural number. If the diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$ are both ordered from $n$, then the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is ordered from $n$.
nodes.title: Apply preserves orderedness

nodes.summary: For every binary Boolean operation $\mathrm{op}$ and all diagrams $t_1$ and $t_2$, the result of apply with $\mathrm{op}$ on $t_1$ and $t_2$ is reduced.
nodes.title: Apply returns reduced diagrams

nodes.summary: Each proposition $A$ whose atoms are natural numbers is sent to a binary decision diagram by recursion on $A$: an atom $x$ goes to the node testing $x$ with the leaf false as its false-child and the leaf true as its true-child, and a conjunction $A \wedge B$, disjunction $A \vee B$ or implication $A \to B$ goes to the result of apply on the diagrams of $A$ and $B$ under the Boolean operation and, or, or…
nodes.title: Diagram of a proposition

nodes.summary: For propositions $A$ and $B$ over natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagrams of $A$ and $B$ are equal if and only if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value under every valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$.
nodes.title: Equal BDDs iff equal truth tables

nodes.summary: For a proposition $A$ over natural-number atoms, the binary decision diagram of $A$ is not the leaf false if and only if some valuation $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ makes $A$ true.
nodes.title: Satisfiable iff the BDD is not the false leaf
Counting satisfying assignments of a BDD

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, a diagram has its variables below $m$ when every variable tested at a node of the diagram is less than $m$.
nodes.title: Variables below a bound

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$ and a diagram $t$, the satisfy-count $c_m(n, t)$ of $t$ from $n$ with bound $m$ is defined by recursion on $t$: a leaf $\mathrm{true}$ gives $2^{m - n}$, a leaf $\mathrm{false}$ gives $0$, and a node testing the variable $v$ with child $t_0$ for false and child $t_1$ for true gives $2^{v - n} (c_m(v + 1, t_0) + c_m(v + 1, t_1))$. nodes.summary: For every binary decision diagram $t$, every variable $x$ and every Boolean $b$, the cofactor $t[x := b]$ is reduced: no node has two equal children.
nodes.title: Restriction yields a reduced diagram

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary decision diagram (tested variables strictly increase along every path), then for every variable $x$ and every Boolean $b$ the cofactor $t[x := b]$ is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram.
nodes.title: Restriction yields an ROBDD

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a binary decision diagram $t$, the existential quantification of $t$ over $x$ is the diagram obtained by combining the cofactors $t[x := \mathrm{false}]$ and $t[x := \mathrm{true}]$ with Bryant's apply under disjunction.
nodes.title: Existential quantification of a diagram

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a binary decision diagram $t$, the universal quantification of $t$ over $x$ is the diagram obtained by combining the cofactors $t[x := \mathrm{false}]$ and $t[x := \mathrm{true}]$ with Bryant's apply under conjunction.
nodes.title: Universal quantification of a diagram

nodes.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary decision diagram (tested variables strictly increase along every path), then for every variable $x$ the existential quantification of $t$ over $x$ is a reduced ordered binary decision diagram.
nodes.title: Existential quantification yields an ROBDD

nodes.summary: The satisfying path of a diagram is found by a depth-first search for a leaf $\mathrm{true}$ that tries the $\mathrm{hi}$ (true) child of each node before its $\mathrm{lo}$ (false) child. It is returned as the list of pairs $(v, c)$ of the variables $v$ tested along the path with the branches $c$ taken (empty at a leaf $\mathrm{true}$), and the search returns nothing when the diagram has no leaf $\mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Satisfying path of a binary decision diagram

nodes.summary: For a path $p$, given as a list of pairs $(v, b)$ of a variable $v \in \mathbb{N}$ and a Boolean $b$, the assignment read off $p$ sends a variable $x$ to the Boolean of the first pair in $p$ whose variable is $x$, and to $\mathrm{false}$ if $x$ occurs in no pair of $p$.
nodes.title: Assignment read off a path

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a binary decision diagram ordered from some $n$ (every tested variable is at least $n$, and tested variables strictly increase along every path). If the satisfying-path search on $t$ returns a path $p$, then $t$ evaluates to true under the assignment read off $p$.
nodes.title: The path assignment satisfies an ordered diagram

nodes.summary: If a binary decision diagram $t$ is reduced and is not the leaf $\mathrm{false}$, then the search for a satisfying path in $t$ succeeds: it returns a path from the root of $t$ to a leaf $\mathrm{true}$.
nodes.title: Reduced diagrams other than false have a satisfying path

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a proposition over atoms indexed by natural numbers, let $t$ be its ROBDD, and let $f$ be a natural number. Then $A$ evaluates to true under some valuation $\sigma$ with $\sigma(f) = \mathrm{false}$ if and only if the cofactor $t[f := \mathrm{false}]$ is not the leaf $\mathrm{false}$.
nodes.title: Satisfiability with one variable fixed to false

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a proposition over natural-number atoms and let $f$ be a natural number. If some assignment $\sigma$ with $\sigma(f) = \mathrm{false}$ satisfies $A$, then the search for a satisfying path in the restriction at $f := \mathrm{false}$ of the ROBDD of $A$ returns a path $p$, and the assignment read off $p$ (the recorded value on each variable of $p$, false elsewhere), changed to send $f$ to $\mathrm{false}$,…
nodes.title: Satisfy-one with a variable fixed to false

nodes.summary: Every proposition $A$ over atoms indexed by natural numbers, built from atoms with $\land$, $\lor$ and $\to$ only, evaluates to true under the valuation that makes every atom true.
nodes.title: The all-true valuation satisfies every proposition

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ over atoms indexed by natural numbers, the satisfying-path search on the ROBDD of $A$ returns a path $p$, and $A$ evaluates to true under the assignment read off $p$.
nodes.title: Satisfy-one for propositions
Conjunctive normal form

nodes.summary: A CNF clause is a finite list of literals, each a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$.
nodes.title: CNF clause

nodes.summary: A CNF formula is a finite list of CNF clauses, read as the conjunction of its clauses.
nodes.title: CNF formula

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable when there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that every clause $C$ of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Satisfiability of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a literal $(x, b)$, with variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, when $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a literal

nodes.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF clause $C$ when at least one literal of $C$ is satisfied by $v$, that is, $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a clause

nodes.summary: An assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ satisfies a CNF formula $\varphi$ when $v$ satisfies every clause of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if there is an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfiability means having a satisfying assignment

nodes.summary: For CNFs $\varphi = C_1 \land \dots \land C_m$ and $\psi = D_1 \land \dots \land D_n$, their disjunction is the CNF with one clause $C_i \lor D_j$ (the literals of $C_i$ followed by those of $D_j$) for each pair $(i, j)$, listed with $i$ as the outer and $j$ as the inner index. It expresses $(\bigwedge_i C_i) \lor (\bigwedge_j D_j)$ as $\bigwedge_{i,j} (C_i \lor D_j)$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of two CNFs

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal $(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF $\mathcal{A}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the disjoining builder $\mathcal{O}_p$. For an atom $a$, $\mathcal{A}_p(a, S)$ is the unit clause…
nodes.title: Accumulating CNF builder

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers, read a literal $(n, p)$ as variable $n$ with polarity $p$, and write $1$ and $0$ for the polarities true and false. For a polarity $p$, a proposition $\varphi$ and a CNF $S$, the CNF $\mathcal{O}_p(\varphi, S)$ is defined by recursion on $\varphi$, together with the accumulating CNF builder $\mathcal{A}_p$. Write $X \otimes S$ for the disjunction of two CNFs $X$ and…
nodes.title: Disjoining CNF builder

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For a polarity $p$ and a proposition $\varphi$, the CNF of $\varphi$ at polarity $p$ is the result of the accumulating CNF builder at polarity $p$ on $\varphi$ with the empty CNF as accumulator; the atom $a$ becomes the variable $\iota(a)$.
nodes.title: CNF of a proposition at a polarity

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity true, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.
nodes.title: CNF of a proposition

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. The complement CNF of a proposition $A$ is its CNF at polarity false, with the atom $a$ as the variable $\iota(a)$.
nodes.title: CNF of the complement of a proposition

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ number the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$ and every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables, the CNF of $A$ built with atom $a$ as variable $\iota(a)$ is satisfied by $\sigma$ if and only if $A$ evaluates to true under the valuation $\sigma \circ \iota$ of the atoms.
nodes.title: Equivalent CNF

nodes.summary: Let the atoms have a distinguished atom $\bot$ and let $\iota$ be an injective numbering of the atoms by natural numbers. For every proposition $A$, the CNF consisting of the unit clause with the single negative literal on variable $\iota(\bot)$ followed by the clauses of the CNF of $A$ (atom $a$ read as variable $\iota(a)$) is satisfiable if and only if some valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false makes…
nodes.title: Satisfiability of a CNF with falsum false

nodes.summary: The variables of a CNF clause $C$ form the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that $C$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.
nodes.title: Variables of a clause

nodes.summary: Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction of a clause by $\ell$ is the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity, keeping the other literals in order.
nodes.title: Restriction of a clause by a literal

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a clause, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal that does not occur in $C$, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the restriction of $C$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $C$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a restricted clause

nodes.summary: The variables of a CNF formula $\varphi$ form the union of the sets of variables of its clauses, that is, the finite set of natural numbers $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, b)$ for some polarity $b$.
nodes.title: Variables of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: Given a literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the restriction of a CNF formula $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is obtained by deleting every clause of $\varphi$ that contains $\ell$ and replacing every other clause by its restriction by $\ell$, the clause obtained by deleting every literal whose variable is $x$, of either polarity; the remaining clauses keep their order.
nodes.title: Restriction of a CNF formula by a literal

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ and every literal $\ell$, every variable of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ is a variable of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Restriction does not add variables

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $F$ and every literal $\ell = (x, b)$, the variable $x$ does not occur in the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$.
nodes.title: The restricted variable no longer occurs

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $(x, b)$ a literal. If $x$ is a variable of $\varphi$, then the set of variables of the restriction of $\varphi$ by $(x, b)$ is a proper subset of the set of variables of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Restricting by an occurring variable shrinks the variable set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal whose variable $x$ occurs in $F$. Then the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$ has strictly fewer distinct variables than $F$.
nodes.title: Restriction reduces the number of variables

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal, and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables with $v(x) = b$. Then $v$ satisfies the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if $v$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a restricted CNF formula

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula and let $v_1, v_2$ be assignments of Booleans to variables with $v_1(x) = v_2(x)$ for every variable $x$ occurring in $F$. If $v_1$ satisfies $F$, then $v_2$ satisfies $F$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula, $\ell = (x, b)$ a literal and $v$ an assignment of Booleans to variables. If $v$ satisfies the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$, then the assignment that agrees with $v$ except that it sends $x$ to $b$ satisfies $F$.
nodes.title: Lifting a satisfying assignment from a restriction

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $F$ and every variable $x$, the formula $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is satisfiable or the restriction of $F$ by the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Splitting on a variable

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a CNF formula that contains the unit clause whose only literal is $\ell$. Then $F$ is satisfiable if and only if the restriction of $F$ by $\ell$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Unit propagation preserves satisfiability
Craig interpolation

nodes.summary: The atoms of a proposition $A$ form the finite set of atoms occurring in $A$: an atom $x$ has the single atom $x$, and the atoms of $B \wedge C$, $B \vee C$ and $B \to C$ are the atoms of $B$ together with the atoms of $C$.
nodes.title: Atoms of a proposition

nodes.summary: If two Boolean valuations $v$ and $w$ agree on every atom of a proposition $A$, then $A$ has the same truth-table value under $v$ as under $w$.
nodes.title: The truth value depends only on the atoms

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$, a Boolean $b$ and a proposition $A$, the proposition $A[p := b]$ is obtained from $A$ by replacing every occurrence of the atom $p$ by the constant $\top$, written $\bot \to \bot$, if $b$ is true, and by $\bot$ if $b$ is false.
nodes.title: Substituting a truth value for an atom

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$ and a proposition $A$, the Boolean quantification $\exists p.\, A$ is the disjunction $A[p := \top] \vee A[p := \bot]$, where $A[p := \top]$ and $A[p := \bot]$ replace the atom $p$ in $A$ by the constant $\top = (\bot \to \bot)$ and by $\bot$ respectively.
nodes.title: Boolean quantification over an atom

nodes.summary: For a list of atoms $p_1, \dots, p_n$ and a proposition $A$, the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is $\exists p_1.\, \exists p_2.\, \cdots \exists p_n.\, A$: $A$ is quantified over $p_n$ first and over $p_1$ last, and for the empty list the result is $A$ itself.
nodes.title: Boolean quantification over a list of atoms

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be a list of atoms that does not contain $\bot$, let $A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation with $v(\bot)$ false. Then the iterated Boolean quantification $\exists p_1 \cdots p_n.\, A$ is true under $v$ if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation $w$ that agrees with $v$ on every atom not in the list.
nodes.title: Truth of a Boolean quantification over a list of atoms

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that every Boolean valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true also makes $B$ true. Then there is a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $A$ true makes $I$ true, and every valuation $v$ with $v(\bot)$ false that makes $I$ true makes $B$ true.
nodes.title: Craig interpolation, semantic form

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be propositions such that $A \to B$ is derivable without assumptions in classical propositional logic $\mathrm{CPL}$ (natural deduction with the axioms $\neg\neg C \to C$). Then there is a proposition $I$ whose atoms all lie among the atoms common to $A$ and $B$ together with $\bot$, such that $A \to I$ and $I \to B$ are both derivable without assumptions in $\mathrm{CPL}$.
nodes.title: Craig interpolation for classical natural deduction
DPLL algorithm
A deterministic DPLL solver

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns the literal $\ell$ of the first clause of $\varphi$ that consists of the single literal $\ell$, and returns nothing when no clause of $\varphi$ has exactly one literal.
nodes.title: First unit literal

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, read as a list of clauses, this returns the variable of the first literal of the first nonempty clause of $\varphi$, that is, the first variable occurring in $\varphi$ in source order, and returns nothing when every clause of $\varphi$ is empty (in particular when $\varphi$ has no clauses).
nodes.title: First variable of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: For an assignment $v$ of Boolean values to the variables $0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and a clause $C$, whose literals are pairs $(x, b)$ of a variable $x$ and a polarity $b$, this Boolean is true exactly when some literal $(x, b)$ of $C$ satisfies $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Boolean clause satisfaction check

nodes.summary: For an assignment $v$ of Boolean values to the variables $0, 1, 2, \ldots$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, this Boolean is true exactly when every clause of $\varphi$ passes the Boolean clause satisfaction check for $v$, that is, every clause contains a literal $(x, b)$ with $v(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Boolean formula satisfaction check

nodes.summary: Given a natural number $n$ (the fuel) and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the procedure returns a Boolean value. Literals are pairs $(x, b)$ of a variable $x$ and a polarity $b$. With fuel $0$ the procedure returns true exactly when $\varphi$ has no clauses. With fuel $n + 1$ it returns true if $\varphi$ has no clauses, and otherwise returns false if some clause of $\varphi$ is empty. Otherwise, if some clause of…
nodes.title: DPLL with a fuel budget

nodes.summary: On a CNF formula $\varphi$, the DPLL procedure runs DPLL with fuel equal to the number of distinct variables occurring in $\varphi$ and returns its Boolean result.
nodes.title: The DPLL procedure
Correctness of the DPLL solver

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $n$ be a natural number at least the number of distinct variables occurring in $\varphi$. Then DPLL with fuel $n$ returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of DPLL with sufficient fuel

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the DPLL procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of DPLL
Functional completeness

nodes.summary: Let $f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms. The Shannon expansion $S(\ell, f)$ of $f$ over a list $\ell$ of atoms is defined by recursion on $\ell$. For the empty list it is $\bot \to \bot$ if $f$ is true at the valuation that makes every atom false, and $\bot$ otherwise. For the list $x \cdot \ell$ with head $x$ and tail $\ell$,
nodes.title: Shannon expansion

nodes.summary: Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be a list of atoms and let $f$ assign a truth value to every valuation of the atoms, such that $f(v) = f(w)$ whenever $v$ and $w$ agree on $x_1, \dots, x_n$. Then for every valuation $v$ that makes $\bot$ false, the Shannon expansion of $f$ over $x_1, \dots, x_n$ has truth value $f(v)$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Shannon expansion

nodes.summary: Every Boolean function of the atoms in a finite list is the truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of some proposition.
nodes.title: Functional completeness

reading_title.source: Propositions built from $\to$ and $\bot$

nodes.summary: A proposition is built from $\to$ and $\bot$ when it contains no conjunction and no disjunction: every atom (including $\bot$, which is an atom) is, and $A \to B$ is exactly when both $A$ and $B$ are.
nodes.title: Propositions built from $\to$ and $\bot$

reading_title.source: Translation into $\to$ and $\bot$

nodes.summary: The translation $A^*$ of a proposition $A$ is defined by recursion on $A$: each atom is unchanged, $(A \to B)^* = A^* \to B^*$, $(A \wedge B)^* = (A^* \to (B^* \to \bot)) \to \bot$ and $(A \vee B)^* = (A^* \to \bot) \to B^*$.
nodes.title: Translation into $\to$ and $\bot$

reading_title.source: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves truth values

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ and every valuation $v$ that makes $\bot$ false, the translation of $A$ into $\to$ and $\bot$ has the same truth value under $v$ as $A$.
nodes.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves truth values

nodes.summary: Every Boolean function of the atoms in a finite list is the truth table, on valuations with `⊥` false, of a proposition built with `→` alone.
nodes.title: Functional completeness of `→` and `⊥`

reading_title.source: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves and reflects classical derivability

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$, let $A^*$ be its translation into $\to$ and $\bot$, which keeps atoms and implications and recursively replaces each $B \wedge C$ by $(B \to (C \to \bot)) \to \bot$ and each $B \vee C$ by $(B \to \bot) \to C$. Then $A^*$ is derivable from no hypotheses in classical propositional logic if and only if $A$ is.
nodes.title: The translation into $\to$ and $\bot$ preserves and reflects classical derivability
Horn satisfiability

nodes.summary: A CNF formula is a Horn formula when every clause contains at most one distinct positive literal.
nodes.title: Horn formula

nodes.summary: For a finite set $T$ of variables and a CNF clause $C$, this Boolean test is true exactly when every negative literal of $C$ has its variable in $T$.
nodes.title: Body of a clause contained in a set

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables, the derived set consists of the variables $x$ such that some clause of $\varphi$ contains the positive literal $x$ and has every one of its negative literals on a variable in $T$.
nodes.title: Forward-chaining step

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a finite set $T$ of variables, the closure of $T$ is computed by iterating the forward-chaining step of $\varphi$: if every variable derived from $T$ already lies in $T$, the closure is $T$; otherwise it is the closure of the union of $T$ with the derived variables.
nodes.title: Forward-chaining closure

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the least model candidate is the assignment that makes a variable true exactly when it lies in the forward-chaining closure of the empty set under $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Least model candidate

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a Horn CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment satisfying $\varphi$. Every variable that the least model candidate of $\varphi$ makes true is also true under $\sigma$.
nodes.title: On Horn formulas, the least model candidate lies below every model

nodes.summary: A Horn CNF formula $\varphi$ is satisfiable if and only if its least model candidate satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Horn satisfiability via the least model

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the Horn satisfiability test returns the Boolean truth value of $\varphi$ under its least model candidate.
nodes.title: Horn satisfiability test

nodes.summary: If $\varphi$ is a Horn CNF formula, then the Horn satisfiability test returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Horn satisfiability test
Model-count-preserving CNF transformations

nodes.summary: The number of Boolean assignments to the variables occurring in a formula that satisfy it.
nodes.title: Model count of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: Rename every occurring variable by its position in the last-occurrence list.
nodes.title: Exact variable compaction of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: Compaction preserves the number of clauses.
nodes.title: Compaction preserves the number of clauses

nodes.summary: Compaction preserves every clause length, in the original clause order.
nodes.title: Compaction preserves clause lengths

nodes.summary: Compaction preserves every upper bound on clause length.
nodes.title: Compaction preserves clause-length bounds

nodes.summary: Compaction preserves the absence of duplicate clauses.
nodes.title: Compaction preserves absence of duplicate clauses

nodes.summary: The variables of a compacted formula are exactly its dense initial range.
nodes.title: Variables of a compacted formula form an initial range

nodes.summary: Satisfaction after compaction is satisfaction before compaction with names translated by their exact last-occurrence positions.
nodes.title: Satisfaction is preserved by variable compaction

nodes.summary: Exact variable compaction preserves the number of assignments to the occurring variables.
nodes.title: Variable compaction preserves the model count

nodes.summary: If every occurring name is below `N`, the count over all `Fin N` assignments is the support count times one Boolean choice for each unused ambient variable.
nodes.title: Counting satisfying assignments over a larger variable range

nodes.summary: The number of fresh variables used by the parsimonious width-three reduction.
nodes.title: Number of fresh variables in the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction

nodes.summary: Reduce a CNF to clauses of length at most three, allocating fresh variables consecutively from `start`. Repeated output clauses are removed in last-occurrence order.
nodes.title: Parsimonious reduction of CNF to 3-CNF

nodes.summary: Satisfaction of the reduced formula implies satisfaction of the original formula under the same values of the original variable names.
nodes.title: Soundness of the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction

nodes.summary: Every output clause has length at most three, and duplicate clauses have been removed.
nodes.title: The parsimonious reduction outputs a duplicate-free 3-CNF

nodes.summary: A width bound on the input gives the source bounds on allocated fresh variables and output clauses.
nodes.title: Size bounds for the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction

nodes.summary: Every satisfying assignment of the original formula has exactly one satisfying extension that can differ only on the allocated fresh-variable interval.
nodes.title: Unique satisfying extension in the parsimonious 3-CNF reduction

nodes.summary: The parsimonious reduction preserves the number of assignments to the variables occurring in the formula.
nodes.title: The parsimonious 3-CNF reduction preserves the model count
Resolution

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. The resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$ is the clause consisting of the literals of $C$ other than $(x, \mathrm{true})$, in order, followed by the literals of $D$ other than $(x, \mathrm{false})$, in order.
nodes.title: Resolvent of two clauses

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $C$, $D$ clauses. Every assignment that satisfies both $C$ and $D$ satisfies the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Resolution rule soundness

nodes.summary: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, the clauses derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution form the smallest set $S$ of clauses that contains every clause of $\varphi$ and, for every variable $x$ and all clauses $C, D \in S$ such that $C$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ and $D$ contains the literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$, contains the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$.
nodes.title: Resolution derivability

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula. Every clause derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ is satisfied by every assignment that satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Soundness of resolution

nodes.summary: If the empty clause is derivable by resolution from a CNF formula $\varphi$, then $\varphi$ is not satisfiable.
nodes.title: Refutable formulas are unsatisfiable

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $\ell$ a literal. A clause $C$ belongs to the restriction of $\varphi$ by $\ell$ if and only if there is a clause $C_0$ of $\varphi$ that does not contain $\ell$ such that $C$ is the restriction of $C_0$ by $\ell$.
nodes.title: Clauses of a restricted formula

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $x$ a variable and $b$ a Boolean value. If a clause $D$ is derivable by resolution from the restriction of $\varphi$ by the literal $(x, b)$, then some clause $D_0$ is derivable by resolution from $\varphi$ such that every literal of $D_0$ is either a literal of $D$ or the complementary literal $(x, \lnot b)$.
nodes.title: Lifting lemma

nodes.summary: If a CNF formula $\varphi$ has no variables and is not satisfiable, then the empty clause is one of the clauses of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Unsatisfiable formulas without variables contain the empty clause

nodes.summary: Refutation completeness of resolution: every unsatisfiable CNF formula has a resolution derivation of the empty clause.
nodes.title: Refutation completeness

nodes.summary: A CNF formula has a resolution refutation iff it is unsatisfiable.
nodes.title: Soundness and refutation completeness
2-satisfiability

nodes.summary: A CNF formula is a 2-CNF formula when each of its clauses, viewed as a list of literals, has length at most $2$ (repeated literals are counted with multiplicity).
nodes.title: 2-CNF formulas

nodes.summary: The complement of a literal $(x, b)$, with variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $b$, is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: same variable, opposite polarity.
nodes.title: Complement of a literal

nodes.summary: In a clause with at most two literals, any two different members $a$ and $b$ are all of its members: every member $c$ of the clause equals $a$ or $b$.
nodes.title: Clauses with at most two literals

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, there is an implication edge from $l$ to $m$ when some clause of $\varphi$ contains both $\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or with $m$ as its only literal (so a unit clause $m$ gives the edge from $\neg m$ to $m$).
nodes.title: Implication edge

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal $l$ reaches a literal $m$ when there is a path of zero or more implication edges of $\varphi$ from $l$ to $m$; that is, reachability is the reflexive-transitive closure of the implication edge relation.
nodes.title: Reachability in the implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then it also has the contrapositive edge from $\lnot m$ to $\lnot l$, where $\lnot$ denotes the complementary literal.
nodes.title: Skew symmetry of the implication graph

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a 2-CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment of truth values to the variables that satisfies $\varphi$. If the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from a literal $l$ to a literal $m$ and $\sigma$ satisfies $l$, then $\sigma$ satisfies $m$.
nodes.title: Satisfying assignments respect implication edges

nodes.summary: A clause $C$ satisfies the invariant with respect to a CNF formula $\varphi$ when for every literal $a$ of $C$ there is a literal $b$ of $C$ such that the complementary literal $\lnot a$ reaches $b$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$ (by a path of zero or more edges).
nodes.title: Resolution invariant of the implication graph

nodes.summary: If a CNF formula $\varphi$ does not contain the empty clause and the empty clause is derivable from $\varphi$ by resolution, then there is a variable $x$ such that the literals $x$ and $\neg x$ reach each other in the implication graph of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Resolution refutations give contradictory cycles

nodes.summary: 2-SAT characterization (Aspvall, Plass, Tarjan): a 2-CNF formula is satisfiable iff it has no empty clause and no variable `x` such that `x` and `¬x` reach each other in the implication graph.
nodes.title: 2-SAT characterization

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, a literal over $\varphi$ is a pair $(x, b)$ of a variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and a polarity $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ such that the variable $x$ occurs in $\varphi$. These literals are the vertices of the implication graph of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Literals over the variables of a formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the complement of a literal $(x, b)$ over the variables of $\varphi$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$, which is again a literal over the variables of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Complement of a literal over a formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of the variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each exactly once, in the order of their last occurrences when the clauses of $\varphi$ and their literals are read from first to last.
nodes.title: Duplicate-free list of the variables of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, this is the list of all literals over the variables of $\varphi$, each appearing exactly once, arranged variable by variable: for each variable $x$ of $\varphi$, the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ is immediately followed by the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$.
nodes.title: List of the literals of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and $l$ a literal over the variables of $\varphi$, and write $\neg l$ for the complementary literal. The successors of $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ such that the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$: some clause of $\varphi$ contains $\neg l$ and $m$, either as two different literals or as its only literal. They are listed without…
nodes.title: Successors in the implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the hash map that sends each literal over the variables of $\varphi$ to the list of its implication-graph successors, that is, of the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge from it to $m$.
nodes.title: Adjacency table of the implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the finite directed graph whose vertices are the literals over the variables of $\varphi$, listed without repetition, and whose out-neighbours of a literal $l$ are the literals $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$ with an implication edge from $l$ to $m$, read from the adjacency table of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Implication graph as a finite directed graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$, if the implication graph of $\varphi$ has an edge from $l$ to $m$, then the variable of $m$ occurs in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Implication edges end over variables of the formula

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and literals $l$ and $m$ over the variables of $\varphi$, $m$ is reachable from $l$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, viewed as a finite directed graph on these literals, if and only if $l$ reaches $m$ by implication edges of $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Reachability in the finite implication graph

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the procedure returns false if $\varphi$ contains the empty clause; otherwise it returns true if and only if no block of the strongly connected components computed for the implication graph of $\varphi$ contains a literal together with its complementary literal.
nodes.title: SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a variable $x$, if the positive literal $(x, \mathrm{true})$ reaches the negative literal $(x, \mathrm{false})$ in the implication graph of $\varphi$, then $x$ occurs in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: A positive literal reaching its complement lies over a variable of the formula

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ in which every clause has at most two literals, the SCC-based 2-SAT decision procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of the SCC-based 2-SAT procedure
Davis–Putnam algorithm

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$, in their order, that contain the literal $x$ and do not contain the literal $\neg x$.
nodes.title: Clauses containing a variable only positively

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$, in their order, that contain the literal $\neg x$ and do not contain the literal $x$.
nodes.title: Clauses containing a variable only negatively

nodes.summary:
Eliminating a variable $x$ from a CNF formula $\varphi$ gives the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$ that contain neither $x$ nor $
eg x$, followed by the resolvents on $x$ of $C$ and $D$, for every clause $C$ of $\varphi$ that contains $x$ but not $
eg x$ and every clause $D$ of $\varphi$ that contains $
eg x$ but not $x$. Clauses containing both $x$ and $
eg x$ are dropped.
nodes.title: Davis-Putnam elimination of a variable

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and let $C$ and $D$ be clauses such that $C$ does not contain $\neg x$ and $D$ does not contain $x$. Then no literal of the resolvent of $C$ and $D$ on $x$ has variable $x$.
nodes.title: Resolvents do not mention the resolved variable

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $\varphi$ a CNF formula. Every assignment that satisfies $\varphi$ also satisfies the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$.
nodes.title: Soundness of a Davis-Putnam step

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable, $\varphi$ a CNF formula and $\sigma$ an assignment that satisfies the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$. Then there is a truth value $b$ such that the assignment that agrees with $\sigma$ except that it sends $x$ to $b$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Completeness of a Davis-Putnam step

nodes.summary: For every variable $x$ and every CNF formula $\varphi$, the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by eliminating $x$ is satisfiable if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Davis-Putnam elimination preserves satisfiability

nodes.summary: Given a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of variables and a CNF formula $\varphi$, eliminate $x_1$ from $\varphi$, then $x_2$ from the result, and so on up to $x_n$. For the empty list the result is $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Successive elimination of a list of variables

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$, the list of the variables occurring in the literals of $\varphi$, each listed exactly once, in order of first occurrence when the clauses of $\varphi$, and the literals within each clause, are read from left to right.
nodes.title: Variable list for Davis–Putnam elimination

nodes.summary: Given a CNF formula $\varphi$, eliminate the variables that occur in $\varphi$ one after another, each exactly once, in the order of their first occurrence in $\varphi$, each elimination being applied to the result of the previous one. The procedure returns true if the resulting formula does not contain the empty clause, and false if it does.
nodes.title: The Davis-Putnam procedure

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the Davis-Putnam procedure returns true on $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.
nodes.title: Correctness of the Davis-Putnam procedure
Tseitin transformation

nodes.summary: The complement of a literal $(x, b)$ with variable $x$ and polarity $b$ is the literal $(x, \lnot b)$: the same variable with the opposite polarity.
nodes.title: Complementary literal

nodes.summary: For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of the gate literal $g$ for the conjunction of $a$ and $b$ are, in this order, the three clauses $\lnot g \lor a$, $\lnot g \lor b$ and $g \lor \lnot a \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the complementary literal of $\ell$ (same variable, opposite polarity).
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses for a conjunction

nodes.summary: For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of the gate literal $g$ for the disjunction of $a$ and $b$ are the three clauses $\lnot g \lor a \lor b$, $g \lor \lnot a$ and $g \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the complementary literal of $\ell$.
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses for a disjunction

nodes.summary: For literals $g$, $a$ and $b$, the defining clauses of the gate literal $g$ for the implication from $a$ to $b$ are, in this order, the three clauses $\lnot g \lor \lnot a \lor b$, $g \lor a$ and $g \lor \lnot b$, where $\lnot \ell$ denotes the complementary literal of $\ell$ (same variable, opposite polarity).
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses for an implication

nodes.summary: Given a rule $\mathit{cl}$ assigning to literals $g$, $a$, $b$ a list of defining clauses, and the results $(a, C_A, k_A)$ and $(b, C_B, k_B)$ of encoding the two operands of a binary connective (each a literal, a clause list and a next unused gate number), the step returns the positive literal $g$ of variable $2k_B+1$, the clause list $C_A$, then $C_B$, then $\mathit{cl}(g, a, b)$, and the next gate number $k_B+1$.
nodes.title: One step of the Tseitin encoding

nodes.summary: Let $c$ map a gate literal and two operand literals to a list of clauses, and let $(a, \varphi_A, k_A)$ and $(b, \varphi_B, k_B)$ be the results for the two operands, each a literal, a clause list and a next free gate number. The step returns the positive literal $g$ of the variable $2k_B + 1$, the clause list $c(g, a, b)$ followed by $\varphi_B$, and the next free gate number $k_B + 1$. Neither $\varphi_A$ nor…
nodes.title: One step of the linear-time Tseitin builder

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $A$, built from atoms with the binary connectives $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\to$, the connective count of $A$ is the number of occurrences of these connectives in $A$. It is $0$ for an atom, and for $B \circ C$, with $\circ$ one of $\wedge$, $\vee$ and $\to$, it is the count of $B$ plus the count of $C$ plus $1$.
nodes.title: Connective count of a propositional formula

nodes.title: Linear-time Tseitin builder

nodes.title: The linear-time Tseitin builder agrees with the reference encoding

nodes.summary: For a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and a formula $A$, run the linear-time Tseitin builder on $A$ with gates numbered from $0$ and the empty accumulator, obtaining a literal $\ell$ naming $A$ and a clause list $C$. The Tseitin CNF of $A$ is the unit clause $[\ell]$ followed by $C$.
nodes.title: Tseitin CNF

nodes.summary: For every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and every formula $A$, the Tseitin CNF of $A$ is the unit clause whose literal is the literal naming $A$ in the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $0$, followed by a list of clauses that is a permutation of the defining clauses of that encoding.
nodes.title: The Tseitin CNF reorders the reference encoding

reading_title.source: Tseitin CNF with $\bot$ false

nodes.summary: For an atom type with a distinguished atom $\bot$, a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers and a formula $A$, this is the CNF consisting of the unit clause whose literal is the negative literal of variable $2\iota(\bot)$, followed by the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$.
nodes.title: Tseitin CNF with $\bot$ false

nodes.summary: For every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every formula $A$ and every gate number $k$, the list of defining clauses produced by the Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$ has length $3c$, where $c$ is the number of binary connectives of $A$.
nodes.title: Number of defining clauses in the Tseitin encoding

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ and every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$, as a list of clauses counted with repetition, has length $3c + 1$, where $c$ is the number of binary connectives of $A$: three defining clauses per connective plus the unit clause asserting $A$.
nodes.title: Number of clauses of the Tseitin CNF

nodes.summary: For every proposition $A$ and every map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, every clause of the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$ has at most three literals.
nodes.title: Tseitin clauses have at most three literals

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign a Boolean value to every natural-number variable, and let $\ell = (x, b)$ be a literal with variable $x$ and polarity $b$. The truth value of $\ell$ under $\sigma$ is true exactly when $\sigma(x) = b$.
nodes.title: Truth value of a literal

nodes.summary: For every assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables and all CNF formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $\sigma$ satisfies the formula consisting of the clauses of $\varphi$ followed by those of $\psi$ if and only if $\sigma$ satisfies both $\varphi$ and $\psi$.
nodes.title: Satisfying a concatenation of CNF formulas

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, a variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ is a gate in range $[k, k')$ if $x = 2j + 1$ for some $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \le j < k'$.
nodes.title: Gate variables in a range

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $k'$, a variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ is allowed for the gate range $[k, k')$ if $x$ is even (it names an atom) or $x$ is a gate in range $[k, k')$, that is, $x = 2j + 1$ for some $j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $k \le j < k'$.
nodes.title: Allowed variables for a gate range

nodes.summary: A function $f$ from assignments $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ to Booleans depends only on the atom variables if $f(\sigma) = f(\tau)$ for all assignments $\sigma$ and $\tau$ with $\sigma(2n) = \tau(2n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Functions of the atom variables

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $r = (\ell, \Phi, k')$ consist of a literal $\ell$, a CNF formula $\Phi$ and a natural number $k'$, and let $v$ map each assignment of Boolean values to the natural-number variables to a Boolean value. Call a variable a gate in range if it equals $2j + 1$ for some $j$ with $k \le j < k'$. The invariant holds for $k$, $r$ and $v$ when $k \le k'$; the variable of $\ell$ and every…
nodes.title: Tseitin encoding invariant

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula and let $\sigma$ and $\tau$ be assignments of Boolean values to the natural-number variables that agree on every variable occurring in a literal of $\varphi$. If $\sigma$ satisfies $\varphi$, then $\tau$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction depends only on the occurring variables

nodes.summary: Given a map $\iota$ from atoms to natural numbers, a proposition $A$ and an assignment $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$, this is the truth value of $A$ under the valuation that gives each atom $a$ the value $\sigma(2\iota(a))$.
nodes.title: Value of a proposition read off the atom variables

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ map atoms to natural numbers, let $A$ be a proposition and $k$ a natural number, and let $(\ell, \Phi, k')$ be the reference Tseitin encoding of $A$ with gates numbered from $k$: the literal naming $A$, its defining clauses and the next unused gate number. For an assignment $\sigma$ of Boolean values to the natural-number variables, let $A[\sigma]$ be the truth value of $A$ when each atom $a$ gets the…
nodes.title: Correctness invariant of the Tseitin encoding

nodes.summary: Let $\iota$ be an injective map from atoms to natural numbers, let $A$ be a proposition and let $v$ be a valuation of the atoms. Then $A$ is true under $v$ if and only if some assignment $\sigma : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ with $\sigma(2\iota(a)) = v(a)$ for every atom $a$ satisfies the Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$.
nodes.title: Tseitin correctness

nodes.summary: Let the atoms have a distinguished atom $\bot$, let $\iota$ be an injective map from atoms to natural numbers and let $A$ be a proposition. The Tseitin CNF of $A$ with respect to $\iota$, together with the unit clause making the variable $2\iota(\bot)$ false, is satisfiable if and only if $A$ is true under some valuation $v$ of the atoms with $v(\bot)$ false.

nodes.summary: For a type of atoms, the family of relation symbols indexed by arity that consists of one nullary relation symbol for each atom $a$ and has no relation symbols of positive arity.
nodes.title: Relation symbols of the propositional language

nodes.summary: For a type of atoms, the first-order language whose relation symbols are exactly one nullary relation symbol for each atom, with no relation symbols of positive arity and no function symbols.
nodes.title: First-order language of propositional atoms

nodes.summary: The translation of propositions over a type of atoms into sentences of the first-order language of propositional atoms, defined by recursion: an atom $a$ becomes the atomic sentence given by the nullary relation symbol of $a$, and $A \wedge B$, $A \vee B$ and $A \to B$ become the conjunction, the disjunction and the implication of the translations of $A$ and $B$.
nodes.title: Embedding propositions as first-order sentences

nodes.summary: Given a valuation $v$ assigning a Boolean to each atom, the Boolean structure of $v$ is the structure for the first-order language of propositional atoms whose domain is the set of Booleans $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}$ and in which the nullary relation symbol of an atom $a$ holds exactly when $v(a)$ is true. The language has no function symbols, so nothing else needs to be interpreted.
nodes.title: Boolean structure of a valuation

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ assigning a Boolean to each atom and every proposition $A$, the first-order sentence obtained by embedding $A$ is true in the Boolean structure of $v$ if and only if the truth-table value of $A$ under $v$ is true.
