nodes.summary: Fix a first-order language $L$ and a type $\alpha$ of variables; formulas and terms below are those of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For a formula $\varphi$ with one additional bound variable and a term $t$, write $\varphi[t]$ for $\varphi$ with $t$ substituted for that bound variable and $\forall \varphi$ for its universal quantification. Write $\neg \psi$ for $\psi \to \bot$, and $\psi, \Gamma$ for the…
nodes.title: Natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be such a formula. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then for every $L$-structure $M$ and every assignment $v \colon \alpha \to M$ under which all members of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds under $v$.
nodes.title: Soundness of first-order natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \alpha \to \beta$ be an injective map between types of variables. For a formula $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, write $f(\psi)$ for the renaming of the free variables of $\psi$ by $f$, and for a finite list $\Gamma$ of such formulas write $f(\Gamma)$ for the list obtained by renaming each member of $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$ is such a list, $\varphi$ is such a formula…
nodes.title: Injective renaming preserves derivability

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \alpha \to \beta$ be an injective map between types of variables. For a formula $\psi$ of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, write $f(\psi)$ for Mathlib's relabeling of $\psi$ by $f$, which replaces each free variable $x$ by $f(x)$, and for a finite list $\Gamma$ of such formulas write $f(\Gamma)$ for the list obtained by applying this to each member of $\Gamma$. If $\Gamma$…
nodes.title: Injective relabeling preserves derivability

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ be finite lists of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ such that every member of $\Gamma$ is a member of $\Delta$, and let $\varphi$ be such a formula. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction, then $\Delta \vdash \varphi$.
nodes.title: Weakening

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, let $\varphi$ and $\psi$ be such formulas, and write $\varphi, \Gamma$ for the list $\Gamma$ with $\varphi$ added in front. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ and $\varphi, \Gamma \vdash \psi$ in natural deduction, then $\Gamma \vdash \psi$.
nodes.title: Cut

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite list of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, let $\varphi$ be such a formula with one additional bound variable, let $t$ be a term, and write $\varphi[t]$ for $\varphi$ with $t$ substituted for that bound variable. If $\Gamma \vdash \varphi[t]$ in natural deduction, then $\Gamma \vdash \exists \varphi$, where $\exists \varphi$ abbreviates…
nodes.title: Existential introduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a list of first-order formulas and let $s$ and $t$ be terms. If the equation $s = t$ is derivable from the hypotheses $\Gamma$, then the equation $t = s$ is derivable from $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of equality in natural deduction

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a list of first-order formulas and let $r$, $s$ and $t$ be terms. If the equations $r = s$ and $s = t$ are both derivable from the hypotheses $\Gamma$, then the equation $r = t$ is derivable from $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Transitivity of equality in natural deduction

nodes.summary: A set $T$ of formulas of a first-order language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ proves such a formula $\varphi$ when there is a finite list $\Gamma$ of members of $T$ with $\Gamma \vdash \varphi$ in natural deduction.
nodes.title: Provability from a set of formulas

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a theory, that is, a set of sentences of a first-order language $L$, and regard each sentence of $T$ as a formula with free variables in $\alpha$. If a formula $\varphi$ with free variables in $\alpha$ is provable from these formulas, then $\varphi$ holds in every model of $T$ under every assignment of elements of the model to the variables in $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Soundness for theories

nodes.summary: The empty context does not derive `⊥`.
nodes.title: Consistency of the calculus
First-order unification

nodes.summary: For a type $C$ of constants, a term over $C$ is either a variable $x$, indexed by a natural number $x \in \mathbb{N}$, or a constant $c \in C$, or a binary node built from two terms $l$ and $r$.
nodes.title: Terms for unification

nodes.summary: A substitution is a map assigning a term to every variable, that is, a function from the set $\mathbb{N}$ of variables to terms.
nodes.title: Substitution

nodes.summary: For a substitution $\sigma$ and a term $t$, the term $t\sigma$ is obtained from $t$ by replacing every variable $x$ by $\sigma(x)$: a variable $x$ becomes $\sigma(x)$, a constant is unchanged, and a node with subterms $l$ and $r$ becomes the node with subterms $l\sigma$ and $r\sigma$.
nodes.title: Applying a substitution to a term

nodes.summary: The size of a term is the number of symbols in it: a variable and a constant have size $1$, and a node with subterms $l$ and $r$ has size equal to the size of $l$ plus the size of $r$ plus $1$.
nodes.title: Size of a term

nodes.summary: The variables of a term form a finite set of natural numbers, defined recursively: the variable $x$ has the variable set $\{x\}$, a constant has no variables, and the variables of a node with subterms $l$ and $r$ are those of $l$ together with those of $r$.
nodes.title: Variables of a term

nodes.summary: If two substitutions $\sigma$ and $\tau$ agree on every variable occurring in a term $u$, then applying $\sigma$ to $u$ gives the same term as applying $\tau$ to $u$.
nodes.title: Substitution depends only on the variables of the term

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a substitution and $t$ a term. Every variable of the term obtained by applying $s$ to $t$ is a variable of $s(y)$ for some variable $y$ of $t$.
nodes.title: Variables of a substituted term

nodes.summary: For every substitution $s$, term $t$ and variable $y$ occurring in $t$, every variable of the term $s(y)$ occurs in the term obtained from $t$ by applying $s$.
nodes.title: Variables of a substituted variable occur in the substituted term

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $t$ a term in which $x$ occurs, with $t$ not the variable $x$ itself. Then for every substitution $\sigma$, the term $\sigma(x)$ has strictly smaller size than $t\sigma$, the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$.
nodes.title: Occurs check: size bound

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable and $t$ a term in which $x$ does not occur. For every term $u$, every variable of the term obtained from $u$ by replacing each occurrence of $x$ with $t$ is a variable of $u$ or of $t$, and is different from $x$.
nodes.title: Substituting for a variable that does not occur in the substituted term

nodes.summary: For substitutions $s$ and $t$, the composite $s \gg t$ (first $s$, then $t$) sends each variable $x$ to the term obtained from $s(x)$ by applying $t$ to every variable of $s(x)$.
nodes.title: Composition of substitutions on first-order terms

nodes.summary: For a variable $x$ and a term $t$, the substitution $[x \mapsto t]$ sends $x$ to $t$ and every other variable $y$ to the term $y$.
nodes.title: Single-variable substitution on first-order terms

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable, $t$ a term, and $[x \mapsto t]$ the substitution replacing $x$ by $t$ and fixing every other variable. If a substitution $\sigma$ satisfies $\sigma(x) = t\sigma$, where $t\sigma$ is the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$, then the composite substitution that applies $[x \mapsto t]$ first and $\sigma$ second equals $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Absorbing a single-variable substitution

nodes.summary: If the variable $x$ does not occur in the term $t$, then applying to $t$ the substitution $[x \mapsto t]$, which replaces $x$ by $t$ and fixes every other variable, leaves $t$ unchanged.
nodes.title: A term is fixed by substituting it for a variable it avoids

nodes.summary: A list of equations over constants $C$ is a finite list of pairs $(t, u)$ of terms over $C$, each pair standing for the equation $t = u$.
nodes.title: Lists of equations

nodes.summary: A substitution $s$ unifies a list $E$ of equations between terms when, for every equation $(t, u)$ in $E$, applying $s$ to $t$ and applying $s$ to $u$ give the same term.
nodes.title: Unifier of a list of equations

nodes.summary: A substitution $s$ is a most general unifier of a list of equations $E$ when $s$ unifies $E$ and every unifier $s'$ of $E$ factors through $s$, that is, $s' = s \gg r$ for some substitution $r$, where $s \gg r$ applies first $s$ and then $r$.
nodes.title: Most general unifier

nodes.summary: For a substitution $\sigma$ and a list $E$ of equations between terms, the result is the list obtained by replacing each equation $u = v$ of $E$, in order, by $u\sigma = v\sigma$, where $u\sigma$ is the result of applying $\sigma$ to $u$.
nodes.title: Applying a substitution to a list of equations

nodes.summary: The variables of a list of equations form the finite set of all variables that occur on either side of any of its equations.
nodes.title: Variables of a list of equations

nodes.summary: The total size of a list of equations is the sum, over all its equations, of the sizes of the two sides, where the size of a term is its number of variable, constant and node symbols.
nodes.title: Total size of a list of equations

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable, $t$ a term in which $x$ does not occur, and $E$ a list of equations. Applying the substitution that replaces $x$ by $t$ (and fixes every other variable) to both sides of every equation of $E$ gives a list of equations with strictly fewer distinct variables than the list obtained by putting the equation $x = t$ in front of $E$.
nodes.title: Eliminating a solved variable lowers the number of variables

nodes.summary: The algorithm takes a list of equations between terms and returns a substitution or fails. On the empty list it returns the identity substitution. Otherwise it looks at the first equation $t = u$ and the remaining list $E$. If $t$ and $u$ are the same variable, or the same constant, the equation is dropped and the algorithm continues on $E$; if they are two different constants, it fails. If $t$ is a variable $x$…
nodes.title: Martelli–Montanari unification

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of equations between terms and $r$ either a substitution or failure. The specification holds for $E$ and $r$ when, if $r$ is a substitution $s$, then $s$ unifies $E$ and every substitution $s'$ that unifies $E$ equals the composite substitution that applies first $s$ and then $s'$; and, if $r$ is failure, then no substitution unifies $E$.
nodes.title: Specification of a unification result

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $E'$ be lists of equations such that a substitution unifies $E$ exactly when it unifies $E'$. If an optional substitution $r$ satisfies the unification specification for $E'$ (a returned substitution $s$ unifies the list and every unifier $s'$ of it satisfies $s' = s \gg s'$, where $s \gg s'$ applies first $s$ and then $s'$, and failure means the list has no unifier), then $r$ satisfies the unification…
nodes.title: Lists of equations with the same unifiers satisfy the same specification

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of equations between terms and let $u = v$ be a further equation, where $u\sigma$ denotes the result of applying a substitution $\sigma$ to $u$. If $u\sigma \ne v\sigma$ for every substitution $\sigma$, then returning no substitution meets the unification specification for the list obtained by putting $u = v$ in front of $E$: no substitution unifies that list.
nodes.title: Failure is correct when the first equation has no unifier

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a variable, $t$ a term in which $x$ does not occur, $e$ an equation and $E$ a list of equations. Suppose that for every substitution $s$, the two sides of $e$ become equal under $s$ exactly when $s(x)$ equals the result of applying $s$ to $t$. Let $\sigma$ be the substitution that replaces $x$ by $t$ and fixes every other variable, and let $E'$ be the list obtained by applying $\sigma$ to both sides of…
nodes.title: The elimination step preserves the unification specification

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of equations between terms, if the Martelli–Montanari algorithm returns a substitution $s$ on $E$, then $s$ unifies $E$: applying $s$ to the two sides of any equation of $E$ gives the same term.
nodes.title: Soundness of unification

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of equations between terms, if the Martelli–Montanari algorithm returns a substitution $s$ on $E$, then every substitution $s'$ that unifies $E$ equals the composite substitution that applies first $s$ and then $s'$.
nodes.title: Most generality of unification

nodes.summary: If the Martelli-Montanari unification algorithm, run on a list of equations $E$, returns a substitution $s$, then $s$ is a most general unifier of $E$.
nodes.title: Unification returns a most general unifier

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of equations between terms, if the Martelli–Montanari algorithm returns a substitution $s$ on $E$, then $s$ is idempotent: the composite substitution that applies first $s$ and then $s$ equals $s$.
nodes.title: Unification returns an idempotent substitution

nodes.summary: For every list $E$ of equations between terms, the Martelli–Montanari algorithm fails on $E$ if and only if no substitution unifies $E$.
nodes.title: Completeness of unification

nodes.summary: Write $V(F)$ for the set of variables of a list $F$ of equations. Let $x_0$ be a variable, $t$ a term in which $x_0$ does not occur, $e = (e_1, e_2)$ an equation such that every variable of $t$ occurs in $e_1$ or $e_2$, and $E$ a list of equations, and let $E'$ be obtained from $E$ by substituting $t$ for $x_0$ on both sides of every equation. Let $s_0$ be a substitution such that, for every variable $x$, every…
nodes.title: The elimination step of unification introduces no variables

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a list of equations between terms. If the unification algorithm succeeds on $E$ and returns the substitution $s$, then for every variable $x$, each variable of the term $s(x)$ is either $x$ itself or a variable occurring in some equation of $E$.
nodes.title: Unification introduces no new variables
Gödel's completeness theorem

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, if $S$ proves $\varphi \to \psi$ and $S$ proves $\varphi$, then $S$ proves $\psi$.
nodes.title: Modus ponens for provability from sets

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. If $S$ proves $\bot$, then $S$ proves every formula $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Ex falso for provability from sets

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be such formulas. If $S \cup \{\varphi\}$ proves $\psi$, then $S$ proves $\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Deduction theorem

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $\alpha$ a type of variables. A set $S$ of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$ is consistent when $S$ does not prove $\bot$.
nodes.title: Consistent set of formulas

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $S$ proves $\varphi$ if and only if $S \cup \{\neg\varphi\}$ is not consistent.
nodes.title: Provability as inconsistency with the negation

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, let $S$ be a set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $S$ proves $\neg\varphi$ if and only if $S \cup \{\varphi\}$ is not consistent.
nodes.title: Refutability as inconsistency

nodes.summary: If $C$ is a nonempty family of sets of formulas that is totally ordered by inclusion and every member of $C$ is consistent, then the union $\bigcup C$ is consistent.
nodes.title: Unions of chains of consistent sets are consistent

nodes.summary: A set $\Delta$ of formulas is maximal consistent when it is consistent and every consistent set of formulas containing $\Delta$ is contained in $\Delta$, that is, equals $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas of a language $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula. If $\Delta \cup \{\varphi\}$ is consistent, then $\varphi \in \Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets absorb consistent extensions

nodes.summary: Every consistent set $S$ of first-order formulas is contained in a maximal consistent set.
nodes.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for first-order logic

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. Every formula $\varphi$ that $\Delta$ proves lies in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets of first-order formulas are deductively closed

nodes.summary:
Let $L$ be a first-order language, let $\alpha$ be an infinite type of variables, and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas of $L$ with free variables in $\alpha$. For every formula $\varphi$, $
eg\varphi \in \Delta$ if and only if $\varphi 
otin \Delta$; so exactly one of $\varphi$ and $
eg\varphi$ lies in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Maximal consistent sets decide every formula

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and for a term $t$ write $\varphi(t)$ for the result of substituting $t$ for $x$. If $\Delta$ contains $\forall x\, \varphi$, then $\Delta$ contains $\varphi(t)$ for every term $t$.
nodes.title: Universal instantiation in maximal consistent sets

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and for a term $u$ write $\varphi(u)$ for the result of substituting $u$ for $x$. If $s$ and $t$ are terms such that $\Delta$ contains the equation $s = t$ and the formula $\varphi(s)$, then $\Delta$ contains…
nodes.title: Substitution of equals in maximal consistent sets

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open and let $c$ be a variable; write $\varphi(c)$ for the result of substituting $c$ for $x$. The Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ is the formula $\neg \forall x\, \varphi \to \neg \varphi(c)$.
nodes.title: Henkin axiom

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $S$ be a consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, and let $c \in \alpha$ be a variable that occurs free neither in $\varphi$ nor in any formula of $S$. Then $S$ together with the Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ is consistent.
nodes.title: Adding a Henkin axiom preserves consistency

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an infinite set of variables and let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\alpha$. Let $\varphi(x)$ be a formula with one bound variable $x$ left open, let $c \in \alpha$, and write $\varphi(c)$ for the result of substituting $c$ for $x$. If $\Delta$ contains the Henkin axiom for $\forall x\, \varphi$ with witness $c$ and contains $\varphi(c)$, then $\Delta$…
nodes.title: Universal formulas from Henkin witnesses

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term and $\varphi$ a first-order formula with $m + 1$ bound variables, and let $\varphi(t)$ be the instance obtained by substituting $t$ for the outermost bound variable. Every free variable of $\varphi(t)$ is a free variable of $\varphi$ or a variable of $t$.
nodes.title: Free variables of an instance

nodes.summary: The depth $d(\varphi)$ of a first-order formula $\varphi$ is the nesting height of its implications and universal quantifiers: $\bot$, equations and relation atoms have depth $0$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ has depth $\max(d(\varphi), d(\psi)) + 1$, and $\forall \varphi$ has depth $d(\varphi) + 1$.
nodes.title: Depth of a formula

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types of variables, let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $\varphi$ be a formula with free variables in $\alpha$ and $n$ further variables reserved for binding by enclosing quantifiers. If two maps $f, g : \alpha \to \beta$ agree on every variable from $\alpha$ that occurs free in $\varphi$, then renaming the variables of $\varphi$ from $\alpha$ along $f$ and along $g$ gives the same formula.
nodes.title: Renaming depends only on the free variables

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types of variables with $\beta$ infinite, and let $f : \alpha \to \beta$ be any map. If $\varphi$ is derivable from the list of hypotheses $\Gamma$ in natural deduction, then the formula obtained from $\varphi$ by renaming each free variable $x$ to $f(x)$ is derivable from the list obtained by renaming the free variables of each formula of $\Gamma$ in the same way.
nodes.title: Renaming free variables along an arbitrary map preserves derivability

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, then the set obtained from $S$ by renaming every free variable $x$ to $2x$ in each of its formulas is consistent.
nodes.title: Doubling the variables preserves consistency

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation on a type $\beta$, let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a property of $n$-tuples $x = (x_i)_{i < n}$ in $\beta$. Suppose that for every tuple $x$, every position $i$ and all $a, b \in \beta$ with $r(a, b)$, if $P$ holds of $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $a$, then $P$ holds of $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $b$. Then for all tuples $x, y$ with $r(x_i, y_i)$ for every $i$,…
nodes.title: Replacing arguments one at a time

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be an $n$-ary function symbol, let $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ be terms over $\mathbb{N}$ and let $i < n$. For a term $u$, write $x[i := u]$ for $x$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $u$. If the equation $a = b$ lies in $\Delta$, then the equation $f(x[i := a]) = f(x[i := b])$ lies in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Congruence for function symbols in a maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be an $n$-ary relation symbol, let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, $a$ and $b$ be terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $i < n$. If $\Delta$ contains $a = b$ and contains $R(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ with $x_i$ replaced by $a$, then $\Delta$ contains $R(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ with $x_i$ replaced by $b$.
nodes.title: Replacing an argument of a relation symbol by an equal term

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a set of first-order formulas in a language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. The term structure of $\Delta$ is the $L$-structure whose domain is the set of $L$-terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$, in which an $n$-ary function symbol $f$ sends terms $t_1, \dots, t_n$ to the term $f(t_1, \dots, t_n)$, and an $n$-ary relation symbol $R$ holds of $t_1, \dots, t_n$ exactly when the atomic…
nodes.title: Term structure of a set of formulas

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of first-order formulas in a language $L$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$. Provable equality in $\Delta$ is the equivalence relation on $L$-terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$ under which $s \sim t$ holds exactly when the equation $s = t$ belongs to $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Provable equality of terms

nodes.summary: For a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the term model of $\Delta$ is the set of terms with variables in $\mathbb{N}$ modulo the equivalence relation that identifies $s$ and $t$ when the formula $s = t$ belongs to $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Term model of a maximal consistent set

nodes.summary: For a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, the canonical assignment sends each variable $x \in \mathbb{N}$ to $[x]$, the class of the variable term $x$ in the term model of $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Canonical assignment of the term model

nodes.summary: A term whose variables are free variables from $\mathbb{N}$ together with bound variables from the empty index set is lowered to the term over $\mathbb{N}$ of the same shape, in which every free variable $x$ stays $x$.
nodes.title: Lowering a term with no bound variables

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta$ be a maximal consistent set of formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every formula $\varphi$ with one bound variable, if $\Delta$ contains $\varphi(t)$ for every term $t$ (where $\varphi(t)$ is the result of substituting $t$ for the bound variable), then $\Delta$ contains $\forall x\,\varphi$. Then a formula $\psi$ with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ holds in the term model of…
nodes.title: Truth lemma for the first-order term model

nodes.summary: For a language with countably many symbols, the formulas $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ are a fixed enumeration, chosen by choice, of all first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ and one bound variable: every such formula is $\varphi_k$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Enumeration of formulas with one bound variable

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a first-order formula whose variables are natural numbers together with $n$ variables reserved for quantifiers. Its variable bound $b(\varphi)$ is one more than the largest natural number occurring as a free variable of $\varphi$, or $1$ when there is none; it is a strict upper bound on these free variables.
nodes.title: Variable bound of a formula

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language with countably many symbols, let $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ be the fixed surjective enumeration of the $L$-formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ and one variable reserved for a quantifier, and let $b(\varphi)$ be one more than the largest free variable of $\varphi$, or $1$ if it has none. The witness bases are defined by $w_0 = b(\varphi_0)$ and…
nodes.title: Witness bases

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language with countably many symbols and let $w_0 < w_1 < \dots$ be its witness bases, built from the fixed enumeration $\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \dots$ of the $L$-formulas with one variable reserved for a quantifier. The $k$-th Henkin witness is the variable $c_k = 2 w_k + 1$. It is odd, so it is not a free variable of any formula whose free variables are all even, and it exceeds every free…
nodes.title: Henkin witnesses

reading_title.source: The $k$-th Henkin axiom

nodes.summary: For a language with countably many symbols and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the $k$-th Henkin axiom is the Henkin axiom $\neg \forall \varphi_k \to \neg \varphi_k(c_k)$, where $\varphi_k$ is the $k$-th formula in the enumeration of formulas with one bound variable and $c_k$ is the $k$-th Henkin witness.
nodes.title: The $k$-th Henkin axiom

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$, in a language with countably many symbols, and let $H_k$ be the $k$-th Henkin axiom. The stages $S_k$ are defined by $S_0 = S$ and $S_{k+1} = S_k \cup \{H_k\}$, so $S_k$ is $S$ together with $H_0, \dots, H_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Stages of the Henkin extension

nodes.summary: For a language with countably many symbols, the Henkin extension of a set $S$ of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ is $S$ together with all Henkin axioms, the $k$-th Henkin axiom for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Henkin extension

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many symbols and let $S$ be a consistent set of first-order formulas with free variables in $\mathbb{N}$ such that every free variable of every formula in $S$ is even. Then $S$ is contained in a maximal consistent set $\Delta$ with the Henkin property: for every formula $\varphi$ with one bound variable, if every instance $\varphi(t)$, for $t$ a term over $\mathbb{N}$, lies in…
nodes.title: Henkin extension of a consistent set

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language with countably many symbols. Linear temporal logic

nodes.summary: For a type $A$ of atoms, the formulas of linear temporal logic (LTL) over $A$ are generated inductively: every atom $a \in A$ is a formula, the truth constant $\top$ is a formula, and if $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are formulas then so are the negation $\neg\varphi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$, the next formula $\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ and the until formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \psi$.
nodes.title: Formulas of linear temporal logic

nodes.summary: The LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) is defined as $\neg\top$, the negation of the truth constant $\top$.
nodes.title: Falsity in LTL

nodes.summary:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the disjunction $\varphi \vee \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \wedge 
eg\psi)$.
nodes.title: Disjunction in LTL

nodes.summary: For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the implication $\varphi \to \psi$ is defined as the disjunction $\neg\varphi \vee \psi$.
nodes.title: Implication in LTL

nodes.summary: For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bi-implication $\varphi \leftrightarrow \psi$ is defined as the conjunction $(\varphi \to \psi) \wedge (\psi \to \varphi)$ of the two implications.
nodes.title: Bi-implication in LTL

nodes.summary: For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ ("eventually $\varphi$") is defined as the until formula $\top \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} \varphi$.
nodes.title: The eventually operator of LTL

nodes.summary:
For an LTL formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ ("always $\varphi$") is defined as $
eg\,\mathbf{F}\,
eg\varphi$, the negation of "eventually $
eg\varphi$".
nodes.title: The always operator of LTL

nodes.summary:
For LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the release formula $\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{R}} \psi$ is defined as $
eg(
eg\varphi \mathbin{\mathbf{U}} 
eg\psi)$, the dual of until.
nodes.title: The release operator of LTL

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation that says which atoms are true at each letter, and for an ω-word $w$ and a natural number $k$ let $w^{(k)}$ be the suffix $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. Whether $w$ satisfies an LTL formula $\varphi$ under $v$, written $w \models \varphi$, is defined by recursion on $\varphi$: an atom $a$ holds when $v$ makes $a$ true at the first letter $w(0)$; truth always holds; $\neg \varphi$ holds when $\varphi$…
nodes.title: Satisfaction of LTL formulas on ω-words

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $k$ a natural number and $\varphi$ an LTL formula. Then $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under $v$ when the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$, satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction at a position

nodes.summary: Given a valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, the ω-language of an LTL formula $\varphi$ is the set of ω-words that satisfy $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Language of an LTL formula

nodes.summary: For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ holds at position $0$ of $w$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction at position zero

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be an ω-word and, for a natural number $k$, let $w^{(k)}$ be its suffix starting at position $k$, the ω-word $i \mapsto w(k + i)$. For every valuation of atoms on letters, every LTL formula $\varphi$ and every natural number $j$, $\varphi$ holds at position $j$ of $w^{(k)}$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at position $k + j$ of $w$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction on a suffix

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every atom $a$, the word $w$ satisfies the atomic formula $a$ under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the first letter $w_0$ of $w$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an atom

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters and every ω-word $w$, the word $w$ does not satisfy the LTL formula $\bot$ (falsity) under $v$.
nodes.title: Falsity is never satisfied

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Semantics of eventually

nodes.summary: For a valuation of atoms on letters, an ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) if and only if for every position $k$, either $\psi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ or $\varphi$ holds at some position $j < k$ of $w$.
nodes.title: Semantics of release

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\neg\mathbf{X}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{X}\,\neg\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.
nodes.title: Next is self-dual

nodes.summary: For every valuation of atoms on letters, ω-word $w$ and LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ until $\psi$) if and only if either $w$ satisfies $\psi$, or $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ and also satisfies $\mathsf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathsf{U}} \psi)$, that is, next ($\varphi$ until $\psi$).
nodes.title: Expansion law for until

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and all LTL formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi$ ($\varphi$ releases $\psi$) under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\psi$ and it satisfies $\varphi$ or $\mathbf{X}(\varphi \mathbin{\mathcal{R}} \psi)$, all under $v$, where $\mathbf{X}$ is the next operator.
nodes.title: Expansion law for release

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if it satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ under $v$, where $\mathbf{G}$ is the always operator.
nodes.title: Idempotence of always

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$ (always eventually $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there are infinitely many $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Always eventually means infinitely often

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ satisfies $\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ (eventually always $\varphi$) under $v$ if and only if there is $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k \ge n$ the suffix of $w$ starting at position $k$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Eventually always means from some point on

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters, $w$ an ω-word, $a$ an atom and $k$ a natural number. The atomic formula $a$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ under $v$ if and only if $v$ makes $a$ true at the letter $w(k)$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of an atom at a position

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a valuation of atoms on letters of an alphabet $\Sigma$, let $f \colon \Sigma' \to \Sigma$ be a map, and let $w$ be an ω-word over $\Sigma'$. For every LTL formula $\varphi$, the relabelled word $i \mapsto f(w(i))$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under the valuation that makes an atom $a$ true at a letter $s$ of $\Sigma'$ exactly when $v$ makes $a$ true at $f(s)$.
nodes.title: Relabelling the letters of an ω-word

nodes.summary: For every valuation $v$ of atoms on letters, every ω-word $w$ and every LTL formula $\varphi$, the word $w$ belongs to the ω-language of $\varphi$ under $v$ if and only if $w$ satisfies $\varphi$ under $v$.
nodes.title: Membership in the language of a formula
Büchi automata for a fragment of linear temporal logic

nodes.summary: The propositional formulas over a set of atoms are generated by the atoms, the constant truth $\top$, negation $\neg\varphi$ and conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas

nodes.summary: A letter is a set $s$ of atoms (the atoms true at it). A propositional formula is evaluated at $s$ by recursion: an atom $a$ is true iff $a \in s$, truth $\top$ is true, $\neg\varphi$ is true iff $\varphi$ is not, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is true iff both $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are true.
nodes.title: Evaluating a propositional formula at a letter

nodes.summary: The translation of propositional formulas into LTL formulas is defined by recursion: an atom $a$ goes to the LTL atom $a$, truth goes to the LTL truth constant $\top$, $\neg\varphi$ goes to the LTL negation of the translation of $\varphi$, and $\varphi \wedge \psi$ goes to the LTL conjunction of the translations of $\varphi$ and $\psi$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas as LTL formulas

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it belongs to that letter, $w$ satisfies the LTL translation of $\varphi$ if and only if $\varphi$ evaluates to true on the first letter $w_0$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the first letter

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula, let $w = w_0 w_1 w_2 \dots$ be an ω-word whose letters are sets of atoms, and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Under the valuation in which an atom holds at a letter exactly when it belongs to that letter, the LTL translation of $\varphi$ holds at position $k$ of $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ evaluates to true on the letter $w_k$.
nodes.title: Propositional formulas are evaluated at the current letter

nodes.summary: The one-state Büchi automaton for `G φ` with `φ` propositional: it stays forever, requiring every letter to satisfy `φ`.
nodes.title: One-state Büchi automaton for always φ

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, the one-state Büchi automaton for $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$ accepts exactly the infinite words of letters (sets of atoms) that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$.
nodes.title: The always automaton recognizes G φ

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and $p$ the set of letters (sets of atoms) at which $\varphi$ evaluates to true. The two-state Büchi automaton for “infinitely often $p$” accepts exactly the infinite words that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{G}\,\mathbf{F}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. Equivalently, a word is accepted iff $\varphi$ holds at infinitely many positions.
nodes.title: The infinitely-often automaton recognizes G F φ

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a propositional formula and $p$ the set of letters (sets of atoms) at which $\varphi$ evaluates to true. The two-state Büchi automaton for “eventually always $p$” accepts exactly the infinite words that satisfy the LTL formula $\mathbf{F}\,\mathbf{G}\,\varphi$, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. Equivalently, a word is accepted iff $\varphi$ holds at all but finitely many…
nodes.title: The eventually-always automaton recognizes F G φ

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, this Büchi automaton over letters that are sets of atoms has a start state $u$ and two verdict states $t$ and $f$, of which only $t$ is accepting. From $u$, on a letter $s$ it moves to $t$ if $\varphi$ evaluates to true at $s$ and to $f$ otherwise; from $t$ and from $f$ it stays in the same state on every letter. So it records the verdict of $\varphi$ on the first letter.
nodes.title: Büchi automaton for a propositional formula

nodes.summary: For a propositional formula $\varphi$, the three-state Büchi automaton for $\varphi$ accepts exactly the infinite words of letters (sets of atoms) that satisfy $\varphi$ read as an LTL formula, where an atom $a$ holds at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$.
nodes.title: The propositional automaton recognizes φ

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Büchi automaton over the alphabet of sets of atoms. Its shift is the Büchi automaton whose states are the states of $A$ together with one new state $\bot$, whose only start state is $\bot$, and whose accepting states are the accepting states of $A$. Its transitions are exactly the following: on every letter, from $\bot$ to each start state of $A$; and on a letter $x$, from a state $q$ of $A$ to a state…
nodes.title: The shift of a Büchi automaton

nodes.summary: For a Büchi automaton $A$ over letters that are sets of atoms, the shift automaton of $A$ accepts an infinite word $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ iff $A$ accepts its tail $x_1 x_2 x_3 \ldots$.
nodes.title: The shift automaton reads the tail

nodes.summary: The safety formulas over a type of atoms are generated by the following rules: every propositional formula $\varphi$ is a safety formula; if $\psi$ and $\rho$ are safety formulas, then so are $\psi \wedge \rho$, $\psi \vee \rho$ and $X\,\psi$ (next $\psi$); and for every propositional formula $\varphi$, $G\,\varphi$ (always $\varphi$) is a safety formula.

The translation $t$ of safety formulas into LTL formulas is defined by recursion: $t(\varphi)$ is the LTL translation of $\varphi$ for a propositional formula $\varphi$; $t(\psi \wedge ho) = t(\psi) \wedge t(ho)$; $t(\psi \vee ho) = 
eg(
eg t(\psi) \wedge 
eg t(ho))$, the derived LTL disjunction; $t(X\,\psi) = X\,t(\psi)$, where $X$ is next; and $t(G\,\varphi) = G\,t(\varphi)$ for a propositional formula…
nodes.title: Safety formulas as LTL formulas

nodes.summary: Take as letters the sets of atoms, an atom $a$ holding at a letter $s$ iff $a \in s$. For every formula $\psi$ of the restricted safety fragment there is a nondeterministic Büchi automaton with finitely many states whose ω-language is exactly the set of infinite words satisfying $\psi$, read as an LTL formula.

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language with at most countably many symbols, and let $T$ be a complete $L$-theory all of whose models are infinite. Call $T$ $\kappa$-categorical if any two models of $T$ of cardinality $\kappa$ are isomorphic. If $T$ is $\kappa$-categorical for some uncountable cardinal $\kappa$, then $T$ is $\mu$-categorical for every uncountable cardinal $\mu$.

First-order language of groups

nodes.summary: The function symbols of the first-order language of groups, graded by arity, are a constant symbol for the identity (arity $0$), a symbol for inversion (arity $1$) and a symbol for multiplication (arity $2$); there are no others.
nodes.title: Group function symbols

nodes.summary: The first-order language of groups has the group function symbols (a constant for the identity, a unary symbol for inversion and a binary symbol for multiplication) as its function symbols and no relation symbols.
nodes.title: The first-order language of groups

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the canonical structure on $G$ for the first-order language of groups interprets the identity constant as the identity $1$ of $G$, inversion as $x \mapsto x^{-1}$ and multiplication as $(x, y) \mapsto xy$; there are no relation symbols to interpret.
nodes.title: The canonical structure on a group

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$-ary function symbols of the first-order language of groups are exactly the group function symbols of arity $n$.
nodes.title: The function symbols of the language of groups

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the first-order language of groups has no $n$-ary relation symbols.
nodes.title: The language of groups has no relation symbols

nodes.summary: For every group $G$ and every pair $(x_0, x_1)$ of elements of $G$, the multiplication symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, sends $(x_0, x_1)$ to $x_0 x_1$.
nodes.title: Multiplication in the canonical structure

nodes.summary: For every group $G$ and every one-element tuple $(x_0)$ of elements of $G$, the inversion symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, sends $(x_0)$ to $x_0^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Inversion in the canonical structure

nodes.summary: For every group $G$, the identity constant symbol of the language of groups, interpreted in the canonical structure on $G$, takes the value $1$ at the empty tuple, where $1$ is the identity of $G$.

nodes.summary: Terms are built from variables $x_i$, one for each natural number $i$ (a de Bruijn index), and integer constants $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, using addition $s + t$, multiplication $s \cdot t$ and negation $-t$.
nodes.title: Terms of the language of ordered rings

nodes.summary: Formulas are built from the atomic formulas $s < t$ and $s = t$, for terms $s$ and $t$, and falsity $\bot$, by implication $\varphi \to \psi$ and universal quantification $\forall \varphi$, which binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$. Negation, truth, disjunction, conjunction and existential quantification are defined from these.
nodes.title: Formulas of the language of ordered rings

nodes.summary: The negation $\neg\varphi$ of a formula $\varphi$ is the formula $\varphi \to \bot$.
nodes.title: Negation of a formula

nodes.summary: The formula $\top$ is the negation $\neg\bot$ of falsity, that is, the formula $\bot \to \bot$.
nodes.title: The true formula

nodes.summary: The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the formula $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.
nodes.title: Disjunction of formulas

nodes.summary: For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is the formula $\neg(\varphi \to \neg\psi)$.
nodes.title: Conjunction of formulas

nodes.summary: For a formula $\varphi$, the formula $\exists \varphi$ is $\neg \forall \neg \varphi$; it binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Existential quantification of formulas

nodes.summary: An environment is a map $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ that assigns a real number to each de Bruijn index. For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the extension of $e$ by $x$ sends index $0$ to $x$ and index $i + 1$ to $e(i)$ for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Extending an environment

nodes.summary: Given an environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the value of a term in $\mathbb{R}$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable with de Bruijn index $i$ has value $e(i)$, the integer constant $k$ has value $k$, and the value of a sum, product or negation of terms is the sum, product or negation in $\mathbb{R}$ of the values of its parts.
nodes.title: Evaluation of terms

nodes.summary: A formula is quantifier free if it contains no universal quantifier $\forall$.
nodes.title: Quantifier-free formulas

nodes.summary: Quantifier elimination is a map sending each formula $\varphi$ of the language of ordered rings to a formula $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$, subject to two requirements: $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free, and for every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ assigning a real number to each variable, $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ does.
nodes.title: Quantifier elimination over the reals

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free.
nodes.title: Quantifier elimination yields quantifier-free formulas

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$ and every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$.
nodes.title: Quantifier elimination preserves truth

nodes.summary: For every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\exists x.\ x \cdot x = a$ holds under $e$ if and only if the formula $\neg(a < 0)$ holds under $e$. In the first formula the bound variable $x$ is de Bruijn index $0$ and $a$ is index $1$; in the second $a$ is index $0$; in both, $a$ denotes $e(0)$. Thus $e(0)$ is a square in $\mathbb{R}$ exactly when $e(0) \ge 0$.

nodes.title: $\kappa$-complete ideal on a cardinal

nodes.summary: Let κ be a cardinal, identified with κ = Iio(κ.ord) = {α : Ordinal ∣ α < κ.ord}, and let I⊆𝒫(κ).
nodes.title: Normal ideal on a cardinal

nodes.summary: Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal, identified with its initial ordinal, let $S$ be a set of ordinals less than $\kappa$, and let $f$ be a function from $S$ to the ordinals less than $\kappa$. Then $f$ is regressive if $f(\alpha) < \alpha$ for every nonzero $\alpha \in S$.
nodes.title: Regressive functions
Diamond principle

nodes.summary: ◇_κ holds iff there is a sequence ⟨ S_α : α < κ⟩ with S_α ⊆ α for all α < κ, such that for every X ⊆ κ, {α < κ : X ∩ α = S_α} is stationary in κ.
nodes.title: Diamond principle

nodes.summary: ◇⁻_κ holds iff there is a sequence ⟨ 𝒜_α : α < κ⟩ with each 𝒜_α ⊆ 𝒫(α) and |𝒜_α| ≤ |α|, such that for every X ⊆ κ the set {α < κ : X ∩ α ∈ 𝒜_α} is stationary in κ.
nodes.title: Diamond-minus principle
Partition calculus

nodes.summary: For ordinals $\alpha$, $\beta$ and a cardinal $c$, the partition property $\alpha \to (\beta, c)^2$ holds if for every coloring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ in red and blue, either some set of vertices whose order type is $\beta$ has all its edges red, or some set of vertices of cardinality exactly $c$ has all its edges blue.
nodes.title: Ordinal–cardinal Ramsey property

nodes.summary: Let $c$ assign a colour in $\gamma$ to each finite subset of a type $I$, and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A set $H \subseteq I$ is homogeneous for $c$ with colour $k \in \gamma$ if $c(s) = k$ for every $n$-element subset $s$ of $H$.
nodes.title: Homogeneous set

nodes.summary: For cardinals $\kappa$ and $\mu$, the relation $\kappa \to (\mu)^2_2$ holds if for every set $X$ of cardinality $\kappa$ and every symmetric colouring $c$ of the ordered pairs of elements of $X$ with two colours, there are a subset $H \subseteq X$ of cardinality $\mu$ and a colour $b$ such that $c(x, y) = b$ for all distinct $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: Partition relation for pairs with two colours

nodes.summary: The statement that for every strictly increasing sequence $n_0 < n_1 < \cdots$ of natural numbers such that the cardinals $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ are strictly increasing in $k$ and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$, the partition relation $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2_2$ holds: for every set $X$ of cardinality $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ and every symmetric colouring of the pairs of elements of $X$ with…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1219: a partition relation for sums of powers of two

nodes.summary: For every strictly increasing sequence $n_0 < n_1 < \cdots$ of natural numbers such that the cardinals $2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ are strictly increasing in $k$ and $2^{\aleph_{n_0}} > \aleph_\omega$, the partition relation $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}} \to (\aleph_\omega)^2_2$ holds: for every set $X$ of cardinality $\sum_k 2^{\aleph_{n_k}}$ and every symmetric colouring of the pairs of elements of $X$ with two colours, some…
nodes.title: Shelah's theorem (Erdős Problem 1219)

nodes.summary: The statement that, for $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$, every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$ (that is, every pair of complementary simple graphs, red and blue, on this set) has a red clique whose order type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation, $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 591

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha = \omega^{\omega^2}$. For every red/blue colouring of the edges of the complete graph on the ordinals less than $\alpha$, that is, every pair of complementary simple graphs (red and blue) on this set, there is a red clique whose order type is $\alpha$ or a blue clique with exactly $3$ elements. In partition notation, $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 591 is true

nodes.summary: For an ordinal $\alpha$ and a natural number $n$, the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$ holds when every colouring of the pairs $x < y$ of ordinals below $\alpha$ in red and blue has a red set of order type $\alpha$ or a blue set of size $n$: either there is a strictly increasing map $f$ from the ordinals below $\alpha$ to the ordinals below $\alpha$ such that the pair $\{f(x), f(y)\}$ is red for all…
nodes.title: Ordinal partition relation

nodes.summary: The statement that for every ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and every natural number $n \ge 3$, the ordinal $\alpha$ also satisfies $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 118 for ordinals

nodes.summary: There exist an ordinal $\alpha$ satisfying the partition relation $\alpha \to (\alpha, 3)^2$ and a natural number $n \ge 3$ such that $\alpha$ does not satisfy $\alpha \to (\alpha, n)^2$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 118 fails for ordinals
Square principle

nodes.summary: Jensen's square principle sequence: C = (C_α : α < κ⁺) is a □_κ-sequence: for every limit α < κ⁺, C_α is club in α of order type at most κ, and the family coheres — C_β = C_α ∩ β whenever β is a limit point of C_α.
nodes.title: Square sequence

nodes.summary: □_κ: a □_κ-sequence exists
nodes.title: Jensen's square principle

nodes.summary: The forcing method and the axioms that assert the existence of generic filters, such as Martin's axiom and the proper forcing axiom, together with combinatorial dichotomies like the open coloring axiom and the P-ideal dichotomy that follow from them.
nodes.title: Forcing and forcing axioms
Martin's axiom

nodes.summary: A partial order $(P, \le)$ has the countable chain condition (c.c.c.) if every antichain of $P$ is countable, where an antichain is a set of pairwise incompatible elements: no two distinct members of it have a common lower bound in $P$.
nodes.title: Countable chain condition

nodes.summary: A partial order $P$ is $\sigma$-centered if there is a map $c : P \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every finite set of elements $p$ with $c(p) = n$ has a common lower bound in $P$. Thus $P$ splits into countably many centered pieces $c^{-1}(n)$; the empty set is among the finite sets, so $P$ must be nonempty.
nodes.title: σ-centered partial orders

nodes.summary: For a cardinal $\kappa$, this is the statement that for every $\sigma$-centered partial order $P$, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at most $\kappa$ dense subsets of $P$ and every $p \in P$, there is a filter $G$ on $P$ with $p \in G$ that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$. Here $D \subseteq P$ is dense if every element of $P$ has an element of $D$ below it, and a filter is a nonempty upward closed subset of $P$ any…
nodes.title: Martin's axiom for σ-centered partial orders

nodes.summary: For a cardinal $\kappa$, $\mathrm{MA}(\kappa)$ is the statement that for every partial order $P$ with the countable chain condition, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at most $\kappa$ dense subsets of $P$ and every $p \in P$, there is a filter $G$ on $P$ with $p \in G$ that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$. Here $D \subseteq P$ is dense if every element of $P$ has an element of $D$ below it, and a filter is a…
nodes.title: Martin's axiom
Open coloring axiom

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space. A set $K \subseteq X \times X$ of ordered pairs is an open coloring of $X$ if $K$ is open in the product topology, symmetric ($(x, y) \in K$ implies $(y, x) \in K$) and irreflexive ($(x, x) \notin K$ for every $x \in X$).
nodes.title: Open coloring of a topological space

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a set and $K \subseteq X \times X$. A set $H \subseteq X$ is $K$-homogeneous if $(x, y) \in K$ for all distinct $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: Homogeneous set for a coloring

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a set and $K \subseteq X \times X$. A set $H \subseteq X$ is $K$-free if $(x, y) \notin K$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: Free set for a coloring

nodes.summary: Todorcevic's Open Coloring Axiom: for every open coloring of a second-countable space, either there is an uncountable homogeneous set, or the space is a countable union of free sets.
nodes.title: Open coloring axiom
P-ideal dichotomy

nodes.summary: For subsets $a$ and $b$ of a set $\alpha$, $a \subseteq^* b$ ($a$ is almost contained in $b$) if the difference $a \setminus b$ is finite.
nodes.title: Inclusion modulo finite

nodes.summary: A family $I$ of subsets of a set $\alpha$ is a P-ideal of countable sets if every member of $I$ is countable, every subset of a member of $I$ is in $I$, every finite subset of $\alpha$ is in $I$, $I$ is closed under binary unions, and for every sequence $(a_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of members of $I$ there is $b \in I$ with $a_n \subseteq^* b$ (that is, $a_n \setminus b$ is finite) for every $n$.
nodes.title: P-ideal of countable sets

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a family of subsets of a set $\alpha$. A set $X \subseteq \alpha$ is orthogonal to $I$ if $X \cap a$ is finite for every $a \in I$.
nodes.title: Orthogonality to a family of sets

nodes.summary: The P-ideal dichotomy (PID): for every P-ideal I of countable subsets of an uncountable set, either some uncountable set has all its countable subsets in I, or the whole set is a countable union of sets orthogonal to I.
nodes.title: P-ideal dichotomy
Proper forcing and the proper forcing axiom

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a set and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. The conditions in $M$ form the set $M_c$ of those $p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union belongs to $M$; informally, $M_c = M \cap \mathbb{P}$.
nodes.title: Conditions in a model

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a set and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. The sets of conditions in $M$ form the family $M_s$ of those $D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union belongs to $M$; informally, $M_s = M \cap \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$.
nodes.title: Sets of conditions in a model

nodes.summary: Two elements $p$ and $q$ of a partial order $\mathbb{P}$ are compatible if there is $r \in \mathbb{P}$ with $r \le p$ and $r \le q$.
nodes.title: Compatible conditions

nodes.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ of elements of a partial order $\mathbb{P}$ is predense below $q \in \mathbb{P}$ if for every $r \le q$ there is $a \in A$ such that $r$ and $a$ are compatible.
nodes.title: Predense below a condition

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial order and $M$ a subset of the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$. Write $M_c$ for the set of $p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in the disjoint union lies in $M$, and $M_s$ for the set of $D \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ whose copy lies in $M$. A condition $q \in \mathbb{P}$ is $(M, \mathbb{P})$-generic if for every $D \in M_s$ that is dense in $\mathbb{P}$ (every element of…
nodes.title: (M, ℙ)-generic conditions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial order and let $X$ be the disjoint union $\mathbb{P} \sqcup \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{P})$; for $M \subseteq X$ write $M_c$ for the set of $p \in \mathbb{P}$ whose copy in $X$ lies in $M$. Then $\mathbb{P}$ is proper if there is a club $C$ in $[X]^\omega$ such that for every $M \in C$ and every $p \in M_c$ there is an $(M, \mathbb{P})$-generic condition $q \le p$. Here a club in $[X]^\omega$…
nodes.title: Proper partial orders

nodes.summary: For every proper partial order $\mathbb{P}$, every family $\mathcal{D}$ of at most $\aleph_1$ dense subsets of $\mathbb{P}$, and every condition $p \in \mathbb{P}$, there is a filter $G \subseteq \mathbb{P}$ with $p \in G$ that meets every member of $\mathcal{D}$, that is, $G \cap D \neq \emptyset$ for every $D \in \mathcal{D}$.
nodes.title: Proper Forcing Axiom

nodes.summary: Order theory studies comparison relations, lattices, intervals, monotonicity, and order-complete constructions.
nodes.title: Order Theory

nodes.summary: Partial, strict and total orders, dense linear orders, monotone maps and sequences, and representations of finite posets.
nodes.title: Ordered sets

nodes.summary: A relation $R$ on a type $\alpha$ is a *dense linear order without endpoints* if it is a strict total order (irreflexive, transitive, and trichotomous: for all $a, b$, at least one of $R(a,b)$, $a = b$, $R(b,a)$ holds), it is dense (whenever $R(a,b)$, there is $c$ with $R(a,c)$ and $R(c,b)$), and it has no endpoints (for every $a$ there are $b$ and $b'$ with $R(b,a)$ and $R(a,b')$).
nodes.title: Dense linear order without endpoints
Monotone sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a preordered set. A sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is monotone (that is, $f(m) \le f(n)$ whenever $m \le n$) if and only if $f(n) \le f(n+1)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Successor criterion for monotone sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a preordered set. A sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ is antitone (that is, $f(n) \le f(m)$ whenever $m \le n$) if and only if $f(n+1) \le f(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Successor criterion for antitone sequences

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a preordered set and let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$ be a sequence. Then $f$ is monotone ($f(m) \le f(n)$ whenever $m \le n$) or antitone ($f(n) \le f(m)$ whenever $m \le n$) if and only if either $f(n) \le f(n+1)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, or $f(n+1) \le f(n)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Successor criterion for monotone or antitone sequences
Strict total orders

nodes.summary: A strict total order on a type $\alpha$ consists of a binary relation $<$ on $\alpha$ that is irreflexive (no $a < a$), transitive ($a < b$ and $b < c$ imply $a < c$) and total on distinct elements (if $a \ne b$, then $a < b$ or $b < a$). It models strict preference.
nodes.title: Strict total order

nodes.summary: Two strict total orders on a type $\alpha$ with the same relation are equal.
nodes.title: Strict total orders are determined by their relation

nodes.summary: Lattices and Boolean algebras, their representation theorems, and Boolean functions viewed as maps between Boolean lattices.
nodes.title: Lattices and Boolean algebras

nodes.summary: Every Boolean algebra $B$ embeds in a power set algebra: there are a set $X$ and an injective map $f$ from $B$ to the power set of $X$ such that $f(a \sqcup b) = f(a) \cup f(b)$ and $f(a \sqcap b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ for all $a, b \in B$, $f(\top) = X$ and $f(\bot) = \emptyset$.
nodes.title: Stone representation theorem
Lattice valuations and the Jaccard distance

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, is a modular valuation when $f(X) + f(Y) = f(X \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y)$ for all $X, Y \in L$.
nodes.title: Modular valuation

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ is strictly positive when $f(X) > 0$ for every $X \in L$.
nodes.title: Strictly positive valuation

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, satisfies the Gilbert condition when $f(X \vee Z) + f(Z \vee Y) + f(X \wedge Y) \ge f(X \wedge Z) + f(Z \wedge Y) + f(X \vee Y \vee Z)$ for all $X, Y, Z \in L$.
nodes.title: Gilbert condition

nodes.summary: For a function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$, the Jaccard distance of $X, Y \in L$ is $d_f(X, Y) = 1 - f(X \wedge Y) / f(X \vee Y)$.
nodes.title: Generalized Jaccard distance

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ on a lattice $L$ satisfies the Gilbert condition if and only if $f$ is a modular valuation and is monotone, that is, $X \le Y$ implies $f(X) \le f(Y)$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the Gilbert condition

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$, with join $\vee$ and meet $\wedge$. Then for all $X, Y \in L$ the Jaccard distance of $X$ and $Y$ with respect to $f$ is $d_f(X, Y) = (f(X \vee Y) - f(X \wedge Y)) / f(X \vee Y)$.
nodes.title: Jaccard distance as a single quotient

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive function on a lattice $L$ that satisfies the Gilbert condition, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then $d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.
nodes.title: Jaccard triangle inequality under the Gilbert condition

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon L \to \mathbb{R}$ be a strictly positive, monotone modular valuation on a lattice $L$, and let $d_f$ be the Jaccard distance of $f$. Then $d_f(U, W) + d_f(W, V) \ge d_f(U, V)$ for all $U, V, W \in L$.
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for the generalized Jaccard distance

nodes.summary: Least and greatest fixed points of monotone and Scott-continuous maps, Kleene iteration, and the complete partial orders that underlie denotational semantics.
nodes.title: Fixed points and domain theory
Least and greatest fixed points on finite sets

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ map subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$, and write $f^n$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $f$. Then $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is the set $f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$, obtained by applying $f$ to the empty set $|\alpha|$ times.
nodes.title: Least fixed point of a finset map by finite iteration

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ map subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$, and write $f^n$ for the $n$-fold iterate of $f$. Then $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is the set $f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$, obtained by applying $f$ to the whole of $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times.
nodes.title: Greatest fixed point of a finset map by finite iteration

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$ be the result of applying $f$ to $\emptyset$ $|\alpha|$ times. Then $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is a fixed point of $f$, that is,…
nodes.title: Finite iteration from the empty set reaches a fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be the result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. Then $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$ is a fixed point of $f$, that is, $f(\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)) = \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.
nodes.title: Finite iteration from the whole type reaches a fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$ be the result of applying $f$ to $\emptyset$ $|\alpha|$ times. If $Z \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies $f(Z) \subseteq Z$, then $\mathrm{lfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) \subseteq Z$.
nodes.title: The finite least fixed point lies in every pre-fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with $|\alpha|$ elements, let $f$ be a map from subsets of $\alpha$ to subsets of $\alpha$ that is monotone for inclusion, and let $\mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f) = f^{|\alpha|}(\alpha)$ be the result of applying $f$ to $\alpha$ $|\alpha|$ times. If $Z \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies $Z \subseteq f(Z)$, then $Z \subseteq \mathrm{gfp}_{\mathrm{fin}}(f)$.
nodes.title: Every post-fixed point lies in the finite greatest fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $f$ map finite subsets of $\alpha$ to finite subsets of $\alpha$, and let $F$ map predicates on $\alpha$ to predicates on $\alpha$. For a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$ write $P_Z$ for the predicate $t \mapsto t \in Z$, and suppose that for every finite $Z \subseteq \alpha$ and every $s \in \alpha$, $s \in f(Z)$ if and only if $F(P_Z)(s)$ holds. Write $f^n$ and $F^n$ for the $n$-fold…

For $Z \subseteq \alpha$ write $P_Z$ for the predicate $t \mapsto t \in Z$, and suppose that for every $Z \subseteq \alpha$ and every $s \in \alpha$, $s \in f(Z)$ if and only if $F(P_Z)(s)$ holds. Write $f^n$ and $F^n$ for the $n$-fold iterates and $\top$ for the…

Let $F$ be a map from predicates on $\alpha$ to predicates on $\alpha$ that is monotone for the pointwise order. For…

Let $F$ be a map from predicates on $\alpha$ to predicates on $\alpha$ that is monotone for the pointwise order. For $Z \subseteq \alpha$…

Scott-continuous maps and least fixed points

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders, and let $g$ be a map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise. If for every $b \in \beta$ the map $a \mapsto g(a)(b)$ is Scott-continuous, then $g$ is Scott-continuous. Here a map is Scott-continuous when it is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains.
nodes.title: Scott continuity into a function space is checked pointwise

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders and let $f : \alpha \times \beta \to \gamma$ be a Scott-continuous map, that is, a map that is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains. Its currying is the Scott-continuous map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise, that sends $a$ to the map $b \mapsto f(a, b)$.
nodes.title: Currying of Scott-continuous maps

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains. The least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ is the supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$, whose $n$-th term is the $n$-fold iterate $f^n(\bot)$.
nodes.title: Least fixed point of a Scott-continuous map

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains. Then the least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ satisfies $f(\operatorname{lfp} f) = \operatorname{lfp} f$.
nodes.title: The least fixed point is a fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains, and let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be the supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$. If $a \in D$ satisfies $f(a) \le a$, then $\operatorname{lfp} f \le a$.
nodes.title: The least fixed point lies below every prefixed point

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$. For a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$, that is, one that is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains, let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be its least fixed point. The map $f \mapsto \operatorname{lfp} f$, from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$, is Scott-continuous.
nodes.title: Scott continuity of the least-fixed-point operator

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$. The least-fixed-point operator, sending a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$ to its least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$, bundled as a Scott-continuous map from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$.
nodes.title: The least-fixed-point operator as a Scott-continuous map
Transitive closure of finite relations

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. For a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$, the set of $r$-successors of $Z$ is the finite set $\mathrm{post}_r(Z) = \{t \in \alpha \mid r(z, t) \text{ for some } z \in Z\}$.
nodes.title: Successors of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and write $\mathrm{post}_r(Z)$ for the set of $r$-successors of elements of a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$. For a finite set $A \subseteq \alpha$, the step map sends a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$ to $\mathrm{post}_r(A) \cup \mathrm{post}_r(Z)$.

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, the denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ is the least common multiple of the denominators (in lowest terms) of the nonzero coefficients of $P$; in particular $\operatorname{denom}(0) = 1$. Thus $\operatorname{denom}(P) = 1$ exactly when $P \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$.

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, its denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ equals $1$ if and only if, for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coefficient of $x^i$ in $P$ is an integer.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$ be an index type, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. The mixed differential of $p$ along the empty list of indices is $p$ itself.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$ be an index type, let $i \in \sigma$, let $L$ be a finite list of indices in $\sigma$, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. The mixed differential of $p$ along the list that starts with $i$ and continues with $L$ equals the mixed differential along $L$ of $p - \partial_i p$, where $\partial_i$ is the partial derivative with respect to $x_i$.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$ be an index type, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. If two finite lists $L$ and $L'$ of indices in $\sigma$ are permutations of each other, then the mixed differentials of $p$ along $L$ and along $L'$ are equal.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$ be an index type, let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$, and let $L$ and $L'$ be finite lists of indices in $\sigma$. The mixed differential of $p$ along the concatenation of $L$ followed by $L'$ equals the mixed differential along $L'$ of the mixed differential of $p$ along $L$.
nodes.title: Mixed differential along a concatenated list

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $i \in \sigma$, let $L$ be a finite list of indices in $\sigma$, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. Writing $\partial_i$ for the partial derivative with respect to $x_i$, the partial derivative $\partial_i$ of the mixed differential of $p$ along $L$ equals the mixed differential along $L$ of $\partial_i p$.

Newton polygon

nodes.summary: The map from exponent vectors of monomials in two variables to $\mathbb{R}^2$ sends $e = (e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ to the point $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Exponent vectors as points of the plane

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables $x_0, x_1$ over a commutative semiring $k$. The Newton support of $f$ is the set of exponent vectors $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of the monomials $x_0^{e_0} x_1^{e_1}$ with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Newton support

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$. The Newton polygon of $f$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the Newton support of $f$, the set of exponent vectors of the monomials with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Newton polygon

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological interior as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Interior of the Newton polygon

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the boundary of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological boundary in $\mathbb{R}^2$: the closure of the Newton polygon minus its interior.
nodes.title: Boundary of the Newton polygon

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, and let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. The restriction of $f$ to $\Gamma$ is the polynomial formed by the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\Gamma$; the other terms are dropped.
nodes.title: Restriction of a polynomial to a set of exponents

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$. A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ lies in the Newton support of $f$ if and only if $x$ is the exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of some monomial with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is contained in the Newton polygon of $f$.

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to the empty set, that is, the sum of the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\emptyset$, is the zero polynomial.

nodes.summary: The claim of Problem 79 of the Scottish Book for the plane is false: there is a polynomial map $P$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ to itself with a polynomial two-sided inverse that is not of the form $x \mapsto Ax + c$ with $A$ an invertible real $2 \times 2$ matrix and $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$. nodes.summary: For a commutative semiring $k$ and index types $\sigma$ and $\tau$, a regular function from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$ is a family $F = (F_t)_{t \in \tau}$ of polynomials in the variables $X_s$, $s \in \sigma$, with coefficients in $k$.

nodes.summary: The Jacobian of a regular function $F = (F_j)_{j \in \tau}$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$ is the $\tau \times \sigma$ matrix, with entries in the polynomial ring $k[X_i : i \in \sigma]$, whose entry in row $j$ and column $i$ is the formal partial derivative $\partial F_j / \partial X_i$.

nodes.summary: For regular functions $G$ from $k^\tau$ to $k^\iota$ and $F$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$, the composition $G \circ F$ is the regular function from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\iota$ whose $i$-th component, for $i \in \iota$, is the polynomial obtained from $G_i$ by substituting $F_t$ for the variable $X_t$ for every $t \in \tau$.
