nodes.summary: For every regular function $F$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$, composing $F$ with the identity regular function on $k^\sigma$, whose components are the variables $X_s$ for $s \in \sigma$, gives $F$, that is, $F \circ \mathrm{id} = F$.

nodes.summary: For regular functions $H$ from $k^\iota$ to $k^\kappa$, $G$ from $k^\tau$ to $k^\iota$ and $F$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$, we have $(H \circ G) \circ F = H \circ (G \circ F)$.

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a commutative semiring and let $S$ be a commutative $k$-algebra. nodes.summary: Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, with every coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant term $f(0) = 1$. If $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, then $f(x^2) \equiv f(x)\,f(-x) \pmod 4$ as polynomials, that is, the two polynomials have the same image in $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})[x]$.

Favard's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field. A family $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of polynomials over $R$ is formally orthogonal if there is an $R$-linear functional $L \colon R[x] \to R$ such that each $p_n$ has degree $n$, $L(p_n p_m) = 0$ whenever $n \ne m$, and $L(p_n^2) \ne 0$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: Formally orthogonal polynomial family

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field and let $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a formally orthogonal family of monic polynomials over $R$. Then there are sequences $(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$ such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Favard's theorem, forward direction

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a field and let $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a family of monic polynomials in $R[x]$. Then $(p_n)$ is formally orthogonal if and only if there are sequences $(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$ such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. The L1 norm of a polynomial $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ with respect to $v$ is the real number $\|p\|_v = \sum_i v(a_i)$, where the sum runs over the indices $i$ with $a_i \neq 0$.
nodes.title: L1 norm of a polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. For every polynomial $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$, the L1 norm $\|p\|_v$ of $p$ with respect to $v$ equals $\sum_{i \in S} v(a_i)$, where $S = \{ i : a_i \neq 0 \}$ is the support of $p$.

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Let $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ and let $n$ be the degree of $p$, with $n = 0$ when $p = 0$. Then the L1 norm of $p$ with respect to $v$ is $\|p\|_v = \sum_{i=0}^{n} v(a_i)$.
nodes.title: L1 norm as a sum up to the degree

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a nontrivial semiring (one with $0 \neq 1$) and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ is monic of degree $n$, then the L1 norm of $f$ with respect to $v$ is $\|f\|_v = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} v(a_i) + 1$.

nodes.summary: A complex polynomial $p$ is real-rooted if every element $z$ of its multiset of roots is real, that is, $\operatorname{Im} z = 0$.
nodes.title: Real-rooted polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a nonzero complex polynomial that is unchanged when complex conjugation is applied to each of its coefficients. If every root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im} z \le 0$, then $p$ is real-rooted.
nodes.title: Conjugation-invariant polynomials with roots in the closed lower half-plane are real-rooted

nodes.summary: For a complex polynomial $p$, let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part $\operatorname{Re} z$ of an element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$, with $\rho(p) = 0$ when that multiset is empty (as it is for nonzero constants and for $p = 0$).
nodes.title: Largest real part of a root

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of an element of its multiset of roots, or $0$ if that multiset is empty. Then every element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z \le \rho(p)$.
nodes.title: Real parts of roots are bounded by the largest one

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a complex polynomial whose multiset of roots is nonempty, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$. Then some root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z = \rho(p)$.

Stable polynomials

nodes.summary: A complex multivariate polynomial is stable if it has no zero when every variable lies in the open upper half-plane.
nodes.title: Stable polynomials

nodes.summary: A complex multivariate polynomial is real stable if it is stable and has real coefficients.
nodes.title: Real stable polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let $i \in \sigma$ and $x : \sigma \to R$. The univariate specialization of $p$ at $i$ and $x$ is the polynomial in $R[X]$ obtained from $p$ by substituting $X$ for $X_i$ and the constant $x_j$ for every $X_j$ with $j \ne i$; the value $x_i$ is not used.

nodes.title: Real-rootedness of univariate specializations of real stable polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then $p - \partial_i p$ is stable.
nodes.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves stability

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then $p - \partial_i p$ is real stable.
nodes.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves real stability

For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list, $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is stable.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list, $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is real stable.

Sturm's theorem

nodes.summary: For real polynomials $a$, $b$ and a natural number $n$, this is the list of polynomials defined recursively by: for $n = 0$ it is the one-entry list $(a)$; for fuel $n + 1$ it is $(a)$ if $b = 0$, and otherwise it is $a$ followed by the list for the pair $b$, $-(a \bmod b)$ with fuel $n$, where $a \bmod b$ is the remainder of $a$ on division by $b$.
nodes.title: Negated-remainder sequence with fuel

nodes.summary: The Sturm chain of a real polynomial $p$ is the list $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_m$ with $p_0 = p$, $p_1 = p'$ and $p_{k+1} = -(p_{k-1} \bmod p_k)$, the negated remainder of $p_{k-1}$ on division by $p_k$, where the list stops at $p_m$ as soon as the next entry would be $0$; thus $p_m$ is its last entry and, for $p \ne 0$, every entry is nonzero. For $p = 0$ the chain is the one-entry list $(0)$.
nodes.title: Sturm chain

nodes.summary: For a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of real numbers, let $y_1, \dots, y_m$ be the entries of the list that are nonzero, in their original order. The number of sign changes of the list is the number of indices $i$ with $1 \le i < m$ and $y_i y_{i+1} < 0$, that is, the number of adjacent pairs of opposite sign once the zeros are removed.
nodes.title: Number of sign changes in a list of reals

nodes.summary: For a real polynomial $p$ with Sturm chain $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_m$ and a real number $x$, $\sigma_p(x)$ is the number of sign changes, ignoring zeros, in the sequence of values $p_0(x), p_1(x), \dots, p_m(x)$.
nodes.title: Sturm sign-variation function

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a squarefree real polynomial and let $a < b$ be real numbers with $p(a) \ne 0$ and $p(b) \ne 0$. Then the number of distinct real roots $x$ of $p$ with $a < x < b$ equals $\sigma_p(a) - \sigma_p(b)$, where $\sigma_p$ is the Sturm sign-variation function of $p$ and the subtraction is truncated subtraction of natural numbers.

Levi decomposition

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over a field $K$ of characteristic zero, and let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Lie module over $L$ and $K$. Then every Lie submodule $W$ of $M$ has a complement: there is a Lie submodule $U$ of $M$ with $W \cap U = 0$ and $W + U = M$.
nodes.title: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field $K$ of characteristic zero, and let $\operatorname{rad}(L)$ be its radical, the largest solvable ideal of $L$. Then there is a semisimple Lie subalgebra $S$ of $L$ (a Levi factor) such that $L = \operatorname{rad}(L) \oplus S$ as $K$-vector spaces, that is, $\operatorname{rad}(L) + S = L$ and $\operatorname{rad}(L) \cap S = 0$.

nodes.summary: Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra $L$ over a field $K$ of characteristic zero has a faithful finite-dimensional representation: there are a natural number $n$ and an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras over $K$ from $L$ into the Lie algebra of $K$-linear endomorphisms of $K^n$ with the commutator bracket.

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $K$. Then $L$ has a faithful finite-dimensional representation: there are a finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over $K$ and an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras over $K$ from $L$ to the Lie algebra of $K$-linear endomorphisms of $V$ with the commutator bracket.

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. An ideal $P$ of $A$ is a Poisson prime when it is both a prime ideal and a Poisson ideal.

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. For an ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is the supremum, in the lattice of ideals of $A$, of the set of all Poisson ideals of $A$ contained in $J$.

Character degrees of symmetric groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. A homomorphism $\rho \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ is irreducible when $n \ge 1$ and every subspace $W$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that $\rho(g) v \in W$ for all $g \in G$ and all $v \in W$ is either $0$ or $\mathbb{C}^n$.
nodes.title: Irreducible complex matrix representations (Kourovka 16.67)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. Two homomorphisms $\rho, \sigma \colon G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ are equivalent when there is a single invertible matrix $P \in \mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ with $\sigma(g) = P \rho(g) P^{-1}$ for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Equivalent complex matrix representations (Kourovka 16.67)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$ there are a natural number $d$ and irreducible representations $\rho_1, \dots, \rho_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ into $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{C})$ that are pairwise inequivalent: $\rho_i$ and $\rho_j$ are not equivalent whenever $i \ne j$.
nodes.title: Moretó's conjecture on equal character degrees of symmetric groups

nodes.summary: Moretó's conjecture holds: for every natural number $k$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$ there are a natural number $d$ and irreducible representations $\rho_1, \dots, \rho_k$ of the symmetric group $S_n$ into $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{C})$ that are pairwise inequivalent.

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$ and functions $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, the convolution $f \ast g : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is defined by $(f \ast g)(x) = \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(y^{-1} x)$ for $x \in G$.

Frobenius group determinant

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, the group matrix of Dedekind and Frobenius is the $G \times G$ matrix over the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ whose entry at $(g, h)$ is the variable $x_{gh}$.
nodes.title: Group matrix

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, the group determinant $\Theta(G)$ is the determinant of the group matrix of $G$, the $G \times G$ matrix over $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ whose entry at $(g, h)$ is the variable $x_{gh}$; it is a polynomial in these variables.
nodes.title: Group determinant

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $r$ be the number of conjugacy classes of $G$. Then there exist polynomials $p_1, \dots, p_r$ in $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ such that each $p_j$ is irreducible, $p_i$ and $p_j$ are not associated for $i \neq j$, and the group determinant of $G$ equals $\prod_{j=1}^{r} p_j^{\deg p_j}$, where $\deg p_j$ is the total degree of $p_j$.
nodes.title: Frobenius determinant theorem

Irreducible characters and class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class function when it is constant on conjugacy classes, that is, $f(h g h^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$.
nodes.title: Class functions on a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. The space of class functions $G \to k$ is the $k$-linear subspace of the vector space of all functions $G \to k$, under pointwise addition and scalar multiplication, consisting of the class functions.
nodes.title: The space of class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every finite-dimensional representation $V$ of $G$ over $k$, the character of $V$, the function sending $g \in G$ to the trace of the linear map by which $g$ acts on $V$, is a class function on $G$.
nodes.title: Characters are class functions

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $f : G \to k$ be a class function with values in a set $k$. If $x, y \in G$ are conjugate, then $f(x) = f(y)$.
nodes.title: Class functions agree on conjugate elements

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a set, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. A function $f : G \to k$ is a class function if and only if there is a function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ such that $f(x) = q([x])$ for all $x \in G$.
nodes.title: Class functions factor through conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field, and write $[x]$ for the conjugacy class of $x \in G$. This is the $k$-linear isomorphism from the space of class functions $G \to k$ to the vector space of all functions from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ that sends a class function $f$ to the function $[x] \mapsto f(x)$; its inverse sends a function $q$ on conjugacy classes to the class function $x \mapsto q([x])$.
nodes.title: Class functions as functions on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every class function $f : G \to k$ and every $x \in G$, the function on conjugacy classes that corresponds to $f$ under the linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes the value $f(x)$ at the conjugacy class of $x$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a class function on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $k$ a field. For every function $q$ from the set of conjugacy classes of $G$ to $k$ and every $x \in G$, the class function that corresponds to $q$ under the inverse of the linear isomorphism between class functions and functions on conjugacy classes takes at $x$ the value of $q$ at the conjugacy class of $x$.
nodes.title: Lifting a function on conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $k$ a field. The space of class functions $G \to k$ is a $k$-vector space whose dimension equals the number of conjugacy classes of $G$.
nodes.title: Dimension of the space of class functions

Rational groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is rational if every element $g \in G$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$, where an element of infinite order has order $0$, so that only $k = 1$ is coprime to it. For finite groups this is the classical equivalent form of the condition that all ordinary characters of $G$ are rational-valued.
nodes.title: Rational groups, conjugacy form

nodes.summary: The conjecture that for every finite rational group $G$, every Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, viewed as a group in its own right, is rational. Here a group is rational if every element $g$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.

nodes.summary: There is a finite rational group with a Sylow $2$-subgroup that is not rational as a group in its own right. Here a group is rational if every element $g$ is conjugate to $g^k$ for every natural number $k$ coprime to the order of $g$.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime and $x \in G$. Then $x$ lies in the $p$-core $O_p(G)$ of $G$ if and only if, for every $g \in G$, the subgroup of $G$ generated by $x$ and $g x g^{-1}$ is a $p$-group, that is, every element of it has order a power of $p$.

reading_title.source: Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem

nodes.summary: Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem. Let $G$ be a finite group and let $t \in G$ be an involution ($t \neq 1$ and $t^2 = 1$) such that every conjugate $g t g^{-1}$ of $t$ that commutes with $t$ equals $t$. Then there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ of odd order such that $g t g^{-1} t^{-1} \in N$ for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Glauberman's $Z^*$-theorem

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, $O(G)$ is the join, in the lattice of subgroups of $G$, of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ such that every element of $N$ has finite odd order. In a periodic group this join is again a normal subgroup consisting of elements of odd order, so it is the largest such subgroup.
nodes.title: Odd core from normal subgroups of odd-order elements

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, let $O(G)$ be the join of all normal subgroups of $G$ all of whose elements have odd order. This is the statement that for every periodic group $G$ and every involution $i \in G$ such that $g^{-1} i g i$ has odd order for every $g \in G$, the image of $i$ in $G / O(G)$ is central, that is, $g i g^{-1} i^{-1} \in O(G)$ for every $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Borovik's question on involutions with odd-order products (Kourovka 11.13)

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, let $O(G)$ be the join of all normal subgroups of $G$ all of whose elements have odd order. There exist a periodic group $G$ and an involution $i \in G$ such that $g^{-1} i g i$ has odd order for every $g \in G$, but the image of $i$ in $G / O(G)$ is not central: $g i g^{-1} i^{-1} \notin O(G)$ for some $g \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 11.13 in the negative.

Fitting classes of supersoluble groups

nodes.summary: A class of groups is a property of groups (in the lowest type universe) that is closed under isomorphism: whenever a group $H$ has the property and $H$ is isomorphic to a group $K$, then $K$ has the property. Only the finite members of a class are used in Kourovka Problem 12.91.
nodes.title: Isomorphism-closed classes of groups (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups is a Fitting class (of finite groups) if, for every finite group $G$: whenever $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, every normal subgroup of $G$ belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$; and whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of $G$ that belong to $\mathfrak{X}$, the subgroup $N_1 N_2$ they generate belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Fitting classes (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble if it has a chain of subgroups $1 = G_0 \le G_1 \le \cdots \le G_k = G$, each normal in $G$, such that for every $i < k$ there is an element $x \in G_{i+1}$ with $G_{i+1} = \langle x \rangle G_i$; that is, every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Supersoluble groups (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is minimal normal if $N$ is a nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$ and every nontrivial normal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $M \le N$ equals $N$.
nodes.title: Minimal normal subgroups (Kourovka 12.91)

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups that is a Fitting class and all of whose finite members are supersoluble, every minimal normal subgroup of every finite group $G \in \mathfrak{X}$ is contained in the center of $G$.
nodes.title: Heineken's question on Fitting classes of supersoluble groups

nodes.summary: There exist a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups that is a Fitting class and all of whose finite members are supersoluble, a finite group $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, and a minimal normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ that is not contained in the center of $G$.

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a set of words in the free group on countably many generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$. A group $G$ satisfies the laws in $W$ when every homomorphism from this free group to $G$ sends every $w \in W$ to $1$. The groups satisfying $W$ form the variety defined by $W$, and every variety arises this way.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a class of groups and let $V$ and $K$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $V$ is $\mathfrak{X}$-maximal in $K$ if $V \le K$, $V$ lies in $\mathfrak{X}$, and no subgroup $W$ of $G$ with $V < W \le K$ lies in $\mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Maximal subgroups within a class of groups

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a class of groups and $G$ a group. A subgroup $V$ of $G$ is an $\mathfrak{X}$-injector of $G$ if, for every subnormal subgroup $N$ of $G$, the intersection $V \cap N$ is $\mathfrak{X}$-maximal in $N$.

nodes.summary: For classes of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$, the class $\mathfrak{X}$ is included in $\mathfrak{Y}$, written $\mathfrak{X} \subseteq \mathfrak{Y}$, if every group that belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$ also belongs to $\mathfrak{Y}$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of group classes

nodes.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is a complete lattice of formations if it is nonempty, every member of $\Theta$ is a formation, for every nonempty subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ the intersection of the classes in $S$ (the class of groups belonging to every member of $S$) belongs to $\Theta$, and $\Theta$ has a member that contains every member of $\Theta$.
nodes.title: Complete lattices of formations

nodes.summary: Let $\Theta$ and $S$ be sets of classes of groups. A class $\mathfrak{J}$ is the join of $S$ in $\Theta$ if $\mathfrak{J} \in \Theta$, every member of $S$ is contained in $\mathfrak{J}$, and $\mathfrak{J}$ is contained in every member of $\Theta$ that contains every member of $S$.
nodes.title: Joins in a set of group classes

nodes.summary: Let $\Theta$ be a set of classes of groups and $\mathfrak{A}$ a class of groups. Then $\mathfrak{A}$ is compact in $\Theta$ if, for every subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ and every join $\mathfrak{J}$ of $S$ in $\Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{J}$, there are a finite subset $S_1 \subseteq S$ and a join $\mathfrak{J}_1$ of $S_1$ in $\Theta$ with $\mathfrak{A} \subseteq \mathfrak{J}_1$.
nodes.title: Compact elements of a set of group classes

nodes.summary: A set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is algebraic if every member $\mathfrak{A}$ of $\Theta$ is the join in $\Theta$ of some subset $S \subseteq \Theta$ all of whose members are compact in $\Theta$.
nodes.title: Algebraic sets of group classes

nodes.summary: The proposition that some set $\Theta$ of classes of groups is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups and is not algebraic.

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups that is not modular, joins being least upper bounds in the lattice and meets being intersections.

nodes.summary: There is a set $\Theta$ of classes of groups that is a complete lattice of formations of finite groups and is not algebraic; that is, Kourovka Problem 18.92(a) has a positive answer.

For formations $\mathfrak F_1$ and $\mathfrak F_2$ it is their meet in the lattice of formations.

nodes.summary: For every finite modular lattice $L$ there is an injective map $f$ from $L$ to the formations of finite groups such that, for all $a, b \in L$, $f(a \wedge b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ and $f(a \vee b)$ is the smallest formation containing $f(a) \cup f(b)$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.51 (Skiba): finite modular lattices embed in the lattice of formations

nodes.summary: There is a finite modular lattice $L$ that admits no injective map $f$ from $L$ to the formations of finite groups such that, for all $a, b \in L$, $f(a \wedge b) = f(a) \cap f(b)$ and $f(a \vee b)$ is the smallest formation containing $f(a) \cup f(b)$. This answers Kourovka Problem 13.51 (Skiba) in the negative.
nodes.title: Not every finite modular lattice embeds in the lattice of formations

nodes.summary: For classes $\mathfrak{F}$ and $\mathfrak{G}$ of finite groups, $\mathfrak{F} \subseteq \mathfrak{G}$ means that every finite group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{G}$.

nodes.title: Local formation of finite groups

nodes.summary: For a class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups and a finite group $G$, the $\mathfrak{F}$-residual $G^{\mathfrak{F}}$ is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $G$ with $G/N \in \mathfrak{F}$.
nodes.title: Residual of a finite group with respect to a class

nodes.summary: A class of finite groups is given by its membership predicate: a proposition about each finite group, true exactly for the members of the class.
nodes.title: Classes of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation if it is closed under isomorphism, contains the trivial group, contains $G/N$ whenever it contains $G$ and $N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$, and is closed under subdirect products: if $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with $G/N_1 \in X$ and $G/N_2 \in X$, then $G/(N_1 \cap N_2) \in X$.
nodes.title: Formations of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: A class $X$ of finite groups is a formation of nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ if $X$ is a formation and every group $G$ in $X$ is nilpotent of class at most $4$, that is, the fourth term $\zeta_4(G)$ of the upper central series of $G$ is all of $G$.
nodes.title: Formations of nilpotent groups of class at most 4

nodes.summary: The meet of two classes $X$ and $Y$ of finite groups is their intersection $X \cap Y$: the class of finite groups that belong to both $X$ and $Y$.
nodes.title: Intersection of classes of finite groups (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: For classes $X$ and $Y$ of finite groups, the formation generated by $X \cup Y$ is the class of finite groups that belong to every formation containing both $X$ and $Y$. For formations $X$ and $Y$ it is their join in the lattice of formations.
nodes.title: Formation generated by two classes (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: For all formations $A$, $B$, $C$ of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$, a finite group lies in $A \cap (B \vee C)$ if and only if it lies in $(A \cap B) \vee (A \cap C)$, where $X \vee Y$ denotes the formation generated by $X \cup Y$. That is, the lattice of formations of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ is distributive (A. N. Skiba).
nodes.title: The distributivity question for nilpotent class-4 formations (Kourovka 10.56)

nodes.summary: There exist formations $A$, $B$, $C$ of finite nilpotent groups of class at most $4$ such that the classes $A \cap (B \vee C)$ and $(A \cap B) \vee (A \cap C)$ differ, that is, some finite group lies in exactly one of them; here $X \vee Y$ denotes the formation generated by $X \cup Y$, the intersection of all formations containing $X$ and $Y$.
nodes.title: The lattice of nilpotent class-4 formations is not distributive (Kourovka 10.56)
Radical hereditary formations

nodes.summary: A class of groups $X$ is a property of groups that is invariant under isomorphism: if a group $H$ belongs to $X$ and $K$ is a group isomorphic to $H$, then $K$ belongs to $X$.
nodes.title: Isomorphism-closed class of groups

nodes.summary: For a class of groups $X$, a group $G$ and a subgroup $N$ of $G$, this holds when $N$ is normal in $G$ and the quotient group $G/N$ belongs to $X$.
nodes.title: Quotient lying in a class

nodes.summary: A class of groups $X$ is a formation if it contains the trivial group, for every finite group $G$ in $X$ and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ the quotient $G/N$ belongs to $X$, and for every finite group $G$ with normal subgroups $N_1, N_2$ such that $G/N_1$ and $G/N_2$ belong to $X$, the quotient $G/(N_1 \cap N_2)$ belongs to $X$.
nodes.title: Formation of finite groups

nodes.summary: A class of groups $X$ is radical if, for every finite group $G$, every normal subgroup of $G$ belongs to $X$ whenever $G$ does, and whenever $N_1, N_2$ are normal subgroups of $G$ that belong to $X$, their product $N_1 N_2$ belongs to $X$.
nodes.title: Radical (Fitting) class

nodes.summary: A class of groups $X$ is hereditary if every subgroup of a finite group in $X$ belongs to $X$.
nodes.title: Hereditary class of groups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $R$ of a group $G$ is the soluble radical of $G$ if $R$ is a soluble normal subgroup of $G$ that contains every soluble normal subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Soluble radical

nodes.summary: A class of groups $X$ is solubly saturated (a composition class) if, for every finite group $G$ with soluble radical $R$, whenever the Frattini subgroup $\Phi(R)$ of $R$ is normal in $G$ and $G/\Phi(R)$ belongs to $X$, the group $G$ belongs to $X$.
nodes.title: Solubly saturated class

nodes.summary: The statement that every radical hereditary formation of finite groups is a composition formation: every class of groups that is a formation, a radical class and a hereditary class is solubly saturated.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.7 (Vasil'ev)

nodes.summary: It is not true that every radical hereditary formation of finite groups is a composition formation: some class of groups that is a formation, a radical class and a hereditary class is not solubly saturated.
nodes.title: Radical hereditary formations need not be composition formations
Subformations of the formation generated by a group

nodes.summary: A class of finite groups is a predicate on finite groups: it assigns to every finite group $G$ a proposition, read as "$G$ belongs to the class". The class need not be closed under isomorphism.
nodes.title: Classes of finite groups

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{F}$ of finite groups is a formation if it is closed under homomorphic images (whenever $f \colon G \to H$ is a surjective homomorphism of finite groups and $G \in \mathfrak{F}$, then $H \in \mathfrak{F}$) and under finite subdirect products (whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of a finite group $G$ with $G / N_1 \in \mathfrak{F}$ and $G / N_2 \in \mathfrak{F}$, then…
nodes.title: Formations of finite groups, possibly empty

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$, the formation generated by $G$ is the class of finite groups $H$ such that $H$ belongs to every formation that contains $G$; that is, it is the intersection of all formations containing $G$.
nodes.title: Formation generated by a finite group

nodes.summary: The statement (V. A. Vedernikov) that for every finite group $G$ only finitely many formations of finite groups are contained in the formation generated by $G$. Here formations may be empty, and a formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is contained in the formation generated by $G$ when every finite group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to the formation generated by $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.31 for finite groups

nodes.summary: There is a finite group $G$ such that infinitely many formations are contained in the formation generated by $G$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 16.31 is negative, even for finite $G$.
nodes.title: The formation generated by a finite group can have infinitely many subformations
Subgroup functors and closed classes of groups

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups is a predicate on finite groups $G$ (with carrier in the lowest type universe, together with their group structure); the groups satisfying it are the members of the class, written $G \in \mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Classes of finite groups (Kourovka 16.82 setting)

nodes.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups is closed when it contains at least one group and is closed under homomorphic images, subgroups and direct products: if $G \in \mathfrak{X}$ and $f : G \to H$ is a surjective homomorphism onto a finite group $H$, then $H \in \mathfrak{X}$; every subgroup of a group in $\mathfrak{X}$ lies in $\mathfrak{X}$; and if $G, H \in \mathfrak{X}$, then $G \times H \in \mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Closed classes of finite groups

nodes.summary: A subgroup assignment $\tau$ assigns to every finite group $G$ (with carrier in the lowest type universe) a set $\tau(G)$ of subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Subgroup assignments

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a class of finite groups. A subgroup assignment $\tau$ is a closed subgroup functor on $\mathfrak{X}$ (A. N. Skiba) when the following three conditions hold. For every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, $G \in \tau(G)$. For every surjective homomorphism $\varphi : A \to B$ with $A, B \in \mathfrak{X}$, $\varphi(H) \in \tau(B)$ for every $H \in \tau(A)$ and $\varphi^{-1}(T) \in \tau(A)$ for every…
nodes.title: Closed subgroup functors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a class of finite groups. For subgroup assignments $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$, $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ when $\tau_1(G) \subseteq \tau_2(G)$ for every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. This is the order of the lattice $F(\mathfrak{X})$ of closed subgroup functors on $\mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Order on subgroup functors

nodes.summary: For a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups, $\pi(\mathfrak{X})$ is the set of primes $p$ that divide the order of some group in $\mathfrak{X}$.
nodes.title: Prime divisors of a class of finite groups

nodes.summary: For a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups, let $\pi(\mathfrak{X})$ be the set of primes dividing the order of some group in $\mathfrak{X}$, and for subgroup assignments $\tau_1, \tau_2$ write $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ when $\tau_1(G) \subseteq \tau_2(G)$ for every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. There is a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups that contains at least one group, is closed under homomorphic…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.82 (Skiba)

nodes.summary: For a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups, let $\pi(\mathfrak{X})$ be the set of primes dividing the order of some group in $\mathfrak{X}$, and for subgroup assignments $\tau_1, \tau_2$ write $\tau_1 \le \tau_2$ on $\mathfrak{X}$ when $\tau_1(G) \subseteq \tau_2(G)$ for every $G \in \mathfrak{X}$. There is no class $\mathfrak{X}$ of finite groups that contains at least one group, is closed under homomorphic…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.82 has a negative answer
Abnormal supersoluble factorizations

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble if there are a natural number $k$ and subgroups $1 = S_0 \le S_1 \le \cdots \le S_k = G$, each normal in $G$, such that for every $i < k$ we have $S_i \le S_{i+1}$ and there is an element $x \in S_{i+1}$ such that $S_{i+1}$ is generated by $x$ and $S_i$; that is, every factor $S_{i+1}/S_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Supersoluble groups via cyclic normal series

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is abnormal in $G$ if every element $g \in G$ lies in the subgroup generated by $H$ and its conjugate $gHg^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Abnormal subgroup

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite group $G$ and all subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$ that are abnormal in $G$ and supersoluble, if $G = AB = BC = CA$ as sets, then $G$ is supersoluble.
nodes.title: Abnormal supersoluble trifactorizations (Kourovka 19.100)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be subgroups of $G$, each abnormal in $G$ and supersoluble, such that $G = AB = BC = CA$ as sets. Then $G$ is supersoluble.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.100 has a positive answer
Alperin groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is an Alperin group when, for all $x, y \in G$, the derived subgroup $[H, H]$ of the subgroup $H = \langle x, y \rangle$ generated by $x$ and $y$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Alperin group

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that every finite Alperin group $G$ has derived length at most $6$, that is, its sixth derived subgroup $G^{(6)}$ is trivial. Here $G$ is an Alperin group when, for all $x, y \in G$, the derived subgroup of the subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$ generated by $x$ and $y$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.33 on the derived length of finite Alperin groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group in which, for all $x, y \in G$, the derived subgroup of the subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$ generated by $x$ and $y$ is cyclic (an Alperin group). Then the sixth derived subgroup $G^{(6)}$ of $G$ is trivial, that is, $G$ has derived length at most $6$.
nodes.title: Finite Alperin groups have derived length at most six
Products of maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a finite group $G$ that is not soluble such that $G = MN$ for every two maximal subgroups $M$ and $N$ of $G$ that are not conjugate in $G$. Here $MN$ is the set of products $mn$ with $m \in M$ and $n \in N$.
nodes.title: Non-soluble products of non-conjugate maximal subgroups (Kourovka 10.34, Monakhov)

nodes.summary: There is no finite group $G$ that is not soluble such that $G = MN$ for every two maximal subgroups $M$ and $N$ of $G$ that are not conjugate in $G$; here $MN$ is the set of products $mn$ with $m \in M$ and $n \in N$. This answers Kourovka Problem 10.34 in the negative.
nodes.title: Finite groups that are the product of every two non-conjugate maximal subgroups are soluble
Supersolubility criteria

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble when it has a series $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ of subgroups, each normal in $G$, such that every factor $H_{i+1}/H_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Supersoluble group (Kourovka 15.81)

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ that is not supersoluble has, for some prime $p$, a non-cyclic Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ with a maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ that has no proper complement in $G$, that is, there is no subgroup $K \ne G$ with $MK = G$ and $M \cap K = 1$.
nodes.title: Uncomplemented maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups (Kourovka 15.81, Skiba)

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ that is not supersoluble, there are a prime $p$ and a non-cyclic Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ of $G$ with a maximal subgroup $M$ of $P$ that has no proper complement in $G$: there is no subgroup $K \ne G$ with $MK = G$ and $M \cap K = 1$. This answers Kourovka Problem 15.81 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Finite non-supersoluble groups have uncomplemented maximal subgroups of Sylow subgroups
σ-solubility, σ-nilpotency and σ-subnormality

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A / B$ is a chief factor of $G$ if $A$ and $B$ are normal in $G$, $B < A$, and every normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $B \le N \le A$ equals $B$ or $A$.
nodes.title: Chief factors

parts: Groups of Fitting height at most
reading_title.source: Groups of Fitting height at most $h$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $h$, a group $G$ has Fitting height (nilpotent length) at most $h$ if there are normal subgroups $1 = G_0 \le G_1 \le \cdots \le G_h = G$ of $G$ such that for every $i < h$ some term of the lower central series of $G_{i+1}$ lies in $G_i$, that is, $G_{i+1} / G_i$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Groups of Fitting height at most $h$

nodes.summary: A group $S$ is a composition factor of a group $K$ if $S$ is simple and some subnormal subgroup $H$ of $K$ has a surjective homomorphism onto $S$.
nodes.title: Composition factors via subnormal subgroups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is conjugacy separable if any two elements $x, y \in G$ whose images are conjugate in every quotient $G / N$ by a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index (that is, $g x g^{-1} y^{-1} \in N$ for some $g \in G$) are conjugate in $G$.
nodes.title: Conjugacy separable groups

reading_title.source: Residually finite $p$-groups

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ is residually a finite $p$-group if every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ lies outside some normal subgroup of $G$ whose index is $p^k$ for some $k \ge 0$, where an infinite index counts as $0$.
nodes.title: Residually finite $p$-groups

nodes.summary: For groups $A$ and $B$, let $A \wr_r B = A^B \rtimes B$ be the regular (unrestricted) wreath product, where $A^B$ is the group of all functions $f : B \to A$ and $b \in B$ acts on it by $(b \cdot f)(x) = f(b^{-1} x)$. The restricted wreath product $A \wr B$ is the subgroup of $A \wr_r B$ generated by the elements $(f, b)$ whose function part $f$ has finite support, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for only finitely many…
nodes.title: Restricted wreath product

nodes.summary: A family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers is a partition of the primes if every $\sigma_i$ is a nonempty set of primes, $\sigma_i$ and $\sigma_j$ are disjoint whenever $i \ne j$, and every prime lies in some $\sigma_i$.
nodes.title: Partitions of the primes

reading_title.source: $\sigma$-primary numbers

nodes.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a natural number $n$ is $\sigma$-primary if there is an index $i$ such that every prime divisor of $n$ lies in $\sigma_i$. For $n = 0$ this means that some $\sigma_i$ contains every prime.
nodes.title: $\sigma$-primary numbers

reading_title.source: $\sigma$-subnormal subgroups

nodes.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$ if there is a chain of subgroups $A = A_0 \le A_1 \le \cdots \le A_n = G$ such that for every $i < n$ either $A_i$ is normal in $A_{i+1}$, or the index in $A_{i+1}$ of the normal core of $A_i$ in $A_{i+1}$ is $\sigma$-primary (an infinite index counts as $0$).
nodes.title: $\sigma$-subnormal subgroups

reading_title.source: $\sigma$-nilpotent groups

nodes.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a group $G$ is $\sigma$-nilpotent if it is the internal direct product of finitely many normal subgroups $H_1, \dots, H_t$ whose orders are $\sigma$-primary (the order of an infinite subgroup counts as $0$): the $H_k$ generate $G$, and each $H_k$ meets the subgroup generated by the others trivially.
nodes.title: $\sigma$-nilpotent groups

reading_title.source: $\sigma$-soluble groups

nodes.summary: For a family $\sigma = (\sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ of sets of natural numbers, a group $G$ is $\sigma$-soluble if for every chief factor $A / B$ of $G$ the index $|A : B|$ is $\sigma$-primary (an infinite index counts as $0$).
nodes.title: $\sigma$-soluble groups

reading_title.source: Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question (Kourovka 19.84)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the set of primes, every finite group $G$ and every subgroup $A$ of $G$, if $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x = xAx^{-1}$ for every $x \in G$, then $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$.
nodes.title: Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question (Kourovka 19.84)

reading_title.source: A counterexample to Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 19.84 is false: there are a partition $\sigma$ of the set of primes, a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $A$ of $G$ such that $A$ is $\sigma$-subnormal in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x = xAx^{-1}$ for every $x \in G$, but $A$ is not $\sigma$-subnormal in $G$.
nodes.title: A counterexample to Skiba's $\sigma$-subnormality question
Frattini and complemented chief factors

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A/B$ is a Frattini chief factor of $G$ when $A/B$ is a chief factor of $G$ and $A$ is contained in every maximal subgroup of $G$ that contains $B$; equivalently, $A/B \le \Phi(G/B)$, where $\Phi$ denotes the Frattini subgroup.
nodes.title: Frattini chief factor

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of a group $G$, $A/B$ is a complemented chief factor of $G$ when $A/B$ is a chief factor of $G$ and some subgroup $M$ of $G$ satisfies $\langle M, A \rangle = G$ and $M \cap A = B$ (as $A$ is normal, the first condition says $MA = G$).
nodes.title: Complemented chief factor

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and every subgroup $H$ of $G$ that covers every Frattini chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is, $A \le \langle H, B \rangle$ (which is $HB$, as $B$ is normal), and avoids every complemented chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is, $H \cap A \le B$, there are $x, y \in G$ such that $H \cap H^x \cap H^y = H_G$, where $H^x = xHx^{-1}$ and $H_G$ is the normal core of $H$,…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.38

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a subgroup of a finite soluble group $G$. Suppose that $H$ covers every Frattini chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is, $A \le \langle H, B \rangle$ (which is $HB$, as $B$ is normal), and avoids every complemented chief factor $A/B$ of $G$, that is, $H \cap A \le B$. Then there are $x, y \in G$ such that $H \cap H^x \cap H^y = H_G$, where $H^x = xHx^{-1}$ and $H_G$ is the normal core of $H$, the largest…
nodes.title: Kamornikov–Shemetkova theorem (Kourovka Problem 19.38)
Schmidt subgroups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $M$ of a group $G$ is minimal non-nilpotent if $M$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $M$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Minimal non-nilpotent subgroup

nodes.summary: The statement that if $H$ is a subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$, then the quotient $H/H_G$ is nilpotent, where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.
nodes.title: Subgroups permuting with all minimal non-nilpotent subgroups (Kourovka 17.56)

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $H$ of $G$ with $HM = MH$ (as sets of products) for every minimal non-nilpotent subgroup $M$ of $G$ such that the quotient $H/H_G$ is not nilpotent, where the normal core $H_G$ is the largest normal subgroup of $G$ contained in $H$.
nodes.title: Permutability with minimal non-nilpotent subgroups does not force a nilpotent core quotient

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Schmidt subgroup when $H$ is not nilpotent but every proper subgroup of $H$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Schmidt subgroup

reading_title.source: $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal in $G$ when $H = G$ or there is a chain of subgroups $H = H_0 < H_1 < \cdots < H_n = G$ in which every index $|H_i : H_{i-1}|$ is a prime number.
nodes.title: $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal subgroup

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. The problem is due to A. F. Vasil'ev, T. I. Vasil'eva and V. N. Tyutyanov.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 18.30

reading_title.source: Finite groups with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are soluble

nodes.summary: Every finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal is soluble. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 18.30 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Finite groups with $\mathbb{P}$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are soluble

nodes.summary: The statement that for every partition $\sigma$ of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks and every finite group $G$ in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal, $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. The problem is due to A. N. Skiba.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 19.85

reading_title.source: Finite groups with $\sigma$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are $\sigma$-nilpotent-by-cyclic

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a partition of the set of all primes into nonempty pairwise disjoint blocks, and let $G$ be a finite group in which every Schmidt subgroup is $\sigma$-subnormal. Then $G$ has a normal $\sigma$-nilpotent subgroup $N$ such that $G / N$ is cyclic: there is $g \in G$ such that every $x \in G$ satisfies $x g^{-k} \in N$ for some integer $k$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 19.85 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Finite groups with $\sigma$-subnormal Schmidt subgroups are $\sigma$-nilpotent-by-cyclic
Supersoluble maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble when there are a natural number $n$ and elements $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1}$ of $G$ that generate $G$ such that, for every $i \le n$, the subgroup $G_i = \langle g_j : j < i \rangle$ is normal in $G$.
nodes.title: Supersoluble group (generator form)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ satisfies Monakhov's condition when every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime factors of the order of $X$ if $X$ is finite, and is empty if $X$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Monakhov's condition

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has a chief factor of rank greater than a natural number $r$ when there are a chief factor $A / B$ of $G$, a prime $p$ and a natural number $k > r$ such that the index $[A : B]$ equals $p^k$.
nodes.title: Chief factor of rank above a bound

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ has $p$-length at most $1$ when there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $N$ is finite of order not divisible by $p$, the index $[M : N]$ equals $p^k$ for some natural number $k$ (an infinite index counting as $0$), and the index $[G : M]$ is finite and not divisible by $p$.
nodes.title: Groups of p-length at most one

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian simple group $S$ there is a finite group $G$ such that $S$ is a composition factor of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 19.55(a) (Monakhov): every non-abelian simple group occurs

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every natural number $h$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ whose Fitting height is greater than $h$ and in which every maximal subgroup $M$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 19.55(b) (Monakhov): unbounded Fitting height

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $r$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ satisfying Monakhov's condition (every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime divisors of $|X|$) that has a chief factor $A/B$ of order $p^k$ for some prime $p$ and some $k > r$. This is the answer to Kourovka 19.55(b) for the rank.
nodes.title: Unbounded chief-factor rank under Monakhov's condition (the claim)

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite soluble group $G$ in which every maximal subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$, and for every prime $p$, the group $G$ has $p$-length at most $1$: there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $p$ does not divide $|N|$, the index $[M : N]$ is a power of $p$, and $p$ does not divide $[G : M]$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 19.55(b) (Monakhov): p-length at most one

nodes.summary: For every finite non-abelian simple group $S$ there is a finite group $G$ such that $S$ is a composition factor of $G$ and every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.
nodes.title: Moretó: every non-abelian simple group occurs in Kourovka 19.55(a)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $h$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ whose Fitting height is greater than $h$ and in which every maximal subgroup $M$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$.
nodes.title: Moretó: soluble groups in Kourovka 19.55 have unbounded Fitting height

nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$ there is a finite soluble group $G$ such that every maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $\pi(M) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of prime divisors of $|X|$, and $G$ has a chief factor $A/B$ (normal subgroups $B < A$ of $G$ with no normal subgroup of $G$ strictly between them) of order $p^k$ for some prime $p$ and some $k > r$.
nodes.title: Unbounded chief-factor rank under Monakhov's condition

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite soluble group in which every maximal subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ is supersoluble, where $\pi(X)$ is the set of primes dividing the order of $X$. Then for every prime $p$ the group $G$ has $p$-length at most $1$: there are normal subgroups $N \le M$ of $G$ such that $p$ does not divide $|N|$, the index $[M : N]$ is a power of $p$, and $p$ does not divide $[G : M]$.
nodes.title: Moretó: soluble groups in Kourovka 19.55 have p-length at most one

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is $p$-soluble when it has a chain of subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$, each normal in the next, such that for every $i < n$ the relative index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ (taken to be $0$ when it is infinite) is a power of $p$ or is coprime to $p$. nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree are the finite words over the alphabet $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$. A permutation $f$ of this set of words is a tree automorphism when, for all words $u$ and $v$, writing $|u|$ for the length of $u$ and $uv$ for the concatenation of $u$ and $v$, the word $f(u)$ has length $|u|$ and the first $|u|$ letters of $f(uv)$ form $f(u)$.

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a permutation of the finite words over $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$ (the vertices of the $d$-regular rooted tree) and let $u$ be a word, of length $|u|$. The section (state) of $f$ at $u$ is the map sending each word $w$ to the word obtained from $f(uw)$ by deleting its first $|u|$ letters, where $uw$ is the concatenation of $u$ and $w$.

Thompson's group F

reading_title.source: Relators of Thompson's group $F$

nodes.summary: In the free group on two generators $x_0$ and $x_1$, this is the set of the two elements $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-1} x_1 x_0]$ and $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-2} x_1 x_0^2]$, where $[a, b] = a b a^{-1} b^{-1}$. They are the relators of the standard presentation of Thompson's group $F$.
nodes.title: Relators of Thompson's group $F$

reading_title.source: Thompson's group $F$ by its standard presentation

nodes.summary: Thompson's group $F$ is the group with generators $x_0, x_1$ and relations $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-1} x_1 x_0] = 1$ and $[x_0 x_1^{-1}, x_0^{-2} x_1 x_0^2] = 1$, where $[a, b] = a b a^{-1} b^{-1}$; that is, the quotient of the free group on $x_0, x_1$ by the normal subgroup generated by these two relators.
nodes.title: Thompson's group $F$ by its standard presentation

reading_title.source: Howson property for Thompson's group $F$

nodes.summary: The statement that Thompson's group $F$ has the Howson property: for all finitely generated subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $F$, the intersection $H \cap K$ is finitely generated.

nodes.summary: It is not the case that the intersection of any two finitely generated subgroups of Thompson's group $F$ is finitely generated: there are finitely generated subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $F$ such that $H \cap K$ is not finitely generated.

Amenable groups

nodes.summary: A discrete group $G$ is *amenable* if it satisfies the Følner condition: for every finite subset $K \subseteq G$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a finite nonempty subset $F \subseteq G$ such that $|sF \mathbin{\triangle} F| / |F| < \varepsilon$ for every $s \in K$. Here $sF = \{sf : f \in F\}$ is the left translate of $F$ by $s$, $\triangle$ is symmetric difference and $|\cdot|$ is cardinality.
nodes.title: Amenable group (Følner condition)

nodes.summary: Every finite group is amenable.
nodes.title: Finite groups are amenable

nodes.summary: Every group with at most one element is amenable; the set $F = \{1\}$ witnesses the Følner condition.
nodes.title: Trivial groups are amenable
Elementary amenable groups

nodes.summary: The class of elementary amenable groups is the smallest class of groups that contains every finite group and every abelian group and is closed under isomorphisms, subgroups, quotients, extensions and directed unions. Closure under extensions means that a group $G$ with a normal subgroup $N$ is elementary amenable whenever $N$ and $G/N$ are; closure under directed unions means that $G$ is elementary amenable…
nodes.title: Elementary amenable groups

nodes.summary: The statement that every finitely presented elementary amenable group $G$ is solvable-by-finite, that is, $G$ has a solvable subgroup of finite index.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.52 (Linnell–Schick)

nodes.summary: There is a finitely presented elementary amenable group $G$ that is not solvable-by-finite: no subgroup of finite index in $G$ is solvable. This answers Kourovka Problem 16.52 (P. Linnell, T. Schick) in the negative.

Følner sets and polynomial growth

nodes.summary: For a finite subset $S$ of a group $\Gamma$ and a natural number $n$, the ball $B_S(n)$ of radius $n$ is the set of products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$, the empty product $1$ included.
nodes.title: Ball in the word metric

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite subset of a group $\Gamma$, and let $B_S(n)$ be the ball of radius $n$ for $S$, the set of products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. Then $\Gamma$ has polynomial growth with respect to $S$ if there are natural numbers $C$ and $d$ such that for every natural number $n$ the ball $B_S(n)$ has at most $C\,(n + 1)^d$ elements.

nodes.summary: For a group $\Gamma$ and finite subsets $S$ and $F$ of $\Gamma$, the boundary of $F$ with respect to $S$ is the set $\partial F = \{\gamma \in \Gamma \setminus F : \gamma s \in F \text{ for some } s \in S\}$.

Growth of groups

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$. The growth function $\gamma_P$ of $P$ assigns to each natural number $n$ the number of elements $g \in G$ whose word length with respect to $P$ is at most $n$, that is, the cardinality of the ball of radius $n$ in the word metric of $P$; when this ball is infinite, $\gamma_P(n)$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Growth function of a generating family

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$, with growth function $\gamma_P$. Then $P$ has polynomial growth if, for every natural number $n$, the ball of radius $n$ (the set of elements of $G$ of word length at most $n$ with respect to $P$) is finite, and there are natural numbers $C$ and $d$ such that $\gamma_P(n) \le C (n + 1)^d$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a group $G$, the growth function of $P$ takes the value $1$ at $0$: the ball of radius $0$ consists of the identity element alone.
nodes.title: The growth function at radius zero

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the growth function of $P$ is positive at $n$: the ball of radius $n$ contains the identity.
nodes.title: The growth function of a finite group is positive

nodes.summary: For every generating family $P$ of a finite group $G$ and every natural number $n$, the value of the growth function of $P$ at $n$ is at most the order of $G$, since every ball is a subset of $G$.
nodes.title: The growth function is bounded by the order of the group

nodes.summary: Every generating family of a finite group has polynomial growth: its growth function is bounded by the order of the group, a polynomial of degree $0$.
nodes.title: Finite groups have polynomial growth

nodes.summary: If a generating family $P$ of a group $G$ has polynomial growth, then the growth function of $P$ is positive at every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Polynomial growth makes the growth function positive

reading_title.source: Growth rate of a $k$-element generating family (Kourovka 14.7)

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a group and $S = (s_1, \dots, s_k)$ a family of $k$ elements generating $\Gamma$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\beta_S(n)$ be the number of elements of $\Gamma$ that are products of at most $n$ elements of $S \cup S^{-1}$. The growth rate of $\Gamma$ with respect to $S$ is the real number $\omega(\Gamma, S) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \beta_S(n)^{1/n}$.

Hyperbolic groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is word-hyperbolic if there are a finite index set $\iota$ and a family $(s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of elements generating $G$ such that $G$, equipped with the word metric of this generating family, is $\delta$-hyperbolic for some real number $\delta$.

Permutation stability

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and permutations $\sigma$, $\tau$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Hamming distance $d_n(\sigma, \tau)$ is the number of points $i < n$ with $\sigma(i) \ne \tau(i)$, divided by $n$, as a real number. For $n = 0$ it is $0$; this single value does not affect statements about limits as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Normalized Hamming distance

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and, for each natural number $n$, let $f_n \colon G \to S_n$ be an arbitrary map, where $S_n$ is the group of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The sequence $(f_n)$ is an almost-homomorphism when for all $g, h \in G$ the normalized Hamming distance $d_n(f_n(g) f_n(h), f_n(gh))$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Almost-homomorphisms to symmetric groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $f_n \colon G \to S_n$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$) be maps into the symmetric groups $S_n$ of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The sequence $(f_n)$ is close to homomorphisms when there are group homomorphisms $\rho_n \colon G \to S_n$ such that for every $g \in G$ the normalized Hamming distance $d_n(\rho_n(g), f_n(g))$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Closeness to homomorphisms

Characteristic quotients of free groups

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n \ge 3$ the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has a characteristic subgroup $C \ne F_n$ such that the quotient $F_n / C$ is generated by two elements, hence by fewer than $n$ elements. This is the positive answer to Problem 17.62 (J. Conrad) in every rank where two generators are fewer than $n$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.62 (two-generated characteristic quotients of free groups)

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 3$, the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators has a characteristic subgroup $C \ne F_n$ such that the quotient $F_n / C$ is generated by two elements; since $2 < n$, the quotient is generated by fewer than $n$ elements.

nodes.summary: The conjecture of V. P. Shaptala that for every free group $F$ and all non-cyclic subgroups $U$ and $V$ of $F$, if the commutator subgroup $[U, U]$ is contained in the commutator subgroup $[V, V]$, then $U$ is contained in $V$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of derived subgroups in free groups (Kourovka 13.62)

nodes.summary: There exist a free group $F$ and non-cyclic subgroups $U$ and $V$ of $F$ such that the commutator subgroup $[U, U]$ is contained in the commutator subgroup $[V, V]$ but $U$ is not contained in $V$. That is, the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 13.62 is false; the Kourovka Archive credits this answer to M. J. Dunwoody.

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators and $r(K) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ the rank of a subgroup $K$. A subgroup $H$ of $F_n$ is compressed when $r(H) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$ containing $H$.

Given a finite list of words, this is the subgroup of $F_n$ generated by the elements of $F_n$ that the words represent, each word representing the product of its letters.
nodes.title: Subgroup of a free group generated by a list of words

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. A subgroup $N$ of $F$ is recursively enumerable when the set of words $w$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) whose image in $F$ lies in $N$ is recursively enumerable.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F$ be the free group on the generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and let $N$ be a subgroup of $F$. The word problem for $F / N$ is solvable when membership in $N$ is decidable: the predicate on words $w$ (finite lists of letters, each a generator together with a sign) that the image of $w$ in $F$ lies in $N$ is computable.

nodes.summary: This is the statement that whenever $G$ is a group without involutions (if $g^2 = 1$ then $g = 1$), $a \in G$ is not the square of any element of $G$, and $n$ is an odd natural number, the quotient of $G$ by the normal closure of $a^n$ has no involutions: every element $y$ of the quotient with $y^2 = 1$ is $1$.

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ has a just finite presentation: a presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ with $X$ and $R$ finite that defines $G$ and such that removing any single relator from $R$ gives a presentation of an infinite group.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $S \subseteq G$ a subset and $\mathbb{Z}G$ the integral group ring of $G$. This is the right ideal of $\mathbb{Z}G$ generated by the elements $g - 1$ with $g \in S$, regarded as a right $\mathbb{Z}G$-submodule of $\mathbb{Z}G$.

Dimension subgroups

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the augmentation ideal $\Delta(G)$ of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ is the $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule spanned by the elements $g - 1$ for $g \in G$. It is the kernel of the augmentation map $\mathbb{Z}G \to \mathbb{Z}$, $\sum_g a_g g \mapsto \sum_g a_g$.
nodes.title: Augmentation ideal of the integral group ring

nodes.summary: Let $\Delta(G)$ be the augmentation ideal of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ of a group $G$, and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\Delta(G)^n$ be its $n$-th power, the $\mathbb{Z}$-span of all products of $n$ elements of $\Delta(G)$. An element $g \in G$ lies in the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G) = G \cap (1 + \Delta(G)^n)$ when $g - 1 \in \Delta(G)^n$.
nodes.title: Dimension subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that for every group $G$, every $n \ge 1$, every element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$ and every $g \in G$, the commutator $x g x^{-1} g^{-1}$ lies in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$, indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$ and $\gamma_{k+1}(G) = [\gamma_k(G), G]$. Equivalently, the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ is central.
nodes.title: Gupta–Kuz'min centrality question (Kourovka 12.22(a))

nodes.summary: The statement that for every group $G$, every $n \ge 1$ and every element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$, the square $x^2$ lies in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$, indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$ and $\gamma_{k+1}(G) = [\gamma_k(G), G]$. Equivalently, the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ has exponent dividing $2$.
nodes.title: Gupta–Kuz'min exponent question (Kourovka 12.22(b))

nodes.summary: There exist a group $G$, an integer $n \ge 1$, an element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$ and an element $g \in G$ such that the commutator $x g x^{-1} g^{-1}$ does not lie in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$ (indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$). That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.22(a) is negative: the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ need not be central.
nodes.title: Dimension quotients need not be central

nodes.summary: There exist a group $G$, an integer $n \ge 1$ and an element $x$ of the $n$-th dimension subgroup $D_n(G)$ such that $x^2$ does not lie in $\gamma_n(G)$, the $n$-th term of the lower central series of $G$ (indexed so that $\gamma_1(G) = G$). That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.22(b) is negative: the image of $D_n(G)$ in $G/\gamma_n(G)$ need not have exponent dividing $2$.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $G$ a commutative group. The inversion of the group ring $R[G]$ is the ring automorphism of $R[G]$ induced by the group automorphism $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ of $G$: it sends $\sum_g r_g\, g$ to $\sum_g r_g\, g^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Inversion on a group ring

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a commutative group and $\iota$ the inversion of the group ring $R[G]$. For every $x \in R[G]$, $\iota(\iota(x)) = x$.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a commutative group and $A$ a module over the group ring $R[G]$. For every $r \in R[G]$ and every element $a$ of the inversion twist of $A$, with underlying element $\bar a \in A$, the underlying element of $r \cdot a$ is $\iota(r) \cdot \bar a$, where $\iota$ is the inversion of $R[G]$ and $\cdot$ on the right is the original action on $A$.
nodes.title: Scalar action on the inversion twist

nodes.summary: $P$ is the group with generators $a$ and $b$ and relators $b^{-1}a^2ba^2$ and $a^{-1}b^2ab^2$, that is, $P = \langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2}, a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$.

nodes.summary: In the group $P$ with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2},\ a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$, $x = a^2$.
nodes.title: The element x of Gardam's group

nodes.summary: In the group $P$ with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2},\ a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$, $y = b^2$.

nodes.summary: In the group $P$ with presentation $\langle a, b \mid b^{-1}a^2b = a^{-2},\ a^{-1}b^2a = b^{-2} \rangle$, $z = (ab)^2$.

In the group ring $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$ set $p = (1 + x)(1 + y)(1 + z^{-1})$, $q = x^{-1}y^{-1} + x + y^{-1}z + z$, $r = 1 + x + y^{-1}z + xyz$ and $s = 1 + (x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1})z^{-1}$, and let $u = p + qa + rb + sab$. Then $P$ is torsion-free (if $g \in P$…

Ore condition for group algebras

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the shift is the automorphism $f \mapsto f(\cdot - 1)$ of the base group $\bigoplus_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Z}/p$, the additive group of finitely supported functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/p$, viewed as a multiplicative group.
nodes.title: Shift of the lamplighter base group

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the lamplighter group $\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}$ is the semidirect product $\left(\bigoplus_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathbb{Z}/p\right) \rtimes \mathbb{Z}$, in which $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ acts on the base group by the $n$-th power of the shift $f \mapsto f(\cdot - 1)$.
nodes.title: Lamplighter group

nodes.summary: An element $s$ of a ring $R$ is a non-zero-divisor when it is neither a left nor a right zero divisor: for every $z \in R$, $zs = 0$ implies $z = 0$ and $sz = 0$ implies $z = 0$.
nodes.title: Non-zero-divisor

nodes.summary: A ring $R$ satisfies the right Ore condition for its non-zero-divisors, so that it has a classical right ring of quotients, when for all $s, t \in R$ with $s$ a non-zero-divisor there are $x, y \in R$ with $x$ a non-zero-divisor and $sy = tx$.
nodes.title: Right Ore ring

nodes.summary: There are a field $k$ and a prime $p$ such that the group algebra $k[\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}]$ of the lamplighter group $\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}$ satisfies the right Ore condition for its non-zero-divisors, that is, has a classical right ring of quotients.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.47: some lamplighter group algebra is Ore

nodes.summary: For every field $k$ and every prime $p$, the group algebra $k[\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}]$ of the lamplighter group $\mathbb{Z}/p \wr \mathbb{Z}$ does not satisfy the right Ore condition for its non-zero-divisors: there are $s$ and $t$ in it, with $s$ a non-zero-divisor, such that $sy = tx$ holds for no $x$ and $y$ with $x$ a non-zero-divisor.
nodes.title: Lamplighter group algebras are not Ore
Projective modules over group rings

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is polycyclic if for some $n \ge 0$ there are subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ such that for each $i < n$, $H_i$ is normal in $H_{i+1}$ and the quotient $H_{i+1} / H_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Polycyclic group

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is almost polycyclic (polycyclic-by-finite) if it has a subgroup of finite index that is polycyclic.
nodes.title: Almost polycyclic group

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that, for every commutative ring $k$, every torsion-free almost polycyclic group $G$ (no element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ has finite order) and every finitely generated projective module $P$ over the group ring $kG$, if $P$ contains two elements that are linearly independent over $kG$, then $P$ is a free $kG$-module.
nodes.title: Artamonov's freeness question (Kourovka 11.5)

nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every commutative ring $k$, every torsion-free almost polycyclic group $G$ (no element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ has finite order) and every finitely generated projective module $P$ over the group ring $kG$ containing two elements that are linearly independent over $kG$, the module $P$ is free over $kG$.
nodes.title: Artamonov's freeness question has a negative answer

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on $x, y$. For nonzero complex numbers $a, b$, this is the homomorphism $\chi \colon F \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ with $\chi(x) = a$ and $\chi(y) = b$.
nodes.title: Twisting character of the free group of rank two

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on $x, y$, let $\mathbb{C}F$ be its complex group algebra, and for nonzero complex numbers $a, b$ let $\chi$ be the character of $F$ with $\chi(x) = a$ and $\chi(y) = b$. The map $\vartheta_{a,b}$ sends $\alpha = \sum_{g \in F} c_g\, g \in \mathbb{C}F$ to $\sum_{g \in F} \chi(g)\, c_g\, g$.

There is a nonzero $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}F$ such that for all complex numbers $a, b \neq 1$ with $|a| = |b| = 1$ the right ideals $\alpha\,\mathbb{C}F$ and…

Zassenhaus conjectures

nodes.summary: Kourovka 17.67 (H. Zassenhaus's conjecture, recorded by V. D. Mazurov): every unit of finite order of the integral group ring `ℤG` of a finite group `G` is conjugate, by a unit of the rational group ring `ℚG`, to an element `±g` with `g ∈ G`.
nodes.title: Zassenhaus conjecture on torsion units

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a unit $u$ of finite order of the integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}G$ such that for every unit $v$ of the rational group ring $\mathbb{Q}G$, every $g \in G$ and every sign $\varepsilon \in \{1, -1\}$, the conjugate $v u v^{-1}$, computed in $\mathbb{Q}G$, is not equal to $\varepsilon g$. That is, the first Zassenhaus conjecture is false.

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an abelian group and let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of $A$. Then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$ when $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic; formally the quotient is taken by $L' \cap L$, regarded as a subgroup of $L$.
nodes.title: Cyclic sublattice of a subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. Then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$ if and only if $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/(L' \cap L)$, with $L' \cap L$ regarded as a subgroup of $L$, is cyclic.
nodes.title: Characterization of cyclic sublattices

nodes.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. If $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$, then $L' \subseteq L$.
nodes.title: A cyclic sublattice is contained in its ambient subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. If $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$, then the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: The quotient by a cyclic sublattice is cyclic

nodes.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. If $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic, then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$.
nodes.title: Criterion for a cyclic sublattice

nodes.summary: An abelian group $A$, written additively, is torsion-free when for every natural number $n \ne 0$ and every $a \in A$, $n a = 0$ implies $a = 0$.

nodes.summary: Every finite abelian group $A$ is isomorphic to its dual group, the group of characters of $A$ under pointwise multiplication, where a character of $A$ is a map $\chi : A \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\chi(0) = 1$ and $\chi(a + a') = \chi(a)\chi(a')$ for all $a, a' \in A$.
nodes.title: A finite abelian group is isomorphic to its dual group

nodes.summary: For all abelian groups $A$ and $B$, the group of characters of $A \times B$ is isomorphic to the product of the character groups of $A$ and $B$. Here a character of $A$ is a map $\chi : A \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\chi(0) = 1$ and $\chi(a + a') = \chi(a)\chi(a')$ for all $a, a' \in A$, and the characters of $A$ form a group under pointwise multiplication.

nodes.summary: For an ultrafilter $U$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and a sequence $(G_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of groups, the ultraproduct $\left(\prod_i G_i\right)/U$ is the quotient of the direct product $\prod_i G_i$ by the ultraproduct kernel, the normal subgroup of sequences $(g_i)_i$ with $\{i : g_i = 1\} \in U$.

Structure of finitely generated abelian groups

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be an abelian group. If $A \cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^{n} \mathbb{Z}/p^{e_i}\mathbb{Z}$ and $A \cong \bigoplus_{j=1}^{m} \mathbb{Z}/p^{f_j}\mathbb{Z}$ for positive integers $e_1, \dots, e_n$ and $f_1, \dots, f_m$, then $n = m$ and the multisets $\{e_1, \dots, e_n\}$ and $\{f_1, \dots, f_m\}$ are equal.

nodes.title: Torsion subgroup of a finitely generated abelian group is finite

nodes.summary: Every finite abelian group $A$ is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_i\mathbb{Z}$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_i > 1$ for every $i$ and $d_i \mid d_j$ whenever $i \le j$.

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a finite set, and for each $i \in I$ let $p_i$ be a prime and $e_i$ a natural number. Then there are $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $d_0, \dots, d_{k-1}$ with $d_j > 1$ for every $j$ and $d_j \mid d_l$ whenever $j \le l$, such that $\bigoplus_{i \in I} \mathbb{Z}/p_i^{e_i}\mathbb{Z}$ is isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{j < k} \mathbb{Z}/d_j\mathbb{Z}$.
