nodes.title: The subgroup $2^kA$

reading_title.source: The two-power layer $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$

nodes.summary: For an abelian group $A$, written additively, and a natural number $j$, this is the quotient group $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, where $2^kA$ denotes the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$ and $2^jA \subseteq 2^{j-1}A$. For $j = 0$, where $j - 1$ is read as $0$, it is the trivial quotient $A / A$.
nodes.title: The two-power layer $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$

reading_title.source: The $2^j$-rank of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, written additively, and let $j \ge 1$ be an integer. Writing $2^kA$ for the subgroup $\{2^k a : a \in A\}$, the $2^j$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2^{j-1}A / 2^jA$, which is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-vector space because $2$ kills it.
nodes.title: The $2^j$-rank of a finite abelian group

reading_title.source: The $4$-rank of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: For a finite abelian group $A$, written additively, the $4$-rank of $A$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of the quotient $2A / 4A$, where $2A = \{2a : a \in A\}$ and $4A = \{4a : a \in A\}$; it is the $2^j$-rank of $A$ for $j = 2$.
nodes.title: The $4$-rank of a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Arithmetic of finite groups through orders: cyclic numbers and groups of a given order (groups of order 10, dihedral groups from an index-two cyclic subgroup), counts of elements of each order, the spectrum (set of element orders), recognition of groups by spectrum or by order and spectrum, Thompson's type, and totient sums; conjugacy-class sizes go to Conjugacy classes.
nodes.title: Group orders, element orders and spectra

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $H$ be a cyclic subgroup of $G$ of index $2$. If $g^2 = 1$ for every element $g$ of $G$ that is not in $H$, then $G$ is isomorphic to the dihedral group $D_n$ of order $2n$, where $n = |H|$.
nodes.title: Dihedral groups from a cyclic subgroup of index two
Counts of elements of each order

nodes.summary: The proposition that if a finite group $G$ has the property that, for every divisor $d > 1$ of $|G|$ and every subgroup $H$ of $G$ whose order is coprime to $d$, $|H|$ divides the number of elements of $G$ of order $d$, then every non-identity element of $G$ has prime-power order.
nodes.title: Shi's question on element-order counts (Kourovka 18.112)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group such that for every divisor $d > 1$ of $|G|$ and every subgroup $H$ of $G$ whose order is coprime to $d$, the order $|H|$ divides the number of elements of $G$ of order $d$. Then every non-identity element of $G$ has prime-power order.
nodes.title: Counting elements of each order forces prime-power orders
Cyclic numbers

nodes.summary: An additive commutative group of squarefree cardinality is additively cyclic.
nodes.title: Additive groups of squarefree order are cyclic

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Every group of order $n$ is cyclic if and only if $n$ is relatively prime to $\varphi(n)$, that is, $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.
nodes.title: Szele's criterion for cyclic numbers
Element orders of extensions of projective linear groups

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a field $F$, $\mathrm{PSL}_n(F)$ is the quotient $\mathrm{SL}_n(F)/Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(F))$ of the special linear group $\mathrm{SL}_n(F)$ of $n \times n$ matrices over $F$ with determinant $1$ by its centre.
nodes.title: Projective special linear group

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every $n \ge 3$, every prime $p$ and every $k \ge 1$, with $q = p^k$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$ the field with $q$ elements, the following holds: whenever $H$ is a nontrivial normal subgroup of a finite group $G$ and $G/H$ is isomorphic to the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, some element of $G$ has an order that is not the order of any element of $G/H$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 14.60: new element orders in extensions of projective special linear groups

nodes.summary: Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 14.60 "Yes, it is true": Zavarnitsine proved it for `n ≠ 4` and Grechkoseeva and Skresanov for `n = 4` (the editors note that an earlier claim of failure for `n = 4` was erroneous). Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.60 (V.…
nodes.title: Extensions of PSL have a new element order
Finite groups with the same spectrum

nodes.summary: The spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of the elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order counts as having order $0$.
nodes.title: Element-order spectrum of a group

nodes.summary: For groups $A$ and $B$, the statement that $A$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $B$ or to a quotient of a normal subgroup of $B$: there is an injective homomorphism $A \to B$, or there are a normal subgroup $N$ of $B$ and a surjective homomorphism $N \to A$.
nodes.title: Subgroup or quotient of a normal subgroup

nodes.summary: Finite groups with equal spectra, neither a subgroup or normal-subgroup quotient of the other (problem). The statement that there exist finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with the same spectrum $\pi_e(G_1) = \pi_e(G_2)$ (the set of orders of elements), such that every finite group with spectrum $\pi_e(G_1)$ has order at most some fixed bound $B$, and such that neither of $G_1$, $G_2$ is isomorphic to a subgroup or to a…
nodes.title: Finite groups with equal spectra, neither a subgroup or normal-subgroup quotient of the other (problem)

Groups of order 10

nodes.summary: Every finite group of order $10$ that is not cyclic is isomorphic to the dihedral group $D_5$ of order $10$.
nodes.title: Noncyclic groups of order 10 are dihedral

nodes.summary: Every finite group of order $10$ is isomorphic either to the cyclic group $C_{10}$ of order $10$ or to the dihedral group $D_5$ of order $10$.
nodes.title: Classification of groups of order 10

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $10$. Then exactly one of the following holds: $G$ is isomorphic to the cyclic group $C_{10}$ of order $10$, or $G$ is isomorphic to the dihedral group $D_5$ of order $10$.
nodes.title: Exclusive classification of groups of order 10

nodes.summary: Let $C_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$ and let $D_5$ denote the dihedral group of order $10$. Every finite group of order $10$ is isomorphic to the direct product $C_5 \times C_2$ or to $D_5$.
nodes.title: Classification of groups of order 10, product form

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $10$, let $C_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$, and let $D_5$ denote the dihedral group of order $10$. Then exactly one of the following holds: $G$ is isomorphic to the direct product $C_5 \times C_2$, or $G$ is isomorphic to $D_5$.
nodes.title: Exclusive classification of groups of order 10, product form
Isospectral finite simple groups

nodes.summary: The spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of its elements, where an element of infinite order is counted as having order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group

nodes.summary: Kourovka 16.25 (A. V. Vasil'ev): there are three pairwise non-isomorphic finite non-abelian simple groups with the same spectrum.
nodes.title: Three isospectral finite simple groups

nodes.summary: There do not exist three pairwise non-isomorphic finite non-abelian simple groups $G_1, G_2, G_3$ with $\omega(G_1) = \omega(G_2) = \omega(G_3)$, where the spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of its elements.
nodes.title: No three non-isomorphic finite non-abelian simple groups are isospectral
Number of groups with a given spectrum

nodes.summary: The spectrum of a group $G$ is the set $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ of the orders of its elements, where an element of infinite order is counted as having order $0$.
nodes.title: The spectrum of a group (Kourovka 12.84)

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every set $\Omega$ of natural numbers, if two non-isomorphic finite groups both have set of element orders $\Omega$, then for every natural number $k$ there are $k$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups whose set of element orders is $\Omega$; that is, infinitely many.
nodes.title: Syskin's question on groups with a given spectrum (Kourovka 12.84)

nodes.summary: There are a set $\Omega$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$ such that two non-isomorphic finite groups have set of element orders $\Omega$, but there are no $k$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups whose set of element orders is $\Omega$.
nodes.title: Two isospectral finite groups do not force infinitely many

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ is the set of orders of elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order counts as having order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group (Kourovka 13.63)

reading_title.source: At most $k$ isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$

nodes.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$, this property holds when, for any finite groups $G_0, \dots, G_k$ (not necessarily distinct) whose spectra $\pi_e(G_i)$ (the sets of orders of elements of $G_i$) all equal $\Gamma$, there are indices $i \ne j$ with $G_i \cong G_j$.
nodes.title: At most $k$ isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$

parts: Infinitely many isomorphism types with spectrum
reading_title.source: Infinitely many isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$

nodes.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, this property holds when, for every natural number $n$, there are $n$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups $G_0, \dots, G_{n-1}$ whose spectra $\pi_e(G_i)$ (the sets of orders of elements of $G_i$) all equal $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many isomorphism types with spectrum $\Gamma$

Shi, that there is a natural number $k$ such that for every set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, either $h(\Gamma) \le k$ or $h(\Gamma) = \infty$, where $h(\Gamma)$ is the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups $G$ whose spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ (set of element orders) is $\Gamma$. Here $h(\Gamma) \le k$ means that among any $k + 1$ finite groups with spectrum $\Gamma$ two are…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.63 (bounded or infinite number of groups per spectrum)

nodes.summary: For a set $\Gamma$ of natural numbers, let $h(\Gamma)$ be the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups $G$ whose spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ (set of element orders) is $\Gamma$; $h(\Gamma) \le k$ means that among any $k + 1$ finite groups with spectrum $\Gamma$ two are isomorphic, and $h(\Gamma) = \infty$ means that for every $n$ there are $n$ pairwise non-isomorphic finite groups with spectrum $\Gamma$. Kourovka…
nodes.title: No uniform bound on the number of groups with a given spectrum
Order-divisibility bijections onto cyclic groups

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite group $G$, of order $n$ say, there is a bijection $f$ from $G$ onto the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ such that for every $x \in G$ the order of $x$ divides the additive order of $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.1 (statement)

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$, of order $n$ say, there is a bijection $f$ from $G$ onto the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ such that for every $x \in G$ the order of $x$ divides the additive order of $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Amiri's theorem (Kourovka Problem 18.1)
Prime divisors of element orders in soluble groups

nodes.summary: The statement, posed by A. Moretó, that there are natural numbers $a$ and $b$ such that for every finite soluble group $G$ and every natural number $m$, if the order of every element of $G$ has at most $m$ distinct prime divisors, then $|G|$ has at most $am + b$ distinct prime divisors.
nodes.title: Linear bound on the prime divisors of a finite soluble group (Kourovka 14.66)

nodes.summary: There are natural numbers $a$ and $b$ such that for every finite soluble group $G$ and every natural number $m$, if the order of every element of $G$ has at most $m$ distinct prime divisors, then $|G|$ has at most $am + b$ distinct prime divisors. That is, Kourovka Problem 14.66 has a positive answer.
nodes.title: Finite soluble groups satisfy a linear prime-divisor bound
Recognition by order and spectrum

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, the set of natural numbers that occur as the order of some element of $G$, where an element of infinite order is counted as having order $0$.
nodes.title: Set of element orders (Kourovka 12.39)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite group $G$ and every finite simple group $S$, if $G$ and $S$ have the same order and the same set of element orders, then $G$ is isomorphic to $S$.
nodes.title: Shi's conjecture on recognition by order and element orders (Kourovka 12.39)

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every finite simple group $S$, if $G$ and $S$ have the same order and the same set of element orders, then $G$ is isomorphic to $S$. That is, Shi's conjecture (Kourovka Problem 12.39) holds.
nodes.title: Finite simple groups are recognized by order and element orders
Recognition of alternating groups by spectrum

nodes.summary: The spectrum $\pi_e(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of orders of the elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order is assigned order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that there is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every finite group $G$ with the same spectrum (set of element orders) as the alternating group $A_n$ is isomorphic to $A_n$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.107 on recognition of alternating groups by spectrum

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every finite group $G$ whose set of element orders equals that of the alternating group $A_n$ is isomorphic to $A_n$.
nodes.title: Large alternating groups are recognizable by spectrum

nodes.summary: The spectrum $\omega(G)$ of a group $G$ is the set of natural numbers that are orders of elements of $G$, where an element of infinite order is assigned order $0$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $m$ a natural number. A sequence $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_m$ of subgroups of $G$ is a composition series of length $m$ if $s_0$ is the trivial subgroup, $s_m = G$, and for each $i < m$ the subgroup $s_i$ is a normal subgroup of $s_{i+1}$ and the quotient $s_{i+1}/s_i$ is a simple group.
nodes.title: Finite composition series

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $s_0, s_1, \dots, s_m$ be subgroups of $G$, and let $i < m$. The $i$-th factor of the chain is non-abelian if $s_i \cap s_{i+1}$ is a normal subgroup of $s_{i+1}$ and the quotient group $s_{i+1}/(s_i \cap s_{i+1})$ is non-abelian, that is, it has elements $x, y$ with $xy \ne yx$. When $s_i \le s_{i+1}$, this quotient is $s_{i+1}/s_i$.
nodes.title: Non-abelian factor of a chain of subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and every finite group $G$ whose spectrum, the set of orders of its elements, equals the spectrum of the alternating group $A_n$, every composition series of $G$ has at most one non-abelian factor.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.27 (statement)

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $G$ be a finite group whose spectrum, the set of orders of its elements, equals the spectrum of the alternating group $A_n$. Then every composition series of $G$ has at most one non-abelian factor.
nodes.title: Groups isospectral to an alternating group (Kourovka Problem 16.27)

reading_title.source: Kourovka Problem 19.80 ($OC_7$-groups)

nodes.summary: The proposition, asked by W. J. Shi, that every $OC_7$-group, that is, every group whose set of element orders is exactly $\{1, 2, \dots, 7\}$ (such a group is periodic), is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.80 ($OC_7$-groups)

reading_title.source: Groups with element orders $1$ to $7$ are isomorphic to $A_7$

nodes.summary: Every group, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders is exactly $\{1, 2, \dots, 7\}$ is isomorphic to the alternating group $A_7$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.80 positively (Mamontov and Jabara).
nodes.title: Groups with element orders $1$ to $7$ are isomorphic to $A_7$
Recognition of PSL(2, 7) by spectrum

nodes.summary: The statement that every group $G$, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ equals $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 7\}$ is isomorphic to $L_2(7) = \mathrm{PSL}(2, 7)$, the projective special linear group of $2 \times 2$ matrices over the field $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.57: recognition of PSL(2, 7) by spectrum

nodes.summary: Every group $G$, finite or infinite, whose set of element orders $\{\operatorname{ord}(g) : g \in G\}$ equals $\{1, 2, 3, 4, 7\}$ is isomorphic to $L_2(7) = \mathrm{PSL}(2, 7)$, the projective special linear group of $2 \times 2$ matrices over the field $\mathbb{Z}/7\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Lytkina–Kuznetsov theorem: PSL(2, 7) is recognizable by spectrum
Subgroups with all prime divisors of a simple group

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a natural number $N$ such that every finite simple group $G$ that is not isomorphic to the alternating group $A_n$ for any natural number $n$ and has a proper subgroup $H$ with $\pi(H) = \pi(G)$ satisfies $|G| \le N$, where $\pi(X)$ denotes the set of prime divisors of the order $|X|$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.64 (Monakhov)

Zenkov) that the symplectic groups `G = S_{4k}(2^s)` have proper subgroups `H ≅ Ω⁻_{4k}(2^s)` with `π(H) = π(G)`, an infinite family of non-alternating finite simple groups. Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 11.64 (V.…
nodes.title: Infinitely many simple groups with proper subgroups of equal prime set
Thompson's problem on groups of the same type

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type when, for every positive integer $n$, the equation $x^n = 1$ has the same number of solutions in $G$ as in $H$. An infinite set of solutions is counted as $0$, so the notion is meant for finite groups.
nodes.title: Same power-equation type

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is almost simple when there is a nonabelian finite simple group $S$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup $A$ of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ that contains the inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S)$.
nodes.title: Almost simple group

nodes.summary: The conjecture that for all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is almost simple and $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type, then $G$ is isomorphic to $H$.
nodes.title: Characterization of almost simple groups by power-equation type (Kourovka 21.134(b))

nodes.summary: There exist finite groups $G$ and $H$ such that $G$ is almost simple, $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type, and $G$ is not isomorphic to $H$. That is, the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 21.134(b) is false.
nodes.title: Power-equation type does not characterize almost simple groups

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same type when, for every integer $n \ge 1$, the equation $x^n = 1$ has the same number of solutions in $G$ as in $H$, where an infinite set of solutions counts as having $0$ elements.
nodes.title: Groups of the same type

nodes.summary: Every finite group of the same type as a finite soluble group is soluble: if $G$ and $H$ are finite groups of the same type and $H$ is soluble, then $G$ is soluble.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 12.37 (J. G. Thompson)

nodes.summary: The answer to Kourovka Problem 12.37 is negative: there are finite groups $G$ and $H$ of the same type such that $H$ is soluble and $G$ is not soluble.
nodes.title: Solubility is not determined by the type
Totient sums of element orders

nodes.summary: The statement that for all finite groups $G$ and $H$ of the same order with $\sum_{g \in G} \varphi(|g|) = \sum_{h \in H} \varphi(|h|)$, where $|g|$ is the order of $g$ and $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function, if $G$ is simple then $H$ is simple.
nodes.title: Curtin–Pourgholi question on totient sums and simplicity (Kourovka 19.25)

nodes.summary: There are finite groups $G$ and $H$ of the same order with $\sum_{g \in G} \varphi(|g|) = \sum_{h \in H} \varphi(|h|)$, where $|g|$ is the order of $g$ and $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function, such that $G$ is simple and $H$ is not simple. So the Curtin–Pourgholi question has a negative answer.
nodes.title: Order and totient sum do not determine simplicity (Kourovka 19.25)

nodes.summary: Conjugacy classes of groups as a structural invariant: class sizes and breadth, the class number, commuting probability, Thompson's conjecture on class sizes, products of conjugacy classes, and relations between class sizes and group structure; class sizes of p-groups go to Finite p-groups, and character-theoretic class arguments to Characters of finite groups.
nodes.title: Conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: Let $\Pr(G)$ denote the commuting probability of a group $G$: $\Pr(G) = |\{(x, y) \in G \times G : xy = yx\}| / |G|^2$ if $G$ is finite, and $\Pr(G) = 0$ if $G$ is infinite. Then the set $\{\Pr(G) : G \text{ a group}\}$ is a closed subset of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The set of commuting probabilities is closed
Breadth of a finite group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a natural number and $g \in G$, and write $g^G$ for the conjugacy class of $g$. When $p \ge 2$, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ is $\lfloor \log_p |g^G| \rfloor$, the largest natural number $k$ with $p^k \le |g^G|$; when $p \le 1$, it is $0$.
nodes.title: Breadth of an element

nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$ and a natural number $p$, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(G)$ of $G$ is the maximum of the element breadths $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ over all $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Breadth of a finite group

nodes.summary: In a finite group $G$, the number of elements of the conjugacy class of any $g \in G$ divides the order $|G|$.
nodes.title: Conjugacy class sizes divide the group order

reading_title.source: Conjugacy classes of a finite $p$-group have $p$-power size

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $G$ a finite $p$-group. For every $g \in G$ there is a natural number $k$ such that the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements.
nodes.title: Conjugacy classes of a finite $p$-group have $p$-power size

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime, $k$ a natural number and $g \in G$. If the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements, then the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ equals $k$.
nodes.title: Breadth from an exact class size

reading_title.source: Class sizes in a $p$-group via breadth

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite $p$-group and $g \in G$, and write $g^G$ for the conjugacy class of $g$. Then the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ satisfies $p^{\operatorname{br}_p(g)} = |g^G|$.
nodes.title: Class sizes in a $p$-group via breadth

nodes.summary: In every group, the conjugacy class of the identity element $1$ is the singleton $\{1\}$.
nodes.title: The conjugacy class of the identity

nodes.summary: In a finite group, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(1)$ of the identity element $1$ is $0$ for every natural number $p$.
nodes.title: Breadth of the identity

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a natural number. For every $g \in G$, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ is at most the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(G)$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Element breadth is at most the group breadth

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a natural number. There is an element $g \in G$ whose breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ equals the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(G)$ of $G$.
nodes.title: The group breadth is attained
Centralizers of maximal order

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ of a group $G$ write $C_G(x)$ for its centralizer. This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every element $a \ne 1$ of $G$ with $|C_G(x)| \le |C_G(a)|$ for every $x \ne 1$ in $G$, every nilpotent subgroup $H$ of $G$ normalized by $C_G(a)$ (that is, $C_G(a)$ is contained in the normalizer of $H$) is contained in $C_G(a)$.
nodes.title: Mukhamet'yanov–Fomin problem on centralizers of maximal order

nodes.summary: For an element $x$ of a group $G$ write $C_G(x)$ for its centralizer. There exist a finite group $G$, an element $a \ne 1$ of $G$ with $|C_G(x)| \le |C_G(a)|$ for every $x \ne 1$ in $G$, and a nilpotent subgroup $H$ of $G$ normalized by $C_G(a)$ (that is, $C_G(a)$ is contained in the normalizer of $H$) such that $H$ is not contained in $C_G(a)$.
nodes.title: Centralizers of maximal order need not contain normalized nilpotent subgroups
Class number of a finite group

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every integer $k \ge 1$ such that some insoluble finite group has exactly $k$ conjugacy classes, every finite group $G$ with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes whose order is at least the order of every finite group with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes is insoluble. This is Kourovka Problem 17.77 (R. Heffernan, D. MacHale).
nodes.title: Heffernan–MacHale problem on groups of maximal order with a given class number

nodes.summary: There are an integer $k \ge 1$, an insoluble finite group with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes, and a soluble finite group $G$ with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes whose order is at least the order of every finite group with exactly $k$ conjugacy classes. So it is not true that whenever some insoluble finite group has exactly $k \ge 1$ conjugacy classes, every finite group of maximal order with exactly $k$ conjugacy…
nodes.title: A finite group of maximal order with a given class number can be soluble

nodes.summary: The proposition that every finite group $G$ has a nilpotent subgroup $N$ whose order $|N|$ is at least the number $k(G)$ of conjugacy classes of $G$. This is Kourovka Problem 14.54 (M. W. Liebeck, L. Pyber).
nodes.title: Liebeck–Pyber problem on the class number and nilpotent subgroups

nodes.summary: There is a finite group $G$ such that the number $k(G)$ of conjugacy classes of $G$ is greater than $|N|$ for every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$.
nodes.title: The class number can exceed the order of every nilpotent subgroup
Largest conjugacy class of perfect groups

nodes.summary: The proposition that every finite group $G$ that is perfect ($[G, G] = G$) and has trivial centre contains an element $x$ with $|G| \le |x^G|^2$, where $x^G$ is the conjugacy class of $x$. Equivalently, $|G| \le n^2$, where $n$ is the largest size of a conjugacy class of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 20.30: the order of a perfect centreless group and its largest conjugacy class

nodes.summary: It is not true that every finite group $G$ that is perfect ($[G, G] = G$) and has trivial centre contains an element $x$ with $|G| \le |x^G|^2$, where $x^G$ is the conjugacy class of $x$. That is, some perfect centreless finite group $G$ satisfies $|G| > n^2$, where $n$ is the largest size of a conjugacy class of $G$.
nodes.title: Perfect centreless groups need not have order at most the square of the largest class size
p-parts of conjugacy class sizes

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has a normal $p$-complement when it has a normal subgroup $N$ and a Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ that are complements of each other: every element of $G$ can be written uniquely as $nq$ with $n \in N$ and $q \in P$.
nodes.title: Groups with a normal p-complement

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$, the $p$-part of a positive integer $m$ is the largest power of $p$ dividing $m$. This is the statement that for every finite group $G$, every prime $p$ and every $p$-element $g$ of $G$ (that is, $g^{p^k} = 1$ for some natural number $k$), if for every $x \in G$ the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $x$ is at most the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $g$, then $G$ has a…
nodes.title: Gorshkov's problem on maximal p-parts of class sizes

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$, the $p$-part of a positive integer $m$ is the largest power of $p$ dividing $m$. There exist a finite group $G$, a prime $p$ and a $p$-element $g$ of $G$ (that is, $g^{p^k} = 1$ for some natural number $k$) such that for every $x \in G$ the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $x$ is at most the $p$-part of the size of the conjugacy class of $g$, but $G$ has no normal $p$-complement.
nodes.title: A maximal p-part of a class size does not force a normal p-complement
Products of conjugacy classes in alternating groups

nodes.summary: The statement that there are a real number $\delta$ with $0 < \delta < 1$ and a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ and all conjugacy classes $A$, $B$, $C$ of the alternating group $\mathrm{Alt}(n)$, each of size at least $|\mathrm{Alt}(n)|^{\delta}$, the product set $ABC$ is all of $\mathrm{Alt}(n)$.
nodes.title: Products of three large conjugacy classes in alternating groups (Kourovka 20.23)

nodes.summary: There are a real number $\delta$ with $0 < \delta < 1$ and a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ and all conjugacy classes $A$, $B$, $C$ of the alternating group $\mathrm{Alt}(n)$, each of size at least $|\mathrm{Alt}(n)|^{\delta}$, the product set $ABC$ is all of $\mathrm{Alt}(n)$. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 20.23.
nodes.title: Three large conjugacy classes multiply to the whole alternating group
Thompson's conjecture on conjugacy class sizes

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, $N(G)$ is the set of natural numbers $|\{y \in G : y \text{ is conjugate to } x\}|$ for $x \in G$, that is, the set of sizes of the conjugacy classes of $G$, where an infinite class counts as size $0$.
nodes.title: The set of conjugacy class sizes

nodes.summary: Write $N(G)$ for the set of sizes of the conjugacy classes of a group $G$. Thompson's conjecture is the statement that for all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is simple and non-abelian, $H$ has trivial centre, and $N(G) = N(H)$, then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic.
nodes.title: Thompson's conjecture on conjugacy class sizes

nodes.summary: For all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is simple and non-abelian, $H$ has trivial centre, and $G$ and $H$ have the same set of conjugacy class sizes, then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic.
nodes.title: Thompson's conjecture on conjugacy class sizes is true
Torsion-free groups with three conjugacy classes

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that has exactly three conjugacy classes and has a subgroup of index $2$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.42 (statement)

nodes.summary: There is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that has exactly three conjugacy classes and has a subgroup of index $2$.
nodes.title: Minasyan's theorem (Kourovka Problem 11.42)

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) with exactly three conjugacy classes in which no element $g \neq 1$ is conjugate to its inverse $g^{-1}$, that is, no nontrivial conjugacy class contains a pair of mutually inverse elements.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.67 (statement)

nodes.summary: There is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) with exactly three conjugacy classes in which no element $g \neq 1$ is conjugate to its inverse $g^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Bagayoko's theorem (Kourovka Problem 11.67)

nodes.summary: Minimal and special generating sets: generator numbers of almost simple and soluble groups, (2,3)-generation, generation by elements of prime-power order, spread, coprime generation, two-generated direct powers, Eulerian functions and probabilistic generation.
nodes.title: Generation of groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $X \subseteq G$ satisfy $X^{-1} = X$, where $X^{-1} = \{x^{-1} : x \in X\}$. Then the subgroup of $G$ generated by $X$ equals $\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} X^n$, where $X^0 = \{1\}$ and $X^{n+1} = X^n X = \{yx : y \in X^n,\ x \in X\}$.
nodes.title: Subgroup generated by a symmetric set
(2,3)-generation of groups

reading_title.source: $(2,3)$-generation of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ (Kourovka 14.49)

nodes.summary: The statement that there are $a, b \in \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $a$ has order $2$, $b$ has order $3$, and $a$ and $b$ generate $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$.
nodes.title: $(2,3)$-generation of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ (Kourovka 14.49)

reading_title.source: $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is not $(2,3)$-generated

nodes.summary: There are no $a, b \in \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ such that $a$ has order $2$, $b$ has order $3$, and $a$ and $b$ generate $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$. Equivalently, $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is not a quotient of the modular group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) \cong C_2 \ast C_3$.
nodes.title: $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ is not $(2,3)$-generated
Coprime generation

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite group $G$, all subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ of coprime orders that together generate $G$, and every natural number $d$, if each of $A$ and $B$ is generated by at most $d$ elements, then $G$ is generated by at most $d + 1$ elements.
nodes.title: Lucchini's coprime generation bound (Kourovka 16.53)

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$, subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ of coprime orders that together generate $G$, and a natural number $d$ such that each of $A$ and $B$ is generated by at most $d$ elements, but no set of at most $d + 1$ elements generates $G$. That is, Kourovka Problem 16.53 has a negative answer.
nodes.title: Lucchini's coprime generation bound fails
Eulerian polynomials of groups

nodes.summary: For a subgroup $H$ of a group, the order polynomial of $H$ is $f(H) = \prod_p x_p^{v_p(|H|)}$ in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$, where $p$ runs over the primes, $x_p$ is the variable indexed by $p$, and $v_p(|H|)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the order $|H|$ of $H$. If $H$ is infinite, $f(H) = 1$.
nodes.title: Order polynomial of a subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $f$ be the order polynomial. A function $\varphi$ from the subgroups of $G$ to the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$ is an Eulerian function of $G$ if $\sum_{K \le H} \varphi(K) = f(H)$ for every subgroup $H$ of $G$, the sum running over the subgroups $K$ of $H$. The value $\varphi(G)$ is the Eulerian polynomial of $G$.
nodes.title: Eulerian function of a group (G. E. Wall)

reading_title.source: $p$-solvable group

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ is $p$-solvable if it has a chain of subgroups $1 = N_0 \le N_1 \le \dots \le N_n = G$ in which each $N_i$ is normal in $N_{i+1}$ and each index $[N_{i+1} : N_i]$, taken to be $0$ when it is infinite, is a power $p^k$ with $k \ge 0$ or is coprime to $p$. For finite $G$ and prime $p$ this says that every factor $N_{i+1}/N_i$ is a $p$-group or has order prime to $p$.
nodes.title: $p$-solvable group

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every Eulerian function $\varphi$ of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$: if there are a finite set $S$ of primes and, for each $q \in S$, an integer polynomial $P_q$ involving no variable other than $x_q$, such that the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ equals $\prod_{q \in S} P_q$, then $G$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.104(a) (Eulerian polynomials and solvability, G. E. Wall)

reading_title.source: Kourovka Problem 11.104(b) (Eulerian polynomials and $p$-solvability)

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every finite group $G$, every prime $p$ and every Eulerian function $\varphi$ of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$: if the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ is a product $PQ$ of integer polynomials where $P$ involves no variable other than $x_p$ and $x_p$ does not occur in $Q$, then $G$ is $p$-solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.104(b) (Eulerian polynomials and $p$-solvability)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\varphi$ be an Eulerian function of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$. If there are a finite set $S$ of primes and, for each $q \in S$, an integer polynomial $P_q$ involving no variable other than $x_q$, such that the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ equals $\prod_{q \in S} P_q$, then $G$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Solvability from one-variable factorizations of the Eulerian polynomial

reading_title.source: Eulerian polynomial factorization implies $p$-solvability

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $\varphi$ be an Eulerian function of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$. If the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ is a product $PQ$ of integer polynomials where $P$ involves no variable other than $x_p$ and $x_p$ does not occur in $Q$, then $G$ is $p$-solvable.
nodes.title: Eulerian polynomial factorization implies $p$-solvability
Generation by elements of prime-power order

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite simple group $G$ is generated by two elements $x, y \in G$ whose orders are prime powers, that is, each of the form $p^k$ with $p$ prime and $k \ge 1$ (the primes and exponents may differ between $x$ and $y$ and depend on the group). The problem is due to J. Krempa.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.52 (generation by two elements of prime-power order)

nodes.summary: Every finite simple group $G$ is generated by two elements $x, y \in G$ whose orders are prime powers, that is, each of the form $p^k$ with $p$ prime and $k \ge 1$, where the prime and the exponent may differ between $x$ and $y$. This answers Kourovka Problem 18.52 positively.
nodes.title: Finite simple groups are generated by two elements of prime-power order
Generator number of almost simple groups

nodes.summary: For subgroups $G$ and $N$ of a group $A$, the relative generator number of $G$ modulo $N$ is the least $k$ such that some $k$ elements of $A$ together with $N$ generate $G$, and $0$ if no finite set of elements does. For a normal subgroup $N \le G$ with $G / N$ finitely generated it is $d(G / N)$, the minimal number of generators of $G / N$.
nodes.title: Relative generator number

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian simple group $S$, identified with its inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S) \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$, and every subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ containing $S$, $d(G) = \max(2, d(G / S))$. Here $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$, and $d(G / S)$, the minimal number of generators of $G / S$, is taken to be the least number of elements of $G$ that…
nodes.title: The generator-number formula for almost simple groups (Kourovka 11.27)

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian simple group $S$, identified with its inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S) \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$, every subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ containing $S$ is generated by at most $3$ elements.
nodes.title: The 3-generator bound for almost simple groups (Kourovka 11.27)

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite non-abelian simple group, identified with its inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S) \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$. For every subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ containing $S$, $d(G) = \max(2, d(G / S))$, where $d(G)$ is the minimal number of generators of $G$ and $d(G / S)$, the minimal number of generators of $G / S$, is taken to be the least number of elements of $G$ that together with $S$ generate…
nodes.title: Generator number of almost simple groups (Kourovka 11.27)

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite non-abelian simple group, identified with its inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S) \le \mathrm{Aut}(S)$. Every subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ containing $S$ is generated by at most $3$ elements.
nodes.title: Almost simple groups are generated by 3 elements (Kourovka 11.27)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is almost simple when there is a nonabelian finite simple group $S$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup $A$ of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ that contains the inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S)$.
nodes.title: Almost simple groups
Rank of a group generated by two subgroups

nodes.summary: Write $d(X)$ for the minimal number of generators of a finite group $X$. This is the proposition that for all finite groups $A$ and $B$ there are a finite group $G$ and subgroups $H, K \le G$ with $H \cong A$, $K \cong B$ and $\langle H, K \rangle = G$ such that $d(G) = d(A) + d(B)$.
nodes.title: Ribes' question on generator counts (Kourovka 12.71)

nodes.summary: Write $d(X)$ for the minimal number of generators of a finite group $X$. There are finite groups $A$ and $B$ such that for every finite group $G$ and all subgroups $H, K \le G$ with $H \cong A$, $K \cong B$ and $\langle H, K \rangle = G$, we have $d(G) \ne d(A) + d(B)$.
nodes.title: Generator counts of groups generated by two subgroups are not always additive (Kourovka 12.71)
Spread of a group

reading_title.source: Spread at least $k$

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has spread at least $k$, for a natural number $k$, when for every family $x_1, \dots, x_k$ of nontrivial elements of $G$, not necessarily distinct, there is an element $y \in G$ such that the subgroup $\langle x_i, y \rangle$ generated by $x_i$ and $y$ is all of $G$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Spread at least $k$

reading_title.source: Spread exactly $k$

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has spread exactly $k$, for a natural number $k$, when $G$ has spread at least $k$ and, for every natural number $m > k$, $G$ does not have spread at least $m$.
nodes.title: Spread exactly $k$

nodes.summary: The conjecture that there exists a group of spread exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Existence of a group of spread exactly one (Kourovka 21.38)

nodes.summary: There exists a group $G$ of spread exactly $1$: for every nontrivial $x \in G$ there is $y \in G$ with $\langle x, y \rangle = G$, but for every natural number $m > 1$ there are nontrivial elements $x_1, \dots, x_m \in G$ such that no single $y \in G$ satisfies $\langle x_i, y \rangle = G$ for all $i$. This answers Kourovka Problem 21.38 affirmatively.
nodes.title: There is a group of spread exactly one

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group. The spread $s(G)$ of $G$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of the natural numbers $k$ such that for any non-trivial elements $x_1, \dots, x_k$ of $G$ (not necessarily distinct) there exists $y \in G$ such that the subgroup $\langle x_i, y \rangle$ generated by $x_i$ and $y$ is all of $G$ for every $i$. In particular $s(G) = \infty$ when there is no largest such $k$.
nodes.title: Spread of a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Then the spread $s(G)$ is at least $2$ if and only if every proper quotient of $G$ is cyclic, that is, $G/N$ is cyclic for every non-trivial normal subgroup $N$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Burness–Guralnick–Harper spread theorem
Two-generated direct powers of simple groups

nodes.summary: The statement, in the form of its resolution, that for every non-abelian finite simple group $G$ there is a natural number $n$ with $n^2 > 4|G|$, that is, $n > 2\sqrt{|G|}$, such that the direct power $G^n$ is generated by two elements. The problem is due to A. Erfanian and J. Wiegold.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.116 (two-generated direct powers of simple groups)

nodes.summary: For every non-abelian finite simple group $G$ there is a natural number $n$ with $n^2 > 4|G|$, that is, $n > 2\sqrt{|G|}$, such that the direct power $G^n$ is generated by two elements. This answers Kourovka Problem 17.116 positively.
nodes.title: Maróti–Tamburini bound for two-generated direct powers

nodes.summary: Sylow theory and its generalization to sets of primes: Hall π-subgroups, the classes E_π, C_π and D_π, pronormality and intersections of Hall subgroups, groups whose maximal subgroups are Hall; questions on supplements of Sylow maximal subgroups forcing solubility go to Soluble and supersoluble finite groups.
nodes.title: Sylow and Hall subgroups
Groups with Hall maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall subgroup when its order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$, where an infinite order or index is counted as $0$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroup (Kourovka Problem 19.109)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is pronormal in $G$ when for every $g \in G$ there is an element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ such that $xHx^{-1} = gHg^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Pronormal subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $K$ of a group $G$ is second maximal when it is a maximal subgroup of a maximal subgroup of $G$: there is a maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $K < M$ and no subgroup $L$ of $G$ with $K < L < M$.
nodes.title: Second maximal subgroup

nodes.summary: For every non-abelian finite simple group $G$, all maximal subgroups of $G$ are Hall subgroups if and only if every second maximal subgroup of $G$ is pronormal in $G$.
nodes.title: Zenkov's question on Hall maximal subgroups (Kourovka Problem 19.109)

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every non-abelian finite simple group $G$, all maximal subgroups of $G$ are Hall subgroups if and only if every second maximal subgroup of $G$ is pronormal in $G$.
nodes.title: Negative answer to Zenkov's question (Kourovka Problem 19.109)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall subgroup when its order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroup (Kourovka 17.92)

nodes.summary: For groups $G$ and $S$, $S$ is a composition factor of $G$ when there are subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ such that $H$ is subnormal in $G$, $H \cap K$ is normal in $H$, and the quotient $H/(H \cap K)$ is a simple group isomorphic to $S$.
nodes.title: Composition factor of a group (Kourovka 17.92)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has this property when $G$ is not soluble and every maximal subgroup of $G$ is a Hall subgroup.
nodes.title: Non-soluble groups with Hall maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: The proposition that every non-abelian composition factor of a finite non-soluble group all of whose maximal subgroups are Hall subgroups is isomorphic to $L_2(7)$, $L_2(11)$ or $L_5(2)$. Here $L_n(q)$ is the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$, the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ by its centre.
nodes.title: Kourovka 17.92, first half: the possible composition factors

nodes.summary: The proposition that each of $L_2(7)$, $L_2(11)$ and $L_5(2)$ is a composition factor of some finite non-soluble group all of whose maximal subgroups are Hall subgroups. Here $L_n(q)$ is the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$, the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ by its centre.
nodes.title: Kourovka 17.92, second half: the three factors occur

nodes.summary: Every non-abelian composition factor of a finite non-soluble group all of whose maximal subgroups are Hall subgroups is isomorphic to $L_2(7)$, $L_2(11)$ or $L_5(2)$, so the first half of the answer to Kourovka 17.92 holds. Here $L_n(q)$ is the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$, the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ by its centre.
nodes.title: Maslova's theorem on groups with Hall maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: Each of $L_2(7)$, $L_2(11)$ and $L_5(2)$ is a composition factor of some finite non-soluble group all of whose maximal subgroups are Hall subgroups, so the second half of the answer to Kourovka 17.92 holds. Here $L_n(q)$ is the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$, the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ by its centre.
nodes.title: The three answer groups of Kourovka 17.92 occur
Hall π-subgroups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A natural number $n$ is a $\pi$-number when every prime divisor of $n$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: π-numbers (Kourovka 18.31)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a $\pi$-subgroup when its order is a $\pi$-number, that is, every prime divisor of $|H|$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: π-subgroups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when it is a $\pi$-subgroup and no prime divisor of its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: Hall π-subgroups (Kourovka 18.31)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a maximal $\pi$-subgroup when it is a $\pi$-subgroup and every $\pi$-subgroup $K$ of $G$ containing $H$ equals $H$.
nodes.title: Maximal π-subgroups (Kourovka 18.31)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ is a $D_\pi$-group when any two maximal $\pi$-subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ are conjugate, that is, $K = gHg^{-1}$ for some $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Dπ-groups

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. For a group $G$, the $\pi$-core $O_\pi(G)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by all normal $\pi$-subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: The π-core

nodes.summary: For every set $\pi$ of natural numbers and every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$, there are Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H_1$, $H_2$, $H_3$ of $G$, not necessarily distinct, with $H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3 = O_\pi(G)$, the $\pi$-core of $G$.
nodes.title: Three Hall π-subgroups meeting in the π-core (Kourovka 18.31)

nodes.summary: It is not the case that for every set $\pi$ of natural numbers every finite $D_\pi$-group $G$ has Hall $\pi$-subgroups $H_1$, $H_2$, $H_3$ with $H_1 \cap H_2 \cap H_3 = O_\pi(G)$, the $\pi$-core of $G$: the answer to Kourovka 18.31 is negative.
nodes.title: Three Hall π-subgroups need not meet in the π-core

reading_title.source: Overgroups of Hall subgroups in $C_\pi$-groups (Vdovin–Revin)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and let $G$ be a finite $C_\pi$-group. Then every subgroup $K$ of $G$ that contains a Hall $\pi$-subgroup of $G$ is itself a $C_\pi$-group. This answers Kourovka Problem 17.44(a) in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Overgroups of Hall subgroups in $C_\pi$-groups (Vdovin–Revin)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and let $G$ be a finite $D_\pi$-group. Then every subgroup $K$ of $G$ that contains a Hall $\pi$-subgroup of $G$ is itself a $D_\pi$-group. This answers Kourovka Problem 17.44(b) in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Overgroups of Hall subgroups in $D_\pi$-groups (Manzaeva, Vdovin–Manzaeva–Revin)

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A natural number $n$ is a $\pi$-number when every prime divisor of $n$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: π-numbers

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers and let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $G$. Then $H$ is a Hall $\pi$-subgroup when its order $|H|$ is a $\pi$-number and no prime divisor of its index $|G : H|$ lies in $\pi$.
nodes.title: Hall π-subgroups

parts: of groups with a Hall π-subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $\pi$ be a set of natural numbers. A group $G$ belongs to the class $E_\pi$ when $G$ has a Hall $\pi$-subgroup.
nodes.title: The class $E_\pi$ of groups with a Hall π-subgroup

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for all sets $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ of natural numbers, every finite group that has a Hall $\pi_1$-subgroup and a Hall $\pi_2$-subgroup also has a Hall $(\pi_1 \cap \pi_2)$-subgroup; that is, writing $E_\pi$ for the class of finite groups with a Hall $\pi$-subgroup, $E_{\pi_1} \cap E_{\pi_2}$ is contained in $E_{\pi_1 \cap \pi_2}$.
nodes.title: Zavarnitsine's question on Hall subgroups for intersections of prime sets

nodes.summary: For all sets $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ of natural numbers, every finite group that has a Hall $\pi_1$-subgroup and a Hall $\pi_2$-subgroup also has a Hall $(\pi_1 \cap \pi_2)$-subgroup; that is, writing $E_\pi$ for the class of finite groups with a Hall $\pi$-subgroup, $E_{\pi_1} \cap E_{\pi_2}$ is contained in $E_{\pi_1 \cap \pi_2}$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroups exist for intersections of prime sets
Pronormality of Hall subgroups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall subgroup when its order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroups (order coprime to index)

nodes.summary: Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H$ is pronormal in $K$ when for every $g \in K$ there is an element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ such that $xHx^{-1} = gHg^{-1}$, that is, $H$ and its conjugate $gHg^{-1}$ are conjugate by an element of $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$.
nodes.title: Pronormality in a subgroup

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every Hall subgroup $H$ of $G$ (a subgroup whose order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$), $H$ is pronormal in its normal closure $\langle H^G \rangle$, the smallest normal subgroup of $G$ containing $H$: for every $g \in \langle H^G \rangle$ there is an element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ with…
nodes.title: Vdovin–Revin question on Hall subgroups and their normal closures

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and a Hall subgroup $H$ of $G$ (that is, the order $|H|$ is coprime to the index $|G : H|$) such that $H$ is not pronormal in its normal closure $\langle H^G \rangle$, the smallest normal subgroup of $G$ containing $H$: for some $g \in \langle H^G \rangle$, no element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ satisfies $xHx^{-1} = gHg^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Hall subgroups need not be pronormal in their normal closure

nodes.summary: How subgroups sit inside a group: subnormal, permutable, propermutable, pronormal, polynormal and paranormal subgroups, maximal subgroups and their conjugates, intersections of conjugates of nilpotent subgroups and injectors with the Fitting subgroup, centralizer lattices and complemented subgroup lattices.
nodes.title: Subgroup embedding and subgroup lattices
Block lattices of groups

nodes.summary: Lattice terms in the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ are built inductively: each variable $x_n$ is a term, and for terms $s$ and $t$ their join $s \vee t$ and their meet $s \wedge t$ are terms.
nodes.title: Lattice terms

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a lattice and $v$ an assignment of an element $v(n)$ of $L$ to each variable $x_n$. The value of a lattice term under $v$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable $x_n$ has value $v(n)$, and a join $s \vee t$ or meet $s \wedge t$ has as value the join or meet in $L$ of the values of $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of lattice terms

nodes.summary: A subset $X$ of a group $G$ is a block if it is empty or a coset $gN$ of a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ (Kourovka Notebook, Archive 9.62). Ordered by inclusion, the blocks of $G$ form the block lattice $C(G)$.
nodes.title: Blocks of a group

nodes.summary: For subsets $X$ and $Y$ of a group $G$, their block join is the intersection of all blocks of $G$ that contain $X \cup Y$. Since blocks are closed under intersections and $G$ itself is a block, this is the smallest block containing $X \cup Y$; for blocks $X$ and $Y$ it is their join in the block lattice of $G$.
nodes.title: Join in the block lattice

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $v$ an assignment of a subset $v(n)$ of $G$ to each variable $x_n$. The value of a lattice term under $v$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable $x_n$ has value $v(n)$, a meet $s \wedge t$ has as value the intersection of the values of $s$ and $t$, and a join $s \vee t$ has as value the block join of the values of $s$ and $t$, the intersection of all blocks of $G$ containing their…
nodes.title: Evaluation of lattice terms in the block lattice

nodes.summary: Kourovka Problem 11.93: do block lattices generate all lattices? The proposition, asked by D. M. Smirnov, that the block lattices of finite groups generate the variety of all lattices. Here the blocks of a group $G$ are the cosets of normal subgroups of $G$ and the empty set; ordered by inclusion they form the block lattice of $G$, whose meet is intersection and whose join of two blocks is the intersection of all…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.93: do block lattices generate all lattices?

nodes.summary: The block lattices of finite groups do not generate the variety of all lattices: there are lattice terms $p$ and $q$ such that $p$ and $q$ take the same value in the block lattice of every finite group $G$ under every assignment of blocks of $G$ to the variables, but take different values in some lattice $L$ under some assignment of elements of $L$ to the variables. Here the blocks of $G$ are the cosets of normal…
nodes.title: Smirnov's negative answer to Kourovka Problem 11.93
Conjugacy of maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that in every finite simple group $G$, any two isomorphic maximal subgroups $X$ and $Y$ that are themselves simple groups are conjugate in $\operatorname{Aut} G$, that is, $\varphi(X) = Y$ for some automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Schmid's question on isomorphic simple maximal subgroups (Kourovka 18.115)

nodes.summary: There are a finite simple group $G$ and isomorphic maximal subgroups $X$ and $Y$ of $G$, both simple groups, such that no automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ satisfies $\varphi(X) = Y$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 18.115 is negative.
nodes.title: Isomorphic simple maximal subgroups need not be conjugate under automorphisms
Fully invariant subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ having, for every divisor $d$ of $|G|$, a fully invariant subgroup of order $d$ (a subgroup $H$ with $\varphi(H) \le H$ for every endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$) is cyclic.
nodes.title: MacHale's question on fully invariant subgroups (Kourovka 16.61)

nodes.summary: Not every finite group $G$ having, for every divisor $d$ of $|G|$, a fully invariant subgroup of order $d$ (a subgroup $H$ with $\varphi(H) \le H$ for every endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$) is cyclic.
nodes.title: Fully invariant subgroups of every order do not force cyclicity
Groups isomorphic to their normal subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that every nontrivial group that is isomorphic to each of its nontrivial normal subgroups is free of infinite rank (isomorphic to the free group on an infinite set), simple, or infinite cyclic.
nodes.title: Hall's question on groups isomorphic to their nontrivial normal subgroups (Kourovka 12.45)

nodes.summary: A group isomorphic to its nontrivial normal subgroups need not be free of infinite rank, simple or infinite cyclic. There is a nontrivial group $G$ that is isomorphic to each of its nontrivial normal subgroups and is neither free of infinite rank (isomorphic to the free group on an infinite set), nor simple, nor infinite cyclic. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 12.45 is negative (V. N. Obraztsov, 1997).
nodes.title: A group isomorphic to its nontrivial normal subgroups need not be free of infinite rank, simple or infinite cyclic
Groups with complemented subgroup lattices

parts: Kourovka Problem 11.128 on normal subgroups of
reading_title.source: Kourovka Problem 11.128 on normal subgroups of $K$-groups

nodes.summary: Call a group $G$ a $K$-group when its subgroup lattice is complemented: every subgroup $A$ of $G$ has a subgroup $B$ with $A \cap B = 1$ and $\langle A, B \rangle = G$. This is the assertion (M. Emaldi) that every normal subgroup of a $K$-group, viewed as a group in its own right, is again a $K$-group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.128 on normal subgroups of $K$-groups

reading_title.source: Normal subgroups of $K$-groups need not be $K$-groups

nodes.summary: There is a group $G$ whose subgroup lattice is complemented (a $K$-group) with a normal subgroup $N$ whose own subgroup lattice is not complemented; so Kourovka Problem 11.128 has a negative answer.
nodes.title: Normal subgroups of $K$-groups need not be $K$-groups
Groups with few maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: Kourovka 17.17 (G. M. Bergman) asks whether a finitely generated group with only finitely many maximal subgroups must be finite. This is the case of three maximal subgroups, which the problem singles out: every finitely generated group with exactly three maximal subgroups is finite.
nodes.title: Bergman's question for three maximal subgroups

nodes.summary: There is a finitely generated infinite group with exactly three maximal subgroups; that is, it is false that every finitely generated group with exactly three maximal subgroups is finite.
nodes.title: Not every finitely generated group with three maximal subgroups is finite
Intersections of conjugate nilpotent subgroups

nodes.summary: The assertion, in the two-subgroup form of its resolution, that for every finite non-abelian simple group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ with $A \cap x B x^{-1} = 1$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 15.40

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian simple group and let $A$ and $B$ be nilpotent subgroups of $G$. Then there is $x \in G$ with $A \cap x B x^{-1} = 1$.
nodes.title: Nilpotent subgroups of a finite simple group have conjugates meeting trivially

nodes.summary: The Fitting subgroup `F(G)`: the join of the nilpotent normal subgroups of `G` (for finite `G` the largest nilpotent normal subgroup).
nodes.title: Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: The assertion that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$ there are $x, y \in G$ with $N \cap x N x^{-1} \cap y N y^{-1} \le F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.40

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent subgroup $N$ of $G$ there are $x, y \in G$ with $N \cap x N x^{-1} \cap y N y^{-1} \le F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Three conjugates of a nilpotent subgroup meet inside the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, this is the set of all subgroups of $G$ of the form $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$, that is, the intersections of $A$ with a conjugate of $B$ and a conjugate of $C$.
nodes.title: Triple intersections with conjugates

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such intersections, that is, that contain no other intersection of this form.
nodes.title: Subgroup generated by the inclusion-minimal triple intersections

nodes.summary: For subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of a group $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) whose order is at most the order of every such intersection.
nodes.title: Subgroup generated by the triple intersections of least order

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ generated by the intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) of least order is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Minimal-order triple intersections and the Fitting subgroup (Kourovka 20.122(a), (c))

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such intersections is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Inclusion-minimal triple intersections and the Fitting subgroup (Kourovka 20.122(b), (c))

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\min_G(A, B, C)$ generated by the intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) of least order is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Minimal-order triple intersections need not lie in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite soluble group $G$ and all nilpotent subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$, the subgroup $\mathrm{Min}_G(A, B, C)$ generated by those intersections $A \cap xBx^{-1} \cap yCy^{-1}$ ($x, y \in G$) that are minimal by inclusion among all such intersections is contained in the Fitting subgroup $F(G)$, the join of all nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Inclusion-minimal triple intersections need not lie in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a nilpotent injector when, for every subnormal subgroup $K$ of $G$, the intersection $H \cap K$ is nilpotent and is a maximal nilpotent subgroup of $K$: every nilpotent subgroup $L$ of $G$ with $H \cap K \le L \le K$ equals $H \cap K$.
nodes.title: Nilpotent injector

nodes.summary: The assertion that there is a natural number $k$ such that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, \dots, g_k \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap \dots \cap g_k H g_k^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.37(a)

nodes.summary: The assertion that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap g_2 H g_2^{-1} \cap g_3 H g_3^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.37(b)

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $k$ such that for every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, \dots, g_k \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap \dots \cap g_k H g_k^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Boundedly many conjugates of a nilpotent injector meet in the Fitting subgroup

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every nilpotent injector $H$ of $G$ there are elements $g_1, g_2, g_3 \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $g_1 H g_1^{-1} \cap g_2 H g_2^{-1} \cap g_3 H g_3^{-1} = F(G)$, where $F(G)$ is the Fitting subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Three conjugates of a nilpotent injector meet in the Fitting subgroup
Lattices of centralizers

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a centralizer if $H = C_G(X)$ for some subset $X \subseteq G$, where $C_G(X)$ is the subgroup of elements of $G$ that commute with every element of $X$.
nodes.title: Centralizer subgroups

nodes.summary: Call a subgroup of a group $G$ a centralizer if it equals $C_G(X)$ for some subset $X \subseteq G$. This is the proposition that for every group $G$ in which the join (in the subgroup lattice) of any two centralizers is again a centralizer, any three centralizers $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$ with $A \le C$ satisfy the modular law $(A \sqcup B) \sqcap C = A \sqcup (B \sqcap C)$, where $\sqcup$ and $\sqcap$ are the join and…
nodes.title: Modularity of centralizer sublattices (Kourovka 11.4)

nodes.summary: Call a subgroup of a group $G$ a centralizer if it equals $C_G(X)$ for some subset $X \subseteq G$. Modularity of centralizer sublattices fails: there is a group $G$ in which the join (in the subgroup lattice) of any two centralizers is again a centralizer, but which has centralizers $A$, $B$, $C$ with $A \le C$ and $(A \sqcup B) \sqcap C \ne A \sqcup (B \sqcap C)$, where $\sqcup$ and $\sqcap$ are the join and meet…
nodes.title: Lattices of centralizers need not be modular (Kourovka 11.4)
Maximal soluble subgroups

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 14.62: a maximal soluble subgroup whose normalizer supplements

nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.
nodes.title: Zenkov–Monakhov–Revin theorem (Kourovka 14.62)
Permutable subgroups of alternating groups

reading_title.source: $G$-permutable subgroups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $G$-permutable when for every subgroup $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ such that $A B^x = B^x A$, where $B^x = x B x^{-1}$ is the conjugate of $B$ by $x$ and the products are products of subsets of $G$.
nodes.title: $G$-permutable subgroups

nodes.summary: This proposition asserts that there is a natural number $n$ such that for every $m > n$, every $A_m$-permutable subgroup of the alternating group $A_m$ is either the trivial subgroup or $A_m$ itself. Here a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $G$-permutable when for every subgroup $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ with $A B^x = B^x A$, where $B^x = x B x^{-1}$ is the conjugate of $B$ by $x$ and products of subgroups are…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.37 on permutable subgroups of alternating groups

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $n$ such that for every $m > n$, every $A_m$-permutable subgroup of the alternating group $A_m$ is either the trivial subgroup or $A_m$ itself. Here a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is $G$-permutable when for every subgroup $B$ of $G$ there is $x \in G$ with $A B^x = B^x A$, where $B^x = x B x^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Permutable subgroups of large alternating groups are trivial or the whole group
Polynormal and paranormal subgroups

nodes.summary: For a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ and an element $x \in G$, the conjugate subgroup is $A^x = x^{-1} A x = \{x^{-1} a x : a \in A\}$.
nodes.title: Conjugate subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is paranormal (Z. I. Borevich) when, for every $x \in G$, the conjugate $A^x = x^{-1} A x$ is contained in the subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^u$ with $u$ in the subgroup $\langle A, A^x \rangle$ generated by $A$ and $A^x$.
nodes.title: Paranormal subgroup

nodes.summary: A subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ is polynormal (Z. I. Borevich) when, for every $x \in G$, the conjugate $A^x = x^{-1} A x$ is contained in the subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^u$ with $u \in A^{\langle x \rangle}$, where $A^{\langle x \rangle}$ is the subgroup generated by the conjugates $A^{x^n}$ with $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Polynormal subgroup

nodes.summary: Kourovka 14.50 (Z. I. Borevich; A. S. Kondratiev): every polynormal subgroup of a finite group is paranormal.
nodes.title: Polynormal subgroups of finite groups are paranormal

nodes.summary: There is a finite group $G$ with a subgroup $A$ that is polynormal but not paranormal. So the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 14.50 is false.
nodes.title: A polynormal subgroup that is not paranormal (Kourovka 14.50 refuted)
Pronormal subgroups

nodes.summary: The statement that there is an infinite group $G$ in which every pronormal subgroup is trivial or equal to $G$. Here a subgroup $H$ of $G$ is pronormal when, for every $g \in G$, the subgroups $H$ and $H^g = gHg^{-1}$ are conjugate by an element of $\langle H, H^g \rangle$.
nodes.title: Infinite groups without nontrivial proper pronormal subgroups (Kourovka 19.74, Revin)

nodes.summary: There is an infinite group $G$ in which every pronormal subgroup is trivial or equal to $G$. Here a subgroup $H$ of $G$ is pronormal when, for every $g \in G$, the subgroups $H$ and $H^g = gHg^{-1}$ are conjugate by an element of $\langle H, H^g \rangle$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.74 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: An infinite group without nontrivial proper pronormal subgroups exists
Propermutable subgroups

nodes.summary: Let $H$ and $X$ be subgroups of a group $G$. Then $H$ permutes with $X$ when $HX = XH$ as subsets of $G$, where $HX = \{hx : h \in H, x \in X\}$ and $XH = \{xh : x \in X, h \in H\}$.
nodes.title: Permuting subgroups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is propermutable in $G$ when there is a subgroup $B$ of $G$ with $G = N_G(H)B$ (every element of $G$ is a product $nb$ with $n$ in the normalizer $N_G(H)$ of $H$ and $b \in B$) such that $H$ permutes with every subgroup $X$ of $B$, that is, $HX = XH$.
nodes.title: Propermutable subgroups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is $2$-nilpotent when it has a normal subgroup $N$ of finite odd order whose index in $G$ is $2^k$ for some natural number $k$.
nodes.title: 2-nilpotent groups

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (A. N. Skiba): there exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(a) (statement)

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (A. N. Skiba), with the range $1 \le k < n$: let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.91(b) (statement)

nodes.summary: There exist a finite group $G$ and subgroups $A \le B \le G$ such that $A$ is propermutable in $G$ but $A$, regarded as a subgroup of $B$, is not propermutable in $B$. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(a).
nodes.title: Propermutability is not inherited by intermediate subgroups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $P$ a non-abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$, with $|P| = 2^n$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $1 \le k < n$. If every subgroup of $P$ of order $2^k$ is propermutable in $G$, and, when $k = 1$, every cyclic subgroup of $P$ of order $4$ is propermutable in $G$, then $G$ is $2$-nilpotent. This is the positive answer to Kourovka Problem 18.91(b).
nodes.title: Propermutable subgroups of a non-abelian Sylow 2-subgroup force 2-nilpotency
Subgroup lattices of Chernikov groups

nodes.summary: A group $Q$ is quasicyclic if it is abelian and infinite and every proper subgroup of $Q$ is finite.
nodes.title: Quasicyclic group

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is a Chernikov group if it has a normal subgroup of finite index that is isomorphic to a direct product $Q_1 \times \dots \times Q_r$ of finitely many quasicyclic groups $Q_1, \dots, Q_r$. The case $r = 0$ is allowed, so every finite group is a Chernikov group.
nodes.title: Chernikov group

nodes.summary: A group $G$ contains a direct product of two quasicyclic groups over the same prime when there are a quasicyclic group $Q$ and an injective group homomorphism $Q \times Q \to G$ (quasicyclic groups over the same prime are isomorphic).
nodes.title: Groups containing the square of a quasicyclic group

nodes.summary: A partially ordered set has finite (order) dimension: its order relation is the intersection of finitely many linear orders on the same set.
nodes.title: Poset of finite order dimension

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every Chernikov group $G$ that does not contain a direct product of two quasicyclic groups over the same prime (that is, there is no quasicyclic group $Q$ with an injective homomorphism $Q \times Q \to G$), the lattice of subgroups of $G$ has finite order dimension: the inclusion order on the subgroups of $G$ is the intersection of finitely many linear orders on that set. nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a finite $p$-group of order $p^n$. Then there are subgroups $G = H_0 \supseteq H_1 \supseteq \cdots \supseteq H_n = \{1\}$ such that for each $i < n$, $H_{i+1}$ is a normal subgroup of $H_i$ and there is a surjective homomorphism $H_i \to \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with kernel $H_{i+1}$. By the first isomorphism theorem, $H_i / H_{i+1} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ for each $i < n$.
