Geometric equivalence of groups

nodes.summary: A quasi-identity consists of a natural number $n$, a finite list of premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and a conclusion $w$, all elements of the free group $F_n$ on the unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. It stands for the formula $\forall x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}\, (w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$.
nodes.title: Quasi-identities of groups

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a quasi-identity with unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and conclusion $w$, all in the free group $F_n$ on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. For $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1}$ in a group $G$ and $u \in F_n$, write $u(g_0, \dots, g_{n-1})$ for the image of $u$ under the homomorphism $F_n \to G$ sending each $x_j$ to $g_j$. Then $q$ holds in $G$ when for all $g_0, \dots, g_{n-1} \in G$ with…
nodes.title: Satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $F_n$ be the free group on the basis $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$, and let $T \subseteq F_n$. The $G$-closure $\mathrm{cl}_G(T)$ is the set of $w \in F_n$ such that $\mu(w) = 1$ for every homomorphism $\mu : F_n \to G$ with $\mu(t) = 1$ for all $t \in T$, that is, the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms $F_n \to G$ that vanish on $T$.
nodes.title: Closure of a set of words with respect to a group

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ are geometrically equivalent (B. I. Plotkin) when $\mathrm{cl}_G(T) = \mathrm{cl}_H(T)$ for every natural number $n$ and every subset $T$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, where $\mathrm{cl}_G(T)$ is the $G$-closure of $T$: the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms $F_n \to G$ that vanish on $T$.
nodes.title: Geometrically equivalent groups

nodes.summary: The proposition (Kourovka Problem 14.71, B. I. Plotkin) that any two groups $G$ and $H$ satisfying the same quasi-identities, meaning that every quasi-identity holds in $G$ if and only if it holds in $H$, are geometrically equivalent.
nodes.title: Plotkin's problem on quasi-identities and geometric equivalence

nodes.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 14.71 is false: there are groups $G$ and $H$ such that every quasi-identity holds in $G$ if and only if it holds in $H$, but $G$ and $H$ are not geometrically equivalent.
nodes.title: Groups with the same quasi-identities need not be geometrically equivalent
Hall's verbal conjectures

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is relatively free if it has a family $(x_i)_{i \in I}$ of elements that generates $G$ such that for every family $(y_i)_{i \in I}$ of elements of $G$ there is an endomorphism $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(x_i) = y_i$ for all $i \in I$.
nodes.title: Relatively free group

nodes.summary: For a word $v$ in the free group on $n$ generators and a group $G$, the set of values of $v$ on $G$ is the set of elements $v(g_1, \dots, g_n)$ obtained by substituting elements $g_1, \dots, g_n \in G$ for the generators, that is, the set of images of $v$ under all homomorphisms from that free group to $G$.
nodes.title: Values of a word

nodes.summary: The statement that for every relatively free group $G$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every word $v$ in the free group on $n$ generators, if $v$ takes only finitely many values on $G$, then the verbal subgroup $v(G)$ of $G$ generated by these values is finite.
nodes.title: Hall's verbal finiteness conjecture for relatively free groups (Kourovka 12.31)

nodes.summary: Hall's verbal finiteness conjecture for relatively free groups is false: there are a relatively free group $G$, a natural number $n$ and a word $v$ in the free group on $n$ generators such that $v$ takes only finitely many values on $G$ but the verbal subgroup $v(G)$ of $G$ generated by these values is infinite.
nodes.title: Hall's conjecture fails for relatively free groups
Lattices of quasivarieties

nodes.summary: For a group $K$, a group $X$ lies in the class $Q(K)$ when $X$ embeds in a direct power of $K$: there are a set $I$ and an injective homomorphism $X \to K^I$.
nodes.title: Quasivariety generated by a finite group

nodes.summary: For groups $G$ and $H$, a group $X$ lies in the class $Q(G, H)$ when $X$ embeds in the product of a direct power of $G$ and a direct power of $H$: there are sets $I$ and $J$ and an injective homomorphism $X \to G^I \times H^J$.

Presentations in the torsion-free quasivariety

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $F_n$ be the free group on the $n$ letters $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and let $S$ be a subset of $F_n$. The relation subgroup of $S$ in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups is the intersection of all normal subgroups $N$ of $F_n$ that contain $S$ and satisfy the following: for every $x \in F_n$ and every integer $k \ge 1$, if $x^k \in N$ then $x \in N$. Equivalently, it is the least…
nodes.title: Relation subgroup of a torsion-free presentation

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is finitely presented in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups if there are a natural number $n$, a finite subset $S$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ letters, and a surjective homomorphism $f \colon F_n \to G$ whose kernel is the relation subgroup of $S$ in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups.
nodes.title: Groups finitely presented in the torsion-free quasivariety

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that is finitely presented in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups but is not a finitely presented group.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.17 (statement)

nodes.summary: There is a torsion-free group $G$ (no element of $G$ other than the identity has finite order) that is finitely presented in the quasivariety of torsion-free groups but is not a finitely presented group.
nodes.title: Budkin's theorem (Kourovka Problem 18.17)
Quasivarieties of groups

nodes.summary: A quasi-identity in $n$ unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ is a formula $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$, given by the number $n$, a finite list of premises $w_1, \dots, w_k$ and a conclusion $w$, all of them elements of the free group on $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Quasi-identities of groups

nodes.summary: A quasi-identity $\forall x\,(w_1 = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_k = 1 \to w = 1)$ in the unknowns $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ holds in a group $G$ when every assignment of elements of $G$ to the unknowns under which each premise $w_1, \dots, w_k$ evaluates to $1$ in $G$ also makes the conclusion $w$ evaluate to $1$.
nodes.title: Quasi-identities holding in a group

nodes.summary: For a set $Q$ of quasi-identities, a group $H$ belongs to the quasivariety defined by $Q$ when every quasi-identity in $Q$ holds in $H$. Every quasivariety of groups has this form.
nodes.title: The quasivariety defined by a set of quasi-identities

nodes.summary: The quasi-theory of a group $G$ is the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. The quasivariety defined by this set is the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$.
nodes.title: The quasi-identities of a group

nodes.summary: For sets $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ of quasi-identities, the quasivariety defined by $Q_1$ is contained in the quasivariety defined by $Q_2$: every group in which all quasi-identities of $Q_1$ hold also satisfies all quasi-identities of $Q_2$.
nodes.title: Inclusion of quasivarieties

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $qG$ be the quasivariety generated by $G$, that is, the quasivariety defined by the set of all quasi-identities that hold in $G$. A set $Q$ of quasi-identities defines a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$ when the quasivariety defined by $Q$ is contained in $qG$ but does not contain $qG$, and every quasivariety $V$ defined by a set of quasi-identities with $V$ containing the…
nodes.title: Maximal proper subquasivarieties

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a finitely generated group $G$ such that the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$ has infinitely many maximal proper subquasivarieties: for every natural number $k$ there are sets of quasi-identities $Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1}$, each defining a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$, such that for $i \ne j$ the quasivarieties defined by $Q_i$ and $Q_j$ are different.
nodes.title: Budkin's problem on maximal subquasivarieties (Kourovka 14.25)

nodes.summary: There is a finitely generated group $G$ such that the quasivariety $qG$ generated by $G$ has infinitely many maximal proper subquasivarieties: for every natural number $k$ there are sets of quasi-identities $Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1}$, each defining a maximal proper subquasivariety of $qG$, such that for $i \ne j$ the quasivarieties defined by $Q_i$ and $Q_j$ are different.
nodes.title: Some finitely generated group has infinitely many maximal subquasivarieties
Independent bases of laws

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on countably many generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$, let $W \subseteq F$ be a set of laws and let $w \in F$. Then $w$ is a consequence of $W$ if $w$ holds in every group $G$ satisfying all laws in $W$: whenever every homomorphism $F \to G$ sends each element of $W$ to $1$, every homomorphism $F \to G$ sends $w$ to $1$.
nodes.title: Consequence of a set of laws

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on countably many generators $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ and let $W \subseteq F$ be a set of laws. The variety defined by $W$ has an independent basis of identities if there is a set $B \subseteq F$ of laws such that a law is a consequence of $B$ exactly when it is a consequence of $W$, and no $b \in B$ is a consequence of $B \setminus \{b\}$.
nodes.title: Independent basis of laws

nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be a set of quasi-identities and $q$ a quasi-identity. Then $q$ is a consequence of $Q$ if $q$ holds in every group in which all members of $Q$ hold.
nodes.title: Consequence of a set of quasi-identities

nodes.summary: The quasi-identities of a group $G$ have an independent basis if there is a set $B$ of quasi-identities such that a quasi-identity is a consequence of $B$ exactly when it holds in $G$, and no $b \in B$ is a consequence of $B \setminus \{b\}$.
nodes.title: Independent basis of quasi-identities
Test ranks of relatively free groups

nodes.summary: Let $F_\mathbb{N}$ be the free group on countably many generators and $W \subseteq F_\mathbb{N}$ a set of words, the laws. A group $G$ satisfies the laws $W$ when $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every $w \in W$ and every homomorphism $\varphi \colon F_\mathbb{N} \to G$, that is, every law takes the value $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. The variety defined by $W$ is the class of these groups.
nodes.title: Groups satisfying a set of laws in countably many variables

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a set of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, and let $F_r$ be the free group on $r$ generators. The verbal subgroup $V_W(F_r)$ of $F_r$ for $W$ is the normal closure in $F_r$ of all elements $\varphi(w)$ with $w \in W$ and $\varphi \colon F_\mathbb{N} \to F_r$ a homomorphism.
nodes.title: Verbal subgroup of a free group of finite rank

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a set of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. The free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ is the quotient $F_r / V_W(F_r)$ of the free group $F_r$ on $r$ generators by its verbal subgroup $V_W(F_r)$ for $W$.
nodes.title: Relatively free group as a quotient of a free group

nodes.summary: A subset $S$ of a group $G$ is a test set when every endomorphism of $G$ that fixes every element of $S$ is bijective, that is, an automorphism of $G$.
nodes.title: Test set of a group

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has test rank $r \in \mathbb{N}$ when $G$ has a test set of cardinality $r$ and every test set of $G$ has cardinality at least $r$ (an infinite set counting as having cardinality $\infty$), that is, when the minimum of the cardinalities of the test sets of $G$ is $r$.
nodes.title: Test rank of a group

nodes.summary: The statement that for every set $W$ of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, if for every $r \ge 1$ the free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ has test rank $r$, then this variety is abelian: every group satisfying the laws $W$ is abelian.
nodes.title: Timoshenko's test rank question, part (a)

nodes.summary: The statement that for every set $W$ of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, if for every $r \ge 1$ the free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ has test rank $r$ and the variety is not periodic (there is no $n > 0$ with $g^n = 1$ for every element $g$ of every group satisfying $W$), then the variety is the variety of all abelian groups: a group satisfies the laws…
nodes.title: Timoshenko's test rank question, part (b)

nodes.summary: There is a set $W$ of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators such that for every $r \ge 1$ the free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ has test rank $r$, but the variety is not abelian: some group satisfying the laws $W$ is not abelian.
nodes.title: Negative answer to Timoshenko's test rank question, part (a)

Basic commutators

nodes.summary: The formal commutators (bracket arrangements) in an alphabet $\alpha$ are the formal expressions generated by two rules: every letter $a \in \alpha$ is a formal commutator, and for formal commutators $u$ and $v$, the bracket $[u, v]$ is a formal commutator.
nodes.title: Formal commutators

nodes.summary: The weight of a formal commutator is the number of occurrences of letters in it: a letter has weight $1$, and $[u, v]$ has weight the weight of $u$ plus the weight of $v$.
nodes.title: Weight of a formal commutator

nodes.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a group, their commutator is $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$ (the convention of the Kourovka Notebook and of Hall).
nodes.title: Commutator, Kourovka–Hall convention

nodes.summary: Each formal commutator in the letters $\alpha$ has a value in the free group $F(\alpha)$ on $\alpha$: a letter $a$ has the value of the generator $a$, and $[u, v]$ has the value $\bar u^{-1} \bar v^{-1} \bar u \bar v$, where $\bar u$ and $\bar v$ are the values of $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Value of a formal commutator

nodes.summary: Let $<$ be a relation on the formal commutators in the letters $\alpha$ (in applications, a linear order). Every letter is basic for $<$, and a formal commutator $[u, v]$ is basic for $<$ when $u$ and $v$ are basic for $<$, $v < u$, and, in case $u = [y, z]$ is itself a bracket, $v < z$ fails (for a linear order: $z \le v$). This is M. Hall's definition.
nodes.title: Basic commutators

For every linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every linear order $<$ on the formal commutators in the letters $\alpha$ that orders the letters as in $\alpha$ and puts formal commutators of smaller weight first (within one weight it is arbitrary), if $a$ and $b$ are formal commutators…

Commutator power identities

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every group $G$ with $[x, y]^n = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$, every element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ has finite order, that is, the derived subgroup of $G$ is periodic.
nodes.title: Derived subgroups under a commutator power identity (Kourovka 13.34)

nodes.summary: There exist an integer $n \ge 1$ and a group $G$ such that $[x, y]^n = 1$ for all $x, y \in G$ but some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ has infinite order. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 13.34 (I. D. Macdonald; V. D. Mazurov) in the negative, by results of G. S. Deryabina and P. A. Kozhevnikov from 1999 and of S. I. Adyan from 2000.
nodes.title: A commutator power identity need not make the derived subgroup periodic
Commutator width

reading_title.source: Products of at most $n$ commutators (Kourovka 14.15)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. An element $z \in G$ is a product of at most $n$ commutators when there are $m \le n$ and elements $x_1, y_1, \dots, x_m, y_m \in G$ with $z = [x_1, y_1] \cdots [x_m, y_m]$, where $[x, y] = xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$; for $m = 0$ the empty product is the identity.
nodes.title: Products of at most $n$ commutators (Kourovka 14.15)

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every $n \ge 3$, writing $F_n$ for the free group on $n$ generators, and for every natural number $k$, some element of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is not a product of at most $k$ commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ of elements of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$. This is the answer $k_n = \infty$ to Bardakov's question, which asks for the supremum $k_n$ of the commutator lengths of…
nodes.title: Unbounded commutator length in Aut(Fₙ) (Kourovka 14.15)

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators. For every natural number $k$ there is an element of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ that is not a product of at most $k$ commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in \operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$. Equivalently, the supremum $k_n$ of the commutator lengths of the elements of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Commutator length in Aut(Fₙ) is unbounded

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, a natural number $m$ and $g \in G$, $g$ is a product of at most $m$ commutators when there are $k \le m$ and $a_1, b_1, \dots, a_k, b_k \in G$ with $g = [a_1, b_1] \cdots [a_k, b_k]$, where $[a, b] = aba^{-1}b^{-1}$; for $k = 0$ the empty product is the identity.
nodes.title: Products of a bounded number of commutators

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with derived subgroup $G'$, the commutator width $w(G')$ is the least positive integer $m$ such that every element of $G'$ is a product of at most $m$ commutators $aba^{-1}b^{-1}$ with $a, b \in G$; it is $0$ when no such $m$ exists.
nodes.title: Commutator width of the derived subgroup

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian group $G$ the commutator width $w(G')$ of its derived subgroup $G'$ satisfies $w(G')/|G| \le 1/6$, and that for the symmetric group $S_3$ equality holds: $w(S_3')/|S_3| = 1/6$.
nodes.title: Bardakov's commutator width ratio claim (Kourovka 16.8)

nodes.summary: For every finite non-abelian group $G$, the commutator width $w(G')$ of its derived subgroup satisfies $w(G')/|G| \le 1/6$, and for the symmetric group $S_3$ equality holds, $w(S_3')/|S_3| = 1/6$; so Kourovka Problem 16.8 has a positive answer.
nodes.title: The maximal commutator width ratio is one sixth

reading_title.source: Products of at most $n$ commutators

nodes.summary: An element $z$ of a group $G$ is a product of at most $n$ commutators when $z = [x_1, y_1] \cdots [x_k, y_k]$ for some $k \le n$ and some $x_1, y_1, \dots, x_k, y_k \in G$, where $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$; for $k = 0$ the product is the identity.
nodes.title: Products of at most $n$ commutators

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has unbounded commutator length when for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Unbounded commutator length

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 14.13(a) (Bardakov)

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a finitely presented simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 14.13(b) (Bardakov)

nodes.summary: There is a simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.13(a) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Archive records examples constructed by Barge and Ghys, and finitely generated ones by Muranov.
nodes.title: A simple group with unbounded commutator length

nodes.summary: There is a finitely presented simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.13(b) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Archive cites Caprace and Fujiwara.
nodes.title: A finitely presented simple group with unbounded commutator length
Engel conditions on involutions

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has this property when every element of $G$ has order a power of $2$, $G$ is generated by its involutions, and $[[x, u], u] = 1$ for every $x \in G$ and every involution $u \in G$, where $[x, u] = x^{-1} u^{-1} x u$.
nodes.title: Involution-generated 2-groups with the Engel condition on involutions

nodes.summary: The proposition (Kourovka 18.57, D. V. Lytkina) that there is a natural number $d$ such that $G^{(d)} = 1$ for every finite group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $2$, which is generated by its involutions, and in which $[[x, u], u] = 1$ for every $x \in G$ and every involution $u \in G$; here $[x, u] = x^{-1} u^{-1} x u$ and $G^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series of $G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 18.57 on the derived length of involution-generated 2-groups

nodes.summary: There is no natural number $d$ such that $G^{(d)} = 1$ for every finite group $G$ in which every element has order a power of $2$, which is generated by its involutions, and in which $[[x, u], u] = 1$ for every $x \in G$ and every involution $u \in G$; here $[x, u] = x^{-1} u^{-1} x u$ and $G^{(d)}$ is the $d$-th term of the derived series of $G$. Thus the derived length of such groups is unbounded.
nodes.title: Negative answer to Kourovka Problem 18.57
Engel elements

nodes.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a group, the commutator is $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$ (the convention of the Kourovka Notebook).
nodes.title: Commutator for Engel lengths

nodes.summary: For elements $h$ and $g$ of a group and a natural number $l$, the iterated commutator $[h, g; l]$ is defined by $[h, g; 0] = h$ and $[h, g; l + 1] = [[h, g; l], g]$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$; in particular $[h, g; 1] = [h, g]$.
nodes.title: Iterated commutators for Engel lengths

nodes.summary: An element $g$ of a group $G$ is an Engel element if there is an $l \ge 1$ such that $[h, g; l] = 1$ for every $h \in G$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$, $[h, g; i + 1] = [[h, g; i], g]$ and $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$.
nodes.title: Bounded Engel element

nodes.summary: For an element $g$ of a group $G$, the Engel length $l(g)$ is the least $k \ge 1$ such that $[h, g; k] = 1$ for every $h \in G$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$, $[h, g; i + 1] = [[h, g; i], g]$ and $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$. If no such $k$ exists, that is, if $g$ is not an Engel element, then $l(g) = 0$.
nodes.title: Engel length

nodes.summary: The statement that every group $G$ has a polynomial $\varphi(x, y)$ in two variables with natural-number coefficients such that $l(uv) \le \varphi(l(u), l(v))$ for all $u, v \in G$ for which $u$, $v$ and $uv$ are Engel elements. Here $g \in G$ is an Engel element if there is a $k \ge 1$ with $[h, g; k] = 1$ for all $h \in G$, and its Engel length $l(g)$ is the least such $k$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$,…
nodes.title: Roman'kov's problem on Engel lengths of products (Kourovka 11.88)

nodes.summary: There is a group $G$ such that for every polynomial $\varphi(x, y)$ in two variables with natural-number coefficients there are $u, v \in G$ such that $u$, $v$ and $uv$ are Engel elements and $l(uv) > \varphi(l(u), l(v))$. Here $g \in G$ is an Engel element if there is a $k \ge 1$ with $[h, g; k] = 1$ for all $h \in G$, and its Engel length $l(g)$ is the least such $k$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$,…
nodes.title: Engel lengths of products admit no polynomial bound (Kourovka 11.88)

nodes.summary: An element $g$ of a group $G$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ there is an $n \ge 0$ with $h_n = 1$, where $h_0 = h$ and $h_{i + 1} = [h_i, g]$ with $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$; that is, some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Engel element

nodes.summary: The statement that no non-abelian simple group contains an Engel element other than the identity: for every simple group $G$ with elements $a$, $b$ such that $ab \ne ba$, every Engel element $g$ of $G$ satisfies $g = 1$. Here $g$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial, where $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$.
nodes.title: Bludov's problem on Engel elements in simple groups (Kourovka 16.17)

nodes.summary: There is a non-abelian simple group $G$ (one with elements $a$, $b$ such that $ab \ne ba$) that contains an Engel element $g \ne 1$. Here $g$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial, where $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$.
nodes.title: Non-abelian simple groups can have nontrivial Engel elements (Kourovka 16.17)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, an element $a$ of a group $G$ is a right $n$-Engel element when $[a, {}_n x] = 1$ for every $x \in G$, where $[y, x] = y^{-1} x^{-1} y x$ and $[a, {}_n x] = [\dots[[a, x], x], \dots, x]$ is the left-normed commutator with $n$ copies of $x$ (so $[a, {}_0 x] = a$).
nodes.title: Right Engel element

nodes.summary: The statement that there are functions $e, c \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $e(n) > 0$ for every $n$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every nilpotent group $G$ and every normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ all of whose elements are right $n$-Engel elements of $G$, the subgroup $H^{e(n)}$ generated by the $e(n)$-th powers of elements of $H$ is contained in the $c(n)$-th term $\zeta_{c(n)}(G)$ of the upper…
nodes.title: Abdollahi's question on right Engel subgroups (Kourovka Problem 17.12)

nodes.summary: There are functions $e, c \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $e(n) > 0$ for every $n$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every nilpotent group $G$ and every normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ all of whose elements are right $n$-Engel elements of $G$, the subgroup $H^{e(n)}$ generated by the $e(n)$-th powers of elements of $H$ is contained in the $c(n)$-th term $\zeta_{c(n)}(G)$ of the upper central series of $G$.
nodes.title: Positive answer to Abdollahi's question on right Engel subgroups (Kourovka Problem 17.12)
Groups with unique ordered-product normal forms

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is polycyclic if it has a finite series of subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ in which each $H_i$ is normal in $H_{i+1}$ and each quotient $H_{i+1} / H_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Polycyclic groups (Kourovka Problem 13.11)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is almost polycyclic, or virtually polycyclic, if some subgroup of finite index in $G$ is polycyclic.
nodes.title: Almost polycyclic groups (Kourovka Problem 13.11)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has a unique product presentation if there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and elements $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1} \in G$ such that every element of $G$ equals $a_0^{k_0} a_1^{k_1} \cdots a_{n-1}^{k_{n-1}}$ for exactly one tuple $(k_0, \dots, k_{n-1}) \in \mathbb{Z}^n$.
nodes.title: Groups with a unique product presentation

nodes.summary: The statement, asked by V. V. Bludov, that every group $G$ which is torsion-free (no element of $G$ other than $1$ has finite order) and has a unique product presentation is almost polycyclic.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.11 (torsion-free groups with a unique product presentation)

nodes.summary: Not every torsion-free group with a unique product presentation is almost polycyclic: there is a group $G$ in which no element other than $1$ has finite order, which has a unique product presentation, and which is not almost polycyclic.
nodes.title: A torsion-free group with a unique product presentation need not be almost polycyclic
Intersection of the derived series

nodes.summary: The conjecture of R. Mikhailov that for every finitely presented group $G$, the intersection $D = \bigcap_{n} G^{(n)}$ of the terms $G^{(n)}$ of the derived series of $G$ satisfies $[D, D] = D$, that is, $D$ has trivial abelianization.
nodes.title: Perfectness of the intersection of the derived series (Kourovka 17.82)

nodes.summary: There exists a finitely presented group $G$ such that the intersection $D = \bigcap_{n} G^{(n)}$ of the terms $G^{(n)}$ of the derived series of $G$ satisfies $[D, D] \ne D$. That is, the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 17.82 is false; the Kourovka Archive credits this answer to V. A. Roman'kov (2011).
nodes.title: The intersection of the derived series need not be perfect
Local word identities

nodes.summary: The statement that for every connected Hausdorff topological group $G$ and every word $W(x, y)$ in the free group on two generators $x$, $y$, if $W(a, b) = 1$ for all $(a, b)$ in some nonempty open subset of $G \times G$, then $W(a, b) = 1$ for all $a, b \in G$.
nodes.title: Local word identities in connected groups (Kourovka 18.71)

nodes.summary: There are a connected Hausdorff topological group $G$, a word $W(x, y)$ in the free group on two generators $x$, $y$ and a nonempty open subset $U$ of $G \times G$ such that $W(a, b) = 1$ for all $(a, b) \in U$ but $W(a, b) \ne 1$ for some $a, b \in G$. This answers Kourovka Notebook Problem 18.71 in the negative.
nodes.title: Local word identities need not hold globally in connected groups
Localization of nilpotent groups

reading_title.source: $p$-local groups

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number. A group $H$ is $p$-local when, for every natural number $n$ coprime to $p$, the map $x \mapsto x^n$ is a bijection of $H$.
nodes.title: $p$-local groups

reading_title.source: $p$-localization of a group

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number. A homomorphism of groups $e \colon G \to L$ is a $p$-localization when $L$ is nilpotent and $p$-local, and every homomorphism $f$ from $G$ to a nilpotent $p$-local group $H$ factors uniquely through $e$: there is exactly one homomorphism $g \colon L \to H$ with $g \circ e = f$.
nodes.title: $p$-localization of a group

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and $\pi \colon G \to Q$ a homomorphism of groups (in the intended use, the quotient map of an extension). Then $\pi$ splits at $p$ when there exist $p$-localizations $e_G \colon G \to G_p$ and $e_Q \colon Q \to Q_p$ and homomorphisms $\pi_p \colon G_p \to Q_p$ and $s \colon Q_p \to G_p$ with $\pi_p \circ e_G = e_Q \circ \pi$ and $\pi_p \circ s = \mathrm{id}_{Q_p}$; that is, the…
nodes.title: Splitting at a prime

nodes.summary: The proposition that every extension of nilpotent groups with finitely generated quotient that splits at every prime splits: for all nilpotent groups $N$, $G$ and $Q$ with $Q$ finitely generated, every injective homomorphism $i \colon N \to G$ and every surjective homomorphism $\pi \colon G \to Q$ with $\operatorname{im} i = \ker \pi$ such that the extension splits at every prime $p$, there is a homomorphism…
nodes.title: Hilton's splitting question for nilpotent extensions (Kourovka 12.93)

nodes.summary: It is not true that every extension of nilpotent groups with finitely generated quotient that splits at every prime splits: there are nilpotent groups $N$, $G$ and $Q$ with $Q$ finitely generated, an injective homomorphism $i \colon N \to G$ and a surjective homomorphism $\pi \colon G \to Q$ with $\operatorname{im} i = \ker \pi$, such that the extension splits at every prime $p$ (for some $p$-localizations $G_p$ of…
nodes.title: Nilpotent extensions that split at every prime need not split
Locally nilpotent groups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is locally nilpotent when every subgroup generated by finitely many elements of $N$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent subgroup

nodes.summary: The Hirsch–Plotkin radical of a group $G$ is the subgroup generated by all locally nilpotent normal subgroups of $G$. By the Hirsch–Plotkin theorem it is the largest locally nilpotent normal subgroup of $G$.
nodes.title: Hirsch–Plotkin radical

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is locally nilpotent if for every finite subset $S \subseteq G$ the subgroup generated by $S$ is nilpotent, that is, every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent group (Kourovka 13.16)

nodes.summary: For a subset $X$ of a group $G$, let $C_G(X)$ be its centralizer, the subgroup of elements of $G$ that commute with every element of $X$. The group $G$ satisfies the minimal condition on centralizers if every nonempty set of such centralizers has a minimal element with respect to inclusion; equivalently, there is no infinite strictly descending chain $C_G(X_0) > C_G(X_1) > \cdots$ of centralizers.
nodes.title: Minimal condition on centralizers (Kourovka 13.16)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is hypercentral if for every proper normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ there is some $g \in G$ with $g \notin N$ and $g h g^{-1} h^{-1} \in N$ for all $h \in G$; that is, every nontrivial quotient $G/N$ has nontrivial centre (equivalently, the transfinite upper central series of $G$ reaches $G$).
nodes.title: Hypercentral group (Kourovka 13.16)

nodes.summary: The proposition that every locally nilpotent group satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is hypercentral.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 13.16 (Wagner)

nodes.summary: Every locally nilpotent group satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is hypercentral. This answers Kourovka Problem 13.16 (F. O. Wagner) in the affirmative (V. V. Bludov, 1998).
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent groups with the minimal condition on centralizers are hypercentral
Non-commutators in finite groups

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a finite group $G$ of order greater than $2$ in which exactly one element is not a commutator, that is, not of the form $x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 17.76 (finite groups with exactly one non-commutator)

nodes.summary: There is a finite group $G$ of order greater than $2$ in which exactly one element is not a commutator, that is, not of the form $x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: A finite group with exactly one non-commutator
Perfect locally nilpotent p-groups

nodes.summary: A group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Locally nilpotent group

reading_title.source: Kourovka 14.86: perfect locally nilpotent $p$-groups with nilpotent proper subgroups

nodes.summary: The proposition that for some prime $p$ there is an infinite locally nilpotent $p$-group $G$ (every element of $G$ has order a power of $p$) such that $G = [G, G]$ and every proper subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Kourovka 14.86: perfect locally nilpotent $p$-groups with nilpotent proper subgroups

reading_title.source: No infinite perfect locally nilpotent $p$-group has only nilpotent proper subgroups

nodes.summary: There is no prime $p$ and no infinite locally nilpotent $p$-group $G$ (every element of $G$ has order a power of $p$) such that $G = [G, G]$ and every proper subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: No infinite perfect locally nilpotent $p$-group has only nilpotent proper subgroups
Residually nilpotent groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is residually nilpotent if for every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is nilpotent.
nodes.title: Residually nilpotent group

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is residually torsion-free nilpotent if for every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ there is a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ with $g \notin N$ such that the quotient $G/N$ is nilpotent and torsion-free, that is, every nontrivial element of $G/N$ has infinite order.
nodes.title: Residually torsion-free nilpotent group

nodes.summary: The assertion that there exist a free group $F$ and a normal subgroup $R$ of $F$ such that $F/R$ is finitely presented and residually torsion-free nilpotent, while $F/[F, R]$ is not residually nilpotent, where $[F, R]$ is the subgroup of $F$ generated by all commutators $[f, r]$ with $f \in F$ and $r \in R$.
nodes.title: Mikhailov–Passi question on free central extensions (Kourovka 16.65)

nodes.summary: There exist a free group $F$ and a normal subgroup $R$ of $F$ such that $F/R$ is finitely presented and residually torsion-free nilpotent, while $F/[F, R]$ is not residually nilpotent; here $[F, R]$ is the subgroup of $F$ generated by all commutators $[f, r]$ with $f \in F$ and $r \in R$.
nodes.title: Free central extensions need not be residually nilpotent
Word maps on Lie groups

reading_title.source: Mycielski's trace-range property for $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.69(a))

nodes.summary: For every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$, the set of traces $\operatorname{tr} w(A, B)$, where $A, B$ range over $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and $w(A, B)$ is obtained by substituting $A$ for $x$ and $B$ for $y$, contains the interval $[-2, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's trace-range property for $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.69(a))

nodes.summary: For every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$, the set of real parts $\operatorname{Re} w(p, q)$, where $p, q$ range over the nonzero real quaternions and $w(p, q)$ is obtained by substituting $p$ for $x$ and $q$ for $y$, contains the interval $[-5/27, 1]$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's real-part property for quaternion word maps (Kourovka 16.69(b))

reading_title.source: Mycielski's trace-range question for $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ has a negative answer

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$ such that some real number $t \ge -2$ is not the trace of $w(A, B)$ for any $A, B \in \mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, where $w(A, B)$ is obtained by substituting $A$ for $x$ and $B$ for $y$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's trace-range question for $\mathrm{GL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ has a negative answer

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group on two generators $x, y$ such that some real number $t$ with $-5/27 \le t \le 1$ is not the real part of $w(p, q)$ for any nonzero real quaternions $p, q$, where $w(p, q)$ is obtained by substituting $p$ for $x$ and $q$ for $y$.
nodes.title: Mycielski's real-part question for quaternion word maps has a negative answer

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ and an element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators $x_0, x_1$, the word map of $w$ is the map $G \times G \to G$ sending $(x, y)$ to $w(x, y)$, the image of $w$ under the group homomorphism $F_2 \to G$ with $x_0 \mapsto x$ and $x_1 \mapsto y$.
nodes.title: Word map

reading_title.source: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.68(a))

nodes.summary: The statement, asked about by J. Mycielski, that for every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.68(a))

reading_title.source: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$ (Kourovka 16.68(b))

nodes.summary: The statement, asked about by J. Mycielski, that for every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$ (Kourovka 16.68(b))

reading_title.source: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.68(c))

nodes.summary: The statement, asked about by J. Mycielski, that for every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective.
nodes.title: Surjectivity of word maps on $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$ (Kourovka 16.68(c))

reading_title.source: Some nontrivial word map on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ is not surjective (Kourovka 16.68(a))

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators whose word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is not surjective. That is, Mycielski's question has a negative answer for $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$.
nodes.title: Some nontrivial word map on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{R})$ is not surjective (Kourovka 16.68(a))

reading_title.source: Nontrivial word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$ are surjective (Kourovka 16.68(b))

nodes.summary: For every nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators, the word map $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \times \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C}) \to \mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is surjective. That is, Mycielski's question has an affirmative answer for $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$.
nodes.title: Nontrivial word maps on $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$ are surjective (Kourovka 16.68(b))

reading_title.source: Some nontrivial word map on $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$ is not surjective (Kourovka 16.68(c))

nodes.summary: There is a nontrivial element $w$ of the free group $F_2$ on two generators whose word map $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \times \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R}) \to \mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$, $(x, y) \mapsto w(x, y)$, is not surjective. That is, Mycielski's question has a negative answer for $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$.
nodes.title: Some nontrivial word map on $\mathrm{SO}(3, \mathbb{R})$ is not surjective (Kourovka 16.68(c))

nodes.summary: Automorphism and endomorphism groups of groups other than free groups: their orders and realizations, outer automorphism groups, class-preserving automorphisms, and automorphisms with few fixed points or twisted conjugacy classes.
nodes.title: Automorphisms of groups

nodes.summary: The automorphism group as an object: orders of automorphism groups, realizing groups as (outer) automorphism groups, class-preserving and inner automorphisms, automorphism orbits, endomorphism counts.
nodes.title: Automorphism groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has finitely many automorphism orbits if the action of its automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ on $G$ has only finitely many orbits.
nodes.title: Groups with finitely many automorphism orbits
Automorphism groups of p-groups

nodes.summary: The statement that for some prime $p$ there are a finite $p$-group $G$ of order greater than $2$ and a proper subgroup $H < G$ whose automorphism groups are isomorphic, $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \cong \mathrm{Aut}(H)$.
nodes.title: Berkovich's problem on automorphism groups of p-groups (Kourovka 15.27)

nodes.summary: For some prime $p$ there are a finite $p$-group $G$ of order greater than $2$ and a proper subgroup $H < G$ with $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \cong \mathrm{Aut}(H)$ as groups.
nodes.title: A p-group and a proper subgroup with isomorphic automorphism groups (Kourovka 15.27)
Class-preserving automorphisms

nodes.summary: For every group $G$: if every automorphism of $G$ sends each element $g \in G$ to a conjugate of $g$ (equivalently, maps every conjugacy class of $G$ into itself), then every automorphism of $G$ is inner, that is, of the form $x \mapsto h x h^{-1}$ for some $h \in G$.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 16.62

nodes.summary: The claim of Kourovka Problem 16.62 is false: there is a group $G$ such that every automorphism of $G$ sends each element $g \in G$ to a conjugate of $g$, but some automorphism of $G$ is not inner, that is, not of the form $x \mapsto h x h^{-1}$ for any $h \in G$.
nodes.title: Groups whose automorphisms all preserve conjugacy classes can have outer automorphisms

nodes.summary: The claim that for every group $G$, every automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ that sends each element to a conjugate of itself (for each $x \in G$ there is $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$) is inner, that is, there is a single $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$ for all $x \in G$.
nodes.title: Claim of Scottish Book Problem 112

nodes.summary: The claim of Scottish Book Problem 112 is false: there are a group $G$ and an automorphism $\alpha$ of $G$ that sends every element to a conjugate of itself (for each $x \in G$ there is $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$) but is not inner (there is no $g \in G$ with $\alpha(x) = g x g^{-1}$ for all $x \in G$).
nodes.title: Class-preserving automorphisms need not be inner
Endomorphisms and partial isomorphisms

nodes.summary: The statement that every finite group $G$ with $|\mathrm{End}(G)| = |\mathrm{PIso}(G)|$ is abelian. Here $\mathrm{End}(G)$ is the set of endomorphisms of $G$, and $\mathrm{PIso}(G)$ is the set of partial isomorphisms of $G$: the triples $(H, K, f)$ of subgroups $H$, $K$ of $G$ and an isomorphism $f \colon H \to K$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.20 (Cameron)

nodes.summary: There is a finite non-abelian group $G$ with $|\mathrm{End}(G)| = |\mathrm{PIso}(G)|$. Here $\mathrm{End}(G)$ is the set of endomorphisms of $G$, and $\mathrm{PIso}(G)$ is the set of partial isomorphisms of $G$: the triples $(H, K, f)$ of subgroups $H$, $K$ of $G$ and an isomorphism $f \colon H \to K$. This answers Kourovka Problem 19.20 (P. J. Cameron) in the negative.
nodes.title: Equal endomorphism and partial isomorphism counts do not force commutativity
Groups as automorphism groups of relations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $Z$ a set and $X \subseteq Z \times Z$ a binary relation on $Z$. Then $G$ is the full automorphism group of $X$ when there is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of $Z$ whose image is exactly the set of permutations $f$ of $Z$ with $(x, y) \in X \iff (f(x), f(y)) \in X$ for all $x, y \in Z$.
nodes.title: Full automorphism group of a binary relation

nodes.summary: For every group $G$ there are a set $Z$ and a binary relation $X \subseteq Z \times Z$ such that $G$ is the full automorphism group of $X$: there is an injective group homomorphism $\varphi$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of $Z$ whose image is exactly the set of permutations $f$ of $Z$ with $(x, y) \in X \iff (f(x), f(y)) \in X$ for all $x, y \in Z$.
nodes.title: Birkhoff's theorem: every group is the automorphism group of a binary relation

Golod groups

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $N$ a non-unital associative $k$-algebra and $y_1, \dots, y_r \in N$. The Golod group of $y$ is the subgroup of the group of units of the unitization $k \oplus N$ generated by the units that are equal to $1 + y_i$ for some $i$. When every $1 + y_i$ is invertible (for example when $N$ is nil), this is the subgroup $\langle 1 + y_1, \dots, 1 + y_r \rangle$ of the adjoint group $1 + N$.

Locally finite simple groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is locally finite when every subgroup of $G$ generated by finitely many elements is finite.
nodes.title: Locally finite group

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of subgroups of a group $G$ is a composition series of $G$ when it contains the trivial subgroup and $G$, it is totally ordered by inclusion, it contains the join and the intersection of every subset of $S$, and for every jump $A < B$ of $S$ (members $A \subsetneq B$ of $S$ with no member of $S$ strictly between them) $A$ is normal in $B$ and the quotient $B / A$ is a simple group.
nodes.title: Composition series in Kurosh's sense

nodes.summary: The statement, asked by R. Phillips, that every locally finite simple group $G$ is absolutely simple: every composition series of $G$ in Kurosh's sense consists of the trivial subgroup and $G$ alone.
nodes.title: Absolute simplicity of locally finite simple groups (Kourovka 11.108)

nodes.summary: There is a locally finite simple group $G$ with a composition series, in Kurosh's sense, other than the series consisting of the trivial subgroup and $G$ alone. That is, the statement of Kourovka Problem 11.108, that every locally finite simple group is absolutely simple, is false.

Minimal condition on centralizers

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is locally finite when for every finite subset $S$ of $G$ the subgroup generated by $S$ is finite, that is, every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite.

nodes.summary: For a subset $X$ of a group $G$, write $C_G(X)$ for the centralizer of $X$ in $G$. The group $G$ satisfies the minimal condition on centralizers when there is no sequence of subsets $X_0, X_1, X_2, \ldots$ of $G$ whose centralizers form a strictly descending chain $C_G(X_0) > C_G(X_1) > C_G(X_2) > \cdots$, where $H > K$ means that $K$ is a proper subgroup of $H$.

Shunkov) when $G$ is infinite, $G$ has an element of order greater than $2$, and for every element $a$ of order greater than $2$ and every proper subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is $g \in G \setminus H$ such that $a$ and $g^{-1} a g$ generate $G$. Products of abelian and locally quaternion groups

nodes.summary: A subgroup $B$ of a group $G$ is locally quaternion if there is a strictly increasing sequence $C_0 < C_1 < C_2 < \cdots$ of subgroups of $G$, each isomorphic to a generalized quaternion group $Q_{2^{k+2}}$ of order $2^{k+2}$ for some $k \ge 1$, whose supremum (for a chain, the union) is $B$. In particular $B$ is infinite.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $A$ is abelian, $B$ is locally quaternion, and $G = AB$, that is, every element of $G$ is a product $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. Then $G$ is soluble.

nodes.summary: The statement, posed by F. de Giovanni, that for every soluble group $G$ and all subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ in which every element has finite order, every subgroup $H$ of $G$ contained in the set $AB$ of all products $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$ has every element of finite order.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a soluble group and let $A$ and $B$ be subgroups of $G$ in which every element has finite order. Then every subgroup $H$ of $G$ contained in the set $AB$ of all products $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$ is periodic: every element of $H$ has finite order. Weak chain conditions on subgroups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ satisfies the weak maximal condition on subgroups when there is no infinite ascending chain $H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots$ of subgroups of $G$ in which every index $|H_{i+1} : H_i|$ is infinite.

This answers Kourovka Problem 10.14(b) negatively.

Arcwise connectedness of metric groups

nodes.summary: A topological space $G$ is connected in the sense of Hausdorff when it is not the union of two disjoint nonempty closed subsets.

nodes.summary: A topological space $G$ is arcwise connected when for any two points $x, y \in G$ there is a continuous map $\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to G$ with $\gamma(0) = x$ and $\gamma(1) = y$.

nodes.summary: The assertion that for every natural number $n$ and every automorphism $\varphi$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the semidirect product $F_n \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z}$, in which $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ acts on $F_n$ by $\varphi^k$, is conjugacy separable.

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every automorphism $\varphi$ of the free group $F_n$ of rank $n$, the semidirect product $F_n \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z}$, in which $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ acts on $F_n$ by $\varphi^k$, is conjugacy separable: any two of its elements whose images are conjugate in every quotient by a normal subgroup of finite index are conjugate.

nodes.summary: A group $G$ satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups when the order on subgroups of $G$ by inclusion is well-founded: every nonempty set of subgroups of $G$ has a minimal element, equivalently there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Minimal condition on subgroups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is a minimax group when it has a finite subnormal series $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \dots \le H_n = G$, with each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, such that every factor $H_{i+1}/H_i$ satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups or the minimal condition on subgroups.
nodes.title: Minimax groups

nodes.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same finite images when, for every finite group $Q$, there is a surjective homomorphism $G \to Q$ exactly when there is a surjective homomorphism $H \to Q$.

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is residually finite when for every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ there is a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$.
nodes.title: Residually finite groups

nodes.summary: The statement that for all groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is a finitely generated soluble minimax group and $H$ is a finitely generated residually finite group with the same finite images as $G$ (a finite group is a homomorphic image of $G$ exactly when it is a homomorphic image of $H$), then $H$ is a minimax group.
nodes.title: Minimax groups and finite images (Kourovka 12.90)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finitely generated soluble minimax group and let $H$ be a finitely generated residually finite group with the same finite images as $G$: a finite group is a homomorphic image of $G$ exactly when it is a homomorphic image of $H$. Then $H$ is a minimax group.

nodes.summary: For a topological group $G$, the generator rank $d(G)$ is the least natural number $k$ such that some finite subset of $G$ with $k$ elements generates a dense subgroup of $G$, that is, a subgroup whose closure is all of $G$. If no finite subset of $G$ generates a dense subgroup, then $d(G)$ is defined to be $0$. For a finite discrete group this is the ordinary minimal number of generators.

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and a topological group $G$, the relation rank $r(G)$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ of the continuous cohomology group $H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $G$ acts trivially on $\mathbb{F}_p$. If this space is infinite-dimensional, then $r(G)$ is defined to be $0$.

Then the generator rank $d(Q)$ and the relation rank $r(Q)$, the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_p$ of the continuous cohomology group $H^2(Q, \mathbb{F}_p)$ with trivial coefficients, satisfy $d(Q)^2 < 4\, r(Q)$.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Profinite rigidity

nodes.summary: The profinite completion of a group $G$ is the inverse limit of the finite quotient groups $G/N$, where $N$ ranges over the normal subgroups of finite index in $G$ and the maps are the quotient maps $G/N \to G/M$ for $N \le M$. It is a profinite group.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a natural number and let $H$ be a subgroup of a group $F$. Then $H$ is separable in the class of finite $p$-groups if for every $x \in F$ with $x \notin H$ there are a finite $p$-group $Q$ (a finite group in which every element $g$ satisfies $g^{p^k} = 1$ for some natural number $k$) and a group homomorphism $f \colon F \to Q$ with $f(x) \notin f(H)$.

Strong completeness of profinite groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ equipped with a topology is *strongly complete* when every subgroup of finite index in $G$ is open.
nodes.title: Strongly complete group

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a profinite group and let $\hat P$ be the profinite completion of $P$ as an abstract group, that is, the inverse limit of the finite quotients $P/N$ over all normal subgroups $N$ of finite index in $P$. If the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is surjective, then every normal subgroup of finite index in $P$ is closed in $P$.
nodes.title: Finite-index normal subgroups are closed when the completion map is onto

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a profinite group and let $\hat P$ be the profinite completion of $P$ as an abstract group, that is, the inverse limit of the finite quotients $P/N$ over all normal subgroups $N$ of finite index in $P$. If the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is surjective, then every normal subgroup of finite index in $P$ is open in $P$.
nodes.title: Finite-index normal subgroups are open when the completion map is onto

Then $P$ is strongly complete if and only if the canonical map $P \to \hat P$ is bijective.

reading_title.source: Caprace's class $\mathcal{S}$

nodes.summary: A group $G$ with a topology belongs to the class $\mathcal{S}$ when it is a topological group that is Hausdorff, totally disconnected, locally compact and not discrete, is generated as a group by some compact subset, and is topologically simple: $G$ is nontrivial and its only closed normal subgroups are the trivial subgroup and $G$ itself.

nodes.title: Caprace's problem on local isomorphism classes (Kourovka 19.22)

nodes.summary: There is a family $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ of groups in Caprace's class $\mathcal{S}$ (non-discrete, compactly generated, topologically simple, totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff topological groups), indexed by an uncountable set $I$, such that $G_i$ and $G_j$ are not locally isomorphic whenever $i \ne j$. nodes.summary: For groups $T$ and $Q$, $T$ is a composition factor of $Q$ when some subnormal subgroup $H$ of $Q$ maps onto $T$, that is, there is a surjective group homomorphism $H \to T$. Here $H$ is subnormal in $Q$ when there is a finite chain of subgroups $H = H_0 \le H_1 \le \dots \le H_k = Q$ in which each $H_j$ is normal in $H_{j+1}$.
nodes.title: Composition factor of a group (via subnormal subgroups)

nodes.summary: For groups $T$ and $G$, $T$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ when it is a composition factor of some finite quotient of $G$: there are a finite group $Q$ and a surjective group homomorphism $G \to Q$ such that $T$ is a composition factor of $Q$, that is, $T$ is a homomorphic image of a subnormal subgroup of $Q$.
nodes.title: Upper composition factors

nodes.summary: The statement that for every family $(T_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite non-abelian simple groups there is a group $G$ generated by $63$ elements such that a finite simple group $Q$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ if and only if $Q$ is isomorphic to $T_i$ for some $i \in I$.

nodes.summary: The statement that for every family $(T_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite non-abelian simple groups there is a group $G$ generated by $3$ elements such that a finite non-abelian simple group $Q$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ if and only if $Q$ is isomorphic to $T_i$ for some $i \in I$. Abelian upper composition factors of $G$ are not restricted.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.57, 3-generator form (statement)

nodes.summary: For every family $(T_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite non-abelian simple groups there is a group $G$ generated by $63$ elements such that a finite simple group $Q$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ (a composition factor of some finite quotient of $G$) if and only if $Q$ is isomorphic to $T_i$ for some $i \in I$. In particular, no cyclic group of prime order is an upper composition factor of $G$.
nodes.title: Segal's theorem on upper composition factors, 63 generators (Kourovka Problem 11.57)

nodes.summary: For every family $(T_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite non-abelian simple groups there is a group $G$ generated by $3$ elements such that a finite non-abelian simple group $Q$ is an upper composition factor of $G$ (a composition factor of some finite quotient of $G$) if and only if $Q$ is isomorphic to $T_i$ for some $i \in I$. nodes.summary: Sapir's group is the group with presentation $\langle a, b, t \mid a^t = ab, b^t = ba \rangle$, where $a^t = t^{-1} a t$: the quotient of the free group on $a$, $b$, $t$ by the normal subgroup generated by $t^{-1} a t (ab)^{-1}$ and $t^{-1} b t (ba)^{-1}$.

nodes.summary: The group $\langle a, b, t \mid a^t = ab, b^t = ba \rangle$, where $a^t = t^{-1} a t$, embeds in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$ for some natural number $n$. That is, Kourovka Problem 17.108 has a positive answer.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ a tuple of natural numbers. nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $k$ a natural number and $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ natural numbers. The group $G$ has a subset factorization of type $(a_0, \dots, a_{k-1})$ when there are finite subsets $A_0, \dots, A_{k-1}$ of $G$ with $|A_i| = a_i$ for every $i$ such that $G = A_0 A_1 \cdots A_{k-1}$, that is, every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{k-1}$ with $x_i \in A_i$ for every $i$.

nodes.summary: This proposition states that there is a natural number $N$ such that every nonabelian finite simple group $G$ that has a subset $S$ closed under conjugation and under inversion with $|S| > |G| / \log_2 |G|$ and $S^2 \ne G$, where $S^2 = \{st : s, t \in S\}$, has order $|G| \le N$. nodes.title: Twist relators of the Kropholler group

nodes.title: The Kropholler group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be the Kropholler group. This is the proposition that $H^4(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$, and $H^n(G, M) = 0$ for every $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$ and every integer $n > 4$; that is, the cohomological dimension of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $4$.

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be the Kropholler group. Then $H^4(G, M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$, and $H^n(G, M) = 0$ for every $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $M$ and every integer $n > 4$. nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $q$ be a prime ideal of $S$. Bhargava p-orderings

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. For $n \in \mathbb N$ and $x \in R$, the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation of $x$ is the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in the principal ideal generated by $\prod_{k < n} (x - a_k)$: the largest $m \in \mathbb N$ such that $\mathfrak p^m$ divides this ideal, or $\infty$ if every power of $\mathfrak p$…
nodes.title: Prefix-product valuation

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. Write $v_n(x)$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation of $x \in R$ with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$, the multiplicity of $\mathfrak p$ in the ideal generated by $\prod_{k < n} (x - a_k)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ when $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for…
nodes.title: Bhargava p-ordering

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ if and only if $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Unfolding the definition of a p-ordering

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $S \subseteq R$. If some sequence in $R$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, then $S$ is infinite.
nodes.title: A set with a p-ordering is infinite

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$. Then $a_n \in S$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: Terms of a p-ordering lie in the set

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Minimality of a p-ordering

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then for every $n$, $v_n(a_n)$ is the least element of $\{v_n(x) : x \in S\}$.
nodes.title: Each term of a p-ordering attains the least valuation

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. If $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$, then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$.
nodes.title: Building a p-ordering

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$. For every $x \in R$, the stage-$0$ prefix-product valuation of $x$ with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$ is $0$: the product is empty, so the ideal is all of $R$.
nodes.title: The stage-zero valuation vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. Then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$ if and only if $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n \ge 1$ and every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: The stage-zero condition of a p-ordering is automatic
Characterizations of Dedekind domains

nodes.summary: An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains as the Noetherian domains where to contain is to divide

nodes.summary: An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal ideal.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains via principal products

nodes.summary: For an integral domain $A$, the following are equivalent: (1) $A$ is a Dedekind domain; (2) $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$; (3) for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal ideal.
nodes.title: Equivalent characterizations of Dedekind domains

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension at most one if and only if $A$ is a Dedekind domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains are the integrally closed Noetherian domains of dimension at most one

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then the localizations $A_P$ at all nonzero prime ideals $P$ of $A$ are discrete valuation rings if and only if $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension at most one.
nodes.title: DVR localizations in a Noetherian domain

nodes.summary: Every quotient of a Dedekind domain by a nonzero ideal is a principal ideal ring.
nodes.title: Quotients of Dedekind domains by nonzero ideals are principal ideal rings

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is a Noetherian ring.
nodes.title: Domains with principal quotients are Noetherian

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then for every nonzero prime ideal $P$ of $A$, the localization $A_P$ is a discrete valuation ring.
nodes.title: Principal quotients give discrete valuation rings at nonzero primes

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is a Dedekind domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains from principal quotients

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ and every nonzero $a \in I$ there is $b \in A$ with $I = (a, b)$. Then for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$, the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring.
nodes.title: Two generators with one prescribed give principal quotients

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ and every nonzero $a \in I$ there is $b \in A$ with $I = (a, b)$. Then $A$ is a Dedekind domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains from two generators with one prescribed

This is the ring isomorphism $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p} \cong A/\mathfrak{p}$ that sends the residue class of the image of each $a \in A$…
nodes.title: Residue field of the completion

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $v$ be a height-one prime of $R$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the valuation ring of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. Then the localization $R_v$ of $R$ at $v$, viewed as a subring of $K$, is the preimage of $\mathcal{O}_v$ under the canonical embedding $K \to K_v$.

Conductor ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $A$ an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. The conductor ideal of $A$ is the ideal of $S$ consisting of all $s \in S$ such that $st \in A$ for every $t \in S$; it is the largest ideal of $S$ contained in $A$.
nodes.title: Conductor ideal of a subalgebra

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative semirings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, and let $A$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. An element $s \in S$ lies in the conductor ideal of $A$ if and only if $st \in A$ for every $t \in S$.
nodes.title: Membership in the conductor ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative semirings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let $A$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $S$, and let $I$ be an ideal of $S$. Then $I$ is contained in the conductor ideal of $A$ if and only if $I$ is contained in $A$.
nodes.title: Universal property of the conductor ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $A$ an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. Then the conductor ideal of $A$ is contained in $A$.
nodes.title: The conductor ideal lies in the subalgebra

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $A \subseteq B$ two $R$-subalgebras of $S$. Then the conductor ideal of $A$ is contained in the conductor ideal of $B$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the conductor ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra. The conductor ideal of $S$, viewed as an $R$-subalgebra of itself, is the unit ideal $S$.
nodes.title: Conductor ideal of the whole algebra

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $A$ an $R$-subalgebra of $S$. The conductor ideal of $A$ is all of $S$ if and only if $A = S$.
nodes.title: The conductor ideal is the unit ideal only for the whole algebra

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $S$ and $T$ commutative $R$-algebras, $f \colon S \to T$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras and $B$ an $R$-subalgebra of $T$. Then the preimage under $f$ of the conductor ideal of $B$ is contained in the conductor ideal of the subalgebra $f^{-1}(B)$ of $S$.
nodes.title: Preimage of a conductor ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $S$ a commutative $R$-algebra and $x \in S$. The conductor ideal of the subalgebra $R[x]$ of $S$ generated by $x$ equals the conductor of $x$, the ideal of all $a \in S$ such that $ab \in R[x]$ for every $b \in S$.
nodes.title: Conductor of a monogenic subalgebra

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, and let $T$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $K$ that is finitely generated as an $R$-module. Then the conductor ideal of the image of $R$ in $T$ (the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $T$) is nonzero.
nodes.title: A finite overring has nonzero conductor

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, $K$ a field that is an $R$-algebra, and $T$ an $R$-subalgebra of $K$. If the conductor ideal of the image of $R$ in $T$ (the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $T$) is nonzero, then $T$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module.
nodes.title: A subalgebra of a field with nonzero conductor is finite

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Noetherian integral domain with fraction field $K$, and let $T$ be an $R$-subalgebra of $K$. Then the conductor ideal of the image of $R$ in $T$ (the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $T$) is nonzero if and only if $T$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module.
nodes.title: Finiteness of an overring via its conductor

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Noetherian integral domain with fraction field $K$, and let $\overline{R}$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $K$, viewed as an $R$-algebra. The conductor ideal of the smallest $R$-subalgebra of $\overline{R}$ (the image of $R$) is a nonzero ideal of $\overline{R}$ if and only if $\overline{R}$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the integral closure via the conductor

Then for every $o \in O$, the residue-ring isomorphism…

Let $\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $B$ and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $B$ with $\mathfrak c \not\subseteq \mathfrak q$ such that for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$ there is $o \in O$ with $\varphi(o) = xb$. Then $O / \varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $B / \mathfrak q$ have the same…

Let $\mathfrak q$ be a maximal ideal of $B$ and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $B$ with $\mathfrak c \not\subseteq \mathfrak q$ such that for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$ there is $o \in O$ with $\varphi(o) = xb$. Then the index of $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ in $O$ equals the index of…
nodes.title: Equal ideal indices away from a denominator-clearing ideal

nodes.summary: Let $O$ and $B$ be commutative rings, let $B$ be an $O$-algebra whose structure map $f \colon O \to B$ is injective, let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal of $O$, and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $O$ with $\mathfrak c + \mathfrak p = O$ such that $f(x)\,b$ lies in the image of $f$ for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$. Then the ideal $\mathfrak p B$ of $B$ generated by $f(\mathfrak p)$ is prime.
nodes.title: Prime ideals stay prime under denominator clearing

nodes.summary: Let $O$ and $B$ be commutative rings, let $B$ be an $O$-algebra whose structure map $f \colon O \to B$ is injective, let $\mathfrak p$ be a maximal ideal of $O$, and let $\mathfrak c$ be an ideal of $O$ with $\mathfrak c + \mathfrak p = O$ such that $f(x)\,b$ lies in the image of $f$ for every $x \in \mathfrak c$ and every $b \in B$. Then the ideal $\mathfrak p B$ of $B$ generated by $f(\mathfrak p)$ is maximal.
nodes.title: Maximal ideals stay maximal under denominator clearing

nodes.title: Contraction after extension fixes primes away from the conductor

nodes.title: Contraction of a nonzero ideal is nonzero

nodes.summary: Extension after contraction is the identity on primes of `B` not containing `𝔠.map f`, using that `B` has Krull dimension at most one.
nodes.title: Extension after contraction fixes primes away from the conductor

nodes.title: Bijection of nonzero primes away from the conductor
Fractional ideals prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\mathfrak p$ a prime ideal of $A$. Every non-zero-divisor of $A$ maps to a non-zero-divisor of the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.title: Non-zero-divisors stay non-zero-divisors in a localization at a prime

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. Then $I$ is prime to $J$ if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ with $J \subseteq \mathfrak p$, the extension $I A_{\mathfrak p}$ of $I$ to the localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$, a fractional ideal of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ in $K$, is the unit fractional ideal $A_{\mathfrak p}$.
nodes.title: Fractional ideals prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the unit fractional ideal $A$ of $A$ in $K$ is prime to $J$.
nodes.title: The unit fractional ideal is prime to every ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. If fractional ideals $I$ and $I'$ of $A$ in $K$ are both prime to $J$, then their product $I I'$ is prime to $J$.
nodes.title: Products of fractional ideals prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. If an invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$ is prime to $J$, then its inverse $I^{-1}$ is prime to $J$.
nodes.title: Inverses of invertible fractional ideals prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. The invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ that are prime to $J$ form a subgroup of the group of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$.
nodes.title: Invertible fractional ideals prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J$ be an ideal of $A$. An invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $A$ in $K$ lies in the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals prime to $J$ if and only if $I$ is prime to $J$.
nodes.title: Membership in the subgroup of units prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $I$ be a fractional ideal of $A$ in $K$ and let $J \subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. If $I$ is prime to $J$, then $I$ is prime to $J'$.
nodes.title: Prime to an ideal implies prime to every larger ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$ and let $J \subseteq J'$ be ideals of $A$. Then the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to $J$ is contained in the subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to $J'$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the subgroups of units prime to an ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $K$. The subgroup of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$ prime to the unit ideal $A$ is the whole group of invertible fractional ideals of $A$ in $K$.
nodes.title: Every invertible fractional ideal is prime to the unit ideal
Ideal class group

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain and let $I$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ be nonzero ideals of $A$. Then there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ with $J + \mathfrak{a} = A$ such that the product $IJ$ is a principal ideal.
nodes.title: Making an ideal principal with a factor coprime to a given ideal

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a nonzero ideal of $A$. Then every class $c$ in the ideal class group of $A$ is the class of some nonzero ideal $K$ of $A$ with $K + \mathfrak{a} = A$.
nodes.title: Ideal classes have representatives coprime to a given ideal

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain. Two nonzero ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$ are similar when their classes in the ideal class group of $R$ are equal.
nodes.title: Similar ideals

nodes.summary: A Dedekind domain $R$ is a unique factorization domain if and only if it is a principal ideal domain.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains: UFD iff PID

nodes.summary: A Dedekind domain $R$ is a principal ideal domain if and only if its ideal class group is trivial.
nodes.title: Dedekind domains: PID iff trivial class group

nodes.summary: A Dedekind domain $R$ is a unique factorization domain if and only if its ideal class group is trivial.
