nodes.title: Field Theory

nodes.summary: Galois theory relates a field extension to its group of automorphisms, covering the Galois correspondence, infinite Galois groups, Hilbert's theorem 90, solvability by radicals and essential dimension.
nodes.title: Galois theory

nodes.summary: In an extension of prime degree, a nontrivial automorphism witnesses that the extension is Galois, has order equal to the degree, and generates the automorphism group.
nodes.title: Extensions of prime degree with a nontrivial automorphism are Galois

nodes.summary: If $L/K$ is a finite-dimensional abelian Galois extension, then the lattice of intermediate fields of $L/K$ is modular.
nodes.title: Intermediate fields of an abelian extension form a modular lattice

nodes.summary: For a Galois extension `M / F` and any `F`-algebra `R`, the norm of an element of `R ⊗[F] M` over `R` is the product of its Galois conjugates.
nodes.title: Norm in a tensor product with a Galois extension

nodes.summary: Let $K/k$ be a Galois extension, not necessarily finite, and give $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ the Krull topology. For every subgroup $H$ of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ with fixed field $K^H$, the closure of $H$ equals the subgroup of $\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$ consisting of the automorphisms that fix $K^H$ pointwise.
nodes.title: The closure of a Galois subgroup is the fixing group of its fixed field
Additive Hilbert's theorem 90

nodes.summary: Let $L/K$ be a finite-dimensional Galois extension and let $\sigma$ be a $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ that generates its Galois group, that is, every $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ is an integer power of $\sigma$. Then the kernel of the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K} \colon L \to K$ equals the image of the $K$-linear map $\sigma - 1 \colon L \to L$, $y \mapsto \sigma(y) - y$.
nodes.title: Additive Hilbert 90 for cyclic extensions

nodes.summary: Let $L/K$ be a finite-dimensional Galois extension and let $\sigma$ be a $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ that generates its Galois group, that is, every $K$-algebra automorphism of $L$ is an integer power of $\sigma$. If $x \in L$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(x) = 0$, then there is $y \in L$ with $\sigma(y) - y = x$.
nodes.title: Additive Hilbert 90, pointwise form

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the fraction field of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ in $n$ indeterminates.
nodes.title: The function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$

reading_title.source: The roots $x_i$

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $i \in \{1, \dots, n\}$, $x_i$ is the $i$-th indeterminate of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, viewed as an element of its fraction field, the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.
nodes.title: The roots $x_i$

nodes.summary: For $0 \le i < n$, the coefficient $a_{i+1}$ is the $(i+1)$-st elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, as an element of the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.
nodes.title: The coefficients of the general polynomial

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ be the field of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates and, for $1 \le k \le n$, let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$. The coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is the intermediate field of $\mathbb{C} \subseteq \mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ generated over $\mathbb{C}$ by $a_1, \dots, a_n$.
nodes.title: Coefficient field of the general polynomial

nodes.summary: For $0 \le i < n$, the coefficient $a_{i+1}$, the $(i+1)$-st elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, regarded as an element of the coefficient field $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$.
nodes.title: Coefficients in the coefficient field

reading_title.source: The roots $x_i$ are pairwise distinct

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the elements $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ are pairwise distinct: $x_i = x_j$ implies $i = j$.
nodes.title: The roots $x_i$ are pairwise distinct

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_1, \dots, e_n \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Algebraic independence of the elementary symmetric polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, let $f : A \to B$ be an injective $\mathbb{C}$-algebra homomorphism, and let $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $A$ that is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$. Then the family $(f(x_i))_{i \in \iota}$ is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Injective algebra maps preserve algebraic independence

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the coefficients $a_1, \dots, a_n$ of the general polynomial, the elementary symmetric functions of $x_1, \dots, x_n$, are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.
nodes.title: The coefficients are algebraically independent

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the roots $x_1, \dots, x_n$ are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{C}$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$.
nodes.title: The roots are algebraically independent

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every polynomial $p \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$, the image of $p$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ lies in the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra generated by the roots $x_1, \dots, x_n$.
nodes.title: Polynomials in the roots

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, every element of the field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ of rational functions in $n$ indeterminates is algebraic over the $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra generated by $x_1, \dots, x_n$: it is a ratio of two polynomials in $x_1, \dots, x_n$.
nodes.title: Rational functions are algebraic over the polynomial subalgebra

nodes.title: Transcendence degree of $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$

nodes.summary: For a field $F$ that is a $\mathbb{C}$-algebra, the numeric transcendence degree of $F$ is its transcendence degree over $\mathbb{C}$ as a natural number when that degree is finite, and $0$ when it is infinite.
nodes.title: Numeric transcendence degree

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the image of the $k$-th elementary symmetric polynomial $e_k \in \mathbb{C}[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ is the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of the multiset of roots $\{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$, that is, the sum of the products $x_{i_1} \cdots x_{i_k}$ over all $i_1 < \dots < i_k$.
nodes.title: Elementary symmetric polynomials evaluated at the roots

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, for $1 \le k \le n$ let $a_k$ be the $k$-th elementary symmetric function of $x_1, \dots, x_n$ in the function field $\mathbb{C}(x_1, \dots, x_n)$, and let $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ be the coefficient field. For each natural number $k$, the element $c_k$ of $\mathbb{C}(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is defined by $c_0 = 1$, $c_k = a_k$ for $1 \le k \le n$, and $c_k = 0$ for $k > n$.

Then the linear system $Ax = b$ has a solution $x \in K^n$ if and only if the rank of $A$ equals the rank of the augmented matrix $(A \mid b)$, whose columns are the columns of $A$ followed by the single column $b$.

Condition numbers of sign matrices

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a sign matrix of order $n$ is encoded as an $n \times n$ matrix with entries in the Booleans $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, whose rows and columns are indexed by $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Boolean encoding of sign matrices

nodes.summary: The realization of a Boolean $n \times n$ matrix $A$ is the real $n \times n$ matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry is $-1$ if $A_{ij}$ is true and $1$ if $A_{ij}$ is false.
nodes.title: Real sign matrix of a Boolean matrix

nodes.title: Realized sign matrices have entries $\pm 1$

nodes.summary: Send each $n \times n$ Boolean matrix to the real matrix whose entry is $-1$ where the Boolean entry is true and $1$ where it is false. A real $n \times n$ matrix $M$ arises in this way if and only if every entry of $M$ is $1$ or $-1$.
nodes.title: Boolean matrices realize exactly the sign matrices

nodes.summary: For a real $n \times n$ matrix $A$, let $\sigma_0 \ge \sigma_1 \ge \dots$ be the singular values of $A$ acting on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, indexed from $0$ and extended by $\sigma_i = 0$ for $i \ge n$. The condition number of $A$, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is $\infty$ if $\sigma_{n-1} = 0$ and $\sigma_0 / \sigma_{n-1}$ otherwise, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Condition number of a square real matrix

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$, the minimum condition number of order $n$ is the least condition number of a real $n \times n$ sign matrix, that is, a matrix all of whose entries are $1$ or $-1$; the minimum is taken over the finitely many such matrices.
nodes.title: Minimum condition number of sign matrices

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix with singular values $\sigma_0 \ge \sigma_1 \ge \dots$ on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, indexed from $0$ and extended by zeros, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$. If $\sigma_{n-1} = 0$, then the condition number of $A$ is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Infinite condition number from a vanishing singular value

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix with singular values $\sigma_0 \ge \sigma_1 \ge \dots$ on Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, indexed from $0$ and extended by zeros, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$. If $\sigma_{n-1} \ne 0$, then the condition number of $A$ equals $\sigma_0 / \sigma_{n-1}$.

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the condition number of the real $n \times n$ zero matrix is $\infty$; this includes the $0 \times 0$ matrix.

nodes.summary: A real number $\alpha$ is an admissible exponent when there is a subpolynomial sequence $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to [0, \infty)$ such that for every positive integer $n$ the minimum condition number $\kappa_n$ of the real $n \times n$ sign matrices satisfies $\kappa_n = 1 + f(n) / n^{\alpha}$, as an equality in $[0, \infty]$.

nodes.summary: The Hadamard hypothesis is the proposition that for every natural number $n$ divisible by $4$ there is an $n \times n$ Hadamard matrix with integer entries, that is, an integer matrix $H$ with all entries $\pm 1$ such that $H H^{\mathsf{T}} = H^{\mathsf{T}} H = n I$.

Maximal unramified subextension

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. An intermediate field $E$ of $L/K$ is finite unramified relative to $A$ if $E$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ and the integral closure of $A$ in $E$ is formally unramified over $A$.
nodes.title: Finite unramified intermediate fields

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. The maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$ is the supremum, in the lattice of intermediate fields of $L/K$, of all intermediate fields of $L/K$ that are finite unramified relative to $A$.
nodes.title: Maximal unramified subextension

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. Every intermediate field $E$ of $L/K$ that is finite unramified relative to $A$ is contained in the maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$.
nodes.title: Finite unramified subfields lie in the maximal unramified subextension

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. An intermediate field $F$ of $L/K$ contains the maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$ if and only if $F$ contains every intermediate field of $L/K$ that is finite unramified relative to $A$.
nodes.title: Universal property of the maximal unramified subextension

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$. If an intermediate field $E$ of $L/K$ is finite unramified relative to $A$, then for every $K$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $L$ the image $\sigma(E)$ is finite unramified relative to $A$.
nodes.title: Automorphisms preserve finite unramified subfields

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L/K$ a field extension such that the map $A \to L$ factors as $A \to K \to L$, and let $M$ be the maximal unramified subextension of $L/K$ relative to $A$. For every $K$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $L$, $\sigma(M) = M$.
nodes.title: The maximal unramified subextension is stable under automorphisms

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 3$ there is a constant $C$ such that $E_n(H) \le C H^{n-1}$ for all sufficiently large natural numbers $H$, where $E_n(H)$ is the number of monic polynomials of degree $n$ with integer coefficients, all non-leading coefficients of absolute value at most $H$, whose Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ has order less than $n!$.
nodes.title: Van der Waerden's conjecture (Bhargava)

nodes.summary: Places, adeles and ideles, Arakelov divisors, ray class groups, Artin map, Hilbert class fields, Neukirch–Uchida-type Galois characterization.

nodes.summary: Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be number fields with separable closures $\overline{K_1}$ and $\overline{K_2}$, and let $\varphi \colon \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K_1}/K_1) \to \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K_2}/K_2)$ be a group isomorphism that is a homeomorphism for the Krull topologies. Then there is a unique field isomorphism $\sigma \colon \overline{K_2} \to \overline{K_1}$ that maps the image of $K_2$ in $\overline{K_2}$ onto the…

Adeles and ideles

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $v$ a nonzero prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The residue field of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$ of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finite residue field of a completed number ring

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $v$ a nonzero prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$ of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$ is a compact subset of $K_v$.
nodes.title: Compactness of the completed ring of integers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $v$ be a height-one prime of $R$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of integers of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. The local integral unit subgroup is the subgroup $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$ of $K_v^\times$, consisting of the units $u$ of $K_v$ with $u \in \mathcal{O}_v$ and $u^{-1} \in \mathcal{O}_v$.
nodes.title: Local integral unit subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. For each height-one prime $v$ of $R$, let $K_v$ be the $v$-adic completion of $K$ and $\mathcal{O}_v$ its ring of integers. The finite idele group is the restricted product of the unit groups $K_v^\times$ over all height-one primes $v$ of $R$ with respect to the subgroups $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$: the families $(x_v)_v$ with $x_v \in K_v^\times$ for every $v$ and…
nodes.title: Finite idele group

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $v$ be a height-one prime of $R$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of integers of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. Then $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$ is an open subset of the unit group $K_v^\times$.
nodes.title: The local integral units are open

nodes.summary: For a field $K$, the infinite idele group is the product $\prod_v K_v^\times$ of the unit groups of the completions $K_v$ of $K$ over all infinite places $v$ of $K$, with componentwise multiplication and the product topology.
nodes.title: Infinite idele group

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The topological idele group is the product $\mathbb{I}_{K,\infty} \times \mathbb{I}_{K,f}$ of the infinite idele group $\mathbb{I}_{K,\infty} = \prod_w K_w^\times$, the product of the unit groups of the completions of $K$ at its infinite places $w$, and the finite idele group $\mathbb{I}_{K,f}$, the restricted product of the unit groups $K_v^\times$ of the…
nodes.title: Topological idele group

nodes.summary: For a field $K$, this is the group homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the infinite idele group of $K$ that sends $x$ to the family of its images in the completions $K_v$ of $K$, one for each infinite place $v$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Diagonal map into the infinite ideles

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. This is the group homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the finite idele group of $R$ and $K$ that sends $x$ to the family of its images in the $v$-adic completions $K_v$ of $K$, one for each height-one prime $v$ of $R$.
nodes.title: Diagonal map into the finite ideles

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. This is the group homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the topological idele group of $R$ and $K$ whose infinite component sends $x$ to its images in the completions of $K$ at all infinite places of $K$, and whose finite component sends $x$ to its images in the $v$-adic completions $K_v$ of $K$ at all height-one primes $v$ of $R$.
nodes.title: Diagonal map into the ideles

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The subgroup of principal ideles is the image of the diagonal homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the topological idele group of $R$ and $K$, which sends $x$ to its images in the completions of $K$ at all infinite places of $K$ and at all height-one primes of $R$.
nodes.title: Principal ideles

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, and let $\mathbb{A}_K$ be the adele ring of $K$ built from the infinite places of $K$ and the height-one primes of $R$. For an infinite place $w$ of $K$ write $K_w$ for the completion of $K$ at $w$, and for a height-one prime $v$ of $R$ write $K_v$ for the $v$-adic completion of $K$. This is the group isomorphism from the unit group $\mathbb{A}_K^\times$ to the…
nodes.title: Ideles as units of the adele ring

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The diagonal homomorphism from $K^\times$ to the topological idele group of $R$ and $K$, which sends $x$ to its images in the completions of $K$ at all infinite places of $K$ and at all height-one primes of $R$, is injective.
nodes.title: The diagonal map into the ideles is injective

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$. The topological idele class group is the quotient group of the topological idele group of $R$ and $K$ by its subgroup of principal ideles, the image of the diagonal homomorphism from $K^\times$.
nodes.title: Topological idele class group

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field, let $v$ be a height-one prime of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $\mathcal{O}_v$ be the ring of integers of the $v$-adic completion $K_v$ of $K$. Then the local integral unit subgroup $\mathcal{O}_v^\times$ is a compact subset of the unit group $K_v^\times$.
nodes.title: Compactness of the local integral units

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For each infinite place $w$ of $K$ let $K_w$ be the completion of $K$ at $w$, with the absolute value $\|\cdot\|_w$ extending $w$, and let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex. For each height-one prime $v$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ let $K_v$ be the $v$-adic completion of $K$, with the normalized absolute value $\|\cdot\|_v$. The adelic norm…
nodes.title: Adelic norm

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. For every idele $a$ of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$), the adelic norm of $a$ equals $\bigl(\prod_w \|a_w\|_w^{m_w}\bigr) \cdot \prod_v \|a_v\|_v$, where $w$ runs over the infinite places of $K$, $\|\cdot\|_w$ is the absolute value on the completion $K_w$ extending $w$, $m_w$ is $1$ for a real place and $2$ for a complex place, $v$ runs over the height-one primes of $\mathcal{O}_K$,…
nodes.title: Formula for the adelic norm

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. The norm-one ideles of $K$ form the kernel of the adelic norm, the subgroup of the topological idele group of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) consisting of the ideles whose adelic norm is $1$.
nodes.title: Norm-one ideles

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. An idele $a$ of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) lies in the subgroup of norm-one ideles if and only if its adelic norm is $1$.
nodes.title: Membership in the norm-one ideles

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. For every $x \in K^\times$, the principal idele of $x$ (its image under the diagonal embedding of $K^\times$ into the topological idele group, with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) has adelic norm $1$.
nodes.title: Product formula for principal ideles

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. The subgroup of principal ideles of $K$ (with $R = \mathcal{O}_K$) is contained in the subgroup of norm-one ideles; that is, every principal idele has adelic norm $1$.
nodes.title: Principal ideles have norm one

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, this is the subgroup of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$ consisting of the principal ideles, that is, of the elements of $I_K^1$ that are images of elements of $K^\times$ under the diagonal embedding.
nodes.title: Principal ideles of norm one

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the norm-one idele class group $C_K^1 = I_K^1 / K^\times$ is the quotient of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$ by its subgroup of principal ideles, the images of the elements of $K^\times$ under the diagonal embedding.
nodes.title: Norm-one idele class group

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field. For every $x \in K^\times$, the principal idele of $x$, viewed as an element of the group $I_K^1$ of ideles of $K$ with adelic norm $1$, has trivial class in the norm-one idele class group $C_K^1 = I_K^1 / K^\times$.
nodes.title: Principal ideles are trivial in the norm-one idele class group

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the subgroup of principal ideles is discrete in the idele group of $K$, where the idele group carries the product of the product topology at the infinite places and the restricted-product topology at the finite places.
nodes.title: The principal ideles are discrete
Arakelov divisors

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain that is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of finite rank, and let $F$ be its field of fractions. For every invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $F$, the absolute norm of $I$, a rational number, is nonzero.
nodes.title: Invertible fractional ideals have nonzero absolute norm

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain that is a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module of finite rank, and let $F$ be its field of fractions. For every invertible fractional ideal $I$ of $R$ in $F$, the absolute norm of $I$, a rational number, is positive.
nodes.title: Invertible fractional ideals have positive absolute norm

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. An Arakelov divisor on $K$ is a pair $(I, r)$, where $I$ is an invertible fractional ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ in $K$ and $r$ assigns a positive real number $r_w$ to each infinite place $w$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Arakelov divisor

nodes.summary: Let $D = (I, r)$ be an Arakelov divisor on a number field $K$. Its archimedean factor is the positive real number $\prod_w r_w^{m_w}$, where the product runs over all infinite places $w$ of $K$ and $m_w$ is $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex.
nodes.title: Archimedean factor

nodes.summary: Let $D = (I, r)$ be an Arakelov divisor on a number field $K$, and for each infinite place $w$ of $K$ let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex. Viewed as a real number, the archimedean factor of $D$ equals the real product $\prod_w r_w^{m_w}$ over all infinite places $w$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Archimedean factor as a real number

nodes.summary: For an Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$ with invertible fractional ideal $I$, the ideal norm of $D$ is the absolute norm $N(I)$ of $I$, regarded as a positive real number; it is positive because $I$ is invertible.
nodes.title: Ideal norm of an Arakelov divisor

nodes.summary: For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$ with fractional ideal $I$, the ideal norm of $D$, viewed as a real number, equals the absolute norm $N(I) \in \mathbb{Q}$ of $I$, viewed as a real number.
nodes.title: Real value of the ideal norm

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the map sending an Arakelov divisor on $K$ to its archimedean factor is a monoid homomorphism from the Arakelov divisors on $K$, multiplied componentwise, to the positive real numbers under multiplication.
nodes.title: Archimedean factor homomorphism

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the map sending an Arakelov divisor $(I, r)$ on $K$ to the absolute norm of $I$, viewed as a positive real number, is a monoid homomorphism from the Arakelov divisors on $K$, multiplied componentwise, to the positive real numbers under multiplication.
nodes.title: Ideal norm homomorphism

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the size homomorphism sends an Arakelov divisor $D = (I, (r_w)_w)$, with $I$ an invertible fractional ideal of the ring of integers of $K$ and $r_w > 0$ for each infinite place $w$, to the positive real number $\prod_w r_w^{m_w} / N(I)$, where $w$ runs over the infinite places of $K$, $m_w$ is $1$ for a real place and $2$ for a complex place, and $N(I)$ is the absolute norm of $I$. It is a…
nodes.title: Size of an Arakelov divisor

nodes.summary: For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$, the size of $D$ equals the archimedean-factor homomorphism evaluated at $D$ divided by the ideal-norm homomorphism evaluated at $D$, the quotient taken in the group of positive reals.
nodes.title: Size as a quotient of homomorphisms

nodes.summary: Let $D = (I, (r_w)_w)$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, where $I$ is an invertible fractional ideal of the ring of integers of $K$ and $r_w > 0$ for each infinite place $w$ of $K$. For each $w$ let $m_w$ be $1$ if $w$ is real and $2$ if $w$ is complex, and let $N(I)$ be the absolute norm of $I$. Then the size of $D$, as a real number, is
nodes.title: Explicit formula for the size of an Arakelov divisor

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, with invertible fractional ideal $I$ and positive real number $r_w$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$. The section set of $D$ is the set of $x \in I$ such that $w(x) \le r_w$ for every infinite place $w$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Section set of an Arakelov divisor

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor of a number field $K$, with invertible fractional ideal $I$ and positive real number $r_w$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$. An element $x \in K$ lies in the section set of $D$ if and only if $x \in I$ and $w(x) \le r_w$ for every infinite place $w$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Membership in the section set

nodes.summary: For every Arakelov divisor $D$ of a number field $K$, the section set of $D$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of section sets

nodes.summary: For a nonzero element $x$ of a number field $K$, this is the family that assigns to each infinite place $w$ of $K$ the positive real number $w(x)$.
nodes.title: Archimedean part of a principal divisor

nodes.summary: For a nonzero element $x$ of a number field $K$, the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$ consists of the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$ together with the positive real number $w(x)$ at each infinite place $w$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Principal Arakelov divisor

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field, $x \in K$ nonzero and $w$ an infinite place of $K$. The positive real number that the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$ assigns to $w$ is $w(x)$, the absolute value of $x$ at $w$.
nodes.title: Infinite component of a principal divisor

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For every nonzero $x \in K$, the fractional ideal component of the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$ is the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$.
nodes.title: Finite component of a principal divisor

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the map sending a nonzero element $x \in K$ to its principal Arakelov divisor is a group homomorphism from the multiplicative group $K^\times$ to the group of Arakelov divisors of $K$.
nodes.title: Principal divisor homomorphism

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the principal subgroup is the image of the principal divisor homomorphism, that is, the subgroup of the group of Arakelov divisors of $K$ consisting of the principal Arakelov divisors of the nonzero elements of $K$.
nodes.title: Subgroup of principal Arakelov divisors

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the degree-zero subgroup of the group of Arakelov divisors on $K$ is the kernel of the size homomorphism, that is, the subgroup of Arakelov divisors of size $1$.
nodes.title: Degree-zero Arakelov divisors

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For every nonzero $x \in K$, the principal Arakelov divisor of $x$, formed by the principal fractional ideal $x\mathcal{O}_K$ and the values $w(x)$ at the infinite places $w$ of $K$, has size $1$.
nodes.title: Principal Arakelov divisors have size one

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the subgroup of principal Arakelov divisors of $K$ is contained in the degree-zero subgroup.
nodes.title: Principal Arakelov divisors have degree zero

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with $s$ complex places and discriminant $d_K$, and let $D$ be an Arakelov divisor on $K$. If the size of $D$ is strictly greater than $(2/\pi)^s \sqrt{|d_K|}$, then the section set of $D$ contains a nonzero element of $K$.
nodes.title: Large Arakelov divisors have a nonzero section

Then $L$ is a Hilbert class field of $K$ if $L/K$ is a finite-dimensional abelian Galois extension, every nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_L$, every infinite place of $L$ is unramified over $K$, and $L$ is maximal with these properties: every number field $M$ that is a finite-dimensional abelian…
nodes.title: Hilbert class field of a number field

nodes.summary: Let $K$ and $L$ be number fields with $L$ an extension of $K$ that is a Hilbert class field of $K$. If $M$ is a number field that is a finite-dimensional abelian Galois extension of $K$, such that every nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ is unramified in $\mathcal{O}_M$ and every infinite place of $M$ is unramified over $K$, then there is a $K$-algebra homomorphism $M \to L$.

Places and completions of the rationals

reading_title.source: Places of $\mathbb{Q}$

nodes.summary: The set $M_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of places of $\mathbb{Q}$, which indexes the inequivalent normalised absolute values on $\mathbb{Q}$. It consists of one infinite place, corresponding to the ordinary archimedean absolute value, and one finite place for each prime number $p$, corresponding to the $p$-adic absolute value.
nodes.title: Places of $\mathbb{Q}$

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value $|\cdot|_v : \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}$ sends $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ to the ordinary absolute value $|q|$ when $v$ is the infinite place. When $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, it sends $q$ to the normalised $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$, where $|0|_p = 0$ and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$, with $v_p(q)$ the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.
nodes.title: Absolute value at a rational place

nodes.summary: A complete normed field bundled with its structure: a type $K$ together with a normed field structure on $K$ for which $K$ is complete with respect to the metric induced by the norm. It is used to package the completed fields $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ at its places $v$.
nodes.title: Bundled complete normed field

nodes.summary: To each place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ this assigns a complete normed field: the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ with the usual absolute value when $v$ is the infinite place, and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers with the $p$-adic norm.
nodes.title: Bundled completed field at a rational place

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is the field $\mathbb{R}$ of real numbers when $v$ is the infinite place and, when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of $p$-adic numbers.
nodes.title: Completed field at a rational place

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ with completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the canonical ring homomorphism $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ sends each rational number to itself, viewed as a real number when $v$ is the infinite place and as a $p$-adic number when $v$ is the finite place at a prime $p$.
nodes.title: Embedding of the rationals into a completion

nodes.summary: For every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value attached to the infinite place of $\mathbb{Q}$, evaluated at $q$, equals the ordinary absolute value $|q|$ of $q$ viewed as a real number.
nodes.title: Absolute value at the infinite rational place

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the absolute value attached to the finite place of $\mathbb{Q}$ at $p$, evaluated at $q$, equals the $p$-adic absolute value $|q|_p$ of $q$. Here $|0|_p = 0$, and $|q|_p = p^{-v_p(q)}$ for $q \neq 0$, where $v_p(q)$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $q$.
nodes.title: Absolute value at a finite rational place

nodes.summary: For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ and every $q \in \mathbb{Q}$, the norm in the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ of the image of $q$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|q|_v$, the absolute value attached to $v$ evaluated at $q$.
nodes.title: Norm of a rational in a completion

nodes.summary: For every place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, with completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$, the image of $\mathbb{Q}$ under the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{Q}_v$ is dense in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.
nodes.title: The rationals are dense in each completion

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some $x \ne 0$. Then there is a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the $p$-adic absolute value at the prime $p$).

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued absolute value on $\mathbb{Q}$ that is nontrivial, that is, $f(x) \ne 1$ for some $x \ne 0$. Then there is exactly one place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $f$ is equivalent to the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ (the ordinary absolute value at the infinite place, the $p$-adic absolute value at the prime $p$).
nodes.title: Ostrowski's theorem for $\mathbb{Q}$, indexed by places

reading_title.source: Embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, normed by a place, into its completion

nodes.summary: For a place $v$ of $\mathbb{Q}$, the ring homomorphism from $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped with the absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ attached to $v$ as its norm, into the completed field $\mathbb{Q}_v$ given by the canonical embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ ($\mathbb{Q}_v = \mathbb{R}$ at the infinite place and $\mathbb{Q}_v = \mathbb{Q}_p$ at a prime $p$).
nodes.title: Embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, normed by a place, into its completion

parts: into its completion at a place is an isometry
reading_title.source: The embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ into its completion at a place is an isometry

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, and let $\mathbb{Q}_v$ be the completed field at $v$. The canonical embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$, equipped with the metric $d(x, y) = |x - y|_v$, into $\mathbb{Q}_v$ is an isometry: for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}$, the distance between the images of $x$ and $y$ in $\mathbb{Q}_v$ equals $|x - y|_v$.
nodes.title: The embedding of $\mathbb{Q}$ into its completion at a place is an isometry

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a place of $\mathbb{Q}$, let $|\cdot|_v$ be the absolute value attached to $v$, let $\mathbb{Q}_v$ be the completed field at $v$, and write $(\mathbb{Q}, |\cdot|_v)$ for the field $\mathbb{Q}$ equipped with $|\cdot|_v$. The image of the canonical ring homomorphism $(\mathbb{Q}, |\cdot|_v) \to \mathbb{Q}_v$, which sends each rational number to itself, is dense in $\mathbb{Q}_v$.
nodes.title: Density of the rationals with a place's absolute value in the completion

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$. The degree-normalized absolute value at $v$ is the absolute value $x \mapsto |x|_v^{1/d}$ on $K$.
nodes.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at a finite place

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_v^{1/d}$.
nodes.title: Value of the degree-normalized absolute value at a finite place

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$, let $v$ be a finite place of $K$, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be the nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers of $K$ that defines $v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_{\mathfrak{p}}^{1/d}$, where $|x|_{\mathfrak{p}} = N(\mathfrak{p})^{-v_{\mathfrak{p}}(x)}$ for $x \neq 0$ and $|0|_{\mathfrak{p}} = 0$, with…
nodes.title: Degree-normalized finite absolute value through the prime ideal

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be an infinite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ and multiplicity $m_v$, equal to $1$ if $v$ is real and $2$ if $v$ is complex. The degree-normalized absolute value at $v$ is the absolute value $x \mapsto |x|_v^{m_v/d}$ on $K$.
nodes.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at an infinite place

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be an infinite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$ and multiplicity $m_v$, equal to $1$ if $v$ is real and $2$ if $v$ is complex. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_v^{m_v/d}$.
nodes.title: Value of the degree-normalized absolute value at an infinite place

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a real infinite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_v^{1/d}$.
nodes.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at a real place

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $d = [K : \mathbb{Q}]$ and let $v$ be a complex infinite place of $K$, with absolute value $|\cdot|_v$. For every $x \in K$, the degree-normalized absolute value of $x$ at $v$ equals $|x|_v^{2/d}$.
nodes.title: Degree-normalized absolute value at a complex place

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, the places of $K$ form the disjoint union of the infinite places of $K$ (the absolute values coming from complex embeddings of $K$) and the finite places of $K$ (the absolute values coming from nonzero prime ideals of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$).
nodes.title: Places of a number field

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, each infinite place $v$ of $K$ is regarded as a place of $K$ via the inclusion of the infinite places into the disjoint union of the infinite and finite places of $K$.
nodes.title: Infinite places as places

nodes.summary: For a number field $K$, each finite place $v$ of $K$ is regarded as a place of $K$ via the inclusion of the finite places into the disjoint union of the infinite and finite places of $K$.
nodes.title: Finite places as places

nodes.summary: Let $v$ be a finite place of a number field $K$ and $\mathfrak{p}_v$ the corresponding nonzero prime ideal of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. The residue norm $N(v)$ is the absolute norm $|\mathcal{O}_K / \mathfrak{p}_v|$ of $\mathfrak{p}_v$, the cardinality of the residue field at $v$, regarded as a real number.

nodes.summary: For a real place $v$ of a number field $K$, let $\mathfrak m_v$ be the modulus of $K$ with finite part the unit ideal $\mathcal O_K$ and infinite part $\{v\}$. The finite part of $\mathfrak m_v$ is the unit ideal $\mathcal O_K$.
nodes.title: Finite part of the modulus of a real place

nodes.title: Infinite part of the modulus of a real place

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with finite part the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ of $\mathcal O_K$. The elements coprime to $\mathfrak m$ form the subgroup of $K^\times$ consisting of those $x$ whose principal fractional ideal $(x)$ is coprime to $\mathfrak m$, that is, has exponent $0$ at every nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$ containing $\mathfrak m_0$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathfrak m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$, with infinite part the finite set $\mathfrak m_\infty$ of real places of $K$. An element $x \in K^\times$ is positive at the infinite part of $\mathfrak m$ when $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every real place $w \in \mathfrak m_\infty$, where $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb R$ is the real embedding corresponding to $w$.

For a nonzero prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $\mathcal O_K$, write $v_{\mathfrak p}(I)$ for the exponent of $\mathfrak p$ in the factorization of a nonzero fractional ideal $I$ of $\mathcal O_K$, and for $y \in K$ write…
nodes.title: Elements congruent to one modulo a modulus

nodes.title: Ray elements have order zero at the primes dividing the modulus

nodes.title: Finite residue map

nodes.summary: For a modulus $\mathfrak m$ of a number field $K$, the ray class map is the canonical quotient homomorphism from the group of nonzero fractional ideals of $K$ coprime to the finite part of $\mathfrak m$ onto the ray class group of $\mathfrak m$, sending each such ideal to its class modulo the ray group of $\mathfrak m$.
nodes.title: Ray class map

nodes.summary: For a real place $w$ of a number field $K$, let $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$ be the corresponding real embedding. nodes.title: Sign of a unit at a real place

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a real place of a number field $K$ with real embedding $\sigma_w \colon K \to \mathbb{R}$. For every $x \in K^\times$, the sign of $x$ at $w$, an element of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ written multiplicatively, is the identity if and only if $\sigma_w(x) > 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be the corresponding real embedding of $K$. For every ray element $x$ of $m$, the infinite sign map of $m$ sends $x$ to the identity if and only if $x$ is positive at the infinite part of $m$, that is, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.
nodes.title: Trivial infinite sign means positivity at the modulus

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be the real embedding of $K$ at $w$. The positive ray elements of $m$ form the subgroup of the ray elements of $m$ defined as the kernel of the infinite sign map of $m$; equivalently, they are the ray elements $x$ with $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.
nodes.title: Ray elements positive at the infinite part

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$ with finite set of real places $m_\infty$, and for a real place $w$ let $\sigma_w$ be the real embedding of $K$ at $w$. A ray element $x$ of $m$ is a positive ray element of $m$ if and only if $x$ is positive at the infinite part of $m$, that is, $\sigma_w(x) > 0$ for every $w \in m_\infty$.

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The residue-sign map of $m$ is the group homomorphism from the ray elements of $m$ to the residue-sign target of $m$ that sends a ray element $x$ to the pair formed by the image of $x$ under the infinite sign map of $m$ and the image of $x$ under the finite residue map of $m$.
nodes.title: Residue-sign map

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. For every ray element $x$ of $m$, the image of $x$ under the residue-sign map of $m$ is the pair whose first component is the image of $x$ under the infinite sign map of $m$ and whose second component is the image of $x$ under the finite residue map of $m$.

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The ray-one subgroup of $m$ is the subgroup of the ray elements of $m$ consisting of the ray elements $x$ that lie in the finite ray-one subgroup of $m$ (those congruent to $1$ at the finite part of $m$) and in the subgroup of ray elements positive at every real place in the infinite part of $m$.
nodes.title: Ray-one subgroup

nodes.title: Surjectivity of the residue-sign map

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. The kernel of the residue-sign map of $m$ is the ray-one subgroup of $m$.
nodes.title: Kernel of the residue-sign map

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a modulus of a number field $K$. Absolute values on fields

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Then every real-valued absolute value $v$ on $K$ is nonarchimedean: $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute values in positive characteristic are nonarchimedean

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a finite field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Then $v(x) = 1$ for every nonzero $x \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute values on finite fields are trivial

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. The topology induced by $v$ on $K$ is the topology pulled back along the identity map from $K$ to $K$ equipped with the norm $v$; equivalently, it is the metric topology of the distance $d(x, y) = v(x - y)$ on $K$.
nodes.title: Topology induced by an absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$, $w$ real-valued absolute values on $K$. The topologies induced on $K$ by $v$ and by $w$ are equal if and only if $v$ and $w$ are equivalent.
nodes.title: Absolute values inducing the same topology are equivalent

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Then $v$ is nonarchimedean, that is, $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$, if and only if $v(n) \le 1$ for every natural number $n$, viewed as the element $n \cdot 1$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Nonarchimedean criterion for absolute values

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $v(n) \le 1$ for every natural number $n$, viewed as the element $n \cdot 1$ of $K$, then $v$ is nonarchimedean: $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute values bounded by one on the natural numbers are nonarchimedean

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Then $v$ is nonarchimedean, that is, $v(x + y) \le \max(v(x), v(y))$ for all $x, y \in K$, if and only if $v(n) \le 1$ for every positive integer $n$, viewed as the element $n \cdot 1$ of $K$.
nodes.title: Nonarchimedean criterion using positive integers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring, $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $R$ and $c$ a real number with $0 < c \le 1$. The $c$-th power of $v$ is the real-valued absolute value $x \mapsto v(x)^c$ on $R$.
nodes.title: Powers of an absolute value

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring, $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $R$ and $c$ a real number with $0 < c \le 1$. The $c$-th power of $v$ takes the value $v(x)^c$ at every $x \in R$.

reading_title.source: Solvability of $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$

nodes.title: Solvability of $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$

nodes.summary: For a field $F$ and nonzero elements $a, b \in F$, the Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_F$ is the integer $1$ if there exist $x, y \in F$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$, and $-1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Hilbert symbol of a field

parts: The Hilbert symbol of a field is
reading_title.source: The Hilbert symbol of a field is $\pm 1$

nodes.summary: For every field $F$ and all nonzero $a, b \in F$, the Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_F$ of $a$ and $b$ over $F$ equals $1$ or $-1$.
nodes.title: The Hilbert symbol of a field is $\pm 1$

reading_title.source: The $p$-adic Hilbert symbol

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ is the integer $1$ if there exist $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$, and $-1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic Hilbert symbol

reading_title.source: When the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $1$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ equals $1$ if and only if there exist $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$.
nodes.title: When the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $1$

reading_title.source: When the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $-1$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ equals $-1$ if and only if there are no $x, y \in \mathbb{Q}_p$ with $ax^2 + by^2 = 1$.
nodes.title: When the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $-1$

reading_title.source: The $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $\pm 1$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and all nonzero $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic Hilbert symbol $(a, b)_p$ equals $1$ or $-1$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic Hilbert symbol is $\pm 1$

Then there is a nonzero vector $(x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{Q}_p^n$ with $a_1 x_1^2 + \dots + a_n x_n^2 = 0$.

reading_title.source: Real Hilbert symbol equal to $-1$

nodes.title: Real Hilbert symbol equal to $-1$

nodes.title: Inclusion of $p$-adic integer units

reading_title.source: Value of the inclusion of $p$-adic integer units

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and a unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p$, the image of $u$ under the inclusion of the units of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ into the units of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, equals $u$ viewed as an element of $\mathbb{Q}_p$.

Krasner's lemma

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a normed field with algebraic closure $\overline{K}$, and let $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ be the spectral norm on $\overline{K}$ over $K$. For $\alpha, \beta \in \overline{K}$, $\alpha$ is the closest conjugate to $\beta$ if $\lVert \beta - \alpha \rVert < \lVert \beta - \sigma(\alpha) \rVert$ for every $K$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $\overline{K}$ with $\sigma(\alpha) \ne \alpha$.
nodes.title: Closest conjugate

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a complete nontrivially normed field whose norm is ultrametric, with algebraic closure $\overline{K}$, let $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ be the spectral norm on $\overline{K}$ over $K$, and let $\alpha, \beta, \alpha' \in \overline{K}$. If $\alpha$ is the closest conjugate to $\beta$ and $\alpha' \ne \alpha$ is a conjugate of $\alpha$ over $K$, then $\lVert \alpha - \beta \rVert < \lVert \alpha - \alpha' \rVert$.
nodes.title: Closest conjugates satisfy Krasner's hypothesis

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a complete nontrivially normed field whose norm is ultrametric, with algebraic closure $\overline{K}$, and let $\alpha, \beta \in \overline{K}$. If $\alpha$ is the closest conjugate to $\beta$ and $\alpha$ is separable over $K$, then $K(\alpha) \subseteq K(\beta)$.

Then there is a real $\delta > 0$ such that every monic $g \in K[X]$ with $\lVert f - g \rVert_1 < \delta$, where $\lVert \cdot \rVert_1$ is the $\ell^1$ norm (the sum of the norms of the coefficients), is irreducible and separable.

Let $f \in L[X]$ be monic, irreducible and separable, and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be real. Morita's p-adic gamma function

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and a natural number $n$, this is the $p$-adic integer $(-1)^n \prod_{0 < j < n,\ p \nmid j} j$: $(-1)^n$ times the product of the positive integers below $n$ that are not divisible by $p$. At $n = 0$ the product is empty and the value is $1$. These are the finite values that Morita's $p$-adic gamma function interpolates.
nodes.title: Morita's p-adic gamma values at natural numbers

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$, a continuous function $\Gamma : \mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ is a Morita $p$-adic gamma function when $\Gamma(0) = 1$, $\Gamma(n)$ equals Morita's finite value $(-1)^n \prod_{0 < j < n,\ p \nmid j} j$ for every positive integer $n$, and $\Gamma(x)$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_p$.
nodes.title: Morita's p-adic gamma function

nodes.summary: For every odd prime $p$ there is exactly one continuous function $\Gamma : \mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ that is a Morita $p$-adic gamma function, that is, $\Gamma(0) = 1$, $\Gamma(n) = (-1)^n \prod_{0 < j < n,\ p \nmid j} j$ for every positive integer $n$, and $\Gamma(x)$ is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}_p$.
nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of Morita's p-adic gamma function
p-adic expansions

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. The $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$ is the natural number $(a_{n+1} - a_n)/p^n$.
nodes.title: Digits of a p-adic integer

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$ is strictly less than $p$.
nodes.title: p-adic digits are less than p

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. The $p$-adic expansion of $a$ is the sequence whose $n$-th term is the $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$, viewed as an element of $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.
nodes.title: p-adic expansion

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th term of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$, read as a natural number, is the $n$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$.
nodes.title: Terms of the p-adic expansion are the digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit $d_n$ of $a$ satisfies $d_n p^n = a_{n+1} - a_n$.
nodes.title: p-adic digits measure the gaps between approximations

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th $p$-adic digit $d_n$ of $a$ satisfies $a_{n+1} = a_n + d_n p^n$.
nodes.title: One-step reconstruction from p-adic digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, $a_{n+1} = a_n + e_n p^n$, where $e_n$ is the $n$-th term of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$, read as a natural number.
nodes.title: One-step reconstruction from the p-adic expansion

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, $a_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} d_k p^k$, where $d_k$ is the $k$-th $p$-adic digit of $a$.
nodes.title: Approximations as sums of p-adic digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, and for each $n \ge 0$ let $a_n$ be the unique natural number with $a_n < p^n$ and $a \equiv a_n \pmod{p^n \mathbb{Z}_p}$. For every $n \ge 0$, $a_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} e_k p^k$, where $e_k$ is the $k$-th term of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$, read as a natural number.
nodes.title: Approximations as truncations of the p-adic expansion

reading_title.source: $p$-adic digits determine a $p$-adic integer

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. If two $p$-adic integers $a, a' \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ have the same $n$-th $p$-adic digit for every $n \ge 0$, then $a = a'$.
nodes.title: $p$-adic digits determine a $p$-adic integer

reading_title.source: Existence of a $p$-adic integer with prescribed digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. For every sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers with $b_n < p$ for all $n$, there is a $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ whose $n$-th $p$-adic digit is $b_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Existence of a $p$-adic integer with prescribed digits

reading_title.source: Existence and uniqueness of $p$-adic integers with prescribed digits

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. For every sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers with $b_n < p$ for all $n$, there is exactly one $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ whose $n$-th $p$-adic digit is $b_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of $p$-adic integers with prescribed digits

reading_title.source: The $p$-adic expansion map is injective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. If two $p$-adic integers $a, a' \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ have the same $p$-adic expansion, then $a = a'$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic expansion map is injective

reading_title.source: The $p$-adic expansion map is surjective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. Every sequence $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with values in $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$ is the $p$-adic expansion of some $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic expansion map is surjective

reading_title.source: The $p$-adic expansion map is bijective

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. The map sending a $p$-adic integer $a \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ to its $p$-adic expansion is a bijection from $\mathbb{Z}_p$ onto the set of all sequences $(b_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with values in $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.
nodes.title: The $p$-adic expansion map is bijective
p-adic Pontryagin duals

reading_title.source: The quotient $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$, $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module, by the image of $\mathbb{Z}_p$ under the canonical inclusion $\mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p$.
nodes.title: The quotient $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$

reading_title.source: Algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module $A$, the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$ is the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}(A, \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p)$ of all $\mathbb{Z}_p$-linear maps from $A$ to $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$; no topology or continuity condition is imposed.
nodes.title: Algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual

reading_title.source: Extensionality for the $p$-adic Pontryagin dual

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $A$ a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module. If two elements $\varphi, \psi$ of the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$ satisfy $\varphi(a) = \psi(a)$ for every $a \in A$, then $\varphi = \psi$.
nodes.title: Extensionality for the $p$-adic Pontryagin dual

reading_title.source: The quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$, this is the canonical projection $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$, $x \mapsto x + \mathbb{Z}_p$, as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-linear map.
nodes.title: The quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$

reading_title.source: The quotient map vanishes on $\mathbb{Z}_p$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and every $z \in \mathbb{Z}_p$, the quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ sends the image of $z$ in $\mathbb{Q}_p$ to $0$.
nodes.title: The quotient map vanishes on $\mathbb{Z}_p$

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$ and every $x \in \mathbb{Q}_p$, the quotient map $\mathbb{Q}_p \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ sends $x$ to its class $x + \mathbb{Z}_p$ in the quotient module.
nodes.title: The quotient map is the quotient projection

reading_title.source: Contragredient action on the $p$-adic Pontryagin dual

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a group and $A$ a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module on which $G$ acts by additive maps commuting with the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action. For $g \in G$ and $\varphi$ in the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$, $g \cdot \varphi$ is the element $a \mapsto \varphi(g^{-1} a)$ of the dual.
nodes.title: Contragredient action on the $p$-adic Pontryagin dual

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a group and $A$ a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module on which $G$ acts by additive maps commuting with the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action. For $g \in G$, $\varphi$ in the algebraic $p$-adic Pontryagin dual of $A$ and $a \in A$, the contragredient action satisfies $(g \cdot \varphi)(a) = \varphi(g^{-1} a)$.
nodes.title: Evaluating the contragredient action
p-adic valuations of polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $f \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. Dilatation data for $f$ at $x_0$ consist of a natural number $e$ and a polynomial $g \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ such that $g(X) = p^{-e} f(x_0 + pX)$ as polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and the reduction of $g$ modulo $p$ is nonzero.
nodes.title: Dilatation of a p-adic polynomial at a point

nodes.summary: For every prime $p$, the exponent $e = 0$ and the polynomial $g = 1$ form dilatation data for the constant polynomial $1 \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ at the point $x_0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Dilatation of the constant polynomial one at zero

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $f \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ have nonzero reduction modulo $p$. Then for every $x_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ there are a natural number $e$ and a polynomial $g \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ with nonzero reduction modulo $p$ such that $g(X) = p^{-e} f(x_0 + pX)$ as polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}_p$; that is, dilatation data for $f$ at $x_0$ exist.
nodes.title: Existence of dilatations of p-adic polynomials

reading_title.source: The $p$-adic valuation of an integer polynomial

nodes.summary: Call $v \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ primitive when the greatest common divisor of its four entries is $1$. For every $X \in \mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ and every primitive $v$, the vector $Xv$ is primitive, so $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ acts on the primitive vectors of $\mathbb{Z}^4$ by $v \mapsto Xv$.
nodes.title: General linear group action on primitive vectors

nodes.summary: The Descartes matrix is the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix $M$ with $M_{ii} = 1$ for every $i$ and $M_{ij} = -1$ for $i \ne j$. It is the matrix of the Descartes form: for $v = (a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ one has $v^{\mathsf T} M v = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2) - (a + b + c + d)^2$.
nodes.title: Descartes matrix

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be the Descartes matrix. The Descartes orthogonal group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ consisting of the matrices $X$ with $X^{\mathsf T} M X = M$, that is, the invertible integer matrices that preserve the Descartes form $2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2) - (a + b + c + d)^2$.
nodes.title: Descartes orthogonal group

nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be the set of vectors $(a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ with $(a + b + c + d)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2)$ and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$. For every matrix $X$ in the Descartes orthogonal group and every $v \in Q$, the vector $Xv$ lies in $Q$, so the Descartes orthogonal group acts on $Q$ by $v \mapsto Xv$.
nodes.title: Descartes orthogonal group action

nodes.summary: An integral primitive Descartes quadruple is a vector $(a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ such that $a + b + c + d > 0$, the Descartes equation $(a + b + c + d)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2)$ holds, and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$.

Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, b, c, 2a + 2b + 2c - d)$.

nodes.summary: The Apollonian group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by the four matrices $S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4$, where $S_i$ agrees with the $4 \times 4$ identity matrix except in row $i$, which has entry $-1$ in column $i$ and entry $2$ in each of the other three columns.

nodes.summary: The transformation group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by the Apollonian group together with all $4 \times 4$ permutation matrices.

nodes.summary: For every $g$ in the transformation group, $g$ maps the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples into itself: if $v \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ is an integral primitive Descartes quadruple, then so is $g v$.

nodes.summary: Each element $g$ of the transformation group sends an integral primitive Descartes quadruple $v$ to $g v$, by matrix–vector multiplication: this is the restriction of the action of the transformation group on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ to the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples, which is closed under the action.
nodes.title: Action of the transformation group on integral primitive Descartes quadruples

nodes.title: Primitive Apollonian circle packing

nodes.title: Curvature set

nodes.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the primitive Apollonian circle packing generated by the integral primitive Descartes quadruple $(-3, 5, 8, 8)$. For every integer $n$, $n^2$ does not belong to the curvature set of $\mathcal{A}$.

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a primitive Apollonian circle packing. The missing curvature set of $A$ is the set of positive integers $n$ that do not lie in the curvature set of $A$ but are congruent modulo $24$ to some element of the curvature set of $A$.
nodes.title: Missing curvature set

nodes.summary: For a primitive Apollonian circle packing $A$ and a real number $N$, the number of missing curvatures of $A$ up to $N$ is the number of elements $n$ of the missing curvature set of $A$ with $n \le N$, regarded as a real number.
nodes.title: Number of missing curvatures

nodes.summary: For a primitive Apollonian circle packing $\mathcal{A}$ and a real number $N$, let $M_{\mathcal{A}}(N)$ be the number of missing curvatures of $\mathcal{A}$ up to $N$. There are infinitely many primitive Apollonian circle packings $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\sqrt{N} = O(M_{\mathcal{A}}(N))$ as $N$ tends to infinity. In other words, for these packings the number of missing curvatures up to $N$ is $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many packings with many missing curvatures

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p > 2$ and $p \ne 5$, and let $\left(\frac{5}{p}\right)$ be the Legendre symbol of $5$ modulo $p$. Then $p$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_{p-1}$ if $\left(\frac{5}{p}\right) = 1$, and $p$ divides the Fibonacci number $F_{p+1}$ otherwise. Since $\left(\frac{5}{p}\right) = \pm 1$, this says that $p$ divides $F_{p - \left(\frac{5}{p}\right)}$.

Then there is a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ the three integers $U_n - 1$, $U_n$ and $U_n + 1$ are all composite, that is, each is greater than $1$ and not prime.

Then there is an integer $K > 0$ such that for every natural number $n$ the three integers $U_n + K - 1$, $U_n + K$ and $U_n + K + 1$ are all composite, that is, each is greater than $1$ and not prime.

nodes.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let $m$ and $u$ be natural numbers. Then $u$ is a primitive divisor of $a_m$ when $m \ge 1$, $u \ge 2$, $u$ divides $a_m$, and $u$ divides no $a_s$ with $1 \le s < m$.

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $n$ and $p$ be natural numbers. Then $p$ is a large Zsigmondy prime for $(a, b, n)$ when $p$ is a primitive prime divisor of the term $a^n - b^n$ of the integer sequence $(a^m - b^m)_{m \ge 0}$, that is, $n \ge 1$, $p$ is prime, $p$ divides $a^n - b^n$ and $p$ divides no $a^m - b^m$ with $1 \le m < n$, and moreover $p^2$ divides $a^n - b^n$ or $p > n + 1$.

reading_title.source: The $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence

nodes.summary: A sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ satisfies the $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence if $F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2} + \dots + F_{n-m}$ for every integer $n$, that is, $F_n = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} F_{n-i-1}$. For $m = 0$ this says $F_n = 0$ for all $n$.
nodes.title: The $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence

reading_title.source: The standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence

nodes.summary: A sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$ is the standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence if it satisfies the $m$-step Fibonacci recurrence, $F_i = 0$ for every natural number $i < m - 1$, and $F_{m-1} = 1$, where $m - 1$ is computed in the integers.
nodes.title: The standard order-$m$ Fibonacci sequence

nodes.summary: For a sequence $F : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Q}$, a natural number $m$, integers $N$ and $l$, and a rational number $q$, $S(m,N,l,q) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} q^k F_{k+l}$; for $N < 0$ this is the empty sum $0$.

The $r$-Fibonacci polynomials $U^{(r)}_n(x, y) \in R$, $n \ge 0$, are defined by $U^{(r)}_0 = 0$, $U^{(r)}_k = x^{k-1}$ for $1 \le k \le r$, and $U^{(r)}_{n+1} = x \, U^{(r)}_n + y \, U^{(r)}_{n-r}$ for $n \ge r$.

nodes.summary: An integer sequence $s \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ is C-finite if there are $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$ and integers $c_0, \dots, c_{p-1}$ such that $s(n + p) = \sum_{i=0}^{p-1} c_i \, s(n + i)$ for every $n \ge q$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and an exponent vector $\alpha = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_k) \in \mathbb{N}^k$, the isobaric weight of $\alpha$ is $\sum_{j=1}^k j \alpha_j$.
nodes.title: Isobaric weight of an exponent vector

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $n$ be natural numbers. A polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Z}[t_1, \dots, t_k]$ is isobaric of degree $n$ if every monomial $t_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots t_k^{\alpha_k}$ occurring in $P$ with nonzero coefficient satisfies $\sum_{j=1}^k j \alpha_j = n$; that is, $P$ is weighted homogeneous of degree $n$ when the variable $t_j$ has weight $j$. In particular, the zero polynomial is isobaric of every degree.

nodes.summary: Let $a_0 < a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers and write $A_n = a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{n-1}$ for the product of its first $n$ terms. Suppose that $(n + 1) \log \log a_n / \log a_{n+1} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, and that there is a real number $c < 2$ such that $\log A_n / \log a_n < c$ for infinitely many $n$. Then $a$ is not a Bonse sequence.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k$ be a natural number and let $n = 2^k p$. Suppose that $n$ is strongly $2$-near perfect, that is, $\sigma(n) = 2n + d + n/d$ for some divisor $d$ of $n$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function. Then there is a natural number $a \le k$ with $p(1 + 2^{k-a}) = 2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1$, that is, $p = (2^{k+1} - 2^a - 1)/(1 + 2^{k-a})$.

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is s-Zumkeller if its proper divisors can be split into two disjoint nonempty sets whose elements have equal sums of squares. Each of the two sums is then $(\sigma_2(n) - n^2)/2$, where $\sigma_2(n)$ is the sum of the squares of the positive divisors of $n$.

A family $(X_p)$, indexed by the primes $p$, of maps $X_p \colon \Omega \to \{-1, 1\}$ into the units of $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Rademacher family for $\mu$ when every $X_p$ is measurable, every $X_p$ has law the Rademacher measure (the uniform measure on $\{-1, 1\}$) under $\mu$, and the family is mutually independent under $\mu$.

For every squarefree natural number $n$, $f(n) = \prod_{p \mid n} \varepsilon_p(\omega)$, the product of the prime signs $\varepsilon_p(\omega)$ at $\omega$ over the distinct primes $p$ dividing $n$.

Rearick logarithm

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued arithmetic function with $f(1) > 0$, and let $f^{-1}$ be its Dirichlet inverse. The Rearick logarithm of $f$ is the arithmetic function $L(f)$ with $L(f)(0) = 0$, $L(f)(1) = \log f(1)$, and $L(f)(n) = \sum_{d \mid n} f(d) \, f^{-1}(n/d) \log d$ for $n > 1$.
nodes.title: Rearick logarithm

nodes.title: The Rearick logarithm as a Dirichlet convolution

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued arithmetic function with $f(1) > 0$, and let $L(f)$ be its Rearick logarithm. Then $f$ is multiplicative (that is, $f(1) = 1$ and $f(mn) = f(m) f(n)$ whenever $m$ and $n$ are coprime) if and only if $L(f)(m) = 0$ for every natural number $m$ that is not a prime power, including $m = 0$ and $m = 1$.

For $n \ge 1$, $v(n)^2$ is the largest square dividing $n$, and $n = u(n)\, v(n)^2$ where $u(n) = n / v(n)^2$ is squarefree.

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring. The unitary convolution of two arithmetic functions $f$ and $g$ with values in $R$ is the arithmetic function $f \sqcup g$ given by $(f \sqcup g)(n) = \sum_{d \parallel n} f(d)\, g(n/d)$, where the sum runs over the unitary divisors $d$ of $n$: for $n \ge 1$ these are the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $\gcd(d, n/d) = 1$, and $0$ has no unitary divisors. In particular $(f \sqcup g)(0) = 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_l)$ be a list of positive integers, with subscripts read modulo $l$. For $1 \le j \le l$ and a natural number $i$, the left-hand index of $k$ at $(j, i)$ is the index $(k_j - i + 1, k_{j+1}, \dots, k_{j+l-1}, i)$ when $1 \le i \le k_j - 1$, and the index $(2)$ otherwise. reading_title.source: The Nagell–Ljunggren cube equation for $n \equiv 5 \pmod 6$

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number with $n \equiv 5 \pmod 6$. Then there are no integers $x$ and $y$ with $x \equiv 2, 3, 5$ or $6 \pmod 9$ such that $x^n - 1 = (x - 1) y^3$. Since such an $x$ is not $1$, this says that $(x^n - 1)/(x - 1) = y^3$ has no such integer solution.

If $q = 2$, or $3 \mid n$, or $4 \mid n$, or $q = 3$ and $n \not\equiv 5 \pmod 6$, then $(x, y, n, q)$ is one of $(3, 11, 5, 2)$, $(7, 20, 4, 2)$, $(18, 7, 3, 3)$ and $(-19, 7, 3, 3)$.

Then the least prime divisor of $n$ is at least $29$, $n$ has at most four prime factors counted with multiplicity, $n$ is prime if $q = 3$, and $n = q$ if $q \mid n$.

Büchi's problem

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a natural number. A sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ is a Büchi sequence of length $M$ when the second differences of its squares equal $2$ along its first $M$ terms, that is, $u_{j+2}^2 - 2u_{j+1}^2 + u_j^2 = 2$ for every $j$ with $j + 2 < M$.
nodes.title: Büchi sequences

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a natural number. A sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ is trivial at length $M$ when there is an integer $x$ with $u_j^2 = (x + j)^2$ for every $j < M$; equivalently, after changing the signs of some of its terms, its first $M$ terms are the consecutive integers $x, x + 1, \dots, x + M - 1$.
nodes.title: Trivial sequences in Büchi's problem

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $M \ge 5$ such that every integer Büchi sequence of length $M$ is trivial: for every sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ with $u_{j+2}^2 - 2u_{j+1}^2 + u_j^2 = 2$ for all $j$ with $j + 2 < M$, there is an integer $x$ with $u_j^2 = (x + j)^2$ for all $j < M$.
nodes.title: Büchi's square-sequence conjecture

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $M \ge 5$ such that every integer Büchi sequence of length $M$ is trivial: for every sequence of integers $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ with $u_{j+2}^2 - 2u_{j+1}^2 + u_j^2 = 2$ for all $j$ with $j + 2 < M$, there is an integer $x$ with $u_j^2 = (x + j)^2$ for all $j < M$.

nodes.summary: For integers $x$ and $y$, we have $x > 0$, $y > 0$ and $x^2 - 3y^2 = 1$ if and only if $x + y\sqrt{3} = (2 + \sqrt{3})^k$ in $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{3}]$ for some natural number $k \ge 1$. Writing $(2 + \sqrt{3})^k = u_k + v_k \sqrt{3}$ for $k \ge 0$, we have $(u_1, v_1) = (2, 1)$, $(u_2, v_2) = (7, 4)$, and $u_{k+2} = 4u_{k+1} - u_k$ and $v_{k+2} = 4v_{k+1} - v_k$ for every $k \ge 0$.

Then $a$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$ when $n \ge 1$, $\lambda > 0$, $a$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{<}$ (that is, $2 \le a_1 < \dots < a_n$, so the unit fractions are distinct), and $\sum_{i=1}^{n} 1/a_i < \lambda$, the sum taken in the real numbers.
nodes.title: Egyptian underapproximations with strictly increasing denominators

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Nondecreasing underapproximations have at least one term

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $\lambda > 0$.
nodes.title: The target of a nondecreasing underapproximation is positive

nodes.summary: If $a = (a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of a real number $\lambda$, then $a$ lies in $\mathcal{E}_n^{\le}$, that is, $2 \le a_1 \le \dots \le a_n$.
nodes.title: Nondecreasing underapproximations have Egyptian denominator tuples

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $a_i \ge 2$ for every $1 \le i \le n$.
nodes.title: Denominators of a nondecreasing underapproximation are at least two

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $a_i \le a_j$ whenever $1 \le i \le j \le n$.
nodes.title: Denominators of a nondecreasing underapproximation are nondecreasing

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a nondecreasing underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $\sum_{i=1}^{n} 1/a_i < \lambda$.
nodes.title: A nondecreasing underapproximation stays below its target

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\lambda$ a real number and $a_1, \dots, a_n$ natural numbers. If $(a_1, \dots, a_n)$ is a strict underapproximation of $\lambda$, then $n \ge 1$.

nodes.title: Strict underapproximations have strictly increasing Egyptian denominators
