Erdős–Straus conjecture

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x$ be a natural number with $\lceil p/4 \rceil \le x \le \lceil p/2 \rceil$. If $d$ is a positive divisor of $x^2$ with $d \equiv -px \pmod{4x - p}$, then there are natural numbers $y$ and $z$ with $(4x - p)\,y = px + d$ and $(4x - p)\,d\,z = px(px + d)$ such that $x \le y \le z$ and $p \nmid y$.
nodes.title: Type I Erdős–Straus triples from divisors of a square

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x \le y \le z$ be positive integers with $4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z$ and $p \nmid y$. Then $\lceil p/4 \rceil \le x \le \lceil p/2 \rceil$, and there is a positive divisor $d$ of $x^2$ with $d \equiv -px \pmod{4x - p}$, $(4x - p)\,y = px + d$ and $(4x - p)\,d\,z = px(px + d)$.
nodes.title: Divisor criterion necessary for type I Erdős–Straus solutions

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $x \le y \le z$ be positive integers with $4/p = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z$ and $p \mid y$. Then $\lceil p/4 \rceil \le x \le \lceil p/2 \rceil$, and there is a positive divisor $d$ of $x^2$ with $d \le x$, $d \equiv -x \pmod{4x - p}$, $(4x - p)\,y = p(x + d)$ and $(4x - p)\,d\,z = px(x + d)$.
nodes.title: Divisor criterion necessary for type II Erdős–Straus solutions

nodes.summary: For a prime $p$, there are positive integers $a \le b \le c$ with $p \nmid a$, $p \mid b$, $p \mid c$ and $4/p = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c$ if and only if there are positive integers $q$, $r$, $s_1$, $s_2$ with $q \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, both $s_1$ and $s_2$ dividing $(q + 1)/4$, and $p + 4 s_1 s_2 = qr$.
nodes.title: Chamberland's characterization of restricted Erdős–Straus representations
Odd greedy algorithm for Egyptian fractions

nodes.summary: For a rational number $r$ and a natural number $d$, $d$ is the odd greedy choice at $r$ when $r > 0$, $d$ is positive and odd, $1/d \le r$, and $d \le e$ for every positive odd natural number $e$ with $1/e \le r$. Equivalently, $1/d$ is the largest unit fraction with odd denominator that does not exceed $r$.
nodes.title: Odd greedy choice

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $r > 0$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice needs a positive remainder

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $d > 0$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice is positive

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $d$ is odd.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice is odd

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $1/d \le r$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy unit fraction does not exceed the remainder

nodes.summary: If $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$, then $d \le e$ for every positive odd natural number $e$ with $1/e \le r$.
nodes.title: The odd greedy choice is minimal

nodes.summary: If $d$ and $d'$ are both odd greedy choices at the same rational number $r$, then $d = d'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the odd greedy choice

nodes.summary: A natural number $d$ is the odd greedy choice at a rational number $r$ if and only if $r > 0$ and $d$ is the least element of the set of positive odd natural numbers $e$ with $1/e \le r$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the odd greedy choice

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be an even natural number and let $d_1, \dots, d_m$ be odd natural numbers. If integers $a$ and $b$ with $b \ne 0$ satisfy $a/b = \sum_{i=1}^{m} 1/d_i$, then $a$ is even.
nodes.title: Even sums of odd unit fractions have even numerator

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $d$ be positive natural numbers and let $x_1$ be an odd natural number. Then $x_1$ is the odd greedy choice at $n/d$ (the first denominator of the odd greedy expansion of $n/d$) if and only if $d \le n x_1$ and $n x_1 < d + 2n$, that is, $0 \le n x_1 - d < 2n$ in the integers.

reading_title.source: $S$-Diophantine tuples

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers. A finite set $s$ of natural numbers is an $S$-Diophantine tuple if all its elements are positive and, for all distinct $a, b \in s$, every prime factor of $ab + 1$ lies in $S$. A tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_m)$ of distinct positive integers is encoded by the set of its entries, which has $m$ elements.

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with an addition and a multiplication, and let $(a_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(b_j)_{j \in J}$ be families in $\alpha$ indexed by arbitrary types $I$ and $J$. They have all pairwise sums square when, for every $i \in I$ and $j \in J$, the sum $a_i + b_j$ is a square in $\alpha$, that is, $a_i + b_j = c \cdot c$ for some $c \in \alpha$.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $k \ge 1$, let $X_1 = \sum_{i=0}^{(p-1)/2} (-1)^i x^{p-1-2i}$ and $Y_1 = \sum_{i=0}^{(p-3)/2} (-1)^i x^{p-2-2i}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, and let $\Phi_{4p^k}$ be the $4p^k$-th cyclotomic polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$. Then $\Phi_{4p^k}(x) = X_1\bigl(x^{p^{k-1}}\bigr)^2 + Y_1\bigl(x^{p^{k-1}}\bigr)^2$.

reading_title.source: Geometric sums for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and odd $n$ are sums of two squares

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, let $n$ be a positive odd integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{p-1} p^{nj} = 1 + p^n + p^{2n} + \cdots + p^{(p-1)n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.

reading_title.source: An alternating sum in coprime integers $x, y$ is a sum of two coprime squares

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be coprime integers, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{2n} (-1)^j x^{4n-2j} y^{2j}$, that is, $S = x^{4n} - x^{4n-2} y^2 + \cdots - x^2 y^{4n-2} + y^{4n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are coprime natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.

Representation numbers of sums of squares

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the solution set is the set of all integer vectors $x = (x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$.
nodes.title: Integer solutions of a sum of squares

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the representation number $r_k(n)$ is the number of elements of the solution set, that is, the number of integer vectors $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$. Representations that differ in the order or the signs of the entries are counted separately.
nodes.title: Representation numbers of sums of squares

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, there are only finitely many integer vectors $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$.
nodes.title: Finitely many representations as a sum of squares

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the representation number $r_k(n)$ equals the number of elements of the finite solution set of integer vectors $(x_1, \dots, x_k) \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = n$.
nodes.title: The representation number counts a finite set

nodes.summary: For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the zero vector of $\mathbb{Z}^k$ has squared norm $0$, that is, it lies in the set of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^k$ with $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_k^2 = 0$.
nodes.title: The zero vector represents zero as a sum of squares

nodes.summary: The set of vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ whose sum of squares (an empty sum) equals $0$ is all of $\mathbb{Z}^0$.
nodes.title: Solution set of the empty sum at zero

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, no vector $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ has sum of squares equal to $n$; that is, the solution set is empty.
nodes.title: Zero squares never sum to a positive integer

nodes.summary: The set of vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^1$ with $x_1^2 = 0$ consists of the zero vector alone.
nodes.title: Solution set of one square equal to zero

nodes.summary: The representation number $r_0(0)$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ whose sum of squares (an empty sum) equals $0$, is $1$.
nodes.title: Zero as a sum of zero squares

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the representation number $r_0(n)$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^0$ whose sum of squares (an empty sum) equals $n$, is $0$.
nodes.title: Positive integers have no representation as a sum of zero squares

nodes.summary: The representation number $r_1(0)$, the number of integer vectors $x \in \mathbb{Z}^1$ with $x_1^2 = 0$, equals $1$.

Representations by squares and triangular numbers

nodes.summary: The square theta series is the formal power series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$: for each $n \ge 0$, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of integers $m$ with $m^2 = n$.
nodes.title: The square theta series

nodes.summary: The triangular theta series is the formal power series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$ with integer coefficients: for each natural number $n$, its coefficient of $q^n$ is the number of natural numbers $m$ with $m(m+1)/2 = n$.
nodes.title: Triangular theta series

nodes.summary: In the square theta series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$, the coefficients of $q^0$, $q^1$, $q^2$ and $q^4$ are $1$, $2$, $0$ and $2$ respectively.
nodes.title: First coefficients of the square theta series

nodes.summary: In the triangular theta series $\psi(q) = \sum_{m \ge 0} q^{m(m+1)/2}$, the coefficients of $q^0$, $q^1$, $q^2$ and $q^3$ are $1$, $1$, $0$ and $1$ respectively.
nodes.title: First coefficients of the triangular theta series

nodes.summary: The square theta series $\theta(q) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} q^{m^2}$ is a unit of the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$ of formal power series with integer coefficients, since its constant coefficient is $1$.
nodes.title: The square theta series is a unit

Since $\theta$ has constant coefficient $1$, it is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, so $\theta^k$ is a power series for negative $k$ as well.

nodes.summary: For a complex number $z$, let $[z] = m + n i$, where $m = \lfloor \operatorname{Re} z + 1/2 \rfloor$ and $n = \lfloor \operatorname{Im} z + 1/2 \rfloor$; that is, the real and imaginary parts of $z$ are rounded to the nearest integer, with halves rounded up. Then $[z]$ is a Gaussian integer nearest to $z$.
nodes.title: Hurwitz rounding to the nearest Gaussian integer

nodes.summary: For a complex number $z$, the Hurwitz iterates are $z_0 = z$ and $z_{n+1} = (z_n - [z_n])^{-1}$ for $n \ge 0$, where $[u]$ is the Gaussian integer nearest to $u$, obtained by rounding the real and imaginary parts of $u$ to the nearest integer with halves rounded up, and where the inverse of $0$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Iterates of the Hurwitz algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz iterates $z_0 = z, z_1, z_2, \dots$. For $n \ge 0$, the $n$-th partial quotient is $a_n = [z_n]$, the Gaussian integer nearest to $z_n$, obtained by rounding the real and imaginary parts of $z_n$ to the nearest integer with halves rounded up.
nodes.title: Partial quotients of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$. This is the sequence whose term for $n \ge 0$ is the pair of pairs of complex numbers $((P_{n-1}, Q_{n-1}), (P_n, Q_n))$, where $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = a_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, and $P_{n+1} = a_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and $Q_{n+1} = a_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Consecutive pairs of Hurwitz convergents

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$. Its convergent numerators $P_n$, $n \ge 0$, are given by $P_{-1} = 1$, $P_0 = a_0$ and $P_{n+1} = a_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Convergent numerators of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz partial quotients $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$. Its convergent denominators $Q_n$, $n \ge 0$, are given by $Q_{-1} = 0$, $Q_0 = 1$ and $Q_{n+1} = a_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Convergent denominators of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: Let $z$ be a complex number with Hurwitz iterates $z_j$ and partial quotients $a_j$. A natural number $n$ is a legal index for $z$ when $z_j \ne a_j$ for every $j < n$, that is, when the Hurwitz expansion of $z$ has not terminated before step $n$.
nodes.title: Legal indices of the Hurwitz expansion

nodes.summary: For every complex number $z$, let $[z]$ be the Gaussian integer nearest to $z$, obtained by rounding the real and imaginary parts to the nearest integer with halves rounded up. Then $|\operatorname{Re}(z - [z])| \le 1/2$ and $|\operatorname{Im}(z - [z])| \le 1/2$.

nodes.title: Quadratic form of an integer matrix

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries represents an integer $m$ if $Q(x) = m$ for some $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, where $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$.
nodes.title: Integers represented by an integer-matrix quadratic form

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ matrix $Q$ with integer entries is universal if its quadratic form $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$ represents every positive integer, that is, for every positive integer $m$ there is $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $Q(x) = m$.
nodes.title: Universal integer-matrix quadratic forms

nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be a positive definite symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with integer entries, with quadratic form $Q(x) = \sum_{i,j} Q_{ij} x_i x_j$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$. Then $Q$ is universal, that is, it represents every positive integer, if and only if it represents every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le 15$.

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ represents a natural number $m$ if there is an integer vector $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j = m$, where the entries of $x$ and the number $m$ are viewed as elements of $R$.

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ is universal if it represents every positive integer: for every positive integer $m$ there is $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ with $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j = m$ in $R$.
nodes.title: Universal quadratic forms over a ring

nodes.summary: For a ring $R$, an $n \times n$ matrix $M$ with entries in $R$ is integral if its quadratic form takes integer values at integer vectors: for every $x \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the value $\sum_{i,j} x_i M_{ij} x_j$ computed in $R$ lies in the image of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $R$.

nodes.summary: For an integer $d$, $R(d)$ is the finite set of integer triples $(a, b, c)$ such that the binary quadratic form $a x^2 + b x y + c y^2$ is Gauss reduced (that is, $a > 0$, $b^2 - 4ac < 0$, $|b| \le a \le c$, and $b \ge 0$ whenever $|b| = a$ or $a = c$) and has discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = d$. In particular $R(d)$ is empty when $d \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Reduced forms of a given discriminant

nodes.summary: For an integer $d$, the Gauss class number $h(d)$ is the number of integer triples $(a, b, c)$ with $b^2 - 4ac = d$ for which the binary quadratic form $ax^2 + bxy + cy^2$ is positive definite ($a > 0$ and $d < 0$), reduced ($|b| \le a \le c$, with $b \ge 0$ whenever $|b| = a$ or $a = c$) and primitive ($\gcd(a, b, c) = 1$).
nodes.title: Gauss class number of a discriminant

nodes.summary: For an integer $d$, the unweighted Hurwitz class number $H(d)$ is the number of elements of the set $R(d)$ of reduced forms of discriminant $d$, that is, the number of integer triples $(a, b, c)$, primitive or not, for which $a x^2 + b x y + c y^2$ is a Gauss-reduced binary quadratic form of discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = d$. nodes.summary: For every natural number $s \ge 3$, every natural number $n$ is a sum of at most $s$ $s$-gonal numbers: there are a finite set $T$ with at most $s$ elements and natural numbers $k_i$ for $i \in T$ such that $n = \sum_{i \in T} P_s(k_i)$, where $P_s(m) = (s - 2)\binom{m}{2} + m$ is the $m$-th $s$-gonal number. The $k_i$ may repeat, and since $P_s(0) = 0$ the case $n = 0$ is the empty sum.

reading_title.source: The convergence exponent $s(\psi)$

nodes.summary: For a function $\psi$ from the positive integers to the nonnegative reals, $s(\psi)$ is the infimum, taken in the nonnegative reals, of the set of real numbers $\beta \ge 0$ for which the series $\sum_{q \ge 1} \varphi(q) (\psi(q)/q)^{\beta}$ converges, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. If there is no such $\beta$, then $s(\psi) = 0$.

reading_title.source: Base-$b$ digits of a real number

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $n$ and a real number $x$, the $n$-th digit of $x$ in base $b$, counting from $n = 0$ just after the radix point, is $\lfloor b^{n+1} \{x\} \rfloor \bmod b$, where $\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$ is the fractional part of $x$.
nodes.title: Base-$b$ digits of a real number

nodes.summary: For a natural number $b$ and a real number $x$, write $a_k$ for the $k$-th base-$b$ digit of $x$ after the radix point, counting from $k = 0$. Then $x$ is simply normal in base $b$ if for every natural number $d < b$ the proportion $\#\{k < n : a_k = d\} / n$ tends to $1/b$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Simply normal numbers

nodes.summary: For a natural number $b$ and a real number $x$, write $a_i$ for the $i$-th base-$b$ digit of $x$ after the radix point, counting from $i = 0$. Then $x$ is normal in base $b$ if for every natural number $k$ and all natural numbers $w_0, \dots, w_{k-1} < b$ the proportion $\#\{i < n : a_{i+j} = w_j \text{ for all } j < k\} / n$ tends to $1/b^k$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Normal numbers

nodes.summary: If a real number $x$ is normal in base $b$, then $x$ is simply normal in base $b$.

Continued fractions of Laurent series

reading_title.source: The variable $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. Formal Laurent series in $x^{-1}$ over $K$ are realized as Laurent series $\sum_n c_n X^n$ in $X = x^{-1}$, and the variable $x$ is the series $X^{-1}$, with coefficient $1$ at $X^{-1}$ and $0$ elsewhere.
nodes.title: The variable $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$

reading_title.source: The variable $x$ times $x^{-1}$ is one

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. In $K((x^{-1}))$, the product of the variable $x$ and the series $x^{-1}$ (coefficient $1$ at $x^{-1}$ and $0$ elsewhere) is $1$.
nodes.title: The variable $x$ times $x^{-1}$ is one

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. The embedding $K[x] \to K((x^{-1}))$ is the $K$-algebra homomorphism that sends $x$ to the element $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$, that is, it evaluates a polynomial at $x$.
nodes.title: Polynomials as Laurent series in the inverse variable

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. The embedding $K[x] \to K((x^{-1}))$ sends the polynomial $x$ to the element $x$ of $K((x^{-1}))$.
nodes.title: The polynomial variable embeds as the Laurent variable

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and write a Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ as $\alpha = \sum_n c_n x^{-n}$. Its polynomial part is $[\alpha] = \sum_{n \le 0} c_n x^{-n}$, the sum of the terms in nonnegative powers of $x$.
nodes.title: Polynomial part of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and write $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ as $\alpha = \sum_n c_n x^{-n}$. For every integer $n$, the coefficient of $x^{-n}$ in the polynomial part $[\alpha]$ is $c_n$ if $n \le 0$ and $0$ if $n > 0$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of the polynomial part of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. In $K((x^{-1}))$ the polynomial part of $x$ is $x$, and the polynomial part of $x^{-1}$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Polynomial parts of the variable and its inverse

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$. The complete quotients of the continued fraction expansion of $\alpha$ are $\alpha_0 = \alpha$ and $\alpha_{n+1} = (\alpha_n - [\alpha_n])^{-1}$ for $n \ge 0$, where $[\beta]$ is the polynomial part of $\beta$ and $0^{-1} = 0$. So the complete quotients become $0$ after a finite expansion ends.
nodes.title: Complete quotients of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ and $n \ge 0$. The $n$-th partial quotient of $\alpha$ is $b_n = [\alpha_n]$, the polynomial part of the $n$-th complete quotient $\alpha_n$ of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Partial quotients of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$. The partial quotient $b_0$ of $\alpha$ is its polynomial part $[\alpha]$, and the complete quotient $\alpha_1$ is $(\alpha - [\alpha])^{-1}$, where $0^{-1} = 0$.
nodes.title: First step of the continued fraction of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. A Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ with partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$ has bounded partial quotients if there is an integer $B$ such that for every $n \ge 0$ and every integer $k > B$ the coefficient of $x^k$ in $b_n$ is zero, that is, every nonzero $b_n$ is a polynomial in $x$ of degree at most $B$.
nodes.title: Laurent series with bounded partial quotients

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ have partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$. The numerators of the convergents of $\alpha$ are $P_{-1} = 1$, $P_0 = b_0$ and $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$. The sequence is indexed with a shift of one: its term at $n \ge 0$ is $P_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Numerators of the convergents of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ and let $b_0, b_1, \dots$ be its partial quotients. The denominators of the convergents of $\alpha$ are given by $Q_{-1} = 0$, $Q_0 = 1$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 0$. They are indexed from $0$ here: the $k$-th term of the sequence is $Q_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Denominators of the convergents

reading_title.source: The convergent $P_1 / Q_1$ of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ have partial quotients $b_0, b_1, \dots$. Let $P_n$ and $Q_n$ be the numerators and denominators of its convergents, given by $P_{-1} = 1$, $Q_{-1} = 0$, $P_0 = b_0$, $Q_0 = 1$, $P_{n+1} = b_{n+1} P_n + P_{n-1}$ and $Q_{n+1} = b_{n+1} Q_n + Q_{n-1}$. Then $P_1 = b_1 b_0 + 1$ and $Q_1 = b_1$.
nodes.title: The convergent $P_1 / Q_1$ of a Laurent series

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. A Laurent series $\alpha \in K((x^{-1}))$ is irrational if $Q \alpha \ne P$ for all polynomials $P, Q \in K[x]$ with $Q \ne 0$, where polynomials are embedded in $K((x^{-1}))$ by sending $x$ to the variable $x$.
nodes.title: Irrational Laurent series

Engel expansions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $k \ge 1$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $k$ is the unique $u$ with $0 \le u < k$ and $u \equiv -n \pmod{k}$: it equals $0$ when $k$ divides $n$ and $k - (n \bmod k)$ otherwise. For $k = 0$ it is defined to be $0$.
nodes.title: Negated remainder

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $u$ with $k \ne 0$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $k$ equals $u$ if and only if $u < k$ and $k$ divides $n + u$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the negated remainder

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is the sequence $t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ of natural numbers with $t_0 = a$ and, for every $j \ge 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$, while if $t_j \ne 0$ then $t_{j+1}$ is the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$: the unique natural number $u < t_j$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t_j}$. Once the trajectory reaches $0$ it stays there.
nodes.title: Engel remainder trajectory

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ has value $a$ at step $0$.
nodes.title: Initial term of the Engel trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then $t_{j+1} = 0$.
nodes.title: Zero is absorbing for the Engel trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j \ne 0$, then $t_{j+1}$ is the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$: the unique natural number $u < t_j$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t_j}$.
nodes.title: Step of the Engel trajectory at a nonzero term

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t \ne 0$. Then the Engel remainder trajectory of $t$ with respect to $n$ is, at step $1$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t$: the unique natural number $u < t$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t}$.
nodes.title: First step of the Engel trajectory

nodes.title: Engel trajectories vanish at a positive step

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. The Engel length $L(n, a)$ is the least $j \ge 1$ with $t_j = 0$.
nodes.title: Engel length

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ satisfies $L(n, a) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Engel length is positive

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $L$ be the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is $0$ at step $L$.
nodes.title: Engel trajectory vanishes at the Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$, and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then the Engel length $L(n, a)$ satisfies $L(n, a) \le j$.
nodes.title: The Engel length is at most any positive vanishing step

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $L$ be the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $1 \le j < L$, then the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is nonzero at step $j$.
nodes.title: Engel trajectory is nonzero at positive steps before the Engel length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the maximal Engel length is $M(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} L(n, a)$, where $L(n, a)$ is the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$; for $n = 0$ the maximum is over the empty set and $M(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Maximal Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a \le n$. Then the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ is at most the maximal Engel length $M(n) = \max_{1 \le b \le n} L(n, b)$.
nodes.title: Each Engel length is at most the maximal Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $B$ be natural numbers. If the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ satisfies $L(n, a) \le B$ for every $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, then the maximal Engel length $M(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} L(n, a)$ (with $M(0) = 0$) satisfies $M(n) \le B$.
nodes.title: A uniform bound on Engel lengths bounds the maximal Engel length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $x$, the Farey staircase of order $n$ is $A_n(x) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \lfloor kx \rfloor / k$, the average of the first $n$ lower rational approximations $\lfloor kx \rfloor / k$ of $x$. For $n = 0$ the sum is empty and $A_0(x) = 0$.

Periodic continued fractions

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a real number with regular continued fraction $[a_0; a_1, a_2, \dots]$. The continued fraction of $x$ is eventually periodic if it does not terminate and its sequence of partial denominators $(a_n)_{n \ge 1}$, which omits the head coefficient $a_0$, is eventually periodic: there are natural numbers $p > 0$ and $n_0 \ge 1$ such that $a_{n+p} = a_n$ for every $n \ge n_0$.

Pierce expansions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is the sequence $t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ of natural numbers with $t_0 = a$ and, for every $j \ge 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$, while if $t_j \ne 0$ then $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ is the remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$. Once the trajectory reaches $0$ it stays there.
nodes.title: Pierce remainder trajectory

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ has value $a$ at step $0$.
nodes.title: Initial term of the Pierce trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then $t_{j+1} = 0$.
nodes.title: Step of the Pierce trajectory at a zero term

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j \ne 0$, then $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$, the remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$.
nodes.title: Step of the Pierce trajectory at a nonzero term

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t \ne 0$. Then the Pierce remainder trajectory of $t$ with respect to $n$ is, at step $1$, equal to $n \bmod t$, the remainder of $n$ modulo $t$.
nodes.title: First step of the Pierce trajectory

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory: $t_0 = a$, and $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ if $t_j \ne 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$. Then $t_i = 0$ for some $i \le a + 1$.
nodes.title: A bound on when a Pierce trajectory vanishes

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ (with $t_0 = a$) satisfies $t_j = 0$ for some $j \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Pierce trajectories vanish at a positive step

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be the Pierce remainder trajectory, with $t_0 = a$, $t_{j+1} = n \bmod t_j$ if $t_j \ne 0$ and $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$. The Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ is the least $j \ge 1$ with $t_j = 0$; such a $j$ always exists.
nodes.title: Pierce length

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Pierce length is positive

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_j)_{j \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_{\ell(n, a)} = 0$, where $\ell(n, a)$ is the Pierce length.
nodes.title: The Pierce trajectory vanishes at the Pierce length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $a$ and $j$ with $j \ge 1$, if the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_j = 0$, then the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le j$.
nodes.title: The Pierce length is at most any positive vanishing step

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $a$ and $j$ with $1 \le j < \ell(n, a)$, where $\ell(n, a)$ is the Pierce length, the Pierce remainder trajectory $(t_i)_{i \ge 0}$ of $n$ and $a$ satisfies $t_j \ne 0$.
nodes.title: The Pierce trajectory is nonzero before the Pierce length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the maximal Pierce length $P(n)$ is the maximum of the Pierce lengths $\ell(n, a)$ over $1 \le a \le n$, with $P(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Maximal Pierce length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le P(n)$, where $P(n) = \max_{1 \le b \le n} \ell(n, b)$ is the maximal Pierce length.
nodes.title: Each Pierce length is at most the maximal Pierce length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $L$ be natural numbers. If the Pierce length $\ell(n, a)$ satisfies $\ell(n, a) \le L$ for every $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, then the maximal Pierce length $P(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} \ell(n, a)$ (which is $0$ when $n = 0$) satisfies $P(n) \le L$.
nodes.title: A uniform bound on Pierce lengths bounds the maximal Pierce length

nodes.summary: A TRIP-Stern tree with node values in a type $\alpha$ consists of a root seed in $\alpha$ together with two maps from $\alpha$ to $\alpha$, the left transition and the right transition. No condition is imposed on the seed or on the two transitions; in the source the seed is $(1,1,1)$ and the left and right transitions are induced by the maps $F_0$ and $F_1$ defined there.
nodes.title: TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with seed $s$, left transition $L$ and right transition $R$. A binary path is a finite sequence of steps, each left or right. The node of $T$ selected by a path $(b_1, \dots, b_k)$ is obtained by starting at $s$ and applying, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $L$ if $b_i$ is a left step and $R$ if $b_i$ is a right step.
nodes.title: Node selected by a binary path

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with left transition $L$. For every binary path $p$, the node of $T$ selected by $p$ followed by one left step equals $L$ applied to the node of $T$ selected by $p$.

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with right transition $R$. For every binary path $p$, the node of $T$ selected by $p$ followed by one right step equals $R$ applied to the node of $T$ selected by $p$.
nodes.title: Extending a path by a right step

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree and $n$ a natural number. The set of nodes of $T$ at depth $n$ is the set of all values $y$ such that some binary path of length $n$ selects $y$ in $T$.

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with seed $s$ and left transition $L$. The left-most node of $T$ at depth $n$ is $L^n(s)$, the result of applying $L$ $n$ times to $s$; that is, it is $s$ at depth $0$, and at depth $n + 1$ it is $L$ applied to the left-most node at depth $n$.
nodes.title: Left-most node of a TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: For a TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and a natural number $n$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n$ is obtained from the seed of $T$ by applying the right transition of $T$ exactly $n$ times: at depth $0$ it is the seed, and at depth $n + 1$ it is the image of the rightmost node at depth $n$ under the right transition.
nodes.title: Rightmost node of a TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the left-most node of $T$ at depth $0$ is the seed of $T$.
nodes.title: Left-most node at depth zero

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with left transition $L$. For every natural number $n$, the left-most node of $T$ at depth $n + 1$ equals $L$ applied to the left-most node of $T$ at depth $n$.

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $0$ is the seed of $T$.

Pisot numbers

nodes.summary: A Pisot number is a real algebraic integer greater than one whose other complex conjugates all have norm less than one.
nodes.title: Pisot number

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a polynomial with real coefficients and $r$ a real number. Then $r$ is the unique Pisot root of $P$ when $r$ is a Pisot number with $P(r) = 0$ and every Pisot number $s$ with $P(s) = 0$ equals $r$.
nodes.title: Unique Pisot root of a polynomial
Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem

nodes.summary: The conjugates of a complex number $\alpha$ are the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$ and it has no conjugates.
nodes.title: Conjugates

nodes.summary: The degree of a complex number $\alpha$ is the degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its minimal polynomial is taken to be $0$, so its degree is $0$.
nodes.title: Degree of a complex number

nodes.summary: For $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$, the trace of $\alpha$ is the sum of its conjugates, that is, of the roots in $\mathbb{C}$ of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, counted with multiplicity. For transcendental $\alpha$ there are no conjugates and the trace is $0$.
nodes.title: Trace as the sum of conjugates

nodes.summary: The absolute trace of a complex number $\alpha$ is the real number obtained by dividing the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ by the degree of $\alpha$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental, its trace and its degree are both $0$, and its absolute trace is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: Absolute trace

nodes.summary: A complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive algebraic integer when it is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ and every conjugate of $\alpha$ (every root in $\mathbb{C}$ of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$) is a strictly positive real number.
nodes.title: Totally positive algebraic integers

nodes.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the real part of the trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer has positive real part

nodes.summary: If $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the imaginary part of the trace of $\alpha$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The trace of a totally positive algebraic integer is real

nodes.summary: If a complex number $\alpha$ is a totally positive algebraic integer, then the absolute trace of $\alpha$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the absolute trace

nodes.summary: The minimal polynomial of $1 \in \mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $X - 1$.
nodes.title: Minimal polynomial of one

nodes.summary: The complex number $1$ is a totally positive algebraic integer.
nodes.title: One is a totally positive algebraic integer

nodes.summary: A real number $\rho$ is admissible when $\rho \ge 0$ and only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ have absolute trace less than $\rho$.
nodes.title: Admissible trace bounds

nodes.summary: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the admissible real bounds: the real numbers $\rho \ge 0$ such that only finitely many complex numbers that are totally positive algebraic integers have absolute trace less than $\rho$.
nodes.title: Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant

nodes.summary: Let $C_{86}$ be the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant, an extended real number. Every admissible real number $\rho$ satisfies $\rho \le C_{86}$ in the extended reals.
nodes.title: Admissible bounds lie below the Schur–Siegel–Smyth constant

nodes.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant is at most $b$ if and only if every admissible real number $c$ satisfies $c \le b$.

Modular functions

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper half-plane is meromorphic at infinity when there are a positive integer $N$ and a function $g \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ meromorphic at $0$ such that $f(\tau) = g(e^{2 \pi i \tau / N})$ for every $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$ with sufficiently large imaginary part.
nodes.title: Meromorphy at infinity

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper half-plane is meromorphic at the cusps when, for every $\gamma \in \mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$, the function $\tau \mapsto f(\gamma \cdot \tau)$ is meromorphic at infinity, where $\gamma$ acts on $\mathbb{H}$ by Möbius transformations.
nodes.title: Meromorphy at the cusps

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper half-plane is meromorphic when there is a function $g \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is meromorphic on the open set $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$ and satisfies $g(\tau) = f(\tau)$ for every $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$.
nodes.title: Meromorphy on the upper half-plane

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper half-plane is invariant under $\Gamma$ when $f(\gamma \cdot \tau) = f(\tau)$ for every $\gamma \in \Gamma$ and every $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$, where $\gamma$ acts on $\mathbb{H}$ by Möbius transformations.
nodes.title: Invariance under a subgroup of the modular group

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}(2, \mathbb{Z})$. A function $f \colon \mathbb{H} \to \mathbb{C}$ on the upper half-plane is a modular function for $\Gamma$ when it is meromorphic on $\mathbb{H}$, invariant under $\Gamma$, and meromorphic at the cusps.

nodes.summary: The Ramanujan exponent of a local-exponent family $F$ with local exponents $m(i)$, $i \in \iota$, is the supremum of the set $\{0\} \cup \{m(i) : i \in \iota\}$. It is the supremum of the local exponents when $\iota$ is nonempty, and $0$ when $\iota$ is empty.

q-Pochhammer symbol

nodes.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $q$, the raw infinite q-Pochhammer product is the unconditional infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, defined for every $q$: when this product does not converge unconditionally (in particular for most $q$ with $|q| \ge 1$), its value is $1$ by convention.
nodes.title: Raw infinite q-Pochhammer product

nodes.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol is $(a;q)_\infty = \prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$, the unconditional infinite product of the factors $1 - a q^n$.
nodes.title: Infinite q-Pochhammer symbol

nodes.summary: For every complex number $q$ with $|q| < 1$, $(0;q)_\infty = 1$, since every factor $1 - 0 \cdot q^n$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol with a = 0

nodes.summary: For all complex numbers $a$ and $q$ with $|q| < 1$, the infinite product $\prod_{n=0}^{\infty} (1 - a q^n)$ converges unconditionally to the infinite q-Pochhammer symbol $(a;q)_\infty$: the products of the factors $1 - a q^n$ over finite sets of indices $n$ tend to $(a;q)_\infty$.
nodes.title: Convergence of the infinite q-Pochhammer product

nodes.summary: The infinite q-Pochhammer symbol satisfies $(1;0)_\infty = 0$, because its factor for $n = 0$ is $1 - 1 \cdot 0^0 = 0$ (with the convention $0^0 = 1$).
nodes.title: The q-Pochhammer symbol vanishes at a = 1 and q = 0

nodes.summary: The raw infinite q-Pochhammer product at $a = 2$ and $q = 1$ equals $1$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the Euler product $f_k = (q^k; q^k)_\infty = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is this infinite product in the ring of integer power series in $q$, taken in the coefficientwise topology. It is used for $k \ge 1$.

reading_title.source: Parity of $(4, p)$-regular partitions in nonresidue progressions

nodes.summary: Let $p \ge 5$ be a prime and let $r$ be a natural number such that $8r + 1$ is not a square modulo $p$ (a quadratic nonresidue). Write $b_{4,p}(m)$ for the number of $(4, p)$-regular partitions of $m$, that is, partitions of $m$ none of whose parts is divisible by $4$ or by $p$. Then $b_{4,p}(pn + r) \equiv 0 \pmod 2$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Parity of $(4, p)$-regular partitions in nonresidue progressions

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 1$ let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ be the Euler product. This is the integer power series $f_4 f_6^2 / (f_1 f_3 f_{12})$ in $q$, where the denominator $f_1 f_3 f_{12}$ is invertible because its constant coefficient is $1$. It is the generating function $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{PD}_2(n) q^n$ of the numbers $\mathrm{PD}_2(n)$ of partitions of $n$ with designated summands into odd parts.
nodes.title: Generating function of odd designated-summand partitions

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the integer $\mathrm{PD}_2(n)$ is defined as the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series $f_4 f_6^2 / (f_1 f_3 f_{12})$, where $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ is the Euler product (the denominator has constant coefficient $1$, so it is invertible). It counts the partitions of $n$ with designated summands in which all parts are odd.

nodes.summary: For an integer $n \ge 0$, $c_2(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ for which there is an integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ such that $j$ appears exactly $j$ times, every part other than $j$ is at least $2j + 1$, and every even part that is at least $2j + 2$ appears only once.

reading_title.source: The initial-repetitions partition function $c_3$

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $c_3(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ for which there is an integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ such that the part $1$ appears exactly $j^2$ or $j^2 + 1$ times, every odd part larger than $1$ appears exactly once, every even part appears exactly once, and every even part greater than $2j$ is at least $4j + 4$ and divisible by $4$.

reading_title.source: The partition function $c_8$

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $c_8(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ such that either (a) all parts are even and distinct, or (b) for some positive integer $j$, the largest odd part is $2j - 1$, every positive odd integer $i \le j$ appears once or twice, every odd integer $i$ with $j < i \le 2j - 1$ appears exactly once, all even parts are distinct, and every even part greater than $j$ is at least $2j + 2$.
nodes.title: The partition function $c_8$

reading_title.source: The initial-repetitions partition function $c_8'$

POND and PEND partitions

nodes.summary: A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition) satisfies the POND condition when no odd number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently, every odd part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the odd parts are not distinct.
nodes.title: The POND condition

nodes.summary: A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition) satisfies the PEND condition when no even number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently, every even part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the even parts are not distinct.
nodes.title: The PEND condition

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ that are POND, that is, in which every odd part that occurs has multiplicity at least $2$ (OEIS A265256).
nodes.title: Number of POND partitions

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ is the number of PEND partitions of $n$: partitions of $n$ in which every even part that occurs appears at least twice (OEIS A265254).
nodes.title: The PEND partition function

nodes.summary: The number $\mathrm{pond}(0)$ of POND partitions of $0$ equals $1$: the only partition of $0$ is the empty partition, and it is POND.
nodes.title: The number of POND partitions of zero

nodes.summary: The number of PEND partitions of $0$ is $1$, that is, $\mathrm{pend}(0) = 1$.

nodes.summary: The Genocchi power series is the formal power series $\frac{2x}{e^x + 1} = 2x \cdot (e^x + 1)^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[x]]$, where $e^x = \sum_{n \ge 0} x^n / n!$ is the exponential power series and $(e^x + 1)^{-1}$ is the inverse of $e^x + 1$ among formal power series. nodes.summary: Given a list $b_1, \dots, b_k$ of natural numbers (binary digits) and a natural number $c$, this is the list, in order of occurrence, of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the sequence consisting of $c$ ones followed by $b_1, \dots, b_k$, where every digit other than $1$ ends a run.
nodes.title: Run lengths of a digit list

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the binary run lengths of $n$ form the list of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$, in the order in which the runs occur when the digits are read from the least significant one. This is the paper's list $\mathcal{L}(n)$, whose order does not matter there; for $n = 0$ the list is empty.
nodes.title: Binary run lengths

nodes.summary: For a sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform of $S$ is the sequence $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ given by $T(n) = \prod_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}(n)} S(\ell)$, where $\mathcal{L}(n)$ is the list of the lengths of the maximal runs of $1$s in the binary expansion of $n$, so that each run contributes one factor.
nodes.title: Run length transform

nodes.summary: For every sequence $S : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, the run length transform of $S$ takes the value $1$ at $0$, since $0$ has no runs of $1$s in binary.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, the extended Cunningham chain generated by $p$ is the sequence $e_0, e_1, e_2, \ldots$ of natural numbers given by $e_0 = p$ and $e_k = 2 e_{k-1} + 1$ for $k \ge 1$; in binary, $e_k$ is obtained from $p$ by appending $k$ digits $1$ on the right.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, $b(N)$ is the smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which $N$ is a palindrome, that is, in which the base-$b$ digits of $N$ read the same forwards and backwards. Such a base exists: $0$ has no digits and is a palindrome in every base, and for $N \ge 1$ the number $N$ is written with the single digit $N$ in base $N + 1$.
nodes.title: Minimum palindromic base

nodes.summary: A natural number $N$ has a base-$b$ representation in binomial form if there are natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ such that the base-$b$ digits of $N$, from the most significant to the least significant, are $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$.

nodes.summary: The smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which the number $2$ is a palindrome is $b(2) = 3$: in base $2$ the number $2$ is written $(1, 0)_2$, which is not a palindrome, while in base $3$ it is the one-digit palindrome $(2)_3$.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $b \ge 2$ be a base, and let $c = 2^n \bmod b$. The base-$b$ representation of $2^n$ is a palindrome with exactly three digits if and only if $b^2 + 1 \le 2^n \le b^3 - 1$, $c \ne 0$, and $\frac{1}{b} \lfloor 2^n / b \rfloor - \frac{b - 1}{b} \le c \le \frac{1}{b} \lfloor 2^n / b \rfloor$.

nodes.summary: Let $g$ and $k$ be integers with $2 \le k < g$, and let $N = (a_n a_{n-1} \cdots a_0)_g$ have base-$g$ digits $a_0, \dots, a_n \in \{0, \dots, g - 1\}$, with units digit $a_0$ and leading digit $a_n \ne 0$. Suppose $N$ is a $(g, k)$ reverse multiple, that is, $k N = (a_0 a_1 \cdots a_n)_g$, and that $a_0 + a_n = g$. Then $(k + 1) a_n = g$; in particular $k + 1$ divides $g$ and $a_n = g / (k + 1)$.

Then $a + b < g$, so $a + b$ is a base-$g$ digit, and $(a\,(a + b)\,b)_g$ is again a $(g, k)$ reverse multiple, that is, $k (a g^2 + (a + b) g + b) = b g^2 + (a + b) g + a$.

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S$ of integers, the base phi value of $S$ is the real number $\sum_{i \in S} \varphi^i$, where $\varphi = (1 + \sqrt 5)/2$ is the golden ratio. It is the number represented by the base phi expansion with digit $1$ at each position in $S$ and digit $0$ at every other position.

nodes.summary: The Zeckendorf-adic integers $\mathbb{X}$ are the digit sequences $x = (x_k)_{k \ge 0}$ with $x_k \in \{0, 1\}$ such that $x_0 = x_1 = 0$ and no two consecutive digits are both $1$, that is, $x_k x_{k+1} = 0$ for every $k$.
nodes.title: The Zeckendorf-adic integers

nodes.summary: Let $F_k$ be the Fibonacci numbers ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = F_2 = 1$). Every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ has a unique Zeckendorf representation $n = F_{k_1} + \dots + F_{k_m}$ with $k_1 > \dots > k_m \ge 2$ and no two consecutive indices. The Zeckendorf digit sequence of $n$ is the binary sequence $(x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $x_k = 1$ if $k$ is one of the indices $k_1, \dots, k_m$ and $x_k = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Zeckendorf digit sequence of a natural number

nodes.summary: The odometer is the map $T$ on digit sequences $x = (x_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $x_k \in \{0, 1\}$ defined as follows. If $x_k = x_{k+1} = 0$ for some $k \ge 2$, let $k$ be the least such index; then $T(x)_j = 0$ for $j < k$, $T(x)_k = 1$ and $T(x)_j = x_j$ for $j > k$. If there is no such $k$, then $T(x)$ is the zero sequence.

Let $p$ be a prime, let $k \ge 0$ and $n_1 \ge 2$ be integers, and let $n = p^k n_1$. Then for every integer $c \ge 1$ and every integer $b$ with $0 \le b < n_1$, $a^{(n)}_{c p^k,\, b p^k + 1} \equiv a^{(n_1)}_{c,\, b + 1} \pmod{p}$.

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 0$ be an integer, let $n \ge 2$ be even, and write $\mathbb{Z}_m = \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ (so $\mathbb{Z}_0 = \mathbb{Z}$). A tuple $x = (x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{Z}_m^n$ has a Ducci predecessor, that is, a tuple $y \in \mathbb{Z}_m^n$ with $y_i + y_{i+1} = x_i$ for all $i$ (indices taken cyclically, so $y_{n+1} = y_1$), if and only if $x_1 - x_2 + x_3 - \cdots + x_{n-1} - x_n = 0$ in $\mathbb{Z}_m$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $p$ and $n$, the value $A_k(p, n)$ is defined by recursion on the fuel $p$, which bounds the recursion depth: $A_k(0, n) = 0$ and $A_k(p + 1, n) = n - g^k(n - 1)$, where $g^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of the function $g(m) = A_k(p, m)$ and both subtractions are truncated at $0$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the function $F_k : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is given by $F_k(0) = 0$ and $F_k(n) = n - F_k^k(n - 1)$ for $n \ge 1$, where $F_k^k$ is the $k$-fold iterate of $F_k$ (the identity when $k = 0$).

If $J_k(2k - 2) \le k - 1$, then $2k - 3$ is high extremal and $2k - 2$ is low extremal. If $J_k(2k - 2) > k - 1$, then $2k - 2$ is high extremal and $2k - 1$ is low extremal. Locally nilpotent polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $u \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. Write $u^{(m)}$ for the $m$-fold iterate of $u$ as a map $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$. Then $u$ is weakly locally nilpotent at $r$ outside $A$ if for every prime $p \notin A$ there is $m \ge 1$ such that $p$ divides $u^{(m)}(r)$. Complementary sequences

nodes.summary: Two sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, indexed from $0$, form a complementary pair when all their terms are positive, both are strictly increasing, no term of $a$ equals a term of $b$, and every positive integer is a term of $a$ or a term of $b$. In particular, the ranges of $a$ and $b$ partition the positive integers.

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $T(k, j) = (k - 2) j (j - 1)/2 + j$ be the $k$-gonal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt{2n/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $T(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s + 1$ if $(k - 2) s (s + 1) < 2n$, and $n + s$ otherwise.

nodes.title: Binomial-power sequences

nodes.summary: An integer sequence $(a(n))_{n \ge 0}$ is Dold realizable when, for every integer $n \ge 1$, the Möbius transform $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, a(n/d)$ is divisible by $n$ and non-negative, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Dold realizable sequences

nodes.summary: If an integer sequence $(a(n))_{n \ge 0}$ is Dold realizable, then for every integer $n \ge 1$, $n$ divides $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, a(n/d)$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Dold realizable sequences satisfy the Dold congruences

nodes.summary: If an integer sequence $(a(n))_{n \ge 0}$ is Dold realizable, then for every integer $n \ge 1$, $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, a(n/d) \ge 0$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: The Möbius transform of a Dold realizable sequence is non-negative

nodes.summary: Let $(a(n))_{n \ge 0}$ be an integer sequence and let $\mu$ be the Möbius function. If for every integer $n \ge 1$ the sum $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, a(n/d)$ over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$ is divisible by $n$, and for every integer $n \ge 1$ this sum is non-negative, then $a$ is Dold realizable.
nodes.title: Criterion for Dold realizability

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $s \ge 0$ be integers and let $A_{r,s}(n) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}^r \binom{n+k}{k}^s$. Then the integer sequence $(A_{r,s}(n))_{n \ge 0}$ is Dold realizable: for every integer $n \ge 1$, the sum $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, A_{r,s}(n/d)$ over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function, is non-negative and divisible by $n$.
nodes.title: Binomial-power sequences are Dold realizable

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $s \ge 0$ be integers and let $A_{r,s}(m) = \sum_{k=0}^{m} \binom{m}{k}^r \binom{m+k}{k}^s$. Then for every integer $n \ge 1$, $n$ divides $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, A_{r,s}(n/d)$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Dold congruences for binomial-power sequences

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$ and $s \ge 0$ be integers and let $A_{r,s}(m) = \sum_{k=0}^{m} \binom{m}{k}^r \binom{m+k}{k}^s$. Then for every integer $n \ge 1$, $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, A_{r,s}(n/d) \ge 0$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function and $d$ runs over the positive divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Non-negativity of the Möbius transform of binomial-power sequences

nodes.summary: A sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ of integers is a Dold sequence when for every integer $m \ge 1$ there is an $m \times m$ matrix $A$ with integer entries such that $a_n = \operatorname{tr}(A^n)$ for every $n$ with $1 \le n \le m$. The term $a_0$ is not constrained.
nodes.title: Dold sequences

nodes.summary: Given a sequence $b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Fermat sequence generated by $b$ is the sequence $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $a_n = \sum_{m \mid n} m \, b_m$ for $n \ge 1$, the sum running over the positive divisors $m$ of $n$, and $a_0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Fermat sequence

nodes.summary: A sequence $a$ of natural numbers $a(0), a(1), \dots$ is almost realizable when there is an integer $m \ge 1$ such that the integer sequence $(m\, a(n))_{n \ge 0}$ is Dold realizable: for every $n \ge 1$, the sum $\sum_{d \mid n} \mu(d)\, m\, a(n/d)$ over the positive divisors $d$ of $n$, where $\mu$ is the Möbius function, is non-negative and divisible by $n$.
nodes.title: Almost realizable sequences

nodes.summary: The constant sequence $a(n) = 0$ is almost realizable.
nodes.title: The zero sequence is almost realizable

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 1$ and $s$, the binomial-power sequence $n \mapsto \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}^r \binom{n+k}{k}^s$ is almost realizable.
nodes.title: Binomial-power sequences are almost realizable

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 1$, $s$ and $t$, the integer sequence $(D(n, r, s, t))_{n \ge 0}$ of Domb-type sums $D(n, r, s, t) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}^r \binom{2k}{k}^s \binom{2(n-k)}{n-k}^t$ is Dold realizable.
nodes.title: Domb-type sums are Dold realizable

nodes.summary: Let $p \ge 13$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, let $l$ be an even natural number with $2 \le l \le p - 3$, and let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy the defining conditions of $a_{p,l}$. Then there is a positive integer $m$ with $2m \le p - 3$ such that $a(2m) \ne a(2)\,a(m)$.

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$, $p$, $r$, the residue sequence satisfies $g_{k,p,r}(1) = 2 \bmod p^r$, the residue class of $2$ modulo $p^r$ (represented by the remainder of $2$ on division by $p^r$).

nodes.summary: For $k = 2$, $p = 3$ and $r = 1$, the residue sequence satisfies $g_{2,3,1}(2) = 0 \bmod 3$; in particular it is not the failure value $F$. Indeed $g_{2,3,1}(1) = 2$ and $(1 \cdot 2 + 2^2) \cdot 2^{-1} = 6 \cdot 2^{-1} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$.

Integer complexity

nodes.summary: An expression is either the constant $1$, or a sum $e_1 + e_2$ of two expressions, or a product $e_1 \times e_2$ of two expressions. Expressions are formal syntax trees, so the tree structure plays the role of parentheses.
nodes.title: Expressions built from one, addition and multiplication

nodes.summary: The value of an expression is the natural number obtained by evaluating it: the constant $1$ has value $1$, the value of $e_1 + e_2$ is the sum of the values of $e_1$ and $e_2$, and the value of $e_1 \times e_2$ is the product of their values.
nodes.title: Value of an expression

nodes.summary: The number of ones of an expression is the number of occurrences of the constant $1$ in it: the constant $1$ has one, and both $e_1 + e_2$ and $e_1 \times e_2$ have as many as $e_1$ and $e_2$ together.
nodes.title: Number of ones in an expression

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n > 0$ there is an expression whose value is $n$.
nodes.title: Every positive integer is the value of an expression

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$ and a natural number $c$, the predicate holds when some expression has value $n$ and exactly $c$ ones.
nodes.title: Achievable numbers of ones

nodes.summary: The integer complexity of a positive integer $n$ is the least number of ones in an expression whose value is $n$, that is, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses.
nodes.title: Integer complexity

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer. If an expression $e$ has value $n$, then the integer complexity of $n$ is at most the number of ones of $e$.
nodes.title: Expressions bound the integer complexity from above

nodes.summary: For all positive integers $a$ and $b$, the integer complexity of $a + b$ is at most the sum of the integer complexities of $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity of a sum

nodes.summary: For all positive integers $a$ and $b$, the integer complexity of $ab$ is at most the sum of the integer complexities of $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity of a product

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the value $\lVert n \rVert$ is the integer complexity of $n$ when $n$ is positive, that is, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses, and $\lVert 0 \rVert = 0$.
nodes.title: Integer complexity extended to all natural numbers

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $a$ be the largest natural number with $3^a \le n$ when $n \ge 1$, and let $a = 0$ when $n = 0$. The function $g$ on the natural numbers is given by $g(n) = 3a$ if $n < \frac{4}{3} \cdot 3^a$, $g(n) = 3a + 1$ if $\frac{4}{3} \cdot 3^a \le n < 2 \cdot 3^a$, and $g(n) = 3a + 2$ if $n \ge 2 \cdot 3^a$.
nodes.title: Lower-bound function for integer complexity

nodes.summary: Write $\lVert n \rVert$ for the integer complexity of a positive integer $n$, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses. nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, the $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expressions are the formal expressions built from leaves using the binary operations $+$ and $\times$; the tree structure plays the role of brackets. Each leaf carries a label $i \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ (so there are $m$ kinds of leaf), and a leaf with label $i$ stands for the number $i + 1 \in \{1, \dots, m\}$.

nodes.summary: The natural number expressed by an $m$-ary Mahler–Popken expression: the leaf with index $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ has value $i + 1$, and the value of a sum or of a product of two expressions is the sum or the product of their values.

reading_title.source: Numbers built from copies of $l$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $l$, $k$ and $n$, the number $n$ can be built from $k$ copies of $l$ when $n$ is the value of an expression that uses exactly $k$ copies of $l$, combined by addition and multiplication with arbitrary parentheses. Inductively, $l$ is built from $1$ copy, and if $x$ is built from $a$ copies and $y$ from $b$ copies, then $x + y$ and $x y$ are built from $a + b$ copies.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the generalized Sylvester sequence $(s_k(n))_{k \ge 0}$ is the sequence of natural numbers defined by $s_0(n) = n + 1$ and $s_{k+1}(n) = s_k(n)^2 - s_k(n) + 1$ for $k \ge 0$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $m$ and $L$, the interval $(m, m + L]$ contains distinct multiples of $1, \dots, n$ when there are pairwise distinct natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ with $m < a_i \le m + L$ and $i \mid a_i$ for every $1 \le i \le n$.

Erdős minimum overlap problem

nodes.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and an integer $k$, the overlap of $A$ and $B$ at $k$ is the number of pairs $(a, b) \in A \times B$ with $a - b = k$.
nodes.title: Overlap count of two finite sets of integers

nodes.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$, the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$ is the natural number obtained as the supremum over all integers $k$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$.
nodes.title: Maximum overlap

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $M(n)$ is the least value of the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$, the supremum over $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$, taken over all pairs of disjoint finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A \cup B = \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ and $|A| = |B|$.
nodes.title: Erdős minimum overlap function

nodes.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ and every integer $k$, the overlap $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$ is at most the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$.
nodes.title: Overlaps are bounded by the maximum overlap

nodes.summary: For finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ there is an integer $k$ such that the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$, the supremum over $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = j\}$, equals $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$.
nodes.title: The maximum overlap is attained

reading_title.source: Balanced partitions of $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$ exist

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the set of maximum overlaps of $A$ and $B$, taken over all pairs of disjoint finite sets of integers $A$ and $B$ with $A \cup B = \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ and $|A| = |B|$, is nonempty.
nodes.title: Balanced partitions of $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$ exist

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ there are disjoint finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A \cup B = \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ and $|A| = |B|$ such that the minimum overlap $M(n)$ equals the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$, the supremum over $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$.
nodes.title: The minimum overlap is attained

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ be disjoint finite sets with $A \cup B = \{1, \dots, 2n\}$ and $|A| = |B|$. Then the minimum overlap $M(n)$ is at most the maximum overlap of $A$ and $B$, the supremum over $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ of $\#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}$.
nodes.title: The minimum overlap bounds every balanced partition

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, the normalized minimum overlap is the real number $M(N) / N$, where $M(N)$ is the Erdős minimum overlap function; for $N = 0$ the quotient is $0$ by the convention $x / 0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Normalized minimum overlap

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is a universal asymptotic lower bound when for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a positive integer $N_0$ such that for every $N \ge N_0$ and all disjoint finite sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ with $A \cup B = \{1, \dots, 2N\}$ and $|A| = |B|$, some integer $x$ satisfies $(c - \varepsilon) N \le \#\{(a, b) \in A \times B : a - b = x\}$.

nodes.title: Continuous support interval

nodes.title: Translation interval of the continuous overlap model

nodes.title: Continuous overlap integrand

nodes.summary: For functions $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a translation $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the overlap of $f$ and $g$ at $x$ is $\int_{-1}^{1} f(t)\,g(x + t)\,dt$, the integral of the overlap integrand over the support interval $[-1, 1]$.
nodes.title: Continuous overlap

nodes.summary: For functions $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the set of overlap values of $f$ and $g$ is the image of the translation interval $[-2, 2]$ under the overlap $x \mapsto \int_{-1}^{1} f(t)\,g(x + t)\,dt$.
nodes.title: Continuous overlap values

nodes.summary: A pair of functions $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is admissible when $f$ and $g$ are almost everywhere measurable with respect to Lebesgue measure, take values in $[0, 1]$ at every point, vanish at every point outside the support interval $[-1, 1]$, satisfy $f(t) + g(t) = 1$ for every $t \in [-1, 1]$, and satisfy $\int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\,dt = 1$.
nodes.title: Admissible pairs for the continuous minimum-overlap problem

nodes.summary: For functions $f, g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the pair score of $f$ and $g$ is the supremum of the overlap values $\int_{-1}^{1} f(t)\,g(x + t)\,dt$ over the translations $x \in [-2, 2]$.
nodes.title: Continuous pair score

nodes.summary: A Hurwitz quaternion is a quaternion $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$ whose rational coordinates $x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3$ are either all integers or all halves of odd integers, and its norm is $\mathrm{Nm}(q) = x_0^2 + x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2$. For every positive integer $N$, the number of Hurwitz quaternions of norm $N$ is $24 \sum_{d \mid N,\ d \text{ odd}} d$, that is, $24$ times the sum of the odd divisors of $N$.

Natural and logarithmic density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, let $S, A \subseteq \beta$ and $b \in \beta$, and write $A_{\lt b} = \{x \in A \mid x < b\}$. The partial density of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$ is the proportion $\lvert S \cap A_{\lt b} \rvert / \lvert A_{\lt b} \rvert$ of elements of $A_{\lt b}$ that lie in $S$, taken to be $0$ when $A_{\lt b}$ is empty. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Partial density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The upper density of $S$ relative to $A$ is the limit superior, as $b \to \infty$ in $\beta$, of the partial densities of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Upper density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The lower density of $S$ relative to $A$ is the limit inferior, as $b \to \infty$ in $\beta$, of the partial densities of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Lower density

The set $S$ has density $\alpha$ relative to $A$ if the partial density $\lvert S \cap A \cap \beta_{\lt b} \rvert / \lvert A \cap \beta_{\lt b} \rvert$, taken to be $0$ when the denominator is $0$, tends to $\alpha$ as…
nodes.title: Density of a set

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The set $S$ has positive density relative to $A$ if there is a real number $\alpha > 0$ such that $S$ has density $\alpha$ relative to $A$. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Positive density

nodes.summary: For a set $S$ of integers and a natural number $N$, the two-sided partial natural density of $S$ at $N$ is $\lvert S \cap [-N, N] \rvert / (2N + 1)$, where $[-N, N]$ is the set of integers $m$ with $-N \le m \le N$.
nodes.title: Two-sided partial density

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of integers has two-sided natural density $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ if $\lvert S \cap [-N, N] \rvert / (2N + 1)$ tends to $\alpha$ as the natural number $N$ tends to infinity, where $[-N, N]$ is the set of integers $m$ with $-N \le m \le N$.
nodes.title: Two-sided natural density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a partial order with a least element and at least two elements, in which every closed interval $[a, b]$ is finite. Then the set of all elements of $\beta$ has density $1$ (relative to all of $\beta$).

nodes.summary: If a set $S$ of natural numbers has natural density $\alpha$ with $\alpha \neq 0$, then $S$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Sets of nonzero natural density are infinite

nodes.summary: A set $A$ of natural numbers has logarithmic density $d \in \mathbb{R}$ if $\frac{1}{\log n} \sum_{k \in A,\, k \le n} \frac{1}{k}$ tends to $d$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm, the term $1/k$ for $k = 0$ is taken to be $0$, and the whole expression is taken to be $0$ when $\log n = 0$.

nodes.summary: A subset $A$ of a commutative monoid $M$ is primitive if for all $x, y \in A$ with $x \mid y$, the elements $x$ and $y$ are associated, that is, $x u = y$ for some unit $u$ of $M$. In $\mathbb{N}$, where $1$ is the only unit, this says that no element of $A$ divides a different element of $A$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, $m$ is a cofactor lower bound for $n$ when, for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements.
nodes.title: Cofactor lower bound

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the cofactor threshold $h(n)$ is the largest natural number $m$ such that for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements.
nodes.title: Erdős cofactor threshold

nodes.summary: Let $h(n)$ denote the cofactor threshold of $n$. The statement is that $\sqrt{n} = O(h(n))$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, there are a real constant $C$ and an $n_0$ such that $\sqrt{n} \le C\,h(n)$ for all natural numbers $n \ge n_0$.
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 539

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $h(n)$ be the largest natural number $m$ such that for every set $A$ of exactly $n$ positive integers, the set $\{a/\gcd(a,b) : a, b \in A\}$ has at least $m$ elements. Then $\sqrt{n} = O(h(n))$ as $n \to \infty$: there are a real constant $C$ and an $n_0$ such that $\sqrt{n} \le C\,h(n)$ for all natural numbers $n \ge n_0$.

reading_title.source: Natural numbers with at most $r$ distinct prime factors

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, $n$ has at most $r$ distinct prime factors when $n = 0$ or at most $r$ distinct primes divide $n$; the number $0$ is counted as having no prime factors.
nodes.title: Natural numbers with at most $r$ distinct prime factors

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$, a natural number $m$ is of this form when $m = 2^k + n$ for some natural numbers $k$ and $n$ such that $n = 0$ or at most $r$ distinct primes divide $n$.
nodes.title: Sums of a power of two and a number with few prime factors

Second, for every real number $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $r$ such that the set of natural numbers of the form $2^k + n$, with $k$ and $n$ natural numbers and with $n = 0$ or at most $r$ distinct primes dividing $n$,…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 851

nodes.summary: The set of natural numbers of the form $2^k + p$, with $k$ a natural number and $p$ prime, has positive lower density. Moreover, for every real number $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $r$ such that the set of natural numbers of the form $2^k + n$, with $k$ and $n$ natural numbers and with $n = 0$ or at most $r$ distinct primes dividing $n$, has lower density at least $1 - \varepsilon$.

Strongly complete sequences

nodes.summary: A set $A$ of rational numbers is strongly complete when, for every finite set $B$ of rational numbers, there is an integer $N_0$ such that every integer $m \ge N_0$ is the sum of the elements of some finite subset of $A \setminus B$.
nodes.title: Strongly complete sets of rationals

nodes.title: Polynomial values plus reciprocals

nodes.summary: This is the proposition that for every polynomial $p$ with rational coefficients and positive leading coefficient, the set $A_p$ of rational numbers $p(n) + 1/n$, where $n$ ranges over the positive integers, is strongly complete.
nodes.title: The strong completeness statement of Erdős Problem 351

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $p$ with rational coefficients and positive leading coefficient, let $A_p$ be the set of rational numbers $p(n) + 1/n$, where $n$ ranges over the positive integers. Then $A_p$ is strongly complete: for every finite set $B$ of rational numbers there is an integer $N_0$ such that every integer $m \ge N_0$ is the sum of the elements of some finite subset of $A_p \setminus B$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and an integer $m$, the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is the number of tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_k)$ of natural numbers with $x_1 a_1 + \dots + x_k a_k = m$, counted as an extended natural number, so that it is $\infty$ when there are infinitely many such tuples.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and $s$, write $d(m; a)$ for the number of representations of an integer $m$ by $a = (a_1, \dots, a_k)$. An integer $g$ is the generalized Frobenius number $g(a; s) = \max \{m \in \mathbb{Z} \mid d(m; a) \le s\}$ when $d(g; a) \le s$ and $d(m; a) > s$ for every integer $m > g$.

Ihara constant

nodes.summary: For a sequence $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \in \mathbb{N}$, the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is the extended nonnegative real $N(g)/g$ when $g > 0$, and $0$ when $g = 0$.
nodes.title: Normalized Ihara ratio

nodes.summary: For a sequence $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is $\limsup_{g \to \infty} N(g)/g \in [0, \infty]$, the limit superior as $g \to \infty$ of the normalized ratios of $N$.
nodes.title: Abstract Ihara constant of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is at most $c$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Eventual ratio bounds bound the abstract Ihara constant

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, let $c \in [0, \infty]$, and for each $g \in \mathbb{N}$ let $r_N(g) \in [0, \infty]$ be the normalized ratio $N(g)/g$, with $r_N(0) = 0$. If $c \le r_N(g)$ for infinitely many $g$, then $c \le \limsup_{g \to \infty} r_N(g)$, the Ihara constant of $N$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the Ihara constant from the normalized ratios

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $g \in \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If $N(g) \le c \cdot g$ in $[0, \infty]$, then the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Linear upper bound on a normalized ratio

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $c \in [0, \infty]$ and $g > 0$ an integer. If $c \cdot g \le N(g)$ in $[0, \infty]$, then $c \le N(g)/g$, where the normalized ratio $N(g)/g$ is taken in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for one normalized Ihara ratio

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If $N(g) \le c \cdot g$ in $[0, \infty]$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Eventual linear upper bound on the abstract Ihara constant

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, $c \in [0, \infty]$ and $d \in [0, \infty)$. If $N(g) \le c \cdot g + d$ in $[0, \infty]$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most $c$.
nodes.title: Eventual affine upper bound on the abstract Ihara constant

nodes.summary: Let $N : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $c \in [0, \infty]$. If there are infinitely many integers $g > 0$ with $c \cdot g \le N(g)$ in $[0, \infty]$, then $c \le \limsup_{g \to \infty} N(g)/g$, the Ihara constant of $N$, where the ratio $N(g)/g$ is taken in $[0, \infty]$ and set to $0$ at $g = 0$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the Ihara constant from a linear bound

nodes.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $g \in \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) \le M(g)$, then the normalized ratio of $N$ at $g$ is at most the normalized ratio of $M$ at $g$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the normalized ratio

nodes.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) \le M(g)$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then the abstract Ihara constant of $N$ is at most that of $M$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the abstract Ihara constant

nodes.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) = M(g)$ for all sufficiently large $g$, then $N$ and $M$ have the same abstract Ihara constant. In particular, changing finitely many values of $N$ does not change its abstract Ihara constant.
nodes.title: The abstract Ihara constant ignores finitely many values

nodes.summary: Let $N, M : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $G \in \mathbb{N}$. If $N(g) = M(g)$ for every $g \ge G$, then $N$ and $M$ have the same abstract Ihara constant.
nodes.title: Agreement from an index onward preserves the abstract Ihara constant

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field. The ring norm on the polynomial ring $F[T]$ sends $f$ to the number of elements of the quotient ring $F[T]/(f)$, written $|f| = |F[T]/(f)|$; for $f = 0$ the quotient is infinite and $|0| = 0$. It is a ring norm: $|f| = 0$ only for $f = 0$, $|-f| = |f|$, $|f + g| \le |f| + |g|$ and $|fg| \le |f|\,|g|$.
