Birational maps and the Cremona group

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ consists of dominant rational maps $f \colon X \dashrightarrow Y$ and $g \colon Y \dashrightarrow X$ that are mutually inverse: $g \circ f$ is the identity rational map of $X$ and $f \circ g$ is the identity rational map of $Y$.
nodes.title: Birational map

nodes.summary: For an irreducible scheme $X$, the identity birational map of $X$ has the identity rational map of $X$ as both its forward and its inverse map.
nodes.title: Identity birational map

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes. The inverse of a birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is the birational map from $Y$ to $X$ whose forward map is the inverse rational map of the original and whose inverse map is its forward rational map.
nodes.title: Inverse birational map

nodes.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be irreducible schemes, let $f$ be a birational map from $X$ to $Y$ and let $g$ be a birational map from $Y$ to $Z$. The composite of $f$ and $g$ is the birational map from $X$ to $Z$ whose forward rational map is the forward map of $f$ followed by the forward map of $g$, and whose inverse rational map is the inverse of $g$ followed by the inverse of $f$.
nodes.title: Composition of birational maps

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible schemes over a scheme $S$. A birational map from $X$ to $Y$ is over $S$ when its forward rational map $X \dashrightarrow Y$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.
nodes.title: Birational maps over a base

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be an irreducible scheme over a scheme $S$. The birational automorphisms of $X$ over $S$ form the subgroup of the group of birational self-maps of $X$ consisting of those birational maps whose forward rational map $X \dashrightarrow X$ is compatible with the structure maps to $S$.

nodes.summary: For a division ring $K$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the projective space $\mathbb{P}^n(K)$ is the projectivization of $K^{n+1}$: the set of nonzero vectors of $K^{n+1}$ modulo multiplication by nonzero scalars, equivalently the lines through the origin.

nodes.title: Projective vanishing set

nodes.summary: A cubic surface over a field $k$ is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial $f \in k[x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3]$ of degree $3$ in the four homogeneous coordinates of $\mathbb{P}^3$, its defining equation. The surface it describes is the projective zero locus $V(f) \subseteq \mathbb{P}^3$.

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$, and let $I_k(Z)$ be the ideal of polynomials in $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ whose image in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ vanishes at every point of $Z$. The set $Z$ is defined over $k$ if the vanishing ideal of $Z$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ equals the ideal generated by the image of $I_k(Z)$ under the coefficient map…
nodes.title: Sets defined over $k$

reading_title.source: Defined over $k$ as an equality of ideals

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$ and let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$. Then $Z$ is defined over $k$ if and only if the vanishing ideal of $Z$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ equals the ideal generated by the image of $I_k(Z)$ under the coefficient map $k[X_1, \dots, X_n] \to \bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$.
nodes.title: Defined over $k$ as an equality of ideals

reading_title.source: Polynomials in the ideal over $k$ vanish on the set

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$, let $Z \subseteq \bar k^n$, and let $f \in I_k(Z)$. Then for every point $P \in Z$, the image of $f$ in $\bar k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$ evaluated at $P$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Polynomials in the ideal over $k$ vanish on the set

reading_title.source: The ideal over $k$ of the empty set

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$. For every $n$, the ideal $I_k(\emptyset)$ of the empty subset of $\bar k^n$ is all of $k[X_1, \dots, X_n]$.
nodes.title: The ideal over $k$ of the empty set

reading_title.source: The ideal over $k$ reverses inclusions

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field with algebraic closure $\bar k$. If $Z_1 \subseteq Z_2 \subseteq \bar k^n$, then $I_k(Z_2) \subseteq I_k(Z_1)$.
nodes.title: The ideal over $k$ reverses inclusions
Line arrangements in the projective plane

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $v \ne w$ be two distinct points of the projective plane $\mathbb{P}(K^3)$. Call two points orthogonal when the dot product of representative vectors in $K^3$ vanishes, and let $v \times w$ be the point spanned by the cross product of representatives of $v$ and $w$, which is nonzero since $v \ne w$. Then a point $p$ equals $v \times w$ if and only if $p$ is orthogonal to both $v$ and $w$.…
nodes.title: Two distinct lines meet in their cross product

nodes.summary: A line arrangement in the projective plane over a field $K$ is a finite set of at least two lines, each line recorded by its coordinate vector, a point of the dual projective plane $\mathbb{P}(K^3)$.
nodes.title: Line arrangement

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. The multiplicity $m_p$ of a point $p$ in $A$ is the number of lines of $A$ through $p$, that is, of lines of $A$ whose coordinate vector has zero dot product with a representative of $p$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a point in a line arrangement

nodes.summary: The singular points of a line arrangement $A$ in the projective plane over a field form the finite set of intersection points of pairs of distinct lines of $A$, where two distinct lines with coordinate vectors $\ell$ and $\ell'$ meet in the point spanned by the cross product $\ell \times \ell'$ of their representatives.
nodes.title: Singular points of a line arrangement

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. A point $p$ is a singular point of $A$ if and only if there are two distinct lines of $A$ that both pass through $p$.
nodes.title: Singular points lie on two distinct lines

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a line arrangement in the projective plane over a field. A point $p$ is a singular point of $A$ if and only if its multiplicity $m_p$ in $A$, the number of lines of $A$ through $p$, satisfies $m_p \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Singular points are the points of multiplicity at least two

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the projective plane over a field. Every point $p$ has multiplicity $m_p \le d$ in $A$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity is at most the number of lines

nodes.summary: Every line arrangement in the projective plane over a field has at least one singular point, since any two of its distinct lines meet.
nodes.title: Every line arrangement has a singular point

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the projective plane over a field, let $S$ be its set of singular points, with $s$ elements, and let $m_p$ be the multiplicity of a point $p$ in $A$. The Harbourne constant of $A$ is the real number
nodes.title: Harbourne constant of a line arrangement
Multiplicity of a hypersurface at a point

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a module over a division ring $K$. For every nonzero scalar $a \in K$ and every nonzero vector $v \in V$, the points of the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(V)$ represented by $a v$ and by $v$ are equal.
nodes.title: Rescaling a representative does not change the projective point

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $m$ a finite set. Let $p, q$ be points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^m)$ and let $\hat p, \hat q \in K^m$ be the fixed nonzero representatives chosen for $p$ and $q$. Then $p$ and $q$ are orthogonal (the dot product of a representative of $p$ with a representative of $q$ vanishes, which does not depend on the representatives) if and only if $\hat p \cdot \hat q = 0$.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of projective points via representatives

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. The order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of $F$ at $v$ is the order at the origin of the Taylor expansion $F(v + X)$, the polynomial obtained from $F$ by substituting $X_i + v_i$ for each $X_i$: the least total degree of a monomial with nonzero…
nodes.title: Order of vanishing at a point

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $F$ a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, and $v \in R^\sigma$. The constant term of the Taylor expansion $F(X + v)$, obtained by substituting $X_i + v_i$ for each $X_i$, is the value $F(v)$.
nodes.title: Constant term of the Taylor expansion

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_j)_{j \in \sigma}$, let $v \in R^\sigma$ and let $i \in \sigma$. Writing $G(X + v)$ for the polynomial obtained from a polynomial $G$ by substituting $X_j + v_j$ for each $X_j$, we have $\frac{\partial}{\partial X_i}\bigl(F(X + v)\bigr) = \frac{\partial F}{\partial X_i}(X + v)$.
nodes.title: Partial derivatives commute with Taylor expansion

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F$ of $F$ at $v$ is at least $1$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing to order at least one

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F$ of $F$ at $v$ is $0$ if and only if $F(v) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Vanishing to order zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $a \in R$ be nonzero. For every point $v \in R^\sigma$, the constant polynomial $a$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v a = 0$ at $v$.
nodes.title: Nonzero constants vanish to order zero

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $F$ be a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ and let $v \in R^\sigma$. Then the order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v F \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ of $F$ at $v$ equals $\infty$ if and only if $F = 0$.
nodes.title: Only the zero polynomial vanishes to infinite order

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain of characteristic zero, $F$ a polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, $v \in R^\sigma$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $F$ vanishes to order at least $n + 1$ at $v$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$ and every first partial derivative $\partial F / \partial X_i$ vanishes to order at least $n$ at $v$.
nodes.title: Order of vanishing via first partial derivatives

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be an integral domain of characteristic zero and let $F$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every point $v \in R^\sigma$, the polynomial $F$ vanishes to order at least $2$ at $v$ if and only if $F(v) = 0$ and $\frac{\partial F}{\partial X_i}(v) = 0$ for every $i \in \sigma$.
nodes.title: Vanishing to order at least two via first partial derivatives

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $F$ be a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ that is homogeneous of some degree $d$. For every nonzero $c \in K$ and every point $v \in K^\sigma$, the orders of vanishing agree: $\operatorname{ord}_{cv} F = \operatorname{ord}_v F$.
nodes.title: Scaling invariance of the order of vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. The multiplicity of $F$ at a point $p$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ is the order of vanishing of $F$ at the chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$ of $p$, as a natural number, with the value $\infty$ read as $0$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a polynomial at a projective point

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a homogeneous polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every nonzero $v \in K^\sigma$, the multiplicity of $F$ at the point $[v]$ of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ spanned by $v$ equals the order of vanishing of $F$ at $v$, with the value $\infty$ read as $0$.
nodes.title: The multiplicity can be computed at any representative

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $F \neq 0$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$. For every point $p$ of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$, the multiplicity of $F$ at $p$, viewed in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, equals the order of vanishing of $F$ at the chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$ of $p$.
nodes.title: The multiplicity of a nonzero polynomial is its order of vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. For every $a \in K$, the constant polynomial $a$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$ has multiplicity $0$ at every point $p$ of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$. For $a = 0$ this is the junk value of the multiplicity of the zero polynomial.
nodes.title: Constants have multiplicity zero

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $F \neq 0$ a polynomial over $K$ in the variables $(X_i)_{i \in \sigma}$, and $p$ a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ with chosen representative $\bar p \in K^\sigma$. The multiplicity of $F$ at $p$ is positive if and only if $F(\bar p) = 0$.
nodes.title: Positive multiplicity means vanishing

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\sigma$ be a finite set and let $w, v \in K^\sigma$ with $w \cdot v = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i v_i \neq 0$. Then the linear form $L = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i X_i$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v L = 0$ at $v$.
nodes.title: A linear form vanishes to order zero off its hyperplane

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $\sigma$ be a finite set and let $w, v \in K^\sigma$ with $w \neq 0$ and $w \cdot v = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i v_i = 0$. Then the linear form $L = \sum_{i \in \sigma} w_i X_i$ has order of vanishing $\operatorname{ord}_v L = 1$ at $v$.
nodes.title: A nonzero linear form vanishes to order one on its hyperplane

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ a finite type and $w \in K^\sigma$ nonzero, and let $p$ be a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ orthogonal to the point $[w]$ spanned by $w$, that is, $p$ lies on the hyperplane $\sum_i w_i x_i = 0$. Then the linear form $\sum_i w_i X_i$ has multiplicity $1$ at $p$.
nodes.title: A hyperplane has multiplicity one at its points

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ a finite type and $w \in K^\sigma$ nonzero, and let $p$ be a point of $\mathbb{P}(K^\sigma)$ that is not orthogonal to the point $[w]$ spanned by $w$, that is, $p$ does not lie on the hyperplane $\sum_i w_i x_i = 0$. Then the linear form $\sum_i w_i X_i$ has multiplicity $0$ at $p$.
nodes.title: A hyperplane has multiplicity zero off it
Regular functions on algebraic sets

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $K$ be commutative rings and $\mathrm{ev} : A \to K$ a ring homomorphism. An element $r$ of the total ring of fractions of $A$ (its localization at the non-zero-divisors) is regular at $\mathrm{ev}$ when there is some $g \in A$ with $\mathrm{ev}(g) \neq 0$ such that $g r$ lies in the image of $A$ in its total ring of fractions.
nodes.title: Regularity of a fraction at an evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a nontrivial commutative ring. For every ring homomorphism $\mathrm{ev} : A \to K$ and every $a \in A$, the image of $a$ in the total ring of fractions of $A$ is regular at $\mathrm{ev}$.
nodes.title: Elements of the base ring are regular

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a nontrivial commutative ring. For every ring homomorphism $\mathrm{ev} : A \to K$, the element $0$ of the total ring of fractions of $A$ is regular at $\mathrm{ev}$.
nodes.title: Zero is regular

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K$ a nontrivial commutative ring. For every ring homomorphism $\mathrm{ev} : A \to K$, the element $1$ of the total ring of fractions of $A$ is regular at $\mathrm{ev}$.
nodes.title: One is regular

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ an index set and $X \subseteq K^\sigma$ a set of points. The affine coordinate ring of $X$ is the quotient $K[x_i : i \in \sigma] / I(X)$ of the polynomial ring over $K$ in variables indexed by $\sigma$ by the vanishing ideal $I(X)$, the ideal of all polynomials that vanish at every point of $X$.
nodes.title: Affine coordinate ring

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ an index set and $X \subseteq K^\sigma$ a set of points. For a point $P \in X$, evaluation at $P$ is the ring homomorphism from the affine coordinate ring of $X$ to $K$ that sends the residue class of a polynomial $f$ to $f(P)$; it is well defined because every polynomial in the vanishing ideal of $X$ vanishes at $P$.
nodes.title: Evaluation at a point of an affine set

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ an index set, $X \subseteq K^\sigma$ a set of points and $P \in X$. For every polynomial $f$ over $K$ in variables indexed by $\sigma$, evaluating the residue class of $f$ in the affine coordinate ring of $X$ at $P$ gives $f(P)$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a residue class

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ an index set and $X \subseteq K^\sigma$ a set of points whose affine coordinate ring $A$ is an integral domain. A rational function on $X$ is an element $r$ of the field of fractions of $A$; it is regular at a point $P \in X$ when there is some $g \in A$ whose value $g(P)$ under evaluation at $P$ is nonzero such that $g r$ lies in the image of $A$ in its field of fractions.
nodes.title: Regularity of a rational function at a point

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\sigma$ an index set and $X \subseteq K^\sigma$ a set of points whose affine coordinate ring $A$ is an integral domain. For every $a \in A$ and every point $P \in X$, the image of $a$ in the field of fractions of $A$ is a rational function on $X$ that is regular at $P$.
nodes.title: Elements of the coordinate ring are regular
Seshadri constants of points in the plane

nodes.summary: A plane polynomial is a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ in two variables $X_0, X_1$ with complex coefficients.
nodes.title: Polynomials in two complex variables

nodes.summary: A point of the complex affine plane is a pair $a = (a_0, a_1)$ of complex numbers, that is, an element of $\mathbb{C}^2$, with coordinates indexed by $0$ and $1$.
nodes.title: Points of the complex affine plane

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2]$ and a point $a = (a_1, a_2) \in \mathbb{C}^2$, the translate of $f$ by $a$ is the polynomial $f(x_1 + a_1, x_2 + a_2)$, obtained by substituting $x_i + a_i$ for $x_i$. It moves the point $a$ to the origin.
nodes.title: Translate of a plane polynomial

nodes.summary: The total degree of the exponent vector $m = (m_0, m_1)$ of a monomial $X_0^{m_0} X_1^{m_1}$ in two variables is $m_0 + m_1$.
nodes.title: Total degree of a monomial

nodes.summary: For a polynomial $f \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ and a point $a = (a_0, a_1) \in \mathbb{C}^2$, the multiplicity of $f$ at $a$ is the least total degree of a monomial occurring with nonzero coefficient in the translated polynomial $f(X_0 + a_0, X_1 + a_1)$. For the zero polynomial it is $0$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a plane polynomial at a point

nodes.summary: For every point $a = (a_0, a_1) \in \mathbb{C}^2$, the polynomial $X_0 - a_0 \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$, which defines the line through $a$ on which the first coordinate is constant, has multiplicity $1$ at $a$.
nodes.title: The first-coordinate line through a point has multiplicity one there

nodes.summary: For a configuration $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, not necessarily distinct, the Seshadri ratios of $x$ are the real numbers $\deg f / \sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$, where $f$ ranges over the nonzero polynomials in $\mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ with $\sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f > 0$, $\deg f$ is the total degree of $f$, and $\operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$ is the…
nodes.title: Seshadri ratios of ten points

nodes.summary: For a configuration $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, not necessarily distinct, the affine Seshadri constant of $x$ is the infimum of the ratios $\deg f / \sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$ over all nonzero polynomials $f \in \mathbb{C}[X_0, X_1]$ with $\sum_{i=0}^{9} \operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f > 0$, where $\deg f$ is the total degree of $f$ and $\operatorname{mult}_{x_i} f$ is the…
nodes.title: Seshadri constant of ten affine points

nodes.summary: For every configuration $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, not necessarily distinct, the affine Seshadri constant of $x$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The affine Seshadri constant is at most one

nodes.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant is the supremum, over all configurations $x = (x_0, \dots, x_9)$ of ten pairwise distinct points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, of the affine Seshadri constant of $x$.
nodes.title: Generic ten-point Seshadri constant

nodes.summary: The ten-point Seshadri constant is the generic ten-point Seshadri constant: the supremum, over all configurations of ten pairwise distinct points of $\mathbb{C}^2$, of their affine Seshadri constants.
nodes.title: Ten-point Seshadri constant

nodes.summary: The proposition that the generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, equals $1/\sqrt{10}$.
nodes.title: Nagata's conjecture for ten points

nodes.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $4/13$.
nodes.title: Eckl's 2008 lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant

nodes.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $177/560$.
nodes.title: Harbourne–Roé lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant

nodes.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $55/174$.
nodes.title: Ciliberto–Miranda lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant

nodes.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at least $117/370$.
nodes.title: Eckl's 2011 lower bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant

nodes.summary: The generic ten-point Seshadri constant of $\mathbb{P}^2$, in the affine-chart model, is at most $1/\sqrt{10}$.
nodes.title: Submaximal upper bound for the ten-point Seshadri constant
Tangent spaces of algebraic sets

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and $P, v \in k^n$, the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along the translated direction $v$ is $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(P)\, v_i \in k$, where $\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}$ is the formal partial derivative.
nodes.title: Total derivative at a point

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a point $P \in k^n$, this is the $k$-linear map $k^n \to k$ sending $v$ to the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$, namely $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(P)\, v_i$.
nodes.title: Total derivative as a linear map

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a point $P \in k^n$, the tangent space of the hypersurface $f = 0$ at $P$ is the kernel of the total derivative of $f$ at $P$, viewed as a $k$-linear map $k^n \to k$: the subspace of vectors $v \in k^n$ with $\sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(P)\, v_i = 0$. The point $P$ is not required to satisfy $f(P) = 0$.
nodes.title: Tangent space of a hypersurface

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, an ideal $I$ of $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a point $P \in k^n$, the tangent space of $I$ at $P$ is the $k$-linear subspace of $k^n$ obtained as the intersection, over all $f \in I$, of the tangent spaces at $P$ of the hypersurfaces $f = 0$. The point $P$ is not required to be a common zero of $I$.
nodes.title: Tangent space of an ideal

nodes.summary: For a field $k$, a polynomial $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and $P, v \in k^n$, the total derivative of $f$ at $P$, viewed as a $k$-linear map $k^n \to k$, sends $v$ to the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$.
nodes.title: Evaluating the total derivative linear map

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $f \in k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and $P, v \in k^n$. Then $v$ lies in the tangent space of the hypersurface $f = 0$ at $P$ if and only if the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$ is zero.
nodes.title: Membership in the tangent space of a hypersurface

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field, $I$ an ideal of $k[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, and $P, v \in k^n$. Then $v$ lies in the tangent space of $I$ at $P$ if and only if, for every $f \in I$, the total derivative of $f$ at $P$ along $v$ is zero.
nodes.title: Membership in the tangent space of an ideal
Topological reconstruction of varieties

nodes.title: Structure morphism of a projective spectrum

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme. A morphism $f : X \to \operatorname{Spec} R$ is projective if there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a closed immersion $i$ of $X$ into $\operatorname{Proj} R[x_1, \dots, x_n]$, the polynomial ring graded by total degree, such that $f$ is $i$ followed by the structure morphism $\operatorname{Proj} R[x_1, \dots, x_n] \to \operatorname{Spec} R$.
nodes.title: Projective morphism to an affine scheme

nodes.summary: A scheme $X$ is normal if for every point $x \in X$ the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X,x}$ is an integrally closed domain.
nodes.title: Normal scheme

nodes.summary: Let $K$ and $L$ be fields of characteristic zero, and let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible normal schemes with projective morphisms $f : X \to \operatorname{Spec} K$ and $g : Y \to \operatorname{Spec} L$. Suppose that the Krull dimension of the underlying topological space of $X$ is at least $4$; or it is at least $3$ and $K$ and $L$ are essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{Q}$; or it is at least $2$ and $K$ and $L$…

Let $n$ be a natural number whose image in the residue field of $R$ is nonzero, let $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be a separable closure of $k$, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a valuation subring of $k^{\mathrm{sep}}$ whose intersection with $k$ is $R$. reading_title.source: Galois elements as automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$

nodes.summary: Each element $\sigma$ of the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ is regarded as the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ of $\mathbb{Q}$. Since $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$ is by definition the group of $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, this map is the identity.
nodes.title: Galois elements as automorphisms of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ be the group of nonsingular points of $W$ with coordinates in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, together with the point at infinity. For $\sigma$ in the absolute Galois group $G_{\mathbb{Q}}$, this is the homomorphism of additive groups $W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \to W(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that sends the point…
nodes.title: Galois action on the points of a Weierstrass curve

Isogeny volcanoes

nodes.summary: A multigraph on a vertex set $V$ is given by an edge multiplicity function $m$ that assigns to every two vertices $v, w \in V$ a natural number $m(v, w)$ and is symmetric: $m(v, w) = m(w, v)$ for all $v, w \in V$. Loops are permitted: $m(v, v)$ may be positive.
nodes.title: Multigraph

nodes.summary: Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of a multigraph $G$ are adjacent when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive.
nodes.title: Adjacency in a multigraph

nodes.summary: For a multigraph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ with edge multiplicity $m$, the degree of a vertex $v$ is $\sum_{w \in V} m(v, w)$. A loop at $v$ contributes its multiplicity once, matching the outgoing-isogeny convention.
nodes.title: Degree of a vertex in a multigraph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$ with edge multiplicity $m$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $V$. The degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ is $\sum_{w \in V,\, P(w)} m(v, w)$.
nodes.title: Degree restricted to a predicate

nodes.summary: Two vertices $v$ and $w$ of a multigraph $G$ are connected when they are related by the reflexive-transitive closure of adjacency, that is, when there is a finite sequence of vertices $v = u_0, u_1, \dots, u_k = w$ with $k \ge 0$ and $u_i$ adjacent to $u_{i+1}$ for each $i < k$.
nodes.title: Connectivity of vertices in a multigraph

nodes.summary: A multigraph $G$ is connected when every two vertices $v$ and $w$ of $G$ are joined by a walk, that is, $w$ is reachable from $v$ by a finite (possibly empty) sequence of steps along edges of positive multiplicity.
nodes.title: Connected multigraph

nodes.summary: In a multigraph $G$, a vertex $v$ is adjacent to a vertex $w$ if and only if $w$ is adjacent to $v$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of adjacency in a multigraph

nodes.summary: In a multigraph $G$, every vertex $v$ is connected to $v$.
nodes.title: Every vertex is connected to itself

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ be a decidable predicate on $V$. Then the degree of $v$ equals the degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ plus the degree of $v$ restricted to $\neg P$.
nodes.title: Degree splits over a predicate and its complement

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $v \in V$ and let $P$ and $Q$ be decidable predicates on $V$. If $P(w) \iff Q(w)$ for every vertex $w$ whose edge multiplicity with $v$ is positive, then the degree of $v$ restricted to $P$ equals the degree of $v$ restricted to $Q$.
nodes.title: Restricted degree depends only on the neighbours

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ be a prime. An $\ell$-isogeny volcano consists of a finite vertex set $V$, a multigraph on $V$ with edge multiplicities $m(v, w)$, a depth $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a surjective level map $\mathrm{lev} : V \to \{0, 1, \dots, d\}$ and a surface degree $s \in \mathbb{N}$ with $s \le 2$, subject to the following conditions, where the surface is the set of vertices of level $0$. Every surface vertex $v$ satisfies…
nodes.title: Isogeny volcano

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the surface of $C$ when its level is $0$.
nodes.title: Surface of a volcano

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ of depth $d$ lies on the floor of $C$ when its level is $d$, the last of the levels $0, 1, \dots, d$.
nodes.title: Floor of a volcano

nodes.summary: The depth of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ is the natural number $d$ recorded in $C$: the levels of the vertices of $C$ are exactly $0, 1, \dots, d$, with level $0$ the surface and level $d$ the floor.
nodes.title: Depth of an isogeny volcano

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a horizontal edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and both $v$ and $w$ lie on the surface, that is, both have level $0$.
nodes.title: Horizontal edge

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a descending edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and $w$ lies one level below $v$, that is, the level of $v$ plus one equals the level of $w$ (level $0$ being the surface).
nodes.title: Descending edge

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is an ascending edge when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and $w$ lies one level above $v$, that is, the level of $w$ plus one equals the level of $v$ (level $0$ being the surface).
nodes.title: Ascending edge

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$, the pair $(v, w)$ of vertices is a vertical edge when it is a descending edge or an ascending edge, that is, when the edge multiplicity between $v$ and $w$ is positive and the levels of $v$ and $w$ differ by exactly one.
nodes.title: Vertical edge

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, for vertices $v$ and $w$, $(v, w)$ is a descending edge if and only if $(w, v)$ is an ascending edge.
nodes.title: Reversing a descending edge gives an ascending edge

nodes.summary: In an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, for vertices $v$ and $w$, $(v, w)$ is an ascending edge if and only if $(w, v)$ is a descending edge.
nodes.title: Reversing an ascending edge gives a descending edge

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an $\ell$-isogeny volcano, with levels numbered from $0$ at the surface, and let $v, w$ be vertices of $C$ whose edge multiplicity is positive. Then $(v, w)$ is a horizontal edge (both $v$ and $w$ have level $0$), a descending edge (the level of $w$ is the level of $v$ plus one) or an ascending edge (the level of $v$ is the level of $w$ plus one).
nodes.title: Every edge of an isogeny volcano is horizontal, descending or ascending

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the surface of $C$ if and only if the level of $v$, as a natural number, is $0$.
nodes.title: Surface vertices are those of level zero

nodes.summary: A vertex $v$ of an $\ell$-isogeny volcano $C$ lies on the floor of $C$ if and only if the level of $v$, as a natural number, equals the depth of $C$.
nodes.title: Floor vertices are those whose level equals the depth

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be an $\ell$-isogeny volcano with edge multiplicities $m$ and surface degree $s$. For every surface vertex $v$ of $C$, that is, every vertex of level $0$, the sum of $m(v, w)$ over all surface vertices $w$ of $C$ equals $s$.
nodes.title: Surface regularity of an isogeny volcano
Point counts and Frobenius traces

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$ with $q$ elements, and let $\#W(F)$ be the number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity. The Frobenius trace of $W$ is the integer $a_q(W) = q + 1 - \#W(F)$.
nodes.title: Frobenius trace

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be an elliptic curve in Weierstrass form over a finite field $F$. The number of $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity, is one more than the number of pairs $(x, y) \in F \times F$ satisfying the Weierstrass equation of $W$.
nodes.title: Point count from affine solutions

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$ with $q$ elements. The number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity, is at most $2q + 1$.
nodes.title: Upper bound on the point count

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$ with $q$ elements, and let $\#W(F)$ be the number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity. Then $\#W(F) = q + 1 - a_q(W)$, where $a_q(W)$ is the Frobenius trace of $W$.
nodes.title: Point count from the Frobenius trace

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$ with $q$ elements, and let $\#W(F)$ be the number of nonsingular $F$-points of $W$, counting the point at infinity. Then $\#W(F) + a_q(W) = q + 1$, where $a_q(W)$ is the Frobenius trace of $W$.
nodes.title: Point count plus Frobenius trace

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $a \ge 1$, and let $F$ be a finite field with $q = p^a$ elements. An integer $\beta$ is the Frobenius trace $q + 1 - \#E(F)$ of some elliptic curve $E$ over $F$ if and only if $\beta^2 \le 4q$ and one of the following holds: 1. $\gcd(\beta, p) = 1$; 2. $a$ is even and $\beta = \pm 2p^{a/2}$; 3. $a$ is even, $p \not\equiv 1 \pmod 3$ and $\beta = \pm p^{a/2}$; 4. $a$ is odd, $p = 2$ or…
nodes.title: Waterhouse's theorem on Frobenius traces

nodes.summary: Let $q \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $A$ be a symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with integer entries. Every complex root $\mu \ne q + 1$ of the characteristic polynomial of $A$ satisfies $|\mu| \le 2\sqrt{q}$ if and only if, for every such root $\mu \ne q + 1$, every complex number $s$ with $1 - \mu q^{-s} + q^{1 - 2s} = 0$ has real part $1/2$.
nodes.title: Ihara's criterion for Ramanujan graphs

nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number and let $A$ be a symmetric $n \times n$ matrix with integer entries such that every complex root $\mu \ne q + 1$ of its characteristic polynomial satisfies $|\mu| \le 2\sqrt{q}$. Let $\mu \ne q + 1$ be a complex root of the characteristic polynomial of $A$ and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $\alpha^2 - \mu\alpha + q = 0$. Then $\alpha$ is an algebraic integer, and every complex root…
nodes.title: Ramanujan graphs give Weil numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $a \in \{1, 2\}$, and let $F$ be a finite field with $q = p^a$ elements. A natural number $N$ is the number $\#E(F)$ of $F$-points (counting the point at infinity) of some elliptic curve $E$ over $F$ with $4 \mid N$ if and only if there are natural numbers $l$ and $m$ with $N = 2m$, $2l + m = q + 1$, $m > 0$ and $(2l - m)^2 \le 4q$.
nodes.title: Elliptic curves with point count divisible by 4 and Ramanujan graphs on two vertices

nodes.summary: Ordinary elliptic curves with point count divisible by 4 and Ramanujan graphs on two vertices. Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $a \ge 1$, and let $F$ be a finite field with $q = p^a$ elements. A natural number $N$ is the number $\#E(F)$ of $F$-points (counting the point at infinity) of some elliptic curve $E$ over $F$ with $4 \mid N$ whose Frobenius trace $q + 1 - \#E(F)$ is coprime to $p$ if and only if there are…
nodes.title: Ordinary elliptic curves with point count divisible by 4 and Ramanujan graphs on two vertices
Supersingular elliptic curves

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then $E$ is called supersingular when every point $P \in E(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ with $pP = 0$ is $P = 0$.
nodes.title: Supersingular elliptic curves

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. If for every integer $r \ge 1$ the only point $P \in E(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ with $p^r P = 0$ is $P = 0$, then $E$ is supersingular.
nodes.title: Supersingularity from trivial prime-power torsion

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $E$ be a supersingular elliptic curve over an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$. Then for every integer $r \ge 1$, every point $P \in E(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p)$ with $p^r P = 0$ is $P = 0$.
nodes.title: Supersingular curves have trivial prime-power torsion
Weierstrass curves

nodes.summary: For a variable change $C = (u, r, s, t)$ over a field $F$, with $u \in F^\times$ and $r, s, t \in F$, the affine coordinate map of $C$ sends $(x, y) \in F^2$ to $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$.
nodes.title: Coordinate map of a Weierstrass variable change

nodes.summary: For a variable change $C = (u, r, s, t)$ over a field $F$, the map $(x, y) \mapsto (u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ is a bijection $F^2 \to F^2$, whose inverse is the corresponding map of the inverse variable change $C^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Variable changes act bijectively on affine coordinates

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. A pair $(x, y) \in F^2$ satisfies the Weierstrass equation of $C \cdot W$ if and only if $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ satisfies the Weierstrass equation of $W$.
nodes.title: Variable changes transform the Weierstrass equation

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve over a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. The map $(x, y) \mapsto (u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$ is a bijection from the solutions $(x, y) \in F^2$ of the Weierstrass equation of $C \cdot W$ onto the solutions in $F^2$ of the Weierstrass equation of $W$; its inverse is the corresponding map of $C^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Variable changes biject affine solutions

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a field $F$, let $C = (u, r, s, t)$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. There is a bijection from the rational points of $C \cdot W$ to the rational points of $W$, where in both cases the point at infinity is included; it sends the point at infinity to the point at infinity and an affine point $(x, y)$ to $(u^2 x + r,\ u^3 y + u^2 s x + t)$.
nodes.title: Variable changes biject rational points

nodes.summary: Let $W$ be an elliptic Weierstrass curve over a finite field $F$, let $C$ be a variable change and let $C \cdot W$ be the transformed curve. Then $C \cdot W$ and $W$ have the same number of rational points.
nodes.title: Variable changes preserve the point count

nodes.summary: The ideal generated by `X - x` and `Y - y` is nonzero.
nodes.title: The ideal of a point on a Weierstrass curve is nonzero
Hasse bound

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. Polynomials $a, b, c \in K[X]$ form a primitive triple when they generate the unit ideal of $K[X]$, that is, when there are $u, v, w \in K[X]$ with $ua + vb + wc = 1$.
nodes.title: Primitive triple of polynomials

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and let $a, b, c \in K[X]$ with $c \neq 0$. If no irreducible polynomial in $K[X]$ divides all of $a$, $b$ and $c$, then $a, b, c$ form a primitive triple: there are $u, v, w \in K[X]$ with $ua + vb + wc = 1$.
nodes.title: Polynomials with no common irreducible factor form a primitive triple

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $u, v, h \in K[X]$ form a primitive triple with $h \neq 0$, and let $x, y \in K(X)$ be nonzero rational functions with $u/h = xy$ and $v/h = x + y$ in $K(X)$. Then $\deg u = \deg \operatorname{num}(x) + \deg \operatorname{num}(y)$, where $\operatorname{num}$ denotes the numerator of a rational function written in lowest terms.
nodes.title: Numerator degrees from a primitive presentation of product and sum

nodes.summary: Let $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $d(n-1) + d(n+1) = 2d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and let $q, N$ be integers with $d(0) = q$ and $d(-1) = N$. Then $d(n) = n^2 + (q + 1 - N)n + q$ for every integer $n$.
nodes.title: Integer sequences with constant second difference two

nodes.summary: Let $a, q \in \mathbb{Z}$. If $n^2 + an + q \ge 0$ for every integer $n$ and there is no integer $n$ with $n^2 + an + q = 0$ and $(n+1)^2 + a(n+1) + q = 0$, then $a^2 \le 4q$.
nodes.title: Discriminant bound for a nonnegative integral quadratic without adjacent zeros

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $q$ and $N$, Manin degree data for $q$ and $N$ is a sequence $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $d(0) = q$, $d(-1) = N$, $d(n-1) + d(n+1) = 2d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and there is no integer $n$ with $d(n) = d(n+1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Manin degree data

nodes.summary: Let $q$ and $N$ be natural numbers and put $a = q + 1 - N \in \mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $n^2 + an + q \ge 0$ for every integer $n$, and there is no integer $n$ at which both $n^2 + an + q$ and $(n+1)^2 + a(n+1) + q$ vanish. Then the sequence $d(n) = n^2 + an + q$ is Manin degree data for $q$ and $N$.
nodes.title: Manin degree data from a quadratic

nodes.summary: Let $q$ and $N$ be natural numbers. If there is Manin degree data for $q$ and $N$, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$, computed in the integers.
nodes.title: Hasse bound from Manin degree data

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field with exactly three elements, let $W$ be any Weierstrass curve over $F$, and let $N$ be the number of nonsingular points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree data for $(3, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = 3$, $d(-1) = N$, $d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with $d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Manin degree data over the field with three elements

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve $y^2 = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_4 x + a_6$ over $F$ (that is, $a_1 = a_3 = 0$) with nonzero discriminant, and let $N$ be the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree data for $(q, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = q$, $d(-1) = N$, $d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for…
nodes.title: Manin degree data for the odd-characteristic normal form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve $y^2 = x^3 + a_2 x^2 + a_4 x + a_6$ over $F$ (that is, $a_1 = a_3 = 0$) with nonzero discriminant. If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.
nodes.title: Hasse bound for the odd-characteristic normal form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field with exactly two elements, let $W$ be any Weierstrass curve over $F$, and let $N$ be the number of nonsingular points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree data for $(2, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = 2$, $d(-1) = N$, $d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with $d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Manin degree data over the field with two elements

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field with exactly four elements, let $W$ be any Weierstrass curve over $F$, and let $N$ be the number of nonsingular points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity. Then there is Manin degree data for $(4, N)$: a function $d : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $d(0) = 4$, $d(-1) = N$, $d(n - 1) + d(n + 1) = 2 d(n) + 2$ for every integer $n$, and no integer $n$ with $d(n) = d(n + 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Manin degree data over the field with four elements

If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity, then…

If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field of characteristic $2$ with $q$ elements and let $W$ be a Weierstrass curve $y^2 + a_3 y = x^3 + a_4 x + a_6$ over $F$ (that is, $a_1 = a_2 = 0$) with nonzero discriminant. If $N$ is the number of points of $W$ over $F$, including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$.
nodes.title: Hasse bound for the supersingular characteristic-two normal form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $F$ given by a Weierstrass equation. If $N$ is the number of points of $E$ with coordinates in $F$, including the point at infinity, then $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Hasse bound

nodes.summary: Algebraic curves and their invariants, including divisors, the genus, Jacobians and the Abel–Jacobi map.
nodes.title: Algebraic curves
Divisors on curves
Divisors on a curve

nodes.summary: For a set $C$ (the points of a curve), a divisor on $C$ is a finitely supported function $D \colon C \to \mathbb{Z}$. Its support is the finite set of points $P \in C$ with $D(P) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Divisors on a curve

nodes.summary: For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and a point $P \in C$, the coefficient of $D$ at $P$ is the integer $D(P)$.
nodes.title: Coefficient of a divisor at a point
Effective parts of curve divisors

nodes.summary: For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is the divisor on $C$ whose coefficient at each point $P \in C$ is $\max(D(P), 0)$.
nodes.title: Zero part of a divisor

nodes.summary: For a divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is the divisor on $C$ whose coefficient at each point $P \in C$ is $\max(-D(P), 0)$.
nodes.title: Pole part of a divisor

nodes.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and every point $P \in C$, the coefficient at $P$ of the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is $\max(D(P), 0)$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of the zero part

nodes.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$ and every point $P \in C$, the coefficient at $P$ of the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is $\max(-D(P), 0)$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of the pole part

nodes.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the zero part $D^+$ of $D$ is effective: $D^+(P) \ge 0$ for every point $P \in C$.
nodes.title: The zero part of a divisor is effective

nodes.summary: For every divisor $D$ on a set of points $C$, the pole part $D^-$ of $D$ is effective: $D^-(P) \ge 0$ for every point $P \in C$.
nodes.title: The pole part of a divisor is effective

nodes.summary: For every set of points $C$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, let $D^+$ be its zero part, with coefficient $\max(D(P), 0)$ at each point $P$, and $D^-$ its pole part, with coefficient $\max(-D(P), 0)$ at each point $P$. Then $D^+ - D^- = D$.
nodes.title: A divisor is its zero part minus its pole part
Evaluation of curve divisors

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$ and a function $f : C \to G$, this is the monoid homomorphism from the group of divisors on $C$, written multiplicatively, to $G$ that sends a divisor $D$ to the finite product $\prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of divisors as a group homomorphism

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, a function $f : C \to G$ and a divisor $D$ on $C$, the evaluation of $D$ against $f$ is the element $f(D) = \prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a divisor against a function

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, the evaluation of $D$ against $f$ equals $\prod_{P \in \operatorname{supp} D} f(P)^{D(P)}$, the product over the points in the support of $D$.
nodes.title: Evaluation is a product over the support

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$ and every function $f : C \to G$, the evaluation of the zero divisor on $C$ against $f$ is the identity element $1$ of $G$.
nodes.title: The zero divisor evaluates to one

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$, every point $P \in C$ and every integer $n$, the divisor $n \cdot P$, with coefficient $n$ at $P$ and $0$ elsewhere, evaluates against $f$ to $f(P)^n$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a one-point divisor

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$ and all divisors $D_1, D_2$ on $C$, writing $f(D)$ for the evaluation of a divisor $D$ against $f$, we have $f(D_1 + D_2) = f(D_1) \, f(D_2)$.
nodes.title: Evaluation is multiplicative

nodes.summary: For a commutative group $G$, every function $f : C \to G$, every integer $n$ and every divisor $D$ on $C$, writing $f(D)$ for the evaluation of $D$ against $f$, we have $f(nD) = f(D)^n$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of an integer multiple
Jacobians of compact Riemann surfaces

nodes.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the genus of $X$ is a natural number.
nodes.title: Genus of a compact Riemann surface

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. The genus of $X$ is $0$ if and only if $X$ is homeomorphic to the unit sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.
nodes.title: A compact Riemann surface has genus zero iff it is a sphere

nodes.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a type in the same universe as $X$.
nodes.title: Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$. Each point $P \in X$ gives a map $X \to J(X)$, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.
nodes.title: Abel–Jacobi map

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$, and let $J(X)$ be its Jacobian, a complex manifold modelled on $\mathbb{C}^g$. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is holomorphic.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is holomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$, an abelian group. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to $0$.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$, and let $P \in X$. If the genus of $X$ is positive, then the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is injective.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is injective in positive genus

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(X)$ to $J(Y)$. It is meant to be the homomorphism induced by $f$; its properties are stated separately.
nodes.title: Pushforward on Jacobians

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, of genera $g_X$ and $g_Y$. The Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a complex-analytic manifold modeled on $\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$, and likewise $J(Y)$ on $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_* : J(X) \to J(Y)$ is holomorphic.
nodes.title: The pushforward on Jacobians is holomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforward of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$: $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(P) = P$.
nodes.title: Pushforward along the identity

nodes.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforwards satisfy $(g \circ f)_*(P) = g_*(f_*(P))$.
nodes.title: Pushforward respects composition

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pullback $f^*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(Y)$ to $J(X)$. It is meant to be the zero map when $f$ is constant and the usual pullback along $f$ otherwise; its…
nodes.title: Pullback on Jacobians

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces of genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, with Jacobians $J(X)$ and $J(Y)$, complex manifolds modelled on $\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$ and $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the induced pullback map $f^* : J(Y) \to J(X)$ is holomorphic.
nodes.title: The pullback map on Jacobians is holomorphic

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pullback of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$: $(\mathrm{id}_X)^*(P) = P$.
nodes.title: Pullback along the identity

nodes.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, and for a holomorphic map $h$ between compact Riemann surfaces write $h^*$ for the induced pullback map on Jacobians. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every point $P$ of the Jacobian $J(Z)$, we have $(g \circ f)^*(P) = f^*(g^*(P))$.
nodes.title: Pullback on Jacobians is compatible with composition

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact connected Hausdorff spaces with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. Every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ has a degree, which is a natural number.
nodes.title: Degree of a holomorphic map

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(Y)$ for the Jacobian of $Y$, an abelian group. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ and every $P \in J(Y)$, the pushforward along $f$ of the pullback of $P$ along $f$ is $\deg(f) \cdot P$, where the degree $\deg(f)$ is a natural number: $f_*(f^*(P)) = \deg(f) \cdot P$.
nodes.title: Pushforward of a pullback is multiplication by the degree
Jacobians of curves

nodes.summary: For a field $k$ and a curve $C$ over $k$, that is, a $k$-scheme that is proper, smooth of relative dimension $1$ and geometrically irreducible, the genus of $C$ is a natural number.
nodes.title: Genus of a smooth proper curve

nodes.summary: For a field $k$ and a curve $C$ over $k$, that is, a $k$-scheme that is proper, smooth of relative dimension $1$ and geometrically irreducible, the Jacobian $J(C)$ of $C$ is a $k$-scheme.
nodes.title: Jacobian of a smooth proper curve

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. The Jacobian $J(C)$ is smooth of relative dimension $g$ over $k$, where $g$ is the genus of $C$.
nodes.title: The Jacobian has dimension equal to the genus

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. Each $k$-rational point $P$ of $C$ gives a morphism of $k$-schemes $C \to J(C)$ from $C$ to its Jacobian, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.
nodes.title: Abel–Jacobi map

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$, let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian, and let $P$ be a $k$-rational point of $C$. The Abel–Jacobi map $C \to J(C)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to the identity point of $J(C)$ for its group scheme structure.
nodes.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$, let $J(C)$ be its Jacobian, let $P$ be a $k$-rational point of $C$, and let $\iota_P : C \to J(C)$ be the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$. Let $A$ be a group scheme over $k$ that is smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible. For every morphism of $k$-schemes $f : C \to A$ sending $P$ to the identity point of $A$, there is a unique…
nodes.title: Universal property of the Jacobian

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over a field $k$. The commutative group structure on the set of $k$-rational points of the Jacobian $J(C)$ is the one induced by its commutative group scheme structure: the product of two $k$-points $x$ and $y$ is $\mu \circ (x, y)$, where $\mu$ is the multiplication morphism of $J(C)$.
nodes.title: Group law on the rational points of the Jacobian

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $g$ and $d$, $c(g, d)$ is a natural number: the constant in the uniform bound on rational points of curves in Theorem 1.1 of Dimitrov, Gao and Habegger.
nodes.title: Uniform Mordell–Lang constant

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $g$ and $d$, the uniform constant satisfies $c(g, d) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The uniform Mordell–Lang constant is at least one

nodes.summary: Let $g \ge 2$ and $d \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $F$ be a number field with $[F : \mathbb{Q}] \le d$, and let $C$ be a proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over $F$. If $C$ has genus $g$, then the number of $F$-rational points of $C$, possibly infinite, is at most $c(g, d)^{1 + \rho}$, where $c$ is the uniform constant and $\rho$ is the free rank of the group of $F$-rational points of the Jacobian of…
nodes.title: Uniform Mordell–Lang for curves

Faltings's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. A place of $F/K$ is a valuation ring of $F$ containing $K$ and different from $F$: a $K$-subalgebra $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$ with $\mathcal{O} \neq F$ such that $z \in \mathcal{O}$ or $z^{-1} \in \mathcal{O}$ for every $z \in F$. See [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.1.4 and 1.1.8].
nodes.title: Place

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. For every $x \in F$, there are only finitely many places $P$ of $F/K$ whose valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_P$ does not contain $x$, that is, $x$ has only finitely many poles. See [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.3.4].
nodes.title: Finitely many poles

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. The adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ of $F/K$ is the restricted product of copies of $F$ indexed by the places $P$ of $F/K$, with respect to their valuation rings $\mathcal{O}_P$ and the cofinite filter: its elements are the families $\alpha = (\alpha_P)_P$ with $\alpha_P \in F$ for every place $P$ and $\alpha_P \in \mathcal{O}_P$ for all but finitely many $P$.…
nodes.title: Adele ring

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. The principal adele map is a ring homomorphism from $F$ to the adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ of $F/K$. It is meant to be the diagonal embedding sending $x \in F$ to the adele whose coordinate at every place $P$ of $F/K$ is $x$, which is well defined since $x$ has only finitely many poles; this coordinate…
nodes.title: Principal adele map

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. For every $x \in F$ and every place $P$ of $F/K$, the coordinate at $P$ of the principal adele of $x$ is $x$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of a principal adele

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. The algebra map $F \to \mathcal{A}_F$ of the $F$-algebra structure on the adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ equals the principal adele map $F \to \mathcal{A}_F$.
nodes.title: The adele algebra map is the principal embedding

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $K$ a field with $F$ a $K$-algebra. The integral adeles $\mathcal{A}_F(0)$ form the $K$-subspace of the adele ring $\mathcal{A}_F$ of $F/K$ consisting of the adeles $\alpha = (\alpha_P)_P$ whose coordinate $\alpha_P$ lies in the valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_P$ of $P$ for every place $P$ of $F/K$. See [Stichtenoth, Definition 1.5.3].
nodes.title: Integral adeles

nodes.summary: For a function field $F$ over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$, the genus of $F/K$ is a natural number $g$, specified by the separately stated formula $g = \dim_K \mathcal{A}_F / (\mathcal{A}_F(0) + F)$, where $\mathcal{A}_F$ is the adele ring and $\mathcal{A}_F(0)$ the integral adeles. See [Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.5.5].
nodes.title: Genus of a function field

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a function field over a field $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. The genus $g$ of $F/K$ equals the dimension over $K$ of the quotient $\mathcal{A}_F / (\mathcal{A}_F(0) + F)$, where $\mathcal{A}_F$ is the adele ring, $\mathcal{A}_F(0)$ the integral adeles, and $F$ is embedded in $\mathcal{A}_F$ by the algebra map of the $F$-algebra structure on the adeles (stated…
nodes.title: Genus as the dimension of the adele class space

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a number field and $F$ a function field over $K$, that is, a finite extension of the rational function field $K(t)$. If the genus of $F/K$ is at least $2$, then $F/K$ has only finitely many places of degree one, that is, places $P$ whose residue field (the quotient of the valuation ring of $P$ by its maximal ideal) has dimension $1$ over $K$.

Varieties over a field

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field. A scheme $X$ with a chosen structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ is a *variety* over $k$ if this morphism is separated, of finite type (quasi-compact and locally of finite type), and geometrically reduced.
nodes.title: Geometrically reduced variety over a field

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme with a structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$. Then $X$ is a variety over $k$ if and only if this structure morphism is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and geometrically reduced.
nodes.title: Characterization of varieties

nodes.summary: If $X$ is a variety over a field $k$, then its structure morphism $X \to \operatorname{Spec} k$ is quasi-separated, since it is separated.
nodes.title: Varieties are quasi-separated

nodes.title: Discrete geometry

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space and let $L \subseteq E$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule (an additive subgroup) that is discrete in the subspace topology. Then the $\mathbb{Z}$-rank of $L$ equals $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} E$ if and only if $L$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-lattice in $E$, that is, $L$ spans $E$ over $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: A discrete subgroup is a lattice iff it has full rank

nodes.summary: An infinite set of points in the plane with pairwise integer distances is collinear.
nodes.title: Erdős–Anning theorem

nodes.summary: Let $V$, $E$ and $F$ be finite sets, let $\iota : V \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be an injective map into Euclidean space, and let $P = \operatorname{conv} \iota(V)$ be the convex hull of its image; assume $P$ has nonempty interior $\operatorname{int} P$, and write $\partial P$ for its frontier. Each edge $e \in E$ has an ordered pair of endpoints $(s(e), t(e)) \in V \times V$, with segment $[e] = [\iota(s(e)), \iota(t(e))]$;…
nodes.title: Euler's polyhedron formula

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite set of subsets of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every member of $T$ is the convex hull of three points $a, b, c$ of the plane (not necessarily distinct), the union of the members of $T$ is the closed unit square $[0,1]^2$, any two distinct members of $T$ have disjoint interiors, and all members of $T$ have the same Lebesgue measure. Then the number of members of $T$ is even.
nodes.title: Monsky's theorem
Blumenthal's minimax angle problem

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, the minimax angle $\alpha_N$ is the supremum of the $\alpha \in [0, \pi]$ such that every set of $N$ points in the Euclidean plane contains three distinct points $x, y, z$ with $\angle xyz \ge \alpha$, where $\angle xyz$ is the unoriented angle at $y$.
nodes.title: Minimax angle

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, let $\alpha_N$ be the minimax angle of $N$ points in the plane: the supremum of the $\alpha \in [0, \pi]$ such that every set of $N$ points in the plane contains three distinct points $x, y, z$ with $\angle xyz \ge \alpha$ (the angle at $y$). The statement is Sendov's answer: $\alpha_3 = \pi/3$, $\alpha_4 = \pi/2$, and for all natural numbers $n \ge 2$ and $N$, if…
nodes.title: Blumenthal's minimax angle values (Erdős Problem 504)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $N$, let $\alpha_N$ be the minimax angle of $N$ points in the plane: the supremum of the $\alpha \in [0, \pi]$ such that every set of $N$ points in the plane contains three distinct points $x, y, z$ with $\angle xyz \ge \alpha$ (the angle at $y$). Then $\alpha_3 = \pi/3$, $\alpha_4 = \pi/2$, and for all natural numbers $n \ge 2$ and $N$: if $2^n < N \le 2^n + 2^{n-2}$, then…
nodes.title: Sendov's solution of Blumenthal's minimax angle problem (Erdős Problem 504)
Continuous Turán numbers of planar patterns

nodes.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f_X(x_0) - f_X(x_1) \ge x_0 - x_1$ whenever $x_0 > x_1$ are $x$-coordinates of points of $P$, $f_Y(y_0) - f_Y(y_1) \ge y_0 - y_1$ whenever $y_0 > y_1$ are $y$-coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_X(x), f_Y(y)) \in S$ for every $(x, y) \in P$.
nodes.title: Containment of planar point sets

nodes.summary: Every set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains the empty set $\emptyset$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets.
nodes.title: Every planar set contains the empty pattern

nodes.summary: For a real number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the continuous Turán number $\operatorname{opx}(n, P)$ is the supremum of the Lebesgue measures $\mu_2(S)$ over all open sets $S \subseteq [0, n]^2$ that do not contain $P$ in the sense of point-set pattern containment; it is $0$ when there is no such set.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number in the plane

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, \emptyset) = 0$: every set contains the empty pattern, so no set avoids it.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of the empty pattern

nodes.summary: For every real number $n$ and every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the value $\operatorname{opx}(n, P)$ does not change when $P$ is replaced by its image under the rotation by $90^\circ$, $(x, y) \mapsto (-y, x)$, under the reflection $(x, y) \mapsto (-x, y)$, or under the reflection $(x, y) \mapsto (x, -y)$.
nodes.title: Rotation and reflection invariance of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a real number, $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a set and $v \in \mathbb{R}^2$ a vector, and let $P + v = \{p + v : p \in P\}$ be the translate of $P$ by $v$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P + v) = \operatorname{opx}(n, P)$.
nodes.title: Translation invariance of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a real number and let $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. If $Q$ contains $P$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets, then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, Q)$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the continuous Turán number under containment

nodes.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and all real numbers $m \le n$, the continuous Turán numbers satisfy $\operatorname{opx}(m, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, P)$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the continuous Turán number in the side length

nodes.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and all real numbers $m, n > 0$, $\operatorname{opx}(m, P) + \operatorname{opx}(n, P) \le \operatorname{opx}(m + n, P)$.
nodes.title: Superadditivity of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $n, \delta$ be real numbers with $n > 0$ and $0 < \delta < n$. Then the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}$ satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) \le \mathrm{opx}(n + \delta, P)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n + \delta, P) < \mathrm{opx}(n, P) + 3 n \delta$.
nodes.title: Increment bound for the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ is a continuous function of $n$ on $(0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c, n$ be real numbers with $c \ge 0$, and let $S \subseteq [0, n]^2$ be an open set that does not contain the closed horizontal segment $[a, a + c] \times \{b\}$ in the sense of containment of planar point sets. Then for every $y \in [0, n]$ the horizontal section $\{x \in \mathbb{R} : (x, y) \in S\}$ has one-dimensional Lebesgue measure at most $c$.
nodes.title: Sections of open sets avoiding a horizontal segment

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and $(x_0, y_0) \in P$ with $x \le x_0$ for every $(x, y) \in P$, and let $c \ge 0$ and $n > 0$ be real numbers. Then
nodes.title: Extending a pattern by a horizontal segment at its right edge

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $(x_0, y_0) \in P$ be such that every point of $P$ has $x$-coordinate at most $x_0$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P \cup \{(x_0 + c, y_0)\}) \le \operatorname{opx}(n, P) + cn$ for all real numbers $c > 0$ and $n > 0$.
nodes.title: Adding a point to the right of a pattern

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be finite, and let $c > 0$ and $d$ be real numbers such that any two consecutive distinct $x$-coordinates of points of $P$ differ by at least $c$ and at most $d$, and likewise for $y$-coordinates. Let $q > 1$ and $qP = \{qp : p \in P\}$. Then for every real $n > 0$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, qP) \le (\lceil qd/c \rceil + 1)^2 \, \mathrm{opx}(m, P)$, where…
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a dilated finite pattern

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, c, n$ be real numbers with $0 \le c \le n$, and let $P = [a, a + c] \times \{b\}$ be the closed horizontal segment of length $c$ at height $b$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = cn$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a horizontal segment

nodes.summary: Let $a, b, n$ be real numbers with $0 < a \le n$ and $0 < b \le n$, and let $P$ be the closed segment from $(0, 0)$ to $(a, b)$. Then the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = (a + b)n - ab$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a diagonal segment

nodes.summary: For every nonempty open set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n^2)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Open patterns have quadratic continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty open set and let $Q_P$ be the set of points of $P$ both of whose coordinates are rational. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, Q_P) = \Theta(n^2)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Rational points of open patterns have quadratic continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $a > 0$ and $b$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be strictly increasing on $[0, a]$ with $(f(t) - f(s)) / (t - s) \le b$ for all $s < t$ in $[0, a]$. Then the graph $P = \{(t, f(t)) : t \in [0, a]\}$ satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of the graph of an increasing function

reading_title.source: Large sets of grid cells with no $r \times r$ all-ones submatrix

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$ there is a set $S$ of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ with $|S| \ge \frac{1}{2} n^{2 - 2/(r+1)}$ that contains no $r \times r$ all-ones submatrix: there are no sets $R, C \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with $|R| = |C| = r$ and $R \times C \subseteq S$.
nodes.title: Large sets of grid cells with no $r \times r$ all-ones submatrix

nodes.summary: Let $s > 0$ and $c > 0$ be real numbers and let $P_{s,2,c} = [0, s] \times \{c, 2c\}$ be the equal-sign pattern, two horizontal segments of length $s$ at heights $c$ and $2c$. Then, as the real number $n$ tends to infinity with $s$ and $c$ fixed, $\operatorname{opx}(n, P_{s,2,c}) = \Theta(s^{1/2} n^{3/2})$.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of the equal-sign pattern

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a natural number and let $c, n$ be real numbers with $c \ge 0$ and $ct \le n$. Let $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^t$ be the set of points $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{t-1})$ such that $y_i < n - ic$ for every $i$, $y_{i+1} + c < y_i$ for every $i < t - 1$, and $y_{t-1} > 0$ if $t \ge 1$. Then the $t$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $X$ is at least $(n/t - c)^t$, where $n/t$ is read as $0$ when $t = 0$.
nodes.title: Lower bound on the volume of a staircase region

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $s, c > 0$ be real numbers, and let $P_{s,t,c} = [0, s] \times \{c, 2c, \dots, tc\}$ be the union of the $t$ horizontal segments of length $s$ at heights $c, 2c, \dots, tc$. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P_{s,t,c}) = O(s^{1/t} n^{2 - 1/t})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity, with $s$, $t$ and $c$ fixed.
nodes.title: Upper bound for stacked horizontal segments

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $a_i \le b_i$ and $y_i$ be real numbers for $i = 1, \dots, k$, such that the intervals $[a_i, b_i]$ are pairwise disjoint and the heights $y_i$ are pairwise distinct, and let $P = \bigcup_{i=1}^k [a_i, b_i] \times \{y_i\}$. Then the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Linear bound for separated horizontal segments

nodes.summary: A set of cells $A \subseteq \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$, each cell written (column, row), contains a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ when there are maps $f_X, f_Y : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $f_X$ is strictly increasing on the set of $x$-coordinates of points of $P$, $f_Y$ is strictly increasing on the set of $y$-coordinates of points of $P$, and $(f_X(x), f_Y(y)) \in A$ for every $(x, y) \in P$.
nodes.title: Containment of a point pattern in a set of grid cells

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ is the largest number of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ forming a set that does not contain $P$ (cells contain $P$ when there are strictly increasing maps from the $x$-coordinates of $P$ to columns and from the $y$-coordinates of $P$ to rows that send every point of $P$ to a cell of the set), and $0$ if…
nodes.title: 0-1 matrix extremal function of a point pattern

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_\emptyset) = 0$, since every set of cells contains the empty pattern.
nodes.title: The extremal function of the empty pattern vanishes

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the 0-1 matrix extremal function of the one-point pattern $\{p\}$ on the $n \times n$ grid is zero: $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_{\{p\}}) = 0$. Indeed, a single point is contained in every nonempty set of cells.
nodes.title: The extremal function of a single point vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ a set, and let $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ be the largest number of cells of the $n \times n$ grid $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}^2$ forming a set that does not contain $P$ ($0$ if there is no such set). Then $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P) \le n^2$.
nodes.title: Trivial upper bound for the 0-1 matrix extremal function

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the inverse Ackermann function $\alpha(n)$ is the least natural number $k$ with $n \le A(k, k)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function, given for all natural numbers $m$ and $j$ by $A(0, j) = j + 1$, $A(m + 1, 0) = A(m, 1)$ and $A(m + 1, j + 1) = A(m, A(m + 1, j))$.
nodes.title: Inverse Ackermann function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, $n \le A(\alpha(n), \alpha(n))$, where $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function and $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.
nodes.title: Defining inequality of the inverse Ackermann function

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $k$, if $n \le A(k, k)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function, then $\alpha(n) \le k$, where $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function.
nodes.title: Upper bound for the inverse Ackermann function

nodes.summary: The inverse Ackermann function $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha(2) = 1$, since $A(0, 0) = 1 < 2 \le 3 = A(1, 1)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.
nodes.title: The inverse Ackermann function at 2

nodes.summary: The inverse Ackermann function $\alpha$ satisfies $\alpha(8) = 3$, since $A(2, 2) = 7 < 8 \le 61 = A(3, 3)$, where $A$ is the two-argument Ackermann function.
nodes.title: The inverse Ackermann function at 8

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then the continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P)$ and the 0-1 matrix extremal function $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P)$ of $P$ on the $n \times n$ grid satisfy $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P))$ as $n \to \infty$ through the natural numbers, with constants depending on $P$.
