nodes.title: Linear bound for permutation-like point patterns

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets of real numbers, let $P = X \times Y$ be the grid they span and let $t = |X|$ be its number of columns. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n^{2 - 1/t})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, where for $t = 0$ (so that $P$ is empty) the exponent $2 - 1/t$ is read as $2$.
nodes.title: Upper bound for the continuous Turán number of a grid

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be finite. Then there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the continuous Turán number satisfies $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n^{2 - \varepsilon})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Power saving for continuous Turán numbers of finite planar patterns

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets of real numbers with $|X| = 2$ and $|Y| \ge 2$, and let $P = X \times Y$ be the grid with $2$ columns and $|Y|$ rows. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n^{3/2})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a grid with two columns

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite sets of real numbers with $|X| = 3$ and $|Y| \ge 3$, and let $P = X \times Y$ be the grid with $3$ columns and $|Y|$ rows. Then $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = \Theta(n^{5/3})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Continuous Turán number of a grid with three columns

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set whose points have pairwise distinct $y$-coordinates. Then there is a natural number $t$ such that $\operatorname{opx}(n, P) = O(n \cdot 2^{\alpha(n)^t})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, where $\operatorname{opx}$ is the continuous Turán number and $\alpha$ is the inverse Ackermann function.

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $d$ and $n$ and every point $p \in \mathbb{R}^d$, $\operatorname{ex}(n, M_{\{p\}}, d) = 0$, since a single point is contained in every nonempty set of cells.
nodes.title: The $d$-dimensional extremal function of a single point vanishes

nodes.summary: Let $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. If $Q$ contains $P$, then $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, Q, d)$ for every real number $n$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers are monotone under containment

nodes.summary: For every set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and all real numbers $m \le n$, $\mathrm{opx}(m, P, d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers are monotone in the side length

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, and let $n, \varepsilon$ be real numbers with $n > 0$ and $0 < \varepsilon < n$. Then the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}$ satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n + \varepsilon, P, d)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n + \varepsilon, P, d) < \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) + d (2n)^{d-1} \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Increment bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$ and every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$ is a continuous function of $n$ on $(0, \infty)$.
nodes.title: Continuity of the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, $n$ a real number and $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, and let $\Pr(P)$ be the subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ obtained by dropping the last coordinate of every point of $P$. Writing $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q, k)$ for the $k$-dimensional continuous Turán number, we have $n \cdot \mathrm{opx}(n, \Pr(P), d) \le \mathrm{opx}(n, P, d + 1)$.
nodes.title: Projection bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ be a set whose points all have the same last coordinate, and let $\mathrm{Pr}(P) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be the set obtained by deleting the last coordinate of each point of $P$. Then for every real number $n$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d + 1) = n \cdot \mathrm{opx}(n, \mathrm{Pr}(P), d)$.
nodes.title: Patterns with a constant last coordinate

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a natural number and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty open set. Let $P' = P \times \{0\}^{m+1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{m+3}$, and let $Q_{P'}$ be the set of points of $P'$ all of whose coordinates are rational. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P'}, m + 3) = \Theta(n^{m+3})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Rational points of an embedded open planar set

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a nonempty open set, and let $Q_P$ be the set of points of $P$ all of whose coordinates are rational. Then, as the real number $n \to \infty$, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = \Theta(n^d)$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_P, d) = \Theta(n^d)$.
nodes.title: Nonempty open patterns in dimension at least two

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be finite and let $c_1, c_2, q, n$ be real numbers with $c_1 > 0$, $q > 1$ and $n > 0$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and all $p, p' \in P$ with $p_i < p'_i$ such that no $r \in P$ has $p_i < r_i < p'_i$, we have $c_1 \le p'_i - p_i \le c_2$. Let $qP = \{q p : p \in P\}$ and $m = \lceil q c_2 / c_1 \rceil + 1$. Then the $d$-dimensional continuous…
nodes.title: Dilation bound for the d-dimensional continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be finite. Then the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d)$ and the $d$-dimensional 0-1 matrix extremal function $\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P, d)$ of $P$ satisfy $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = \Theta(\mathrm{ex}(n, M_P, d))$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity, with constants depending on $P$.
nodes.title: Higher-dimensional continuous Turán numbers versus extremal functions

nodes.summary: For every $d$ there is a real number $C$ such that for every real $c > 0$ there is a real number $K$ with the following property. Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of $k$ points such that, for each coordinate $i$, distinct points of $P$ have distinct $i$-th coordinates and consecutive values of the $i$-th coordinate on $P$ differ by at most $c$. Then…
nodes.title: Upper bound for higher-dimensional permutation-type patterns

nodes.summary: Let $X_1, \dots, X_d$ be finite sets of real numbers, $k_i = |X_i|$, and $P = X_1 \times \dots \times X_d \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. Put $\alpha = \max_i k_i / \prod_i k_i$ if $d \ge 1$ and every $k_i$ is positive, and $\alpha = 0$ otherwise. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = O(n^{d - \alpha})$ as the natural number $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Upper bound for higher-dimensional grid patterns

parts: Power saving for continuous Turán numbers of finite patterns in
reading_title.source: Power saving for continuous Turán numbers of finite patterns in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be finite. Then there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the $d$-dimensional continuous Turán number satisfies $\mathrm{opx}(n, P, d) = O(n^{d - \varepsilon})$ as the natural number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Power saving for continuous Turán numbers of finite patterns in $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite set of at least two points with pairwise distinct $x$-coordinates and pairwise distinct $y$-coordinates, and for $i \in \{2, 3\}$ let $P_i = \{(x, y, j) : (x, y) \in P,\ j \in \{1, \dots, i\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then, as $n$ tends to infinity through the natural numbers, $\mathrm{opx}(n, P_2, 3) = \Theta(n^{5/2})$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n, P_3, 3) = \Theta(n^{8/3})$.
nodes.title: Stacked permutation patterns in three dimensions

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$ and $t \ge 2$ be natural numbers and let $c > 0$. For $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ let $Q_{P,t,c} = \{(x, ic) : x \in P,\ i \in \{1, \dots, t\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$. Then there is a real constant $K$, depending only on $d$, $t$ and $c$, such that for every $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and every real $n > 0$,…
nodes.title: Upper bound for continuous Turán numbers of stacked patterns

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ have at least two points, and suppose that $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity. Let $c > 0$ and $Q_{P,2,c} = \{(x, y, z) : (x, y) \in P,\ z \in \{c, 2c\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,2,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{5/2})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Two-layer stacks of patterns with linear continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contain three points with pairwise distinct $x$-coordinates, and suppose that $\mathrm{opx}(n, P) = O(n)$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity. Let $c > 0$ and $Q_{P,3,c} = \{(x, y, z) : (x, y) \in P,\ z \in \{c, 2c, 3c\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,3,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{8/3})$ as the real number $n$ tends to infinity.
nodes.title: Three-layer stacks of patterns with linear continuous Turán number

nodes.summary: Let $a > 0$, $b$ and $c > 0$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be strictly increasing on $[0, a]$ with $(f(t) - f(s)) / (t - s) \le b$ whenever $0 \le s < t \le a$. Let $P = \{(t, f(t)) : t \in [0, a]\}$ be the graph of $f$ over $[0, a]$ and, for $k \ge 1$, let $Q_{P,k,c} = \{(x, y, ic) : (x, y) \in P,\ i \in \{1, \dots, k\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then, as the real number $n \to \infty$,…
nodes.title: Stacked graphs of increasing functions in three dimensions

nodes.summary: Let $r > 0$ and $c > 0$, let $P = \{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| \le r,\ |y| \le r,\ x = 0 \text{ or } y = 0\}$ be the plus sign of size $r$, and for $t \in \{2, 3\}$ let $Q_{P,t,c} = \{(x, y, ic) : (x, y) \in P,\ i \in \{1, \dots, t\}\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Then, as the real number $n$ tends to infinity, $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,2,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{5/2})$ and $\mathrm{opx}(n, Q_{P,3,c}, 3) = \Theta(n^{8/3})$.
nodes.title: Stacked plus signs in three dimensions
Dehn invariant

nodes.summary: The Dehn group is the tensor product $\mathbb{R} \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} (\mathbb{R} / 2\pi\mathbb{Z})$ of abelian groups; it is the target of the Dehn invariant.
nodes.title: Dehn group

nodes.summary: An edge, as recorded for the Dehn invariant, is a pair of real numbers: its length and its dihedral angle in radians. No positivity or range condition is imposed on either.
nodes.title: Edge of a polyhedron

nodes.summary: The Dehn invariant of a list of edges is the sum, over the edges, of $\ell \otimes \theta$ in the Dehn group, where $\ell$ is the length of the edge and $\theta$ its dihedral angle taken modulo $2\pi$.
nodes.title: Dehn invariant

nodes.summary: The real number $\arccos(1/3)$, the dihedral angle of a regular tetrahedron in radians.
nodes.title: Dihedral angle of the regular tetrahedron

nodes.summary: For a real number $\ell$, the edge list of a cube of side $\ell$ consists of $12$ edges, each of length $\ell$ with dihedral angle $\pi / 2$.
nodes.title: Edge list of a cube

nodes.summary: For a real number $\ell$, the edge list of a regular tetrahedron with edge length $\ell$ is the list of $6$ edges, each of length $\ell$ and dihedral angle $\arccos(1/3)$.
nodes.title: Edge list of the regular tetrahedron

nodes.summary: The empty list of edges has Dehn invariant $0$.
nodes.title: Dehn invariant of the empty edge list

nodes.summary: Let $e$ be an edge of length $\ell$ and dihedral angle $\theta$, and let $L$ be a list of edges. Then the Dehn invariant of the list obtained by putting $e$ in front of $L$ equals $\ell \otimes \theta$ plus the Dehn invariant of $L$, where $\theta$ is taken modulo $2\pi$.
nodes.title: The Dehn invariant splits off the first edge

nodes.summary: For lists of edges $L_1$ and $L_2$, the Dehn invariant of the concatenation of $L_1$ and $L_2$ is the sum of the Dehn invariants of $L_1$ and $L_2$.
nodes.title: Additivity of the Dehn invariant under concatenation

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an edge of length $\ell$ and dihedral angle $\theta$, the Dehn invariant of the list consisting of $n$ copies of that edge is $n \cdot (\ell \otimes \theta)$ in the Dehn group, where $\theta$ is taken modulo $2\pi$.
nodes.title: Dehn invariant of a repeated edge

reading_title.source: A $\mathbb{Q}$-linear functional separating $\alpha$ from $\pi$

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a real number such that $\alpha / \pi$ is irrational. Then there is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(\pi) = 0$ and $f(\alpha) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: A $\mathbb{Q}$-linear functional separating $\alpha$ from $\pi$

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ and $\alpha$ be real numbers with $\ell \neq 0$ and $\alpha / \pi$ irrational. Then the pure tensor $\ell \otimes [\alpha]$ is nonzero in the Dehn group $\mathbb{R} \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} (\mathbb{R} / 2\pi\mathbb{Z})$, where $[\alpha]$ is the class of $\alpha$ modulo $2\pi$.
nodes.title: Nonvanishing of an edge term in the Dehn group

nodes.summary: For every real number $\ell$, the edge list of a cube of side $\ell$ (twelve edges of length $\ell$, each with dihedral angle $\pi / 2$) has Dehn invariant $0$.
nodes.title: The Dehn invariant of the cube is zero

nodes.summary: Suppose that $\arccos(1/3) / \pi$ is irrational. Then for every nonzero real number $\ell$, the edge list of a regular tetrahedron of side $\ell$ (six edges of length $\ell$, each with dihedral angle $\arccos(1/3)$) has nonzero Dehn invariant.
nodes.title: Nonzero Dehn invariant of the regular tetrahedron, conditional on irrationality

nodes.summary: Suppose that $\arccos(1/3) / \pi$ is irrational. Then for all real numbers $\ell$ and $\ell'$ with $\ell' \ne 0$, the edge list of a cube of side $\ell$ and the edge list of a regular tetrahedron of side $\ell'$ have different Dehn invariants.
nodes.title: Conditionally, the cube and the regular tetrahedron have different Dehn invariants
Distinct and unit distances

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite set of points in a metric space and let $d$ be a real number. The multiplicity of $d$ in $P$ is the number of unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$ of distinct points of $P$ with $\operatorname{dist}(p, q) = d$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a distance

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S$ of points in a metric space, the number of unit distances of $S$ is the number of unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$ of points of $S$ with $\operatorname{dist}(p, q) = 1$, that is, the multiplicity of the distance $1$ in $S$.
nodes.title: Number of unit distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in a metric space, the distance set of $P$ is the finite set of real numbers $\operatorname{dist}(p, q)$ with $p$ and $q$ distinct points of $P$.
nodes.title: Distance set of a finite point set

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in a metric space, the number of distinct distances of $P$ is the number of elements of its distance set, that is, the number of distinct values $\operatorname{dist}(p, q)$ with $p$ and $q$ distinct points of $P$.
nodes.title: Number of distinct distances

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space and $n$ a natural number such that $X$ contains a set of exactly $n$ points. The minimum number of distinct distances for $n$ points in $X$ is the least number of distinct distances determined by a set of exactly $n$ points of $X$.
nodes.title: Minimum number of distinct distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in a metric space and a point $x$ of the space, this is the number of distinct values $\operatorname{dist}(y, x)$ with $y$ a point of $P$ other than $x$.
nodes.title: Number of distinct distances from a point

nodes.summary: For a finite set of $n$ points in a metric space, the number of unit distances is at most $\binom{n}{2}$, the total number of unordered pairs of distinct points.
nodes.title: Trivial upper bound on unit distances

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real constant $C$ such that for every nonempty finite set $A$ of points of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^4$ and every natural number $f$, if for every $x \in A$ there is a real number $r > 0$ such that at least $f$ points of $A$ lie at distance $r$ from $x$, then $f \le |A|/2 + C$. Equivalently, $f(n) \le n/2 + O(1)$, where $f(n)$ is the largest $f$ such that some set $A$ of…
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 754

reading_title.source: Erdős Problem 754: favourite distances in $\mathbb{R}^4$

nodes.summary: There is a real constant $C$ such that for every nonempty finite set $A$ of points of the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^4$ and every natural number $f$, if for every $x \in A$ there is a real number $r > 0$ such that at least $f$ points of $A$ lie at distance $r$ from $x$, then $f \le |A|/2 + C$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 754: favourite distances in $\mathbb{R}^4$

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real constant $C$ such that for every sufficiently large natural number $n$ there is a set $P$ of $n$ points of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every $4$-element subset of $P$ determines at least $3$ distinct distances and $P$ determines at most $C n / \sqrt{\log n}$ distinct distances.
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 659

nodes.summary: There is a real constant $C$ such that for every sufficiently large natural number $n$ there is a set $P$ of $n$ points of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every $4$-element subset of $P$ determines at least $3$ distinct distances and $P$ determines at most $C n / \sqrt{\log n}$ distinct distances.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 659: few distances with every four points spanning three

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a real number $\delta$, this is the number of unordered pairs $\{p, q\}$ of distinct points $p, q \in P$ with Euclidean distance $|p - q| = \delta$, computed as half the number of ordered pairs $(p, q)$ of distinct points of $P$ at distance $\delta$ and taken as a real number.
nodes.title: Number of pairs at a given distance

nodes.summary: The proposition that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there are a set $P$ of $n$ distinct points on the unit sphere $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \|x\| = 1\}$ and a real number $\delta$ for which the number of unordered pairs of distinct points of $P$ at distance $\delta$ is at least $f(n) \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 605 (repeated distances on the sphere)

nodes.summary: There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there are a set $P$ of $n$ distinct points on the unit sphere $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \|x\| = 1\}$ and a real number $\delta$ for which the number of unordered pairs of distinct points of $P$ at distance $\delta$ is at least $f(n) \cdot n$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 605 is true

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, the unit distance count of $P$ is the number of unordered pairs of points of $P$ at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Unit distance count of a planar point set

nodes.summary: There is a real number $\delta > 0$ such that for every natural number $N$ there are an integer $n \ge N$ and a set $P$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with at least $n^{1+\delta}$ unordered pairs of points of $P$ at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Erdős's unit distance conjecture is false

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, the number of unit-distance pairs of $P$ is the number of unordered pairs of points of $P$ at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Number of unit-distance pairs in a planar point set

nodes.summary: There is a constant $C > 0$ such that every finite set of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ has at most $C n^{4/3}$ unordered pairs of points at distance exactly $1$.
nodes.title: Spencer–Szemerédi–Trotter unit distance bound

nodes.summary: The real Euclidean plane is the space $\mathbb{R}^2$ of pairs of real numbers with the Euclidean inner product and norm.
nodes.title: Euclidean plane for Erdős Problem 652

nodes.summary: For a finite set $X$ of points in the Euclidean plane and a real number $t$, the number of points $x \in X$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $t$.
nodes.title: Points with few distinct distances

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and a real number $c$, the property that some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane contains at least $k$ points $x$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $c\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.title: Many points with few distinct distances

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is admissible for $k \in \mathbb{N}$ if there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean plane contains at least $k$ points $x$ such that the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $X$ is less than $c\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.title: Admissible constants in Erdős Problem 652

For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\alpha_k$ be the infimum of the reals $c$ for which there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ some set $X$ of exactly $n$ points in the plane has at least $k$ points $x$ with $R_X(x) < c\sqrt{n}$ (an empty set or a set unbounded below…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 652 is true

nodes.summary: For a finite set $A$ of points in the Euclidean plane and a natural number $k$, the rich distances of $A$ at level $k$ are the distances $d$ between two distinct points of $A$ such that at least $k$ unordered pairs of distinct points of $A$ are at distance $d$.
nodes.title: Rich distances

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the largest, over all sets $A$ of $n$ points in the Euclidean plane, of the number of rich distances of $A$ at level $n + 1$, that is, of distances that occur for at least $n + 1$ unordered pairs of distinct points of $A$.
nodes.title: Maximal number of rich distances

nodes.summary: For a finite set $A$ of points in the Euclidean plane, call a distance $k$-rich for $A$ if at least $k$ unordered pairs of distinct points of $A$ lie at that distance, and let $f(n)$ be the largest number of $(n+1)$-rich distances of a set of $n$ points. This is the assertion that there is a constant $C$ with $n \le C f(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$; that for every $n$ there is a set of $n$ points with at…

Then there is a constant $C$ with $n \le C f(n)$ for all sufficiently large $n$; for every $n$ there is a set of $n$ points with at least $\lfloor n/4 \rfloor$…

Convex and general position of point sets

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a ternary relation on a type $\alpha$ and let $s \subseteq \alpha$. The relation $r$ holds triplewise on $s$ if $r(x, y, z)$ holds for all pairwise distinct $x, y, z \in s$.
nodes.title: Relation holding triplewise on a set

nodes.summary: A set $A$ of points in the plane is non-trilinear if no three distinct points of $A$ lie on a common line.
nodes.title: Sets with no three collinear points

reading_title.source: Sets with no $n$ collinear points

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of points in a Euclidean affine space has no $n$ collinear points if no subset of $S$ consisting of exactly $n$ points is collinear.
nodes.title: Sets with no $n$ collinear points

reading_title.source: Sets containing a convex $n$-gon

nodes.summary: A set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ contains a convex $n$-gon if there is a set $S \subseteq P$ of exactly $n$ points that is convex independent: no point of $S$ lies in the convex hull of the other points of $S$.
nodes.title: Sets containing a convex $n$-gon

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space. Points $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1} \in P$ form a counterclockwise convex polygon if for all indices $i < j < k$ the oriented angle $\measuredangle p_i p_j p_k$ at $p_j$ has sign $-1$, that is, $p_i, p_j, p_k$ are not collinear and lie in counterclockwise order with respect to the orientation of $P$. Every list of at most two points qualifies.
nodes.title: Counterclockwise convex polygons

nodes.summary: Points $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$ of an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space form a convex polygon if one of the lists $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{n-1}$ and $p_0, p_{n-1}, p_{n-2}, \dots, p_1$ is a counterclockwise convex polygon: for any three of its entries $q, r, s$, in the order in which they occur in that list, the oriented angle $\measuredangle q r s$ at $r$ has sign $-1$. Thus for $n \ge 3$ the points are the…
nodes.title: Convex polygons

nodes.summary: If three points $A, B, C$ of an oriented two-dimensional Euclidean affine space are affinely independent, then $A, B, C$ form a convex polygon.
nodes.title: Affinely independent triples are convex polygons

nodes.summary: Let $\omega$ be the area form of the given orientation of the Euclidean plane, so that $\omega(u, v)$ is the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by the vectors $u$ and $v$. For points $a$, $b$, $c$ of the plane, the oriented area of the triangle with vertices $a$, $b$, $c$ is the real number $\omega(a - c, b - c) / 2$.
nodes.title: Oriented triangle area

nodes.summary: For a finite set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ and a point $x \in X$, let $R_X(x)$ be the number of distinct distances $\lvert y - x \rvert$ from $x$ to the points $y \in X$ other than $x$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $g(n)$ is the maximum, over all sets $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of exactly $n$ points, of the number of distinct values among the numbers $R_X(x)$ with $x \in X$.
nodes.title: Maximum number of distinct distance counts

nodes.summary: A set $X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, finite or infinite, is in _general position_ if no three distinct points of $X$ are collinear and no four distinct points of $X$ lie on a common circle.
nodes.title: Points in general position

nodes.summary: Points $a, b, c$ of a Euclidean affine space are the vertices of a right-angled triangle if they are pairwise distinct and the unoriented angle at one of the three vertices equals $\pi / 2$: $\angle bac = \pi / 2$, $\angle abc = \pi / 2$ or $\angle bca = \pi / 2$.
nodes.title: Right-angled triangles

nodes.summary: Points $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{R}^2$ are the vertices, in counterclockwise order, of an isosceles trapezoid if they are in strictly convex position and listed counterclockwise (for any three of them $p, q, r$, in the order in which they occur in the list $a, b, c, d$, the oriented angle $\measuredangle p q r$ at $q$ has sign $-1$), the line through $a$ and $b$ is parallel to the line through $c$ and $d$ (the two…
nodes.title: Isosceles trapezoids

nodes.summary: A set $A$ in a space with a distance function $d$ is isosceles-free if there are no three distinct points $x, y, z \in A$ such that two of the distances $d(x, y)$, $d(y, z)$, $d(z, x)$ are equal.
nodes.title: Isosceles-free sets

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a division ring and $P$ an affine space over $k$. A family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of $P$ is in general position through dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$ if for every finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ of at most $d + 1$ indices, the subfamily $(p_i)_{i \in S}$ is affinely independent over $k$.
nodes.title: General position of affine points

nodes.summary: If a family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of an affine space over a division ring $k$ is affinely independent over $k$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$ for every $d \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Affinely independent families are in general position

nodes.summary: Let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If a family of points of an affine space over a division ring $k$ is in general position through dimension $e$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$.
nodes.title: General position in affine space is monotone in the dimension

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a division ring and $V$ a vector space over $k$, with projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$. A family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of $\mathbb{P}(V)$ is in general position through dimension $d \in \mathbb{N}$ if for every finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ of at most $d + 1$ indices, the subfamily $(p_i)_{i \in S}$ is projectively independent.
nodes.title: General position of projective points

nodes.summary: If a family $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$ of a vector space $V$ over a division ring $k$ is projectively independent, then it is in general position through dimension $d$ for every $d \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Projectively independent families are in general position

nodes.summary: Let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If a family of points of the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$ of a vector space $V$ over a division ring $k$ is in general position through dimension $e$, then it is in general position through dimension $d$.
nodes.title: General position in projective space is monotone in the dimension

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $f_k(n)$ is the least natural number $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others). If there is no such $m$, then $f_k(n) = 0$.
nodes.title: Convex position threshold

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ let $f_k(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others), with $f_k(n) = 0$ if there is no such $m$. The claim is that for every $k \ge 2$ there is a real $c > 0$ with $(1 + c)^n < f_k(n)$ for all…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 651: exponential growth of convex position thresholds

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ let $f_k(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every set of $m$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ in general position (any at most $k + 1$ of them affinely independent) contains $n$ points in convex position (none of them in the convex hull of the others), with $f_k(n) = 0$ if there is no such $m$. It is not the case that for every $k \ge 2$ there is a real $c > 0$ with $(1 + c)^n < f_k(n)$ for all…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 651 has a negative answer
Equiangular lines

nodes.summary: For a real number $\alpha$ and a natural number $d$, an equiangular system with inner product $\pm\alpha$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of unit vectors in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space such that any two distinct vectors $x$ and $y$ in it satisfy $|\langle x, y \rangle| = \alpha$.
nodes.title: Equiangular systems of unit vectors

nodes.summary: For a real number $\alpha$ and a natural number $d$, $N_\alpha(d)$ is the supremum, taken in $\mathbb{N}$, of the cardinalities of the equiangular systems of unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with inner product $\pm\alpha$. Here an infinite set counts as having cardinality $0$, and a set of natural numbers that is not bounded above has supremum $0$.
nodes.title: Maximum number of equiangular lines

nodes.summary: For a real number $\lambda$, the spectral radius order $k(\lambda) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least natural number $k$ such that some simple graph on $k$ vertices has an adjacency matrix with spectral radius $\max(\lambda, 0)$, and $k(\lambda) = \infty$ if there is no such graph.
nodes.title: Spectral radius order

nodes.summary: Fix a real number $\alpha$ with $0 < \alpha < 1$, let $\lambda = (1 - \alpha)/(2\alpha)$ and let $k = k(\lambda)$ be the spectral radius order of $\lambda$. Let $N_\alpha(d)$ be the maximum number of equiangular lines in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with common angle $\arccos \alpha$. Then: (a) if $k < \infty$, then $N_\alpha(d) = \lfloor k(d - 1)/(k - 1) \rfloor$ for all sufficiently large $d$; (b) if $k = \infty$, then…
nodes.title: Equiangular lines with a fixed angle
Equilateral triangles in planar point sets

nodes.summary: For a real number $s$, a finite set $T$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is an equilateral triangle of side $s$ when $T$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct points of $T$ are at distance $s$.
nodes.title: Equilateral triangle with given side

nodes.summary: A finite set $T$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a unit equilateral triangle when it is an equilateral triangle of side $1$: $T$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct points of $T$ are at distance $1$.
nodes.title: Unit equilateral triangle

nodes.summary: A finite set $T$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$ is an equilateral triangle of any size when there is a real number $s > 0$ such that $T$ is an equilateral triangle of side $s$: $T$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct points of $T$ are at distance $s$.
nodes.title: Equilateral triangle of any size

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, this is the number of three-element subsets of $P$ that are unit equilateral triangles, that is, whose three points are pairwise at distance $1$.
nodes.title: Number of unit equilateral triangles in a point set

nodes.summary: For a finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, this is the number of three-element subsets of $P$ that are equilateral triangles of some positive side length $s$, that is, whose three points are pairwise at distance $s$.
nodes.title: Number of equilateral triangles in a point set

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $n$, $T_1(d, n)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$, over all sets $P$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, of the number of unit equilateral triangles spanned by $P$ (the three-element subsets of $P$ whose points are pairwise at distance $1$). When such sets exist this is the largest such number; when none exist (only for $d = 0$ and $n \ge 2$) it is $0$.
nodes.title: Maximum number of unit equilateral triangles

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $n$, $T(d, n)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$, over all sets $P$ of exactly $n$ points in the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^d$, of the number of equilateral triangles of positive side length spanned by $P$ (the three-element subsets of $P$ whose points are pairwise at the same positive distance). When such sets exist this is the largest such number; when none exist (only for $d = 0$ and…
nodes.title: Maximum number of equilateral triangles

nodes.summary: Let $T_1(n)$ be the largest number of unit equilateral triangles spanned by a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^6$, and let $T(n)$ be the largest number of equilateral triangles of positive side length spanned by a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^6$; a triangle spanned by a set is a three-element subset of it whose points are pairwise at the same distance. The statement asserts both of the following: there is a…
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 755

nodes.summary: Let $T_1(n)$ be the largest number of unit equilateral triangles spanned by a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^6$, and let $T(n)$ be the largest number of equilateral triangles of positive side length spanned by a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^6$; a triangle spanned by a set is a three-element subset of it whose points are pairwise at the same distance. Then there is a function $o : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 755 holds (Clemen–Dumitrescu–Liu)
Kakeya sets in finite fields

nodes.summary: For a type $F$ and a natural number $d$, $F^d$ denotes the set of $d$-tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_d)$ of elements of $F$, that is, functions from a $d$-element index set to $F$.
nodes.title: Coordinate space

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $d$ a natural number. For $x, y \in F^d$, the dot product is $x \cdot y = \sum_{i} x_i y_i \in F$, the sum running over the $d$ coordinates.
nodes.title: Dot product

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $d$ a natural number. For $y, x \in F^d$, the affine line with base point $y$ and direction $x$ is the set $\{y + a x : a \in F\} \subseteq F^d$. When $x = 0$ this set is the single point $\{y\}$.
nodes.title: Affine line

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $d$ a natural number. A set $K \subseteq F^d$ is a Kakeya set if for every $x \in F^d$ there is $y \in F^d$ such that the affine line $\{y + a x : a \in F\}$ is contained in $K$; that is, $K$ contains a line in every direction.
nodes.title: Kakeya set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $d$ a natural number and $K \subseteq F^d$. A function $\mu : F^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a probability measure on $K$ if $\mu(x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in F^d$, $\sum_{x \in F^d} \mu(x) = 1$, and $\mu(x) \ne 0$ implies $x \in K$.
nodes.title: Probability measure supported on a set

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field, $d$ a natural number and $\chi$ an additive character of $F$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. For $\mu : F^d \to \mathbb{R}$ and $\xi \in F^d$, the Fourier transform of $\mu$ at $\xi$ is $\hat{\mu}(\xi) = \sum_{x \in F^d} \chi(-\xi \cdot x)\, \mu(x) \in \mathbb{C}$, where $\xi \cdot x$ is the dot product.
nodes.title: Finite-field Fourier transform

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements, let $d \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $K \subseteq F^d$ be a Kakeya set and let $\chi$ be a nontrivial additive character of $F$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. Then, first, there is a probability measure $\mu$ on $K$ whose Fourier transform $\hat{\mu}$ with respect to $\chi$ satisfies $|\hat{\mu}(\xi)| \le q^{-1}$ for every nonzero $\xi \in F^d$. Second, this bound is…
nodes.title: Fraser's Fourier decay theorem for finite-field Kakeya sets

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real number $c > 0$ such that for every finite field $F$ and every Kakeya set $E \subseteq F^3$, that is, a set such that for every $x \in F^3$ there is $y \in F^3$ with $\{y + a x : a \in F\} \subseteq E$, we have $|E| \ge c\,|F|^3$.
nodes.title: Statement of the finite field Kakeya bound in dimension three

nodes.summary: There is a real number $c > 0$ such that for every finite field $F$ and every Kakeya set $E \subseteq F^3$, that is, a set such that for every $x \in F^3$ there is $y \in F^3$ with $\{y + a x : a \in F\} \subseteq E$, we have $|E| \ge c\,|F|^3$.
nodes.title: Finite field Kakeya sets in dimension three have cubic size
Lattice points in dilated regions

nodes.summary: For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, the integer unit cube at $v$ is the half-open cube $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the set of $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $v_i \le x_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Integer unit cube

nodes.summary: For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $x$ lies in the integer unit cube at $v$ if and only if $v_i \le x_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Membership in an integer unit cube

nodes.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and a real number $t$, the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ is the set of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ such that $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for some $x$ in the integer unit cube $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. For $t > 0$ these are the $v$ with $Q_v$ meeting $tS$; for $t = 0$ the division is read as $x_i/0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Outer cube set

nodes.summary: For $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, $v$ belongs to the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ if and only if $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for some $x$ in the integer unit cube at $v$.
nodes.title: Membership in the outer cube set

nodes.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and a real number $t$, the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ is the set of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ such that $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for every $x$ in the integer unit cube $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. For $t > 0$ these are the $v$ with $Q_v \subseteq tS$; for $t = 0$ the division is read as $x_i/0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Inner cube set

nodes.summary: For $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in \mathbb{R}$ and $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$, $v$ belongs to the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ if and only if $(x_1/t, \dots, x_n/t) \in S$ for every $x$ in the integer unit cube at $v$.
nodes.title: Membership in the inner cube set

nodes.summary: For every set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and every real $t$, the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$ is contained in the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$.
nodes.title: Inner cube indices are outer cube indices

nodes.summary: If $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is bounded and $t > 0$, then the outer cube set of $S$ at scale $t$, the set of $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ whose integer unit cube $\prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$ meets $tS$, is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the outer cube set

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be bounded, let $t > 0$, and let $\mathrm{vol}(S)$ be the Lebesgue (outer) measure of $S$, which is finite. For $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ let $Q_v = \prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$. Let $I$ be the inner cube set of $S$ at scale $t$, the $v$ with $Q_v \subseteq tS$, and $O$ the outer cube set, the $v$ with $Q_v$ meeting $tS$. Then $|I| \le \mathrm{vol}(S)\, t^n \le |O|$.
nodes.title: Cubical measure sandwich

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is the $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule of $\mathbb{R}^d$ (the real-valued functions on $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$) spanned by the standard basis vectors $e_0, \dots, e_{d-1}$.
nodes.title: The standard integer lattice

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the standard lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the integer span of the standard basis vectors of $\mathbb{R}^d$, exactly when every coordinate $x_i$ of $x$ is an integer.
nodes.title: Membership in the standard lattice

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t$, this is the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Lattice points in a dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t$, this is the number of elements of the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$, where an infinite set is assigned the value $0$.
nodes.title: Lattice-point count of a real dilate

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real $t$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the translated lattice-point set is $((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$, the set of points of the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $t \cdot P$ translated by $x$.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point set

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real $t$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the translated lattice-point count is the number of elements of the translated lattice-point set $((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$, taken to be $0$ when this set is infinite.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point count for arbitrary sets

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t > 0$, this is the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$.
nodes.title: Lattice points in a positive dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t > 0$, the lattice-point enumerator $L_P(t)$ is the number of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$, that is, $L_P(t) = |(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$.
nodes.title: Lattice-point enumerator

nodes.summary: For $d \in \mathbb{N}$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real $t > 0$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, this is the set $((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $t \cdot P$ translated by $x$. No boundedness of $P$ is assumed.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point set at a positive dilation

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, let $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded set, let $t > 0$ be real and let $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$. The translated lattice-point enumerator is $F_{t,P}(x) = |((t \cdot P) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$, the number of points of the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $t \cdot P$ translated by $x$.
nodes.title: Translated lattice-point enumerator of a bounded set

nodes.summary: For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the origin of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the standard integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$.
nodes.title: The origin is a lattice point

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$ and every real number $t$, the lattice-point count of the empty set $\emptyset \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ at the dilate $t$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The lattice-point count of the empty set vanishes

nodes.summary: For every $d \in \mathbb{N}$, every real $t$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the translated lattice-point count $|((t \cdot \emptyset) + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The translated lattice-point count of the empty set is zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and any real number $t$, the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $t > 0$, the set $(tP) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the dilate $tP = \{tp : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a positive dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, any real number $t$ and a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the set $(tP + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the translated dilate $tP + x = \{tp + x : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a translated dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a bounded set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, a real number $t > 0$ and a vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the set $(tP + x) \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ of points of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in the translated dilate $tP + x = \{tp + x : p \in P\}$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the lattice points in a translated positive dilate

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, the closed unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ is the set of points $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $0 \le x_i \le 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: The unit cube

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space and $d$ a natural number. A set $B \subseteq X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable if there are a natural number $n$ (possibly $0$) and Lipschitz maps $f_1, \dots, f_n : [0, 1]^d \to X$ out of the closed unit cube $[0, 1]^d \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ such that $B$ equals the union of their images, $B = f_1([0, 1]^d) \cup \dots \cup f_n([0, 1]^d)$.
nodes.title: Lipschitz parametrizable sets

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d$, the origin of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the closed unit cube $[0, 1]^d$.
nodes.title: The origin lies in the unit cube

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. For every natural number $d$, the empty subset of $X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable, via the empty family of maps.
nodes.title: The empty set is Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. For every natural number $d$ and every point $x \in X$, the set $\lbrace x \rbrace$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable, via a single constant map.
nodes.title: Singletons are Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space and $d$ a natural number. Every finite set $s$ of points of $X$, given as a finset, is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable.
nodes.title: Finsets are Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a metric space. Every finite set $B \subseteq X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable for every natural number $d$.
nodes.title: Finite sets are Lipschitz parametrizable

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be metric spaces, let $d$ be a natural number and let $f : X \to Y$ be a Lipschitz map. If a set $B \subseteq X$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable, then its image $f(B) \subseteq Y$ is $d$-Lipschitz parametrizable.
nodes.title: Lipschitz images of Lipschitz parametrizable sets

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $t$ be a real number. The integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$ is the set of integer vectors $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ for which some point $y$ of the unit cube satisfies $v_i \le t f(y)_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$, that is, the set of integer vectors whose half-open unit cube $\prod_i [v_i, v_i + 1)$ meets the dilate $t \cdot f([0, 1]^d)$.
nodes.title: Integer cube set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $t$ be a real number and let $v \in \mathbb{Z}^n$. Then $v$ belongs to the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$ if and only if some point $y$ of the unit cube satisfies $v_i \le t f(y)_i < v_i + 1$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Membership in the integer cube set

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$, $b$ and $D$ with $|a - b| \le D$, the integers $\lfloor a \rfloor$ and $\lfloor b \rfloor$ satisfy $|\lfloor a \rfloor - \lfloor b \rfloor| \le \lceil D \rceil$.
nodes.title: Floor differences are bounded by a ceiling

parts: Dilated Lipschitz maps vary by at most
reading_title.source: Dilated Lipschitz maps vary by at most $K$ on cells of size $1/T$

nodes.summary: Let $K \ge 0$, let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance, and let $t$ and $T$ be real numbers with $0 < t \le T$. If $y$ and $y'$ are points of the unit cube at distance at most $1/T$, then $|t f(y)_i - t f(y')_i| \le K$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Dilated Lipschitz maps vary by at most $K$ on cells of size $1/T$

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $K \ge 0$, and let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance. For every real $t \ge 1$, the cardinality of the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$, taken as a natural number, is at most $\lceil t \rceil^d \, (2 \lceil K \sqrt{d} \rceil + 3)^n$.
nodes.title: Counting integer cubes met by a dilated Lipschitz image

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $K \ge 0$, and let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance. For every real $t \ge 1$, the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$ is finite.
nodes.title: Dilated Lipschitz images meet finitely many integer cubes

reading_title.source: Dilated Lipschitz images meet $O(t^d)$ integer cubes

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $n$ be natural numbers, let $K \ge 0$, and let $f$ be a $K$-Lipschitz map from the unit cube $[0, 1]^d$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, both carrying the sup distance. Then there is a real number $C > 0$ such that for every real $t \ge 1$, the cardinality of the integer cube set of $f$ at scale $t$, taken as a natural number, is at most $C t^d$.
nodes.title: Dilated Lipschitz images meet $O(t^d)$ integer cubes

Moving sofa problem

nodes.summary: The corridor is the L-shaped set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$ (the horizontal arm, extending to the left) together with the points $z$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $\operatorname{Im} z \ge 0$ (the vertical arm, extending upward): two perpendicular semi-infinite arms of width one.
nodes.title: Corridor

nodes.summary: The entrance region of the unit right-angle corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$, the part of its horizontal arm to the left of the corner square.
nodes.title: Entrance of the corridor

nodes.summary: The exit region of the unit right-angle corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 1\}$, the part of its vertical arm above the corner square.
nodes.title: Exit of the corridor

nodes.summary: A motion consists of a continuous map $t \mapsto u_t$ from $[0, 1]$ to the unit circle $\{u \in \mathbb{C} : |u| = 1\}$ (the rotation) and a continuous map $t \mapsto c_t$ from $[0, 1]$ to $\mathbb{C}$ (the translation).
nodes.title: Planar rigid motion

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a motion with rotation $u(t)$ in the unit circle and translation $c(t) \in \mathbb{C}$ at each time $t \in [0, 1]$. The position at time $t$ of a point $z \in \mathbb{C}$ is $u(t)\,z + c(t)$.
nodes.title: Position under a rigid motion

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ can pass the corridor if there are continuous maps $u$ from $[0, 1]$ to the unit circle $\{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| = 1\}$ and $c$ from $[0, 1]$ to $\mathbb{C}$ such that, writing $K_t = \{u(t) z + c(t) : z \in K\}$ for the position of $K$ at time $t$, $K_0$ lies in the entrance arm, $K_1$ lies in the exit arm, and $K_t$ lies in the corridor for every $t \in [0, 1]$.
nodes.title: Passing the corridor

nodes.title: Sofa shapes

nodes.summary: Let the corridor be $L = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\} \cup \{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z\}$, with entrance $E = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$ and exit $X = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 1 \le \operatorname{Im} z\}$. A sofa is a…

nodes.summary: The unit square is the set of complex numbers $z$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$, that is, the square $[0,1] \times [0,1]$ in the complex plane.
nodes.title: Unit square

nodes.summary: The motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = 2t - 1$ for $t \le 1/2$ and $\tau(t) = (2t - 1)i$ for $t \ge 1/2$: it moves a shape one unit to the right during the first half of the time interval and then one unit upward.
nodes.title: The square's translation through the corner

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a motion, $t \in [0, 1]$ a time, and write $m_t(z)$ for the position of a point $z \in \mathbb{C}$ under $m$ at time $t$. Then $|m_t(z) - m_t(w)| = |z - w|$ for all $z, w \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Motions preserve distance

nodes.summary: The unit square $[0,1] \times [0,1]$ is a measurable set for the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of the complex plane.
nodes.title: The unit square is Borel measurable

nodes.summary: The unit square $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$ is a nonempty connected subset of $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: The unit square is connected

nodes.summary: The unit square $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$ has Lebesgue measure $1$.
nodes.title: The unit square has area one

nodes.summary: Let the corridor be $L = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\} \cup \{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z\}$, with entrance $E = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$ and exit $X = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : 0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1,\ 1 \le \operatorname{Im} z\}$. For the unit…
nodes.title: The unit square passes the corridor

nodes.summary: The unit square $[0,1] \times [0,1]$ in the complex plane is a sofa: it is null-measurable for Lebesgue measure, connected, and there are continuous maps $u \colon [0,1] \to \{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| = 1\}$ and $v \colon [0,1] \to \mathbb{C}$ such that the motion $z \mapsto u(t) z + v(t)$ carries the square into the entrance $\{z : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$ at $t = 0$, into the…
nodes.title: The unit square is a sofa

nodes.summary: The optimal sofa area, that is, the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the Lebesgue areas of all sofas, is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The optimal sofa area is at least one

nodes.summary: The mirrored corridor is the set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \ge -1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$ (the horizontal arm, extending to the right) together with the points $z$ with $-1 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 0$ and $\operatorname{Im} z \ge 0$ (the vertical arm, extending upward). It is the reflection of the corridor in the imaginary axis, so passing it requires the opposite turn.
nodes.title: Mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: The entrance arm of the mirrored corridor is the set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \ge 0$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$: the part of its horizontal arm beyond the corner square $-1 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 0$, $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$.
nodes.title: Entrance arm of the mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: The exit region of the mirrored unit corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : -1 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ \operatorname{Im} z \ge 1\}$, the part of its vertical arm above its corner square.
nodes.title: Exit of the mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ can pass the mirrored corridor if there are continuous maps $u$ from $[0, 1]$ to the unit circle $\{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| = 1\}$ and $c$ from $[0, 1]$ to $\mathbb{C}$ such that, writing $K_t = \{u(t) z + c(t) : z \in K\}$ for the position of $K$ at time $t$, $K_0$ lies in the entrance arm of the mirrored corridor, $K_1$ lies in the exit arm of the mirrored corridor, and $K_t$ lies in…
nodes.title: Passing the mirrored corridor

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$, the Z-shaped corridor with corner separation $d$ is the set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ lying in at least one of three pieces: the lower horizontal arm, where $\operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$; the middle channel, where $0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 2 + d$; and the upper horizontal arm, where $\operatorname{Re} z \ge 0$…
nodes.title: Z-shaped corridor

nodes.summary: The entrance region of the Z corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$, the part of its horizontal entrance arm to the left of the middle channel.
nodes.title: Entrance arm of the Z corridor

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$ (the corner separation), the exit region of the Z corridor with separation $d$ is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \ge 1,\ 1 + d \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 2 + d\}$, the part of its horizontal exit arm to the right of the middle channel.
nodes.title: Exit arm of the Z corridor

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$, a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ can pass the Z corridor with corner separation $d$ if there are continuous maps $u$ from $[0, 1]$ to the unit circle $\{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| = 1\}$ and $c$ from $[0, 1]$ to $\mathbb{C}$ such that, writing $K_t = \{u(t) z + c(t) : z \in K\}$ for the position of $K$ at time $t$, $K_0$ lies in the entrance arm of the Z corridor, $K_1$ lies in the exit arm of the…
nodes.title: Passing the Z corridor at a given separation

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ can pass the Z corridor if there is a real number $D$ such that, for every real $d \ge D$, $K$ can pass the Z corridor with corner separation $d$; that is, $K$ passes whenever the corners are sufficiently separated.
nodes.title: Passing the Z corridor for all large separations

nodes.summary: For a real number $d$, the motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = 3t - 1$ for $t \le 1/3$, $\tau(t) = (1 + d)(3t - 1)i$ for $1/3 \le t \le 2/3$, and $\tau(t) = (3t - 2) + (1 + d)i$ for $t \ge 2/3$: it translates a shape by $1$, then by $(1 + d)i$, then by $1$, each segment taking a third of the time interval.
nodes.title: The square's translation through the Z corridor

nodes.summary: For every real $d \ge 0$, the unit square passes the Z corridor with corner separation $d$.
nodes.title: Z-corridor passage of the unit square

nodes.summary: The square's translation through the Z corridor at separation $d = 1$: the motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = 3t - 1$ for $t \le 1/3$, $\tau(t) = 2(3t - 1)i$ for $1/3 \le t \le 2/3$, and $\tau(t) = (3t - 2) + 2i$ for $t \ge 2/3$.
nodes.title: The square's translation through the Z corridor at separation one

nodes.summary: The unit square passes the Z corridor with corner separation $1$.
nodes.title: Z-corridor passage of the unit square at separation one

nodes.summary: There is a real $D$ such that for every $d \ge D$ the unit square passes the Z corridor with corner separation $d$.
nodes.title: Z-corridor passage of the unit square for large separations

nodes.summary: A set $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ is an ambidextrous sofa when it is a sofa and there is a real number $D$ such that, for every corner separation $d \ge D$, a single motion places $K$ inside the entrance arm of the Z corridor with separation $d$ at time $0$, inside its exit arm at time $1$, and inside that corridor at every time; such a passage turns once in each direction.
nodes.title: Ambidextrous sofa shapes

nodes.summary: The ambidextrous optimal area is the supremum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the Lebesgue areas of all ambidextrous sofas $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Optimal area of ambidextrous sofas

nodes.summary: The supremum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the Lebesgue areas of all ambidextrous sofas is at most the supremum of the Lebesgue areas of all sofas. This holds because every ambidextrous sofa is a sofa.
nodes.title: The ambidextrous optimal area is at most the optimal area

nodes.summary: The motion with no rotation that sends a point $z$ at time $t \in [0,1]$ to $z + \tau(t)$, where $\tau(t) = -2t$ for $t \le 1/2$ and $\tau(t) = -1 + (2t - 1)i$ for $t \ge 1/2$: it moves a shape one unit to the left during the first half of the time interval and then one unit upward.

nodes.summary: The unit square $[0,1] \times [0,1]$ in the complex plane is an ambidextrous sofa.
nodes.title: The unit square is an ambidextrous sofa

nodes.summary: The supremum of the Lebesgue areas of all ambidextrous sofas, taken in $[0, \infty]$, is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The ambidextrous sofa constant is at least one

nodes.summary: The supremum of the areas of ambidextrous sofas, taken in $[0, \infty]$, is at most $2\sqrt{2}$.
nodes.title: Hammersley upper bound for the ambidextrous sofa

nodes.summary: The supremum of the areas of ambidextrous sofas, taken in $[0, \infty]$, is at most $22195/10000 = 2.2195$.
nodes.title: Baek upper bound for the ambidextrous sofa

nodes.summary: The supremum of the areas of ambidextrous sofas, taken in $[0, \infty]$, is at least $164495/100000 = 1.64495$.
nodes.title: Gibbs lower bound for the ambidextrous sofa

nodes.title: Romik lower bound for the ambidextrous sofa

nodes.summary: The moving sofa constant, the supremum of the areas of connected Lebesgue-measurable planar shapes that a continuous rigid motion can carry through the right-angled corridor of width $1$, is at most $2\sqrt{2}$.
nodes.title: Hammersley's upper bound for the moving sofa constant

nodes.summary: The moving sofa constant, the supremum of the areas of connected Lebesgue-measurable planar shapes that a continuous rigid motion can carry through the right-angled corridor of width $1$, is at most $2.37$.

Pancake cutting with exotic knives

nodes.summary: For a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of cuts, the number of regions into which $K$ divides the plane is the number of connected components of the complement $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$, or $0$ if there are infinitely many components.
nodes.title: Number of regions cut out of the plane

nodes.summary: The empty set of cuts divides the plane into exactly one region.
nodes.title: No cuts, one region

nodes.summary: A long-legged three-armed V is the union of three rays $\{c + s u_j : s \ge 0\}$, $j = 1, 2, 3$, from a common tip $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$, with nonzero direction vectors $u_1, u_2, u_3 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ in arbitrary directions. For every natural number $n$, the largest number of regions into which the union of $n$ long-legged three-armed V's can divide the plane is $(9n^2 - 5n + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Maximum region count for three-armed V's

nodes.summary: For points $p, q \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and nonzero vectors $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the 3-chain is the union of the ray $\{p + s u : s \ge 0\}$, the segment $[p, q]$ and the ray $\{q + s v : s \ge 0\}$; the directions are arbitrary and the 3-chain may intersect itself. For every natural number $n$, the largest number of regions into which the union of $n$ 3-chains can divide the plane is $(9n^2 - 5n + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Maximum region count for 3-chains

nodes.summary: For a tip $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$, nonzero vectors $u_1, u_2 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and reals $a, b > 0$, the long-legged A is the union of the rays $\{c + s u_1 : s \ge 0\}$ and $\{c + s u_2 : s \ge 0\}$ and the crossbar segment $[c + a u_1, c + b u_2]$. For every natural number $n$, the largest number of regions into which the union of $n$ long-legged A's can divide the plane is $(9n^2 - 5n + 2)/2$.
nodes.title: Maximum region count for long-legged A's

nodes.summary: For a point $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, the constrained long-legged T $\bar T(c, \theta)$ is the union of the crossbar, the line $\{c + s(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta) : s \in \mathbb{R}\}$, and the stem, the ray $\{c + s(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) : s \ge 0\}$. For all $c_1, c_2 \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and $\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \mathbb{R}$, if $\bar T(c_1, \theta_1) \cap \bar T(c_2, \theta_2)$…
nodes.title: Four-point intersections of constrained T's

nodes.summary: For a point $c = (a, b) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, a radius $r > 0$ and an angle $\theta \in \mathbb{R}$, the lollipop with center $c$, radius $r$ and stem direction $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ consists of the circle $\{(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : (x - a)^2 + (y - b)^2 = r^2\}$ and the stem $\{c + s(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) : s \ge r\}$, the part of the ray from $c$ in that direction outside the open disc. Pick's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $u, v \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ with $u_0 v_1 - u_1 v_0 \neq 0$, and let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the convex hull of $0$, $u$ and $v$. Let $I$ be the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in the interior of $T$ and $B$ the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ on the boundary of $T$. Then the area (two-dimensional Lebesgue measure) of $T$ equals $I + B/2 - 1$.
nodes.title: Pick's theorem for lattice triangles with a vertex at the origin

nodes.summary: Let $V \subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ be a finite set of lattice points, let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the convex hull of $V$, and suppose that $P$ has nonempty interior. Let $I$ be the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in the interior of $P$ and $B$ the number of points of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ on the boundary of $P$. Then the area (two-dimensional Lebesgue measure) of $P$ equals $I + B/2 - 1$.
nodes.title: Pick's theorem for convex lattice polygons

nodes.summary: The map $\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ sending a lattice point $(a, b)$ to the point $(a, b)$ of the real plane.
nodes.title: Lattice points in the plane

nodes.summary: Given integer points $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the lattice polygon on $v$ is the polygon in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $n$ vertices whose $i$-th vertex is $v_i$, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: Lattice polygon

nodes.summary: For a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$, the region enclosed by $S$ is the set of points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in the complement $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus S$ is bounded. For a simple closed curve $S$ this is the Jordan interior.
nodes.title: Region enclosed by a planar set

nodes.summary: The area enclosed by a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is the Lebesgue measure, as a real number, of the region enclosed by $S$ (the points $x \notin S$ whose connected component in $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus S$ is bounded); it is taken to be $0$ when that measure is infinite.
nodes.title: Enclosed area

nodes.summary: Two indices $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ are adjacent when $j \equiv i + 1 \pmod n$ or $i \equiv j + 1 \pmod n$.
nodes.title: Cyclically adjacent indices

nodes.summary: For integer points $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the number of lattice points $z \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ that lie on the boundary (the union of the edges) of the lattice polygon on $v$.
nodes.title: Number of boundary lattice points

nodes.summary: For integer points $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the number of lattice points $z \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ that lie in the region enclosed by the boundary of the lattice polygon on $v$, that is, the points off the boundary whose connected component in its complement is bounded.
nodes.title: Number of interior lattice points

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and let $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1} \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ be integer points such that the lattice polygon $P$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with vertices $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$ is simple. Then the area of the region enclosed by the boundary of $P$ equals $I + B/2 - 1$, where $I$ is the number of lattice points in that region and $B$ is the number of lattice points on the boundary of $P$.
