nodes.title: Two-component links as labeled links

nodes.summary: A labeled parametrized link with two components $0$ and $1$ is sent to the two-component link in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose first component is the knot with the same parametrization as component $0$ and whose second component is the knot with the same parametrization as component $1$.
nodes.title: Labeled two-component links as two-component links

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be oriented two-component smooth links in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and regard each as an oriented labeled smooth link with two components, whose component $0$ is its first component and whose component $1$ is its second. Then $L_1$ and $L_2$ are ambient isotopic, meaning that a single smooth ambient isotopy carries each component of $L_1$ onto the corresponding component of $L_2$ up to…
nodes.title: Two-component link isotopy agrees with labeled link isotopy

nodes.summary: There exist two oriented smooth two-component links $L_1$ and $L_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that are not ambient isotopic as oriented links with ordered components: no ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries the first component of $L_1$ to the first component of $L_2$ and the second component of $L_1$ to the second component of $L_2$, each up to an orientation-preserving reparametrization of the circle.
nodes.title: Non-isotopic two-component links exist

nodes.summary: There are two oriented smooth knots $K_1$ and $K_2$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that are not ambient-isotopic.
nodes.title: Existence of non-isotopic knots
Distortion of knots

nodes.summary: For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and a real number $t$, the speed of $K$ at $t$ is the Euclidean norm $\lVert \gamma'(t) \rVert$ of the derivative of $\gamma$ at $t$.
nodes.title: Speed of a knot

nodes.summary: For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$, the arc length of $K$ between $s$ and $t$ is $\left| \int_s^t \lVert \gamma'(u) \rVert \, du \right|$, the length of the arc that $\gamma$ traces between the parameters $s$ and $t$. It does not depend on the order of $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Arc length between two parameters

nodes.summary: For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$, the total arc length of $K$ is the arc length of $K$ between the parameters $0$ and $2\pi$, namely $\left| \int_0^{2\pi} \lVert \gamma'(u) \rVert \, du \right|$.
nodes.title: Total arc length of a knot

nodes.summary: For a knot $K$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$, let $\ell$ be the arc length of $K$ between the parameters $s$ and $t$, and let $L$ be the total arc length of $K$. The intrinsic distance between $s$ and $t$ is $\min(\ell, L - \ell)$. When $s$ and $t$ lie in one closed interval of length $2\pi$, this is the length of the shorter of the two arcs of $K$ joining the points with parameters $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Intrinsic distance on a knot

nodes.summary: For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$, the distortion ratio of $K$ at $s$ and $t$ is the intrinsic distance between $s$ and $t$ along $K$ divided by the Euclidean distance $\lVert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rVert$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, where division by $0$ gives $0$.
nodes.title: Distortion ratio

nodes.summary: For a knot $K$, the distortion of $K$ is the supremum in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ of the distortion ratios of $K$ at $s$ and $t$, taken over all distinct parameters $s \ne t$ in the half-open interval $[0, 2\pi)$.
nodes.title: Distortion of a knot

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, the standard $(p, q)$-torus curve is the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ sending $t$ to $((2 + \cos qt) \cos pt,\ (2 + \cos qt) \sin pt,\ \sin qt)$. It lies on the torus of revolution about the $z$-axis with major radius $2$ and minor radius $1$, and as $t$ runs over $[0, 2\pi]$ it winds $p$ times around the $z$-axis and $q$ times around the core circle of the torus.
nodes.title: Standard torus curve

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be coprime positive integers, let $T_{p,q}$ be the standard $(p, q)$-torus curve, and let $K$ be a knot with parametrization $\gamma$. Suppose there are an ambient isotopy $H$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$, with time-one map $H_1$, and a strictly increasing diffeomorphism $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{R}$ with $\sigma(t + 2\pi) = \sigma(t) + 2\pi$ for all real $t$, such that $H_1(\gamma(t)) = T_{p,q}(\sigma(t))$ for…
nodes.title: Pardon's lower bound for the distortion of torus knots
Quadrisecant theorem

nodes.summary: The period is the real number $2\pi$.
nodes.title: Period

nodes.summary: The standard circle is the curve $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ given by $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$, the unit circle in the $xy$-plane.
nodes.title: Standard circle

nodes.summary: A knot $K$ is unknotted when there is a knot $J$ whose parametrization is the standard circle $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$ such that $K$ is ambient-isotopic to $J$ as an oriented knot.
nodes.title: Unknotted knot

nodes.summary: A knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ has a quadrisecant when there are pairwise distinct reals $t_0, t_1, t_2, t_3 \in [0, 2\pi)$, a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^3$, a nonzero vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and reals $a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3$ such that $\gamma(t_i) = p + a_i v$ for each $i$, that is, the four points $\gamma(t_i)$ lie on one line.
nodes.title: Quadrisecant of a knot

nodes.summary: Every smooth knot $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is not unknotted has a quadrisecant.
nodes.title: Quadrisecant theorem (Pannwitz–Kuperberg)
Slice knots

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be the PL knot traced by the braid closure on $4$ strands of the braid word $\sigma_1^{-2} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_2 \sigma_1^{-1} \sigma_3 \sigma_2^{-2} \sigma_3^2$ for the Conway knot 11n34. Then $K$ is topologically slice: there is a smooth knot $J$ whose image is unoriented topologically ambient isotopic in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to the image of $K$, and $J$ is topologically slice.
nodes.title: The Conway knot is topologically slice

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be the Conway knot $11n34$, realized as a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$ (the braid closure of a 4-strand braid word for it), and let $N$ be its number of vertices. The periodic piecewise-linear parametrization of $K$, which traverses each edge in unit time, is injective on the interval $[0, N)$.
nodes.title: The Conway knot polyline is a simple closed curve

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be the Conway knot $11n34$, realized as a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$. There is no smooth knot $J$, that is, a smooth $2\pi$-periodic map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with nowhere vanishing derivative that is injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, with both of the following properties: some topological ambient isotopy of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries the image of $J$ onto the image of $K$; and there is a smooth map…
nodes.title: The Conway knot is not smoothly slice (Piccirillo)

nodes.summary: There is a PL knot $K$ (a closed polyline in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with at least three vertices, not required to be simple) that is topologically slice but not smoothly slice. Here $K$ is smoothly (respectively topologically) slice when some smooth knot whose image is topologically ambient isotopic to the image of $K$ bounds a smooth (respectively locally flat) properly embedded $2$-disk in…
nodes.title: A topologically slice knot that is not smoothly slice
Knot diagrams

nodes.summary: A dart diagram consists of a finite set $V$ of crossings, a fixed-point-free involution $\mathrm{pair}$ of the set $V \times \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ of darts, and a natural number counting isolated crossingless components.
nodes.title: Dart diagram

nodes.summary: The darts of a dart diagram $D$ with crossing set $V$ are the pairs $(v, i)$ with $v \in V$ and $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$; the dart $(v, i)$ is the $i$-th incident half-edge at the crossing $v$.
nodes.title: Darts of a dart diagram

nodes.summary: The crossing count of a dart diagram $D$ is the number of vertices of $D$, each vertex being one crossing.
nodes.title: Number of crossings of a dart diagram

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation of a dart $(v, i)$ of $D$, with $v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, is the dart $(v, i + 1)$: one step counterclockwise around the crossing $v$.
nodes.title: Rotation of a dart

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d = (v, i)$ of $D$, the opposite dart is obtained by rotating $d$ twice counterclockwise around its crossing $v$; it is the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.
nodes.title: Opposite dart

nodes.summary: The four darts at a crossing of a dart diagram carry the labels $0, 1, 2, 3$ in cyclic order. A dart lies on the over-strand at its crossing when its label is $0$ or $2$.
nodes.title: Over-strand darts

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the edge-pairing permutation is the edge-pairing involution of $D$ regarded as a permutation of the darts of $D$; it is its own inverse.
nodes.title: Edge-pairing permutation

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the rotation permutation is the permutation of the darts of $D$ sending a dart $(v, i)$, with $v$ a crossing and $i \in \mathbb{Z}/4$, to $(v, i + 1)$; its inverse sends $(v, i)$ to $(v, i - 1)$.
nodes.title: Rotation permutation of darts

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the opposite-dart permutation of the darts of $D$ is the square of the quarter-turn rotation permutation: it sends the dart $(v, i)$ at crossing $v$ to the dart $(v, i + 2)$, with labels taken modulo $4$.
nodes.title: Opposite-dart permutation

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$ and a dart $d$ of $D$, the next dart after $d$ is the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$: cross the edge segment at $d$, then go straight through the crossing reached.
nodes.title: Strand traversal step

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, the strand traversal permutation of the darts of $D$ is the edge-pairing permutation followed by the opposite-dart permutation: it sends a dart $d$ to the dart opposite $\mathrm{pair}(d)$ at its crossing, where $\mathrm{pair}$ is the edge-pairing involution of $D$.
nodes.title: Strand traversal permutation

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a dart diagram, and for a dart $d$ of $D$ let $\operatorname{next}(d)$ be the dart reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and then going straight through the next crossing. Then for every dart $d$ of $D$, the darts $d$ and $\operatorname{next}(d)$ lie in the same cycle of the strand traversal permutation of $D$, the permutation of the darts of $D$ that sends each dart $e$ to…
nodes.title: A traversal step stays in its strand cycle

nodes.summary: A dart diagram is alternating when, for every dart $d$, the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$, reached from $d$ by crossing its edge segment and going straight through the next crossing, has the opposite over/under status to $d$. In other words, consecutive crossings on every strand have opposite over/under status.
nodes.title: Alternating dart diagrams

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, two darts of $D$ lie in the same component when they are related by the equivalence relation on darts generated by $d \sim \operatorname{pair}(d)$, crossing an edge segment, and $d \sim \operatorname{opposite}(d)$, going straight through a crossing.
nodes.title: Same component relation on darts

nodes.summary: For a dart diagram $D$, this is the equivalence relation on the darts of $D$ generated by relating each dart $d$ to its partner across an edge segment and to the opposite dart of $d$ at the same crossing. Two darts are related exactly when they lie on the same unoriented strand component.
nodes.title: Strand-connectivity relation on darts

nodes.summary: For every dart $d$ of a dart diagram $D$, the dart $\operatorname{next}(d)$ reached by one step of strand traversal lies in the same component as $d$.
nodes.title: A traversal step stays in the same component

nodes.summary: The number of components of a dart diagram $D$ is the number of classes of darts of $D$ under unoriented strand connectivity, plus the recorded number of isolated crossingless components of $D$.
nodes.title: Number of components of a dart diagram

nodes.summary: For every dart diagram $D$, the number of isolated crossingless components recorded in $D$ is at most the number of components of $D$.
nodes.title: Isolated components are counted in the component count

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, the empty dart diagram with $k$ isolated components has no crossings, hence no darts, and records $k$ isolated crossingless components.
nodes.title: Empty dart diagram

nodes.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm, the target plane of the fixed standard projection frame.
nodes.title: Euclidean plane

nodes.summary: The standard projection sends a point $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2)$ of Euclidean 3-space to the point $(x_0, x_1)$ of the Euclidean plane, forgetting the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Standard projection to the plane

nodes.summary: The height of a point $x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$ of Euclidean 3-space is its third coordinate $x_3$.
nodes.title: Height in the standard projection frame

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a parameter point consists of a component index $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a real parameter $t$ with $0 \le t < 2\pi$, the fundamental half-open period. It represents the point at parameter $t$ of component $i$ of a parametrized link with $n$ components.
nodes.title: Parameter point

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point $a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the point of $L$ at $a$ is $\gamma_i(t) \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
nodes.title: Point of a link at a parameter point

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and $i < n$, the projected curve of component $i$ is the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^2$, $t \mapsto \pi(\gamma_i(t))$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ is the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Projected curve of a link component

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with components $\gamma_0, \dots, \gamma_{n-1} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a parameter point $a = (i, t)$, with $i < n$ and $t \in [0, 2\pi)$, the projected point of $L$ at $a$ is $\pi(\gamma_i(t)) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, where $\pi(x_0, x_1, x_2) = (x_0, x_1)$ forgets the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Projected point of a link at a parameter point

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and let $a$ be a parameter point of $L$, given by a component $i$ and a parameter $t$. The projected tangent vector of $L$ at $a$ is the vector of $\mathbb{R}^2$ obtained by applying the standard projection $(x, y, z) \mapsto (x, y)$ to the derivative $\gamma_i'(t)$ of the curve $\gamma_i$ of the $i$-th component of $L$ at $t$.
nodes.title: Projected tangent vector

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components and a parameter point $a$ of $L$, the height of $L$ at $a$ is the height (the third coordinate) of the point of Euclidean 3-space that $a$ represents on $L$.
nodes.title: Height of a parameter point

nodes.summary: For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the double-point set of $L$ is the set of points $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ for which there are two distinct parameter points of $L$ (each a component index together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) whose images under the standard projection, which forgets the third coordinate, both equal $p$.
nodes.title: Double points of a link projection

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link; a parameter point of $L$ is a component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$. The standard projection of $L$ to the plane, which forgets the third coordinate, is regular when the following hold: at every parameter point, the projection of the velocity vector of the component curve is nonzero; the double-point set is finite; no three pairwise distinct parameter points have…
nodes.title: Regular projections

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. If two distinct parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ have the same projected point, then the heights of $L$ at $a$ and at $b$ are different.
nodes.title: Points with the same projection have different heights

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components. A crossing of $L$ is a point of the double-point set of $L$, that is, a point $p$ of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that two distinct parameter points of $L$ both have image $p$ under the standard projection forgetting the third coordinate.
nodes.title: Crossings of a link projection

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ whose standard projection is regular, the crossing count of $L$ is the number of crossings of the projection, that is, the number of points of its double-point set.
nodes.title: Crossing count of a regular projection

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a point of the double-point set of $L$. Then there are parameter points $a \ne b$ of $L$ whose projected points are both $p$, and every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is $a$ or $b$.
nodes.title: Double points have exactly two preimages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an over point of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.
nodes.title: Being the over-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link and $p$ a crossing of its standard projection to the plane. A parameter point $a$ of $L$ is an under point of $p$ when $a$ projects to $p$ and every other parameter point that projects to $p$ has strictly greater height than $a$.
nodes.title: Being the under-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an over-strand preimage of $p$: the projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has height strictly less than the height of $a$.
nodes.title: The over-strand preimage exists and is unique

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. There is exactly one parameter point $a$ of $L$ that is an under-strand preimage of $p$: the projected point of $a$ is $p$, and every other parameter point whose projected point is $p$ has height strictly greater than the height of $a$.
nodes.title: The under-strand preimage exists and is unique

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The over-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and such that every other parameter point projecting to $p$ has strictly smaller height than $a$.
nodes.title: Over-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. The under-strand preimage of $p$ is the unique parameter point $a$ of $L$ that projects to $p$ and whose height is strictly less than the height of every other parameter point projecting to $p$; the height of a parameter point is the third coordinate of the corresponding point of $L$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
nodes.title: Under-strand preimage of a crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of this projection. Then the under-strand preimage of $p$ and the over-strand preimage of $p$ are distinct parameter points of $L$.
nodes.title: Over and under preimages differ

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. The height of $L$ at the under-strand preimage of $p$ is strictly less than its height at the over-strand preimage of $p$.
nodes.title: The under-strand lies strictly below the over-strand

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the over-strand parameter point at $p$ is $p$.
nodes.title: The over-strand preimage lies over its crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of $L$, that is, a point of the double-point set of its projection. Then the projected point of the under-strand parameter point at $p$ is $p$.
nodes.title: The under-strand preimage lies over its crossing

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link with $n$ components whose standard projection is regular, and let $p$ be a crossing of that projection. Every parameter point of $L$ whose projected point is $p$ is either the over-strand preimage or the under-strand preimage of $p$.
nodes.title: The over and under preimages exhaust a crossing

nodes.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then the crossing count of $L$ is $0$.
nodes.title: A crossing-free regular projection has crossing count zero

nodes.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection with at least one crossing, then the crossing count of $L$ is positive.
nodes.title: A regular projection with a crossing has positive crossing count

nodes.summary: For an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the crossing number of $L$ is the infimum in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, over all parametrized links $L'$ with $n$ components that are ambient isotopic to $L$ and whose standard projection to the plane is regular, of the number of crossings (double points) of that projection of $L'$. It is $\infty$ when no such $L'$ exists.
nodes.title: Crossing number of a link

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components, with $L'$ ambient isotopic to $L$, and suppose the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular. Then the crossing number of $L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection of $L'$.
nodes.title: Regular projections of isotopic links bound the crossing number

nodes.summary: If the standard projection of an oriented labeled parametrized link $L$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is at most the number of crossings of this projection.
nodes.title: A link's own regular projection bounds its crossing number

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be oriented labeled parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L'$ is ambient isotopic to $L$ and the standard projection of $L'$ to the plane is regular, then the crossing number of $L$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of the crossing number

nodes.summary: If two parametrized links $L_1$ and $L_2$ with $n$ components are isotopic, then $L_1$ and $L_2$ have the same crossing number.
nodes.title: The crossing number is an isotopy invariant

nodes.summary: Let $L$ and $L'$ be parametrized links with $n$ components such that $L'$ is isotopic to $L$. If the standard projection of $L'$ is regular and its double-point set is empty, then the crossing number of $L$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Crossing number zero from a crossing-free representative

nodes.summary: A parameter point $a$ of a parametrized link $L$ (a component of $L$ together with a parameter in $[0, 2\pi)$) is a crossing preimage when its image under the standard projection to the plane lies in the double-point set of $L$.
nodes.title: Crossing preimages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular, and let $a$ be a crossing preimage of $L$. The over/under status at $a$ is true when $a$ is the over-strand preimage of the crossing at the projection of $a$, that is, the preimage of that crossing of greatest height, and false otherwise.
nodes.title: Over/under status at a crossing preimage

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If $a \ne b$ are crossing preimages of $L$ with the same projection, then the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.
nodes.title: The two preimages of a crossing have opposite status

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be parameter points with parameters $s$, $u$, $t \in [0, 2\pi)$ respectively. Then $c$ lies in the open counterclockwise arc from $a$ to $b$ when $s < t < u$ in case $s < u$, and when $s < t$ or $t < u$ in case $u \le s$. Only the parameters are compared; the components of $a$, $b$, $c$ play no role.
nodes.title: Open arc on the parameter circle

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be an oriented labeled parametrized link, with each component parametrized by $t \in [0, 2\pi)$. Two distinct parameter points $a$ and $b$ of $L$ on the same component are cyclically adjacent, in this order, when both are crossing preimages (they project to double points of the standard projection) and no crossing preimage on that component lies in the open arc from $a$ to $b$ in the direction of increasing…
nodes.title: Cyclically adjacent crossing preimages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. The projection is alternating when, for any two cyclically adjacent crossing preimages $a$ and $b$ of $L$ (distinct, on the same component, with no other crossing preimage of that component in the open arc of parameters from $a$ to $b$), the over/under status at $a$ differs from the over/under status at $b$.
nodes.title: Alternating regular projections

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a parametrized link whose standard projection to the plane is regular. If the double-point set of this projection is empty, then the projection is alternating.
nodes.title: Crossingless regular projections are alternating

nodes.summary: A parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram when there is a parametrized link $L'$ isotopic to $L$ whose standard projection is regular and alternating.
nodes.title: Links admitting an alternating diagram

nodes.summary: Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be parametrized links with $n$ components. If $L_1$ is isotopic to $L_2$ and $L_1$ admits an alternating diagram, then $L_2$ admits an alternating diagram.
nodes.title: Admitting an alternating diagram is an isotopy invariant

nodes.summary: If a parametrized link $L$ has a regular standard projection whose double-point set is empty, then $L$ admits an alternating diagram.
nodes.title: Links with a crossing-free regular projection admit alternating diagrams

nodes.summary: For a parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components, the union over all components $i$ of the images of the projected curves of $L$ equals the image of the trace of $L$ under the standard projection to the plane.
nodes.title: The projected trace is the union of the projected components
Ropelength and crossing number

nodes.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm.
nodes.title: Euclidean 3-space

nodes.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the family indexed by $\{0, 1, 2\}$ that sends $0 \mapsto p$, $1 \mapsto q$ and $2 \mapsto r$.
nodes.title: Ordered triple of points

nodes.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space whose ordered triple $(p, q, r)$ is affinely independent, the triangle in Euclidean 3-space with vertices $p$, $q$, $r$, in that order.
nodes.title: Triangle on three affinely independent points

nodes.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is the following value in $[0, \infty]$. If $p, q, r$ are affinely independent, it is the circumradius of the triangle with vertices $p$, $q$ and $r$. Otherwise, that is, when the three points are collinear (in particular when two of them coincide), it is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius of three points

nodes.summary: Let $p, q, r$ be points of Euclidean 3-space and let $T$ be a triangle in Euclidean 3-space whose vertices, in order, are $p$, $q$ and $r$. Then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ equals the circumradius of $T$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius of a triangle

nodes.summary: If $p, q, r$ are points of Euclidean 3-space and the set $\{p, q, r\}$ is collinear, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Collinear points have infinite extended circumradius

nodes.summary: If $p, q, r$ are points of Euclidean 3-space with $p = q$, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.
nodes.title: Equal first two points give infinite extended circumradius

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(q, p, r)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the first two points

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, r, q)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the last two points

nodes.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(r, q, p)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Extended circumradius is invariant under reversal

nodes.summary: For every vector $v$ and all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(v + p, v + q, v + r)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.
nodes.title: Translation invariance of the extended circumradius

nodes.summary: The thickness of a set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the extended circumradii of $(p, q, r)$ over all points $p, q, r \in s$. Since the extended circumradius of three collinear points (in particular of three points two of which coincide) is $\infty$, this is also the infimum over the triples of pairwise distinct points of $s$.
nodes.title: Thickness

nodes.summary: For every set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space and all points $p, q, r \in s$, the thickness of $s$ is at most the extended circumradius of $p, q, r$.
nodes.title: Thickness is at most every circumradius

nodes.summary: If $s \subseteq t$ are sets in Euclidean 3-space, then the thickness of $t$ is at most the thickness of $s$: enlarging a set can only add triples and hence can only decrease the infimum.
nodes.title: Thickness is antitone

nodes.summary: The empty subset of Euclidean 3-space has thickness $\infty$, as an empty infimum in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Thickness of the empty set

nodes.summary: For every point $p$ of Euclidean 3-space, the set $\{p\}$ has thickness $\infty$: its only triple $(p, p, p)$ is degenerate.
nodes.title: Thickness of a single point

nodes.summary: Let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space and let $a, b$ be real numbers. The contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the total variation of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$: the supremum, over all finite sequences $t_0 \le t_1 \le \dots \le t_n$ of points of $[a, b]$, of $\sum_{i < n} \lVert \gamma(t_{i+1}) - \gamma(t_i) \rVert$. It is a value in $[0, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Contour length

reading_title.source: Contour length of a $C^1$ curve

nodes.summary: Let $a \le b$ be real numbers and let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space that is continuously differentiable on $[a, b]$. Then the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ equals $\int_a^b \lVert \gamma'(t) \rVert \, dt$.
nodes.title: Contour length of a $C^1$ curve

nodes.summary: For a curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and reals $a, b$, the ropelength ratio of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ divided by the thickness of the trace $\gamma([a, b])$. The quotient is taken in $[0, \infty]$, where $c / 0 = \infty$ for $c \ne 0$, $0 / 0 = 0$ and $c / \infty = 0$.
nodes.title: Ropelength ratio

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is admissible when $c \ge 0$ and, for every $n$ and every oriented labeled link type with $n$ components that admits an alternating diagram and whose crossing number is a natural number $k$, the ropelength of the type is at least $c k$.
nodes.title: Admissible constants for the tight alternating knot inequality

nodes.summary: The tight alternating knot constant $C_{22b} = b_0$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals, of the set of real numbers $c$ admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality: those $c \ge 0$ such that every link type $K$ that admits an alternating diagram and has finite crossing number $\mathrm{Cr}(K)$ has ropelength $\mathrm{L}(K) \ge c\,\mathrm{Cr}(K)$. The supremum is not assumed to be attained.
nodes.title: Tight alternating knot constant

nodes.summary: The constant $c = 0$ is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality.
nodes.title: Zero is an admissible alternating constant

nodes.summary: Admissible alternating constants are downward closed among nonnegative reals. If a real number $c$ is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality and $c'$ is a real number with $0 \le c' \le c$, then $c'$ is admissible as well.
nodes.title: Admissible alternating constants are downward closed among nonnegative reals

nodes.summary: Admissible constants are at most the tight alternating knot constant. Every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality is at most the tight alternating knot constant.
nodes.title: Admissible constants are at most the tight alternating knot constant

nodes.summary: The tight alternating knot constant, an extended real number, is at least $0$.
nodes.title: The tight alternating knot constant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the tight alternating knot constant is at most $b$ if and only if every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight alternating knot inequality satisfies $c \le b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the tight alternating knot constant

nodes.summary: If an oriented labeled link type with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram, then its crossing number is finite: the alternating representative is itself a regular projection.
nodes.title: Alternating link types have finite crossing number

nodes.summary: If an oriented labeled link type with $n$ components admits an alternating diagram, then its crossing number equals some natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Alternating link types have a natural-number crossing number

nodes.summary: A real number $c$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality when $c \ge 0$ and, for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every parametrized link $L$ with $n$ components and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the crossing number of $L$ equals $k$, the ropelength of $L$ is at least $c \, k^{3/4}$, the inequality being read in $[0, \infty]$. Here the crossing number and the ropelength of $L$ are those of its oriented labeled…
nodes.title: Admissible constants for the tight-knot inequality

nodes.summary: The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the set of real numbers $c$ that are admissible for the tight-knot inequality $\mathrm{ropelength} \ge c \cdot (\text{crossing number})^{3/4}$ on link types. The supremum is not assumed to be attained.
nodes.title: Tight knot constant

nodes.summary: The real number $0$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality between the ropelength and the crossing number of link types.
nodes.title: Zero is an admissible tight-knot constant

nodes.summary: If a real number $c$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality and $c'$ is a real number with $0 \le c' \le c$, then $c'$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality as well.
nodes.title: Admissibility passes to smaller nonnegative constants

nodes.summary: Let $C_{22a}$ be the tight knot constant. Every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight-knot inequality satisfies $c \le C_{22a}$ in the extended reals.
nodes.title: Admissible constants are bounded by the tight knot constant

nodes.summary: The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ satisfies $0 \le C_{22a}$ in the extended reals.
nodes.title: The tight knot constant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every extended real number $b$, the tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ satisfies $C_{22a} \le b$ if and only if every real number $c$ that is admissible for the tight-knot inequality satisfies $c \le b$.
nodes.title: Upper bounds for the tight knot constant

nodes.summary: Point-set topology of topological and metric spaces: connectedness, separation and cardinal invariants, homogeneous spaces, direct and inverse limits of spaces, restricted products, and dimension theory.
nodes.title: General topology

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a preconnected subset of a topological space $X$ and let $A \subseteq X$. If both $s \cap A$ and $s \cap (X \setminus A)$ are nonempty, then $s$ meets the frontier $\partial A = \overline{A} \setminus \operatorname{int} A$ of $A$, that is, $s \cap \partial A$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: A preconnected set meets the frontier of every set it crosses

reading_title.source: Bounded metric $d/(1+d)$ is equivalent to $d$

nodes.summary: Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and define
nodes.title: Bounded metric $d/(1+d)$ is equivalent to $d$

nodes.summary: A topological space is homogeneous if its homeomorphism group acts transitively.
nodes.title: Homogeneous topological space

nodes.summary: A proper closed subset of an irreducible set has Krull dimension at least one less than the ambient set.
nodes.title: Krull dimension drops on proper closed subsets of irreducible sets

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a topological space and $s \subseteq X$. The sets that can be obtained from $s$ by applying closure and complement finitely many times (including $s$ itself) form a finite family of at most $14$ distinct sets.
nodes.title: Kuratowski's closure-complement theorem

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a pseudo-extended metric space (distances lie in $[0, \infty]$ and distinct points may be at distance $0$), write $d$ for its extended distance, and let $\varepsilon \in [0, \infty]$. A set $s \subseteq X$ is $\varepsilon$-separated if $\varepsilon \le d(x, y)$ for all distinct points $x, y \in s$.
nodes.title: Non-strictly separated sets
Covering and inductive dimension

nodes.summary: A topological space $X$ has covering dimension at most $n \in \mathbb{N}$ if every finite open cover $U_1, \dots, U_m$ of $X$ has a finite open refinement $V_1, \dots, V_k$ (open sets covering $X$, each contained in some $U_i$) in which any $n + 2$ members with distinct indices have empty intersection, that is, the refinement has order at most $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Covering dimension at most n

nodes.summary: Scottish Book Problem 187, part (2), has a negative answer: it is not the case that for every compact Hausdorff space $X$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $X$ has small inductive dimension at most $n$ if and only if $X$ has covering dimension at most $n$.
nodes.title: Small inductive and covering dimension can differ for compact Hausdorff spaces
Dimension-raising open maps

nodes.summary: An interior (open) mapping can raise dimension: there are compact metrizable spaces $X$ and $Y$, where $X$ has small inductive dimension exactly $1$ and $Y$ has small inductive dimension exactly $2$, and a continuous open surjective map $f \colon X \to Y$. A space has small inductive dimension exactly $n$ when its small inductive dimension is at most $n$ but not at most $n - 1$.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov's open map raising dimension

nodes.summary: For $p \in \mathbb{N}$, the cube $I^p = [0,1]^p$ is the set of points of $\mathbb{R}^p$ all of whose coordinates lie in $[0,1]$, with the subspace topology.
nodes.title: The p-dimensional cube

nodes.summary: There are natural numbers $p < q$ and a continuous, open, surjective map $f \colon I^p \to I^q$, where $I^p = [0,1]^p$ and $I^q = [0,1]^q$ are the $p$- and $q$-dimensional cubes.
nodes.title: Open maps can raise the dimension of a cube
Direct limits of topological spaces

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by a preorder $I$, with maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$ for $i \le j$ forming a directed system ($f_{ii}$ is the identity and $f_{jk} \circ f_{ij} = f_{ik}$ for $i \le j \le k$). This relation on the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} X_i$ relates $(i, x)$ to $(j, f_{ij}(x))$ for all $i \le j$ and $x \in X_i$, and relates no other pairs.
nodes.title: Generating relation of a direct limit

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by a preorder $I$, with maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$ for $i \le j$ forming a directed system. This is the smallest equivalence relation on the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} X_i$ that relates $(i, x)$ to $(j, f_{ij}(x))$ for all $i \le j$ and $x \in X_i$.
nodes.title: Direct limit equivalence relation

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a preorder, $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ a family of topological spaces, and $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$ for $i \le j$ continuous maps forming a directed system ($f_{ii}$ is the identity and $f_{jk} \circ f_{ij} = f_{ik}$ for $i \le j \le k$). The direct limit $\varinjlim X_i$ is the quotient of the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} X_i$ by the equivalence relation generated by $(i, x) \sim (j, f_{ij}(x))$ for…
nodes.title: Direct limit of topological spaces

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a directed system of topological spaces over a preorder $I$ with continuous transition maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$. For $i \in I$, the canonical map $\iota_i : X_i \to \varinjlim X_i$ into the direct limit sends $x$ to the class of $(i, x)$.
nodes.title: Canonical map into the direct limit

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a directed system of topological spaces over a preorder $I$ with continuous transition maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$. For every $i \in I$, the canonical map $\iota_i : X_i \to \varinjlim X_i$ into the direct limit is continuous.
nodes.title: Canonical maps into the direct limit are continuous

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a directed system of topological spaces over a preorder $I$ with continuous transition maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$. The canonical maps $\iota_i : X_i \to \varinjlim X_i$ into the direct limit satisfy $\iota_j(f_{ij}(x)) = \iota_i(x)$ for all $i \le j$ and $x \in X_i$.
nodes.title: Canonical maps commute with the transition maps

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a directed system of topological spaces over a preorder $I$ with continuous transition maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$, and let $Y$ be a topological space. A family of maps $\psi_i : X_i \to Y$ with $\psi_j(f_{ij}(x)) = \psi_i(x)$ for all $i \le j$ and $x \in X_i$ induces the map $\varinjlim X_i \to Y$ from the direct limit that sends the class of $(i, x)$ to $\psi_i(x)$.
nodes.title: Map out of the direct limit

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a directed system of topological spaces over a preorder $I$ with continuous transition maps $f_{ij} : X_i \to X_j$, and let $Y$ be a topological space. If the maps $\psi_i : X_i \to Y$ are continuous and satisfy $\psi_j(f_{ij}(x)) = \psi_i(x)$ for all $i \le j$ and $x \in X_i$, then the induced map $\varinjlim X_i \to Y$ from the direct limit, sending the class of $(i, x)$ to $\psi_i(x)$,…
nodes.title: The induced map out of the direct limit is continuous
Inverse limits of topological spaces

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a preordered set, let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of sets, and for every $i \le j$ let $f_{ij} \colon X_j \to X_i$ be a map. The inverse limit is the set of tuples $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ in the product $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ such that $f_{ij}(x_j) = x_i$ whenever $i \le j$.
nodes.title: Inverse limit as compatible tuples

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a preordered set, let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of sets, and for every $i \le j$ let $f_{ij} \colon X_j \to X_i$ be a map. A tuple $x \in \prod_{i \in I} X_i$ lies in the inverse limit if and only if $f_{ij}(x_j) = x_i$ for all $i \le j$.
nodes.title: Membership in the inverse limit

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a preordered set, let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of sets, and for every $i \le j$ let $f_{ij} \colon X_j \to X_i$ be a map. If $x = (x_i)_{i \in I}$ lies in the inverse limit, then $f_{ij}(x_j) = x_i$ for all $i \le j$.
nodes.title: Elements of the inverse limit are compatible

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a preordered set, let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of Hausdorff topological spaces, and for every $i \le j$ let $f_{ij} \colon X_j \to X_i$ be a continuous map. Then the inverse limit $\{x \in \prod_{i \in I} X_i : f_{ij}(x_j) = x_i \text{ for all } i \le j\}$ is closed in the product $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$.
nodes.title: The inverse limit is closed

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a preordered set, let $(X_i)_{i \in I}$ be a family of compact Hausdorff topological spaces, and for every $i \le j$ let $f_{ij} \colon X_j \to X_i$ be a continuous map. Then the inverse limit $\{x \in \prod_{i \in I} X_i : f_{ij}(x_j) = x_i \text{ for all } i \le j\}$ is compact in the product $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$.
nodes.title: The inverse limit of compact Hausdorff spaces is compact
Networks and monolithic spaces

nodes.summary: A topological space $X$ has a countable network if there is a countable family $\mathcal{N}$ of subsets of $X$ such that for every open set $U \subseteq X$ and every point $x \in U$ there is some $V \in \mathcal{N}$ with $x \in V \subseteq U$.
nodes.title: Countable network

nodes.summary: Every second-countable topological space has a countable network.
nodes.title: Second-countable spaces have a countable network

nodes.summary: A topological space is countably monolithic (ω-monolithic) if the closure of every countable subspace has a countable network.
nodes.title: Countably monolithic space
Restricted products of topological spaces

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family of types with subsets $U_i \subseteq X_i$. For a finite set $S$ of indices, the piece $X_S$ is the set of tuples $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} X_i$ such that $x_i \in U_i$ for every $i \notin S$.
nodes.title: Piece of a restricted product supported in a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family of types with subsets $U_i \subseteq X_i$, and for a finite set $S$ of indices let $X_S$ be the set of tuples $x \in \prod_{i \in \iota} X_i$ with $x_i \in U_i$ for every $i \notin S$. nodes.title: The pieces grow with the finite set

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be sets with subsets $U_i \subseteq X_i$, and let $x$ be an element of the restricted product of the $X_i$ with respect to the $U_i$, that is, a tuple $x \in \prod_i X_i$ with $x_i \in U_i$ for all but finitely many $i$. Then there is a finite set $S \subseteq \iota$ such that $x_i \in U_i$ for all $i \notin S$, that is, $x$ lies in the piece $X_S$.
nodes.title: Every element of the restricted product lies in a piece

nodes.summary: Let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be sets with subsets $U_i \subseteq X_i$. The support of an element $x$ of the restricted product of the $X_i$ with respect to the $U_i$ (a tuple with $x_i \in U_i$ for all but finitely many $i$) is the finite set of indices $i$ with $x_i \notin U_i$.

Numerical range and numerical radius

nodes.summary: The numerical radius of a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ is the real number $w(T) = \sup \{ |\langle T x, x \rangle| : x \in H,\ \|x\| = 1 \}$, the supremum of the moduli of the values $\langle T x, x \rangle$ over the unit vectors of $H$ (taken to be $0$ when $H = 0$).
nodes.title: Numerical radius

nodes.summary: For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space with adjoint $T^*$, the real Cartesian part of $T$ is the bounded linear operator $(T + T^*)/2$.
nodes.title: Real Cartesian part of an operator

nodes.summary: For a bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space with adjoint $T^*$, the imaginary Cartesian part of $T$ is the bounded linear operator $(T - T^*)/(2i)$.
nodes.title: Imaginary Cartesian part of an operator

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$. The set $\{|\langle Tx, x\rangle| : x \in H,\ \|x\| = 1\}$ is bounded above.
nodes.title: The numerical-radius family is bounded above

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex inner product space, the numerical radius $w(T)$ of $T$ satisfies $w(T) \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the numerical radius

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$ with $\|x\| = 1$, $|\langle Tx, x\rangle| \le w(T)$.
nodes.title: The numerical radius bounds the quadratic form on unit vectors

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex inner product space $H$ and let $c \ge 0$ be a real number. If $|\langle T x, x\rangle| \le c$ for every unit vector $x \in H$, then the numerical radius of $T$ satisfies $w(T) \le c$.
nodes.title: Bounding the numerical radius from above

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex inner product space, the numerical radius $w(T)$ is at most the operator norm: $w(T) \le \|T\|$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius at most the operator norm

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex inner product space $H$. For every $x \in H$, $\langle T(\|x\|^{-1} x), \|x\|^{-1} x \rangle = \|x\|^{-2} \langle T x, x \rangle$, where $0^{-1}$ is read as $0$, so that for $x = 0$ both sides vanish.
nodes.title: Quadratic form at the normalized vector

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a nonzero vector in a complex inner product space. Then the vector $\|x\|^{-1} x$ has norm $1$.
nodes.title: Normalizing a nonzero vector gives a unit vector

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, $|\operatorname{Re} \langle Tx, x\rangle| / \|x\|^2 \le w(T)$, where division by zero is taken to be $0$, so the case $x = 0$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Numerical radius bounds the normalized real part of the quadratic form

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, $|\operatorname{Im} \langle Tx, x\rangle| / \|x\|^2 \le w(T)$, where division by zero is taken to be $0$, so the case $x = 0$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Numerical radius bounds the normalized imaginary part of the quadratic form

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $H$, with numerical radius $w(T)$. For every $x \in H$, the Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re} \langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$, taken to be $0$ at $x = 0$, satisfies $|R_T(x)| \le w(T)$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius bounds the Rayleigh quotient

nodes.summary: The complex conjugate of $1/2 \in \mathbb{C}$ is $1/2$, that is, $\overline{1/2} = 1/2$.
nodes.title: Complex conjugate of one half

nodes.summary: The complex conjugate of $-i/2 \in \mathbb{C}$ is $i/2$, that is, $\overline{-i/2} = i/2$.
nodes.title: Complex conjugate of minus half the imaginary unit

nodes.summary: For every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with adjoint $T^*$, the real Cartesian part $A = (T + T^*)/2$ is symmetric: $\langle Ax, y\rangle = \langle x, Ay\rangle$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: The real Cartesian part is symmetric

nodes.summary: For every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with adjoint $T^*$, the imaginary Cartesian part $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ is symmetric: $\langle Bx, y\rangle = \langle x, By\rangle$ for all $x, y \in H$.
nodes.title: The imaginary Cartesian part is symmetric

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and let $A = (T + T^*)/2$ be the real Cartesian part of $T$. Then for every $x \in H$ one has $\langle A x, x \rangle = \operatorname{Re} \langle T x, x \rangle$.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the real Cartesian part

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$, whose inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument, and let $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ be the imaginary Cartesian part of $T$. Then for every $x \in H$ one has $\langle B x, x \rangle = -\operatorname{Im} \langle T x, x \rangle$.
nodes.title: Quadratic form of the imaginary Cartesian part

nodes.summary: Every bounded linear operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space satisfies $T = A + iB$, where $A = (T + T^*)/2$ and $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ are the real and imaginary Cartesian parts of $T$ and $T^*$ is the adjoint of $T$.
nodes.title: Cartesian decomposition

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, with adjoint $T^*$, and let $A = (T + T^*)/2$ be its real Cartesian part. Then $\|A\| \le w(T)$, where $\|A\|$ is the operator norm of $A$ and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.
nodes.title: Norm of the real part is at most the numerical radius

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, with adjoint $T^*$, and let $B = (T - T^*)/(2i)$ be its imaginary Cartesian part. Then $\|B\| \le w(T)$, where $\|B\|$ is the operator norm of $B$ and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.
nodes.title: Norm of the imaginary part is at most the numerical radius

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space, $\|T\| \le 2\,w(T)$, where $\|T\|$ is the operator norm and $w(T)$ is the numerical radius of $T$.
nodes.title: Operator norm at most twice the numerical radius

nodes.summary: If $T$ is a self-adjoint bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space, then its numerical radius equals its operator norm: $w(T) = \|T\|$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius of a self-adjoint operator

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$, with adjoint $T^*$. For every $x \in H$, $|\langle T^* x, x\rangle| = |\langle T x, x\rangle|$, since $\langle T^* x, x\rangle$ is the complex conjugate of $\langle T x, x\rangle$.

nodes.summary: For every bounded operator $T$ on a complex Hilbert space, the numerical radius of its adjoint $T^*$ equals the numerical radius of $T$: $w(T^*) = w(T)$.
nodes.title: Numerical radius of the adjoint

nodes.summary: For a bounded linear operator $A$ on a complex inner product space $E$, the numerical range of $A$ is the set $W(A) = \{\langle A x, x \rangle : x \in E,\ \|x\| = 1\} \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, where the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ of $E$ is conjugate-linear in its first argument and linear in its second.

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex inner product space $E$. A complex number $c$ lies in the numerical range $W(A)$ if and only if there is a vector $x \in E$ with $\|x\| = 1$ and $\langle A x, x \rangle = c$.

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a self-adjoint bounded linear operator on a nonzero Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Then $\operatorname{Re}\langle Tu, u\rangle \ge 0$ for every $u \in H$ if and only if every element $\mu$ of the spectrum of $T$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re}\mu \ge 0$.

Then for every real number $t$ and every nonzero $x \in H$, $R_{tI - T}(x) = t - R_T(x)$.

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a self-adjoint bounded linear operator on a nonzero Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re}\langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$. Then every $\mu$ in the spectrum of $T$ satisfies $\inf_{x \ne 0} R_T(x) \le \operatorname{Re}\mu \le \sup_{x \ne 0} R_T(x)$, where the infimum and supremum range over the nonzero vectors $x \in H$.

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a self-adjoint bounded linear operator on a nonzero Hilbert space $H$ over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with Rayleigh quotient $R_T(x) = \operatorname{Re}\langle Tx, x\rangle / \|x\|^2$ for $x \ne 0$ and $R_T(0) = 0$. Riesz–Schauder theory

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T : E \to E$ be a compact bounded linear operator, let $\mu \neq 0$ be a scalar and let $I$ be the identity of $E$. Then the kernel of $\mu I - T$ is finite-dimensional.
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem, kernel part

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $K$ be a finite-dimensional subspace of $E$. Then there is a continuous linear map $P : E \to E$ such that $P x = x$ for every $x \in K$ and $P x \in K$ for every $x \in E$.
nodes.title: Continuous projection onto a finite-dimensional subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T : E \to E$ be a compact bounded linear operator, let $\mu \neq 0$ be a scalar and let $I$ be the identity of $E$. Then the range of $\mu I - T$ is closed in $E$.
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem, range part

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T : E \to E$ be a compact bounded linear operator, let $\mu \neq 0$ be a scalar and let $I$ be the identity of $E$. Then either $\mu I - T$ is bijective, or the kernel of $\mu I - T$ is nonzero and finite-dimensional and the range of $\mu I - T$ is closed.
nodes.title: Fredholm alternative, Riesz–Schauder form

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a compact operator on $E$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\mu \ne 0$, and let $I$ be the identity operator on $E$. Then the range of $\mu I - T$ is the orthogonal complement of the kernel of its adjoint: $\operatorname{ran}(\mu I - T) = \ker\big((\mu I - T)^*\big)^\perp$.
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem on a Hilbert space

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$ with adjoint $T^*$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ and let $I$ be the identity operator on $E$. Then $(\mu I - T)^* = \overline{\mu} I - T^*$, where $\overline{\mu}$ is the complex conjugate of $\mu$ (so $\overline{\mu} = \mu$ when $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$).
nodes.title: Adjoint of a shifted operator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a compact operator on $E$ with adjoint $T^*$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\mu \ne 0$, and let $I$ be the identity operator on $E$. Then the range of $\mu I - T$ is the orthogonal complement of the kernel of $\overline{\mu} I - T^*$, where $\overline{\mu}$ is the complex conjugate of $\mu$:…
nodes.title: Riesz–Schauder theorem on a Hilbert space, adjoint form
Schauder's theorem on compact adjoints

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If a bounded linear operator $T : E \to F$ has finite-dimensional range, then its adjoint $T^* : F \to E$ is a compact operator.
nodes.title: The adjoint of a finite-rank operator is compact

nodes.summary: The adjoint of a compact operator between Hilbert spaces is compact.

nodes.summary: A bounded operator between Hilbert spaces is compact if and only if its adjoint is compact.

Spectrum of compact operators

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$, let $(\lambda_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be pairwise distinct scalars in $\mathbb{K}$, and let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be nonzero vectors in $E$ with $T u_n = \lambda_n u_n$ for every $n$. Then for every $n$, the vector $u_n$ does not lie in the linear span of $\{u_i : i < n\}$.
nodes.title: Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are not in the span of earlier ones

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$, let $(\lambda_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathbb{K}$ and $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ satisfy $T u_n = \lambda_n u_n$ for every $n$, and for each $n$ let $V_n$ be the linear span of $\{u_i : i < n\}$. Then for every $n$ and every $y \in V_{n+1}$, we have $T y - \lambda_n y \in V_n$.
nodes.title: An operator acts as a scalar on a span of eigenvectors modulo a smaller span

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$, and let $(\lambda_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $\mathbb{K}$ and $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ satisfy $T u_n = \lambda_n u_n$ for every $n$. Then for every $n$ and every $y$ in the linear span of $\{u_i : i \le n\}$, the vector $T y$ also lies in that span.
nodes.title: Invariance of spans of eigenvectors

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be vectors in $E$, and for each $n$ let $V_n$ be the linear span of $\{u_i : i < n\}$. Suppose $u_n \notin V_n$ for every $n$. Then for every $n$ there is a vector $y \in V_{n+1}$ with $\|y\| = 1$ and $\|y - z\| \ge 1/2$ for every $z \in V_n$.
nodes.title: Riesz separation for nested spans

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a compact bounded linear operator on $E$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be real. Then the set of eigenvalues $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ of $T$ with $|\mu| \ge \varepsilon$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finiteness of eigenvalues of a compact operator bounded away from zero

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $T$ be a compact bounded linear operator on $E$. If $(\lambda_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a sequence of pairwise distinct eigenvalues of $T$, then $\lambda_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a compact operator tend to zero along any injective sequence

nodes.summary: If `T` is compact and `E` is infinite-dimensional, then `T` has no two-sided inverse among bounded operators. (Completeness of `E` is not needed for this statement.)
nodes.title: A compact operator on an infinite-dimensional space is not a unit

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $T$ be a compact bounded linear operator on $E$. Then $T$ is not bijective.
nodes.title: A compact operator on an infinite-dimensional Banach space is not bijective

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $T$ be a compact bounded linear operator on $E$. Then $0$ lies in the spectrum of $T$ in the algebra of bounded linear operators on $E$; that is, $T$ has no bounded two-sided inverse.
nodes.title: Zero lies in the spectrum of a compact operator on an infinite-dimensional space

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space with dual space $E^*$ of continuous linear functionals, and let $T : E \to E^*$ be a linear map that is symmetric: $(Tx)(y) = (Ty)(x)$ for all $x, y \in E$. Then $T$ is bounded: there is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $\|Tx\| \le C \|x\|$ for all $x \in E$, where $\|Tx\|$ is the operator norm of the functional $Tx$.
nodes.title: A symmetric linear map from a Banach space to its dual is bounded

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be real Banach spaces and let $T : E \to F$ be a surjective continuous linear map. Then there are a continuous map $g : F \to E$, in general not linear, and a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $T(g(y)) = y$ for every $y \in F$, $g(0) = 0$, $g(t y) = t \, g(y)$ for every real $t \ge 0$ and every $y \in F$, and $\|g(y)\| \le C \|y\|$ for every $y \in F$.
nodes.title: Bartle–Graves theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space, let $K$ be a nonzero compact operator on $E$, and let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$ with $TK = KT$. Then there is a closed linear subspace $M$ of $E$ with $M \ne \{0\}$ and $M \ne E$ that is invariant under $T$: $T x \in M$ for every $x \in M$.
nodes.title: Lomonosov's invariant subspace theorem

Then $T_n \to T$ in the strong operator topology, that is, $T_n x \to T x$ for every $x \in H$, if and only if both $T_n \to T$ in the weak…

nodes.summary: Eidelheit's claim in Problem 173 is false: there is a real Banach space $E$ in which the bounded linear operators $E \to E$ that have a bounded linear two-sided inverse are not dense, for the operator norm, in the space of all bounded linear operators on $E$.

Bilateral shift

nodes.summary: For a function $x : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ with values in any set $K$, the bilateral (forward) shift of $x$ is the function $Sx : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ given by $(Sx)(n) = x(n - 1)$.
nodes.title: Bilateral shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: For a function $x : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ with values in any set $K$, the bilateral backward shift of $x$ is the function $Bx : \mathbb{Z} \to K$ given by $(Bx)(n) = x(n + 1)$.
nodes.title: Bilateral backward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $S : \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Sx)(n) = x(n - 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral backward shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $B : \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Bx)(n) = x(n + 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.title: Bilateral backward shift as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ be the Hilbert space of square-summable functions $\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$. The bilateral shift is the bounded $\mathbb{K}$-linear operator $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Sx)(n) = x(n - 1)$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $\bar{\mu}$ for the complex conjugate of $\mu$. This is the function $f_{\mu,N} : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{K}$ with $f_{\mu,N}(n) = \bar{\mu}^{\,n}$ for $-N \le n \le N$ and $f_{\mu,N}(n) = 0$ otherwise (negative powers are inverses, with the convention $0^{n} = 0$ for $n < 0$).
nodes.title: Truncated approximate eigenfunction of the bilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$, and write $\bar{\mu}$ for the complex conjugate of $\mu$. This is the vector $v_{\mu,N} \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ whose $n$-th coordinate is the truncated approximate eigenfunction $f_{\mu,N}(n)$, that is, $\bar{\mu}^{\,n}$ for $-N \le n \le N$ and $0$ otherwise; it lies in $\ell^2$ because it has finite…
nodes.title: Truncated approximate eigenvector of the bilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. The truncated approximate eigenvector $v_{\mu,N} \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, whose $n$-th coordinate is $\bar{\mu}^{\,n}$ for $-N \le n \le N$ and $0$ otherwise ($\bar{\mu}$ the complex conjugate of $\mu$), satisfies $\|v_{\mu,N}\|^2 = 2N + 1$.
nodes.title: Norm of the truncated approximate eigenvector

reading_title.source: Applying $\mu I - T$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, and let $\mu I$ be the image of $\mu$ under the algebra map from $\mathbb{K}$ to the bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, that is, $\mu$ times the identity. Then for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, $(\mu I - T)x = \mu x - Tx$.
nodes.title: Applying $\mu I - T$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the bilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let $f_{\mu,N}$ be the truncated approximate eigenfunction and $v_{\mu,N} \in \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ the corresponding truncated approximate eigenvector. Then the $n$-th coordinate of $(\mu I - S)v_{\mu,N}$ is…
nodes.title: Coordinates of the residual of the truncated approximate eigenvector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the bilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$, and let $N \in \mathbb{N}$. The truncated approximate eigenvector $v_{\mu,N}$ satisfies $\|(\mu I - S)v_{\mu,N}\|^2 = 2$, where $\mu I$ is $\mu$ times the identity operator.
nodes.title: Residual of the truncated approximate eigenvector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be the bilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$ lies in the spectrum of $S$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, that is, $\mu I - S$ is not invertible there, where $\mu I$ is $\mu$ times the identity operator.
nodes.title: Every point of the unit circle lies in the spectrum of the bilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum of the bilateral shift, as a bounded operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$, is the set of scalars $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $|\mu| = 1$; for $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{C}$ this is the unit circle.
nodes.title: Spectrum of the bilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $B$ be the bilateral backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$. The spectrum of $B$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{K})$ is the unit circle $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : |\mu| = 1\}$.
nodes.title: Spectrum of the bilateral backward shift

nodes.summary: On its bounded finite domain, the fiber supremum agrees with the supremum of natural cardinalities. Its value is independent of the chosen bound and evidence.

nodes.summary: Fiber bounds compose: the fibers of `ψ ∘ φ` are bounded by the product of the bounds.

nodes.summary: A permutation symbol has fibers of size one.

nodes.title: Permutation composition operators are unitary

nodes.summary: `C_ψ` is injective iff `ψ` is surjective: a missing value gives a basis vector in the kernel, and a surjective symbol lets every coordinate be read off from the image.
nodes.title: Composition operator is injective iff its symbol is surjective

nodes.summary: `C_ψ` is surjective iff `ψ` is injective: if `ψ a = ψ b` with `a ≠ b`, the `a`-th and `b`-th coordinates of every vector in the range agree, so `e_a` is not in the range; if `ψ` is injective, the preimage of `y` is obtained by applying the adjoint and reading off the fiber sums.
nodes.title: Composition operator is surjective iff its symbol is injective

nodes.summary: Halving pairs: the map `n ↦ n / 2` has fibers of size at most two.

nodes.summary: A composition operator on `ℓ²(ℕ, 𝕜)` is never compact: the images of the basis vectors indexed by the (necessarily infinite) range of `ψ` are pairwise orthogonal and bounded below in norm, so they have no Cauchy subsequence.
