nodes.summary: The claim that every real sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with the following property satisfies $\sum_n n |a_n| < \infty$: for every real sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $|x_n| \le 1$ for all $n$, each series $\sum_n a_{m+n} x_n$ with $m \ge 0$ converges, as the limit of its partial sums, to some $L_m$, and $\sum_m |L_m| < \infty$.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 88 (Mazur)

nodes.summary: The Scottish Book Problem 88 claim is false: there is a real sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ such that for every real sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $|x_n| \le 1$ for all $n$, each series $\sum_n a_{m+n} x_n$ with $m \ge 0$ converges, as the limit of its partial sums, to some $L_m$, and $\sum_m |L_m| < \infty$, but $\sum_n n |a_n|$ diverges.
nodes.title: Mazur's Scottish Book Problem 88 fails
Unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The forward shift of a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ is the sequence $S x$ with $(S x)_0 = 0$ and $(S x)_{n+1} = x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Forward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: For any type $K$, the backward shift of a sequence $x \colon \mathbb{N} \to K$ is the sequence $n \mapsto x_{n+1}$: it drops the coordinate $x_0$ and shifts every other coordinate down by one.
nodes.title: Backward shift of a sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every square-summable sequence $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots)$ in $\mathbb{K}$, the forward-shifted sequence $(0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ is also square-summable, that is, it belongs to $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The forward shift of a square-summable sequence is square-summable

reading_title.source: The backward shift of an $\ell^2$ sequence is in $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the backward shift $n \mapsto x_{n+1}$ of the sequence $x$ is square-summable, that is, it lies in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The backward shift of an $\ell^2$ sequence is in $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The forward shift is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ sending $x$ to the forward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, to $(0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$, which is again square-summable.
nodes.title: Forward shift as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward-shift linear map is the $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $B$ from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ to itself given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$ for all $x$ and all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Backward shift as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the forward-shift linear map applied to $x$ equals the $i$-th term of the forward shift of the sequence $x$, namely $0$ for $i = 0$ and $x_{i-1}$ for $i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the forward-shift linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the image of $x$ under the backward-shift linear map $B$ is the $i$-th term of the backward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, $(Bx)_i = x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the backward-shift linear map

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the forward shift $S x = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$ of $x$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |(S x)_i|^2 = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|^2$.
nodes.title: Square sum of the forward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the backward shift $(x_1, x_2, \dots)$ of $x$ satisfies $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_{i+1}|^2 \le \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} |x_i|^2$: the left side is a tail of the right side.
nodes.title: Square sum of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the forward shift on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, viewed as a linear map and given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The forward shift linear map preserves norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be the backward shift on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, viewed as a linear map and given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then $\|Bx\| \le \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The backward shift linear map does not increase norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift is the bounded linear operator $S$ on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$ given by $S(x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. It is bounded because $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward shift is the bounded linear operator $B$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$ for all $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(Sx)_i$ is the $i$-th term of the forward shift of $x$: $(Sx)_0 = 0$ and $(Sx)_{n+1} = x_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the backward shift $Bx$ is the $i$-th term of the backward shift of the sequence $x$, that is, $(Bx)_i = x_{i+1}$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $\|Sx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift preserves norms

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is an isometry: $\|Sx - Sy\| = \|x - y\|$ for all $x, y \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift preserves distances

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then the operator norm of $S$ is $\|S\| = 1$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift has operator norm one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be the backward shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then the operator norm of $B$ satisfies $\|B\| \le 1$.
nodes.title: The backward shift has operator norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The adjoint of the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the backward shift $B$: $S^* = B$.
nodes.title: Adjoint of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The backward shift $B$ is a left inverse of the unilateral shift $S$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$: $BS = I$, where $I$ is the identity operator.
nodes.title: Left inverse of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is injective.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift is injective

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$ let $S$ be the unilateral shift, $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$, and $B$ the backward shift, $(Bx)_n = x_{n+1}$. Then for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coordinate $(SBx)_i$ is $0$ if $i = 0$ and is $x_i$…
nodes.title: Coordinates of the unilateral shift after the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be the unilateral (forward) shift and $B$ the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, and let $e_0$ be the first standard basis vector. Then $S \circ B = 1 - P$, where $P$ is the rank-one operator $P x = \langle e_0, x \rangle e_0 = x_0 e_0$.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift composed with the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$, given by $S(x_0, x_1, \dots) = (0, x_0, x_1, \dots)$. Then $S$ is not surjective.
nodes.title: The unilateral shift is not surjective

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. Then the sequence $(c^i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ lies in $\ell^2$, that is, $\sum_{i} \|c^i\|^2 < \infty$.
nodes.title: Geometric sequences with ratio of norm less than one are square-summable

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. The geometric vector of $c$ is the sequence $(1, c, c^2, \dots)$, that is $i \mapsto c^i$, regarded as an element of the Hilbert space $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ of square-summable sequences.
nodes.title: Geometric vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. For every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the $i$-th coordinate of the geometric vector of $c$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is $c^i$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the geometric vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. The geometric vector $(1, c, c^2, \dots)$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is nonzero, since its $0$-th coordinate is $1$.
nodes.title: The geometric vector is nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $c \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|c\| < 1$. Let $v = (1, c, c^2, \dots)$ be the geometric vector of $c$ in $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and let $B$ be the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Then $Bv = c\,v$.
nodes.title: Backward shift of the geometric vector

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The operator norm of the identity operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The identity on ℓ²(ℕ) has norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, let $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$, and let $\mu I$ be the image of $\mu$ under the algebra map from $\mathbb{K}$ into the bounded operators, i.e. $\mu$ times the identity $I$. Then $(\mu I - T)x = \mu x - Tx$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Applying a scalar operator minus an operator on ℓ²(ℕ)

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be the unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|\mu\| < 1$ lies in the spectrum of $S$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The open unit ball lies in the spectrum of the unilateral shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $B$ be the backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. Every $\mu \in \mathbb{K}$ with $\|\mu\| < 1$ lies in the spectrum of $B$ in the algebra of bounded operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: The open unit ball lies in the spectrum of the backward shift

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The spectrum over $\mathbb{K}$ of the unilateral shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is the closed unit ball $\{\mu \in \mathbb{K} : |\mu| \le 1\}$ of $\mathbb{K}$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $x$ under the weighted forward shift operator with weights $w$ is as a sequence the weighted forward shift of $x$: its term at index $0$ is $0$ and its term at index $n + 1$ is $w_n x_n$ for every $n$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be a weight sequence whose norms $\|w_n\|$ are bounded above. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the image of $x$ under the weighted forward shift linear map, viewed as a sequence, is the weighted forward shift of $x$: its coordinate $0$ is $0$ and its coordinate $n + 1$ is $w_n x_n$ for every $n$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with $\sup_n |w_n| < \infty$, and let $(e_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be the standard basis vectors of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and write $e_n$ for the $n$-th standard basis vector of $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $n$, the weighted backward shift $B_w$ satisfies $B_w e_{n+1} = \overline{w_n}\, e_n$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli, and let $S_w$ be the weighted forward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. If $C$ is a real number with $|w_n| \le C$ for every $n$, then the operator norm of $S_w$ is at most $C$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. The weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ has operator norm $\|S_w\| = \sup_n |w_n|$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$. The weighted backward shift $B_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$, has operator norm $\|B_w\| = \sup_n |w_n|$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $(w_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a bounded sequence in $\mathbb{K}$, and let $B_w$ be the weighted backward shift on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, given by $(B_w x)_i = \overline{w_i}\, x_{i+1}$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the composite $S_w B_w$ satisfies $(S_w B_w x)_0 = 0$ and $(S_w B_w x)_i = |w_{i-1}|^2 x_i$ for every $i \ge 1$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{K}$ be weights with bounded moduli. If $w_n = 0$ for some $n$, then the weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ is not injective.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\sum_{k=0}^{n} x(k) = (n+1)\,(Cx)(n)$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every natural number $N$, the norm of $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$, computed in $\mathbb{K}$, equals the real number $(\sqrt{N})^{-1}$; for $N = 0$ both sides are $0$, with the convention $0^{-1} = 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $C$ be the Cesàro operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$. nodes.summary: For a bounded continuous function $f$ on $[0, 1]$, its clamped extension is the function $\tilde f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $\tilde f(t) = f(\max(0, \min(1, t)))$. Thus $\tilde f(t) = f(0)$ for $t < 0$, $\tilde f(t) = f(t)$ for $t \in [0, 1]$, and $\tilde f(t) = f(1)$ for $t > 1$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$. The essential range of $\varphi$ with respect to $\mu$ is the set of $z \in \mathbb{C}$ such that $\mu(\{x \in \alpha : |\varphi(x) - z| < \varepsilon\}) > 0$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$ and let $\varphi, \psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$. If $\varphi = \psi$ $\mu$-almost everywhere, then $\varphi$ and $\psi$ have the same essential range with respect to $\mu$.

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on a measurable space $\alpha$, let $\varphi : \alpha \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$. nodes.summary: A rectilinear cycle is a finitely supported function from rectilinear rectangles to $\mathbb{Z}$, that is, a finite formal sum $\sum_r n_r\, r$ of rectilinear rectangles $r$ with integer coefficients $n_r$, read as the corresponding integer combination of oriented rectangle boundaries.
nodes.title: Rectilinear cycle

nodes.summary: For a rectilinear rectangle $r$, this is the rectilinear cycle in which $r$ has coefficient $1$ and every other rectangle has coefficient $0$, that is, the boundary of $r$ with the orientation given by its corner order.
nodes.title: The cycle of a single rectangle

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. For a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, a finite formal sum $\sum_r n_r\, r$ of rectangles $r$ with integer coefficients $n_r$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is $\sum_r n_r \int_{\partial r} f$, where $\int_{\partial r} f$ is the boundary integral of $f$ over the oriented rectangle $r$.
nodes.title: Contour integral over a rectilinear cycle

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. For rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma + \Lambda$ equals the integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ plus the integral of $f$ over $\Lambda$.
nodes.title: Additivity of the contour integral in the cycle

nodes.summary: For every rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, every complex Banach space $E$ and every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$, the contour integral of $f$ over $-\Gamma$ is the negative of the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Reversing a cycle negates its integral

nodes.summary: For rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$, a complex Banach space $E$ and a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma - \Lambda$ equals the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ minus the contour integral of $f$ over $\Lambda$.
nodes.title: Integral over a difference of cycles

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. The map sending a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ to the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is an additive group homomorphism from rectilinear cycles to $E$.
nodes.title: Contour integration as an additive map

nodes.summary: Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. A rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, read as a filling by rectangles, is supported in $G$ when, for every rectangle $r$ whose coefficient in $\Gamma$ is nonzero, the closed carrier of $r$ is contained in $G$.
nodes.title: Rectangle filling supported in a set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ be complex differentiable on $G$. If $\Gamma$ is a rectilinear cycle whose rectangle filling is supported in $G$, that is, the closed rectangle of every rectangle occurring in $\Gamma$ with nonzero coefficient is contained in $G$, then the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Cauchy–Goursat theorem for rectilinear cycles

nodes.summary: Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Two rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are homologous in $G$ when the rectangle filling of $\Gamma - \Lambda$ is supported in $G$: every rectangle with nonzero coefficient in $\Gamma - \Lambda$ has its closed carrier contained in $G$.
nodes.title: Rectilinear cycles homologous in a set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ be complex differentiable on $G$. nodes.summary: For a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ and a point $w \in \mathbb{C}$, the index of $\Gamma$ about $w$ is $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma \frac{dz}{z - w}$, the contour integral over $\Gamma$ of $z \mapsto (z - w)^{-1}$, multiplied by $(2\pi i)^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Index of a rectilinear cycle

nodes.summary: For a fixed point $w \in \mathbb{C}$, the map sending a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ to its index about $w$ is an additive group homomorphism from rectilinear cycles to $\mathbb{C}$.

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$ when $f$ is holomorphic on some punctured disc $0 < |z - c| < r$ with $r > 0$, $f(z)$ has no finite limit as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$, and $|f(z)|$ does not tend to $\infty$ as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$.
nodes.title: Essential isolated singularity

nodes.summary: Suppose $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$. Then there is at most one $w \in \mathbb{C}$ for which some $r > 0$ makes the set $\{z : 0 < |z - c| < r,\ f(z) = w\}$ finite; that is, with at most one exception, $f$ takes every complex value infinitely often on every punctured disc around $c$.

Normal families

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$. The sequence is locally uniformly bounded on $U$ when every $x \in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$ and a real $C \ge 0$ such that $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in V$.
nodes.title: Locally uniformly bounded sequence of functions

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open, let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $C \ge 0$ be real. If $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in U$, then $(F_n)$ is locally uniformly bounded on $U$.
nodes.title: A uniformly bounded sequence on an open set is locally uniformly bounded

nodes.summary: Let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is locally uniformly bounded on $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Then for every compact set $K \subseteq U$ there is a real $C \ge 0$ with $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in K$.
nodes.title: Locally uniformly bounded sequences are uniformly bounded on compact subsets

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, each holomorphic on $U$, that is locally uniformly bounded on $U$. Then there are a strictly increasing map $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, holomorphic on $U$, such that $F_{\varphi(n)} \to f$ locally uniformly on $U$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: Montel's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and preconnected, and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, each holomorphic on $U$, that is locally uniformly bounded on $U$. Let $S \subseteq U$ have an accumulation point $x_0 \in U$, and let $g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $F_n(z) \to g(z)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every $z \in S$. Then there is a function…

Removable lines for holomorphic functions

nodes.summary: The real axis is the set $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z = 0\}$.
nodes.title: Real axis

nodes.summary: The imaginary axis is the set $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z = 0\}$.
nodes.title: Imaginary axis

nodes.summary: The coordinate axes of $\mathbb{C}$: the union of the real axis and the imaginary axis.
nodes.title: Coordinate axes

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and holomorphic on the complement of the coordinate axes. Then $f$ is holomorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Continuous functions holomorphic off the coordinate axes are entire
Rouché's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $c \in \mathbb{C}$ and $R > 0$, and let $f$ and $g$ be analytic at every point of the closed disc $|z - c| \le R$. If $|g(z)| < |f(z)|$ for every $z$ on the circle $|z - c| = R$, then $f$ and $f + g$ have the same number of zeros in the open disc $|z - c| < R$, counted with multiplicity: the divisors of $f$ and of $f + g$ on the open disc have equal sums.
nodes.title: Rouché's theorem on a disc

nodes.summary: Let $R > 0$, let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$ and in normal form (at every point $f$ is either analytic, or has a pole and takes the value $0$ there), and let $g : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be analytic on $\mathbb{C}$. If $|g(z)| < |f(z)|$ for every $z$ with $|z| = R$, then $f + g$ and $f$ have the same number of zeros in the closed disk $|z| \le R$, counted with multiplicity: the…

reading_title.source: A $1$-periodic entire function bounded by $C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ is constant

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be entire with $f(s + 1) = f(s)$ for all $s \in \mathbb{C}$, and suppose there is a real constant $C$ such that $|f(s)| \le C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ for every $s$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$. Then $f$ is constant.
nodes.title: A $1$-periodic entire function bounded by $C e^{|\operatorname{Im} s|}$ is constant

nodes.summary: There is a sequence $(a_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of complex numbers, not all zero, such that the power series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} a_k z^k$ converges absolutely for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and its sum vanishes at infinitely many points $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: A nonzero entire power series with infinitely many zeros

nodes.summary: Let $f$ and $g$ be entire functions with $f(z)^3 + g(z)^3 = 1$ for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$. Then $f$ and $g$ are constant.
nodes.title: Entire solutions of the Fermat cubic are constant

nodes.summary: If $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is entire and injective, then there are $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $a \ne 0$ such that $f(z) = az + b$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Injective entire functions are affine

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set all of whose points are isolated: for each $z \in S$ there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that no point $w \ne z$ of $S$ satisfies $|w - z| < \varepsilon$. Then there is an entire function $f$ whose zeros are exactly the points of $S$, all of them simple: $f'(z) \ne 0$ for every $z \in S$.
nodes.title: Weierstrass theorem on prescribed simple zeros
Countable dense sets as preimages under entire functions

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for any two countable dense subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$, there is an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $f(z) \in B$ if and only if $z \in A$; that is, $f^{-1}(B) = A$.
nodes.title: Erdős's problem on countable dense preimages

nodes.summary: For any two countable dense subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\mathbb{C}$, there is an entire function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ such that for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $f(z) \in B$ if and only if $z \in A$; that is, $f^{-1}(B) = A$.
nodes.title: Every countable dense set is a preimage of any other under an entire function

reading_title.source: Hayman auxiliary function $A$

nodes.summary: For a function $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, $A(r)$ is the real part of $r\,G'(r)/G(r)$, where $G'$ is the complex derivative of $G$.
nodes.title: Hayman auxiliary function $A$

reading_title.source: Hayman auxiliary function $B$

nodes.summary: For a function $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, $B(r) = r\,A'(r)$, where $A$ is the Hayman auxiliary function of $G$, viewed as a real function of $r$, and $A'$ is its derivative.
nodes.title: Hayman auxiliary function $B$

nodes.summary: Let $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, let $R_0$ and $\rho$ be real numbers, write $G'$ for the complex derivative of $G$ and $A$, $B$ for the Hayman auxiliary functions of $G$, and say that a property holds for $r$ near $\rho$ if there is $\eta > 0$ such that it holds for every $r \in (R_0, \rho)$ with $r > \rho - \eta$. Then $G$ is Hayman admissible on $(R_0, \rho)$ when $0 < R_0 < \rho$; $G$ is analytic on the…
nodes.title: Hayman-admissible function (finite radius)

nodes.summary: Let $G : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be Hayman admissible on $(R_0, \rho)$, with Hayman auxiliary functions $A$ and $B$. Let $(c_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be complex numbers such that $\sum_{n \ge 0} c_n z^n$ converges absolutely to $G(z)$ for every complex $z$ with $|z| < \rho$, and let $(r_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be real numbers such that for all sufficiently large $n$, $r_n \in (R_0, \rho)$, $A(r_n) = n$, and $r_n$ is the only…

Liouville-type theorems

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be holomorphic on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}$, and suppose that there is a real number $C$ with $|f(z)| \le C$ for every $z \ne 0$. Then there is a constant $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for every $z \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Bounded holomorphic functions on the punctured plane are constant

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be an entire function. If there is a complex polynomial $p$ such that the $k$th derivative of $f$ satisfies $f^{(k)}(z) = p(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$, then there is a complex polynomial $q$ such that $f(z) = q(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: An entire function with a polynomial derivative is a polynomial

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be an entire function such that $f(z)/z \to 0$ as $|z| \to \infty$. Then $f$ is constant: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $f(z) = c$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: An entire function of sublinear growth is constant
Mittag-Leffler theorem

nodes.summary: For a point $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and a finitely supported sequence $c = (c_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of complex coefficients, the principal part at $s$ with coefficients $c$ is the function $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $z \mapsto \sum_k c_k (z - s)^{-(k+1)}$, the sum running over the finitely many $k$ with $c_k \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Principal part with finitely many coefficients

nodes.summary: For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and every finitely supported sequence $c$ of complex coefficients, the principal part at $s$ with coefficients $c$ is analytic at every point $z \neq s$.
nodes.title: The principal part is analytic away from its pole

nodes.summary: For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$ and every finitely supported sequence $c$ of complex coefficients, the principal part at $s$ with coefficients $c$ is meromorphic at every point of $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: The principal part is meromorphic

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set that is discrete in the subspace topology, and for each $s \in S$ let $c_s$ be a finitely supported sequence of complex coefficients. Then there is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic on $\mathbb{C} \setminus S$, meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$, and such that for every $s \in S$ the difference between $f$ and the principal part at $s$ with…
nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler theorem, discrete-subspace form

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be a closed set such that every $z \in S$ has a radius $\varepsilon > 0$ for which the punctured disk $\{w : 0 < |w - z| < \varepsilon\}$ contains no point of $S$, and for each $s \in S$ let $c_s$ be a finitely supported sequence of complex coefficients. Then there is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is holomorphic on $\mathbb{C} \setminus S$, meromorphic on all of…

nodes.title: Hayman Problem 2.32: a non-exponential solution of the Rényi–Vincze conditions

nodes.summary: There are no function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real numbers $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ such that $f$ is not the function $z \mapsto c\,e^z$ for any real $c > 0$; $a_n \ge 0$ for every $n$; $a_n \ne 0$ for infinitely many $n$; for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ has sum $f(z)$; $f$ is entire; and either $\int_0^\infty a_n x^n / f(x)\,dx = 1$ for every $n \ge 0$, or…
nodes.title: No non-exponential solution of the Rényi–Vincze conditions
Spherical area and valence of meromorphic functions

nodes.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, $a \in \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, the root count of $f$ at $a$ in radius $r$ is the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in the open disk $|z| < r$, counted with multiplicity: the sum over $z \in \mathbb{C}$ of the positive part of the divisor of $f - a$ on that disk at $z$ (the sum is taken to be $0$ if infinitely many terms are nonzero).
nodes.title: Root count

nodes.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, $n(f, r)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$, over all $a \in \mathbb{C}$, of the root count of $f$ at $a$ in radius $r$, that is, of the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Maximum valence

nodes.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the spherical density of $f$ at $z$ is $|f'(z)|^2 / (1 + |f(z)|^2)^2$, where $f'(z)$ is the complex derivative of $f$ at $z$, taken to be $0$ where $f$ is not differentiable.
nodes.title: Spherical density

nodes.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, the normalized spherical area $A(f, r)$ of $f$ on the disk $|z| < r$ is $\frac{1}{\pi}$ times the Lebesgue integral of the spherical density of $f$ over the open disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < r\}$ (the integral is taken to be $0$ if the density is not integrable there).
nodes.title: Normalized spherical area

nodes.summary: A function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is nonconstant if there are points $u, v \in \mathbb{C}$ at which $f$ is complex differentiable and $f(u) \ne f(v)$.
nodes.title: Germ-wise nonconstant function

nodes.summary: A function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has bounded root counts if for every real $r$ the root counts of $f$ in radius $r$, that is, the numbers of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity, are bounded above as $a$ ranges over $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Bounded root counts

nodes.summary: The statement that every function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and nonconstant (complex differentiable at two points where it takes different values) has bounded root counts (for every real $r$, the numbers of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$, counted with multiplicity, are bounded above as $a$ ranges over $\mathbb{C}$) and satisfies
nodes.title: Hayman's spherical-area ratio conjecture

nodes.summary: Not every function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and nonconstant (complex differentiable at two points where it takes different values) has bounded root counts and satisfies $\liminf_{r \to \infty} n(f, r)/A(f, r) = 1$, where $n(f, r)$ is the maximum valence and $A(f, r)$ the normalized spherical area of $f$ on the disk $|z| < r$.
nodes.title: Hayman's spherical-area ratio conjecture is false
Turán's three-value problem

reading_title.source: Multiplicity of a root of $f = w$

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $w, z \in \mathbb{C}$. The multiplicity of $z$ as a root of the equation $f = w$ is an extended natural number: it is $\infty$ if $f(t) = w$ for every $t \neq z$ in some neighbourhood of $z$; otherwise it is $n$ if $f - w$ has meromorphic order $n \ge 0$ at $z$, and it is $0$ if that order is negative or $f - w$ is not meromorphic at $z$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a root of $f = w$

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. The multiplicity of $z$ as a pole of $f$, that is, the multiplicity of the value $\infty$ at $z$, is $-n$ if $f$ has finite meromorphic order $n < 0$ at $z$, and $0$ otherwise. In particular it is $0$ unless $f$ has a pole at $z$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a pole

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $w$ be a point of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$. The multiplicity of $w$ as a value of $f$ at $z$ is the multiplicity of $z$ as a root of $f = w$ when $w$ is finite, and the multiplicity of $z$ as a pole of $f$ when $w = \infty$.
nodes.title: Multiplicity of a value on the Riemann sphere

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has bounded value distribution if for every real $r > 0$ there is a natural number $C$ such that, for every value $w$ of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ and every open disc of radius $r$, the multiplicities of $w$ as a value of $f$ at the points of any finite subset of the disc add up to at most $C$.
nodes.title: Bounded value distribution

nodes.summary: The statement that every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with the following properties has bounded value distribution: $f$ is meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$; for every $w \in \mathbb{C}$ there is a point at which $f - w$ has finite meromorphic order; and there are three distinct values $w_1, w_2, w_3$ of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ such that for every real $r > 0$ there is a natural number…
nodes.title: Turán's three-value question

nodes.summary: There is a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, meromorphic on $\mathbb{C}$, such that for every $w \in \mathbb{C}$ there is a point at which $f - w$ has finite meromorphic order, together with three distinct values $w_1, w_2, w_3$ of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ such that for every real $r > 0$ there is a natural number $C$ for which, for each $i$ and every open disc of radius $r$, the…
nodes.title: Turán's three-value question has a negative answer
Wiman–Valiron theory

nodes.summary: For a function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and real numbers $p$ and $x_0$, this is the set of real numbers $x \ge x_0$ such that $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, where $h(x)^p$ is the real power and $h'(x)$ is the derivative of $h$ at $x$, taken to be $0$ where $h$ is not differentiable.
nodes.title: Power-growth exceptional set

nodes.summary: Let $p > 1$ and $x_0$ be real numbers, and let $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuously differentiable, with $h(x) > 0$ for all $x \ge x_0$ and $h$ nondecreasing on $[x_0, \infty)$. Then the power-growth exceptional set of $h$, the set of $x \ge x_0$ with $h(x)^p \le h'(x)$, has finite Lebesgue measure.
nodes.title: The power-growth exceptional set has finite measure

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin is $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$, where $f^{(n)}$ is the $n$th iterated complex derivative of $f$.
nodes.title: Wiman Taylor coefficient

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, a real number $r$ and a natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$ is the real number $|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Taylor coefficient of $f$ at the origin. It is the modulus of the $n$th Taylor term of $f$ on the circle of radius $|r|$.
nodes.title: Wiman term

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term $\mu(f, r)$ is the supremum over $n \in \mathbb{N}$ of the Wiman terms $|a_n| \, |r|^n$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ is the $n$th Wiman Taylor coefficient of $f$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum term

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and a real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus $M(f, r)$ is the supremum of $|f(z)|$ over all $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = |r|$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum modulus

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $|r|$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.
nodes.title: Wiman term at the absolute value of the radius

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum term at the absolute value of the radius

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $|r|$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: Wiman maximum modulus at the absolute value of the radius

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, every real number $r$ and every natural number $n$, the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $-r$ and index $n$ equals the Wiman term of $f$ at radius $r$ and index $n$.
nodes.title: Wiman term at a negated radius

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum term of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: The Wiman maximum term is even in the radius

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and every real number $r$, the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $-r$ equals the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: The Wiman maximum modulus is even in the radius

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is transcendental when there is no complex polynomial $p$ with $f(z) = p(z)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Transcendental functions

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous, let $r$ be a real number and let $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|z| = r$. Then $|f(z)| \le M(f, r)$, where $M(f, r)$ is the Wiman maximum modulus of $f$ at radius $r$.
nodes.title: Values on a circle are bounded by the maximum modulus

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $\mu$ be real numbers with $M \ge 0$, $\mu \ge 0$ and $\log \mu \ge 0$, where $\log$ is the real logarithm with $\log 0 = 0$. If $M \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$, then $M^3 \le \mu^3 (\log \mu)^2$.
nodes.title: Cubing a Wiman 2/3 bound

nodes.summary: For every real $C > 0$ there is a real $U > 1$ such that for all reals $\mu$ and $A$ with $U \le \mu \le A$ and $A \le C \mu \bigl(1 + (\log A)^{81/128}\bigr)$, we have $A \le \mu (\log \mu)^{2/3}$.
nodes.title: Absorbing constants into the exponent gap

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $r \ge 0$. Then there is a point $z$ with $|z| = r$ such that $|f(w)| \le |f(z)|$ for every $w$ with $|w| = r$, and the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|w| = r} |f(w)|$ equals $|f(z)|$.
nodes.title: The maximum modulus is attained

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and a real number $r$, the radial majorant of $f$ at $r$ is $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$, the sum of the radial Taylor terms at radius $|r|$. By convention $M_f(r) = 0$ when this series diverges.
nodes.title: Radial majorant

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $0 \le |a_n| \, |r|^n$.
nodes.title: Radial Taylor terms are nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every real $r$, the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ converges.
nodes.title: Summability of the radial Taylor terms

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin and every real number $r$, the radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ (taken to be $0$ when the series diverges) satisfies $0 \le M_f(r)$.
nodes.title: The radial majorant is nonnegative

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{k \ge 0} |a_k| \, |r|^k$ be its radial majorant. For every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n| \, |r|^n \le M_f(r)$.
nodes.title: Each radial Taylor term is at most the radial majorant

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin, and let $M_f(r) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| \, |r|^n$ be its radial majorant, taken to be $0$ when the series diverges. For a real number $x$, the Wiman growth of $f$ at $x$ is $\log M_f(e^x)$, the logarithm of the radial majorant at radius $e^x$, with the convention $\log 0 = 0$.
nodes.title: Wiman growth function

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, the Wiman coefficient measure of $f$ is the measure $\mu_f = \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n|\,\delta_n$ on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n$ mass $|a_n|$.
nodes.title: Wiman coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ have Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, with mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For a real number $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ is the exponential tilt of $\mu_f$ by $n \mapsto xn$: the measure with density $e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$.
nodes.title: Tilted coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $\mu_f(\{n\}) = |a_n|$.
nodes.title: Point masses of the Wiman coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which gives each $n \in \mathbb{N}$ mass $|a_n|$, where $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. For every real $x$, the function $n \mapsto e^{xn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.
nodes.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure are finite

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. The set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$ is all of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The exponential-integrability set of the Wiman coefficient measure is the whole line

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. Every real $x$ lies in the interior of the set of real $t$ for which $n \mapsto e^{tn}$ is integrable with respect to $\mu_f$.
nodes.title: Every real parameter is interior to the exponential-integrability set

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$ at $0$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$,
nodes.title: Exponential moments of the Wiman coefficient measure equal the Wiman majorant

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, and let $\mu_f$ be its coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$, which has mass $|a_n|$ at $n$. For every real $x$, the moment generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the radial majorant $M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$.
nodes.title: Moment generating function of the coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the cumulant generating function of $n \mapsto n$ under $\mu_f$ at $x$, namely $\log \int e^{xn}\,d\mu_f(n)$, equals the Wiman growth $G_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$, where $M_f$ is the Wiman majorant of $f$.
nodes.title: The Wiman growth is the cumulant generating function of the coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$. If $a_n \ne 0$ for some $n$, then the Wiman coefficient measure $\mu_f$ of $f$ is not the zero measure.
nodes.title: A nonzero Taylor coefficient makes the Wiman coefficient measure nonzero

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function such that $f^{(n)}(0)/n! \ne 0$ for some $n$, and let $\mu_f$ be its Wiman coefficient measure on $\mathbb{N}$. For every real $x$, the Wiman tilted measure of $f$ at $x$, which has density $n \mapsto e^{xn} / \int e^{xm}\,d\mu_f(m)$ with respect to $\mu_f$, is a probability measure.
nodes.title: The Wiman tilted measure is a probability measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms $T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ gives the singleton $\{n\}$ mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).
nodes.title: Atoms of the tilted coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and Taylor terms $T_n(r) = |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $x$, the tilted coefficient measure $\mu_{f,x}$ equals $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \frac{T_n(e^x)}{M_f(e^x)}\,\delta_n$, the measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with mass $T_n(e^x) / M_f(e^x)$ at each $n$ (with the convention $t/0 = 0$).
nodes.title: Atomic form of the tilted coefficient measure

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$ be the logarithm of its radial Taylor majorant at radius $e^x$ (with $\log 0 = 0$). Then $\Phi$ is twice continuously differentiable on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The logarithmic majorant is $C^2$

nodes.summary:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $
u_x$ be the coefficient measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with $
u_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi'(x) = \int n \, d
u_x(n)$, the mean of $n$ under $
u_x$.
nodes.title: Derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a mean

nodes.summary:
Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. For real $x$, let $
u_x$ be the coefficient measure tilted at $x$, the probability measure on $\mathbb{N}$ with $
u_x(\{n\}) = |a_n| e^{nx} / \sum_{m \ge 0} |a_m| e^{mx}$. Then $\Phi''(x)$ is the variance of $n$ under $
u_x$.
nodes.title: Second derivative of the logarithmic majorant as a variance

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function whose Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin are not all zero, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. Then $\Phi''(x) \ge 0$ for every real $x$.
nodes.title: The logarithmic majorant has nonnegative second derivative

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $r$ be real. Then the set of Taylor terms $\{|a_n|\,|r|^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is bounded above.
nodes.title: The Taylor terms are bounded above

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_k |a_k|\,|r|^k$. For every real $r$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le \mu(r)$.
nodes.title: Each Taylor term is at most the maximum term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For all real $r$ and $c$, $\mu(r) \le c$ if and only if $|a_n|\,|r|^n \le c$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Bounding the maximum term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. For every real $r$ there is an $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $|a_n|\,|r|^n = \mu(r)$.
nodes.title: The maximum term is attained by a Taylor term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0)/n!$, radial majorant $M_f(r) = \sum_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$, maximum term $\mu_f(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and logarithmic majorant $g_f(x) = \log M_f(e^x)$. For every real $x$, $M_f(e^x) \le 8\,\mu_f(e^x)\,\bigl(1 + \sqrt{g_f''(x)}\bigr)$.
nodes.title: Corrected Rosenbloom estimate

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$ and maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = |r|} |f(z)|$. Then $\mu(r) \le M(r)$ for every real $r > 0$.
nodes.title: Cauchy's inequality for the maximum term

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n = f^{(n)}(0) / n!$ at the origin. For every $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} a_n z^n$ converges unconditionally to $f(z)$.

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and let $r \ge 0$. Then the maximum modulus $M(r) = \sup_{|z| = r} |f(z)|$ satisfies $M(r) \le \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| r^n$.
nodes.title: The maximum modulus is at most the radial Taylor majorant

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\mu(r) > 1$ for all real $r \ge R$.

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an entire function that is not a polynomial function, with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin and maximum term $\mu(r) = \sup_n |a_n|\,|r|^n$. Then there is $R$ such that $\log \mu(r) > 0$ for all real $r \ge R$.

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire function with Taylor coefficients $a_n$ at the origin, and let $\Phi(x) = \log \sum_{n \ge 0} |a_n| e^{nx}$. nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ carry its Haar measure normalized to total mass $1$. There is no continuous $\mathbb{C}$-linear map $\pi : L^1(\mathbb{T}) \to H^1$ with $\pi(f) = f$ for every $f \in H^1$.

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the set of functions $x : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. It represents $\{-1, 1\}^n$, with true standing for $1$ and false for $-1$.
nodes.title: Boolean cube

nodes.summary: The sign of a Boolean value $b$ is the real number $\sigma(b)$ given by $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

nodes.summary: For a set $S$ of coordinates among $n$, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ is the real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates given by $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate: $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$. That is, $\hat f(S)$ is the uniform expectation of $f \chi_S$.

nodes.title: Lagrange basis polynomials on the cube are point indicators

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $y$ be a point of the cube, identified with the point of $\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$ is true and $0$ when it is false. Then the real multilinear extension of $f$ evaluated at $y$ equals $1$ if $f(y)$ is true and $0$ if $f(y)$ is false.
nodes.title: The multilinear extension agrees with its function on the cube

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every Boolean value $b$, the real multilinear extension of the constant function $b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the constant polynomial $1$ if $b$ is true and the constant polynomial $0$ if $b$ is false.
nodes.title: Multilinear extension of a constant function

nodes.summary: For every coordinate $i$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, the real multilinear extension of the projection $x \mapsto x_i$ is the variable $X_i$.
nodes.title: Multilinear extension of a coordinate projection

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, and read true as $1$ and false as $0$. The Boolean degree of $f$ is the total degree of the multilinear extension of $f$: the real multilinear polynomial in $n$ variables that takes the value $f(x)$ at every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$.
nodes.title: Boolean degree

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every Boolean value $b$, the constant function $x \mapsto b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean degree $0$.
nodes.title: Constant functions have Boolean degree zero

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $i < n$, the coordinate projection $x \mapsto x_i$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean degree $1$.
nodes.title: Coordinate projections have Boolean degree one

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the all-true function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the Boolean AND of all coordinates: it sends $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ to true exactly when $x_i$ is true for every $i < n$. In dimension $0$ it is constantly true.
nodes.title: All-true function

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the real multilinear extension of the AND function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ (true exactly when every coordinate is true) is the monomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i$.
nodes.title: Multilinear extension of the AND function

nodes.summary: The all-true function on the Boolean cube of dimension $2$, $(x_0, x_1) \mapsto x_0 \wedge x_1$, has Boolean degree $2$; that is, its real multilinear extension has total degree $2$.
nodes.title: The two-bit AND has Boolean degree two

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $g$ be the real function with $g(x) = 1$ if $f(x)$ is true and $g(x) = 0$ otherwise. Then $g$ has Fourier degree at most the Boolean degree of $f$: every Fourier coefficient $\hat g(S)$ with $|S|$ greater than the total degree of the multilinear extension of $f$ vanishes.
nodes.title: Fourier degree is at most Boolean degree

nodes.summary: For finite sets $S$ and $T$, the Fourier character of $S$ at $T$ is the real number $\chi_S(T) = (-1)^{|S \cap T|}$.
nodes.title: Fourier character on finite sets

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. For a finite subset $S$ of $\iota$, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ over $E$ is
nodes.title: Fourier coefficient on the subsets of a finite set

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has exactly $2^n$ points.
nodes.title: Number of points of the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For a finite set $E$, this is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the functions $b$ from $E$ to $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ given by $b(a) = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and $b(a) = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$. Its inverse sends $b$ to the set $\{a \in E : b(a) = \mathrm{false}\}$.
nodes.title: Subsets of a finite set as indicator functions

nodes.summary: For a finite set $E$ with $n = |E|$ elements, fix a bijection $e$ from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (an enumeration of $E$, chosen noncanonically). This is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ that sends $T$ to the point $x$ with $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$, for every $a \in E$.
nodes.title: Subsets of a finite set as points of the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in the fixed order $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$ used to encode subsets of $E$ as points of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$. For every subset $T \subseteq E$ and every coordinate $j < m$, the $j$-th coordinate of the point encoding $T$ is true if $e_j \notin T$ and false if $e_j \in T$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of an encoded subset

nodes.summary: For finite sets $S \subseteq E$ with $n = |E|$, let $e$ be the fixed bijection from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the enumeration of $E$ used to identify subsets of $E$ with points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$). The reindexed set is the image $e(S) = \{e(a) : a \in S\}$, a subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Reindexing a subset as a set of coordinates

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$; this order identifies subsets of $E$ with points of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$. A point $x$ of that cube decodes to the subset $\{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$ of $E$; this inverts the encoding of subsets of $E$ as cube points.
nodes.title: Decoding a cube point as a subset

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$. Encode a subset $T \subseteq E$ as the point $x_T$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ whose $j$-th coordinate is false exactly when $e_j \in T$, and decode a point $x$ as the subset $\{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$. Then for every subset $T \subseteq E$, decoding $x_T$ gives back $T$.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts encoding

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$, and encode a subset $T \subseteq E$ as the point $x_T$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ whose $j$-th coordinate is false exactly when $e_j \in T$. For all subsets $S, T \subseteq E$,
nodes.title: Subset characters agree with cube characters

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ with $m$ elements, listed in a fixed order as $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$, and decode a point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$ as the subset $D(x) = \{e_j : x_j = \mathrm{false}\}$ of $E$. Let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$ and let $S \subseteq E$. Then the Fourier coefficient…
nodes.title: Subset Fourier coefficients agree with cube Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite subset of a type $\iota$ and let $f$ be a function from finite subsets of $\iota$ to $\mathbb{R}$. For every subset $T \subseteq E$,
nodes.title: Fourier inversion on the subsets of a finite set
