Fourier transform on finite abelian groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$. The discrete Fourier transform of $f$ is the function on the additive characters $\psi$ of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$ (maps with $\psi(0) = 1$ and $\psi(a + b) = \psi(a)\psi(b)$) given by $\hat f(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) f(x)$.
nodes.title: Discrete Fourier transform on a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|$ elements, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat f(\psi) = \sum_{y \in G} \psi(y) f(y)$ for the discrete Fourier transform of $f$ at an additive character $\psi$ of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. Then for every $x \in G$, $f(x) = \frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} \overline{\psi(x)} \, \hat f(\psi)$, where $\psi$ runs over all additive characters of $G$ with values in…
nodes.title: Fourier inversion on a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with $|G|$ elements, let $f, g : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat h(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) h(x)$ for the discrete Fourier transform of $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$ at an additive character $\psi$ of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$. Then $\sum_{x \in G} \overline{f(x)} \, g(x)$ equals $\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} \overline{\hat f(\psi)} \, \hat g(\psi)$, where $\psi$ runs over all…
nodes.title: Plancherel formula on a finite abelian group

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $t \in G$, and $\psi$ an additive character of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat h(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) h(x)$ for the discrete Fourier transform of $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$. If $g(x) = f(x - t)$ for all $x \in G$, then $\hat g(\psi) = \psi(t) \hat f(\psi)$.
nodes.title: Translation modulates the discrete Fourier transform
Donoho–Stark uncertainty principle

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $\psi$ be an additive character of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$, that is, a map $\psi : G \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\psi(0) = 1$ and $\psi(a + b) = \psi(a)\psi(b)$. Then $|\psi(x)| = 1$ for every $x \in G$.
nodes.title: Characters of a finite abelian group have absolute value one

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then $\sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 = |G| \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$, where $\psi$ runs over all additive characters of $G$.
nodes.title: Squared-norm Plancherel identity for the finite Fourier transform

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ such that the discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$. Then for every $x \in G$, $|f(x)|^2 \le \frac{|B|}{|G|} \sum_{y \in G} |f(y)|^2$.
nodes.title: Pointwise bound from a small Fourier support

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ such that the discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$. Then for every $A \subseteq G$, $\sum_{x \in A} |f(x)|^2 \le \frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|G|} \sum_{x \in G} |f(x)|^2$.
nodes.title: Concentration bound for a function with small Fourier support

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $A \subseteq G$, let $B$ be any set of additive characters of $G$, and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ vanish outside $A$, with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then $\sum_{\psi \in B} |\hat f(\psi)|^2 \le \frac{|A| \cdot |B|}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} |\hat f(\psi)|^2$, where the last sum runs over all additive characters $\psi$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Concentration bound for the Fourier transform of a function with small support

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ be a nonzero function with discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$. Then $|G| \le |\{x \in G : f(x) \neq 0\}| \cdot |\{\psi : \hat f(\psi) \neq 0\}|$, where $\psi$ ranges over the additive characters of $G$.
nodes.title: Donoho–Stark uncertainty principle

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $A \subseteq G$, and let $B$ be a set of additive characters of $G$ with $|A| \cdot |B| < |G|$. If $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ vanishes outside $A$ and its discrete Fourier transform $\hat f$ vanishes outside $B$, then $f = 0$.
nodes.title: Functions with small support and small Fourier support vanish
Influences and the noise operator on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For a point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ is obtained from $x$ by negating its $i$-th coordinate (exchanging true and false) and leaving every other coordinate unchanged.
nodes.title: Coordinate flip on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the $i$-th coordinate of $x^{\oplus i}$, the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, is the negation $\lnot x_i$ of $x_i$ (true and false exchanged).
nodes.title: A coordinate flip negates the flipped coordinate

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and all coordinates $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $j \ne i$, the $j$-th coordinate of $x^{\oplus i}$, the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, is $x_j$.
nodes.title: A coordinate flip fixes the other coordinates

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, we have $(x^{\oplus i})^{\oplus i} = x$.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate twice

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the map $x \mapsto x^{\oplus i}$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, which flips the $i$-th coordinate, is an involution: applying it twice gives the identity.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate is an involution

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ obtained from $x$ by flipping its $i$-th coordinate is different from $x$.
nodes.title: A coordinate flip moves every point

nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, the sign of its negation is the negative of its sign: $\sigma(\lnot b) = -\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.
nodes.title: Sign of a negated Boolean value

nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ (equal to $1$ for true and $-1$ for false) is nonzero.
nodes.title: Coordinate signs are nonzero

nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$, which is $1$ for true and $-1$ for false, satisfies $|\sigma(b)| = 1$.
nodes.title: Coordinate signs have absolute value one

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i < n$, and write $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped. Then the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = -\chi_S(x)$ if $i \in S$, and $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = \chi_S(x)$ if $i \notin S$.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate in a Fourier character

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f$ a function from the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ to $M$, and $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For a point $x$ of the cube write $x^{\oplus i}$ for the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Then $\sum_x f(x^{\oplus i}) = \sum_x f(x)$, both sums ranging over all points $x$ of the cube.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate preserves sums over the cube

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid that is a module over the nonnegative rationals, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates to $M$, and let $i < n$. Writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped, the uniform average of $f(x^{\oplus i})$ over all points $x$ of the cube equals the uniform average of $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Averages are invariant under flipping a coordinate

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.
nodes.title: Uniform average over the Boolean cube as a sum

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is the average of $f(x) \chi_S(x)$ over all points $x$ of the cube, $\hat f(S) = \mathbb{E}_x [f(x) \chi_S(x)]$, where $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients as averages

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_x f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where the sum runs over all points $x$ of the cube and $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients as sums over the cube

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)$ of $f$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(\emptyset)$ of $f$ at the empty set.
nodes.title: Average over the Boolean cube as the empty Fourier coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ and $T$ be subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\chi_S$ and $\chi_T$ be their Fourier characters. Then $\sum_x \chi_S(x) \chi_T(x)$, the sum ranging over all points $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, equals $2^n$ if $S = T$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the sum of the Fourier character $\chi_S$ over all points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ equals $2^n$ if $S$ is empty and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Sum of a Boolean cube character

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y$ be points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\chi_S$ be the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \chi_S(x) \chi_S(y)$, the sum ranging over all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, equals $2^n$ if $x = y$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Dual orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $x$ be a point of the cube. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\hat f(S)$ be the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $\chi_S$ the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \hat f(S) \chi_S(x) = f(x)$, the sum ranging over all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Fourier inversion on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all functions $f, g : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f g$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the products of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) g(x) = \sum_S \hat f(S) \hat g(S)$.
nodes.title: Plancherel's identity on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f^2$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)^2 = \sum_S \hat f(S)^2$.
nodes.title: Parseval's identity on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: If two real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates have the same Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S) = \hat g(S)$ at every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, then $f = g$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients determine the function

nodes.summary: For all real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $f + g$ at $S$ is the sum of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$: $\widehat{f + g}(S) = \hat f(S) + \hat g(S)$.
nodes.title: Additivity of Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: For real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the Fourier coefficient of $f - g$ at $S$ is $\widehat{f - g}(S) = \hat f(S) - \hat g(S)$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a difference

nodes.summary: For every real $c$, every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $c f$ at $S$ is $c$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$: $\widehat{c f}(S) = c \hat f(S)$.
nodes.title: Homogeneity of Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: For every real $c$ and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates is $c$ if $S = \emptyset$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a constant function

nodes.summary: For all sets $S$ and $T$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the Fourier character $\chi_T$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, $\chi_T(x) = \prod_{i \in T} \sigma(x_i)$ with $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$, is $1$ if $T = S$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a character

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a_T$ indexed by the sets $T \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $g(x) = \sum_T a_T \chi_T(x)$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$, where $\chi_T$ is the Fourier character of $T$. Then for every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $S$ is $\hat g(S) = a_S$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the Fourier expansion

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $g(x) = f(x^{\oplus i})$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Write $\hat f(S)$ and $\hat g(S)$ for the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at a set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates. Then for every such $S$, $\hat g(S) = -\hat f(S)$ if $i \in S$ and $\hat g(S) = \hat f(S)$ if…
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate negates the Fourier coefficients of the sets containing it

nodes.summary: For a real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of $i$ on $f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[\big((f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})) / 2\big)^2\big]$, where the expectation is over $x$ uniform on the cube and $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.
nodes.title: Influence of a coordinate

nodes.summary: For a function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is the sum of the influences of its $n$ coordinates, $\mathrm{I}[f] = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$, where $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x \left[\left(\frac{f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})}{2}\right)^2\right]$, $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped and $\mathbb{E}_x$ is the uniform average over the…
nodes.title: Total influence on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, its variance under the uniform distribution is $\mathrm{Var}[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[(f(x) - \mathbb{E}_y[f(y)])^2\big]$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$ denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.
nodes.title: Variance on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ of coordinate $i$ on $f$ satisfies $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Influences are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Total influence is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution is at least $0$.
nodes.title: Variance on the Boolean cube is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Constant functions have zero influence

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has total influence $0$.
nodes.title: Constant functions have zero total influence

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has variance $0$ under the uniform distribution.
nodes.title: Constant functions have zero variance

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ that takes only the values $1$ and $-1$, and let $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ equals the probability, for $x$ uniform on the cube, that $f(x^{\oplus i}) \ne f(x)$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.
nodes.title: Influence of a Boolean function as a flip probability

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \sum_{S \ni i} \hat f(S)^2$, where $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and the sum runs over the sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain $i$.
nodes.title: Fourier formula for influence

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution equals $\sum_{S \neq \emptyset} \hat f(S)^2$, where the sum runs over the nonempty sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
nodes.title: Variance in terms of Fourier coefficients

nodes.title: Choquet's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a real Banach space with its Borel σ-algebra and let $K \subseteq X$ be compact and convex. For every $x \in K$ there is a probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ such that the complement of the set of extreme points of $K$ has $\mu$-measure $0$ and the barycenter $\int y \, d\mu(y)$ (a Bochner integral) equals $x$.
nodes.title: Choquet's representation theorem in Banach spaces

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a real Banach space with its Borel σ-algebra, let $K \subseteq X$ be compact and convex, and let $x$ be an extreme point of $K$. If $\mu$ is a probability measure on $X$ with $\mu(X \setminus K) = 0$ whose barycenter $\int y \, d\mu(y)$ (a Bochner integral) equals $x$, then $\mu$ is the Dirac measure at $x$.
nodes.title: Bauer's uniqueness theorem at extreme points
Discontinuous linear functionals

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $E$ is not finite-dimensional, then there exists a linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ that is not continuous.
nodes.title: A discontinuous linear functional on an infinite-dimensional normed space

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Every linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ is continuous if and only if $E$ is finite-dimensional.
nodes.title: Every linear functional is continuous if and only if the space is finite-dimensional

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $E$ is not finite-dimensional, then there is a linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ that differs from every continuous linear functional $g \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: The algebraic dual is strictly larger than the topological dual
F-spaces

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type (F) when addition $E \times E \to E$ and scalar multiplication $\mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ are continuous and there is a metric $d$ on $E$ that is translation invariant, $d(x + z, y + z) = d(x, y)$ for all $x, y, z \in E$, that induces the topology of $E$, and that is complete: every Cauchy sequence for $d$ converges for $d$.
nodes.title: Spaces of type (F)

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space. A set $K \subseteq E$ is a sphere when $0 \notin K$ and for every $x \ne 0$ in $E$ there is exactly one real $t > 0$ with $t x \in K$; that is, every open ray from the origin meets $K$ exactly once.
nodes.title: Spheres in the ray sense

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology. A set $R \subseteq E$ is bounded when for every sequence $(x_n)$ of points of $R$ and every sequence $(t_n)$ of real numbers with $t_n \to 0$, the sequence $(t_n x_n)$ tends to $0$ in $E$.
nodes.title: Sequentially bounded sets

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type (B) when there is a function $\|\cdot\| : E \to \mathbb{R}$ with $\|x\| \ge 0$, with $\|x\| = 0$ exactly when $x = 0$, with $\|x + y\| \le \|x\| + \|y\|$ and with $\|a x\| = |a| \, \|x\|$ for all $x, y \in E$ and $a \in \mathbb{R}$, such that a set $U \subseteq E$ is open exactly when every $x \in U$ has an $\varepsilon > 0$ with $y \in U$ whenever…
nodes.title: Spaces of type (B)

nodes.summary: The claim of Mazur and Orlicz that every real vector space $E$ with a topology that is of type (F) and contains a bounded sphere is of type (B).
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 15.1

nodes.summary: The Mazur–Orlicz claim of Problem 15.1 is false: there is a real vector space $E$ with a topology that is of type (F) and contains a bounded sphere, but is not of type (B).
nodes.title: Negative answer to Scottish Book Problem 15.1

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type (F) if there is a metric $d$ on $E$ that induces its topology, is translation invariant, $d(x + z, y + z) = d(x, y)$ for all $x, y, z \in E$, and is complete, and if addition $E \times E \to E$ and scalar multiplication $\mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ are continuous.
nodes.title: Spaces of type (F) in Scottish Book Problem 26

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space with a topology. A set $R \subseteq E$ is bounded if for every sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of points of $R$ and every real sequence $(t_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $t_n \to 0$, we have $t_n x_n \to 0$ in $E$.
nodes.title: Bounded sets in Scottish Book Problem 26

reading_title.source: Spaces of type $\{F_o\}$

nodes.summary: A real vector space $E$ with a topology is of type $\{F_o\}$ if it is of type (F) and, for every sequence $(x_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $E$ with $x_n \to 0$ and every real sequence $(t_n)_{n \ge 0}$ with $\sum_n |t_n| < \infty$, the series $\sum_n t_n x_n$ converges in $E$.
nodes.title: Spaces of type $\{F_o\}$

nodes.summary: The claim that for every real vector space $E$ with a topology that is of type $\{F_o\}$ and every sequence $(F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$, if $F_n \to 0$ uniformly on every bounded set $R \subseteq E$, then there is an open set $U \subseteq E$ containing $0$ on which $F_n \to 0$ uniformly.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 26 (Mazur and Orlicz's claim)

nodes.summary: The claim of Scottish Book Problem 26 is false: there are a real vector space $E$ with a topology, of type $\{F_o\}$, and a sequence $(F_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{R}$ that converges to $0$ uniformly on every bounded subset of $E$ but does not converge to $0$ uniformly on any open set containing $0$.
nodes.title: Mazur and Orlicz's Problem 26 has a negative answer
Hahn–Banach theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a seminormed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $M$ be a subspace of $E$, let $C \ge 0$ be a real number, and let $f \colon M \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional with $\|f(m)\| \le C\|m\|$ for all $m \in M$. If $x_0 \in E$ does not lie in $M$, then $M$ is strictly contained in $M' = M + \mathbb{K} x_0$, and there is a continuous linear functional…
nodes.title: One-step Hahn–Banach extension

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a linear subspace of $E$, and give $E/S$ the quotient seminorm. Then for every $x \in E$ the class $q(x)$ of $x$ under the quotient map $q \colon E \to E/S$ satisfies $\|q(x)\| = d(x, S)$, where $d(x, S) = \inf_{s \in S} \|x - s\|$ is the distance from $x$ to $S$.
nodes.title: Quotient seminorm equals distance to the subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a linear subspace of $E$, and give $E/S$ the quotient seminorm. Then the quotient map $q \colon E \to E/S$, a continuous linear map, has operator norm $\|q\| \le 1$.
nodes.title: The quotient map has norm at most one

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a linear subspace of $E$, not necessarily closed, and let $x \in E$. Then there is a continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ with $\|f\| \le 1$ that vanishes on $S$ and satisfies $f(x) = d(x, S)$, where $d(x, S) = \inf_{s \in S} \|x - s\|$ is the distance from $x$ to $S$.
nodes.title: Hahn–Banach distance formula, attainment form

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a linear subspace of $E$, and let $x \in E$ have positive distance $d(x, S) = \inf_{s \in S} \|x - s\| > 0$ from $S$. Then there is a continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ with $\|f\| = 1$ that vanishes on $S$ and satisfies $f(x) = d(x, S)$.
nodes.title: Norm-one annihilating functional at positive distance

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a closed linear subspace of $E$ and let $x \in E$ with $x \notin S$. Then there is a continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ with $\|f\| = 1$ that vanishes on $S$ and satisfies $f(x) = d(x, S)$, where $d(x, S) = \inf_{s \in S} \|x - s\|$ is the distance from $x$ to $S$.
nodes.title: Norm-one annihilating functional outside a closed subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a linear subspace of $E$, not necessarily closed, and let $x \in E$. Then the distance $d(x, S) = \inf_{s \in S} \|x - s\|$ from $x$ to $S$ equals the supremum of $|f(x)|$ over all continuous linear functionals $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ with $\|f\| \le 1$ that vanish on $S$.
nodes.title: Hahn–Banach distance formula

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space and let $A, B \subseteq E$ be convex bodies, that is, convex, closed and bounded sets with nonempty interior. If there is $\varepsilon > 0$ with $\operatorname{dist}(a, b) \ge \varepsilon$ for all $a \in A$ and $b \in B$, then there are a nonzero continuous linear functional $F : E \to \mathbb{R}$ and a constant $c \in \mathbb{R}$ with $F(a) \le c$ for all $a \in A$ and $c \le F(b)$…
nodes.title: Separation of convex bodies at positive distance
Annihilators and the bipolar theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological annihilator of a subspace $S$ of $E$ is the subspace of $E^*$ consisting of the continuous linear functionals $f$ with $f(x) = 0$ for all $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological coannihilator of a subspace $\Phi$ of $E^*$ is the subspace of $E$ consisting of the vectors $x$ with $f(x) = 0$ for all $f \in \Phi$.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a subspace of $E$, and let $f : E \to \mathbb{K}$ be a continuous linear functional. Then $f$ lies in the topological annihilator of $S$ if and only if $f(x) = 0$ for every $x \in S$.
nodes.title: Membership in the topological annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\Phi$ be a subspace of the continuous dual of $E$, and let $x \in E$. Then $x$ lies in the topological coannihilator of $\Phi$ if and only if $f(x) = 0$ for every $f \in \Phi$.
nodes.title: Membership in the topological coannihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S \subseteq T$ be subspaces of $E$. Then the topological annihilator of $T$ is contained in the topological annihilator of $S$.
nodes.title: The topological annihilator reverses inclusion

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. If $\Phi \subseteq \Psi$ are subspaces of $E^*$, then the topological coannihilator of $\Psi$ is contained in the topological coannihilator of $\Phi$.
nodes.title: The topological coannihilator is antitone

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. The topological annihilator of the zero subspace of $E$ is the whole continuous dual of $E$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of the zero subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological annihilator of $E$, viewed as a subspace of itself, is the zero subspace of $E^*$: a continuous linear functional vanishing everywhere on $E$ is zero.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of the whole space

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological coannihilator of the zero subspace of $E^*$ is all of $E$.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator of the zero subspace

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. The topological coannihilator of $E^*$ itself is the zero subspace of $E$: a vector killed by every continuous linear functional is zero.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator of the whole dual

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Every subspace $S$ of $E$ is contained in the topological coannihilator of the topological annihilator of $S$.
nodes.title: A subspace lies in its double annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every subspace $S$ of $E$, the topological annihilator of the topological closure $\overline{S}$ equals the topological annihilator of $S$: a continuous linear functional vanishing on $S$ vanishes on $\overline{S}$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of the closure

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a subspace of $E$, and let $x \in E$ lie outside the topological closure of $S$. Then some continuous linear functional $f$ in the topological annihilator of $S$ satisfies $f(x) \neq 0$.
nodes.title: Separation

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $S$ be a subspace of $E$, and let $x \in E$ lie outside the topological closure of $S$. Then some continuous linear functional $f$ in the topological annihilator of $S$ satisfies $f(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: Separation, normalized

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $S$ be a subspace of $E$. The topological coannihilator of the topological annihilator of $S$, that is, the subspace of vectors of $E$ killed by every continuous linear functional vanishing on $S$, is the topological closure of $S$.
nodes.title: Bipolar theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ be a subspace of $E$. The topological annihilator of $S$ is the zero subspace of the continuous dual of $E$ if and only if $S$ is dense in $E$.
nodes.title: Density criterion via the annihilator

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ and $T$ be subspaces of $E$. Then $S$ and $T$ have the same topological annihilator if and only if they have the same topological closure.
nodes.title: The annihilator determines the closure

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $S$ and $T$ be subspaces of $E$. The topological annihilator of $S + T$ is the intersection of the topological annihilators of $S$ and $T$.
nodes.title: Topological annihilator of a sum of subspaces

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with continuous dual $E^*$. For subspaces $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ of $E^*$, the topological coannihilator of their supremum $\Phi + \Psi$ is the intersection of the topological coannihilators of $\Phi$ and $\Psi$.
nodes.title: Topological coannihilator of a sum of subspaces
Hamel bases of Banach spaces

nodes.summary: If `E` is a complete normed space over `𝕜 = ℝ, ℂ` admitting a Hamel basis indexed by a countable type, then `E` is finite-dimensional. Completeness is essential: it is what the Baire category argument uses.
nodes.title: A Banach space with a countable Hamel basis is finite-dimensional

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a complete normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $E$ is not finite-dimensional, then no Hamel basis of $E$ is indexed by a countable set.
nodes.title: An infinite-dimensional Banach space has no countable Hamel basis
James' reflexivity theorem

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a real normed space, write $X^*$ for its dual space of continuous linear functionals and $X^{**}$ for the dual of $X^*$, and let $T \in X^{**}$ with $\|T\| \le 1$. Then for every finite set $s \subseteq X^*$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $x \in X$ with $\|x\| \le 1$ such that $|z(x) - T(z)| < \varepsilon$ for every $z \in s$.
nodes.title: Finite-coordinate Goldstine theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K}$. The canonical embedding of $E$ into its bidual $E^{**}$ is surjective if and only if every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$ attains its norm on the closed unit ball, that is, there is $x \in E$ with $\|x\| \le 1$ and $|f(x)| = \|f\|$.
nodes.title: James' reflexivity theorem
Mazur's lemma

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector space by restricting scalars. If a sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ converges to $x \in E$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear functionals on $E$), then for every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ the point $x$ lies in the norm closure of the…
nodes.title: Mazur's lemma, hull form

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector space by restricting scalars. If a sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ converges to $x \in E$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear functionals on $E$), then $x$ lies in the norm closure of the real convex hull of the set…
nodes.title: Mazur's lemma, hull form for the whole sequence

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector space by restricting scalars. If a sequence $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ in $E$ converges to $x \in E$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by the continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear functionals on $E$), then for every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a…
nodes.title: Mazur's lemma, explicit finite convex combinations

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K}$, where $\mathbb{K}$ is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, regarded also as a real vector space by restricting scalars. Let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and $x \in E$ such that $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every continuous $\mathbb{K}$-linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$. Then for every $N \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a finite…
nodes.title: Mazur's lemma in the textbook phrasing
Weak topology and weak convergence

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, then the norms are bounded above: there is a real number $C$ with $\|u_n\| \le C$ for all $n$.
nodes.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm-bounded

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, that is, $u_n$ converges weakly to $x$, then $\|x\| \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \|u_n\|$.
nodes.title: Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be normed spaces over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T \colon E \to F$ be a continuous linear map, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, then $g(T u_n) \to g(T x)$ for every continuous linear functional $g \colon F \to \mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: Bounded operators preserve weak convergence

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by all continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$), then $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: Weak convergence gives convergence under every functional

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $f(u_n) \to f(x)$ as $n \to \infty$ for every continuous linear functional $f \colon E \to \mathbb{K}$, then $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by all continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$).
nodes.title: Convergence under every functional gives weak convergence

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by all continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$), then there is a real number $C$ with $\|u_n\| \le C$ for all $n$.
nodes.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm-bounded (weak topology form)

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a normed space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$ (the topology induced by all continuous linear functionals $E \to \mathbb{K}$), then $\|x\| \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} \|u_n\|$.
nodes.title: Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm (weak topology form)

nodes.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be normed spaces over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $T \colon E \to F$ be a continuous linear map, let $(u_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in $E$ and let $x \in E$. If $u_n \to x$ in the weak topology of $E$, then $T u_n \to T x$ in the weak topology of $F$; here the weak topology of a space is the one induced by its continuous linear functionals.
nodes.title: Bounded operators preserve weak convergence (weak topology form)

nodes.summary: Finitely many continuous linear functionals on an infinite-dimensional normed space have a common nonzero kernel vector.
nodes.title: Finitely many functionals have a common nonzero kernel vector

nodes.summary: Every nonempty weakly open set contains a whole line through each of its points: if `U` is weakly open and `x ∈ U`, then `x + t • v ∈ U` for all scalars `t` and some nonzero `v` (a common kernel vector of the finitely many functionals constraining a basic weak neighbourhood of `x`).
nodes.title: Weakly open sets contain lines through each point

nodes.summary: Every nonempty weakly open set in an infinite-dimensional normed space is unbounded in norm.
nodes.title: Weakly open sets are unbounded in infinite dimensions

nodes.summary: The open unit ball is not weakly open in infinite dimensions.
nodes.title: Open unit ball is not weakly open in infinite dimensions

nodes.summary: The unit sphere is not weakly open in infinite dimensions.
nodes.title: Unit sphere is not weakly open in infinite dimensions

nodes.summary: In an infinite-dimensional normed space, the weak closure of the unit sphere is the closed unit ball.
nodes.title: Weak closure of the unit sphere is the closed unit ball

nodes.summary: The unit sphere is not weakly closed in infinite dimensions: its weak closure is the whole closed unit ball.
nodes.title: Unit sphere is not weakly closed in infinite dimensions

nodes.summary: The unit sphere is not weakly compact in infinite dimensions.
nodes.title: Unit sphere is not weakly compact in infinite dimensions

nodes.summary: In finite dimensions the identity map from the norm topology to the weak topology is an open map: the weak topology agrees with the norm topology.
nodes.title: Weak topology equals norm topology in finite dimensions

nodes.summary: In infinite dimensions the identity map from the norm topology to the weak topology is not an open map: the open unit ball is norm-open but not weakly open.
nodes.title: Weak topology is strictly coarser in infinite dimensions

nodes.summary: Convexity and smoothness of norms (uniform convexity, Kadec–Klee, Birkhoff–James), extreme points of balls, Auerbach and Schauder bases, approximation property, isometries (Banach–Stone, Mazur–Ulam), Banach–Mazur, Dvoretzky–Rogers, Grothendieck, Rademacher type, Daugavet, Bishop–Phelps.
nodes.title: Geometry of Banach spaces

nodes.summary: Every separable real Banach space $E$ admits a linear isometric embedding $e \colon E \to C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ into the space of continuous real functions on $[0, 1]$ with the supremum norm, such that the range of $e$ is closed.
nodes.title: Banach–Mazur embedding theorem

nodes.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Hausdorff spaces, and let $C(X, \mathbb{R})$ and $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$ be the real Banach spaces of continuous real functions on them with the supremum norm. If there is a surjective linear isometry from $C(X, \mathbb{R})$ onto $C(Y, \mathbb{R})$, then $X$ and $Y$ are homeomorphic.
nodes.title: Banach–Stone theorem for real scalars

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a Banach space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, with dual space $E^*$. The functionals that attain their norm on the closed unit ball, that is, the $f \in E^*$ such that $|f(x)| = \|f\|$ for some $x \in E$ with $\|x\| \le 1$, form a dense subset of $E^*$ in the norm topology.
nodes.title: Bishop–Phelps theorem

nodes.summary: Let $C[0,1]$ be the real Banach space of continuous functions $[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with the supremum norm, and let $I$ be the identity operator on it. Every compact bounded linear operator $T : C[0,1] \to C[0,1]$ satisfies $\|I + T\| = 1 + \|T\|$, where the norms are operator norms.
nodes.title: Daugavet's theorem for compact operators

Symmetric hulls of nowhere dense convex sets

nodes.summary: The claim that for every real Banach space $E$ and every convex set $W \subseteq E$ with $0 \in W$, if the closure of $W$ has empty interior (that is, $W$ is nowhere dense), then the closure of the convex hull of $W \cup (-W)$ also has empty interior. Dickman–de Bruijn function

nodes.summary: A function $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function if $\rho(u) = 0$ for every real $u < 0$, $\rho$ maps $[0, \infty)$ into $[0, 1]$, $\rho$ is continuous on $[0, \infty)$, $\rho(u) = 1$ for every $u \in [0, 1]$, and for every real $u > 1$ the function $\rho$ is differentiable at $u$ with $u \rho'(u) + \rho(u - 1) = 0$.
nodes.title: Dickman–de Bruijn functions

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) = 0$ for every real $u < 0$.

nodes.title: Continuity of the Dickman–de Bruijn function on the nonnegative reals

nodes.summary: If $\rho : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a Dickman–de Bruijn function, then $\rho(u) = 1$ for every $u \in [0, 1]$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a complex number $z$, this is the complex number $\frac{(-1)^n z^{n+1}}{(n+1) \cdot (n+1)!}$, the term of index $j = n + 1$ in the series $\operatorname{Ein}(z) = \sum_{j \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^{j+1} z^j}{j \cdot j!}$.

Then $\cos x \ne 0$, the series $T(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} (-1)^k \frac{\tan^{2k+1} x}{(2k+1)^2}$ (the inverse tangent integral of $\tan x$) and $F(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{\sin((4j+2)x)}{(2j+1)^2}$ are both summable, and $T(x) = P(x) + F(x)$.

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a pair of $\mathbb{R}$-linearly independent complex numbers $\omega_1, \omega_2$ with period lattice $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}\omega_1 + \mathbb{Z}\omega_2$. A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is lattice-periodic for $L$ when every element of $\Lambda$ is a period of $f$, that is, $f(z + \omega) = f(z)$ for all $\omega \in \Lambda$ and all $z \in \mathbb{C}$.

nodes.summary: A period pair is a pair $(\omega_1, \omega_2)$ of complex numbers that are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$, and its lattice is $\Lambda = \mathbb{Z}\omega_1 + \mathbb{Z}\omega_2 \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Two period pairs $L$ and $L'$ with lattices $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$ are homothetic when there is a nonzero complex number $c$ such that $\Lambda' = c\Lambda = \{c\lambda : \lambda \in \Lambda\}$.

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let the order of $f$ at $z$ be its meromorphic order, an element of $\mathbb{Z} \cup \{\infty\}$ that is $0$ by convention when $f$ is not meromorphic at $z$. The pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ is nonzero if and only if this order is negative, that is, if and only if $f$ has a pole at $z$.

nodes.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, let $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ be meromorphic on $U$ and let $z \in U$. Then the pole multiplicity of $f$ at $z$ equals $\max(0, -D(z))$.

Riemann integral

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, a partition of the closed interval $[a, b]$ consists of a natural number $n$, the number of subintervals, together with $n + 1$ points forming a strictly increasing sequence $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$.
nodes.title: Partition of an interval

nodes.summary: A tagged partition of $[a, b]$ is a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ together with a choice of a tag $\xi_k \in [x_{k-1}, x_k]$ in each subinterval, for $k = 1, \dots, n$.
nodes.title: Tagged partition

nodes.summary: The mesh (also called the norm) of a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ is the maximum subinterval length $\max_{1 \le k \le n} (x_k - x_{k-1})$ when $n \ge 1$, and $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Mesh of a partition

nodes.summary: The point set of a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ is the set of its points $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$.
nodes.title: Points of a partition

nodes.summary: For partitions $P$ and $Q$ of $[a, b]$, $Q$ is a refinement of $P$ when every point of $P$ is a point of $Q$, that is, when the point set of $P$ is contained in the point set of $Q$.
nodes.title: Refinement of a partition

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $T$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$, with points $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ and tags $\xi_k \in [x_{k-1}, x_k]$ for $k = 1, \dots, n$. The Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $T$ is $S_f(x, \xi) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} f(\xi_k)\,(x_k - x_{k-1})$ (an empty sum, equal to $0$, when $n = 0$).
nodes.title: Riemann sum

nodes.summary: If $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and the interval $[a, b]$ has a partition, then $a \le b$.
nodes.title: Endpoints of a partition are ordered

nodes.summary: If $a < b$, then every partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ has at least one subinterval, that is, $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: A partition of a nondegenerate interval has a subinterval

nodes.summary: If $a < b$, then every partition of $[a, b]$ has strictly positive mesh.
nodes.title: The mesh is positive on a nondegenerate interval

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with no subintervals, the Riemann sum of $f$ is $0$, since it is an empty sum.
nodes.title: Riemann sum over a trivial partition

nodes.summary: If $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ is a partition of $[a, b]$, then $x_{i+1} - x_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ with $0 \le i < n$.
nodes.title: Subintervals of a partition have nonnegative length

nodes.summary: Let $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ be a partition of $[a, b]$. Then for every $i$ with $0 \le i < n$, the subinterval length $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is at most the mesh of the partition.
nodes.title: Subinterval lengths are at most the mesh

nodes.summary: If $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ is a partition of $[a, b]$, then the lengths of its subintervals sum to the length of the interval: $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (x_{i+1} - x_i) = b - a$.
nodes.title: Subinterval lengths of a partition telescope

nodes.summary: Every tag $\xi_k$ of a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ lies in $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Tags of a tagged partition lie in the interval

nodes.summary: For every real constant $c$ and every tagged partition of $[a, b]$, the Riemann sum of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ equals $c(b - a)$.
nodes.title: Riemann sum of a constant function

nodes.title: Telescoping over the fibers of an assignment

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ with points $a = x_0 < \dots < x_n = b$ and $a = x'_0 < \dots < x'_{n'} = b$ respectively. Tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$ consist of a map $\sigma$ assigning to each index $j < n'$ an index $\sigma(j) < n$ such that $x_{\sigma(j)} \le x'_j$ and $x'_{j+1} \le x_{\sigma(j)+1}$ for every $j < n'$ (so the $j$-th subinterval of $T'$ lies in the $\sigma(j)$-th…
nodes.title: Tagged-refinement data

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ such that every point of $T$ is a point of $T'$. Then tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$ exist: an assignment of each subinterval of $T'$ to a subinterval of $T$ that contains it, such that for each subinterval of $T$ the lengths of the subintervals of $T'$ assigned to it add up to its length.
nodes.title: Refinements carry tagged-refinement data

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $T$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with points $x_0 < \dots < x_n$ and tags $\xi_0, \dots, \xi_{n-1}$, and let $T'$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with points $x'_0 < \dots < x'_{n'}$, together with tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$ assigning to each $j < n'$ an index $\sigma(j) < n$. Then the Riemann sum $S_f(T)$ of $f$ over $T$ satisfies
nodes.title: Riemann sum regrouped over a refinement

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ together with tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$, and let $\omega \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \|T\|$, where $\|T\|$ is the mesh of $T$. Writing $S_f(T)$ for the Riemann sum of $f$ over $T$, we have $|S_f(T) - S_f(T')| \le \omega (b - a)$.
nodes.title: Riemann sums under refinement, given refinement data

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ such that every point of $T$ is a point of $T'$, and let $\omega \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \|T\|$, where $\|T\|$ is the mesh of $T$. Writing $S_f(T)$ for the Riemann sum of $f$ over $T$, we have $|S_f(T) - S_f(T')| \le \omega (b - a)$.
nodes.title: Riemann sums under refinement

Suppose $\omega_1, \omega_2 \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy, for $i = 1, 2$, $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega_i$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \|T_i\|$. nodes.title: Riemann sums of two partitions with a common refinement

nodes.summary: Let $a, b$ be real numbers. For any two tagged partitions $T_1$ and $T_2$ of $[a, b]$, there is a tagged partition $T''$ of $[a, b]$ that is a tagged refinement of both $T_1$ and $T_2$.
nodes.title: Common refinement of two tagged partitions

nodes.title: Continuity, regularity and functional equations

nodes.summary: There exists a continuous function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is differentiable at no point of $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: A continuous nowhere differentiable function

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ there is a dense set $D \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ such that the restriction of $f$ to $D$ is continuous.
nodes.title: Blumberg's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $a < b$ be real numbers and let $\varphi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $(a, b)$ and satisfy $\varphi\bigl(\frac{x+y}{2}\bigr) \le \frac{\varphi(x) + \varphi(y)}{2}$ for all $x, y \in (a, b)$. Then $\varphi$ is convex on $(a, b)$.
nodes.title: Continuous midpoint-convex functions are convex

nodes.summary: There is a function $\varphi : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{R}$ that is not continuous, satisfies $\varphi(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{C}$, is not identically $0$ and not identically $1$, and satisfies $\varphi(x + y) \le \varphi(x) + \varphi(y)$ and $\varphi(xy) = \varphi(x)\varphi(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Discontinuous subadditive multiplicative functions on $\mathbb{C}$

nodes.summary: Let $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^n$, and let $F$ be the set of $x\in E$ for which there is a sequence $(x_k)$ in $E\setminus\{x\}$ with $x_k \to x$ and $f(x_k) \to f(x)$. Then $E \setminus F$ is countable.
nodes.title: Isolated points of a graph are countable

nodes.summary: There is a continuous function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(x) > 0$ for every real $x$ such that, for every real $x$, the series $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} f(x + n)$ converges and its sum is $1$.
nodes.title: Steinhaus's periodization problem (Scottish Book Problem 181)
Almost additive functions

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for almost every $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$, there is a function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $h(x + y) = h(x) + h(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ and $f(x) = h(x)$ for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1126 on almost additive functions

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for almost every $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. Then there is a function $h : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $h(x + y) = h(x) + h(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ and $f(x) = h(x)$ for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Almost additive functions agree almost everywhere with additive functions
Approximate derivatives and monotonicity

nodes.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ has right-hand density $0$ at $0$ if the Lebesgue outer measure of $S \cap (0, \delta]$, divided by $\delta$, tends to $0$ as $\delta \to 0^+$.
nodes.title: Right density zero at the origin

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is approximately continuous at $x$ if, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, the set $S_\varepsilon = \{y : |f(y) - f(x)| < \varepsilon\}$ has density $1$ at $x$: the Lebesgue outer measure of $S_\varepsilon \cap (x - \delta, x + \delta)$, divided by $2\delta$, tends to $1$ as $\delta \to 0^+$.
nodes.title: Approximate continuity

nodes.summary: The upper right-hand approximate derivative of $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ at $x$ is positive: there are $a > 0$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $\delta > 0$ there is $\delta' \in (0, \delta]$ for which the Lebesgue outer measure of $\{h \in (0, \delta'] : (f(x + h) - f(x))/h > a\}$ is at least $\varepsilon \delta'$.
nodes.title: Positive upper right approximate derivative

nodes.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be approximately continuous at every point, and suppose that at every point $x$ the upper right-hand approximate derivative of $f$ is positive. Then $f$ is monotone nondecreasing.
nodes.title: Approximate derivative test for monotonicity (Scottish Book Problem 157)
Exponential functional equation

nodes.summary: If a continuous function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfies $f(0) = 1$ and $f(r + s) = f(r) f(s)$ for all real $r$ and $s$, then there is a complex number $L$ such that $f(r) = e^{rL}$ for every real $r$.
nodes.title: Continuous solutions of the exponential functional equation

reading_title.source: Continuous nonzero solutions of $f(x)f(y) = f(x+y)$ are exponentials

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function that is not identically zero and satisfies $f(x)f(y) = f(x+y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$. Then there is a real constant $c$ such that $f(x) = e^{cx}$ for every real $x$.
nodes.title: Continuous nonzero solutions of $f(x)f(y) = f(x+y)$ are exponentials
Functions with continuous differences

nodes.summary: The statement that every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $x \mapsto f(x + h) - f(x)$ is continuous for every $h > 0$ can be written as $f = g + a$ with $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous and $a : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ additive, that is, $a(x + y) = a(x) + a(y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 907

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that for every $h > 0$ the function $x \mapsto f(x + h) - f(x)$ is continuous. Then there are functions $g, a : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $g$ continuous and $a$ additive, that is, $a(x + y) = a(x) + a(y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$, such that $f = g + a$.
nodes.title: De Bruijn's theorem on continuous differences (Erdős Problem 907)
Hyers–Ulam stability

nodes.summary: The dyadic approximants `2 ^ (-n) • f (2 ^ n • x)` used in Hyers' proof.
nodes.title: Dyadic approximants in Hyers' proof

nodes.summary: Norm of a natural-number multiple in a real normed space.
nodes.title: Norm of a natural-number multiple

nodes.summary: If `f : E → F` between real normed spaces, with `F` complete, satisfies `‖f (x + y) - f x - f y‖ ≤ δ` for all `x, y`, then there is an additive map `A : E →+ F` with `‖f x - A x‖ ≤ δ` for all `x`. The bound `δ` is sharp: for `f x = x + c` on `ℝ` the defect is `‖c‖` and the best additive approximant is the identity, at distance exactly `‖c‖`.
nodes.title: Hyers' theorem (Hyers–Ulam stability of the Cauchy equation)

nodes.summary: Two additive maps both within `δ` of the same `f` are equal: their difference is additive, hence `n`-homogeneous, while staying bounded by `2 * δ`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness in Hyers' theorem

nodes.summary: If the midpoint (Jensen) defect `‖f ((1/2) • (x + y)) - (1/2) • (f x + f y)‖` is `≤ δ` for all `x, y`, then `f` is within `4 * δ` of an additive map plus the constant `f 0`. The factor `4` comes from doubling the two Jensen estimates at `(x + y, 0)` and `(x, y)`.
nodes.title: Hyers–Ulam stability of Jensen's functional equation

nodes.summary: If `f` is continuous at `0` (in particular if `f` itself is continuous), the additive approximant from Hyers' theorem is continuous, hence a continuous real-linear map. The proof: continuity of `f` at `0` bounds `f` on a small ball, so the approximant is bounded on that ball, and an additive map bounded on a ball is continuous at `0` by the dyadic scaling argument.
nodes.title: Continuous Hyers–Ulam stability
Modulus of continuity

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, real numbers $a$ and $b$, and a scale $\eta \in \mathbb{R}$, the modulus of continuity of $f$ on $[a, b]$ at scale $\eta$ is
nodes.title: Modulus of continuity

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$. Then for every $\eta \in \mathbb{R}$ the set $\{|f(x) - f(y)| : x, y \in [a, b],\ |x - y| \le \eta\}$ is bounded above.
nodes.title: The set defining the modulus of continuity is bounded above

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$, let $\eta \in \mathbb{R}$, and let $\omega_f(\eta)$ be the modulus of continuity of $f$ on $[a, b]$ at scale $\eta$. For all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \eta$, we have $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega_f(\eta)$.
nodes.title: The modulus of continuity bounds increments

nodes.summary: Let $a \le b$ and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$. For every $\eta \ge 0$, the modulus of continuity $\omega_f(\eta)$ of $f$ on $[a, b]$ at scale $\eta$ satisfies $0 \le \omega_f(\eta)$.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the modulus of continuity

nodes.summary: Let $a \le b$, let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$, and write $\omega_f(\eta)$ for the modulus of continuity of $f$ on $[a, b]$ at scale $\eta$. If $0 \le \eta_1 \le \eta_2$, then $\omega_f(\eta_1) \le \omega_f(\eta_2)$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the modulus of continuity

nodes.summary: Let $a \le b$ and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$. Then the modulus of continuity $\omega_f(\eta)$ of $f$ on $[a, b]$ tends to $0$ as $\eta \to 0^+$.
nodes.title: Theorem I (Modulus of continuity vanishes)
Pointwise and uniform Hölder conditions

nodes.summary: Auerbach's Problem 83 from the Scottish Book: if a continuous function `f` satisfies, at every point `x`, that the difference quotients `|f (x + h) - f x| / |h| ^ a` stay below a constant `M` for all sufficiently small nonzero `h` — that is, if the limsup of the quotients as `h → 0` is `< M`, with `0 < a < 1` — does `f` then satisfy a Hölder condition of exponent `a`?
nodes.title: Auerbach's Hölder condition problem (Scottish Book 83)

nodes.summary: Auerbach's Problem 83 is false: the pointwise limsup condition does not imply a Hölder condition. Source: H. Auerbach, Problem 83 of the Scottish Book; typescript Ad 83 records the negative answer, with Marcinkiewicz's counterexample: a triangular function on intervals `1 / n - xₙ`, `1 / n + xₙ` with height `1 / n` and suitably small half-widths `xₙ`, whose difference quotients are small near every point but which…
nodes.title: Pointwise difference-quotient bounds do not imply Hölder continuity
Rising sun lemma

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a, b$ and a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the rising sun set of $f$ on $(a, b)$ is the set of points $x \in (a, b)$ for which there is some $t$ with $x < t \le b$ and $f(x) < f(t)$.
nodes.title: Rising sun set

nodes.summary: A set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ has a rising sun decomposition for a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ if there are sequences $(c_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $(d_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of real numbers such that $E$ is the union of the open intervals $(c_n, d_n)$, these intervals are pairwise disjoint, and $f(c_n) \le f(d_n)$ for every $n$.
nodes.title: Rising sun decomposition

nodes.summary: Let $a, b$ be real numbers, let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, and let $S$ be the rising sun set of $f$ on $(a, b)$. Then $f$ has the rising sun property on $[a, b]$ if $S$ is open, $S$ is empty if and only if $f$ is antitone (non-increasing) on $[a, b]$, and, whenever $S$ is nonempty, $S$ has a rising sun decomposition for $f$.
nodes.title: Rising sun property

nodes.summary: Let $a < b$ be real numbers and let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$. Then $f$ has the rising sun property on $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Riesz's rising sun lemma
Smooth functions and analytic functions on perfect sets

nodes.summary: A set $s \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is perfect if it is closed, nonempty, and has no isolated points: every $x \in s$ lies in the closure of $s \setminus \{x\}$.
nodes.title: Perfect sets of real numbers

The claim is stated for `C ^ ∞` functions, which is the case refuted by Zahorski's construction.

Takagi function

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $i$, the binary digit $n_i \in \{0, 1\}$ of $n$ is the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$ when $i \ge 0$, and $n_i = 0$ when $i < 0$.
nodes.title: Binary digits of a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $k$ an integer, and write $n_j$ for the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$ (so $n_j = 0$ for $j < 0$). The Takagi coefficients $\ell_i(n, k)$, for natural numbers $i$, are the natural numbers given by $\ell_0(n, k) = 0$ and, for every natural number $i$, with $s_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i-1} n_{k-j}$, by $\ell_{i+1}(n, k) = s_i$ if $n_{k-i} = 0$ and $\ell_{i+1}(n, k) = i - s_i$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Takagi coefficients

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $k$, the Takagi value $\tau(n, k)$ of the dyadic presentation $n / 2^{k+1}$ is the sum of the real series $\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \ell_{i+1}(n, k) / 2^{i+1}$, where $\ell_i(n, k)$ denotes the $i$-th Takagi coefficient of $n$ and $k$.
nodes.title: Takagi function on dyadic presentations

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $i$, the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ equals $1$ if $i \ge 0$ and the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$ is $1$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the binary digits

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi coefficient $\ell_0(n, k)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The Takagi coefficient at index zero

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, every integer $k$ and every natural number $i$, let $s_i = \sum_{j=0}^{i-1} n_{k-j}$, where $n_j$ denotes the binary digit of $n$ at position $j$. Then the Takagi coefficient $\ell_{i+1}(n, k)$ equals $s_i$ if $n_{k-i} = 0$, and equals $i - s_i$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the Takagi coefficients

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi value $\tau(n, k)$ of the dyadic presentation $n / 2^{k+1}$ satisfies $\tau(n, k) = \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} \ell_{i+1}(n, k) / 2^{i+1}$, where $\ell_i(n, k)$ denotes the $i$-th Takagi coefficient of $n$ and $k$.
nodes.title: Series for the Takagi value

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $i < 0$, the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Binary digits at negative positions vanish

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every integer $k$, the Takagi coefficient $\ell_1(n, k)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: The first Takagi coefficient vanishes

nodes.summary: The number $\delta(n)$ of D-nodes in the divide-and-conquer tree on $n$ leaves (OEIS A296062) is defined by the recurrence the paper quotes from Coronado et al.: $\delta(1) = 0$, and for every natural number $m \ge 1$, $\delta(2m) = 2\,\delta(m)$ and $\delta(2m+1) = \delta(m) + \delta(m+1) + 1$. The value at $0$ is the junk value $\delta(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Number of D-nodes of the divide-and-conquer tree

nodes.summary: The divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(1) = 0$.

nodes.summary: For every integer $m > 0$, the divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(2m+1) = \delta(m) + \delta(m+1) + 1$.
nodes.title: Odd-argument recurrence for the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: The divide-and-conquer D-node count $\delta$ satisfies $\delta(2) = 0$, $\delta(3) = 1$, $\delta(4) = 0$, $\delta(5) = 2$, $\delta(6) = 2$ and $\delta(7) = 2$.
nodes.title: Small values of the divide-and-conquer D-node count

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, let $n_i$ be the binary digit of $n$ at position $i$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$). The level count $\lambda_i(n)$ is $n \bmod 2^i$ if $n_i = 0$, and $2^i - (n \bmod 2^i)$ if $n_i = 1$.
nodes.title: Level counts of D-nodes

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $i$ be natural numbers such that the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$) equals $0$. Then the level count of D-nodes is $\lambda_i(n) = n \bmod 2^i$.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $i$ be natural numbers such that the binary digit $n_i$ of $n$ (the coefficient of $2^i$ in the binary expansion of $n$) equals $1$. Then the level count of D-nodes is $\lambda_i(n) = 2^i - (n \bmod 2^i)$.

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the level count of D-nodes on level $0$ is $\lambda_0(n) = n \bmod 2$.

reading_title.source: Number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree

nodes.summary: A $D$-node of a full binary tree is an interior node whose two subtrees have different numbers of leaves. The number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree is the number of its interior nodes that are $D$-nodes.
nodes.title: Number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree

reading_title.source: Number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree

nodes.summary: An $S$-node of a full binary tree is an interior node whose two subtrees have the same number of leaves. The number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree is the number of its interior nodes that are $S$-nodes.
nodes.title: Number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree

nodes.summary: A divide-and-conquer tree is a full binary tree in which, at every interior node, the numbers of leaves of the two subtrees differ by at most $1$. In particular a single leaf is a divide-and-conquer tree.
nodes.title: Divide-and-conquer trees

reading_title.source: Recursion for the number of $D$-nodes

nodes.summary: Write $D(t)$ for the number of $D$-nodes of a full binary tree $t$. If the root of $t$ has left subtree $l$ and right subtree $r$, then $D(t) = \varepsilon + D(l) + D(r)$, where $\varepsilon = 0$ if $l$ and $r$ have the same number of leaves and $\varepsilon = 1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Recursion for the number of $D$-nodes

reading_title.source: Recursion for the number of $S$-nodes

nodes.summary: Write $S(t)$ for the number of $S$-nodes of a full binary tree $t$. If the root of $t$ has left subtree $l$ and right subtree $r$, then $S(t) = \varepsilon + S(l) + S(r)$, where $\varepsilon = 1$ if $l$ and $r$ have the same number of leaves and $\varepsilon = 0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Recursion for the number of $S$-nodes

nodes.summary: The full binary tree consisting of a single leaf has no $D$-nodes and no $S$-nodes, and it is a divide-and-conquer tree.

nodes.summary: A full binary tree whose root has left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is a divide-and-conquer tree if and only if the numbers of leaves of $L$ and $R$ differ by at most $1$ and both $L$ and $R$ are divide-and-conquer trees.

reading_title.source: A finite identity for $\sum_k r^k/(1-ax^k)$ over a field

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $a, r, x \in K$ and let $n \ge 0$ be an integer. Suppose that $1 - a x^k \ne 0$ and $1 - r x^{k-1} \ne 0$ for every integer $k$ with $1 \le k \le n$. Then $\sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{r^k}{1 - a x^k} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{(a r x^k)^k}{1 - a x^k} + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{a^{k-1} \left( (r x^{k-1})^k - (r x^{k-1})^{n+1} \right)}{1 - r x^{k-1}}$. For $n = 0$ all three sums are empty.
nodes.title: A finite identity for $\sum_k r^k/(1-ax^k)$ over a field

Bisection method

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and reals $a$, $b$, two sequences $u, v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ form a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$ when $u_0 = a$, $v_0 = b$, and for every $n$, writing $m_n = (u_n + v_n)/2$ for the midpoint, either $f(m_n) \le 0$, $u_{n+1} = m_n$ and $v_{n+1} = v_n$, or $f(m_n) \ge 0$, $u_{n+1} = u_n$ and $v_{n+1} = m_n$.
nodes.title: Bisection sequence

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $a \le b$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then $a \le u_n \le v_n \le b$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Bisection intervals stay inside the initial interval

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \le b$ with $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ we have $a \le u_n \le v_n \le b$ and $f(u_n) \le 0 \le f(v_n)$.
nodes.title: Bisection invariants

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $a \le b$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $u_n \le u_{n+1} \le v_{n+1} \le v_n$.
nodes.title: Bisection intervals are nested

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $a, b$ be real, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then $v_n - u_n = (b - a)/2^n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Length of the bisection intervals

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and all reals $a$, $b$, there are sequences $u, v$ forming a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$.
nodes.title: Existence of bisection sequences

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \le b$ with $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$. Then there is a bisection sequence $u, v$ for $f$ from $a$ to $b$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $u_n \le u_{n+1} \le v_{n+1} \le v_n$, $v_n - u_n = (b - a)/2^n$, and $f(u_n)\,f(v_n) \le 0$.
nodes.title: Nested bisection intervals from a sign bracket

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$, where $a \le b$ and $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$. Then there is a bisection sequence $u, v$ for $f$ from $a$ to $b$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $u_n \le u_{n+1} \le v_{n+1} \le v_n$, $v_n - u_n = (b - a)/2^n$, and $f(u_n)\,f(v_n) \le 0$.
nodes.title: Bisection method: nested intervals

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a, b]$, where $a \le b$ and $f(a) \le 0 \le f(b)$, and let $u, v$ be a bisection sequence for $f$ from $a$ to $b$. Then there is $c \in [a, b]$ with $f(c) = 0$ such that the midpoints $(u_n + v_n)/2$ converge to $c$ and $|(u_n + v_n)/2 - c| \le (b - a)/2^{n+1}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Bisection method converges at a linear rate

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real normed space, let $t_0 < T$ be real numbers, let $f : \mathbb{R} \times E \to E$ be $C^2$, and let $x : \mathbb{R} \to E$ be differentiable at every $t \in [t_0, T]$ with $x'(t) = f(t, x(t))$. Equilibrium points of logarithmic potentials

nodes.summary: A charge sequence is an arbitrary sequence $(z_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of complex numbers, read as the positions of the charges.
nodes.title: Charge sequences

nodes.summary: A charge sequence $(z_n)$ has distinct positions when its terms are pairwise distinct: $z_m \neq z_n$ whenever $m \neq n$.
nodes.title: Distinct charge positions

nodes.summary: A charge sequence $(z_n)$ is summable when $z_n \neq 0$ for every $n$ and $\sum_n 1/|z_n| < \infty$.
nodes.title: Summable charge sequences

nodes.summary: For a charge sequence $(z_n)$ and a point $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the field at $z$ is the sum $\sum_n 1/(z - z_n)$, where a term with $z_n = z$ counts as $0$ and the sum is taken to be $0$ when the family $\bigl(1/(z - z_n)\bigr)_n$ is not summable.
nodes.title: Field of a charge sequence

nodes.summary: The conjecture states that there exists a charge sequence $(z_n)$ whose positions are pairwise distinct, which is summable ($z_n \neq 0$ for every $n$ and $\sum_n 1/|z_n| < \infty$), and whose field $\sum_n 1/(z - z_n)$ is nonzero at every point $z \in \mathbb{C}$ that is not one of the $z_n$.
nodes.title: Equilibrium-free logarithmic potential conjecture

nodes.summary: There is no charge sequence $(z_n)$ whose positions are pairwise distinct, which is summable ($z_n \neq 0$ for every $n$ and $\sum_n 1/|z_n| < \infty$), and whose field $\sum_n 1/(z - z_n)$ is nonzero at every point $z \in \mathbb{C}$ that is not one of the $z_n$.
nodes.title: The equilibrium-free logarithmic potential conjecture is false

nodes.summary: Let $m > 2$ be a natural number. The function $x \mapsto 1/|x|^{m-2}$ on the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^m$, where $|x|$ is the Euclidean norm, is harmonic on $\mathbb{R}^m \setminus \{0\}$.

nodes.summary: The function $g(x) = \log|x|$, where $|x|$ is the Euclidean norm of $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$, is harmonic on $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0\}$: near every point $x \ne 0$ it is twice continuously differentiable and its Laplacian vanishes.

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real inner product space of dimension $3$, and define $N : E \to \mathbb{R}$ by $N(y) = -1/(4\pi\|y\|)$ for $y \neq 0$ and $N(0) = 0$. Then the Laplacian of $N$ vanishes at every point $x \neq 0$ of $E$.
