nodes.summary: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypergraph on a vertex type $V$ and let $\alpha$ be a type. An $\alpha$-coloring of $\mathcal{H}$ is a map $c$ from the set of edges of $\mathcal{H}$ to $\alpha$ such that $c(e_1) \ne c(e_2)$ for any two distinct edges $e_1$ and $e_2$ of $\mathcal{H}$ that have a vertex in common.
nodes.title: Edge coloring of a hypergraph

nodes.summary: A hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is linear if any two distinct edges of $\mathcal{H}$ have at most one vertex in common.
nodes.title: Linear hypergraph

nodes.summary: The chromatic index of a hypergraph $\mathcal{H}$ is the least natural number $n$ such that $\mathcal{H}$ has a coloring with colors in $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and $0$ if there is no such $n$.
nodes.title: Chromatic index of a hypergraph

nodes.summary: For every sufficiently large natural number $n$, every linear hypergraph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ has chromatic index at most $n$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture for sufficiently many vertices
Hitting sets for partial designs

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every real $c$ with $0 < c < 1$ there is a natural number $C$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every family $\mathcal{B}$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which each member has more than $c\sqrt{n}$ elements and any two distinct members share at most one element, some set $B \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ meets every member of $\mathcal{B}$ in at least $1$ and at most $C$…
nodes.title: Bounded hitting sets for large partial designs (Erdős Problem 664)

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every real $c$ with $0 < c < 1$ there is a natural number $C$ such that for every natural number $n$ and every family $\mathcal{B}$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which each member has more than $c\sqrt{n}$ elements and any two distinct members share at most one element, some set $B \subseteq \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ meets every member of $\mathcal{B}$ in at least $1$ and at most $C$…
nodes.title: Large partial designs need not have uniformly bounded hitting sets
Hypergraph chromatic number

nodes.summary: A hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, given as a finite set of edges (sets of vertices), is $k$-colorable when some coloring of the vertices with $k$ colors leaves no edge monochromatic: every edge of $H$ contains two vertices of different colors.
nodes.title: Colorable hypergraph

nodes.summary: The statement that for every integer $r \ge 3$ there is a $K$ such that for every $k \ge K$, every $n$ and every $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with chromatic number $k$ (it is $k$-colorable but not $(k-1)$-colorable), $H$ has at least $\binom{(r-1)(k-1)+1}{r}$ edges, and if it has exactly that many edges then it is the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on some set of $(r-1)(k-1)+1$…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 832

nodes.summary: There is an integer $r \ge 3$ such that for infinitely many $k$ there are an $n$ and an $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with chromatic number $k$ (it is $k$-colorable but not $(k-1)$-colorable) that either has fewer than $\binom{(r-1)(k-1)+1}{r}$ edges, or has exactly that many edges but is not the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on any set of $(r-1)(k-1)+1$ of its vertices.
nodes.title: Alon's refutation of Erdős Problem 832
Degrees in 3-chromatic hypergraphs

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a real $c > 0$ such that for every natural number $r \ge 2$, every $n$ and every hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (a finite set of edges, each a set of exactly $r$ vertices) that is $3$-colorable but not $2$-colorable, some vertex lies in at least $(1 + c)^r$ edges of $H$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 833

nodes.summary: There is a real $c > 0$ such that for every natural number $r \ge 2$, every $n$ and every hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (a finite set of edges, each a set of exactly $r$ vertices) that is $3$-colorable but not $2$-colorable, some vertex lies in at least $(1 + c)^r$ edges of $H$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 833 holds
Independence in linear triple systems

nodes.summary: A finite family $H$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a linear triple system (a $3$-uniform linear hypergraph, or partial Steiner triple system) when every member of $H$ has exactly three elements and any two distinct members of $H$ share at most one element.
nodes.title: Linear triple systems

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f(n)$ is the largest $m \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every linear triple system $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has an independent set of size at least $m$: a set $I$ of at least $m$ vertices such that no triple of $H$ is a subset of $I$. The largest such $m$ exists because $m = 0$ qualifies and no such $m$ exceeds $n$.
nodes.title: Independence number of linear triple systems

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $f(n)$ be the independence number of linear triple systems on $n$ vertices: the largest $m$ such that every linear triple system on $n$ vertices has an independent set (a set of vertices containing no triple of the system) of at least $m$ vertices. This is the statement that $f(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n \log n})$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f(n) = O(\sqrt{n \log n})$ and…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1024: the Phelps–Rödl asymptotic

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $f(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that every linear triple system on $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (a family of $3$-element sets, any two distinct ones sharing at most one element) has an independent set of at least $m$ vertices, that is, a set of at least $m$ vertices containing no triple of the system. Then $f(n) = \Theta(\sqrt{n \log n})$ as $n \to \infty$: there are constants $c, C > 0$ such that…
nodes.title: Phelps–Rödl theorem on independence in linear triple systems
Independent sets in hypergraphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite hypergraph, that is a finite family of finite sets of vertices, called its edges. A finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in $H$ when no edge $e$ of $H$ satisfies $e \subseteq I$.
nodes.title: Independent set in a hypergraph

nodes.summary: A finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in a finite hypergraph $H$ if and only if no edge $e$ of $H$ satisfies $e \subseteq I$.
nodes.title: Independence unfolded

nodes.summary: Every finite set of vertices is independent in the empty hypergraph, the hypergraph with no edges.
nodes.title: Every set is independent in the empty hypergraph

nodes.summary: If a finite set $I$ of vertices is independent in a finite hypergraph $H$ and $J \subseteq I$, then $J$ is independent in $H$.
nodes.title: Subsets of independent sets are independent

nodes.summary: For a finite hypergraph $H$, the empty set is independent in $H$ if and only if every edge of $H$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: When the empty set is independent

nodes.summary: A finite hypergraph $H$ on a vertex type $V$, that is a finite family of finite subsets of $V$, is a Steiner triple system when it is $3$-uniform (every edge of $H$ has exactly $3$ elements) and any two distinct vertices $u \ne v$ of $V$ lie together in exactly one edge of $H$.
nodes.title: Steiner triple system

nodes.summary: If $H$ is a Steiner triple system, then $H$ is $3$-uniform: every edge of $H$ has exactly $3$ elements.
nodes.title: Steiner triple systems are 3-uniform

nodes.summary: If $H$ is a Steiner triple system on a vertex type $V$, then for all vertices $u \ne v$ of $V$ there is exactly one edge $e$ of $H$ with $u \in e$ and $v \in e$.
nodes.title: Pairs in a Steiner triple system

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a finite set of vertices and let $P$ be a property of finite sets of vertices. If $t$ satisfies $P$, then there is exactly one finite set $e$ of vertices with $e \in \{t\}$ and $P(e)$.
nodes.title: Unique element of a singleton family
Independent sets of set mappings on pairs

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ assign to each unordered pair $\{x, y\}$ of elements of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (possibly with $x = y$) an element of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. A finite set $X \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is independent for $f$ if $f(\{x, y\}) \notin X$ for all distinct $x, y \in X$.
nodes.title: Independent set of a set mapping on pairs

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $g(n)$ is the largest $k$ such that every map $f$ from the unordered pairs $\{x, y\}$ of elements of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (possibly with $x = y$) to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $f(\{x, y\}) \notin \{x, y\}$ for all distinct $x, y$ has an independent set of at least $k$ elements, that is, a set $X \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $|X| \ge k$ and $f(\{x, y\}) \notin X$ for all distinct…
nodes.title: Independence number of set mappings on pairs

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $g(n)$ be the largest $k$ such that every map $f$ from the unordered pairs of elements of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $f(\{x, y\}) \notin \{x, y\}$ for all distinct $x, y$ admits a set $X$ of at least $k$ elements with $f(\{x, y\}) \notin X$ for all distinct $x, y \in X$ (and $g(n) = 0$ if no largest such $k$ exists). This is the proposition that…
nodes.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 1025

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $g(n)$ be the largest $k$ such that every map $f$ from the unordered pairs of elements of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $f(\{x, y\}) \notin \{x, y\}$ for all distinct $x, y$ admits a set $X$ of at least $k$ elements with $f(\{x, y\}) \notin X$ for all distinct $x, y \in X$ (and $g(n) = 0$ if no largest such $k$ exists). Then there are constants $c, C > 0$ such that…
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1025 (Spencer; Conlon, Fox and Sudakov)
Intersecting families with large cover number

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers is an Erdős–Lovász family of order $n$ when every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has exactly $n$ elements, any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ (not necessarily distinct) have a common element, and every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member of $\mathcal{F}$, where $n - 1$ is read as $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Lovász family

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a natural number $C$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers in which every member has exactly $n$ elements, any two members have a common element, every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member, and $|\mathcal{F}| \le C n$. This expresses $f(n) \ll n$, where $f(n)$ is the least size of such a family.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 21 (Erdős–Lovász)

nodes.summary: There is a natural number $C$ such that for every $n \ge 1$ there is a finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of finite sets of natural numbers with the following properties: every member of $\mathcal{F}$ has exactly $n$ elements, any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ have a common element, every set of at most $n - 1$ natural numbers is disjoint from some member of $\mathcal{F}$, and $|\mathcal{F}| \le C n$.
nodes.title: Kahn's theorem on the Erdős–Lovász problem
Kneser hypergraphs

nodes.summary: The statement that for all natural numbers $n, k, r, t$ with $r \ge 1$, $t \ge 1$ and $n \ge kr + (t - 1)(k - 1)$, every coloring of the $r$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with $t$ colors has a color class containing $k$ pairwise disjoint $r$-element subsets.
nodes.title: Erdős's Kneser hypergraph problem

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n, k, r, t$ with $r \ge 1$, $t \ge 1$ and $n \ge kr + (t - 1)(k - 1)$, every coloring of the $r$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with $t$ colors has a color class containing $k$ pairwise disjoint $r$-element subsets.
nodes.title: Alon–Frankl–Lovász theorem on Kneser hypergraphs
Sets meeting but not containing members of a family

nodes.summary: For a finite family $F$ of finite sets of natural numbers with union $X$, this is the finite set of all $B \subseteq X$ that meet every member of $F$ and contain none of them.
nodes.title: Sets meeting but not containing the members of a family

nodes.summary: For every real $c > 0$ there is a real $\delta > 0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every finite family $F$ of finite sets of natural numbers, each of size $n$, with $|F| \le c \cdot 2^n$ and with union $X$, has at least $\delta \cdot 2^{|X|}$ subsets $B \subseteq X$ that meet every member of $F$ and contain none of them.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1027 (sets meeting but not containing members of a family)

nodes.summary: For every real $c > 0$ there is a real $\delta > 0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every finite family $F$ of finite sets of natural numbers, each of size $n$, with $|F| \le c \cdot 2^n$ and with union $X$, has at least $\delta \cdot 2^{|X|}$ subsets $B \subseteq X$ that meet every member of $F$ and contain none of them.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 1027 holds
Strong matchings and covers in hypergraphs

nodes.summary: For a hypergraph on a vertex set $V$ whose edges form a set $E$ of finite subsets of $V$, a set $M$ is a matching when $M \subseteq E$ and any two distinct members of $M$ are disjoint.
nodes.title: Matching in a hypergraph

nodes.summary: For a hypergraph with edge set $E$, a set $M$ is a strongly maximal matching (Aharoni) when $M$ is a matching of $E$ and every matching $M'$ of $E$ satisfies $|M' \setminus M| \le |M \setminus M'|$, comparing the cardinalities as cardinal numbers.
nodes.title: Strongly maximal matching

nodes.summary: The statement that for every vertex set $V$ and every set $E$ of finite subsets of $V$ such that some natural number $k$ bounds the number of elements of every edge in $E$, the hypergraph with edge set $E$ has a strongly maximal matching.
nodes.title: Strongly maximal matchings in hypergraphs with bounded edges

nodes.summary: There are a vertex set $V$, a set $E$ of finite subsets of $V$ and a natural number $k$ such that every edge in $E$ has at most $k$ elements, but the hypergraph with edge set $E$ has no strongly maximal matching.
nodes.title: Bounded edge size does not guarantee a strongly maximal matching

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a set of finite subsets of a type $V$, the edges of a hypergraph. A set $X \subseteq V$ is a (vertex) cover of $E$ if it meets every edge: every $e \in E$ contains some $v \in X$.
nodes.title: Vertex cover of a hypergraph

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a set of finite subsets of a type $V$, the edges of a hypergraph. A set $X \subseteq V$ is a strongly minimal cover of $E$ (Aharoni) if $X$ is a cover of $E$, that is, it meets every edge in $E$, and $|X \setminus X'| \le |X' \setminus X|$, as cardinals, for every cover $X'$ of $E$.
nodes.title: Strongly minimal cover

nodes.summary: The statement that for every type $V$, every set $E$ of finite subsets of $V$ (the edges of a hypergraph, possibly infinitely many) and every natural number $k$ such that each edge in $E$ is nonempty and has at most $k$ elements, the hypergraph with edge set $E$ has a strongly minimal cover.
nodes.title: Aharoni's strongly minimal cover conjecture

nodes.summary: There are a type $V$, a set $E$ of finite subsets of $V$ (the edges of a hypergraph) and a natural number $k$ such that every edge in $E$ is nonempty and has at most $k$ elements, but no strongly minimal cover of $E$ exists. Here a cover of $E$ is a set $X \subseteq V$ that meets every edge in $E$, and a cover $X$ is strongly minimal if $|X \setminus X'| \le |X' \setminus X|$, as cardinals, for every cover $X'$ of…
nodes.title: Aharoni's strongly minimal cover conjecture is false
Transversal-critical triple systems

nodes.summary: There exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that some set of at most $3$ vertices meets every edge of $H$, no set of at most $2$ vertices meets every edge of $H$, for every edge $e$ of $H$ some set of at most $2$ vertices meets every edge of $H$ other than $e$, and every vertex lies in at least $7$ edges of $H$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 834 for transversal-critical triple systems

nodes.summary: There are no $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that some set of at most $3$ vertices meets every edge of $H$, no set of at most $2$ vertices meets every edge of $H$, for every edge $e$ of $H$ some set of at most $2$ vertices meets every edge of $H$ other than $e$, and every vertex lies in at least $7$ edges of $H$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 834 fails for transversal-critical triple systems
Uniform hypergraphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform when every edge $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.
nodes.title: Uniform hypergraphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges when there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$ such that at least $k$ edges of $H$ are subsets of $S$.
nodes.title: Subhypergraph containment

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$ and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform if and only if every member $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.
nodes.title: Characterization of uniform hypergraphs

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$ and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges if and only if there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$ such that at least $k$ members of $H$ are subsets of $S$.
nodes.title: Characterization of subhypergraph containment

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting when every two distinct members meet: for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: Intersecting families

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting if and only if for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.
nodes.title: Characterization of intersecting families

nodes.summary: Block designs, Steiner systems, pairwise balanced designs and linear spaces, Latin squares and transversals, Hadamard and partial Hadamard matrices, magic squares, 0-1 matrices with prescribed margins (Gale–Ryser), binary matrices up to rotation, and sign tables from determinant-moment expansions; cyclic difference sets go to Sidon sets and difference sets.
nodes.title: Designs, Latin squares and combinatorial matrices

nodes.summary: Let $m, n \ge 1$. For an $m \times n$ matrix $x$ with entries $x_{r,s} \in \{0, 1\}$, rows indexed by $0 \le r < m$ and columns by $0 \le s < n$, put $N(x) = \sum_{r=0}^{m-1} \sum_{s=0}^{n-1} x_{r,s} \, 2^{rn+s}$, and for $0 \le i < m$, $0 \le j < n$ let $x^{(i,j)}$ be the rotated matrix with entries $x^{(i,j)}_{r,s} = x_{(r+i) \bmod m, \, (s+j) \bmod n}$. The number of such matrices $x$ with…
nodes.title: Counting binary matrices up to cyclic rotations

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, write $[n] = \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $A$ and $B$ be Latin squares of order $n$ with rows, columns and entries indexed by $[n]$: every row and every column of each square is a bijection of $[n]$. For a row index $i$ write $A_i$ and $B_i$ for the permutations $j \mapsto A_{ij}$ and $j \mapsto B_{ij}$ of $[n]$. Then the map $(i, j) \mapsto (A_{ij}, B_{ij})$ is a bijection of…
nodes.title: Mann's product criterion for orthogonal Latin squares
Block-compatible sequences of pairwise balanced designs

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite list of blocks $B_1, \ldots, B_m \subseteq \{0, \ldots, n - 1\}$ is a pairwise balanced design on these $n$ points when the blocks are pairwise distinct, every block has at least two points, and every two distinct points lie in exactly one common block.
nodes.title: Pairwise balanced design

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite sequence $(x_1, \ldots, x_m)$ of natural numbers is block-compatible for $n$ when $x_1 \ge x_2 \ge \cdots \ge x_m$, every $x_k$ satisfies $2 \le x_k \le n$, and there is a pairwise balanced design on the point set $\{0, \ldots, n - 1\}$ whose blocks, listed in order as $B_1, \ldots, B_m$, have sizes $|B_k| = x_k$ for every $k$.
nodes.title: Block-compatible sequences

nodes.summary: The statement that there are a real number $c > 0$ and a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ there is a finite set of at least $\exp(c \sqrt{n} \log n)$ distinct finite sequences of natural numbers, each of which is block-compatible for $n$. Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Many block-compatible sequences

nodes.summary: There are a real number $c > 0$ and a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ there is a finite set of at least $\exp(c \sqrt{n} \log n)$ distinct finite sequences of natural numbers, each of which is block-compatible for $n$. Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Many block-compatible sequences (Erdős Problem 732)
Even tables in random determinant moments

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $M$ a commutative monoid and $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to M$ a function. A column is a finite list of entries from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$; for each $j$ in this range let $c_j$ be the number of times $j$ occurs in the column. The weight of the column is the product $\prod_{j=0}^{n-1} f(c_j)$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Column weight

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, an even $k \times n$ table is a $k \times n$ array of entries from $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $k$ is even, every row is a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and in every column each value that occurs there occurs an even number of times.
nodes.title: Even table

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a commutative monoid and $f : \mathbb{N} \to M$. The weight of an even $k \times n$ table $t$ with respect to $f$ is the product of the column weights of its $n$ columns with respect to $f$:
nodes.title: Weight of an even table
Existence of Steiner systems

nodes.summary: The statement that for all natural numbers $r < k$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $\binom{k-i}{r-i} \mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0 \le i < r$, there is a Steiner system $S(r, k, n)$: a family $F$ of $k$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that every $r$-element subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is contained in exactly one member of $F$ (Erdős Problem 722).
nodes.title: Existence conjecture for Steiner systems

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $r < k$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $\binom{k-i}{r-i} \mid \binom{n-i}{r-i}$ for all $0 \le i < r$, there is a Steiner system $S(r, k, n)$: a family $F$ of $k$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that every $r$-element subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is contained in exactly one member of $F$.
nodes.title: Keevash's existence theorem for Steiner systems
Gale–Ryser theorem

nodes.summary: For a sequence $r = (r_0, \dots, r_{m-1})$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k$, the prefix sum of $r$ of length $k$ is $\sum_{i < \min(k, m)} r_i$, the sum of the first $k$ entries of $r$, or of all entries when $k \ge m$.
nodes.title: Prefix sum

nodes.summary: For a sequence $r = (r_0, \dots, r_{m-1})$ of natural numbers and a natural number $k \le m$, the prefix sum of $r$ of length $k$ equals $\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} r_i$.
nodes.title: Prefix sums within the sequence length

nodes.summary: Let $r = (r_0, \dots, r_{m-1})$ and $c = (c_0, \dots, c_{n-1})$ be nonincreasing sequences of natural numbers. There is an $m \times n$ matrix with entries in $\{0, 1\}$ whose $i$-th row sums to $r_i$ for every $i$ and whose $j$-th column sums to $c_j$ for every $j$ if and only if $\sum_{i < m} r_i = \sum_{j < n} c_j$ and, for every $k \le m$,
nodes.title: Gale–Ryser theorem
High-girth Steiner triple systems

nodes.summary: The statement that for every integer $g \ge 2$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $n \equiv 1$ or $n \equiv 3 \pmod 6$ there is a Steiner triple system on the $n$ points $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (three-point blocks, every pair of distinct points in exactly one block) in which every set of $j$ distinct blocks, with $2 \le j \le g$, covers at least $j + 3$ points.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 207

nodes.summary: For every integer $g \ge 2$ there is an $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ with $n \equiv 1$ or $n \equiv 3 \pmod 6$ there is a Steiner triple system on the $n$ points $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ in which every set of $j$ distinct blocks, with $2 \le j \le g$, covers at least $j + 3$ points.
nodes.title: High-girth Steiner triple systems exist
Line counts of linear spaces

nodes.summary: A family $A_1, \dots, A_t$ of subsets of $\{1, \dots, v\}$ is a $2$-design (also called a pairwise balanced design or a linear space) when every block $A_i$ has at least two points and every pair of distinct points of $\{1, \dots, v\}$ lies in exactly one block.
nodes.title: Linear spaces (2-designs)

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every prime power $p$, with $n = p^2 + p + 1$, every $2$-design $A_1, \dots, A_t$ on $\{1, \dots, n\}$ with more than $n$ blocks has at least $n + p$ blocks. Here a $2$-design is a family of subsets in which every block has at least two points and every pair of distinct points lies in exactly one block.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 903: line counts just above a projective plane

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime power and $n = p^2 + p + 1$. Let $A_1, \dots, A_t$ be a $2$-design on $\{1, \dots, n\}$: every block $A_i$ has at least two points and every pair of distinct points lies in exactly one block. If $t > n$, then $t \ge n + p$.

nodes.title: Equal line sums from two orthogonal diagonal Latin squares

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ array $M$ of natural numbers, with rows and columns indexed by $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, is a *magic square* when there is a natural number $s$ such that every row of $M$ and every column of $M$ sums to $s$, and also $\sum_i M_{i,i} = s$ (the main diagonal) and $\sum_i M_{i,n-1-i} = s$ (the anti-diagonal).
nodes.title: Magic squares

nodes.summary: An $n \times n$ array $M$ of natural numbers is a *reduced magic square of order $n$* when it is a magic square and its entries are $0, 1, \dots, n^2 - 1$, each exactly once; equivalently, every entry of $M$ is less than $n^2$ and distinct cells of $M$ hold distinct entries.
nodes.title: Reduced magic squares

nodes.summary: The $3 \times 3$ square with rows $(7, 0, 5)$, $(2, 4, 6)$ and $(3, 8, 1)$, a form of the Lo Shu square with every entry reduced by $1$, is a reduced magic square of order $3$; its magic sum is $12$.
nodes.title: The reduced Lo Shu square

nodes.summary: The $2 \times 2$ square with rows $(0, 1)$ and $(2, 3)$ is not a reduced magic square.

nodes.summary: The sign of a bit $b \in \{0, 1\}$ is the integer $\sigma(b)$ given by $\sigma(0) = -1$ and $\sigma(1) = 1$.
nodes.title: Sign of a bit

nodes.summary: Read a bit $b \in \{0, 1\}$ as the sign $\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma(0) = -1$ and $\sigma(1) = 1$. An $n \times t$ matrix $M$ with entries in $\{0, 1\}$ is a partial Hadamard matrix when its rows are pairwise orthogonal as sign vectors: for all distinct rows $i \ne i'$, $\sum_{j < t} \sigma(M_{ij}) \sigma(M_{i'j}) = 0$.
nodes.title: Partial Hadamard matrices

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $t$, $N_{n,t}$ is the number of $n \times t$ partial Hadamard matrices, that is, of $n \times t$ matrices with entries in $\{0, 1\}$ whose rows are pairwise orthogonal when each entry $0$ is read as the sign $-1$ and each entry $1$ as the sign $1$.
nodes.title: Number of partial Hadamard matrices

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the number $N_{n,0}$ of $n \times 0$ partial Hadamard matrices is $1$: the orthogonality conditions are empty sums, so the empty matrix is the only one.
nodes.title: Width-zero partial Hadamard count

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of odd order, written additively, and let $A, B \subseteq G$ be subsets with $|A| = |B|$. Then there is a bijection $f \colon A \to B$ such that the sums $a + f(a)$, for $a \in A$, are pairwise distinct.

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field. A matroid $M$ on a type $E$ is algebraic over $K$ if it has an algebraic representation over $K$ whose extension field lies in the larger of the universes of $K$ and $E$.

nodes.summary: A matroid $M$ on a type $E$ is algebraic if it has an algebraic representation over some field whose base field and extension field lie in the same universe as $E$.

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $M$ a matroid on a type $E$. If $M$ has an algebraic representation over $K$ whose extension field lies in the larger of the universes of $K$ and $E$, then $M$ is algebraic over $K$.

nodes.summary: If a matroid $M$ on a type $E$ has an algebraic representation over some field whose base field and extension field lie in the same universe as $E$, then $M$ is algebraic.

nodes.summary: For a matroid $M$ and a set $X$, this is the rank $r(X)$ of $X$ in $M$, the size of a largest independent set of $M$ contained in $X$, taken as a natural number; it is $0$ when this rank is infinite.
nodes.title: Rank of a set in a matroid, as a natural number

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite matroid on the ground set $E$ with rank function $r$, and let $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$ be its characteristic polynomial. For a natural number $j$, this is the integer coefficient of $\lambda^j$ in $\chi_M$, that is, the sum of $(-1)^{|I|}$ over the subsets $I \subseteq E$ with $r(E) - r(I) = j$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of a matroid

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite matroid on the ground set $E$ with rank function $r$ and characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$. For a natural number $k$, $w_k(M)$ is the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r(E) - k}$ in $\chi_M$ when $k \le r(E)$, and $w_k(M) = 0$ when $k > r(E)$.
nodes.title: Absolute coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of a matroid

nodes.summary: For every finite matroid $M$ on a ground set $E$ with rank function $r$, let $w_k(M)$ be the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r(E) - k}$ in the characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$ when $k \le r(E)$, and $w_k(M) = 0$ when $k > r(E)$. Then $w_{k-1}(M) \, w_{k+1}(M) \le w_k(M)^2$ for every natural number $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Log-concavity of the characteristic polynomial of a matroid, statement

nodes.summary: For every finite matroid $M$ on a ground set $E$ with rank function $r$, let $w_k(M)$ be the absolute value of the coefficient of $\lambda^{r(E) - k}$ in the characteristic polynomial $\chi_M(\lambda) = \sum_{I \subseteq E} (-1)^{|I|} \lambda^{r(E) - r(I)}$ when $k \le r(E)$, and $w_k(M) = 0$ when $k > r(E)$. Then $w_{k-1}(M) \, w_{k+1}(M) \le w_k(M)^2$ for every natural number $k \ge 1$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, $H^d_n$ denotes the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$, including the zero polynomial.
nodes.title: Homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$

nodes.summary: $P^d_n$ is the set of homogeneous polynomials $f$ of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$ such that the coefficient in $f$ of every monomial of degree $d$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: Homogeneous polynomials with positive coefficients

nodes.summary: For a homogeneous polynomial $f$ of degree $2$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$, its Hessian is the real $n \times n$ matrix $\mathcal{H}_f$ of second partial derivatives of $f$: the diagonal entry $(i, i)$ is twice the coefficient of $w_i^2$ in $f$, and for $i \ne j$ the entry $(i, j)$ is the coefficient of $w_i w_j$ in $f$.
nodes.title: Hessian of a quadratic form

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the set $\mathring{L}^d_n$ of strictly Lorentzian polynomials of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$ is defined by recursion on $d$. Let $P^d_n$ be the set of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in which every monomial of degree $d$ has a strictly positive coefficient, and let $\partial_i$ be the partial derivative with respect to $w_i$. Then $\mathring{L}^0_n = P^0_n$ and…
nodes.title: Strictly Lorentzian polynomials

nodes.summary: A subset $J \subseteq \mathbb{N}^n$ is M-convex if for all $\alpha, \beta \in J$ and every index $i$ with $\alpha_i > \beta_i$ there is an index $j$ with $\alpha_j < \beta_j$ and $\alpha - e_i + e_j \in J$, where $e_1, \dots, e_n$ are the standard unit vectors of $\mathbb{N}^n$.
nodes.title: M-convex sets

nodes.summary: $M^d_n$ is the set of homogeneous polynomials $f$ of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$ whose coefficients are all nonnegative and whose support, the set of exponent vectors $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n$ of the monomials with nonzero coefficient in $f$, is M-convex.
nodes.title: Homogeneous polynomials with M-convex support

nodes.summary: A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$ is stable if either $f$ is the zero polynomial or $f(z_1, \dots, z_n) \ne 0$ for all $z_1, \dots, z_n$ in the open upper half plane $\mathbb{H} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Im} z > 0\}$.
nodes.title: Stable polynomials

nodes.summary: $S^d_n$ is the set of homogeneous polynomials $f$ of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$ whose coefficients are all nonnegative and that are stable: either $f$ is the zero polynomial or $f$ has no zero in $\mathbb{H}^n$, where $\mathbb{H}$ is the open upper half plane in $\mathbb{C}$.
nodes.title: Stable homogeneous polynomials with nonnegative coefficients

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the set $L^d_n$ of Lorentzian polynomials is a set of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$, defined by recursion on $d$. For $d \le 2$, $L^d_n = S^d_n$, the set of homogeneous stable polynomials of degree $d$ with nonnegative coefficients. For $d \ge 3$, $L^d_n$ is the set of $f \in M^d_n$ (the homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ with nonnegative…
nodes.title: The set of Lorentzian polynomials

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $d$, the closure of the set $\mathring{L}^d_n$ of strictly Lorentzian polynomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables, taken in the space $H^d_n$ of homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{R}[w_1, \dots, w_n]$ with the Euclidean topology on coefficients, is the set $L^d_n$ of Lorentzian polynomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables.

nodes.title: Matroid intersection for abstract rank functions

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be matroids on a finite type $\alpha$, with arbitrary ground sets, and let $k$ be a natural number. There is a set $I \subseteq \alpha$ independent in both $M_1$ and $M_2$ with $|I| \ge k$ if and only if every $X \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies $k \le r_1(X) + r_2(\alpha \setminus X)$, where $r_i(Y)$ is the largest size of a subset of $Y$ independent in $M_i$.
nodes.title: Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be matroids on a finite type $\alpha$, each with ground set all of $\alpha$, and let $k$ be a natural number. There is a set $I \subseteq \alpha$ independent in both $M_1$ and $M_2$ with $|I| \ge k$ if and only if every $X \subseteq \alpha$ satisfies $k \le r_1(X) + r_2(\alpha \setminus X)$, where $r_i$ is the rank function of $M_i$.
nodes.title: Edmonds' matroid intersection theorem for matroids on the whole type
Matroid partition theorem

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set, let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E(M) \subseteq E$, let $S \subseteq E$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $S = J_1 \cup \dots \cup J_k$ for some sets $J_1, \dots, J_k$ that are independent in $M$ (not necessarily disjoint) if and only if $|X| \le k \, r_M(X)$ for every $X \subseteq S$, where $r_M(X)$ denotes the rank in $M$ of $X \cap E(M)$.
nodes.title: Edmonds' matroid partition theorem, arbitrary ground set

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set, let $M$ be a matroid whose ground set is all of $E$, let $S \subseteq E$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $S = J_1 \cup \dots \cup J_k$ for some sets $J_1, \dots, J_k$ that are independent in $M$ (not necessarily disjoint) if and only if $|X| \le k \, r_M(X)$ for every $X \subseteq S$, where $r_M$ is the rank function of $M$.

nodes.summary: A matroid $M$ on elements of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is simple when the set $\{e, f\}$ is independent in $M$ for all $e, f \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, so that every set of at most two of these elements is independent (no loops, no parallel pairs).

nodes.summary: Given real weights $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ on the points $0, \dots, n-1$, the weight of a set $S$ of points is $\sum_{i \in S} a_i$.

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a matroid on elements of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ be real weights, the weight of a set of points being the sum of the weights of its points. The graph of non-negative lines has as vertices the points $i$ with $a_i \ge 0$, and two distinct vertices are adjacent when some line of $M$ (a flat of rank $2$) contains both and has non-negative weight.

nodes.title: Partially ordered sets
Chain polynomials of posets

nodes.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $P$ and each natural number $k$, let $c_k(P)$ be the number of $k$-element chains of $P$, that is, of $k$-element subsets of $P$ any two of whose elements are comparable; in particular $c_0(P) = 1$, counting the empty chain. The chain polynomial of $P$ is the polynomial $C(P, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(P)\, t^k$ with integer coefficients.
nodes.title: Chain polynomial

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite distributive lattice $L$, every complex root of the chain polynomial $C(L, t)$ is real, where $C(L, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(L)\, t^k$ and $c_k(L)$ is the number of $k$-element chains of $L$.
nodes.title: Stanley's Problem 20' on chain polynomials of distributive lattices

nodes.summary: It is not true that for every finite distributive lattice $L$ every complex root of the chain polynomial $C(L, t)$ is real, where $C(L, t) = \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k(L)\, t^k$ and $c_k(L)$ is the number of $k$-element chains of $L$.
nodes.title: Stanley's Problem 20' has a negative answer
Dilworth's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partially ordered set. A finite set $C$ of finite subsets of $\alpha$ is a chain cover of $\alpha$ when every member of $C$ is a chain and every element of $\alpha$ lies in some member of $C$.
nodes.title: Chain cover

nodes.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum antichain size of $\alpha$ (its width) is the largest number of elements of an antichain in $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Maximum antichain size

nodes.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the minimum chain cover size of $\alpha$ is the smallest number of chains in a chain cover of $\alpha$, that is, in a finite set of chains of $\alpha$ whose union is $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Minimum chain cover size

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially ordered set. Every antichain $A$ in $\alpha$ has at most as many elements as the maximum antichain size of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Antichains are no larger than the maximum antichain size

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially ordered set. If $C$ is a chain cover of $\alpha$, that is, a finite set of chains of $\alpha$ whose union is $\alpha$, then the minimum chain cover size of $\alpha$ is at most the number of chains in $C$.
nodes.title: Chain covers bound the minimum chain cover size

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially ordered set. The maximum antichain size of $\alpha$ equals its minimum chain cover size: the largest number of elements of an antichain in $\alpha$ equals the smallest number of chains whose union is $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Dilworth's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially ordered set. Some antichain in $\alpha$ has exactly as many elements as the maximum antichain size of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: The maximum antichain size is attained

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite partially ordered set. Some chain cover $C$ of $\alpha$, a finite set of chains of $\alpha$ whose union is $\alpha$, consists of exactly as many chains as the minimum chain cover size of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: The minimum chain cover size is attained

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 0$, $k - 1 < k$.
nodes.title: A positive natural number exceeds its predecessor

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a map $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ is an increasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$ when $\varphi(i) < \varphi(j)$ and $f(\varphi(i)) < f(\varphi(j))$ for all $i < j$.
nodes.title: Increasing subsequence

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, a map $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ is a decreasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$ when $\varphi(i) < \varphi(j)$ and $f(\varphi(j)) < f(\varphi(i))$ for all $i < j$.
nodes.title: Decreasing subsequence

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$, a position $p$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the statement that $k \ge 1$ and $f$ has an increasing subsequence $\varphi$ of length $k$ (indices and values strictly increasing) ending at $p$, that is, with $\varphi(k-1) = p$.
nodes.title: Increasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$, a position $p$ and $k \in \mathbb{N}$, this is the statement that $k \ge 1$ and $f$ has a decreasing subsequence $\varphi$ of length $k$ (indices strictly increasing and values strictly decreasing) ending at $p$, that is, with $\varphi(k-1) = p$.
nodes.title: Decreasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: There are no $i, j \in \{0\}$ with $i < j$.
nodes.title: No strict pair in a one-element set

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every position $p$, the subsequence of length $1$ consisting of the term at position $p$ is a strictly increasing subsequence of $f$.
nodes.title: One-term subsequences are increasing

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every position $p$, the subsequence of length $1$ consisting of the term at position $p$ is a strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$.
nodes.title: One-term subsequences are decreasing

nodes.summary: For $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a position $p$, this is the largest $k \le N$ such that $f$ has an increasing subsequence of length $k$ ending at $p$, where indices and values both increase strictly.
nodes.title: Length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: For a real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and an index $p$, this is the largest $k$ such that $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $k$ ending at $p$, that is, indices $i_1 < \dots < i_k = p$ with $f(i_1) > \dots > f(i_k)$. The maximum exists: $k = 1$ qualifies, and every such $k$ is at most $N$.
nodes.title: Length of the longest decreasing subsequence ending at a point

nodes.summary: If $\varphi \colon \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ is strictly increasing, that is $\varphi(i) < \varphi(j)$ whenever $i < j$, then $k \le N$.
nodes.title: Subsequences are no longer than the sequence

nodes.summary: For every $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every position $p$, $f$ has an increasing subsequence ending at $p$ whose length equals the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: The longest increasing subsequence ending at a position is attained

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every index $p$, $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence ending at $p$ whose length equals the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: The longest decreasing subsequence ending at a point is attained

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and let $p$ be a position. If $f$ has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $k$ ending exactly at $p$, then $k$ is at most the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Bound by the longest increasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and let $p$ be a position. If $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $k$ ending exactly at $p$, then $k$ is at most the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Bound by the longest decreasing subsequence ending at a position

nodes.summary: For every $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every position $p$, the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: Longest increasing subsequences ending at a position have length at least one

nodes.summary: For every real sequence $f$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every index $p$, the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$ is at least $1$.
nodes.title: The longest decreasing subsequence ending at a point has length at least one

nodes.summary: Given $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and $p \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$, the appended map on $\{0, \dots, k\}$ sends each $i < k$ to $\varphi(i)$ and sends $k$ to $p$.
nodes.title: Appending an entry to a map of indices

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ be strictly increasing with $\varphi(k-1) = q$. Then $\varphi(i) \le q$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: Entries of a strictly increasing index map lie at or below its last entry

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ map $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ to $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ so that $f(\varphi(i)) < f(\varphi(j))$ whenever $i < j < k$. If $\varphi(k-1) = q$, then $f(\varphi(i)) \le f(q)$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: The last value is the largest along a strictly increasing selection

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ map $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$ to $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$ so that $f(\varphi(j)) < f(\varphi(i))$ whenever $i < j < k$. If $\varphi(k-1) = q$, then $f(q) \le f(\varphi(i))$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: The last value is the smallest along a strictly decreasing selection

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ and let $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ be strictly increasing with last value $\varphi(k-1) = q$. If $p$ is an index with $q < p$, then the map on $\{0, \dots, k\}$ obtained by appending $p$ to $\varphi$, which sends each $i < k$ to $\varphi(i)$ and sends $k$ to $p$, is strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Appending a later index keeps indices increasing

nodes.summary: For every map $\varphi : \{0, \dots, k-1\} \to \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and every $p \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$, the map obtained by appending $p$ to $\varphi$ takes the value $p$ at its last index $k$.
nodes.title: The last entry of an appended map

nodes.summary: Let $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ be an increasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$ (indices and values strictly increasing) with last index $\varphi(k-1) = q$. If $p \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ satisfies $q < p$ and $f(q) < f(p)$, then $f$ has an increasing subsequence of length $k + 1$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Extending an increasing subsequence

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, let $k \ge 1$, and let $\varphi$ be a decreasing subsequence of $f$ of length $k$, that is, indices $\varphi(0) < \dots < \varphi(k-1)$ with $f(\varphi(0)) > \dots > f(\varphi(k-1))$, whose last index is $\varphi(k-1) = q$. If $p$ is an index with $q < p$ and $f(p) < f(q)$, then $f$ has a decreasing subsequence of length $k + 1$ that ends at $p$.
nodes.title: Extending a decreasing subsequence

nodes.summary: Let $f : \{0, \dots, N-1\} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $q < p$ be positions with $f(q) < f(p)$. Then the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $q$ is strictly less than the length of the longest increasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Longest increasing subsequence lengths increase strictly along increasing pairs

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$, and let $q < p$ be indices with $f(p) < f(q)$. Then the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $q$ is strictly less than the length of the longest strictly decreasing subsequence of $f$ ending at $p$.
nodes.title: Longest decreasing subsequence lengths grow along a descent

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. If $f$ has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $k$, then for every $r \le k$ it has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $r$.
nodes.title: Increasing subsequences of every smaller length

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. If $f$ has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $k$, then for every $s \le k$ it has a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $s$.
nodes.title: Decreasing subsequences of every smaller length

nodes.summary: Let $r, s \ge 1$ be natural numbers, let $N = (r - 1)(s - 1) + 1$, and let $f$ be an injective real sequence indexed by $\{0, \dots, N-1\}$. Then $f$ has a strictly increasing subsequence of length $r$, that is, indices $i_1 < \dots < i_r$ with $f(i_1) < \dots < f(i_r)$, or a strictly decreasing subsequence of length $s$, that is, indices $j_1 < \dots < j_s$ with $f(j_1) > \dots > f(j_s)$.

Linear extensions of posets

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements. Its linear extensions are represented as rank functions: the set of linear extensions of $\alpha$ is the finite set of all maps $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that are bijective and monotone, meaning that $x \le y$ implies $\sigma(x) \le \sigma(y)$.
nodes.title: Linear extensions of a finite poset

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements. A map $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ belongs to the set of linear extensions of $\alpha$ if and only if $\sigma$ is bijective and monotone.
nodes.title: Membership in the linear extensions

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements, and fix a linear order on $\alpha$ extending its partial order (one exists by Szpilrajn's extension theorem; it is chosen once and for all). This is the order isomorphism from $\alpha$ with that linear order onto $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ with its usual order.
nodes.title: Ranking a Szpilrajn linear extension

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite poset with $n$ elements, and fix a linear order on $\alpha$ extending its partial order (one exists by Szpilrajn's extension theorem; it is chosen once and for all). The chosen linear extension of $\alpha$ is the rank function $\alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ sending each element to its position in that linear order, counted from $0$.
nodes.title: A chosen linear extension

nodes.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$ with $n$ elements, the chosen linear extension of $\alpha$, viewed as a rank function $\alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, is a bijection.
nodes.title: The chosen linear extension is bijective

nodes.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$ with $n$ elements, the chosen linear extension of $\alpha$, viewed as a rank function $\sigma : \alpha \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, is monotone: $x \le y$ implies $\sigma(x) \le \sigma(y)$.
nodes.title: The chosen linear extension is monotone

nodes.summary: Every finite poset has a linear extension.
nodes.title: Existence of linear extensions

nodes.summary: For every finite poset $\alpha$, the number of linear extensions of $\alpha$ is positive.
nodes.title: The number of linear extensions is positive

nodes.summary: For a finite subset $A$ of a partially ordered set $P$, the maximal elements of $A$ form the subset of those $x \in A$ such that every $y \in A$ with $x \le y$ equals $x$.
nodes.title: Maximal elements of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite subset of a partially ordered set $P$ and let $x \in P$. Then $x$ belongs to the set of maximal elements of $A$ if and only if $x \in A$ and every $y \in A$ with $x \le y$ equals $x$.
nodes.title: Membership in the maximal elements
Mirsky's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partially ordered set. A finite family $C$ of finite subsets of $\alpha$ is a finite antichain cover of $\alpha$ when every member of $C$ is an antichain and every element of $\alpha$ belongs to some member of $C$.
nodes.title: Finite antichain covers

nodes.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum chain size of $\alpha$ is the largest cardinality of a chain in $\alpha$, that is, of a set of pairwise comparable elements.
nodes.title: Maximum chain size

nodes.summary: For a finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the minimum antichain cover size of $\alpha$ is the smallest number of antichains in $\alpha$ whose union is all of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Minimum antichain cover size

nodes.summary: For every finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum chain size of $\alpha$ equals its minimum antichain cover size: the largest cardinality of a chain in $\alpha$ equals the smallest number of antichains whose union is $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Dual of Dilworth's theorem

nodes.summary: For every finite partially ordered set $\alpha$, the maximum chain size of $\alpha$ equals its minimum antichain cover size: the largest cardinality of a chain in $\alpha$ equals the smallest number of antichains whose union is $\alpha$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, an arc set on $n$ points is a finite set of ordered pairs $(i, j)$, called arcs, with $i, j \in \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Arc sets

nodes.summary: An arc set $P$ on $n$ points is noncrossing when every arc $(i, j) \in P$ has $i < j$ and any two distinct arcs $(i, j)$ and $(k, l)$ of $P$ satisfy $i \ne k$, $j \ne l$, and not $i < k < j < l$. So distinct arcs do not cross and share neither a left nor a right endpoint.
nodes.title: Noncrossing arc sets

nodes.summary: For an arc $a = (i, j)$ and an arc set $P$ on $n$ points, the toggle $\tau_{i,j}$ sends $P$ to $P \setminus \{a\}$ if $a \in P$; otherwise to $P \cup \{a\}$ if $P \cup \{a\}$ is a noncrossing arc set; and otherwise it leaves $P$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Toggle at an arc

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the toggle order on $n$ points is the list of all arcs $(i, i + d)$ with $d \ge 1$, $i \ge 0$ and $i + d \le n - 1$, ordered by length $d = 1, \dots, n - 1$ and, for each length, by increasing left endpoint $i$. In $1$-indexed form it is $(1,2), (2,3), \dots, (n-1,n), (1,3), \dots, (n-2,n), \dots, (1,n)$.
nodes.title: Toggle order

nodes.summary: The toggle composite $\sigma$ on $n$ points sends an arc set $P$ on $n$ points to the arc set obtained from $P$ by applying the toggles $\tau_{i,j}$ at the arcs $(i, j)$ of the toggle order on $n$ points one after another, in the order of that list.
nodes.title: Toggle composite

nodes.summary: The block count of an arc set $P$ on $n$ points is $n - |P|$, where the subtraction is truncated at $0$.
nodes.title: Block count

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma_n$ be the toggle composite on $n$ points and $\sigma_n^k$ its $k$-fold iterate. The claim states that for every $n \ge 1$, every noncrossing arc set $P$ on $n$ points and every $L \ge 1$ with $\sigma_n^L(P) = P$, twice the sum of the block counts of $P, \sigma_n(P), \dots, \sigma_n^{L-1}(P)$ equals $L(n + 1)$. That is, the number of blocks is homomesic under $\sigma_n$ with average $(n + 1)/2$.
nodes.title: Block-count homomesy claim for toggling noncrossing partitions

nodes.summary: The block-count homomesy claim holds: with $\sigma_n$ the toggle composite on $n$ points and $\sigma_n^k$ its $k$-fold iterate, for every $n \ge 1$, every noncrossing arc set $P$ on $n$ points and every $L \ge 1$ with $\sigma_n^L(P) = P$, twice the sum of the block counts of $P, \sigma_n(P), \dots, \sigma_n^{L-1}(P)$ equals $L(n + 1)$.
nodes.title: Block-count homomesy for toggling noncrossing partitions

nodes.summary: Face numbers and h-vectors of simplicial spheres and polytopes (Dehn–Sommerville, upper bound theorem), Cohen–Macaulay, partitionable and interval-decomposable complexes, simplicial homology, Ehrhart polynomials, h*-vectors and the integer decomposition property, lattice parallelograms, and hyperplane arrangements.
nodes.title: Polytopes, Ehrhart theory and simplicial complexes

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{Q}^d$ and a natural number $m$, the ordinary Ehrhart count is the number $|mP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$ of integer points in the dilate $mP = \{m x : x \in P\}$, where $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is viewed inside $\mathbb{Q}^d$; it is $0$ when $mP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Ordinary Ehrhart count
Clean lattice parallelograms

nodes.summary: The lattice points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ are the points $(a, b)$ with $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$; they form the image of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
nodes.title: The integer lattice in the plane

nodes.summary: For $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the parallelogram spanned by $u$ and $v$ is the set $\{s u + t v : 0 \le s \le 1,\ 0 \le t \le 1\}$.
nodes.title: Parallelogram spanned by two vectors

reading_title.source: The parallelogram $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $n$, the set $P_{a,n} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is the closed parallelogram spanned by $(1, 0)$ and $(a, n)$, that is, the set of points $s (1, 0) + t (a, n)$ with $0 \le s \le 1$ and $0 \le t \le 1$. For $n \ge 1$ it is the parallelogram with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$ and $(a + 1, n)$.
nodes.title: The parallelogram $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: For a $2 \times 2$ integer matrix $M$ with entries $m_{ij}$ and an integer vector $u = (u_1, u_2) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the map $T_{M,u} : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is $T_{M,u}(x, y) = (m_{11} x + m_{12} y + u_1, m_{21} x + m_{22} y + u_2)$, that is, $p \mapsto M p + u$. It is an affine unimodular map when $\det M = \pm 1$; the definition itself puts no condition on $\det M$.
nodes.title: Integer affine maps of the plane

nodes.summary: Two sets $P, Q \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ are unimodularly equivalent when some affine unimodular map sends $P$ onto $Q$: there are a $2 \times 2$ integer matrix $M$ with $\det M = 1$ or $\det M = -1$ and an integer vector $u \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $\{M x + u : x \in P\} = Q$.
nodes.title: Unimodularly equivalent sets

nodes.summary: Every subset $P$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is unimodularly equivalent to itself (take the identity matrix and the zero translation).
nodes.title: Unimodular equivalence is reflexive

nodes.summary: For points $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the parallelogram spanned by $u$ and $v$ is clean when $u$ and $v$ are lattice points and the lattice points on the boundary of the parallelogram are exactly $0$, $u$, $v$ and $u + v$.
nodes.title: Clean lattice parallelogram

reading_title.source: Interior lattice points of $P_{a,n}$ on a vertical line

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $n$, let $P_{a,n}$ be the parallelogram spanned by $(1, 0)$ and $(a, n)$, with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$. For an integer $k$, the set $S_k$ is the set of integers $y$ such that $(k, y)$ lies in the interior of $P_{a,n}$, that is, the $y$-coordinates of the lattice points in the interior of $P_{a,n}$ on the line $x = k$.
nodes.title: Interior lattice points of $P_{a,n}$ on a vertical line

nodes.summary: Let $u$ and $v$ be linearly independent vectors in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and let $P$ be the parallelogram they span. The map $p \mapsto u + v - p$ is a bijection from the set of points of the triangle $\operatorname{conv}\{0, u, v\}$ that lie in the interior of $P$ onto the set of points of the triangle $\operatorname{conv}\{u, v, u + v\}$ that lie in the interior of $P$.
nodes.title: Point reflection between the two triangles of a parallelogram

reading_title.source: Unimodular equivalences between the parallelograms $P_{b,n}$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $b$ and $n$ let $P_{b,n}$ be the parallelogram spanned by $(1, 0)$ and $(b, n)$, with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(b, n)$, $(b + 1, n)$. Let $n$, $a$ and $a'$ be natural numbers with $n > 1$, $1 \le a < n$, $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, $1 \le a' < n$ and $a a' \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$. Then $P_{a,n}$ is unimodularly equivalent to each of $P_{n-a,n}$, $P_{a',n}$ and $P_{n-a',n}$.
nodes.title: Unimodular equivalences between the parallelograms $P_{b,n}$

nodes.summary: Let $u$ and $v$ be lattice points spanning a clean lattice parallelogram $P$ whose area is an integer $n \ge 2$. Then there is an integer $a$ with $1 \le a < n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$ such that $P$ is unimodularly equivalent to the standard clean parallelogram $P_{a,n}$.
nodes.title: Clean parallelograms are unimodularly equivalent to standard ones

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le a < n$ with $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n} = \{s (1, 0) + t (a, n) : 0 \le s \le 1,\ 0 \le t \le 1\}$, and write $\langle x \rangle = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$ for the fractional part of a real number $x$. The lattice points in the interior of $P_{a,n}$ are exactly the points $\langle k(n - a)/n \rangle \, (1, 0) + (k/n) \, (a, n)$ for $k = 1, \dots, n - 1$.
nodes.title: Interior lattice points of a standard clean parallelogram

reading_title.source: The point reflection symmetry of $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a < n$ and $\gcd(a, n) = 1$, let $P_{a,n} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be the parallelogram with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(a, n)$, $(a + 1, n)$, and let $S : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be $S(x, y) = (a + 1 - x, n - y)$. Then $S(P_{a,n}) = P_{a,n}$, and $S$ is an isometry of $\mathbb{R}^2$ for the maximum distance $d((x, y), (x', y')) = \max(|x - x'|, |y - y'|)$.
nodes.title: The point reflection symmetry of $P_{a,n}$

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a finite simplicial $(d-1)$-sphere, that is, a finite geometric simplicial complex in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose underlying space is homeomorphic to the unit sphere of $\mathbb{R}^d$. nodes.summary: A 3-clause on $n$ variables is a pair $(S, p)$ of a three-element set $S$ of variables among the $n$ and a polarity $p$ assigning a Boolean value to every variable, with $p$ equal to false at every variable outside $S$. This normalization gives each clause in the usual sense (a three-element variable set with one of $2^3$ polarity patterns) exactly one representative.

When there are no such formulas, which happens exactly when $n < 3$ and $m > 0$, the quotient is taken to be $0$; this…

nodes.summary: A real number $\rho$ is an upper threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT when, for every real $r > \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses); equivalently, such a formula is unsatisfiable with probability tending to $1$.

nodes.summary: A real number $\rho$ is a lower threshold cutoff for random 3-SAT when, for every real $r < \rho$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses).

nodes.summary: There is a real number $c$ that is both a lower and an upper threshold cutoff: for every real $r < c$, the probability that a uniformly random formula with $\lfloor r n \rfloor$ clauses on $n$ variables is satisfiable tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$, and for every real $r > c$ this probability tends to $0$ (when $r n < 0$ the formula has no clauses).

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a finite set, $p \in [0, 1]$, and $\mathcal F$ a family of subsets of $X$. Then $\mathcal F$ is weakly $p$-small if there is a function $g$ from subsets of $X$ to the nonnegative reals such that $\sum_{S \subseteq T} g(S) \ge 1$ for every $T \in \mathcal F$ and $\sum_{S \subseteq X} g(S)\, p^{|S|} \le 1/2$.

For a family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $X$, $p_c(\mathcal F)$ is some $p \in [0, 1]$ with $\mu_p(\mathcal F) = 1/2$ if such a $p$ exists, and $0$ otherwise.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, the sequence $a_{p,q,n}$, $n \ge 0$, is defined as follows. If $q \ge 1$ and $n \ge p + q$, then $a_{p,q,n} = a_{p,q,n-q} + a_{p,q,n-p-q}$. Otherwise, if $p \ge q$, then $a_{p,q,n} = 0$ for $n < p - q$ and $a_{p,q,n} = 1$ for $n \ge p - q$; and if $p < q$, then $a_{p,q,n} = 1$ for $n < 2p$ and $a_{p,q,n} = 2$ for $n \ge 2p$.

Otherwise, if $q \le p$, then $a^{(m)}_{p,q,n}$ is $1$ for $n = p - q$ and $0$ for every other $n$, and if $p < q$, then $a^{(m)}_{p,q,n}$ is $1$ for $n = 2p$ and $0$ for every other $n$.

nodes.summary: For a natural number $\ell$, a finite set $A$ of natural numbers is *$\ell$-strong Schreier* if $\ell |A| + 1 \le a + \ell$ for every $a \in A$; equivalently, $A$ is empty or $\min A \ge \ell |A| - \ell + 1$.
nodes.title: Strong Schreier sets

nodes.summary: A finite set of natural numbers is *sparse* if the differences between consecutive elements in increasing order are non-decreasing.
nodes.title: Sparse sets

nodes.summary: A finite set of natural numbers is *strongly sparse* if the differences between consecutive elements in increasing order are strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Strongly sparse sets

reading_title.source: The partition number $p(u)$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $u$, $p(u)$ is the number of partitions of $u$, that is, of multisets of positive integers summing to $u$; in particular $p(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: The partition number $p(u)$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $\ell$, $|A^s_{n,\ell}|$ is the number of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ with $n \in A$ that are strongly sparse, meaning that the differences between consecutive elements of $A$ in increasing order are strictly increasing, and $\ell$-strong Schreier, meaning that every element of $A$ is at least $\ell|A| - \ell + 1$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $\ell$, $|B_{n,\ell}|$ is the number of sets $B \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ with $n \in B$ that are $\ell$-strong Schreier, that is, every element of $B$ is at least $\ell|B| - \ell + 1$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $\ell$ and $k$, $|E_{n,\ell,k}|$ is the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ parts, all of which are at least $\ell$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $\ell$, $k$ and $q$, $|E_{n,\ell,k,q}|$ is the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ parts, all at least $\ell$, whose largest part exceeds the second largest part (counted with multiplicity) by exactly $q$; such a partition has at least two parts, so the count is $0$ for $k < 2$.

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, and let $s = (s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ (the seed sequence) and $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be sequences in $M$. The seeded partial sums $t^s_{k,n}$, for $k, n \ge 0$, are defined by recursion on $k$: $t^s_{0,n} = a_n$ and $t^s_{k+1,n} = s_k + \sum_{i\lt n} t^s_{k,i}$.
nodes.title: Seeded partial sums

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and let $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$. For $k, m \ge 0$, the $k$-fold iterated partial sum $P^{(k)}(a)(m)$ is the seeded partial sum $t^s_{k,m}$ of $a$ for the zero seed sequence $s = 0$. Thus $P^{(0)}(a)(m) = a_m$ and $P^{(k+1)}(a)(m) = \sum_{i\lt m} P^{(k)}(a)(i)$.
nodes.title: Iterated partial sums

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, let $s = (s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be sequences in $M$, and write $t^s_{k,n}$ for the seeded partial sums of $a$ with seed sequence $s$. Then $t^s_{k+1,0} = s_k$ for every $k \ge 0$.

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid and let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$. For every $m \ge 0$, the $1$-fold iterated partial sum of $(a_n)$ at $m$ is the ordinary partial sum: $P^{(1)}((a_n)_{n \ge 0})(m) = \sum_{i\lt m} a_i$.
nodes.title: The first iterated partial sum

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, let $a = (a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a sequence in $M$, and write $P^{(k)}(a)(m)$ for its $k$-fold iterated partial sum at $m$. Then for all $k, m \ge 0$, $P^{(k+1)}(a)(m+1) = P^{(k+1)}(a)(m) + P^{(k)}(a)(m)$.

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$ with $k \ge 1$, $n > k$ and $n > 2$, the weighted Schreier counts satisfy $a_{k,n} = a_{k,n-1} + a_{k-1,n-2}$. At $k = 1$ the term $a_{0,n-2}$ is the same count with $\omega_0(E)$, the number of elements of $E$ different from $0$, equal to the number $|E|$ of all elements of $E$, since no element of a set $E \subseteq \{1, \dots, n-2\}$ equals $0$.

Then for all $k, n \ge 0$, $t^b_{k,n} - t^0_{k,n} = \sum_{i\lt k} \binom{n}{i} b_{k-1-i}$, where the binomial coefficients are read as elements of $R$.

Then for all $k, \ell \ge 0$, $P^{(k)}((F_{n+2})_{n \ge 0})(\ell) = P^{(k)}((F_n)_{n \ge 0})(\ell) + P^{(k)}((F_n)_{n \ge 0})(\ell + 1)$.

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, $H$ is a minor of $G$ when there is a finite sequence $H = G_0, G_1, \dots, G_k = G$ of finite graphs, with $k \ge 0$, such that for each $i < k$, $G_i$ arises from $G_{i+1}$ by one minor step: an isomorphism, the deletion of one vertex, the deletion of one edge, or the contraction of one edge.

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, if $H$ arises from $G$ by one minor step, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.
nodes.title: A single minor step gives a minor

nodes.summary: For finite graphs $H$ and $G$, if $H$ is isomorphic to $G$, then $H$ is a minor of $G$.

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a family of finite simple graphs that is closed under taking minors: whenever $G \in F$ and $H$ is a minor of $G$, also $H \in F$. Then any two finite graphs that are minors of each other are isomorphic, and there is a finite set $O$ of finite graphs such that a finite graph $G$ belongs to $F$ if and only if no graph in $O$ is a minor of $G$.

nodes.summary: For finite simple graphs $G$ and $H$, $G$ has $H$ as a minor if there is a family of vertex sets $B_w$ of $G$, one for each vertex $w$ of $H$, such that each $B_w$ is nonempty and induces a connected subgraph of $G$, the sets $B_u$ and $B_v$ are disjoint whenever $u \ne v$, and for every edge $uv$ of $H$ some vertex of $B_u$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex of $B_v$.

nodes.title: Straight-line planar embedding

nodes.summary: A finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is universal for $n$-vertex planar graphs if every straight-line planar simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding $p$ with $p(v) \in P$ for every vertex $v$.

nodes.title: Graph coloring
Part 1 of 2

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph and let $\Delta$ be its maximum degree: every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $\Delta$ and some vertex has degree exactly $\Delta$. If $G$ is not complete and is not isomorphic to a cycle graph on an odd number of vertices, then $G$ has a proper vertex coloring with $\Delta$ colors.
nodes.title: Brooks' theorem

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $g$ with $g \ge 3$, there is a finite simple graph $G$ that has a cycle, whose girth (the length of a shortest cycle) is at least $g$, and whose chromatic number is at least $k$.
nodes.title: Erdős's theorem on graphs of high girth and high chromatic number
Centered colorings

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proper vertex coloring of a simple graph $G$, let $s$ be a set of vertices of $G$ and let $v$ be a vertex of $G$. Then $v$ is a $\varphi$-center of $s$ if $v \in s$ and no other vertex of $s$ has the color $\varphi(v)$.
nodes.title: Center of a vertex set under a coloring

nodes.summary: A proper vertex coloring $\varphi$ of a simple graph $G$ is centered if, for every set $s$ of vertices of $G$ whose induced subgraph is connected, some vertex is a $\varphi$-center of $s$.
nodes.title: Centered coloring

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a proper vertex coloring of a simple graph $G$, let $s$ be a set of vertices of $G$ and let $v$ be a vertex of $G$. Then $v$ is a $\varphi$-center of $s$ if and only if $v \in s$ and there is exactly one vertex $u \in s$ with $\varphi(u) = \varphi(v)$.
nodes.title: Centers via unique existence

nodes.summary: For every proper vertex coloring $\varphi$ of a simple graph $G$ and every vertex $v$ of $G$, $v$ is a $\varphi$-center of $\{v\}$.
nodes.title: A vertex is a center of its singleton

nodes.summary: Every injective proper vertex coloring of a simple graph is centered: any vertex of a set whose induced subgraph is connected is a center of that set.
nodes.title: Injective colorings are centered

nodes.summary: For every simple graph $G$ with vertex set $V$, the proper vertex coloring of $G$ by $V$ that gives each vertex itself as its color is centered.
nodes.title: The identity coloring is centered
