Calculus of constructions

nodes.summary: The sorts are $\mathrm{Prop}$ and $\mathrm{Type}_i$ for every natural number $i$. In the calculus, $\mathrm{Prop}$ is impredicative and the $\mathrm{Type}_i$ form a predicative hierarchy.
nodes.title: Sorts of CCω

nodes.summary: A term is a variable $\#i$ with de Bruijn index $i \in \mathbb{N}$, a sort $s$ (either $\mathrm{Prop}$ or $\mathrm{Type}_i$ for some $i \in \mathbb{N}$), an application $f\,a$ of a term $f$ to a term $a$, an abstraction $\lambda (x : A).\, b$ with domain $A$ and body $b$, or a dependent product $\Pi (x : A).\, B$ with domain $A$ and codomain $B$.
nodes.title: Terms of the calculus of constructions

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $c$, shifting a term $t$ by $d$ above the cutoff $c$ adds $d$ to every variable index $i \ge c$ and leaves every index $i < c$ unchanged. The cutoff goes up by one under each binder, that is, in the body of a $\lambda$ and in the codomain of a $\Pi$ (not in the type annotation or the domain), and sorts are unchanged. Thus the free variables of $t$ with index at least $c$ are increased by…
nodes.title: Shifting de Bruijn indices

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and terms $u$ and $t$, the term $t[k := u]$ is defined by recursion on $t$. For a variable, $\#i[k := u]$ is $\#i$ if $i < k$, is $u$ with every free variable raised by $k$ if $i = k$, and is $\#(i - 1)$ if $i > k$. A sort is unchanged, $(f\,a)[k := u] = f[k := u]\,a[k := u]$, $(\lambda (x : A).\, b)[k := u] = \lambda (x : A[k := u]).\, b[k + 1 := u]$, and…
nodes.title: Substitution for a de Bruijn variable

nodes.summary: One-step beta reduction is the smallest relation on terms that contains every beta step $(\lambda (x : A).\, b)\, a \to b[a/x]$, where $b[a/x]$ substitutes $a$ for the bound variable $x$ in $b$, and that is closed under every term former: a step inside the function or the argument of an application, inside the type annotation or the body of a $\lambda$, or inside the domain or the codomain of a $\Pi$ is a step of…
nodes.title: One-step beta reduction

nodes.summary: Beta conversion is the equivalence closure of one-step beta reduction: every term is convertible to itself, and if $t$ is convertible to $u$ and $u$ reduces to $v$ in one step, or $v$ reduces to $u$ in one step, then $t$ is convertible to $v$.
nodes.title: Beta conversion

nodes.summary: The axioms say which sort has which sort as its type: $\mathrm{Prop}$ has type $\mathrm{Type}_0$, and $\mathrm{Type}_i$ has type $\mathrm{Type}_{i+1}$ for every natural number $i$. No other pair of sorts is related.
nodes.title: Sort axioms of CCω

nodes.summary: The product rules say in which sort $s_3$ a dependent product $\Pi (x : A).\, B$ lives when $A$ lives in the sort $s_1$ and $B$ lives in the sort $s_2$. There are exactly three rules: for every sort $s$, a product with domain in $s$ and codomain in $\mathrm{Prop}$ lives in $\mathrm{Prop}$ (the impredicativity of $\mathrm{Prop}$); for all natural numbers $i$ and $j$, a product with domain in $\mathrm{Type}_i$ and…
nodes.title: Product rules of CCω

nodes.summary: A context is a list of terms whose head is the most recent binding. Well-formedness of contexts is defined together with the typing judgement $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ as the least predicate such that the empty context is well formed, and if $\Gamma$ is well formed and $\Gamma \vdash A : s$ for some sort $s$, then the context obtained from $\Gamma$ by adding $A$ at the head is well formed.
nodes.title: Well-formed contexts

nodes.summary: A context $\Gamma$ is a list of terms whose head is the type of the most recent variable; write $\Gamma, A$ for $\Gamma$ extended by $A$ at the head. The judgement $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ ($t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$) is defined together with well-formedness of contexts as the least relation closed under the following rules.
nodes.title: Typing judgement of the calculus of constructions with universes

nodes.summary: The strongly normalizing terms are defined inductively: a term $t$ is strongly normalizing when every term to which $t$ reduces in one beta step is strongly normalizing. Equivalently, classically, there is no infinite chain of one-step beta reductions starting from $t$.
nodes.title: Strongly normalizing terms

nodes.summary: In the empty context, the polymorphic identity $\lambda (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \lambda (x : A).\, x$ has type $\Pi (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \Pi (x : A).\, A$.
nodes.title: Typing the polymorphic identity

nodes.summary: Write $\bot$ for $\Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$. In the empty context, the application of the polymorphic identity $\lambda (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \lambda (x : A).\, x$ to $\bot$ has type $\Pi (x : \bot).\, \bot$.
nodes.title: Typing the polymorphic identity applied to falsity

nodes.summary: The polymorphic identity $\lambda (A : \mathrm{Prop}).\, \lambda (x : A).\, x$ applied to $\bot = \Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$ reduces in one beta step to $\lambda (x : \bot).\, x$.
nodes.title: Beta step of the applied polymorphic identity

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context and $t$, $t'$, $A$ terms of the calculus of constructions with universes. If $t$ has type $A$ in $\Gamma$, that is $\Gamma \vdash t : A$, and $t$ reduces to $t'$ in one step of beta reduction (anywhere inside $t$), then $\Gamma \vdash t' : A$.
nodes.title: Subject reduction

nodes.summary: Every well-typed term is strongly normalizing: if $\Gamma \vdash t : A$ for some context $\Gamma$ and some term $A$, then $t$ is strongly normalizing.
nodes.title: Strong normalization of CCω

nodes.summary: No closed term has type $\Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$: there is no term $t$ with $\vdash t : \Pi (P : \mathrm{Prop}).\, P$ in the empty context.
nodes.title: Consistency of CCω
Hindley–Milner type inference

nodes.summary: An expression is a variable $x$, an application $e_1\,e_2$, an abstraction $\lambda x.\, e$, or a let-binding $\mathsf{let}\ x = e_1\ \mathsf{in}\ e_2$, where $e$, $e_1$, $e_2$ are expressions and variable names $x$ are strings.
nodes.title: Expressions of the λ-calculus with let

nodes.summary: A monotype over a set $B$ of base types is a term over the constants $B$: a type variable $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$, a base type $b \in B$, or an arrow $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ of two monotypes (a binary node).
nodes.title: Monotypes

nodes.summary: A type scheme over base types $B$ is a term over the constant set $B \oplus \mathbb{N}$: its variables $\alpha \in \mathbb{N}$ are the free type variables, a constant $\mathrm{inl}\, b$ is the base type $b \in B$, a constant $\mathrm{inr}\, i$ is the bound variable $i$, and a node of two schemes is an arrow.
nodes.title: Type schemes

nodes.summary: Every monotype $\tau$ is read as the type scheme with no bound variables of the same shape: a type variable stays the same type variable, a base type $b$ becomes the constant $\mathrm{inl}\, b$, and an arrow $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ becomes the arrow of the images of $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$.
nodes.title: Monotypes as type schemes

nodes.summary: Given maps $f$ and $g$ from natural numbers to monotypes over $B$, a type scheme $\sigma$ over $B$ evaluates to the monotype obtained by replacing each free type variable $x$ of $\sigma$ by $f(x)$ and each bound variable $i$ by $g(i)$, keeping every base type $b$ unchanged. An arrow $\sigma_1 \to \sigma_2$ evaluates to the arrow from the evaluation of $\sigma_1$ to the evaluation of $\sigma_2$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a type scheme

nodes.summary: Given monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, the instance of a scheme $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$ is the monotype obtained from $\sigma$ by replacing each bound variable $i$ by $t_i$, keeping its free type variables and base types unchanged.
nodes.title: Instantiation of a type scheme

nodes.summary: For a type substitution $s$ and a type scheme $\sigma$, $s\sigma$ is the scheme obtained from $\sigma$ by replacing every free type variable $x$ with the monotype $s(x)$, read as a scheme with no bound variables. The bound variables of $\sigma$ are left unchanged.
nodes.title: Applying a type substitution to a scheme

nodes.summary: For every type substitution $s$, every scheme $\sigma$ and all monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, instantiating each bound variable $i$ of $s(\sigma)$ by $s(t_i)$ gives $s$ applied to the instance of $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$. Here $s$ acts on a scheme through its free type variables only.
nodes.title: Instantiation commutes with substitution

nodes.summary: If two type substitutions $s$ and $t$ satisfy $s(x) = t(x)$ for every free type variable $x$ of a type scheme $\sigma$, then applying $s$ to $\sigma$ gives the same scheme as applying $t$.
nodes.title: Substitution into a scheme depends only on its free variables

nodes.summary: A typing context over base types $B$ is a finite list of bindings $(x, \sigma)$, each pairing a name $x$ (a string) with a type scheme $\sigma$ over $B$. A name may be bound more than once; the first binding of a name in the list is the visible one.
nodes.title: Typing context

nodes.summary: The lookup of a name $x$ in a typing context $\Gamma$ is the scheme of the first binding of $x$ in $\Gamma$ (the visible one), or nothing if $\Gamma$ has no binding of $x$.
nodes.title: Context lookup

nodes.summary: For a typing context $\Gamma$ and a name $x$, this is the set of free type variables of the scheme that $\Gamma$ binds to $x$ (the first binding of $x$ in $\Gamma$), or the empty set if $\Gamma$ does not bind $x$.
nodes.title: Free type variables of a name's visible scheme

nodes.summary: The free type variables of a typing context $\Gamma$ are the type variables occurring free in the visible scheme of some name bound in $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Free type variables of a context

nodes.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ give every name $x$ the same visible scheme (or both bind no scheme to $x$), then $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ have the same free type variables.
nodes.title: Free type variables depend only on visible bindings

nodes.summary: For a type substitution $s$ and a typing context $\Gamma$, $s\Gamma$ is the context obtained by applying $s$ to the scheme of every binding of $\Gamma$, keeping the names and their order.
nodes.title: Applying a type substitution to a context

nodes.summary: If two type substitutions $s$ and $t$ agree on every free type variable of a context $\Gamma$, then for every name $x$ the lookups of $x$ in $s(\Gamma)$ and in $t(\Gamma)$ are equal: both give no scheme, or both give the same scheme.
nodes.title: Substitutions agreeing on a context give the same lookups

nodes.summary: Given a typing context $\Gamma$ and a monotype $\tau$, the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma$ is the type scheme obtained from $\tau$ by turning each type variable $\alpha$ that is not free in $\Gamma$ into the bound variable with index $\alpha$, while type variables free in $\Gamma$ stay free.
nodes.title: Generalization of a monotype

nodes.summary: The syntax-directed Damas–Milner typing relation $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$ between a context $\Gamma$, an expression $e$ and a monotype $\tau$ is the least relation closed under the following rules, where $\Gamma, x : \sigma$ is $\Gamma$ extended by the binding $x : \sigma$ in front.
nodes.title: Hindley–Milner typing

nodes.summary: A scheme $\sigma'$ is more general than a scheme $\sigma$ when every instance of $\sigma$ is also an instance of $\sigma'$ and every free type variable of $\sigma'$ is a free type variable of $\sigma$.
nodes.title: More general type scheme

nodes.summary: A context $\Gamma'$ is more general than a context $\Gamma$ when the same names are visible in both and, for each such name $x$, the visible scheme of $x$ in $\Gamma'$ is more general than its visible scheme in $\Gamma$. Only lookups matter, so shadowed bindings play no role.
nodes.title: More general context

nodes.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ give the same lookup result for every name $x$ (the same visible scheme, or none in both), then $\Gamma'$ is more general than $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Contexts with the same lookups are related by generality

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ be typing contexts such that $\Gamma'$ is more general than $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a name, and let $\sigma'$ and $\sigma$ be type schemes such that $\sigma'$ is more general than $\sigma$. Then the context obtained by putting the binding $x : \sigma'$ in front of $\Gamma'$ is more general than the context obtained by putting the binding $x : \sigma$ in front of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Extending more general contexts by a binding

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma'$ and $\Gamma$ be typing contexts such that every free type variable of $\Gamma'$ is a free type variable of $\Gamma$, and let $\tau$ be a monotype. Then the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma'$ is more general than the generalization of $\tau$ with respect to $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Generalizing in a context with fewer free variables

nodes.summary: If $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$ and $\Gamma'$ is a context more general than $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma' \vdash e : \tau$.
nodes.title: Typing is preserved in more general contexts

nodes.summary: For a finite set $S$ of natural numbers, this is the number $\max S + 1$, where the maximum of the empty set is taken to be $0$. It is strictly greater than every element of $S$.
nodes.title: Strict upper bound of a finite set of naturals

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $\tau$ a monotype and $s$ a type substitution. Write $s\Gamma$ for the context obtained by applying $s$ to every scheme of $\Gamma$, and let $N$ be one more than the largest free type variable of $s\Gamma$, with $N = 1$ if $s\Gamma$ has none. Let $\rho$ be the substitution sending a type variable $y$ to $s(y)$ if $y$ is free in $\Gamma$, and to the type variable $y + N$ otherwise.…
nodes.title: Renaming step of the substitution lemma

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $e$ an expression and $\tau$ a monotype with $\Gamma \vdash e : \tau$. Then for every type substitution $s$, $s\Gamma \vdash e : s\tau$, where $s\Gamma$ applies $s$ to every scheme of $\Gamma$ and $s\tau$ applies $s$ to $\tau$.
nodes.title: Hindley–Milner typing is stable under type substitution

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $x$ a name and $\tau$ a monotype. Then $\Gamma \vdash x : \tau$ holds for the variable expression $x$ if and only if there are a type scheme $\sigma$ and monotypes $(t_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that the lookup of $x$ in $\Gamma$ gives $\sigma$ and $\tau$ is the instance of $\sigma$ at $(t_i)$.
nodes.title: Typing inversion for variables

nodes.summary: For all monotypes $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$, $\tau_1 \ne (\tau_1 \to \tau_2)$.
nodes.title: No monotype is an arrow out of itself

reading_title.source: The abstraction $\lambda f.\, f\, f$ has no type

nodes.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$, every variable name $f$ and every monotype $\tau$, the judgment $\Gamma \vdash \lambda f.\, f\, f : \tau$ does not hold.
nodes.title: The abstraction $\lambda f.\, f\, f$ has no type

nodes.summary: For every typing context $\Gamma$, all variable names $f$ and $x$, and every type variable $\alpha$, the expression $\mathtt{let}\ f = \lambda x.\, x\ \mathtt{in}\ f\, f$ has type $\alpha \to \alpha$ in $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: `let` generalizes

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $s$ a type substitution, $x$ a variable name, $e_1, e_2$ expressions and $\tau_1, \tau_2$ monotypes, and write $s\Gamma$ for the context obtained by applying $s$ to every type scheme of $\Gamma$. Suppose $e_1$ has type $\tau_1$ in $\Gamma$, and $e_2$ has type $\tau_2$ in the context obtained from $s\Gamma$ by binding $x$, in front, to the type scheme that results from applying $s$…
nodes.title: The let rule under a type substitution

nodes.summary: The bound-variable supremum of a type scheme $\sigma$ is one more than the largest index $i$ of a bound variable occurring in $\sigma$, and $0$ if no bound variable occurs in $\sigma$.
nodes.title: Bound-variable supremum of a type scheme

nodes.summary: Given a typing context $\Gamma$, an expression $e$ and a counter $n$, Algorithm W either fails or returns a substitution, a monotype and a new counter; type variables $\alpha_m$ with $m \ge n$ serve as fresh. Write $\tau_1 \to \tau_2$ for the arrow type, $s\Gamma$ for $\Gamma$ with the substitution $s$ applied to every type scheme, and $s(\tau)$ for $s$ applied to a monotype $\tau$. Algorithm W is defined by…
nodes.title: Algorithm W

nodes.summary: Type inference on an expression $e$ runs Algorithm W on $e$ in the empty context with fresh-variable counter $0$. If W succeeds with a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a counter $n'$, the inferred type of $e$ is $\tau$; if W fails, $e$ has no inferred type.
nodes.title: Type inference for closed expressions

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context, $e$ an expression and $n$ a natural number. If Algorithm W, run on $\Gamma$ and $e$ with fresh-variable counter $n$, succeeds and returns a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a counter $n'$, then $e$ has type $\tau$ in the context $s\Gamma$ obtained by applying $s$ to every type scheme of $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Soundness of Algorithm W

nodes.summary: For every expression $e$ and monotype $\tau$, if type inference for closed expressions returns $\tau$ on $e$, then $e$ has type $\tau$ in the empty context.
nodes.title: Soundness of type inference for closed expressions

nodes.summary: A term $t$ has all its variables below $n$ when every variable $z$ occurring in $t$ satisfies $z < n$.
nodes.title: Variables below a bound

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context and $n$ a natural number such that every free type variable of $\Gamma$ is less than $n$. If Algorithm W succeeds on $\Gamma$ and an expression $e$ with counter $n$, returning a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a new counter $n'$, then $n \le n'$, every type variable of $\tau$ is less than $n'$, and for every type variable $x < n$ every type variable of $s(x)$ is less than…
nodes.title: Freshness invariants of Algorithm W

nodes.summary: For a typing context $\Gamma$, a monotype $\tau$ and a type substitution $r$, the scheme obtained by applying $r$ to the free type variables of the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma$ is more general than the generalization of $r(\tau)$ in $r(\Gamma)$: every instance of the latter is an instance of the former, and every free type variable of the former is a free type variable of the latter.
nodes.title: Substituting into a generalization is more general

nodes.summary: If two typing contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ have the same free type variables, then for every monotype $\tau$ the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma$ equals the generalization of $\tau$ in $\Gamma'$.
nodes.title: Generalization depends only on the free variables of the context

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a typing context and $n$ a natural number such that every free type variable of $\Gamma$ is less than $n$. If, for some type substitution $u$, an expression $e$ has a monotype $\tau'$ in the context $u(\Gamma)$, then Algorithm W succeeds on $\Gamma$ and $e$ with counter $n$, returning a substitution $s$, a monotype $\tau$ and a new counter $n'$, and there is a type substitution $r$ such that…
nodes.title: Completeness of Algorithm W

nodes.summary: If an expression $e$ has a monotype $\tau'$ in the empty context, then type inference succeeds on $e$ and returns a monotype $\tau$ of which $\tau'$ is a substitution instance: $\tau' = r(\tau)$ for some type substitution $r$.
nodes.title: Completeness of type inference for closed expressions

nodes.summary: Type inference succeeds on an expression $e$ if and only if $e$ has some monotype in the empty context.
nodes.title: Type inference succeeds exactly on typable closed expressions

nodes.summary: The inferred type of a closed expression is one of its types, and every type of it is an instance of the inferred one.
nodes.title: Principal types
Simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: Given a type $B$ of base types, the simple types over $B$ are generated by two rules: every base type $b \in B$ is a simple type, and for simple types $A$ and $C$ the function type $A \Rightarrow C$ is a simple type.
nodes.title: Simple types

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ (a list of simple types) and a simple type $A$, the variables of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ are generated by two rules: the variable $0$ is a variable of type $A$ in the context $A :: \Gamma$ obtained by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$, and if $x$ is a variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, then for every simple type $B$ the successor of $x$ is a variable of type $A$ in $B :: \Gamma$.
nodes.title: Typed de Bruijn variables of the simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ range over simple types and $\Gamma$ over contexts (lists of simple types); write $A \Rightarrow B$ for the function type from $A$ to $B$ and $A :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$. The terms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ are generated by three rules: every variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ is a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$; if $f$ is a term of type…
nodes.title: Intrinsically typed terms of the simply typed lambda calculus

nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ (lists of simple types), a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ assigns to every simple type $A$ and every variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ a variable of type $A$ in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Renamings of simply typed contexts

nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ (lists of simple types), a substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ assigns to every simple type $A$ and every variable of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Simultaneous substitutions of simply typed contexts

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$, the identity renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ sends each variable to itself.
nodes.title: Identity renaming of a simply typed context

nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$, $\Delta$ and $\Xi$, a renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and a renaming $\sigma$ from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$, the composite of $\rho$ followed by $\sigma$ is the renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.
nodes.title: Composition of renamings of simply typed contexts

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and let $A$ be a simple type, and write $A :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $A$ to $\Gamma$. The lift of $\rho$ is the renaming from $A :: \Gamma$ to $A :: \Delta$ that sends the variable $0$ to $0$ and sends the successor of a variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the successor of $\rho(x)$.
nodes.title: Lifting a renaming under a binder

nodes.summary: For a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the renaming $t[\rho]$ of a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$ defined by recursion on $t$: $x[\rho] = \rho(x)$ for a variable $x$, $(f\,a)[\rho] = f[\rho]\,a[\rho]$ for an application, and $(\lambda s)[\rho] = \lambda (s[\rho^{\uparrow}])$ for an abstraction, where $\rho^{\uparrow}$ is the lift of…
nodes.title: Renaming a simply typed term

nodes.summary: For a term $t$ of type $A$ in a context $\Gamma$ and a simple type $B$, write $B :: \Gamma$ for the context obtained by prepending $B$ to $\Gamma$. The weakening of $t$ is the term of type $A$ in the context $B :: \Gamma$ obtained by renaming $t$ along the renaming that sends each variable of $\Gamma$ to its successor in $B :: \Gamma$.
nodes.title: Weakening a simply typed term

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$, the identity substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ sends each variable of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of that variable alone.
nodes.title: Identity substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)

nodes.summary: For contexts $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ and a type-preserving renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, the induced substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of the variable $\rho(x)$ alone.
nodes.title: Substitution induced by a renaming (simply typed lambda calculus)

nodes.summary: Write $A :: \Gamma$ for the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Given a substitution $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and a type $A$, its lift is the substitution from $A :: \Gamma$ to $A :: \Delta$ that sends the newest variable to the term consisting of the newest variable alone, and sends the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the weakening of the term…
nodes.title: Lifting a substitution under a binder (simply typed lambda calculus)

nodes.summary: Write $A :: \Gamma$ for the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Given a term $a$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the single-variable substitution for $a$ is the substitution from $A :: \Gamma$ to $\Gamma$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and sends the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term consisting of the variable $x$ alone.
nodes.title: Single-variable substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the result $t[\sigma]$ of applying $\sigma$ to a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the term of type $A$ in context $\Delta$ defined by recursion on $t$: $x[\sigma] = \sigma(x)$ for a variable $x$, $(f\,a)[\sigma] = f[\sigma]\,a[\sigma]$ for an application, and $(\lambda u)[\sigma] = \lambda\,(u[\sigma'])$ for an abstraction with…
nodes.title: Simultaneous substitution (simply typed lambda calculus)

Given a term $t$ of type $B$ in context $A :: \Gamma$ and a term $a$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the instantiation of $t$ with $a$ is the term of type $B$ in context $\Gamma$ obtained by applying to $t$ the single-variable substitution for $a$, which replaces the newest variable by $a$ and leaves the older variables…
nodes.title: Instantiating a binder body (simply typed lambda calculus)

nodes.summary: Given a term $a$ of type $A$ in a context $\Delta$ and a substitution $\sigma$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, the extension of $\sigma$ by $a$ is the substitution from the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$ to $\Delta$ that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Extension of a simply typed substitution

nodes.summary: For substitutions $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$ and $\tau$ from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$, the composite of $\sigma$ followed by $\tau$ is the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the term obtained by applying $\tau$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Composition of simply typed substitutions

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and $B$ a type. Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of type $B$ and then renaming by the lift of $\rho$ under that variable gives the same term as renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then weakening by a new newest variable of type $B$.
nodes.title: Renaming commutes with weakening for intrinsically typed STLC terms

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, $\rho$ a renaming from $\Delta$ to $\Xi$ and $t$ a term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Renaming by $\rho$ the result of applying $\sigma$ to $t$ gives the result of applying to $t$ the substitution that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(x)$ renamed by $\rho$.
nodes.title: Renaming after substitution in the simply typed calculus

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $\sigma$ a substitution from $\Delta$ to the typing context $\Xi$, and $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. Renaming $t$ by $\rho$ and then applying $\sigma$ gives the same term as applying to $t$ the substitution that sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\sigma(\rho(x))$.
nodes.title: Renaming then substituting an intrinsically typed STLC term

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and $B$ a type. Weakening $t$ by a new newest variable of type $B$ and then applying the lift of $\sigma$ under that variable gives the same term as applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then weakening by a new newest variable of type $B$.
nodes.title: Lifted substitution commutes with weakening for intrinsically typed STLC terms

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a substitution from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$, $\tau$ a substitution from $\Delta$ to the typing context $\Xi$, and $t$ a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. Applying $\sigma$ to $t$ and then applying $\tau$ gives the same term as applying to $t$ the composite substitution, which sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the result of applying $\tau$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Composition of substitutions for intrinsically typed STLC terms

nodes.summary: For every simultaneous substitution $\sigma$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the composite of $\sigma$ followed by the identity substitution on $\Delta$ sends $x$ to $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.title: Right identity law for composition of substitutions

nodes.summary: Given a substitution $\sigma$ from the typing context $\Gamma$ to the typing context $\Delta$ and a renaming $\rho$ from $\Delta$ to the typing context $\Xi$, the substitution from $\Gamma$ to $\Xi$ obtained by renaming images sends each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to the renaming of the term $\sigma(x)$ by $\rho$.

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in the typing context $\Gamma$ and $a$ a term of type $B$ in context $\Gamma$. nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, $b$ a term of type $B$ in the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$, and $a$ a term of type $A$ in $\Gamma$. Instantiating the newest variable of $b$ by $a$ gives the same term as applying to $b$ the substitution that sends the newest variable to $a$ and each older variable to itself, that is, the extension of the identity substitution on $\Gamma$ by $a$.
