nodes.summary: Let $q$ be a natural number. For $r, s, r', s' \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ (the challenges and answers of two transcripts), the extracted exponent is $(s - s')(r - r')^{-1} \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, where $u^{-1}$ is the inverse of $u$ in $\mathbb{Z}/q$ when $u$ is a unit (and, otherwise, a conventional element of $\mathbb{Z}/q$ depending on $u$). For $q$ prime and $r \ne r'$ it is $(s - s')/(r - r')$.
nodes.title: Schnorr knowledge extractor

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q$ a prime and $g, y \in G$ with $g^q = 1$ and $y^q = 1$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. Let $I \in G$ and $r, s, r', s' \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ with $r \ne r'$, and suppose both transcripts $(I, r, s)$ and $(I, r', s')$ are accepted, that is, $g^s (y^r)^{-1} = I$ and…
nodes.title: Special soundness

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g \in G$; for $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $g^a$ for $g^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For a secret key $x$, prover randomness $k$ and challenge $r$, all in $\mathbb{Z}/q$, the honest transcript is the element $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ of $G \times \mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$.
nodes.title: Honest Schnorr transcript

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g, y \in G$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For a challenge $r$ and an answer $s$ in $\mathbb{Z}/q$, the simulated transcript is the element $(g^s (y^r)^{-1}, r, s)$ of $G \times \mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$.
nodes.title: Simulated Schnorr transcript

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g \in G$; for $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $g^a$ for $g^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For a secret key $x \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, this is the law of the honest transcript $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ when $(k, r)$ is uniform on $\mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$.
nodes.title: Distribution of honest Schnorr transcripts

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g, y \in G$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. The simulator's distribution is the law of the simulated transcript $(g^s (y^r)^{-1}, r, s)$ when $(r, s)$ is uniform on $\mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$; it uses only $g$ and the public key $y$.
nodes.title: Schnorr simulator

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a commutative group, $q \ge 1$ and $g \in G$ with $g^q = 1$; for $h \in G$ and $a \in \mathbb{Z}/q$ write $h^a$ for $h^{\bar a}$, where $\bar a \in \{0, \dots, q - 1\}$ is the representative of $a$. For every secret key $x \in \mathbb{Z}/q$, with public key $y = g^x$, the honest transcript $(g^k, r, rx + k)$ with $(k, r)$ uniform on $\mathbb{Z}/q \times \mathbb{Z}/q$ has the same distribution as the…
nodes.title: Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge

nodes.summary: Relational algebra, functional dependencies, normal forms and lossless decomposition, and transaction concurrency control (conflict serializability, two-phase locking).
nodes.title: Databases
Conflict serializability

nodes.summary: The kind of access an operation makes to its data item is one of two values: a read or a write.
nodes.title: Read or write access

nodes.summary: For $n$ transactions, numbered $0, \dots, n - 1$, and data items of type $X$, an operation consists of a transaction $t \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, an occurrence identifier $k \in \mathbb{N}$, an access, which is a read or a write, and a data item $x \in X$: transaction $t$ reads or writes $x$, and $k$ makes repeated accesses of $t$ to an item distinct operations.
nodes.title: Operation of a schedule

nodes.summary: Two operations of a schedule conflict when they belong to different transactions, access the same data item, and at least one of the two accesses is a write.
nodes.title: Conflicting operations

nodes.summary: Two operations $a$ and $b$ are order-relevant when they belong to the same transaction or they conflict. These are the pairs whose relative order a conflict-equivalent schedule must keep.
nodes.title: Operations whose relative order matters

nodes.summary: A schedule $s'$ is conflict-equivalent to a schedule $s$ when $s'$ is a permutation of $s$ and, for any two operations $a$ and $b$ that belong to the same transaction or conflict, an occurrence of $a$ comes before an occurrence of $b$ in $s$ if and only if the same holds in $s'$.
nodes.title: Conflict equivalence

nodes.summary: For a schedule $s$ and transactions $i$ and $j$, transaction $i$ precedes transaction $j$ in $s$ when every operation of $i$ in $s$ occurs in $s$ before every operation of $j$ in $s$.
nodes.title: One transaction before another in a schedule

nodes.summary: A schedule $s$ is serial when, for any two distinct transactions $i$ and $j$, either every operation of $i$ in $s$ occurs before every operation of $j$ in $s$, or every operation of $j$ in $s$ occurs before every operation of $i$ in $s$.
nodes.title: Serial schedule

nodes.summary: A schedule $s$ is conflict-serializable when some serial schedule is conflict-equivalent to $s$.
nodes.title: Conflict-serializable schedule

nodes.summary: For a schedule $s$ and transactions $i$ and $j$, there is a precedence edge from $i$ to $j$ in $s$ when some operation of $i$ occurs in $s$ before some operation of $j$ in $s$ that conflicts with it.
nodes.title: Edge of the precedence graph

nodes.summary: The precedence (serialization) graph of a schedule $s$ of $n$ transactions is the directed adjacency graph whose vertices are the transactions $0, \dots, n - 1$, listed in increasing order, and whose adjacency list at a transaction $i$ lists, in increasing order, the transactions $j$ such that there is a precedence edge from $i$ to $j$ in $s$.
nodes.title: Precedence graph

nodes.summary: For a list $\sigma$ of transactions and a schedule $s$, the serialization of $s$ along $\sigma$ sorts the operations of $s$ by the position of the first occurrence of their transaction in $\sigma$, where a transaction that does not occur in $\sigma$ gets the length of $\sigma$ as its position. The sort is stable: operations with the same position keep their relative order in $s$.
nodes.title: Serialization of a schedule along a transaction order

nodes.summary: If a schedule $s$ in which no operation occurs twice is conflict-serializable, then the precedence graph of $s$ is acyclic.
nodes.title: A conflict-serializable schedule has an acyclic precedence graph

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a schedule and $L$ a list in which every transaction occurs. Then the schedule obtained from $s$ by stably sorting its operations by the first position of their transaction in $L$ is serial.
nodes.title: Serializing along a complete transaction order gives a serial schedule

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a schedule in which no operation occurs twice, and let $L$ be a topological order of the precedence graph of $s$. Then the schedule obtained from $s$ by stably sorting its operations by the first position of their transaction in $L$ is conflict-equivalent to $s$.
nodes.title: Serializing along a topological order preserves conflict equivalence

nodes.summary: A schedule without duplicate operations is conflict-serializable exactly when its precedence graph is acyclic.
nodes.title: The serializability theorem

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a schedule in which no operation occurs twice. If $r$ is a function from the transactions to the natural numbers with $r(i) < r(j)$ whenever the precedence graph of $s$ has an edge from $i$ to $j$, then $s$ is conflict-serializable.
nodes.title: A rank increasing along precedence edges gives conflict serializability
Functional dependencies

nodes.summary: A functional dependency $X \to Y$ over a type $A$ of attributes consists of two finite sets of attributes $X, Y \subseteq A$: the determining attributes $X$ (its left side) and the determined attributes $Y$ (its right side).
nodes.title: Functional dependency

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a type of attributes and $V$ a type of values. A functional dependency $X \to Y$ on $A$ holds in a relation $r$, a set of tuples $A \to V$, when any two tuples $t, u \in r$ that agree on every attribute of $X$ also agree on every attribute of $Y$.
nodes.title: A functional dependency holds in a relation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over attributes $A$, and let $r$ be a relation, given as a set of tuples $A \to V$ with values in a type $V$. Then $r$ satisfies $F$ when every dependency of $F$ holds in $r$.
nodes.title: A relation satisfies a set of dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a type of attributes. A finite set $F$ of functional dependencies on $A$ entails a functional dependency $f$ on $A$ when, for every type $V$ and every relation $r$ with values in $V$ (a set of tuples $A \to V$) that satisfies $F$, the dependency $f$ holds in $r$.
nodes.title: Entailment of functional dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a set $A$ of attributes. Derivability from $F$ is the least property of functional dependencies over $A$ such that, for all finite sets $X$, $Y$, $Z$ of attributes: every dependency of $F$ is derivable; $X \to Y$ is derivable whenever $Y \subseteq X$ (reflexivity); if $X \to Y$ is derivable, then so is $X \cup Z \to Y \cup Z$ (augmentation); and if $X \to Y$…
nodes.title: Derivability with Armstrong's axioms

nodes.summary: A derivable dependency holds in every relation satisfying `F`.
nodes.title: Armstrong's axioms are sound

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X$, $Y$, $Z$ finite sets of attributes with $Z \subseteq Y$. If $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to Z$.
nodes.title: Decomposition rule

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y, Z$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ and $X \to Z$ are derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to Y \cup Z$.
nodes.title: Union rule

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y, W, Z$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ and $Y \cup W \to Z$ are derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \cup W \to Z$.
nodes.title: Pseudotransitivity rule

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $X, Y$ finite sets of attributes. If $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, then so is $X \to X \cup Y$.
nodes.title: Adding the left side to the right side

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies and a finite set $Y$ of attributes, one closure round returns $Y$ together with the right side of every dependency of $F$ whose left side is contained in $Y$, that is, the set $Y \cup \bigcup \{R : (L \to R) \in F,\ L \subseteq Y\}$.
nodes.title: One round of the attribute-closure algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, $n$ a natural number and $Y$ a finite set of attributes. The loop returns $Y$ if $n = 0$ or if one closure round for $F$ leaves $Y$ unchanged; otherwise it returns the loop with $n - 1$ rounds started from the result of one closure round applied to $Y$. Thus it repeats closure rounds from $Y$ until nothing changes, for at most $n$ rounds.
nodes.title: Iterated closure rounds

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. The attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$ is computed by the closure algorithm: starting from $X$, repeat closure rounds (each adds the right side of every dependency of $F$ whose left side is already included) until nothing changes, for at most $|A|$ rounds.
nodes.title: Attribute closure

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. Applying one closure round for $F$ to the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$ returns $X^+$.
nodes.title: The attribute closure is a fixed point of a closure round

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes, $X$ a set of attributes and $X^+$ its attribute closure under $F$. For every dependency $Y \to Z$ in $F$ with $Y \subseteq X^+$, also $Z \subseteq X^+$.
nodes.title: The attribute closure is closed under the dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X \subseteq A$. The closure witness relation for $X$ is the relation with values in $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ whose tuples are the tuple that is $\mathrm{true}$ on every attribute and the tuple that is $\mathrm{true}$ exactly on the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$. These two tuples agree exactly on…
nodes.title: Closure witness relation

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. For every set $X \subseteq A$ of attributes, the closure witness relation for $X$ under $F$ satisfies $F$.
nodes.title: The closure witness satisfies the dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $X, Y \subseteq A$. Then $X \to Y$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms if and only if $Y \subseteq X^+$, where $X^+$ is the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$ computed by the closure algorithm.
nodes.title: The closure algorithm decides derivability

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes and $X$ a set of attributes. An attribute $a$ lies in the attribute closure $X^+$ of $X$ under $F$, as computed by the closure algorithm, if and only if the dependency $X \to \{a\}$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms.
nodes.title: The closure algorithm computes the attribute closure

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $f$ a functional dependency over $A$. If $f$ holds in every relation with values in $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ that has at most two tuples and satisfies every dependency of $F$, then $f$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms.
nodes.title: Completeness of Armstrong's axioms, two-tuple form

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite set of attributes, $F$ a finite set of functional dependencies over $A$ and $f$ a functional dependency over $A$. Then $f$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms if and only if $F$ entails $f$, that is, $f$ holds in every relation (with values in any type) that satisfies every dependency of $F$. In other words, Armstrong's axioms are sound and complete for functional dependencies.
nodes.title: Armstrong's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes $A$. A set of attributes $K$ is a superkey for $F$ when the dependency $K \to A$ is derivable from $F$ with Armstrong's axioms, that is, $K$ determines every attribute.
nodes.title: Superkey

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. A set $K \subseteq A$ of attributes is a candidate key for $F$ when $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and no proper subset of $K$ is a superkey for $F$.
nodes.title: Candidate key

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes. If $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and $K \subseteq K'$, then $K'$ is a superkey for $F$.
nodes.title: Supersets of superkeys are superkeys

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $K$ be a superkey for $F$. Let $V$ be a type of values. If a relation $r$, a set of tuples $A \to V$, satisfies $F$, then any two tuples $t, u \in r$ that agree on every attribute of $K$ are equal.
nodes.title: Tuples that agree on a superkey are equal

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. A set $K \subseteq A$ of attributes is a candidate key for $F$ if and only if $K$ is a superkey for $F$ and, for every $a \in K$, the set $K \setminus \{a\}$ is not a superkey for $F$.
nodes.title: Candidate keys are the superkeys minimal under single removals

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies over a finite set of attributes. Given a list $l$ of attributes and a set of attributes $K$, go through $l$ in order and, for each attribute $a$, remove $a$ from the current set whenever the attribute closure under $F$ of the current set without $a$ is the set of all attributes (that is, the set without $a$ is still a superkey); the result is the set reached at the…
nodes.title: Shrinking a key along a list

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $l$ be a list of attributes. The key-finding algorithm starts from the set $K = A$ of all attributes and goes through $l$ in order: for each listed attribute $a$, it replaces $K$ by $K \setminus \{a\}$ when the attribute closure of $K \setminus \{a\}$ under $F$ is all of $A$, and keeps $K$ otherwise. It returns the final…
nodes.title: Key-finding algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$, and let $l$ be a list in which every attribute of $A$ occurs. Then the output of the key-finding algorithm on $F$ and $l$, which starts from the set of all attributes and goes through $l$ in order, removing each listed attribute whenever what remains is still a superkey, is a candidate key for $F$.
nodes.title: The key-finding algorithm returns a candidate key

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies on a finite set of attributes $A$. Every superkey $K$ for $F$ has a subset $K' \subseteq K$ that is a candidate key for $F$.
nodes.title: Every superkey contains a candidate key
Relational algebra

nodes.summary: For a type $A$ of attributes and a type $D$ of values, a tuple is a partial assignment of values to attributes: a function that assigns to each attribute $a \in A$ either a value in $D$ or no value, in which case the tuple is undefined at $a$.
nodes.title: Tuple

nodes.summary: A tuple $t$ is over the schema $S$, a finite set of attributes, when $t$ is defined exactly on the attributes of $S$: for every attribute $a$, the value $t(a)$ is defined if and only if $a \in S$.
nodes.title: Tuple over a schema

nodes.summary: Two tuples $t$ and $u$ are compatible (joinable) when they agree on every attribute where both are defined: for every attribute $a$, either $t$ is undefined at $a$, or $u$ is undefined at $a$, or $t(a) = u(a)$.
nodes.title: Compatible tuples

nodes.summary: The merge of tuples $t$ and $u$ is the tuple whose value at each attribute $a$ is $t(a)$ if $t$ is defined at $a$, and $u(a)$ otherwise; it is undefined at $a$ when neither $t$ nor $u$ is.
nodes.title: Merge of two tuples

nodes.summary: For tuples $t$, $u$, $v$: $t$ and $u$ are compatible and the merge of $t$ and $u$ is compatible with $v$ if and only if $t$, $u$, $v$ are pairwise compatible, that is, $t$ and $u$, $t$ and $v$, and $u$ and $v$ are compatible.
nodes.title: Compatibility with a merge, grouped from the left

nodes.summary: For tuples $t$, $u$, $v$: $u$ and $v$ are compatible and $t$ is compatible with the merge of $u$ and $v$ if and only if $t$, $u$, $v$ are pairwise compatible, that is, $t$ and $u$, $t$ and $v$, and $u$ and $v$ are compatible.
nodes.title: Compatibility with a merge, grouped from the right

nodes.summary: For a finite set $T$ of attributes and a tuple $t$, the restriction $t|_T$ is the tuple that agrees with $t$ on every attribute in $T$ and is undefined on every attribute outside $T$.
nodes.title: Restriction of a tuple

nodes.summary: The selection conditions over attributes $A$ and values $D$ are generated by: the condition that always holds; the equality $a = c$ of an attribute $a$ with a constant $c \in D$; the equality $a = b$ of two attributes $a$ and $b$; the negation of a condition; and the conjunction of two conditions.
nodes.title: Selection conditions

nodes.summary: The truth value of a selection condition on a tuple $t$ is defined by recursion: the always-true condition holds; $a = c$ holds when $t$ is defined at $a$ with value $c$; $a = b$ holds when $t(a) = t(b)$ as possibly undefined values, so it also holds when $t$ is undefined at both $a$ and $b$; a negation holds when the negated condition fails; and a conjunction holds when both conditions hold.
nodes.title: Truth value of a selection condition

nodes.summary: The set of attributes mentioned by a selection condition, defined by recursion: it is empty for the always-true condition; for the comparison $a = d$ of an attribute $a$ with a constant $d$ it is $\{a\}$; for the comparison $a = b$ of attributes $a$ and $b$ it is $\{a, b\}$; for the negation $\neg \varphi$ of a condition $\varphi$ it is the set of attributes of $\varphi$; and for the conjunction…
nodes.title: Attributes of a selection condition

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a selection condition, $t$ a tuple and $T$ a finite set of attributes containing every attribute of $c$. Then $c$ has the same truth value on the restriction of $t$ to $T$ as on $t$.
nodes.title: Selection conditions depend only on their attributes

nodes.summary: A finite set $r$ of tuples is a relation over the schema $S$, a finite set of attributes, when every tuple $t \in r$ is over $S$, that is, $t$ is defined exactly on the attributes of $S$.
nodes.title: Relation over a schema

nodes.summary: For a selection condition $c$ and a finite set $r$ of tuples, the selection $\sigma_c(r)$ is the set of tuples $t \in r$ on which $c$ evaluates to true.
nodes.title: Selection

nodes.summary: Write $\sigma_c$ for selection by a selection condition $c$. For selection conditions $c$ and $c'$ and a finite set $r$ of tuples, $\sigma_c(\sigma_{c'}(r)) = \sigma_{c' \land c}(r)$: selecting by $c'$ and then by $c$ is the same as selecting once by the conjunction $c' \land c$.
nodes.title: Cascade of selections

nodes.summary: For all selection conditions $c$ and $c'$ and every finite set $r$ of tuples, selecting by $c'$ and then by $c$ gives the same result as selecting by $c$ and then by $c'$: $\sigma_c(\sigma_{c'}(r)) = \sigma_{c'}(\sigma_c(r))$.
nodes.title: Selections commute

nodes.summary: The natural join $r \bowtie s$ of finite sets of tuples $r$ and $s$ is the set of merges of $t$ and $u$ over all pairs of tuples $t \in r$ and $u \in s$ that are compatible, that is, agree on every attribute where both are defined. The merge of $t$ and $u$ takes the value of $t$ where $t$ is defined and the value of $u$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Natural join

nodes.summary: For a permutation $f$ of the attributes and a finite set $r$ of tuples, the renaming $\rho_f(r)$ is the finite set of the tuples $t \circ f^{-1}$ for $t \in r$: each tuple keeps its values, and its value at an attribute $a$ moves to the attribute $f(a)$.
nodes.title: Renaming of attributes

nodes.summary: For all finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, $r \bowtie s = s \bowtie r$, where $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Commutativity of the natural join

nodes.summary: For all finite sets $r$, $s$ and $w$ of tuples, $(r \bowtie s) \bowtie w = r \bowtie (s \bowtie w)$, where $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Associativity of the natural join

nodes.summary: If $r$ and $s$ are relations over the same schema $S$, that is, finite sets of tuples each over $S$, then their natural join is their intersection: $r \bowtie s = r \cap s$.
nodes.title: The natural join on a common schema is the intersection

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. Let $c$ be a selection condition and write $\sigma_c$ for selection by $c$. For finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, $\sigma_c(r \cup s) = \sigma_c(r) \cup \sigma_c(s)$.
nodes.title: Selection distributes over union

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. Let $c$ be a selection condition and write $\sigma_c$ for selection by $c$. For finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, $\sigma_c(r \setminus s) = \sigma_c(r) \setminus \sigma_c(s)$.
nodes.title: Selection distributes over difference

nodes.summary: For a finite set $T$ of attributes and a finite set $r$ of tuples, the projection $\pi_T(r)$ is the finite set of the restrictions to $T$ of the tuples of $r$: $\pi_T(r) = \{ t|_T : t \in r \}$.
nodes.title: Projection of a relation

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation over the schema $S$ and $s$ a relation over the schema $S'$, that is, finite sets of tuples each over $S$, respectively each over $S'$. A tuple $t$ belongs to the natural join $r \bowtie s$ if and only if $t$ is over $S \cup S'$, the restriction of $t$ to $S$ belongs to $r$, and the restriction of $t$ to $S'$ belongs to $s$.
nodes.title: Membership in a join

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation over a schema $S$, that is, a finite set of tuples each defined exactly on the attributes of $S$, and let $s$ be any finite set of tuples. If every attribute of the selection condition $c$ lies in $S$, then $\sigma_c(r \bowtie s) = \sigma_c(r) \bowtie s$, where $\sigma_c$ is selection by $c$ and $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Selection pushdown into the left operand of a join

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a relation over a schema $S'$, that is, a finite set of tuples each defined exactly on the attributes of $S'$, and let $r$ be any finite set of tuples. If every attribute of the selection condition $c$ lies in $S'$, then $\sigma_c(r \bowtie s) = r \bowtie \sigma_c(s)$, where $\sigma_c$ is selection by $c$ and $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Selection pushdown into the right operand of a join

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. For all finite sets of attributes $T$ and $T'$ and every finite set $r$ of tuples, $\pi_T(\pi_{T'}(r)) = \pi_{T \cap T'}(r)$, where $\pi_T$ is projection onto $T$.
nodes.title: Cascade of projections

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. For finite sets of attributes $T \subseteq T'$ and every finite set $r$ of tuples, $\pi_T(\pi_{T'}(r)) = \pi_T(r)$, where $\pi_T$ is projection onto $T$.
nodes.title: Cascade of projections onto a subset

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. Let $c$ be a selection condition, $T$ a finite set of attributes containing every attribute of $c$, and $r$ a finite set of tuples. Then $\sigma_c(\pi_T(r)) = \pi_T(\sigma_c(r))$, where $\sigma_c$ is selection by $c$ and $\pi_T$ is projection onto $T$.
nodes.title: Selection commutes with projection

nodes.summary: For every finite set $T$ of attributes and all finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, the projection onto $T$ of $r \cup s$ is the union of the projections onto $T$ of $r$ and of $s$: $\pi_T(r \cup s) = \pi_T(r) \cup \pi_T(s)$.
nodes.title: Projection distributes over union

nodes.summary: The relational algebra queries over base relations named by $N$, with attributes $A$ and values $D$, are generated by: the base relation named $n$ for each $n \in N$; the selection $\sigma_c(e)$ of a query $e$ by a selection condition $c$; the projection $\pi_T(e)$ of a query $e$ on a finite set of attributes $T$; the natural join of two queries; the union of two queries; the difference of two queries; and the…
nodes.title: Relational algebra queries

nodes.title: Schema of a query

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a set of relation names. A database schema assigns to each name $n \in N$ a finite set of attributes $\mathrm{sch}(n)$, and a database assigns to each name $n$ a finite set of tuples $\mathrm{db}(n)$. The database $\mathrm{db}$ conforms to the database schema $\mathrm{sch}$ when, for every name $n$, the set $\mathrm{db}(n)$ is a relation over $\mathrm{sch}(n)$.
nodes.title: Databases conforming to a schema

nodes.summary: A well-formed query evaluates, on every conforming database, to a relation over its inferred schema.

Two queries $e$ and $e'$ are equivalent with respect to $\mathrm{sch}$ when there is a finite set of attributes $S$ such that the inferred schemas of $e$ and of $e'$ with respect to $\mathrm{sch}$ are both $S$ (in particular both queries are well-formed), and $e$ and $e'$ evaluate to the same relation on every…

Let $e$ and $e'$ be well-formed queries with schemas $S$ and $S'$, and let $c$ be a selection condition all of whose attributes lie in $S$. Let $e$ be a well-formed query with schema $S$, and let $c$ and $c'$ be selection conditions all of whose attributes lie in $S$. Then the query $\sigma_c(\sigma_{c'}(e))$, the selection by $c$ of the selection of $e$ by $c'$, is equivalent to the query $\sigma_{c' \land c}(e)$, the selection of $e$ by the…

Then the query $\pi_T(\pi_{T'}(e))$, the projection onto $T$ of the projection of $e$ onto $T'$, is equivalent to the query $\pi_T(e)$, the projection of $e$ onto $T$: both are well-formed with the…

Lossless decomposition and normal forms

nodes.summary: If the dependency `R₁ ∩ R₂ → R₁` holds in a relation `r` over `R₁ ∪ R₂`, then `r` is the natural join of its projections onto `R₁` and `R₂`.
nodes.title: Heath's theorem

nodes.summary: A relation $r$ satisfies a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies on a set $S$ of attributes when every dependency $X \to Y$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$ that is derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms holds in $r$.
nodes.title: Satisfying a set of dependencies on a scheme

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be finite sets of attributes, and let $D$ be a type of values. The decomposition of $R_1 \cup R_2$ into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$ when every relation $r$ over $R_1 \cup R_2$ with values in $D$ that satisfies $F$ on $R_1 \cup R_2$ (every dependency $X \to Y$ with $X, Y \subseteq R_1 \cup R_2$ that is derivable from…
nodes.title: Lossless decomposition into two schemes

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and let $R_1$, $R_2$ be sets of attributes. If $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1$ or $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2$ is derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms, then for every value type $D$ the decomposition of $R_1 \cup R_2$ into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$.
nodes.title: Lossless binary decompositions from derivable dependencies

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be schemes whose union is the set of all attributes, and let $D$ be a value type containing at least two distinct elements. If the decomposition of $R_1 \cup R_2$ into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$, then $F$ derives $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1$ or $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2$.
nodes.title: Converse of the lossless-join test for two schemes

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies, let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be sets of attributes whose union is the set of all attributes, and suppose that the value type $D$ has two distinct elements. Then the decomposition into $R_1$ and $R_2$ is lossless for $F$ with values in $D$ if and only if $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_1$ or $R_1 \cap R_2 \to R_2$ is derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms.
nodes.title: Lossless binary decompositions

nodes.summary: The relation containing only the empty tuple, the unit of the natural join.
nodes.title: Unit relation of the natural join

nodes.summary: For a relation $r$ (a finite set of tuples) and a list of schemes $S_1, \dots, S_n$, this is the natural join of the projections $\pi_{S_1} r, \dots, \pi_{S_n} r$, computed as $\pi_{S_1} r \bowtie (\pi_{S_2} r \bowtie (\cdots \bowtie (\pi_{S_n} r \bowtie U)))$, where $U$ is the relation containing only the empty tuple; for the empty list it is $U$.
nodes.title: Join of the projections of a relation

nodes.summary: For a list $S_1, \dots, S_n$ of schemes (finite sets of attributes), this is the union $S_1 \cup \dots \cup S_n$; for the empty list it is the empty set.
nodes.title: Union of a list of schemes

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation over a schema $R$ and let $S_1, \dots, S_n$ be a list of schemes, each contained in $R$. A tuple $t$ belongs to the natural join of the projections $\pi_{S_1} r, \dots, \pi_{S_n} r$ if and only if $t$ is a tuple over $S_1 \cup \dots \cup S_n$ and, for every $i$, the restriction of $t$ to $S_i$ belongs to $\pi_{S_i} r$.
nodes.title: Membership in a join of projections

nodes.summary: A scheme $S$ is in Boyce–Codd normal form for a set $F$ of functional dependencies when, for every dependency $X \to Y$ derivable from $F$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$, either $Y \subseteq X$ or $F$ derives $X \to S$ (that is, $X$ is a superkey of $S$).
nodes.title: Boyce–Codd normal form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies and $S$ a scheme, and write $X^+$ for the attribute closure of a set $X$ of attributes under $F$. A set $X \subseteq S$ violates BCNF in $S$ when $S \not\subseteq X^+$ and $X^+ \cap S \not\subseteq X$, that is, when the closure $X^+ \cap S$ of $X$ within $S$ is neither $X$ nor $S$.
nodes.title: BCNF violations

nodes.summary: Given a list $l$ of attributes and a set $S$ of attributes, the candidate violations of BCNF in $S$ are all subsets of the set of attributes that occur in $l$ and lie in $S$, listed once each. Duplicates in $l$ are removed first, so there are $2^k$ candidates when $k$ distinct attributes of $l$ lie in $S$.
nodes.title: Candidate BCNF violations

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, $l$ a list of attributes, $n$ a natural number and $S$ a scheme. For $n = 0$ the result is the list $[S]$. For $n > 0$, the candidate violations of BCNF in $S$ built from $l$ are searched in order for the first $X$ that violates BCNF in $S$ for $F$. If there is none, the result is $[S]$. Otherwise, with $X^+$ the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$, the result is the…
nodes.title: BCNF decomposition with bounded depth

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, $l$ a list of attributes and $S$ a scheme. The BCNF decomposition of $S$ for $F$ and $l$ is the BCNF decomposition with bounded depth run on $S$ with depth bound $|S|$. At each step, if some candidate violation of BCNF in the current scheme $T$ built from $l$ violates BCNF in $T$ for $F$, the first such $X$ is used: with $X^+$ the attribute closure of $X$ under $F$, $T$…
nodes.title: BCNF decomposition

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies, $l$ a list of attributes and $S$ a set of attributes, and let $r$ be a relation over $S$ that satisfies every dependency $X \to Y$ derivable from $F$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$. Then $r$ is the natural join of its projections onto the schemes of the BCNF decomposition of $S$ for $F$ and $l$.
nodes.title: The BCNF decomposition is lossless

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a set of functional dependencies and $l$ a list containing every attribute. Then for every scheme $S$, every scheme in the BCNF decomposition of $S$ for $F$ and $l$ is in Boyce–Codd normal form for $F$.
nodes.title: The BCNF decomposition produces BCNF schemes

nodes.summary: Two sets $F$ and $G$ of functional dependencies are equivalent when $F$ derives every dependency of $G$ and $G$ derives every dependency of $F$.
nodes.title: Equivalent sets of functional dependencies

nodes.summary: For a finite set $F$ of functional dependencies and a set $S$ of attributes, this is the finite set of all dependencies $X \to Y$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$ that are derivable from $F$ by Armstrong's axioms, that is, the projection onto $S$ of the closure $F^+$ of $F$.
nodes.title: Projection of the dependency closure onto a scheme

nodes.summary: A list $l$ of schemes is dependency-preserving for a set $F$ of functional dependencies when every dependency of $F$ is derivable from the union, over the schemes $S$ of $l$, of the sets of dependencies $X \to Y$ derivable from $F$ with $X, Y \subseteq S$.
nodes.title: Dependency-preserving decompositions

nodes.summary: Given a list $G$ of functional dependencies and a set of attributes $K$, the synthesized decomposition is the list of schemes consisting of $K$ followed by, for each dependency $X \to Y$ of $G$ in order, the scheme $X \cup Y$.
nodes.title: Synthesis

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite set of functional dependencies and $G$ a list of functional dependencies equivalent to $F$ (each derives every dependency of the other). Then for every set of attributes $K$, the decomposition synthesized from $G$ and $K$, with one scheme $X \cup Y$ for each dependency $X \to Y$ of $G$ together with the scheme $K$, is dependency-preserving for $F$.
nodes.title: Synthesis is dependency-preserving

nodes.summary: For a cover `G` of `F` and a superkey `K` of all attributes, every relation over all attributes satisfying `F` is the join of its projections onto the synthesized schemes.
nodes.title: Synthesis is lossless
Two-phase locking

nodes.summary: A lock is held in one of two modes: shared (a read lock) or exclusive (a write lock).
nodes.title: Lock mode

nodes.summary: A lock mode $m'$ covers a lock mode $m$ when a lock in mode $m'$ permits what a lock in mode $m$ permits: an exclusive lock covers both modes, and a shared lock covers only the shared mode.
nodes.title: Lock mode coverage

nodes.summary: The lock mode an access requires: shared for a read, exclusive for a write.
nodes.title: Lock mode required by an access

nodes.summary: For $n$ transactions, numbered $0, \dots, n-1$, and a type $X$ of data items, an action of a locked schedule is one of three kinds: a read or write operation; a lock request, in which a transaction $t$ acquires a lock on an item $x \in X$ in a lock mode $m$ (shared or exclusive); or a release, in which a transaction $t$ releases its lock on an item $x \in X$.
nodes.title: Action of a locked schedule

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$, the schedule of reads and writes of $s$: its reads and writes in order, with the lock requests and releases erased.
nodes.title: Reads and writes of a locked schedule

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a locked schedule, $t$ a transaction, $x$ a data item, $m$ a lock mode and $p$ a natural number. Transaction $t$ holds a lock on $x$ covering mode $m$ just before position $p$ of $s$ when there is a position $q < p$ at which $s$ has a lock request by $t$ on $x$ in some mode $m'$ that covers $m$, and for no position $r$ with $q < r < p$ is the action of $s$ at $r$ a release of $x$ by $t$.
nodes.title: Holding a lock

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is covered by locks when every read or write is protected by a lock of its transaction: whenever $s$ has at position $p$ a read or write $o$ by transaction $t$ on item $x$, just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds a lock on $x$ (acquired at an earlier position and not released since) whose mode covers the mode $o$ requires, namely shared for a read and exclusive for a write; an exclusive…
nodes.title: Schedules covered by locks

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ releases its locks when every lock request is followed by a matching release: whenever $s$ has at position $q$ a lock request (in either mode) by transaction $t$ on item $x$, there is a position $r > q$ at which $s$ has a release by $t$ of $x$.
nodes.title: Schedules that release every lock

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ (a list of reads, writes, lock requests and lock releases of transactions) is well formed when its accesses are covered by locks and it releases its locks: every read or write in $s$ is preceded by a lock request of its own transaction on its item, in a mode covering the access (shared or exclusive for a read, exclusive for a write), with no release of that item by that transaction in between;…
nodes.title: Well-formed locked schedules

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is legal just before position $p$ when, for every data item $x$, all distinct transactions $t \ne t'$ and all lock modes $m$, $m'$: if $t$ holds a lock on $x$ covering $m$ and $t'$ holds a lock on $x$ covering $m'$ just before position $p$ of $s$, then $m$ and $m'$ are both the shared mode. In words, two transactions do not both hold locks on the same item unless both locks are shared.
nodes.title: Lock compatibility at a point

nodes.summary: The list of data items locked in a locked schedule $s$: for each lock request of $s$, in order, the item it locks, so an item appears once for each lock request on it.
nodes.title: Locked items

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ of length $\ell$ is legal when it satisfies lock compatibility at every point $p \le \ell$: just before position $p$, no two distinct transactions both hold locks on the same item unless both locks are shared.
nodes.title: Legal locked schedule

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is two-phase when every lock request of a transaction precedes every release of that transaction: whenever $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ and at position $q$ a lock request by $t$ (on any items, in any mode), then $q < p$.
nodes.title: Two-phase schedules

nodes.summary: A locked schedule $s$ is strict two-phase when it is two-phase and every transaction releases its exclusive locks only after its last read or write: whenever $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ of item $x$ and just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds an exclusive lock on $x$, every read or write of $t$ in $s$ occurs at a position before $p$.
nodes.title: Strict two-phase schedules

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and a position $p$: if $s$ has at position $p$ a read or write $o$ by transaction $t$ on item $x$, then just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds a lock on $x$ whose mode covers the mode $o$ requires (shared for a read, exclusive for a write; an exclusive lock covers both modes). If position $p$ holds a lock request or a release, or lies beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds…
nodes.title: Lock coverage at a position

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and a position $q$: if $s$ has at position $q$ a lock request (in either mode) by transaction $t$ on item $x$, then there is a position $r$ with $q < r$ and $r$ less than the length of $s$ at which $s$ has a release by $t$ of $x$. If position $q$ holds a read, a write or a release, or lies beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds trivially.
nodes.title: Release of the lock requested at a position

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and positions $p$ and $q$: if $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ and at position $q$ a lock request by the same transaction $t$, then $q < p$. For every other pair of positions, including positions beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds trivially.
nodes.title: Two-phase condition at a pair of positions

nodes.summary: For a locked schedule $s$ and positions $p$ and $q$: if $s$ has at position $p$ a release by transaction $t$ of item $x$, just before position $p$ transaction $t$ holds an exclusive lock on $x$, and $s$ has at position $q$ a read or write by $t$, then $q < p$. For every other pair of positions, including positions beyond the end of $s$, the condition holds trivially.
nodes.title: Strictness at a pair of positions

nodes.summary: For a transaction $t$, this Boolean test on the actions of a locked schedule returns true exactly when the action is a release by $t$ of its lock on some item.
nodes.title: Release test

nodes.summary: If the reads and writes of a locked schedule are distinct, are covered by locks, and the schedule is legal and two-phase, then its reads and writes form a conflict-serializable schedule.
nodes.title: The two-phase locking theorem

nodes.summary: If the reads and writes of a locked schedule are distinct, are covered by locks, and the schedule is legal and strict two-phase, then its reads and writes form a conflict-serializable schedule.
nodes.title: Strict two-phase locking theorem

nodes.title: Quantum algorithms
Grover's algorithm

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ (the search space), a real amplitude vector indexed by $\alpha$ is a function $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, assigning a real amplitude to each point of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Real amplitude vectors

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ and a finite set $M \subseteq \alpha$ of marked elements, the phase oracle sends a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on $\alpha$ to the amplitude vector whose value at $x$ is $-\psi(x)$ if $x \in M$ and $\psi(x)$ if $x \notin M$; that is, it negates exactly the amplitudes at the marked elements.
nodes.title: Phase oracle

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$ and a real amplitude vector $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the squared norm of $\psi$ is its squared Euclidean norm $\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi(x)^2$.
nodes.title: Squared norm of an amplitude vector

nodes.summary: For a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on a type $\alpha$ and a finite set $M \subseteq \alpha$ of marked elements, the marked probability is $\sum_{x \in M} \psi(x)^2$. When $\alpha$ is finite and $\psi$ has squared norm $1$, this is the probability of observing a marked outcome.
nodes.title: Probability of the marked outcomes

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$, the uniform amplitude vector on $\alpha$ is the real amplitude vector whose value at every point is $1/\sqrt{|\alpha|}$, where $|\alpha|$ is the number of elements of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Uniform amplitude vector

nodes.summary: For every nonempty finite type $\alpha$, the uniform amplitude vector on $\alpha$ has squared Euclidean norm $1$.
nodes.title: The uniform amplitude vector is normalized

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$ and a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on $\alpha$, the mean amplitude of $\psi$ is $\bigl(\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi(x)\bigr) / |\alpha|$, the arithmetic mean of its amplitudes. When $\alpha$ is empty it is $0$.
nodes.title: Mean amplitude

nodes.summary: For a finite type $\alpha$, the diffusion operator sends a real amplitude vector $\psi$ on $\alpha$ to the amplitude vector $x \mapsto 2\bar\psi - \psi(x)$, where $\bar\psi$ is the arithmetic mean of the amplitudes of $\psi$.
nodes.title: Inversion about the mean

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a set of marked elements. Write $O_M$ for the phase oracle, which negates the amplitudes at the points of $M$, and $D$ for inversion about the mean, which sends an amplitude vector $\varphi$ on $\alpha$ to $x \mapsto 2\bar\varphi - \varphi(x)$, where $\bar\varphi$ is the arithmetic mean of the amplitudes of $\varphi$. One Grover step sends a real amplitude…
nodes.title: Grover step

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a search space $\alpha$, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. The symmetric amplitude vector with marked amplitude $a$ and unmarked amplitude $b$ is the real amplitude vector on $\alpha$ whose value is $a$ at every element of $M$ and $b$ at every element outside $M$.
nodes.title: Symmetric amplitude vector

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, let $M^c$ be the set of unmarked elements, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. The oracle mean is $(|M^c|\, b - |M|\, a) / N$.
nodes.title: Mean amplitude after the phase oracle

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, let $M^c$ be the set of unmarked elements, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. With $\mu = (|M^c|\, b - |M|\, a) / N$, the next marked amplitude is $2\mu + a$.
nodes.title: Marked amplitude after a Grover step

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, let $M^c$ be the set of unmarked elements, and let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$. With $\mu = (|M^c|\, b - |M|\, a) / N$, the next unmarked amplitude is $2\mu - b$.
nodes.title: Unmarked amplitude after a Grover step

nodes.summary: For a finite search space $\alpha$ and a marked set $M \subseteq \alpha$, the Grover angle of $M$ is $\theta = \arcsin \sqrt{|M| / |\alpha|}$, where the quotient $|M| / |\alpha|$ is taken to be $0$ when $\alpha$ is empty.
nodes.title: Grover angle

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set with complement $M^c$. For a real number $\varphi$, this is the real amplitude vector on $\alpha$ whose value is $\sin\varphi / \sqrt{|M|}$ at every point of $M$ and $\cos\varphi / \sqrt{|M^c|}$ at every point of $M^c$.
nodes.title: Symmetric Grover state at a given angle

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a real amplitude vector $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$, the $k$-th Grover iterate of $\psi$ is the vector obtained by applying the Grover step for $M$ to $\psi$ $k$ times; the $0$-th iterate is $\psi$ itself.
nodes.title: Grover iterate

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set. For every real amplitude vector $\psi : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\psi_k$ be the vector obtained from $\psi$ by applying the Grover step for $M$ $k$ times. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi_k(x)^2 = \sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi(x)^2$.
nodes.title: Grover iteration preserves the squared norm

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a nonempty finite search space, $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set, and $u$ the uniform amplitude vector, given by $u(x) = 1/\sqrt{|\alpha|}$ for every $x \in \alpha$. For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\psi_k$ be the vector obtained from $u$ by applying the Grover step for $M$ $k$ times. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha} \psi_k(x)^2 = 1$.
nodes.title: Grover iterates of the uniform state are unit vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space, $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set and $\theta$ the Grover angle of $M$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the Grover phase of $M$ after $k$ iterations is the real number $(2k + 1)\theta$.
nodes.title: Grover phase

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite search space and $M \subseteq \alpha$ a marked set such that both $M$ and its complement are nonempty, and let $\theta = \arcsin \sqrt{|M| / |\alpha|}$ be the Grover angle of $M$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\psi_k$ be the vector obtained by applying the Grover step for $M$ $k$ times to the uniform amplitude vector, whose value is $1/\sqrt{|\alpha|}$ at every point. Then the marked…
nodes.title: Exact success probability of Grover search

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$, and let $\theta = \arcsin \sqrt{|M| / N}$ be its Grover angle. The standard iteration count is $\lfloor \pi / (4\theta) \rfloor$, the largest natural number at most $\pi / (4\theta)$; it is $0$ when $\theta = 0$, that is, when no element is marked.
nodes.title: Standard Grover iteration count

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a nonempty set of marked elements of a finite search space of size $N$ with $4|M| = N$. Starting from the uniform amplitude vector, one Grover iteration produces an amplitude vector whose marked probability is $1$.
nodes.title: One Grover iteration suffices when a quarter is marked
Shor's reduction of factoring to order finding

nodes.summary: Let $N$, $a$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $N > 1$ and $a \ge 1$. Suppose $a^r \equiv 1 \pmod{N}$, $r$ is even, $a^{r/2} \not\equiv 1 \pmod{N}$ and $a^{r/2} \not\equiv -1 \pmod{N}$. Then $d = \gcd(a^{r/2} - 1, N)$, the value computed by the classical post-processing, is a nontrivial factor of $N$: $d$ divides $N$ and $1 < d < N$.
nodes.title: Shor's order-to-factor reduction

nodes.summary: Let $N$, $a$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $N > 1$ and $a \ge 1$. If $a^r \equiv 1 \pmod{N}$, $r$ is even, $a^{r/2} \not\equiv 1 \pmod{N}$ and $a^{r/2} \not\equiv -1 \pmod{N}$, then $N$ has a nontrivial factor: there is a natural number $d$ with $d \mid N$ and $1 < d < N$.
nodes.title: Shor's order-to-factor reduction, existential form

Alternating bit protocol

nodes.summary: The channel names of the alternating-bit protocol are $\mathit{acc}$ (accept a message from the user), $\mathit{del}$ (deliver a message to the user), and, for each bit $b$, the internal names $\mathit{send}_b$ (sender to data channel), $\mathit{recv}_b$ (data channel to receiver), $\mathit{reply}_b$ (receiver to acknowledgement channel) and $\mathit{ack}_b$ (acknowledgement channel to sender).
nodes.title: Alternating-bit channel names

nodes.summary: For each bit $b$, the sender has three states: $\mathrm{accept}(b)$, ready to accept a message to be sent with bit $b$; $\mathrm{transmit}(b)$, about to transmit a frame tagged with bit $b$; and $\mathrm{await}(b)$, waiting for the acknowledgement of bit $b$.
