nodes.summary: The reconstruction `(W H)_fn = ∑_k w_fk h_kn`.
nodes.title: Reconstruction matrix in nonnegative matrix factorization

nodes.summary: The data-fit term `D_1(V | W H) = ∑_{f,n} d(v_fn | (W H)_fn)`.
nodes.title: Data-fit term of the ARD-NMF objective

nodes.summary: The `H`-dependent part `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑_{k,n} h_kn / λ_k` of the `ℓ₁`-ARD objective (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 20, `β = 1`).
nodes.title: H-dependent part of the ARD-NMF objective

nodes.summary: The `ℓ₁`-ARD multiplicative update of `H` for `β = 1` (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 32, Algorithm 2): `h_kn ← h_kn (∑_f w_fk v_fn / (W H)_fn) / (∑_f w_fk + φ / λ_k)`.
nodes.title: ARD multiplicative update of H

nodes.summary: The `H` update is monotone (Tan–Févotte 2013, §IV-B, `β = 1`): it does not increase `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑ h_kn / λ_k`, for `φ > 0`, `λ > 0`, `V ≥ 0`, `W ≥ 0` with no zero row, and `H > 0` entrywise.
nodes.title: The `H` update is monotone

nodes.summary: The `W`-dependent part `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑_{f,k} w_fk / λ_k` of the `ℓ₁`-ARD objective (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 20, `β = 1`).
nodes.title: W-dependent part of the ARD-NMF objective

nodes.summary: The `ℓ₁`-ARD multiplicative update of `W` for `β = 1` (Tan–Févotte, Algorithm 2): `w_fk ← w_fk (∑_n v_fn h_kn / (W H)_fn) / (∑_n h_kn + φ / λ_k)`.
nodes.title: ARD multiplicative update of W

nodes.summary: It does not increase `D_1(V | W H) / φ + ∑ w_fk / λ_k`, for `φ > 0`, `λ > 0`, `V ≥ 0`, `H ≥ 0` with no zero column, and `W > 0` entrywise (the transpose of `objectiveH_updateH_le`).
nodes.title: The `W` update is monotone

nodes.summary: The relevance update `λ_k = (‖w_k‖₁ + ‖h_k‖₁ + b) / c` (Tan–Févotte, Eq. 33, `ℓ₁` prior; `c = F + N + a + 1`).
nodes.title: Relevance update in ARD-NMF

nodes.summary: The relevance update is the exact minimizer (Tan–Févotte, §IV-C): for `A > 0` and `c > 0`, `λ ↦ A / λ + c log λ` attains its minimum over `λ > 0` at `λ = A / c`.
nodes.title: The relevance update is the exact minimizer

nodes.summary: If `λ > 0` does as well as `A / c`, then `λ = A / c`.
nodes.title: The minimizer is unique

nodes.summary: The relevance never falls below its floor `b / c` (`W, H ≥ 0`, `c > 0`).
nodes.title: Lower bound on the relevance update

nodes.summary: Pruning (Tan–Févotte, §IV-D): the relevance equals its floor `b / c` exactly when the `k`-th column of `W` and the `k`-th row of `H` are zero (`W, H ≥ 0`, `c > 0`).
nodes.title: Pruning

nodes.summary: The multiplicative update maps a zero entry of `H` to zero.
nodes.title: A pruned entry stays pruned

nodes.summary: The multiplicative update maps a zero entry of `W` to zero.
nodes.title: A pruned entry stays pruned
Tumour purity, ploidy and copy-ratio algebra

nodes.summary: Average absolute copy number `α q + 2 (1 - α)` of a locus with copy number `q` in the cancer cells, in a sample of purity `α` whose normal cells are diploid (Carter et al. 2012). With `q = τ` this is the sample ploidy `D` of Eq. 1; with the local copy number it is `D_s` of Eq. 2.
nodes.title: Average absolute copy number of a tumor sample

nodes.summary: Relative copy ratio `R = (α q + 2 (1 - α)) / (α τ + 2 (1 - α))` of a locus with copy number `q`, purity `α` and cancer-cell ploidy `τ` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 1).
nodes.title: Relative copy ratio

nodes.summary: The copy-ratio slope `α / D` of Eq. 1 (Carter et al. 2012), the copy ratio of one extra copy per cancer cell.
nodes.title: Copy-ratio slope

nodes.summary: The copy-ratio intercept `2 (1 - α) / D` of Eq. 1 (Carter et al. 2012), the copy ratio of a homozygously deleted locus.
nodes.title: Copy-ratio intercept

nodes.summary: Expected allelic fraction `α s / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a clonal somatic point mutation with multiplicity `s` (copies per cancer cell) at a locus of copy number `q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 2; Eq. 10 is `s = 1`).
nodes.title: Expected allelic fraction of a somatic mutation

nodes.summary: Expected allelic fraction `((1 - α) + α g) / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a heterozygous germline variant present in `g` copies per cancer cell at a locus of copy number `q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 11).
nodes.title: Expected allelic fraction of a germline variant

nodes.summary: The purity `α / (m - (m - 1) α)` that, together with all copy numbers multiplied by `m`, reproduces the copy ratios and allelic fractions of purity `α` (derived from Carter et al. 2012, Eqs. 1, 2, 11).
nodes.title: Rescaled purity

nodes.summary: The mixture copy number is positive in the biological domain `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 < q`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the mixture copy number

nodes.summary: `R = (α / D) q + 2 (1 - α) / D`, for all real arguments.
nodes.title: Eq. 1 is affine in `q`

nodes.summary: If the segment weights `w` sum to one and the ploidy is the weighted mean copy number `τ = ∑ w q`, the weighted mean copy ratio is `1` (Carter et al. 2012, Methods: "correctly calibrated copy-ratio data always has mean = 1").
nodes.title: Calibrated copy ratios have mean `1`

nodes.summary: Allelic fractions are determined by the copy-ratio slope (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 2): `α s / D_s = (α / D) s / R`, whenever `D ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Allelic fractions are determined by the copy-ratio slope

nodes.summary: Inverse of Eq. 1, purity: `α = 2 b / (2 b + δ)` for the slope `b` and intercept `δ`, when `0 < α ≤ 1` and `0 < τ`.
nodes.title: Purity from copy-ratio slope and intercept

nodes.summary: Inverse of Eq. 1, ploidy: `τ = (1 - δ) / b` for the slope `b` and intercept `δ`, when `0 < α ≤ 1` and `0 < τ`.
nodes.title: Ploidy from copy-ratio slope and intercept

nodes.summary: The map `(α, τ) ↦ (α / D, 2 (1 - α) / D)` is a bijection from `{0 < α ≤ 1, 0 < τ}` onto `{0 < b, 0 ≤ δ < 1}`.
nodes.title: Purity and ploidy are identifiable from the slope and intercept of Eq. 1

nodes.summary: The denominator `m - (m - 1) α = m (1 - α) + α` of the rescaled purity is positive for `m > 0` and `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the rescaled purity denominator

nodes.summary: The rescaled purity is again a purity: `0 ≤ α / (m - (m - 1) α) ≤ 1` for `m > 0` and `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Rescaled purity lies in (0, 1)

nodes.summary: Scaling every copy number and the ploidy by `m > 0` and the purity to `α / (m - (m - 1) α)` leaves every copy ratio of Eq. 1 unchanged.
nodes.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, copy ratios

nodes.summary: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, somatic allelic fractions (Eq. 2): with copy number and multiplicity both scaled by `m > 0` and the purity rescaled, the allelic fraction is unchanged.
nodes.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, somatic allelic fractions

nodes.summary: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, germline allelic fractions (Eq. 11): with copy number and germline multiplicity both scaled by `m > 0` and the purity rescaled, the allelic fraction is unchanged.
nodes.title: Ploidy-scaling non-identifiability, germline allelic fractions

nodes.summary: The rescaled solution is a genuinely different purity: for `0 < α < 1` and `m ≠ 1`, `α / (m - (m - 1) α) ≠ α`.
nodes.title: Rescaled purity differs from the original purity

nodes.summary: Doubling every copy number and the ploidy and replacing the purity by `α / (2 - α)` reproduces every copy ratio (the `m = 2` case of `copyRatio_scale`).
nodes.title: Genome doubling

nodes.summary: Somatic allelic fractions are nonnegative in the biological domain.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of somatic allelic fractions

nodes.summary: A somatic allelic fraction is at most one when the multiplicity does not exceed the copy number (`s ≤ q`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction is at most one

nodes.summary: The somatic allelic fraction increases with the purity (`0 ≤ s`, `0 < q`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction increases with purity

nodes.summary: The somatic allelic fraction decreases with the local copy number (`0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ s`, `0 < q ≤ q'`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction decreases with copy number

nodes.summary: The somatic allelic fraction increases with the multiplicity (`0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `0 < q`).
nodes.title: Somatic allelic fraction increases with multiplicity
Detection power for somatic mutations

nodes.summary: The binomial probability `C(n, i) p^i (1 - p)^(n - i)` of `i` successes in `n` trials, as a function of `i : ℕ`. It vanishes for `i > n` (the binomial coefficient is zero there, so the truncated subtraction `n - i` is harmless).
nodes.title: Binomial probability mass function

nodes.summary: The binomial upper tail `ℙ_p(X ≥ m) = ∑_{m ≤ i ≤ n} C(n, i) p^i (1 - p)^(n - i)`, Carter's `P(m)` with `p = ε / 3`.
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail probability

nodes.summary: Binomial probabilities are nonnegative for `0 ≤ p ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of binomial probabilities

nodes.summary: Binomial probabilities are positive on `{0, …, n}` for `0 < p < 1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of binomial probabilities

nodes.summary: Binomial probabilities vanish above `n`.
nodes.title: Binomial probabilities vanish above n

nodes.summary: The binomial law sums to one (the binomial theorem), for every real `p`.
nodes.title: Binomial probabilities sum to one

nodes.summary: Tail probabilities are nonnegative for `0 ≤ p ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of binomial tail probabilities

nodes.summary: `P(0) = 1`, for every real `p`.
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail from zero is one

nodes.summary: `P(m) = 0` for `m > n`.
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail beyond n is zero

nodes.summary: Carter's form of the tail: `P(m) = 1 - ∑_{i < m} Binom(i | n, p)`, for every `m`.
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail as one minus a lower sum

nodes.summary: One step of the tail recursion: `P(m) = Binom(m | n, p) + P(m + 1)`.
nodes.title: Recursion for the binomial upper tail

nodes.summary: `m ↦ P(m)` is antitone for `0 ≤ p ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Binomial upper tail is decreasing
Binomial tails increase with the success probability

nodes.summary: For `a ≤ n` and `0 ≤ p ≤ p' ≤ a / n`, `Binom(a | n, p) ≤ Binom(a | n, p')`.
nodes.title: The binomial likelihood is unimodal in `p`, increasing part

nodes.summary: For `a ≤ n` and `a / n ≤ p ≤ p' ≤ 1`, `Binom(a | n, p') ≤ Binom(a | n, p)`.
nodes.title: The binomial likelihood is unimodal in `p`, decreasing part

nodes.summary: Carter's critical count `k = min {m | P(m) ≤ FPR}` for the null success probability `p₀ = ε / 3` (Online Methods, before Eq. 9).
nodes.title: Critical count of the mutation detection test

nodes.summary: The randomization probability `d = (FPR - P(k)) / (P(k - 1) - P(k))` of Eq. 9.
nodes.title: Randomization probability of the detection test

nodes.summary: The power `Pow(n, f) = P_f(X ≥ k) + d Binom(k - 1 | n, f)` of the exact-size randomized test (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 9, with the randomization at `k - 1`; see the module doc).
nodes.title: Power of the randomized mutation detection test

nodes.summary: The critical count meets the false-positive bound: `P(k) ≤ FPR` (for `FPR ≥ 0`).
nodes.title: Critical count meets the false-positive bound

nodes.summary: The critical count is at most `n + 1` (for `FPR ≥ 0`).
nodes.title: Upper bound on the critical count

nodes.summary: The critical count is positive when `FPR < 1`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the critical count

nodes.summary: Minimality of the critical count: `FPR < P(k - 1)` (for `0 ≤ FPR < 1`).
nodes.title: Minimality of the critical count

nodes.summary: The gap `P(k - 1) - P(k)` is the null probability of the boundary point `k - 1`.
nodes.title: Tail gap at the critical count
The randomization is a probability

nodes.summary: Exact size (Carter et al. 2012, Eq. 9 with the randomization at `k - 1`): under the null `f = p₀` the rejection probability is exactly `FPR`, for `0 ≤ FPR < 1`.
nodes.title: Exact size

nodes.summary: The power is the mixture `(1 - d) P_f(X ≥ k) + d P_f(X ≥ k - 1)` of two tail probabilities.
nodes.title: Detection power as a mixture of tail probabilities

nodes.summary: `Pow(n, f) ≤ Pow(n, f')` for `0 ≤ f ≤ f' ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Power increases with the allelic fraction

nodes.summary: Power increases with purity at the ABSOLUTE allelic fraction `α s / (α q + 2 (1 - α))` of a clonal mutation of multiplicity `0 ≤ s ≤ q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eqs. 2, 9, 10).
nodes.title: Power increases with purity

nodes.summary: Power decreases with local copy number at the ABSOLUTE allelic fraction, for a clonal mutation of multiplicity `0 ≤ s ≤ q ≤ q'` (Carter et al. 2012, Eqs. 2, 9, 10).
nodes.title: Power decreases with local copy number

nodes.summary: Power increases with multiplicity at the ABSOLUTE allelic fraction, for `0 ≤ s ≤ s' ≤ q` (Carter et al. 2012, Eqs. 2, 9).
nodes.title: Power increases with multiplicity
Cancer cell fraction estimation

nodes.summary: Posterior probability that the parameter `c i` exceeds `t`, for prior weights `prior` and likelihoods `lik i` of the observed data: `∑_{c i > t} prior i lik i / ∑_i prior i lik i`.
nodes.title: Posterior tail probability on a grid

nodes.summary: If the kernels `L` (data `x`) and `L'` (data `x'`) satisfy the TP2 inequality `L' i L j ≥ L i L' j` whenever `c j ≤ c i`, then for a nonnegative prior every posterior tail `P(c > t)` is at least as large under `L'` as under `L` (both normalizers positive).
nodes.title: Monotone likelihood ratio implies stochastically larger posteriors

nodes.summary: The binomial family is TP2 (monotone likelihood ratio in the success probability): for `a ≤ a'` and `0 ≤ p ≤ p' ≤ 1`, `Binom(a | n, p') Binom(a' | n, p) ≤ Binom(a' | n, p') Binom(a | n, p)`.
nodes.title: The binomial family is TP2

nodes.summary: Landau et al.'s posterior probability that the CCF exceeds `t`, given `a` of `n` reads, purity `α`, copy number `q`, a prior `prior` on the grid points `grid k`: `∑_{grid k > t} π_k Binom(a | n, f(grid k)) / ∑_k π_k Binom(a | n, f(grid k))`, with `f(c) = α c / (α q + 2 (1 - α))`.
nodes.title: Posterior probability that the cancer cell fraction exceeds a threshold

nodes.summary: Landau et al.'s clonal call: `P(CCF > t | a) > γ` (they take `t = 0.95`, `γ = 0.5`).
nodes.title: Clonal call for a mutation

nodes.summary: Hypotheses on the CCF grid model: purity `0 < α ≤ 1`, copy number `q > 0`, grid in `[0, q]` and within the defining CCF bound `≤ 1`, a nonnegative prior, and one grid point of positive prior weight whose allelic fraction lies strictly inside `(0, 1)` (this makes every posterior well defined).
nodes.title: Grid model for the cancer cell fraction

nodes.summary: In a grid model every posterior normalizer `∑_k π_k Binom(a | n, f(grid k))`, `a ≤ n`, is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the grid posterior normalizer

nodes.summary: The CCF posterior is stochastically increasing in the read count (Landau et al. 2013 with the monotone-likelihood-ratio argument): `P(CCF > t | a) ≤ P(CCF > t | a')` for `a ≤ a' ≤ n`.
nodes.title: The CCF posterior is stochastically increasing in the read count

nodes.summary: The clonal call is upward closed in the read count.
nodes.title: The clonal call is upward closed in the read count

nodes.summary: For every CCF threshold `t` and posterior level `γ` there is `a₀` such that, for `a ≤ n`, the mutation is called clonal iff `a₀ ≤ a` (`a₀ = n + 1` when no count is called clonal).
nodes.title: The clonal call is a read-count threshold

nodes.summary: The continuous maximum-likelihood CCF `ĉ = min 1 (a / (n κ))` for the allelic-fraction slope `κ = α / (α q + 2 (1 - α))`. Landau et al. (2013) use the grid posterior; this continuous maximizer over `[0, 1]` is derived here.
nodes.title: Maximum-likelihood cancer cell fraction

nodes.summary: For `0 < α ≤ 1`, `q ≥ 1`, `a ≤ n` and `0 < n`, the likelihood `c ↦ Binom(a | n, f(c))` on `[0, 1]` is maximized at `ĉ = min 1 (a / (n κ))`.
nodes.title: The continuous CCF MLE
Saturation power for cancer gene discovery

nodes.summary: Power of the one-sided binomial test of Lawrence et al. (2014): the probability, when each of `N` patients is mutated with probability `p₁`, of observing a count `x` whose background p-value `ℙ_{p₀}(X ≥ x)` is at most `γ`.
nodes.title: Saturation power of the binomial gene discovery test

nodes.summary: Background probability `p₀ = 1 - (1 - μ f_g)^(3L/4)` that a patient carries at least one non-silent background mutation in a gene of `L` coding bases (Lawrence et al. 2014).
nodes.title: Background mutation probability per patient

nodes.summary: Signal probability `p₁ = p₀ + r (1 - m)` for a gene mutated in a fraction `r` of patients above background, with miss rate `m` (Lawrence et al. 2014).
nodes.title: Signal mutation probability per patient

nodes.summary: For `0 ≤ p₀ < p₁ ≤ 1` and any level `γ > 0`, the power of the binomial test tends to `1` as the number of patients grows.
nodes.title: Power tends to one

nodes.summary: For every target power `β < 1` there is a cohort size beyond which the power is at least `β` (Lawrence et al. 2014 take `β = 0.9`).
nodes.title: `N_β` exists

nodes.summary: The background probability is a probability below one: `0 ≤ p₀ < 1` for `0 ≤ μ f_g < 1` and `L ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Background mutation probability lies in (0, 1)

nodes.summary: A driver mutated above background raises the per-patient probability: `p₀ < p₀ + r (1 - m)` for `r > 0` and `m < 1`.
nodes.title: Driver genes raise the per-patient mutation probability

nodes.summary: Differential-equation models of population growth, species interaction and evolutionary change, such as logistic growth, predator–prey systems, replicator dynamics and quasispecies.
nodes.title: Population and evolutionary dynamics
Eigen's quasispecies error threshold

nodes.summary: The master-sequence vector field of the single-peak quasispecies without back mutation: `x' = σ Q x - (σ x + (1 - x)) x`, where `σ` is the master fitness relative to the mutants and `Q` the probability of an error-free copy. Meaningful for `σ > 1`, `0 ≤ Q ≤ 1`, `0 ≤ x ≤ 1`; it is a polynomial and is defined for all reals.
nodes.title: Master-sequence vector field of the single-peak quasispecies

nodes.summary: The interior equilibrium `x* = (σ Q - 1) / (σ - 1)` of the master frequency. For `σ = 1` (no selective advantage) Lean's `x / 0 = 0` gives the junk value `0`; every result below assumes `1 < σ`.
nodes.title: Interior equilibrium of the master-sequence frequency

nodes.summary: The master-sequence equation is logistic: `x' = x ((σ Q - 1) - (σ - 1) x)`.
nodes.title: Master-sequence equation is logistic

nodes.summary: The equilibria of the master frequency are `0` and `x* = (σ Q - 1)/(σ - 1)`.
nodes.title: Equilibria of the master-sequence frequency

nodes.summary: The mutant frequency at the interior equilibrium is `1 - x* = σ (1 - Q)/(σ - 1)`.
nodes.title: Mutant frequency at the interior equilibrium

nodes.summary: For `σ > 1`, the interior equilibrium is positive iff `σ Q > 1`.
nodes.title: Error threshold

nodes.summary: For `σ > 1` and `Q ≤ 1` the interior equilibrium is at most `1`.
nodes.title: Interior quasispecies equilibrium is at most 1

nodes.summary: For per-site fidelity `0 < q < 1` and `σ > 0`, `σ q ^ L > 1` iff `L < log σ / (-log q)`.
nodes.title: Maximal genome length

nodes.summary: The interior equilibrium depends continuously on `Q`, so any sequence of fidelities with `Q_L → Qlim` has `x*(Q_L) → x*(Qlim)`.
nodes.title: Continuity of the interior equilibrium in the copying fidelity

nodes.summary: With per-site fidelity `q_L = 1 - μ / L`, so that the expected number of mutations per genome copy is `μ`, the error-free probability is `q_L ^ L → e^{-μ}` and the master equilibrium converges to `(σ e^{-μ} - 1)/(σ - 1)`.
nodes.title: Fixed-`q_L` limit

nodes.summary: In the fixed-`q_L` limit the master sequence persists iff `μ < log σ`.
nodes.title: Eigen's error threshold

nodes.summary: If `σ > 1`, `σ Q > 1` and `x` solves the master equation on `[0, ∞)` from a positive master frequency, then `x t → x*`.
nodes.title: Convergence above the threshold

nodes.summary: If `σ > 1`, `σ Q ≤ 1` and `x` solves the master equation on `[0, ∞)` from a positive master frequency, then `x t → 0`.
nodes.title: Loss of the master at or below the threshold
Logistic growth equation

nodes.summary: Explicit solution of the logistic equation `x' = r x (1 - x / K)` with `x 0 = x₀`: `K x₀ e^{r t} / (K + x₀ (e^{r t} - 1))`.
nodes.title: Explicit solution of the logistic equation

nodes.summary: The logistic solution starts at `x₀` (for `K ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Initial value of the logistic solution

nodes.summary: In the biological domain (`K > 0`, `x₀ > 0`, `r t ≥ 0`, or `x₀ ≤ K`) the denominator of the logistic solution is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the logistic solution's denominator

nodes.summary: Wherever the denominator `K + x₀ (e^{r t} - 1)` is nonzero, `x' = r x (1 - x / K)` (all real parameters, `K ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: The explicit solution solves the logistic equation

nodes.summary: Uniqueness of the logistic solution on `[0, T]`: in the biological domain (`K > 0`, `x₀ > 0`, `r ≥ 0`), any function continuous on `[0, T]`, with right derivative `r x (1 - x / K)` on `[0, T)` and `x 0 = x₀`, equals the explicit solution on `[0, T]`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the logistic solution

nodes.summary: For `r > 0` and `x₀ > 0`, `x(t) → K` as `t → ∞` (the identity needs no sign condition on `K`; biologically `K > 0`).
nodes.title: Convergence to the carrying capacity

nodes.summary: For fixed `r`, `x₀`, `t`, the logistic solution tends to the exponential-growth solution `x₀ e^{r t}` as the carrying capacity `K → ∞`.
nodes.title: Exponential limit

nodes.summary: Log-odds grow linearly for a frequency (`K = 1`): for `0 < x₀ < 1` and all `r`, `t`, `log (x(t) / (1 - x(t))) = log (x₀ / (1 - x₀)) + r t`.
nodes.title: Log-odds grow linearly

nodes.summary: Starting from frequency `a ∈ (0, 1)` with `r ≠ 0`, the logistic frequency reaches `1 - a` at time `(2 / r) log ((1 - a) / a)`.
nodes.title: Exact deterministic transit time

reading_title.source: Logistic transit time from $1/(2N)$ to $1 - 1/(2N)$

nodes.summary: The transit time from `1 / (2N)` to `1 - 1 / (2N)` is `(2 / r) log (2N - 1)`, for `N ≥ 1` and `r ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Logistic transit time from $1/(2N)$ to $1 - 1/(2N)$

nodes.summary: For `r > 0` and `0 < x₀ < K` the logistic solution is strictly increasing, so the transit time of `logistic_transitTime` is the unique time at which `1 - a` is reached.
nodes.title: Logistic solution is strictly increasing
Lotka–Volterra predator–prey model

nodes.summary: The Lotka–Volterra first integral `V(x, y) = δ x - γ log x + β y - α log y` for the system `x' = α x - β x y`, `y' = δ x y - γ y`. It is meaningful on the open positive quadrant `x, y > 0`; elsewhere `Real.log` takes junk values (`log 0 = 0`, `log (-x) = log x`).
nodes.title: First integral of the Lotka–Volterra system

nodes.summary: If `x' = α x - β x y` and `y' = δ x y - γ y` at time `t` and `x t, y t > 0`, then `t ↦ V(x t, y t)` has derivative `0` at `t`.
nodes.title: Lotka–Volterra first integral

nodes.summary: If `(x, y)` solves the Lotka–Volterra system on `[0, ∞)` and both populations stay positive there, then `V(x t, y t) = V(x 0, y 0)` for all `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Positive solutions lie on level curves

nodes.summary: For positive parameters and `x, y > 0`, `V(γ / δ, α / β) ≤ V(x, y)`.
nodes.title: The coexistence equilibrium minimizes the first integral
Replicator dynamics

nodes.summary: The mean fitness `f̄(x) = ∑ i, x i * f x i` of the population state `x` for the fitness function `f`.
nodes.title: Mean fitness of a population state

nodes.summary: `x` solves the replicator equation `x_i' = x_i (f_i(x) - f̄(x))` for all times `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Solution of the replicator equation

nodes.summary: `x` is a rest point of the replicator equation: `x_i (f_i(x) - f̄(x)) = 0` for all `i`.
nodes.title: Rest point of the replicator equation

nodes.summary: If every strategy is present (`x i > 0`), then `x` is a rest point iff every strategy has fitness equal to the mean fitness.
nodes.title: Rest points in the interior are equalizers

nodes.summary: The total frequency `∑ x_i` evolves by `(∑ x_i)' = f̄(x) (1 - ∑ x_i)`.
nodes.title: Evolution of the total frequency under replicator dynamics

nodes.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a solution with `∑ x_i(0) = 1` satisfies `∑ x_i(t) = 1` for all `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Invariance of the simplex hyperplane

nodes.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a strategy absent at time `0` (`x_i(0) = 0`) stays absent for all `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Invariance of the faces of the simplex

nodes.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a strategy with positive frequency at time `0` has positive frequency for all `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Present strategies stay present

nodes.summary: For continuous fitness `f`, a solution starting in the standard simplex (`x i ≥ 0` for all `i` and `∑ i, x i = 1`) stays in it for all `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Invariance of the simplex (Hofbauer–Sigmund 1998, §7.1)

nodes.summary: Reaction–diffusion models of biological spread and spatial patterning, including travelling waves, morphogen gradients and Turing instabilities.
nodes.title: Reaction–diffusion and pattern formation
Fisher–KPP travelling waves

nodes.summary: `U` is a traveling-wave profile of speed `c` for `∂u/∂t = D ∂²u/∂x² + r u (1 - u)`: it is twice differentiable with first derivative `U'` and `U'' = -(c U' + r U (1 - U)) / D`, which for `D ≠ 0` is the profile equation `D U'' + c U' + r U (1 - U) = 0`.
nodes.title: Traveling-wave profile of the Fisher–KPP equation

nodes.summary: A traveling front of speed `c`: a wave profile with `0 < U < 1`, `U → 1` at `-∞` and `U → 0` at `+∞`.
nodes.title: Traveling front of the Fisher–KPP equation

nodes.summary: Time derivative of the wave `u(x, t) = U(x - c t)`: `∂u/∂t = -c U'(x - c t)`.
nodes.title: Time derivative of a traveling wave

nodes.summary: Space derivative of the wave: `∂u/∂x = U'(x - c t)`.
nodes.title: Space derivative of a traveling wave

nodes.summary: Second space derivative of the wave; with `hD : D ≠ 0` it gives the PDE `-c U' = D U'' + r U (1 - U)`, i.e. `∂u/∂t = D ∂²u/∂x² + r u (1 - u)`.
nodes.title: Traveling wave solves the Fisher–KPP equation

nodes.summary: If `D, r > 0` and `c² < 4 r D`, a wave profile tending to `0` at `+∞` is not eventually positive. (This excludes `|c| < 2 √(r D)`, not `c < 2 √(r D)` for negative `c`.)
nodes.title: No traveling wave with `c² < 4 r D`

nodes.summary: A front of speed `c` needs `c² ≥ 4 r D`; for `c ≥ 0` this is `c ≥ 2 √(r D)`.
nodes.title: Minimal speed of Fisher–KPP traveling fronts

nodes.summary: The rate `κ = √(r / (6 D))` of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave.
nodes.title: Rate of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave

nodes.summary: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella speed `c = 5 √(r D / 6)` (`5 / √6` when `D = r = 1`).
nodes.title: Speed of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave

nodes.summary: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella profile `U(z) = (1 + C exp (κ z))⁻²`.
nodes.title: Ablowitz–Zeppetella wave profile

nodes.summary: The derivative of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella profile, `-2 κ C e^{κ z} (1 + C e^{κ z})⁻³`.
nodes.title: Derivative of the Ablowitz–Zeppetella profile

nodes.summary: For `D, r, C > 0`, `(1 + C exp (z √(r / (6 D))))⁻²` is a front of speed `5 √(r D / 6)`.
nodes.title: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella front

nodes.summary: The Ablowitz–Zeppetella speed exceeds the minimal speed: `2 √(r D) < 5 √(r D / 6)`.
nodes.title: Ablowitz–Zeppetella speed exceeds the minimal front speed

nodes.summary: Kolmogorov–Petrovsky–Piskunov: fronts exist at every speed `c ≥ 2 √(r D)`, and they are strictly decreasing.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov–Petrovsky–Piskunov: fronts exist at every speed `c ≥ 2 √(r D)`
Morphogen gradients and the French flag model

nodes.summary: The decay length `λ = √(D / k)` of a morphogen with diffusion coefficient `D` and linear degradation rate `k` (both positive in the model).
nodes.title: Decay length of a morphogen gradient

nodes.summary: The steady-state gradient `c(x) = (j / √(D k)) e^{-x/λ}`, `λ = √(D / k)`, for source flux `j` at `x = 0`. Meaningful for `D, k > 0`.
nodes.title: Steady-state exponential morphogen profile

nodes.summary: The French-flag boundary for threshold `θ`: `x_θ = λ log(c(0) / θ)`, where `c(0) = j / √(D k)`. Meaningful for `D, k, j, θ > 0`; it is negative when `θ > c(0)` (no cell is above threshold).
nodes.title: French-flag boundary position for a threshold

nodes.summary: A bounded steady state of the synthesis–diffusion–degradation model on `[0, ∞)`, with `c' = dc/dx`: `D c'' = k c` for `x > 0`, `c` and `c'` continuous up to the source, source flux `-D c'(0) = j`, and `c` bounded on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Bounded steady state of the synthesis–diffusion–degradation model

nodes.summary: The decay length is positive for positive `D` and `k`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the decay length

nodes.summary: `D / λ² = k`.
nodes.title: Diffusion coefficient over squared decay length equals degradation rate

nodes.summary: `√(D k) = D / λ`, so the source amplitude is `c(0) = j λ / D`.
nodes.title: Source amplitude in terms of the decay length

nodes.summary: The profile has slope `c'(x) = -c(x)/λ`.
nodes.title: Slope of the morphogen profile

nodes.summary: The exponential profile is a bounded steady state with source flux `j`.
nodes.title: Exponential profile is a bounded steady state

nodes.summary: Every bounded steady state with source flux `j` is the exponential profile on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness

nodes.summary: The profile is strictly decreasing in `x` for a positive source.
nodes.title: Morphogen profile is strictly decreasing

nodes.summary: The profile equals `θ` at the boundary `x_θ`.
nodes.title: Profile equals the threshold at the French-flag boundary

nodes.summary: For positive parameters and threshold `θ`, `c(x) = θ` exactly at `x = x_θ = λ log(c(0)/θ)`.
nodes.title: French-flag boundary

nodes.summary: A cell at `x` is at or above threshold `θ` iff it lies within the boundary `x_θ`: `θ ≤ c(x) ↔ x ≤ x_θ`.
nodes.title: French-flag regions

nodes.summary: Scaling the source flux by `a > 0` moves every French-flag boundary by `λ log a`.
nodes.title: Boundary shift

parts: Doubling the source flux shifts boundaries by
reading_title.source: Doubling the source flux shifts boundaries by $\lambda \log 2$

nodes.summary: Doubling the source flux shifts every French-flag boundary away from the source by exactly `λ log 2`.
nodes.title: Doubling the source flux shifts boundaries by $\lambda \log 2$
Turing patterns and diffusion-driven instability

nodes.summary: The diffusion matrix `D = diag(d_u, d_v)` of a two-species reaction-diffusion system.
nodes.title: Diffusion matrix of a two-species system

nodes.summary: The mode matrix `J - k² D` governing the Fourier mode of wavenumber `k` of the linearized system `w_t = D w_xx + J w`, where `J` is the Jacobian of the kinetics at the steady state (convention: `J i j` is the partial derivative of the `i`-th reaction term with respect to the `j`-th species, so `J = [[f_u, f_v], [g_u, g_v]]`).
nodes.title: Mode matrix of a linearized reaction-diffusion system

nodes.summary: The Fourier mode of wavenumber `k` is *linearly unstable*: the mode matrix `J - k² D` has a complex eigenvalue `μ` with `0 < Re μ`.
nodes.title: Linearly unstable Fourier mode

nodes.summary: The complex Fourier mode `w(t, x) = e^{μ t} cos(k x) v` with growth rate `μ`, wavenumber `k` and amplitude vector `v`. (The real part of a complex solution of the real linear system is a real solution.)
nodes.title: Complex Fourier mode

nodes.summary: `w` is a classical solution of the linearized reaction-diffusion system `w_t = D w_xx + J w` on `ℝ × ℝ`: `w(t, ·)` is twice differentiable with first and second derivatives `wx`, `wxx`, and `w(·, x)` is differentiable with the prescribed time derivative.
nodes.title: Classical solution of the linearized reaction-diffusion system

nodes.summary: The dispersion polynomial `h(q) = d_u d_v q² - (d_v f_u + d_u g_v) q + det J`, so that `det (J - k² D) = h(k²)` (`det_modeMatrix`).
nodes.title: Dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: The squared critical wavenumber `k_c² = (d_v f_u + d_u g_v) / (2 d_u d_v)`, the minimizer of the dispersion polynomial (meaningful for `d_u, d_v > 0`; division by zero gives `0`).
nodes.title: Squared critical wavenumber

nodes.summary: The discriminant `(d_v f_u + d_u g_v)² - 4 d_u d_v det J` of the dispersion polynomial.
nodes.title: Discriminant of the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: Lower end `q₋ = (S - √Δ) / (2 d_u d_v)` of the unstable band of squared wavenumbers, where `S = d_v f_u + d_u g_v` and `Δ = bandDiscriminant` (meaningful when `0 < Δ`, `d_u, d_v > 0`).
nodes.title: Lower end of the unstable wavenumber band

nodes.summary: Upper end `q₊ = (S + √Δ) / (2 d_u d_v)` of the unstable band of squared wavenumbers (meaningful when `0 < Δ`, `d_u, d_v > 0`).
nodes.title: Upper end of the unstable wavenumber band

nodes.summary: The Neumann wavenumber `k_n = n π / L` of the mode `cos(n π x / L)` on `[0, L]`. Meaningful only for `0 < L`; at `L = 0` the totalized division gives `0`, so every labeled Neumann mode collapses to the homogeneous mode.
nodes.title: Neumann wavenumber on an interval

nodes.summary: `tr (J - k² D) = tr J - k² (d_u + d_v)`.
nodes.title: Trace of the mode matrix

nodes.summary: `det (J - k² D) = h(k²)`.
nodes.title: Determinant of the mode matrix is the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: A real `2 × 2` matrix has a complex eigenvalue with positive real part iff its trace is positive or its determinant is negative.
nodes.title: Routh–Hurwitz for `2 × 2` matrices

nodes.summary: Mode `k` is unstable iff `0 < tr (J - k² D)` or `det (J - k² D) < 0`.
nodes.title: Instability criterion for a Fourier mode via trace and determinant

nodes.summary: The Fourier mode `e^{μ t} cos(k x) v` is a classical solution of the linearized system `w_t = D w_xx + J w` iff `(J - k² D) v = μ v`.
nodes.title: Dispersion relation

nodes.summary: The amplitude of a Fourier mode: `‖w(t, 0)‖ = e^{Re μ · t} ‖v‖`.
nodes.title: Amplitude of a Fourier mode

nodes.summary: `‖w(t, 0)‖` is the amplitude of the mode: `‖w(t, x)‖ ≤ ‖w(t, 0)‖` for every `x`.
nodes.title: Fourier mode is largest at the origin

nodes.summary: A nonzero Fourier mode grows without bound iff its growth rate has positive real part.
nodes.title: Fourier mode grows unboundedly iff its growth rate is positive

nodes.summary: A Fourier mode grows iff `J - k² D` has an eigenvalue with positive real part.
nodes.title: A Fourier mode grows iff `J - k² D` has an eigenvalue with positive real part

nodes.summary: The homogeneous mode `k = 0` is stable when the kinetics are stable (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`).
nodes.title: Homogeneous mode is stable for stable kinetics

nodes.summary: If `tr J < 0` and `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, mode `k` is unstable iff `h(k²) < 0`.
nodes.title: Mode instability iff the dispersion polynomial is negative

nodes.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`), `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, and `det (J - k² D) < 0`, then the homogeneous mode is stable while mode `k` is unstable.
nodes.title: Diffusion-driven instability (Turing 1952)

nodes.summary: The value of the dispersion polynomial at its minimizer: `h(k_c²) = det J - (d_v f_u + d_u g_v)² / (4 d_u d_v)`.
nodes.title: Minimum value of the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: The critical squared wavenumber minimizes the dispersion polynomial over all real `q`.
nodes.title: Critical squared wavenumber minimizes the dispersion polynomial

nodes.summary: The Turing condition in squared form: `2 √(d_u d_v det J) < S` iff `0 < S` and `4 d_u d_v det J < S²`, where `S = d_v f_u + d_u g_v`. This holds for all real inputs: when `d_u d_v det J < 0`, `Real.sqrt` returns `0` and both sides reduce to `0 < S`.
nodes.title: Turing condition in squared form

nodes.summary: For `d_u, d_v > 0` and `0 < det J`, the dispersion polynomial is negative at some `q ≥ 0` iff `2 √(d_u d_v det J) < d_v f_u + d_u g_v`.
nodes.title: Turing's criterion for diffusion-driven instability

nodes.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion (`tr J < 0`, `0 < det J`) and `d_u, d_v > 0`, some Fourier mode is unstable iff `d_v f_u + d_u g_v > 2 √(d_u d_v det J)`.
nodes.title: Turing's criterion

nodes.summary: Under Turing's criterion the critical wavenumber `k_c = √(k_c²)` is itself unstable (and `0 < k_c²`).
nodes.title: Critical wavenumber is unstable under Turing's criterion

nodes.summary: At the bifurcation threshold `d_v f_u + d_u g_v = 2 √(d_u d_v det J)` the critical squared wavenumber is `k_c² = √(det J / (d_u d_v))` and `h(k_c²) = 0`.
nodes.title: Critical wavenumber at the Turing bifurcation threshold

nodes.summary: If the steady state is stable without diffusion and `d_u, d_v ≥ 0`, diffusion-driven instability forces `f_u g_v < 0`.
nodes.title: `f_u` and `g_v` have opposite signs

nodes.summary: In the activator-inhibitor sign pattern (`u` is the activator, `0 < f_u`; then `g_v < 0` follows from `tr J < 0`), diffusion-driven instability of a kinetically stable state forces `d_u < d_v`.
nodes.title: The inhibitor diffuses faster

nodes.summary: For `d_u, d_v > 0`, the dispersion polynomial is negative exactly on the open band `(q₋, q₊)`, which is nonempty iff the discriminant is positive.
nodes.title: Dispersion polynomial is negative exactly on the unstable band

nodes.summary: The Neumann mode `cos(k_n x)` has zero flux at both ends of `[0, L]`: the `x`-derivative of the Fourier mode with wavenumber `k_n = n π / L` vanishes at `x = 0` and `x = L`.
nodes.title: Neumann modes have zero flux at the boundary

nodes.summary: On `[0, L]` with Neumann boundary conditions, if `tr J < 0` and `d_u, d_v > 0`, mode `n` is unstable iff `k_n² = (n π / L)²` lies in the unstable band `(q₋, q₊)` (which requires a positive discriminant).
nodes.title: Finite domain

nodes.summary: Only finitely many Neumann modes are unstable on `[0, L]` (for `d_u, d_v, L > 0`, any `J`).
nodes.title: Only finitely many Neumann modes are unstable

nodes.summary: If the first nonhomogeneous mode already lies beyond the band, `q₊ ≤ (π / L)²`, then no Neumann mode is unstable on `[0, L]`.
nodes.title: Small domains admit no pattern

nodes.summary: Every long enough interval has a squared Neumann wavenumber inside a given nonempty open band `(qlo, qhi)` with `0 < qhi`: there is `L₀ > 0` such that for all `L ≥ L₀` some `(n π / L)²` lies in `(qlo, qhi)`.
nodes.title: Long intervals have a squared Neumann wavenumber in any given band

nodes.summary: Under Turing's criterion, every long enough interval `[0, L]` has an unstable Neumann mode.
nodes.title: Large domains pattern

nodes.summary: Schnakenberg's reaction terms `(f, g) = (a - u + u² v, b - u² v)` as a map on `x = (u, v) : Fin 2 → ℝ`, with source rates `a, b` (biologically `a, b > 0`).
nodes.title: Schnakenberg reaction kinetics

nodes.summary: The homogeneous steady state `(u₀, v₀) = (a + b, b / (a + b)²)` of the Schnakenberg kinetics (meaningful for `a + b ≠ 0`; at `a + b = 0` the division gives the junk `v₀ = 0`).
nodes.title: Steady state of the Schnakenberg kinetics

nodes.summary: The Jacobian of the Schnakenberg kinetics at its steady state, `[[(b - a) / (a + b), (a + b)²], [-2 b / (a + b), -(a + b)²]]`.
nodes.title: Jacobian of the Schnakenberg kinetics at its steady state

nodes.summary: `(a + b, b / (a + b)²)` is a steady state of the Schnakenberg kinetics when `a + b ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Schnakenberg steady state is an equilibrium

nodes.summary: The Jacobian matrix of the Schnakenberg kinetics at the steady state is `schnakenbergJacobian a b`.
nodes.title: Computation of the Schnakenberg Jacobian at the steady state

nodes.summary: `det J = (a + b)²` for the Schnakenberg Jacobian (`a + b ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Determinant of the Schnakenberg Jacobian

nodes.summary: The Schnakenberg steady state is stable without diffusion iff `b - a < (a + b)³` (for `0 < a + b`; then `0 < det J` automatically).
nodes.title: Stability of the Schnakenberg steady state without diffusion

nodes.summary: Turing instability of the Schnakenberg kinetics (Murray 2003, ch. 2). With `d_u = 1`, `d_v = d > 0`, `0 < a + b` and `b - a < (a + b)³` (stable without diffusion), some Fourier mode is unstable iff `2 √d (a + b)² < d (b - a) - (a + b)³`.
nodes.title: Turing instability of the Schnakenberg kinetics

nodes.summary: Gierer–Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics in Murray's nondimensional form `(f, g) = (a - b u + u² / v, u² - v)` on `x = (u, v)` (biologically `a, b > 0` and `u, v > 0`; at `v = 0` the division gives the junk `u² / 0 = 0`).
nodes.title: Gierer–Meinhardt activator-inhibitor kinetics

nodes.summary: The homogeneous steady state `(u₀, v₀) = ((a + 1) / b, ((a + 1) / b)²)` of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics (meaningful for `b ≠ 0`, `a + 1 ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Steady state of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics

nodes.summary: The Jacobian of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at its steady state, `[[b (1 - a) / (1 + a), -(b / (a + 1))²], [2 (a + 1) / b, -1]]`.
nodes.title: Jacobian of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at its steady state

nodes.summary: `((a + 1) / b, ((a + 1) / b)²)` is a steady state of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics when `a + 1 ≠ 0` and `b ≠ 0`.
nodes.title: Gierer–Meinhardt steady state is an equilibrium

nodes.summary: The Jacobian matrix of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics at the steady state is `giererMeinhardtJacobian a b`.
nodes.title: Computation of the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian at the steady state

nodes.summary: `det J = b` for the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian (`a + 1 ≠ 0`, `b ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Determinant of the Gierer–Meinhardt Jacobian

nodes.summary: The Gierer–Meinhardt steady state is stable without diffusion iff `b (1 - a) < 1 + a` (for `0 < a + 1`; then `0 < det J = b` for `0 < b`).
nodes.title: Stability of the Gierer–Meinhardt steady state without diffusion

nodes.summary: With `d_u = 1`, `d_v = d > 0`, `0 < a + 1`, `0 < b` and `b (1 - a) < 1 + a` (stable without diffusion), some Fourier mode is unstable iff `2 √(d b) < d b (1 - a) / (1 + a) - 1`.
nodes.title: Turing instability of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics

nodes.summary: Compartmental, renewal and branching-process models of infectious disease transmission and their reproduction numbers.
nodes.title: Mathematical epidemiology
Euler–Lotka equation and the reproduction number

nodes.summary: The reproductive number implied by growth rate `r` and generation-interval law `g`: `R = 1 / M_g(-r)` (Wallinga–Lipsitch 2007, eq. 2.9).
nodes.title: Reproductive number from growth rate and generation interval

nodes.summary: `g₁ ≤cx g₂` if `∫ φ dg₁ ≤ ∫ φ dg₂` for every convex `φ : ℝ → ℝ` that is integrable under both laws (Shaked–Shanthikumar 2007, §3.A).
nodes.title: Convex order

nodes.summary: For `c ≠ 0`, the exponential `b(t) = c e^{r t}` solves `b(t) = R ∫ b(t - a) g(da)` for every `t` iff `R M_g(-r) = 1`. This is meaningful when `a ↦ e^{-r a}` is `g`-integrable; otherwise Lean's integral and `M_g(-r)` are both `0` and both sides of the equivalence are false.
nodes.title: Renewal equation for exponential growth

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `renewal_exp_iff`, exponential growth at rate `r` solves the renewal equation iff `R = 1 / M_g(-r)`.
nodes.title: Euler–Lotka

nodes.summary: The reproductive number is positive when `M_g(-r)` is finite.
nodes.title: Positivity of the reproductive number

nodes.summary: Fixed generation interval `T`: `R = e^{r T}` (for all real `r`, `T`).
nodes.title: Fixed generation interval

nodes.summary: Gamma generation interval with shape `α > 0` and rate `β > 0`: for `r > -β`, `R = (1 + r / β)^α`.
nodes.title: Gamma generation interval

nodes.summary: Exponential generation interval with mean `T > 0` (rate `1 / T`): for `r T > -1`, `R = 1 + r T` (Wallinga–Lipsitch 2007, eq. 3.1).
nodes.title: Exponential generation interval

nodes.summary: If `g₁ ≤cx g₂` and both have finite `M(-r)`, then `R(g₂) ≤ R(g₁)` at growth rate `r` (any real `r`). In particular, among generation intervals with a given mean, the fixed interval maximizes `R`.
nodes.title: More spread lowers `R`

nodes.summary: If the generation interval has finite mean `T̄ = ∫ a g(da)` and finite `M_g(-r)`, then `R ≤ e^{r T̄}` (any real `r`); Wallinga and Lipsitch (2007, §3) note that the fixed interval gives this upper bound.
nodes.title: Jensen bound
Kermack–McKendrick SIR model

nodes.summary: `(S, I, R)` solves the Kermack–McKendrick SIR system with transmission rate `β`, removal rate `γ` and population size `N` for all times `t ≥ 0`: `S' = -β S I / N`, `I' = β S I / N - γ I`, `R' = γ I`.
nodes.title: Solution of the Kermack–McKendrick SIR system

nodes.summary: Along a solution, `S + I + R` is constant on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Conservation of the population

nodes.summary: If initially `I(0) > 0`, with `γ > 0` and `N > 0`, the number of infectives initially increases, `I'(0) > 0`, iff `R₀ S(0) / N > 1` with `R₀ = β / γ`.
nodes.title: Threshold theorem (Kermack–McKendrick 1927)

nodes.summary: For `γ ≠ 0`, the quantity `S(t) e^{R₀ R(t) / N}` (`R₀ = β / γ`) is constant along a solution on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Conserved quantity behind the final-size relation

nodes.summary: If along a solution (`γ ≠ 0`) `S(t) → S∞` and `R(t) → R∞` as `t → ∞`, then `S∞ = S(0) e^{-R₀ (R∞ - R(0)) / N}` with `R₀ = β / γ`. See `final_size_eq` for the classical form.
nodes.title: Final-size relation (Kermack–McKendrick 1927)

nodes.summary: If the population is `N = S + I + R`, nobody is removed initially (`R(0) = 0`), `γ ≠ 0`, `S(t) → S∞` and the epidemic dies out (`I(t) → 0`), then `S∞ = S(0) e^{-R₀ (N - S∞) / N}` with `R₀ = β / γ`.
nodes.title: Final-size equation (Kermack–McKendrick 1927)
Next-generation matrix and the basic reproduction number

nodes.summary: The basic reproduction number `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹)`: the spectral radius (largest modulus of a complex eigenvalue) of the next-generation matrix `F V⁻¹` (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, Eq. (4)). It is meaningful when `V` is invertible (for a nonsingular M-matrix it is).
nodes.title: Basic reproduction number of the next-generation matrix

nodes.summary: `R₀` as a threshold for the linearized infected subsystem (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, proof of Theorem 2). If `F` is entrywise nonnegative and `V` is a nonsingular M-matrix, then every eigenvalue of `F - V` has negative real part iff `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) < 1`.
nodes.title: `R₀` as a threshold for the linearized infected subsystem

nodes.summary: `R₀ > 1` gives an unstable mode (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, proof of Theorem 2). If `F` is entrywise nonnegative and `V` is a nonsingular M-matrix, then `F - V` has an eigenvalue with positive real part iff `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) > 1`.
nodes.title: `R₀ > 1` gives an unstable mode

nodes.summary: The complex eigenvalues of a block lower-triangular real matrix `[[A, 0], [C, D]]` are those of `A` together with those of `D`.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a block lower-triangular matrix

nodes.summary: A block lower-triangular real matrix `[[A, 0], [C, D]]` is Hurwitz iff both diagonal blocks are.
nodes.title: Hurwitz criterion for block lower-triangular matrices

nodes.summary: Threshold theorem, stability half, conditional decay form (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, Theorem 2). Let `x₀` be an equilibrium of `x' = f(x)` on `ℝ^{ι ⊕ κ}` (infected compartments `ι`, the others `κ`), with `f` differentiable at `x₀` and Jacobian `[[F - V, 0], [C, D]]` as in their Lemma 1, where `F ≥ 0`, `V` is a nonsingular M-matrix and `D` is Hurwitz. If `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) < 1`, then every solution defined on all…
nodes.title: Threshold theorem, stability half, conditional decay form

nodes.summary: Threshold theorem, instability half, spectral form (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, Theorem 2). With `F ≥ 0` and `V` a nonsingular M-matrix, if `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) > 1` then the Jacobian `[[F - V, 0], [C, D]]` at the disease-free equilibrium has an eigenvalue with positive real part (whatever `C` and `D`).
nodes.title: Threshold theorem, instability half, spectral form
Superspreading and negative-binomial offspring

nodes.summary: Abstract form of the sharpness theorem: a magnetization satisfying the mean-field differential inequality above `β_c` obeys `m(β) ≥ √(1 - (β_c/β)²)`, and correlations satisfying Simon's self-consistent bound with `φ < 1` are summable with sum at most `|S|/(1 - φ)`. The hypotheses are inputs; the unconditional statement is `ising_sharp_phase_transition`.
